- The screens show a size that is not known as the shared "no value" with a title that says why, and a partial size with **≥** before
  it and a title that says what it leaves out ([R-UI-110](#r-ui-110--a-packages-versions-as-one-table)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`oci`, `TestR_OCI_031_AnIndexCountsThePlatformsTheRepositoryHolds`): an index with every platform held has the whole sum, one of two a partial sum, none no number; an
  attestation manifest is not counted.
- Unit (`formattest`, check 11): a `ViewSizer` that answers a number for a size it does not know fails the kit.
- Integration (`ociremote`, `TestR_API_081_…`): a remote index none of whose platforms was fetched lists `sizeBytes: null`; after one
  platform a partial size; after both the whole size.
- Unit (UI, `version-size.spec.ts`): a size that is not known renders the no-value with its title, never "0 B".

### R-API-081 · A remote repository lists what was fetched through it
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-19 (W-24, "Option A"): a remote repository lists what was fetched through it, and every cell of such
a row is true ([Q-API-343](#q-api-343--a-remote-lists-a-version-once-a-client-fetched-it-or-a-mirror-pass-stored-it)).

- A remote repository lists a version once a client fetched it through the repository, the background download a probe started
  stored it ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-065), a download ahead of a client stored it
  ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-010) or, in mirror mode, a pass stored it; nothing the upstream
  merely knows (the upstream is the upstream catalogue's, another surface, R-CUR-007). A stored version that the repository's delivery
  rules do not deliver (fetched for examination, or blocked after it was fetched) is listed like every stored version, and its
  repository entry says `available: false` with `unavailableReason` `blocked`, `notAllowed` or `outsideRange` (a version outside the
  range of versions of its package's allow, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-026), so no install command is offered through
  it ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-014, Q-CUR-26). A client that only checked a version lists it once its background download stored the content. Per format:

  | Format | A version is listed once | The upstream's metadata alone lists nothing |
  |---|---|---|
  | npm | its tarball is stored (a client's download, a background download or a pass) | the packument |
  | NuGet | its `.nupkg` is stored | the registration and flat-container documents |
  | Ansible Galaxy | its collection archive is stored | the collection and version documents |
  | Debian | a package file of it is stored; the version is named by the parsed index row of the file's path (Q-REPO-330) | `Release` and the indexes |
  | OCI | its tag's manifest was downloaded by a client (R-API-079), a background download stored the whole content of the tag's document (`remote_cache_entries.background_sha256`, migration 00083), or the repository is in mirror mode and holds the tag | a `HEAD` of the tag, which stores its document and downloads nothing until its background download ended |
  | generic | (the files view: every cached file) | |

- The content fill of npm, NuGet, Ansible Galaxy and Debian is a client's download in mode pull-through, so a listed row has one; the
  download is in the statistics within a flush interval (R-STOR-015). A row in mirror mode, or one a background download stored, that no
  client fetched says **Never** and 0 downloads, which is true: Quader fetched it, no client did.
- The note above a remote repository's table says it: "Only what clients have fetched through this repository is listed here, what it
  downloaded after a client asked about a version, and, in mirror mode, what a pass has fetched."; for OCI "Only the tags clients have
  pulled through this repository are listed here, those it downloaded after a client asked about them, and, in mirror mode, those a pass
  has fetched." (Q-UI-217, R-REPO-065).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (`ociremote`, `TestR_API_081_…`): a `HEAD` of a tag lists nothing on a remote whose `downloadOnProbe` is off; the `GET`
  of the tag lists it. With `downloadOnProbe` on, the `HEAD` lists the tag once its background download stored the content
  (`TestR_REPO_065_…`).
- Integration (`debremote`, `TestR_API_081_…`): a Debian remote that holds only indexes lists nothing; the package file a client fetched
  lists its package and version with the file's size; its removal takes the version with it.

### R-API-053 · Guides of the formats
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the guide of R-UI-049 for every registry variant (format × repository
class × client). The format contributes the text (`Guide()` of the format contract, [architecture.md](architecture.md)
R-ARCH-008, Q-ARCH-235); this page owns the operations (Q-API-175).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/guide?client=` | The guide of a repository for one of its format's clients | `read` on the repository (`404` otherwise, like a missing repository) |
| GET | `/api/v1/formats/{format}/guide?class=&client=` | The guide of a class of a format, without a repository | as `GET /api/v1/formats`: authenticated; anonymous while `publicContent` is true (R-AUTH-037) |

- The answer holds `format`, `class`, `client`, `repository` (`null` for the guide of a format), `registryUrl`,
  `publishTarget`, `credentials`, `exposureRules`, `snippets` (R-API-070) and `sections` of `{id, topic, title, html}`. The
  sections are those of the format's guide that are written for the class and the client, in the topic order `what`,
  `configure`, `authenticate`, `install`, `publish`, `maintain`, `audit`, `lockfiles`, `endpoint`, `troubleshooting`; a section
  that renders to nothing is left out, and so are the sections R-API-070 leaves out for a reader who may not publish.
- A section's Markdown is a template over the data of the setup templates plus the class, the client, the publish target
  the caller may deploy to, whether the caller is anonymous, whether the endpoint has exposure rules, and the name of
  `ui.client_setup.token_env_var` (`GuideData`); it has no credential field. The server renders it with the renderer and
  the sanitizer of R-UI-008, with a source bound of its own (256 KiB) instead of `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, which
  bounds untrusted READMEs (Q-API-178).
- The snippets are those of R-API-030 for the same repository, client and credential mode, rendered by the same code
  (R-API-070). The credential mode is `env` for a signed-in caller and `none` for an anonymous one; the guide never carries a
  token or the placeholder of one, and the reference `${QUADER_TOKEN}` of a section's text is rewritten like a snippet's
  (Q-API-176).
- The guide of a format writes `<project>` and `<repository>` where the project key and the repository key go and names
  no target. The guide of a virtual repository
  names its deployment target only to a caller who may deploy there and never lists the members, which are configuration
  (Q-API-179). Both operations answer `503` while no base URL is configured for the endpoint, like R-API-030.
- An unknown format answers `404`; a client or class the format does not have, or a format without clients, `400
  malformed_request`. No answer matches `qdr_(pat|sat|cit)_`.

Acceptance criteria:

- For each npm client, the `snippets` of `GET …/repositories/npm-local/guide` equal the snippets of
  `GET …/repositories/npm-local/client-setup?credentials=env` byte for byte
  (`TestR_API_053_TheGuideShowsTheSnippetsOfTheClientSetup`, and through the stack
  `TestR_API_053_TheGuideThroughTheStack`).
- The guide of a remote repository has no `publish` and no `maintain` section; for an anonymous caller and for a caller
  without `deploy` on the target the guide of a local repository has neither, and an anonymous caller's snippets hold no
  credential line.
- On an endpoint with exposure rules the guide carries the `endpoint` section and the endpoint's own addresses; on the
  default endpoint it does not (`TestR_API_053_TheGuideOnAnEndpointWithRules`).
- No answer, for any class, client and caller, matches `qdr_(pat|sat|cit)_`.

### R-API-070 · A guide carries its snippets beside its sections
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The page **Set up client** shows the snippets first and the explanation below them (R-UI-121, owner, 2026-11-18). The guide's
answer therefore carries the snippets apart from the sections (Q-API-310):

- `Guide.snippets` holds every snippet of R-API-030 for the guide's address, client and credential mode, in the order of the
  format's templates, each with its `tab`. A section carries no snippets; the format contract's `GuideSection` has no field that
  names a setup section ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008), and kit check 8 requires the `configure` and `install`
  templates of every client of a format with a guide instead.
- The guide of a repository holds the publish snippets, and the sections of the topics `publish` and `maintain`, only for a
  caller who may publish there: who holds `deploy` on the repository that receives the publish (`publishTarget`, R-API-030). A
  reader's guide holds what the reader can do.
- The guide of a class (`GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide`) holds the publish snippets for a signed-in caller and a class that
  takes publishing (local, virtual), on the address with `<project>` and `<repository>`; it names no target.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_API_070_AReaderWhoMayNotPublishGetsNoPublishing`: a caller without `deploy` gets no publish snippet and no `publish` or
  `maintain` section from the guide of a local npm repository; the guide of the class local holds a publish snippet, that of
  the class remote none.
- `TestR_API_053_TheGuideShowsTheSnippetsOfTheClientSetup` and `TestR_GENERIC_016_TheGuideShowsTheSnippetsOfTheClientSetup`: the
  guide's snippets equal the client setup's with `credentials=env`.

### R-API-054 · The manual
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-01: the documentation for the people who use Quader and the people who run it is
delivered by Quader itself, behind the Documentation link of the UI (R-UI-050). The manual is Markdown in
[docs/manual/](../manual/README.md), embedded into the binary (`docs/manual/embed.go`), so an installation always shows the
manual of the version it runs; [internal/manual](../../internal/manual/) loads and renders it once at start-up (Q-UI-89).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/manual` | The sections (`user`, `admin`) in reading order with each page's id, title and summary | as `GET /api/v1/formats`: authenticated; anonymous while `publicContent` is true (R-AUTH-037) |
| GET | `/api/v1/manual/{section}/{page}` | One page: `title`, `summary`, `html`, `headings` (levels 2 and 3, with their anchors), `previous` and `next` | as above |

- A page starts with a `# Title` line and a summary paragraph of plain text; the HTML is the page below the title, rendered
  by the renderer and the sanitizer of R-UI-008 with a source bound of 1 MiB. A relative link to another page
  (`access-tokens.md#create-a-token`, `../admin/endpoints.md`) becomes `help/<section>/<page>` with
  `#user-content-<slug>` for a heading, a link inside the page `#user-content-<slug>`; every other relative link is removed
  as in a README.
- The contents are fixed in `internal/manual`; a page that is missing, a file outside the contents, a page without a title
  or summary and a link to a page or a heading that does not exist stop the load, so start-up fails rather than serve a
  broken manual. The test of the package loads the embedded files, so such a manual never passes CI.
- Both answers carry the same strong ETag, a hash over every rendered page and the renderer version; a matching
  `If-None-Match` answers `304`. An unknown section or page answers `404`. The text is English (Q-UI-86 applies).

Acceptance criteria:

- The embedded manual loads; `docs/manual/README.md` lists the same sections and pages in the same order with the same
  titles (`TestR_API_054_EmbeddedManualLoads`, `TestR_API_054_ReadmeListsTheContents`).
- A link to another page with a heading becomes `help/<section>/<page>#user-content-<slug>`; a link to a missing page or
  heading, a link into the repository and a page outside the contents stop the load
  (`TestR_API_054_LinksBecomeHelpRoutes`, `TestR_API_054_DefectsAreRefused`, `TestR_API_054_LinkedRenderingResolvesRelativeLinks`).
- The contents list `user` before `admin`; a page carries its headings and neighbours; both answer `304` for the ETag and
  an unknown page `404`; an anonymous caller gets `200` while `publicContent` is true and `401` otherwise
  (`TestR_API_054_TheManualOperations`, `TestR_API_054_AnonymousReadersFollowPublicContent`).

### R-API-055 · User avatars
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-07, in two parts. A user who has not uploaded an avatar gets a generated robot avatar in
the UI (R-UI-051); the UI bundles the generator and loads nothing from outside Quader's origin. A user can upload an avatar,
and the owner fixed its shape: only PNG, JPEG and WebP and never SVG; the server decodes the image and stores a new one; at
most 1 MiB is accepted; the image is stored as a blob; the `api` role serves it from Quader's origin. Everything below that
the owner did not say is the development agent's decision, recorded as Q-API-207 to Q-API-210, Q-AUTH-195 to Q-AUTH-197 and
Q-STOR-166, Q-STOR-167.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| PUT | `/api/v1/users/me/avatar` | Set the caller's avatar; the body is the image, `Content-Type` is `image/png`, `image/jpeg` or `image/webp`; answers the user record | authenticated; a user or the break-glass account |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/avatar` | Remove the caller's avatar; `204` also when there is none | as above |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{username}/avatar` | Remove another user's avatar (moderation); `204` also when there is none | `identities:write` (`admin`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/avatars/{digest}` | The image, named by the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 of its bytes | authenticated |

- **The user record names the image.** `User.avatarUrl` (R-AUTH-016) is `/api/v1/avatars/<sha256>` or `null` for a user
  without an avatar; the UI shows the generated avatar for `null`. It is on `GET /api/v1/users/me`, `GET /api/v1/users/{username}`
  and every item of `GET /api/v1/users`. Nothing else is needed to find another user's avatar: the digest is in the record.
- **The input is untrusted and is never stored or served.** The server decides the format from the bytes, not from the
  declared type (Q-API-208). In this order: the declared media type must be one of the three, else `415`; the body is read
  through a reader that stops at 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes), a longer body is `413 payload_too_large` and is not held; the first
  512 bytes must sniff as PNG, JPEG or WebP, else `415`, and as the declared one, else `415` (an SVG, an HTML page, a GIF or
  a polyglot never gets this far); an animated PNG or WebP is `422`; the size in the header is read before any pixel is
  allocated and must be at least 32 x 32 and at most 4,194,304 pixels in all, else `422` (a header that declares 100,000 x
  100,000 pixels in a few bytes costs nothing); a JPEG with more than 64 scans, or whose scans add up to more than 3,145,728 block visits (Q-UI-174), is `422` `too_complex`, and one whose estimated
  decode memory (Q-API-211) is above 48 MiB is `422` `invalid_dimensions`; the image is decoded with the Go decoders
  (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `golang.org/x/image/webp`, decoder only) under a deadline of 5 s, which on expiry is `422`
  `too_complex`, and one that does not decode, a truncated one included, is `422`.
- **The result is a new image.** The centre square of the decoded pixels is scaled to 256 x 256 (Catmull-Rom) and encoded as a
  PNG from the pixels alone: no metadata (EXIF, GPS position, ICC profile, text chunks), nothing appended, one frame. The
  EXIF orientation of a JPEG is applied first, because the result has no EXIF to apply it later. Transparency is kept. The
  same image always gives the same bytes, so it gives the same digest.
- **Bounded cost.** A replica decodes two images at a time (`avatar.MaxConcurrent`); a request that finds no free slot within
  2 s is `503 server_busy` with `Retry-After: 1`. The memory of one decode is estimated from the header and bounded to 48 MiB,
  so the decoding of a replica holds at most 96 MiB, which the admission guard does not charge (H-563). The decode stops at its
  next read after 5 s or when the client leaves; the reads of its input are 16 bytes at most, so a file of few bytes and many scans is
  stopped too (Q-UI-174). The slowest image the checks accept costs about 0.5 s of CPU for the whole of `Process` (Q-UI-173). The management API's rate limits (R-API-016) apply as to any write.
- **The image answer.** `Content-Type: image/png`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src
  'none'; sandbox`, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="avatar.png"`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`,
  `ETag: "<sha256>"` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`: the answer is for a signed-in caller and the
  URL never changes its content (Q-API-209). These replace the headers R-API-017 gives a JSON answer. A digest that is no
  user's avatar, a replaced or removed one included, is `404`; the route reads no other blob of the store. The page's CSP
  (`img-src 'self' data:`, R-UI-001) admits the URL, which is on Quader's origin.
- **Storage.** The PNG is a blob of the object store, committed by the protocol of R-STOR-005 and deduplicated; the table
  `user_avatars` names it for the user, with `ON DELETE CASCADE` from the user (Q-STOR-166, Q-STOR-167). A replaced or removed
  avatar's blob is queued for collection by the reference triggers (R-STOR-024); deleting a user does the same. The
  table is exported by a backup (R-BAK-004, `data`).
- **Audit.** `user.avatar.set` (`details.source` `self`, `sha256`, `size`) and `user.avatar.removed` (`source` `self` or
  `admin`, `sha256`), transactional with the change (Q-AUTH-197). An upload of the image the user already has records nothing.
- **Who.** A user changes only their own avatar. A service account and a CI token have no avatar and answer `403` on the two
  `me` routes, and so does a token whose scope is narrower than its owner's rights (`x-quader-owner-rights`, R-API-021, Q-API-213, Q-API-214); a session
  and a token that inherits the owner's rights may. An administrator removes, never sets, another user's avatar (Q-AUTH-196). Any authenticated caller reads an
  image (Q-AUTH-195).
- **Writes from the browser** are session writes: `X-CSRF-Token` is required (R-API-006), `If-Match` is not (the image is
  replaced as a whole and addressed by its digest, R-API-012).

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | The body is empty |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The caller is a service account or a CI token, or a token limited to part of its owner's rights; or lacks `identities:write` for another user's avatar |
| 403 | `csrf_failed` | A session write without the CSRF header |
| 404 | `not_found` | `GET`: no avatar has this digest; `DELETE` of another user: no such user |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The body is longer than 1 MiB |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` | The declared type is not PNG, JPEG or WebP; the content is not; the content is another of the three than declared |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | `errors[0].code` `animated_image`, `invalid_dimensions` (under 32 x 32, over 4,194,304 pixels, or above the decode memory bound), `too_complex` (more than 64 JPEG scans, or a decode over 5 s) or `undecodable_image` (damaged or truncated) |
| 503 | `server_busy` | No decoding slot became free within 2 s; `Retry-After: 1` |
| 503 | `unavailable`, `object_store_unavailable` | The store or the object store cannot take the request |

Acceptance criteria:

- A PNG, a JPEG and a WebP (lossy, lossless and with alpha) each come out as a PNG of 256 x 256 pixels, the corner of the
  source in the corner of the result; a 96 x 64 image is cropped to its centre square; the same input gives the same bytes
  (`TestR_API_055_ReEncodesToTheFixedSquare`).
- A JPEG with an EXIF block holding a position and a comment, and a PNG with a text chunk and an HTML page after `IEND`, come
  out with no such byte, with the chunks `IHDR`, `IDAT` and `IEND` only and nothing after `IEND`
  (`TestR_API_055_ResultCarriesNoMetadataAndNoAppendedData`); the orientation of a photo is applied
  (`TestR_API_055_AppliesTheExifOrientationOfAPhoto`, `FuzzR_API_055_ExifOrientation`).
- An SVG, an HTML page, a GIF and a GIF-and-script polyglot are refused whatever type they declare, and an image of another
  accepted format than declared is refused (`TestR_API_055_RefusesWhatIsNotAPNGJPEGOrWebP`).
- A body of 1 MiB + 1 byte is refused and one of 1 MiB is not (`TestR_API_055_RefusesABodyAboveTheLimit`); an image whose
  header declares 100,000 x 100,000 pixels, or a canvas of 16,000 x 16,000, is refused by its size and not by a failed decode
  (`TestR_API_055_RefusesTheDimensionsBeforeDecoding`); a truncated image (`TestR_API_055_RefusesAnImageThatDoesNotDecode`) and
  an animated PNG or WebP (`TestR_API_055_RefusesAnimatedImages`) are refused; a replica with no free slot answers busy
  (`TestR_API_055_BoundsTheImagesDecodedAtOnce`).
- On a running `api` replica: an upload, the read with the headers above by the owner, another user and an administrator, the
  `304` for the ETag, the replacement (the old URL is `404` and its blob queued), the removal by the owner and by an
  administrator, the refusal for another user and for a service account, the cascade when the user is deleted, the refusals
  of every error row, and the CSRF header for a session
  (`TestR_API_055_AvatarLifecycle`, `TestR_API_055_AvatarRefusals`,
  `TestR_API_055_AvatarWritesNeedTheCSRFHeaderOfASession`).

### R-API-056 · The installation's visibility settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033 (the installation's default level, Q-AUTHZ-264) and R-AUTHZ-037 (the
restricted levels, R-API-075):

| Method | Path | operationId | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/settings/visibility` | `getVisibilitySettings` | The default level, the restricted levels, whether `public` is available, and the objects that are `public` | `settings:read` |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/settings/visibility` | `updateVisibilitySettings` | Change the default level and the restricted levels (JSON Merge Patch, R-API-013; `If-Match`, R-API-012) | `security-settings:write`; recent authentication |

```json
{
  "defaultLevel": "private",
  "restrictedLevels": [],
  "publicAvailable": true,
  "publicObjects": {"projects": ["web"], "repositories": ["web/npm-public"], "truncated": false}
}
```

*(example answer; `defaultLevel` `private` and `restrictedLevels` `[]` are the defaults)*

- `defaultLevel` (`private`, `internal`, `public`) is the level a project takes when it is created and the upper bound of the
  levels a repository takes when it is created (R-AUTHZ-033). A `PATCH` is `{"defaultLevel": "internal"}`; the other two
  members are read-only and ignored in a `PATCH` body, so a `GET` body can be sent back (Q-AUTH-45).
- `publicAvailable` is the default endpoint's `auth.anonymous` ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010). While it is `false`,
  a `defaultLevel` of `public` answers 409 `public_not_allowed`.
- `publicObjects` lists the projects and the repositories whose artifacts are `public`, at most 100 of each in key order,
  `truncated` when there are more; the UI shows it as the summary of what anyone can read (R-UI-032, R-UI-053). The built-in project
  `upstream` is not listed: its stored `public` admits nobody ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-041); its `public`
  repositories are.
- `restrictedLevels` is R-API-075.
- A change writes `settings.visibility.changed` with `defaultLevel` and `restrictedLevels` before and after
  ([Q-API-332](#q-api-332--one-audit-event-carries-both-settings-before-and-after)); it is not journaled, because it decides only later writes
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-036). The values are read in the transaction that creates or changes a project or
  a repository and are cached nowhere. The `ETag` moves with both.

Schemas in `api/openapi.yaml`: `VisibilityLevel` (enum `private`, `internal`, `public`), `VisibilitySettings`,
`VisibilitySettingsPatch`, `PublicObjects`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `PATCH /api/v1/settings/visibility` with `{"defaultLevel": "internal"}` and the `ETag` of the `GET` answers 200; a project
  created afterwards reads back `"visibility": "internal"`, and the projects that existed keep their levels.
- With `endpoints.default.auth.anonymous: false`, `GET` answers `"publicAvailable": false` and a `PATCH` to `public` answers
  409 `public_not_allowed`.
- A caller with `settings:read` and without `security-settings:write` (the `auditor`) reads the settings and gets 403 on the
  `PATCH`.

### R-API-057 · The visibility of projects and repositories in the API
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033 and R-AUTHZ-035:

| Method | Path | operationId | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/visibility` | `setProjectVisibility` | Set the project's level: `{"level": "internal"}`; `If-Match` with the project's `ETag` | `projects:write`; recent authentication |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects` | `createProject` | `visibility` in the body, default the installation's `defaultLevel` | `projects:write`; recent authentication for a level above `private` |
| PATCH, PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` | `updateRepository`, `replaceRepository` | the member `visibility` of the document ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004) | as for the document; the project's Owner or `repositories:write-config`; recent authentication when a level rises |

- **The project's answer.** `setProjectVisibility` answers 200 with the project and a member `lowered`: the qualified names of
  the repositories whose levels the change lowered, with their levels before (`[{"repository": "web/npm-public", "before":
  {"artifacts": "public", "wiki": "internal"}}]`), empty when it lowered none. The answer carries `Quader-Authz-Epoch`
  (R-AUTHZ-032). 409 `public_not_allowed` while the default endpoint admits no request without a credential; 403
  `visibility_level_restricted` for a restricted level and a caller without `security-settings:write` ([authorization.md](authorization.md)
  R-AUTHZ-037); 412 for a stale `If-Match`; 403 for an Owner without `projects:write`.
- **The repository's member.** `visibility` is `{"artifacts": "<level>", "wiki": "<level>"}` in every view of the document,
  the reduced consumer view of R-REPO-010 included, so every reader sees how open a repository is. A merge patch may name one
  part. The answers are 422 `validation_failed` with `visibility_above_project` or `visibility_wiki_above_artifacts` at
  `/visibility/artifacts` or `/visibility/wiki`, 409 `public_not_allowed`, and 403 `visibility_level_restricted` with the part
  in `errors[]` for a restricted level the caller may not choose (R-AUTHZ-037; the order of
  [R-AUTHZ-038](authorization.md#r-authz-038--the-order-in-which-a-level-is-refused)); a write that opens a remote repository with
  `cacheFillAction: read` to the public carries the warning `public_populates_remote`
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-008).
- **Lists.** `GET /api/v1/repositories` and the project's list accept `visibility=` (one or more levels, comma-separated),
  matched against the artifacts level, and carry `visibility` in the summary view; `GET /api/v1/projects` carries each
  project's `visibility` and accepts `membership=true` (R-API-047).
- Schemas: `VisibilityLevel`, `RepositoryVisibility` (`artifacts`, `wiki`), `ProjectVisibilityRequest`,
  `ProjectVisibilityResult` (the project and `lowered`), the member `visibility` of `Project` and `Repository`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `PUT /api/v1/projects/web/visibility` with `{"level": "private"}` while `web/npm-public` is `public` answers 200 with
  `lowered` naming `web/npm-public`; `GET /api/v1/projects/web/repositories/npm-public` then shows `{"artifacts": "private",
  "wiki": "private"}`.
- `GET /api/v1/repositories?visibility=public` lists exactly the repositories whose artifacts are `public` among those the
  caller may read.
- A merge patch `{"visibility": {"wiki": "internal"}}` on a repository whose artifacts are `public` answers 200 and leaves the
  artifacts `public`.

### R-API-075 · The restricted levels in the visibility settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) [R-AUTHZ-037](authorization.md#r-authz-037--restricted-visibility-levels). The member `restrictedLevels` of
`GET` and `PATCH /api/v1/settings/visibility` (R-API-056):

```json
{"restrictedLevels": ["public"]}
```

*(example patch: only an administrator may make a project or a repository public)*

- **Read.** An array of levels in the order `private`, `internal`, `public`, each once; `[]` when nothing is restricted. It never holds
  `defaultLevel`.
- **Write** ([Q-API-331](#q-api-331--restrictedlevels-is-a-set-that-a-merge-patch-replaces-whole)). A merge patch that names `restrictedLevels` replaces the whole
  set, as RFC 7396 replaces an array; a level named twice counts once. A value that is no level answers 422 `validation_failed`
  with `invalid_value` at `/restrictedLevels/<index>`. A result whose set holds the default answers 422 `validation_failed` with
  `default_level_restricted`, at `/restrictedLevels` when the patch names the set and at `/defaultLevel` otherwise
  ([Q-AUTHZ-284](authorization.md#q-authz-284--the-default-level-is-never-restricted-and-a-restricted-level-never-becomes-the-default)). A patch may change both members at once; the result is checked.
- **Audit.** `settings.visibility.changed` with `{"before": {"defaultLevel": …, "restrictedLevels": […]}, "after": {…}}`
  ([Q-API-332](#q-api-332--one-audit-event-carries-both-settings-before-and-after)); a patch that changes nothing records nothing.
- **What it changes.** Later choices of a level by callers without `security-settings:write`; no stored level of a project or a
  repository (R-AUTHZ-037 rule 4).

Acceptance criteria (`TestR_AUTHZ_037_RestrictedLevels`, `TestR_API_075_APatchOfTheRestrictedLevels`,
`TestR_API_075_TheChangeIsAuditedWithBothSettings`):

- `PATCH` with `{"restrictedLevels": ["public", "public"]}` answers 200 with `"restrictedLevels": ["public"]` and records one
  `settings.visibility.changed` whose `before.restrictedLevels` is `[]` and `after.restrictedLevels` `["public"]`.
- With the default `private`, `{"restrictedLevels": ["private"]}` answers 422 `default_level_restricted`; with `public` restricted,
  `{"defaultLevel": "public"}` does too.

### R-API-076 · The levels a caller may choose
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The forms that choose the level of a project or a repository show a level the caller cannot choose disabled with its reason
(R-UI-141). They read it from an operation every signed-in caller may call, not from the administrator's settings
([Q-API-330](#q-api-330--the-forms-read-the-levels-a-caller-may-choose-from-an-operation-every-signed-in-caller-may-call)):

| Method | Path | operationId | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/visibility-choices` | `getVisibilityChoices` | The default level, the restricted levels, whether the caller may choose them, whether `public` is available | any signed-in caller (`authenticated`) |

```json
{"defaultLevel": "private", "restrictedLevels": ["public"], "mayChooseRestricted": false, "publicAvailable": true}
```

*(example answer of a project's Owner)*

- `mayChooseRestricted` is `true` for a caller who holds `security-settings:write` for the request, its token's scope included
  ([Q-AUTHZ-283](authorization.md#q-authz-283--an-administrator-is-whoever-holds-security-settingswrite-for-the-request)). The read writes no audit event.
- It is read from PostgreSQL on every call and has no `ETag`: a form reads it once when it opens.
- What it answers is the server's rule beforehand, never the rule itself: a write is decided on its own (R-AUTHZ-038), so a form
  that read it before a change of the settings is answered with the refusal of the write.
- An anonymous caller gets 401; nothing an anonymous visitor sees chooses a level.

Schema: `VisibilityChoices`.

Acceptance criteria (`TestR_AUTHZ_037_RestrictedLevels`, "R-API-076 every signed-in caller reads its choices"): with `public`
restricted, the project's Owner reads `"mayChooseRestricted": false` and the administrator `true`; without a credential the read
answers 401.

### R-API-077 · The principal lookup of a project answers what a member's row shows
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's W-12 (2026-11-18): a person is chosen from a search that shows the people it found, each with the avatar, the name and
the username (R-UI-150). Inside a project the search is the lookup of
[Q-AUTHZ-182](authorization.md#q-authz-182--how-a-project-administrator-finds-the-users-and-groups-it-names),
`GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/principals?q=&kind=&limit=`, which its Owner and a holder of `identities:read` call; it keeps its
callers, its minimum of 2 characters, its limit of 20 and the rate limit of its class
([Q-API-336](#q-api-336--the-project-lookup-answers-the-rows-display-name-and-avatar-finds-the-projects-service-accounts-and-matches-words)):

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q` | Required. 2 to 128 characters after trimming; compared lower-cased as the start of the name or of one of its words, never as a pattern (`422 prefix_too_short`, `prefix_too_long`) |
| `kind` | `user`, `group`, `service_account`; repeated or comma-separated; every kind when absent (`422 invalid_kind` for another) |
| `limit` | 1 to 20, default 20 (`422 invalid_limit`) |

```json
{"items": [
  {"kind": "user", "principal": "user:swantje", "name": "swantje", "displayName": "Swantje Wagner", "id": "0192f0c4-7a7e-7b51-9b1e-2f0d6c9e1a10", "avatarUrl": null},
  {"kind": "group", "principal": "group:swat-team", "name": "swat-team"},
  {"kind": "service_account", "principal": "sa:web/swagger-sync", "name": "web/swagger-sync", "project": "web"}
]}
```

- **Matches.** A user matches when its username starts with `q`, or a word of its display name (split at white space) or of its
  username (split at every character that is no letter or digit) does; a group by its name or a word of it; a service account by
  its stored name, its name within the project, or a word of it. Ranked together: the name equal to `q`, then a name that starts with
  it, then a word that does; within a rank users, groups, service accounts; then by name.
- **What is never offered.** A disabled principal, the break-glass account (an emergency sign-in, not a person to grant to), and an
  auto-join group, which a project neither takes as a member nor names in a policy (R-AUTHZ-026, Q-AUTHZ-200).
- **Service accounts** are the project's own, which its Owner lists anyway (`GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts`),
  and for a holder of `identities:read` also the instance-wide ones, which that capability lists anyway. Another project's accounts
  are never offered: a project policy cannot name them (`422 principal_outside_project`).
- **What an item holds.** The kind, the reference to write, the name; a user's display name, its ID (the seed of the generated
  avatar, R-UI-002) and the path of its uploaded avatar (R-API-055); a service account's project. Never the e-mail address, a status,
  an origin, a sign-in time or a membership.

Schema: `ProjectPrincipal`, `ProjectPrincipalList`.

Acceptance criteria (`TestR_AUTHZ_026_PrincipalLookupBounds` in `test/integration/projects`, `TestR_API_077_*` in
`internal/api/v1` and `internal/project`): `q=swa&kind=user` finds the user whose display name is "Swantje Albers" by its word and
answers its display name and ID without an e-mail address; `q=al` answers at most 20 and never a disabled user or an auto-join
group; `kind=service_account` answers the Owner the project's account only and the administrator also the instance-wide one;
`q=ops&kind=group` finds `al-ops` and `zed-ops` by a word; `q=ps` finds nothing; `kind=ci_mapping` answers 422.

### R-API-078 · The admin area's principal search: service accounts and avatars in the suggestions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Outside a project the fields that name a principal sit in the admin area, whose screens need `identities:read` or a capability every
role that holds it pairs with `identities:read` (R-AUTHZ-010). They search through the suggestions of R-API-060, which answer the kinds
`user` and `group` to that capability already, extended by
[Q-API-335](#q-api-335--the-admin-areas-fields-search-through-the-suggestions-which-gain-service-accounts-and-the-avatar):

- A new kind `service_account`, under the same rule as `user` and `group` (`identities:read`, else `403` before any lookup): the
  active accounts of which every term is part of the stored name, ranked 0 equal, 1 starts with, 3 any other, then by name. An item is
  `{"name", "description", "project"}`; `name` is the stored name (`<project>/<name>` for a project's account, the reference
  `sa:<name>`), `project` `null` for an instance-wide one.
- A user suggestion carries `avatarUrl` beside `id`, `username`, `displayName` and `disabled`.
- The members of a group (`GET /api/v1/groups/{name}/members`, `identities:read`) carry each member's `id`, and a user's
  `displayName` and `avatarUrl`, so a member's row shows what the field's row shows (R-UI-151). The answer of a write does not.

Acceptance criteria (`TestR_API_060_TheAnswerHoldsAMemberPerKindAsked`, `TestR_API_061_TheAdminKindsAreRefusedBeforeAnyLookup`,
`TestR_API_061_ASuggestionNamesOnlyWhatTheCallerMayRead` in `test/integration/search`): `kind=user,group,service_account` answers the
members `users`, `groups` and `serviceAccounts`; `kind=service_account` without `identities:read` answers 403 the same for every `q`;
the administrator's `q=bot&kind=service_account` names the instance-wide `bot` with `project: null`.

Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Owned by [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073 (semantics, bodies, the item, errors) and
[authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-041 (who), under the OpenAPI tag `upstream`
([Q-API-360](#q-api-360--the-well-known-repositories-have-operations-of-their-own-beside-the-repository-document)):

| PUT | `/api/v1/upstream-repositories/{key}/state` | `setUpstreamRepositoryState` | `repositories:write-config` |

| PUT, DELETE | `/api/v1/upstream-repositories/{key}/address` | `setUpstreamRepositoryAddress`, `resetUpstreamRepositoryAddress` | `repositories:write-config`; `x-quader-recent-auth: true`; `If-Match` |
| PUT, DELETE | `/api/v1/upstream-repositories/{key}/account` | `setUpstreamRepositoryAccount`, `removeUpstreamRepositoryAccount` | `repositories:write-config`; `x-quader-recent-auth: true`; `If-Match` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/upstream-repositories/{key}/clients` | `setUpstreamRepositoryClients` | `repositories:write-config`; recent authentication inside the write when it switches on ([Q-API-382](#q-api-382--the-clients-of-the-clamav-definitions-are-an-operation-and-a-member-of-the-item)) |
| GET | `/api/v1/formats/{format}/upstream-repositories` | `listFormatUpstreamRepositories` | `repositories:write-config` or an Owner of any project (`projectRole: owner` without `project`, [Q-API-364](#q-api-364--a-writer-of-a-virtual-repository-reads-the-state-and-the-level-of-a-formats-well-known-repositories-through-an-operation-of-its-own)) |

- `switch-on-all` and `set-visibility` are reserved names of the collection (R-API-004) and listed in the `key` schema's

  [Q-API-363](#q-api-363--the-item-counts-the-listing-virtual-repositories-and-their-projects-and-an-answer-about-one-repository-names-them)),

  the warning `member_inactive` of [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-071.
