  ([Q-API-361](#q-api-361--a-bulk-operation-of-the-well-known-repositories-is-one-transaction-and-answers-what-it-changed)).

Acceptance criteria:

- `api/openapi.yaml` holds the operations with their declarations; the declaration test of R-API-008 and the reserved-names check of
  R-API-004 pass.
- The `auditor` lists the well-known repositories (200) and gets 403 on `setUpstreamRepositoryState`; a `repository-admin` switches
  one on (200).
- `listFormatUpstreamRepositories` answers an anonymous caller 401, a reader of a project 403 and the Owner of a project who holds no
  capability of the instance the preset repositories of the format with `state` and `visibility` and without address and account.

### R-API-084 · The operations of the installation's registry presets
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Owned by [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-076 (what a preset is, the validation, who), under the
OpenAPI tag `upstream`
([Q-API-383](#q-api-383--the-registry-presets-are-one-document-read-and-replaced-whole-under-if-match)):

| Method | Path | operationId | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/settings/registry-presets` | `getRegistryPresets` | `repositories:read-config` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/settings/registry-presets` | `setRegistryPresets` | `repositories:write-config`; `If-Match` |

- Schemas: `RegistryPresets` (`presets`), `RegistryPreset` (`format`, `displayName`, `url`, `extraHosts` of `RemoteExtraHost`), both with
  `additionalProperties: false`, so a body with a credential member is `400 malformed_request`; `RepositoryDefaults` gains
  `registryPresets`, an array of `RegistryPresetChoice` (`displayName`, `url`, `extraHosts`).
- No recent authentication: a preset carries no credential and grants nothing a holder of `repositories:write-config` cannot do to
  a repository directly.
- The audit event `settings.registry_presets.changed` (category `config`, transactional, not journaled), with `before` and `after`,
  each the list of presets.

Acceptance criteria:

- `api/openapi.yaml` holds both operations with their declarations; the declaration test of R-API-008 and the `If-Match` test of
  R-API-012 pass.
- The `auditor` reads the list (200) and gets 403 on `setRegistryPresets`; a `repository-admin` replaces it (200).

### R-API-085 · A deprecated version or package is marked alike in every format that has it
Priority: **P1** · Covers: PKG-NPM-020

The owner's rules (2026-11-19 and 2026-11-25): what is decided at one format holds for every format that has the same thing, and metadata
that is there is used and shown. npm, NuGet and Ansible Galaxy each have a deprecation; only npm's reached a screen, and only its version's
page (W-30, G4). One state, one look, one operation
([Q-API-440](#q-api-440--deprecation-is-a-member-of-the-views-summary-and-the-format-decides-the-write),
[ADR-286](../decisions.md#adr-286--deprecation-is-one-state-of-the-format-contract-set-through-one-management-operation-and-decided-by-the-format)):

| Format | What is deprecated | Read from | Set by | Served to clients as | What the clients do with it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| npm | one version, with a message (at most 1,024 characters) | `npm_versions.deprecated`: a local publisher's, a remote's upstream's from the stored package document (R-NPM-050) | the operation below; `npm deprecate` itself is not built ([H-2160](formats/npm.md#h-2160--npm-deprecate-is-not-built-the-management-operation-sets-an-npm-deprecation)) | `versions[v].deprecated` of the package document | `npm install` prints `npm warn deprecated <name>@<version>: <message>`; a range picks a version that is not deprecated where one satisfies it; `npm view` shows `DEPRECATED` |
| NuGet | one version, with reasons (`Legacy`, `CriticalBugs`, `Other`), an optional message and an optional alternate package | the member `deprecation` of `nuget_version.metadata`: a local version's set below, a remote's cached version's from its upstream's registration ([R-NUGET-036](formats/nuget.md#r-nuget-036--a-version-is-deprecated-with-reasons-a-message-and-an-alternate-package)) | the operation below | `deprecation` of the registration's catalog entry and of a search result | `dotnet list package --deprecated` lists it with its reasons and alternative; Visual Studio marks it and links the alternate; a restore warns of nothing; the message is shown by no client |
| Ansible Galaxy | the whole collection, every version of it | `ansible_collection_deprecations`: a local collection's set below, a remote's from its upstream's collection document ([R-ANS-060](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-060--a-collection-is-deprecated-as-a-whole)) | the operation below | `deprecated: true` of the collection document | no release of `ansible-galaxy` reads it: a deprecated collection installs as any other, without a warning |
| OCI | an image: none in the format. A Helm chart: that version, without a message, when its `Chart.yaml` says `deprecated: true` | the chart's facts of `oci_manifests.config_facts` (formats/oci.md R-OCI-042), a stored tag's and a remote's cached tag's ([Q-API-444](#q-api-444--a-helm-charts-deprecation-is-one-bit-of-its-configuration-every-reader-of-the-version-sees)) | pushing the chart; the operation below refuses it | `deprecated: true` of the `Chart.yaml` in the chart's config blob | `helm install` and `helm upgrade` print `WARNING: This chart is deprecated`; `helm lint`, `helm search` and `helm pull` say nothing |
| Debian | none: a transitional package says it in its description, a convention | — | — | — | — |
| generic files, ClamAV definitions | none | — | — | — | — |

NuGet's **unlisted** is not a deprecation: an unlisted version is hidden from search and still restored by its exact number, a deprecated
one is found, restored and marked ([Q-NUGET-142](formats/nuget.md#q-nuget-142--unlisted-and-deprecated-are-two-states-with-two-marks)). Both
are shown, each with its own word.

**The API.**
- `deprecation` (`PackageDeprecation`: `scope` `version` or `package`, `message`, `reasons`, `alternatePackage` with `name`, `range` and,
  on a version's details, `packageId` where the caller may read a version of it) is a member of a version's details, of every entry of the
  version list and of a package of the list, which carries its latest version's
  ([Q-API-441](#q-api-441--a-package-is-shown-deprecated-when-its-latest-version-is-and-the-filter-asks-the-same)); `unlisted: true` of a
  version that is unlisted. Both are read with the summary of the format's view (`ViewData`), so a list pays no read of the details.
  npm's message is no longer the metadata member `deprecated`.
- A suggestion of the search field carries `deprecated: true` when the package's latest version in the repository it is placed in is
  deprecated, for a repository the caller reads whole ([Q-API-443](#q-api-443--a-suggestion-is-marked-for-a-repository-the-caller-reads-whole)).
- `GET /api/v1/packages?deprecated=true` keeps the packages whose latest visible version is deprecated, in every format that has it.
- `PUT /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/packages/{packageName}/deprecation` sets a deprecation, or changes it, and
  answers the one the subject holds now; `DELETE` of the same path (`?version=` for a format that deprecates versions) clears it
  ([Q-API-442](#q-api-442--one-operation-on-a-repositorys-package-the-format-decides-the-subject)). The format decides as its own
  protocol write does: deploy on the package, and npm's and NuGet's ownership of the name; the lock of the package; a version or a
  collection the caller may not read answered as missing (404); what its protocol cannot carry refused with `422 validation_failed`
  and the reason (a version for Ansible Galaxy, reasons for npm, no reason for NuGet, an alternate package's range that is no NuGet range);
  the rows, the package's revision and the audit event in one transaction: `npm.deprecate` for npm, `package.metadata_changed` with the
  change `deprecate` or `undeprecate` for NuGet and Ansible Galaxy. A remote repository shows its upstream's state and a virtual one its
  members': both answer `409 not_applicable`, as a format without deprecation does. A repeat changes nothing and records nothing.

**The screens** ([Q-UI-1300](#q-ui-1300--one-mark-deprecated-is-a-warning-badge-unlisted-a-plain-one)):
- The version's page says it in a banner above its tabs: **Deprecated.**, for a collection "Every version of this collection is
  deprecated.", the message as text (never markup; an address in it stays text), NuGet's reasons in words and **Use instead** with the
  alternate package, a link where the reader may read it and its range unless it is `*`. An unlisted version keeps its banner.
- The mark **Deprecated** (a warning badge, the message as its title) and **Unlisted** stand beside the version in the table of
  versions, in the switch of the version's head, in the opened row of a repository's content, beside the package in a repository's
  package list, the product's list **Packages**, the search's hits and suggestions, and on the tab **Upstream** of a remote, where the
  catalogue's hit and an opened package's version rows carry the upstream's flags.
- The act ([Q-UI-1301](#q-ui-1301--deprecating-is-an-act-in-the-menu-of-the-versions-head-with-a-small-dialog)): a menu at the end of
  the version's head, for a reader who may deploy the package in a local repository that holds the version: **Deprecate version**
  (npm, NuGet) or **Deprecate collection** (Ansible Galaxy), which opens a small dialog of what the format carries; on a deprecated
  version **Change deprecation** and **Undo deprecation**. The page, its switch and its package's row show the new state at once (R-UI-213).
- The filter **State: Deprecated only** in the drawer of the list **Packages** ([Q-UI-1302](#q-ui-1302--the-filter-deprecated-stands-in-the-drawer-of-the-list-packages)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/packages/view`, `TestR_API_085_TheVersionListMarksDeprecatedAndUnlistedVersionsInOneSummaryRead`, milliseconds): a page
  of the version list carries each version's deprecation and unlisted mark from one summary read.
- Unit (`npm`, `nuget`, `ansible`, milliseconds): what each format carries and refuses (`TestR_NPM_018_ADeprecationCarriesAMessageOnly`,
  `TestR_NUGET_036_…`, `TestR_ANS_060_…`).
- Integration (`npm`, `TestR_API_085_AnNPMVersionIsDeprecatedThroughTheManagementAPIAndServed`; `nuget`,
  `TestR_NUGET_036_ALocalVersionIsDeprecatedThroughTheManagementAPIAndServed`; `ansiblelocal`,
  `TestR_ANS_060_ACollectionIsDeprecatedThroughTheManagementAPIAndServed`; about a second each): the write, the refusals, the served
  document, the version list, the filter, the suggestion, the clear.
- Web unit (`deprecation-mark.spec.ts`, `deprecation-dialog.spec.ts`, `package-version.spec.ts`, `package-list.spec.ts`): the marks, the
  dialog per format, the banner, the act and its refusal, the filter.
- The renders `deprecation-*` and `ui-states` of the dialog and its refusal (light and dark, 390, 1,024 and 1,440 px, English and German).

### R-API-086 · A version's page lists the packages that depend on its package
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's rules (2026-11-25): metadata that is there is used and shown, and what holds for one format holds for every format that has
the same thing. Galaxy ("Used by" and the search filter `dependency`), nuget.org ("Used By") and npmjs.com ("Dependents") show who depends on
a package; Quader stores every version's dependencies and showed them one way only (W-30, G5).

**What is kept** ([Q-API-455](#q-api-455--who-depends-on-what-is-one-side-table-written-where-a-versions-facts-are-written)): one row of
`package_dependencies` (migration 00139) per name a stored version depends on, with the range it asks for as written and the kind its format
names it by, and per name a Debian version provides. Each format has one extractor (`Dependencies` of `internal/formatdata/<format>`), which
reads the format's own stored row where that row is written, in the same transaction:

| Format | Kinds | A name is matched | Written for a local version | Written for a remote's cached version |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| npm | `dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `devDependencies` (`bundleDependencies` names what `dependencies` holds) | as written (the name rule, case kept); an alias `npm:<name>@<range>` depends on `<name>` | the publish's commit (`npm_versions`) | the job `npm-remote-describe` (R-NPM-050) |
| NuGet | one list (kind `""`), every target framework's group; a range per distinct range | the ID in lower case (`packages.name`) | the push's commit (`nuget_version.metadata`) | the fill's commit (origin `cache`) |
| Debian | `Pre-Depends`, `Depends`, `Recommends`, `Suggests`, `Enhances`; `Provides` kept as provided names | as written, the architecture qualifier dropped (`python3:any` is `python3`); every alternative of `a \| b` | the upload's commit, from every file of the version (`deb_binaries`) | the job `deb-remote-describe` (R-DEB-037) |
| Ansible Galaxy | one list (kind `""`) | `<namespace>.<name>` in lower case | the publish's commit and the reindex (`ansible_collection_versions`) | the fill's commit |
| OCI | none: an image's base image is no dependency the format states; a Helm chart's dependencies name a chart and a repository address, which no stored package matches by its name alone ([H-2221](#h-2221--a-helm-charts-dependencies-are-not-matched-to-the-charts-quader-holds)) | — | — | — |
| generic files, ClamAV definitions | none | — | — | — |

What was stored before, what a restore left without rows (the table is derived and not exported, R-BAK-004) and what an older extractor read
are read by an entry of the task `remote-describe` from the same stored rows, without reading an archive: a worker that starts queues it
while a version is left, a batch of 100 versions per transaction, the cursor saved after each. Until it has run, a version stored before
has no dependents and is in no list filtered by `dependsOn`; its own Dependencies block is unchanged (it reads the version's metadata).

**The read** ([Q-API-456](#q-api-456--used-by-lists-each-dependent-once-by-its-newest-version-that-depends-across-the-projects-the-reader-may-read),
[Q-API-458](#q-api-458--a-dependent-the-reader-may-not-read-is-not-read)):
- `GET /api/v1/packages/{packageId}/dependents` answers the packages of the format that depend on the package's name, or on a name its
  visible versions provide (Debian, [Q-API-457](#q-api-457--a-debian-package-is-used-under-the-names-it-provides-and-every-alternative-counts)),
  in the repositories the caller may read: each once, by its newest visible version that depends (a release before a pre-release), with
  that version's relations (`kind`, `range`, `via`: the name asked for), at most 50 by name, and `total`, the count of them all. The scope
  is the package list's (the endpoint's exposure included); `project` narrows it to a project's repositories as the list does.
- A dependent in a repository the caller may not read is neither listed nor counted, and is not read: the repositories are decided first,
  and the statement walks the index `package_dependencies_by_name (repo_id, name)` for those alone. The answer depends on nothing the
  caller may not read: a name no visible repository holds has its dependents answered all the same. `whole` says whether the caller reads
  every repository of the format whole, the same for every package of the format.
- "Used by" lists the packages that depend on the package, with the range each asks for; whether that range holds the version on the
  page is not decided ([H-2223](#h-2223--used-by-does-not-say-whether-a-dependents-range-holds-the-version-on-the-page)).
- `GET /api/v1/packages?format=<one format with dependencies>&dependsOn=<name>` keeps the packages with a visible version that depends on
  it, the same packages; a format without dependencies, or none or several, answers `400`
  ([Q-API-459](#q-api-459--the-list-filters-by-dependson-as-by-keyword-planned-for-its-values)).
- A remote's tab **Upstream** shows none: who depends on a package at an upstream is the upstream's to know, and Quader asks it nothing.

**The screen** ([Q-UI-1350](#q-ui-1350--used-by-stands-under-the-dependencies-in-their-block),
[Q-UI-1351](#q-ui-1351--past-50-the-section-says-how-many-more-and-leads-to-the-projects-package-list)): the tab **Details** of a version's
page shows **Used by** right after **Dependencies**, in npm, NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy (an Ansible role has none): one line per
dependent, its name a link to its version that depends, the version, then each relation as the format names it (the kind, the name it
asks for where it is a name the package provides, the range muted). Past 50: "and N more." and **Packages of this project that use it**,
the project's package list filtered by `dependsOn`, where the filter is a chip **Depends on**. None: "No package the installation holds
depends on it." for a caller who reads every repository of the format whole, else "No package you may read depends on it." It reads again
while it is seen (R-UI-213).

Measured (2026-11-26, `TestMeasureUsedBy`, [packages.md](../developer/packages.md#who-depends-on-a-package)): with 50,000 npm packages of which
5,000 depend on one name, the read answers in 31 ms for a caller who reads 10,000 dependents and in 23 ms for a reader of the repository
of 5,000 beside a second one she may not read with 5,000 more; the list filtered by `dependsOn` in 150 to 160 ms, the list without the
filter in 270 to 290 ms on the same data.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/formatdata/npm`, `nuget`, `deb`, `ansible`: `TestR_API_086_…`, microseconds each): what each format's extractor reads of
  its stored row; `internal/packages/dependents`: a row is kept once within the bounds of the table.
- Integration (`packages`, `TestR_API_086_UsedByListsThePackagesTheCallerMayReadThatDependOnAPackage`, about 9 s with a replica of the role
  api and one of the role worker): the npm commit writes the rows; the read on the role api, each dependent once by its newest version with
  its kinds; a dependent the caller may not read neither listed nor counted; the project; the filter `dependsOn` and its refusals; the task
  writes the rows of versions stored without them.
- Integration, one assertion in the area of each writer: `deblocal` (`TestR_DEB_038_039_…`: a name a package provides, a qualifier dropped,
  the filter), `debremote` (`TestR_DEB_037_…`: the describe job), `ansiblelocal` (`TestR_ANS_060_…`), `nuget` (the push of `semver2Push`),
  `npm` (`TestR_NPM_050_…`: the describe job), each read on the role api where the area reads.
- Integration (`search`, `TestR_API_086_TheReadOfDependentsWalksTheIndexOfTheRepositoriesTheCallerMayRead`, about a second): both
  statements walk `package_dependencies_by_name` by the repositories they are given.
- Web unit (`package-version.spec.ts`, `package-list.spec.ts`): the section, its links and its sentences; the chip and the filter.

### R-API-058 · Operations that serve wiki content
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

An operation of the management API that serves only wiki content ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034) carries
the extension `x-quader-part: wiki` in `api/openapi.yaml`. The document validator accepts the extension only on a `GET`
operation whose permission is the read of a repository's content (the declaration of R-API-029's operations) and refuses it
elsewhere; it is read into `Operation.Part`, as `x-quader-maintenance` is read into `Operation.MaintenanceAllowed`
([Q-API-247](#q-api-247--the-wiki-part-of-an-operation-is-an-extension-of-the-document-read-into-the-operation)).

- The shared authorization step admits such an operation as it admits the other reads of R-API-029, whose read is decided per
  repository in the handler; the handler then asks the wiki of the repository that holds the version through
  `authz.ReadScope.MayReadWiki` and answers the 404 of a missing README when it is refused. Like the filter of a listing, the
  question writes no `authz.denied` (R-AUTHZ-029): the caller may read the package and asked about a member of it. Nothing tells
  the caller that a README exists.
- A member of a management answer that carries wiki content (`hasReadme` of R-API-029, `metadata.docs` of the Ansible format)
  is decided with `MayReadWiki` and is `false` or absent when refused. The format's view adapter returns the wiki members
  marked, so that the API, not the format, drops them.
- A member a format read from the content of a version's files beyond its document (an OCI image's configuration and the facts of its
  labels, [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-040) is decided with the read of those files' paths (`authz.PathReader.MayReadPath`, the
  protocol's decision of a read of the path) and is absent when one is refused. It is absent as well while a download of one of those
  files would not be served to the caller now: the serve point of stored content decides it with the checks of the download (the malware
  gate, the vulnerability block, the delivery rules, the signature gate; `files.Service.Hold` over `sgate.Serve.Hold`, which takes its
  answer from the decision `Run` takes its own from and records nothing), and `metadata.contentHeld` (`{"code": …}`) names the code the
  download would answer (`malware_found`, `vulnerability_blocked`, `not_allowed_in_repository`, `signature_not_verified`,
  `malware_not_checked`, `vulnerability_data_missing`, or `malware_check_pending` and `signature_check_pending` while a check runs). The
  view adapter names the members and the paths (`ContentMetadata`, `ContentPaths`), and the API drops them; a list and a search carry no
  such member.
- Today's operations with `x-quader-part: wiki`: `getPackageVersionReadme`; the documentation operations of
  [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) (T-19) join with their requirement.
- A test walks the document and fails when an operation whose response schema holds a README or a documentation body lacks
  the extension (`TestR_API_058_WikiOperationsAreMarked`).

Acceptance criteria:

- `getPackageVersionReadme` carries `x-quader-part: wiki`; a document with the extension on a `PUT` operation fails to load.
- For a caller who reads the artifacts of `web/npm-public` and not its wiki, `GET …/readme` answers 404 with the body of a
  missing README.

### R-API-060 · One operation answers the suggestions of the search field
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task T-22 (2026-11-12): one search field with live suggestions for every caller (R-UI-095 to R-UI-099).
`GET /api/v1/search/suggestions` answers, in one request, the best matches of a text for each kind the field shows
([Q-API-270](#q-api-270--one-operation-answers-the-suggestions-and-the-results-page-reads-the-three-lists)):

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q` | Required. The text, trimmed: 2 to 100 characters, else `400 malformed_request` with the pointer `q` |
| `kind` | `repository`, `package`, `project`, `documentation` ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-058: the modules, plugins and roles of the newest version of every collection the caller may read, whose wiki it may read), `user`, `group`, `service_account` (R-API-078); repeated or comma-separated; default `repository,package,project`. An unknown kind answers `400 malformed_request` |
| `limit` | Suggestions per kind, 1 to 10, default 5 |

```json
{
  "repositories": {"items": [{"project": "web", "key": "npm-local", "format": "npm", "class": "local"}], "more": false},
  "packages": {"items": [{"id": "pkg_nzyg2acao5swel3vnewww2lu", "format": "npm", "name": "@web/ui-kit", "project": "web", "repository": "npm-local"}], "more": true},
  "projects": {"items": [{"key": "web", "displayName": "Web platform"}], "more": false}
}
```

- One member per kind asked (`repositories`, `packages`, `projects`, `users`, `groups`, `serviceAccounts`), absent for a kind not
  asked; `items` in the order of R-API-062, `more` by R-API-061. A user is `{"id", "username", "displayName", "disabled",
  "avatarUrl"}`, a group `{"name", "description"}`, a service account `{"name", "description", "project"}` (R-API-078); a package's `name` is its display name, `key` the normalized name its address uses (an Ansible role's `role/<id>`, [Q-UI-1261](#q-ui-1261--a-packages-address-is-its-key-its-title-its-name-and-the-search-finds-the-name)) and `id` the identifier of `GET /api/v1/packages/{packageId}`
  ([Q-API-271](#q-api-271--the-answer-holds-one-typed-member-per-kind-and-no-cursor)).
- Not a list of R-API-010: no `cursor`, `nextCursor` or `Link`. The results page reads the lists (R-UI-098).
- Permission: any caller (`x-quader-permission: public: true`), decided in the handler by R-API-061. Without a credential `401`
  while no repository's artifacts are `public`, as the lists answer. `kind` `user`, `group` or `service_account` needs `identities:read`; without it
  the answer is `403`, before any lookup and the same for every `q`
  ([Q-API-272](#q-api-272--users-and-groups-need-identitiesread-checked-before-any-lookup)).
- Rate limit: the class `read` with a credential, `anonymous` without (R-API-016); no class of its own
  ([Q-API-281](#q-api-281--the-suggestions-use-the-read-and-anonymous-classes-and-q-is-2-to-100-characters)).
- Freshness: the repositories are matched over the grant index of the request (R-AUTHZ-028), on which they are decided anyway, so a
  repository created through another replica is suggested within the propagation bound of R-API-052; projects, packages, users and
  groups are read from PostgreSQL. `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` (R-AUTHZ-032) applies as on every operation.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` (R-API-017).

Acceptance criteria:

- `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=n` and a `q` of 101 characters answer `400 malformed_request`; `kind=file` `400`; `limit=11`
  `400`.
- `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=npm&kind=repository` answers only the member `repositories`.
- The answer carries `RateLimit-Policy: "read";q=200;w=4` with the defaults.

### R-API-061 · A suggestion names only what the caller may read
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The suggestions are a listing in the sense of [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-016: they hold only what the caller may
read, and nothing in the answer depends on an object it may not read. Per kind the rule is the one of that kind's list, on the same
decision point and the same index of the request:

| Kind | Suggested when | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| repository | the caller may read it, by a grant, a role or its artifacts level (R-AUTHZ-035), or, holding `repositories:read-config`, the endpoint of the request exposes it; a repository being deleted is never in the index | `acc.Readable`, `acc.Exposed` for `repositories:read-config`, as `GET /api/v1/repositories` |
| package | in a physical repository the caller reads whole (read shape `ReadAll`), one version is live and served; in one it reads in part (`ReadRows`), the caller may read the package's document and the repository's include and exclude patterns admit the name ([Q-API-275](#q-api-275--a-package-in-a-repository-read-in-part-is-decided-on-its-document)) | the read scope of `GET /api/v1/packages` (`authz.ReadScope`) |
| project | the caller is a member, holds `projects:read`, or the project's level admits it (R-AUTHZ-035 rule 8) | the rule of `GET /api/v1/projects` |
| user, group, service account | the caller holds `identities:read` | the capability, checked before any lookup |

- **Hidden existence holds.** `hideExistence` (R-AUTHZ-017) changes only the status of a refused read. A repository with
  `hideExistence: false` that the caller cannot read is suggested no more than any other. A virtual repository is suggested by its own
  gate (R-AUTHZ-009 rule 1); its members are not suggested through it.
- **Levels, users and tokens.** The level `internal` admits every internal subject (R-AUTHZ-030): every authenticated caller - a
  user, a service account's technical token, a CI token, through a Bastion as at the main door - but a user flagged external and
  that user's tokens, which get what grants, roles and `public` give them. A token's scope narrows
  what grants and `internal` give, not what `public` gives (R-AUTHZ-035 rule 3).
- **A project is named by its key** in a repository's or a package's entry
  ([Q-API-277](#q-api-277--an-entry-names-the-project-of-a-repository-or-a-package-by-its-key)). Its display name appears only in a
  project entry, which the project rule admits.
- **Filtered before it is cut** ([Q-API-276](#q-api-276--more-reports-only-readable-matches-the-answer-left-out)). Each kind is ranked
  among the readable matches (R-API-062) and then cut at `limit`. `more` is `true` when the kind left out a readable match it found.
  The work per request is bounded (R-API-064), so `more` may be `false` while the results page holds more; it is never `true` because
  of an object the caller cannot read.
- **The same for every text.** `400`, `401` and `403` do not depend on `q`.

Acceptance criteria, each a test of the integration area `search` on the worked rows of R-AUTHZ-035 (project `web`, `public`;
`npm-public` with artifacts `public` and wiki `internal`; `npm-internal`, both `internal`; `npm-private`, both `private`, with
`hideExistence: false`; the virtual `npm-all`, `internal`, over the three; each local repository holds `@web/button`; Erin flagged
external with `read` on `npm-private`; Frank internal without grants):

- Without a credential, `q=npm` answers the repository `web/npm-public` alone, and `q=button` the package `@web/button` with
  `repository: npm-public` (a package name is matched by the text, and `npm` is no part of `@web/button`).
- Frank: `npm-all`, `npm-internal` and `npm-public`, never `npm-private`. Erin: `npm-private` and `npm-public`, never `npm-internal`
  or `npm-all`.
- Frank with a token scoped to `mobile/*`: `npm-public` alone.
- Frank's `kind=user` answers `403` for `q=fr` and for `q=zz`, with the same body.
- Twenty packages `button-<n>` added to `npm-private` change neither Frank's answer to `q=button` nor its `more`.

### R-API-062 · How a suggestion matches and is ranked
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

`q` is trimmed and lower-cased (Unicode simple case folding); its **terms** are its parts between white space.

| Kind | Matches when | Rank, best first | Then by |
|---|---|---|---|
| repository | every term is part of `<project>/<key>` | 0 the key or `<project>/<key>` equals `q`; 1 the key starts with `q`; 2 `<project>/<key>` starts with `q`; 3 any other | `<project>/<key>`, byte order |
| project | every term is part of the key or of the display name | 0 the key equals `q`; 1 the key starts with `q`; 2 the display name or one of its words starts with `q`; 3 any other | key |
| package | the name starts with `q`, or every **word** of `q` begins a word of the name; a word is a run of `a` to `z` and `0` to `9` ([Q-API-274](#q-api-274--package-names-a-whole-name-prefix-on-a-c-collation-b-tree-and-word-prefixes-on-a-gin-tsvector-without-pg_trgm)) | 0 the name equals `q`; 1 the name starts with `q`; 2 by words | the name, byte order; then the format |
| user | every term is part of the username or of the display name | 0 the username equals `q`; 1 the username starts with `q`; 2 the display name or one of its words starts with `q`; 3 any other | username |
| group | every term is part of the name | 0 equal; 1 starts with `q`; 3 any other | name |
| service account | every term is part of the stored name; active accounts only (R-API-078) | 0 equal; 1 starts with `q`; 3 any other | name |

- A package matches on its stored name (`packages.name`, the format's normalized name), by a word also on its display name (an Ansible
  role `role/<id>` by the words of `<owner>.<name>`), and shows its display name. A package held by
  several repositories is one entry, placed in the first of them by qualified name that the caller reads; these are local and
  remote repositories, because a virtual repository holds no package rows (R-REPO-018).
- Descriptions are not matched by the suggestions. The lists that the results page reads match them (R-UI-098), and they match
  every suggestion of their kind: `GET /api/v1/repositories` matches `<project>/<key>` besides the key and the description
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-012,
  [Q-API-279](#q-api-279--the-repository-lists-q-matches-the-qualified-name)).

Acceptance criteria:

- `q=npm` orders the repositories `web/npm`, then `mobile/npm-local` and `web/npm-local`, then `web/my-npm`.
- `q=@acme/ui` suggests `@acme/ui-kit` (rank 1) before `@acme/kit-ui` (rank 2, by words); `q=kit` suggests both; `q=it` neither.
- `GET /api/v1/repositories?q=web/npm` lists `web/npm-local`.

### R-API-063 · The repository list answers named repositories
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

`GET /api/v1/repositories` takes `name`, a qualified name `<project>/<key>`, repeated or comma-separated, at most 50
([Q-API-278](#q-api-278--the-repository-list-takes-name)). The answer holds the named repositories the caller may see, in the list's
order, by the rules of [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-012. A name that does not exist and a name of a
repository the caller may not see are both absent, so the answer tells them apart for nobody. A malformed name, or more than 50,
answers `400 malformed_request`. The UI resolves the frequently visited repositories of R-UI-096 and the side bar's **Recently
opened** (R-UI-167) with one such request each.

Acceptance criteria:

- `name=web/npm-public&name=web/npm-private&name=web/nope` as Frank of R-API-061 lists `web/npm-public` alone.
- 51 names answer `400`.

### R-API-064 · The indexes and the bounds of the suggestions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Data model ([Q-API-274](#q-api-274--package-names-a-whole-name-prefix-on-a-c-collation-b-tree-and-word-prefixes-on-a-gin-tsvector-without-pg_trgm)),
in migration `00076_search.sql`, and the words of a display name that is more than the name's casing in `00135_packages_display_words.sql`
([Q-UI-1261](#q-ui-1261--a-packages-address-is-its-key-its-title-its-name-and-the-search-finds-the-name)):

```sql
ALTER TABLE packages
    ADD COLUMN name_words tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS
        (to_tsvector('simple'::regconfig, regexp_replace(lower(name), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))) STORED;
CREATE INDEX packages_name_words ON packages USING gin (name_words);
CREATE INDEX packages_name_lower ON packages ((lower(name) COLLATE "C"));
-- 00135, one statement without a transaction:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS packages_display_words ON packages
    USING gin ((to_tsvector('simple'::regconfig, regexp_replace(lower(display_name), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))))
    WHERE lower(display_name) <> lower(name);
```

The display words' index holds only the rows whose display name is more than the name's casing: the packages of Ansible roles a remote
read today, at most one row per role and repository (a NuGet ID differs only in case and is found by its name). Its step writes no row
of `packages` and does not block its writes; it reads the table once to build the index, as every index step does. Statement B matches
a word in `name_words` or, for such a row, in the display name.

How each kind is read ([Q-API-273](#q-api-273--repositories-are-matched-over-the-requests-grant-index-and-projects-over-their-rows-without-an-index)):

| Kind | Read | Index | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| repository | the repositories of the request's grant index, in memory; no statement | — | every active repository, 10,000 in the reference environment ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-027 P-15) |
| project | one statement over `project`, as the project list | none | every project |
| package | statement A: names that start with `q` in the repositories the caller reads whole or in part, as the range `low <= lower(p.name) COLLATE "C" < high`, where `low` is `q` and `high` the least string above every string that starts with `q`, ordered by the same expression, at most 200 rows; statement B, only when A found fewer than `limit + 1` readable packages: names whose words begin with the words of `q` (`p.name_words @@ to_tsquery('simple', 'w1:* & w2:*')`), without A's rows, at most 200 rows. Every row needs a live, served version: `EXISTS` over `package_version_listing` (`package_versions_live`), without the withheld versions of the formats, read as `GET /api/v1/packages` reads them. Both run in one transaction after `SET LOCAL plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan` | A: `packages_name_lower`; B: `packages_name_words` | 400 candidate rows, one served-version check each |
| user, group, service account | one statement each over `principal` with `app_user` (and `user_avatars` for the avatar), `user_group` or `service_account`, `kind` fixed, `strpos` on the lower-cased columns, ranked in the statement and cut at `limit + 1` | none (`principal` is unique on `kind, name`) | every user, group or service account |

- The words of a tsquery are runs of `a` to `z` and `0` to `9` taken from `q`, so no operator of the tsquery syntax reaches the
  database; the name prefix is two bound values, not a pattern, so no character of `q` is an operator there either.
- Each package statement is planned for its text
  ([Q-API-283](#q-api-283--the-package-statements-take-the-name-prefix-as-two-bounds-and-are-planned-for-their-text)): a
  prepared statement may otherwise take a generic plan after its fifth run,
  and a generic plan cannot know whether `q` makes the word index or the name order the cheaper read (it chose a walk over every
  package for a rare word).
- A request costs at most a fixed number of statements, independent of the number of matches and of the rows read: the project
  statement, the user and group statements for the kinds asked, and for packages the withheld query of each format that has one,
  the plan setting, statement A and, when A leaves room, statement B.
- Quader does not create `pg_trgm` (migration 00017), so an infix inside a word of a name (`it` in `ui-kit`) is not suggested; the
  results page's `GET /api/v1/packages?q=` finds it.

Acceptance criteria:

- With `SET enable_seqscan = off`, `EXPLAIN` of statement A shows `packages_name_lower` and of statement B `packages_name_words`.
- A request with the five kinds costs the same number of statements with 10 and with 10,000 matching packages (integration area
  `querybudget`).

### R-API-031 · Users, groups and service accounts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-004, ADMAPI-005, ADMAPI-006, ADMAPI-007, ADMAPI-008, ADMAPI-009, ADMAPI-012, ADMAPI-013, ADMAPI-014, ADMAPI-015, ADMAPI-016, ADMAPI-017, ADMAPI-018

Owned by [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md); users are addressed by
username:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/users` | List; filters `q`, `status`, `origin`, `group`, `admin`, `external` | `admin` or `identities:read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/users` | Pre-provision a user linked to an identity-provider identity, with its `external` flag | `admin` |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/{username}` | Read, with `external` | `admin`, `identities:read` |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/users/{username}` | Change display name, email, identities, and the `external` flag (`identities:write`, recent authentication, R-AUTH-044) | `admin` |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/{username}/disable`, `/enable` | Disable (optionally revoking tokens) or enable | `admin` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{username}` | Delete | `admin` |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/users/{username}/groups` | `{"add": [...], "remove": [...]}` on manual memberships | `admin` |
| GET, DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{username}/sessions` | List or end a user's sessions | `admin` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{username}/tokens` | Revoke all tokens of a user | `admin` |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/{breakGlassName}/unlock` | Unlock the locked break-glass account | `admin` |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/groups` | List and create | `admin`; reads also `identities:read` |
| GET, PATCH, DELETE | `/api/v1/groups/{name}` | Read, change (including rename), delete | as list |
| GET, PATCH | `/api/v1/groups/{name}/members` | Members with their sources; add and remove manual members | as list |
| GET | `/api/v1/service-accounts` | Instance-wide list of every service account, each with `project` (`null` for an account of no project); filters `q`, `project` | `admin`, `identities:read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/service-accounts` | Create a service account of no project | `admin` (`identities:write`); owners from P1 |
| GET, PATCH, DELETE | `/api/v1/service-accounts/{name}` | Read, change, delete an account of no project | as list; changes `admin` |
| POST | `/api/v1/service-accounts/{name}/disable`, `/enable` | Disable or enable an account of no project | `admin` |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts` | List and create the project's service accounts; a name is unique within the project | `identities:read` (list) or `identities:write`, or Owner of the project; recent authentication for the create |
| GET, PATCH, DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts/{name}` | Read, change the description, delete | as the project list (`identities:write` or Owner for writes) |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts/{name}/disable`, `/enable` | Disable or enable | `identities:write`, or Owner of the project |

A service account of a project is referenced as `sa:<projectKey>/<name>`, one of no project as `sa:<name>`
([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-020,
[Q-AUTHZ-209](authorization.md#q-authz-209--a-projects-policies-and-service-accounts-are-named-within-the-project-administrators-keep-instance-wide-ones)).
`/api/v1/service-accounts/{name}` never addresses an account of a project. System roles of users and groups are role
bindings (R-API-033), not user fields. There are no user
passwords (INV-7); the lockout of ADMAPI-012 exists only for the break-glass account (R-AUTH-038).

Acceptance criteria:

- `GET /api/v1/users?q=jdoe` as administrator returns the user; as a non-administrator without
  `identities:read`, 403.
- `POST /api/v1/users/jdoe/disable` with `{"revokeTokens": true}` makes `jdoe`'s tokens fail with
  401 on every replica within 2 s (R-AUTH-023, R-API-052).

### R-API-032 · Access tokens
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-039, ADMAPI-040, ADMAPI-043, ADMAPI-044, ADMAPI-045, ADMAPI-046

Owned by [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) (token model, scope
grammar, lifetimes, revocation):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/tokens` | Create a personal token for the caller | user with session (recent authentication) or a PAT under the derivation rule |
| POST | `…/service-accounts/{name}/technical-tokens`, `…/technical-tokens/{tokenName}/secrets` at the instance, a project or a repository | Create a technical token of a service account with its first secret, or a new secret of one ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-045, R-API-082); for an Owner without `identities:write` never non-expiring, `admin: false`, no `system` item ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026, Q-AUTHZ-177) | `admin`, or Owner of the project of a project's or a repository's account; recent authentication for sessions |
| GET | `/api/v1/tokens` | List own tokens; all with `tokens:read`; an Owner also the tokens of its project's service accounts (`project=<key>`) | `self`, `tokens:read`, Owner |
| GET | `/api/v1/tokens/{id}`, `/api/v1/tokens/current` | Read one token | `{id}`: owner, `tokens:read`; `current`: the presenting token itself, CI tokens included ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-013) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/tokens/{id}`, `/api/v1/tokens/current` | Revoke | `{id}`: owner, owners of the service account (P1), an Owner of the project of the service account, `tokens:revoke`, `admin`; `current`: the presenting token itself, of every type, CI tokens (`qdr_cit_`) included (R-AUTH-029; [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-013) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/tokens` | Revoke all own tokens | `self` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/service-accounts/{name}/tokens` | Revoke all tokens of a service account of no project | `admin` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts/{name}/tokens` | Revoke all tokens of a project's service account | `admin`, `tokens:revoke`, or Owner of the project |
| POST | `/api/v1/tokens/revoke` | Revoke by value | anyone, no authentication |
| POST | `/api/v1/tokens/{id}/rotate`, `/api/v1/tokens/current/rotate` | Rotate (P1, R-AUTH-030); CI tokens cannot be rotated | PAT: its owner only, through a session with recent authentication or a token of the owner under the derivation rule; SAT: `admin`, owners of the service account from P1, or a SAT of the account under the derivation rule; `current/rotate`: the token itself, only if `selfRotatable`. `tokens:revoke` alone never rotates (R-AUTH-030) |

API conventions that apply: the secret appears only in the create and rotate answers, which are
`no-store`, uncompressed (R-API-017) and never stored for idempotency replay (R-API-014).

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"description":"t","ttlSeconds":3600}' "$QUADER_URL/api/v1/tokens"`
  returns a value starting with `qdr_pat_` (field names per
  [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)); `GET /api/v1/tokens/{id}`
  never contains it.
- `POST /api/v1/tokens/revoke` without credentials and with a valid token value revokes it.
- `DELETE /api/v1/tokens/current` with a `qdr_cit_` token answers 204, and the same token then gets
  401 on every replica within 2 s (R-AUTH-023, R-API-052).
- A token whose scope is `{"system": ["tokens:revoke"]}` gets 403 `forbidden` from
  `POST /api/v1/tokens/{id of another user's PAT}/rotate` and 204 from `DELETE` of the same ID
  (P1, with rotation).

### R-API-033 · Permission policies and system roles
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-020, ADMAPI-021, ADMAPI-022, ADMAPI-023, ADMAPI-024, IAM-031

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/permission-policies` | Instance-wide list of every policy, each with `project` (`null` for a policy of no project); filters `principal` (with `expandGroups`), `repository` (the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`), `project` | `policies:read`; delegated managers see their policies |
| POST | `/api/v1/permission-policies` | Create a policy of no project; its selectors take the instance form `<projectGlob>/<keyGlob>[:<format>]` or a class ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-004) | `policies:write`; recent authentication |
| GET | `/api/v1/permission-policies/{name}` | Read a policy of no project, with `ETag` | as list |
| PUT, PATCH | `/api/v1/permission-policies/{name}` | Replace or merge patch; `If-Match` required (428) | as create; delegated managers per R-AUTHZ-025 (P1) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/permission-policies/{name}` | Delete | as create |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/policies` | List and create the project's policies; a name is unique within the project; selectors are bare keys, key globs and classes of the project | `policies:read` (list) or `policies:write`, or Owner of the project; recent authentication for the create |
| GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/policies/{name}` | Read with `ETag`, replace, merge patch, delete | as the project list; delegated managers per R-AUTHZ-025 (P1) |
| POST | `/api/v1/authz/validate-policy` | Validate without storing; errors, warnings, covered repositories; a policy of a project names it in the body | `policies:read`, or Owner of the named project |
| GET | `/api/v1/roles` | The fixed system roles and their capabilities | authenticated |
| GET | `/api/v1/role-bindings` | List bindings; filters `role`, `principal` | `roles:read` |
| PUT, DELETE | `/api/v1/role-bindings/{role}/{principalRef}` | Bind (idempotent) or unbind; 409 `last_admin` | `roles:write`; recent authentication |

Every successful write of a policy or a role binding answers with `Quader-Authz-Epoch`, which a
later request names in `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` to see the change on any replica (R-API-052,
R-AUTHZ-032).

Acceptance criteria:

- After creating a policy that grants group `team-a` `read` and `deploy` on `web/npm-team-a` for
  `@team-a/**`, a member of `team-a` can `npm publish` `@team-a/ui` there and gets 403 for
  `@team-b/x`.
- A policy of no project with the selector `npm-team-a` (a bare key) answers 422 `invalid_pattern`; the same selector in
  `POST /api/v1/projects/web/policies` is accepted.
- Unbinding the last administrator answers 409 `last_admin`.

### R-API-034 · Effective permissions and decision explanation
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-008, IAM-030, ART-031

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) (R-AUTHZ-024):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/authz/effective?repository=&package=` or `&path=` (`repository` is the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`) | Every principal holding actions on a coordinate, members of the repository's project by their role included, with the granting policies; CI mappings whose templates could render to it marked `conditional` | `policies:read`, or `manage` on the coordinate |
| POST | `/api/v1/authz/explain` | Decision trace for a principal or token on a coordinate | `policies:read` (plus `tokens:read` for a token) |

The UI explainer (R-UI-028) and the effective permissions in the Details of a file's page (R-UI-010, P1) render these answers.
The explanation comes from the evaluator that enforces decisions, run in trace mode; nothing is
reimplemented for display.

Acceptance criteria:

- A property-based test generates random policies, principals and coordinates and asserts that
  `decision` of `explain` always equals the enforcement result of the same request.

| POST, DELETE | `/api/v1/ci/issuers/{issuer}/delegations…` | Delegate mapping management for a scope to a group (P1; covers project-scoped mappings, ADMAPI-030) | `admin` |
| GET | `/api/v1/ci/issuances`, `/api/v1/ci/issuances/{tokenId}` | Issued CI tokens with job context | `admin`, `tokens:read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/ci/issuances/revoke` | Revoke matching CI tokens | `admin`, `tokens:revoke` |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/oidc/token` | Exchange a CI ID token for a `qdr_cit_` token (INV-10) | anonymous; the ID token is the proof |

The permission column names the role that holds the capabilities of the operations: the issuer, mapping,
dry-run and snippet operations declare `ci:read` (the reads, the dry run and the snippet) and `ci:write` (the writes,
the key refresh, with recent authentication on create, replace and delete), the issuance operations `tokens:read` and
`tokens:revoke` (R-AUTHZ-010, Q-CI-22). A CI token is refused on all of them (`403 ci_token_restricted`, Q-CI-18).

API conventions that apply: the evaluation endpoint takes claims, never a token, and the UI decodes
pasted tokens in the browser (R-UI-036). The exchange speaks OAuth to OAuth clients: its answers
carry `Cache-Control: no-store` and the field names of RFC 8693, and its errors are OAuth error
responses ([RFC 6749 §5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-5.2),
`Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: no-store`) with `error` and
`error_description` plus Quader's members `reason` (left out under
`ci.exchange.expose_reason: false`) and `requestId`, not problem details (R-API-009). A rejected
subject token answers 400 `invalid_request` ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-008,
Q-CI-8).

Acceptance criteria:

- In a GitLab CI job using the snippet of `GET …/snippets/gitlab-ci?mapping=team-a-protected&format=npm`,
  the exchange succeeds and `npm publish` of `@team-a/ui` succeeds.
- An exchange with an expired ID token answers 400 with `Content-Type: application/json`,
  `Cache-Control: no-store`, `error` `invalid_request`, `reason` `token_expired` and a `requestId`
  equal to the `X-Request-Id` header, and no `type` or `title` member.
- `POST …/evaluate` with a claim set that matches no mapping answers 200 with no matched mapping and
  the failing condition per candidate.

### R-API-036 · Format helper operations handed to format pages
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-046, API-166

- PyPI JSON project metadata (API-046) is served by the PyPI protocol handler on its protocol path
  (`/api/pypi/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/…`, INV-6) in the shape of the [PyPI JSON API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/json/),
  not under `/api/v1/`; owned by the future PyPI format page.
- Container image promotion (API-166) is reserved as
  `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/images/promote` with
  `{"image", "tag", "targetRepository", "targetImage", "targetTag", "copy"}` (`tag: null` = all
  tags; permissions as copy and move in R-API-027); owned by the future Docker/OCI format page.
- Maven metadata calculation (API-043) and Helm index recalculation (API-050) are `reindex`
  (R-API-024).

Acceptance criteria: defined on the owning format pages; this page requires that the reserved
paths are used for nothing else.

### R-API-037 · Settings surface
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-042, ADMAPI-047, ADMAPI-050, ADMAPI-055, ADMAPI-071

Runtime settings are owned by the page whose behavior they change. This index is what the
settings screens (R-UI-031 to R-UI-034) call:

| Setting | Where | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| New users external, token default and maximum lifetimes, expiry notices (ADMAPI-042, ADMAPI-047) | `GET`, `PATCH /api/v1/settings/auth`, bounded by YAML ceilings | R-AUTH-040, R-AUTH-044 |
| The installation's default visibility level, its restricted levels, whether `public` is available, what is `public` | `GET`, `PATCH /api/v1/settings/visibility`; the levels a caller may choose in `GET /api/v1/visibility-choices` | R-API-056, R-API-075, R-API-076, [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033, R-AUTHZ-037 |
| Break-glass lockout (ADMAPI-050), client authentication switches including Basic (ADMAPI-055) | YAML; read-only in `GET /api/v1/settings/auth` | R-AUTH-038, R-AUTH-040 |
| Public base URL (ADMAPI-071) | YAML `server.base_url`; read-only in `GET /api/v1/system/info` | R-OPS-005 |
| Hiding unauthorized resources | YAML `authz.hide_existence`, per-repository override | R-AUTHZ-017 |
| Trash can, storage behavior | `GET`, `PUT /api/v1/settings/storage` | [storage.md](storage.md) |
| Delivery by signed links of the object store: the switch, the minimum size, the link's life, the public addresses | `GET`, `PATCH /api/v1/download-links/settings`; the test link `POST /api/v1/download-links/test` | [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-014, R-STOR-074 |
| Global offline mode | `GET`, `PUT /api/v1/system/proxy-offline` | [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) |
| Outbound proxies, client certificates | `/api/v1/system/outbound-proxies…`, `/api/v1/system/client-certificates…` | [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) |
| Banner | `GET`, `PUT /api/v1/system/banner` | [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) |
| Maintenance (read-only) mode | `GET`, `PUT /api/v1/system/maintenance` | [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) |

Rule for all settings documents: a value set in YAML or its environment override (INV-15) is shown
with its source and cannot be changed through the API (409 `managed_by_config`, Q-API-19), so operators who manage settings
through Helm keep control.

Acceptance criteria:

- `PATCH /api/v1/settings/auth` with a PAT maximum above the YAML ceiling answers 400
  `exceeds_ceiling`.
- With `server.base_url` set, `GET /api/v1/system/info` reports `baseUrlSource` `config`.

### R-API-038 · System information, version and jobs
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-069, ADMAPI-070, API-033, OPS-008

Owned by [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) and
[architecture.md](architecture.md):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/system/version` | Version and revision | per [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/info` | Installation facts: version, base URL and source, maintenance mode, replicas per role (live, ready, degraded, nodes) and per version, database and schema versions, Valkey installation facts (mode, primary name, number of configured Sentinels, TLS mode, key prefix, keyspace, degraded replicas), backup status | `system.read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/replicas` | Replicas with version, roles, node, state, heartbeat, readiness checks and each replica's view of Valkey (state, reason, circuit, primary, Sentinels reachable and configured, server version, last primary change) | `system.read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/tasks`, POST `/api/v1/system/tasks/{name}/run` | Scheduled tasks and manual runs (R-OPS-019) | `system.read`; `admin` to run |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/migrations` | Schema state, the answering replica's binary, pending and applied schema steps, background data migrations with their states; owned by [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-018 (the upgrade verification of R-HA-020, step 4 of R-HA-021) | `system.read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/upstream-downloads`, `…/summary` | The running downloads from the upstreams of remote repositories and the last 100 finished; owned by [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-049 to R-OPS-052 | `content:metadata-read` |

**M0 stand-in, still in place after authentication shipped (M1).** Before it, no principal held `system.read`. The configuration
key `system.bootstrap_anonymous_read` (default `false`; `true` in the development profile) lets anonymous
callers read `/api/v1/system/info` and `/api/v1/system/replicas`. A request that presents an
`Authorization` header gets `401`. Startup refuses the key when `server.base_url` is an `https` origin other
than localhost, and a warning is logged when it is set. The key is removed with the identity work
(Q-API-14).
| GET | `/api/v1/system/jobs`, `/api/v1/system/jobs/{id}`, POST `…/cancel` | Jobs (R-OPS-019, R-API-015) | `system.read`; `admin` to cancel |

Liveness, readiness and Prometheus metrics stay on the operations listener (INV-6) and are not
duplicated under `/api/v1/`; this covers ADMAPI-069 and API-033 by reference.

The replica registry and the system information are owned by
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003 and R-OPS-004, which
define their shapes; this page adopts them unchanged and lists what the system status screen
(R-UI-038, Q-UI-7) reads. A disagreement between this list and those requirements is settled in
their favour.

- **Per replica** (`/system/replicas`, R-OPS-003):
  - `roles`: `["web"]`, `["worker"]`, or `["all"]` for the development role (INV-2); from P1 also
    the pool of [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-062;
  - `state` (`starting`, `ready`, `unready`, `draining`) and `lost`;
  - `node`, the Kubernetes node name from the downward API (`spec.nodeName` through the
    environment variable `QUADER_NODE_NAME`), `null` outside Kubernetes;
  - `checks`, the status of each gating and reported check (`pass`, `fail`, `degraded`), and
    `degraded`, the reported checks that fail (R-OPS-001);
  - `valkey`, the replica's view of Valkey as one nested object:

    | Field | Content |
    |---|---|
    | `state` | `available` or `degraded` |
    | `reason` | `null`, or the reason of the `valkey` check in R-OPS-001's vocabulary: an error kind of `quader_valkey_errors_total` (`timeout`, `connection`, `readonly`, `auth`, `tls`, `oom`), `no_primary` or `unsupported_version` |
    | `circuit` | The state of the replica's Valkey circuit breaker ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-057), for example `closed` or `open` |
    | `primary` | The primary address (host and port) the replica's client currently uses; `null` while it has none |
    | `sentinelsReachable`, `sentinelsConfigured` | The Sentinels this replica reaches, and the number configured |
    | `serverVersion` | The Valkey server version the replica's client sees |
    | `lastPrimaryChangeAt` | The replica's last change of primary |

  No credential, ACL user name or key appears. The nested object replaces the flat fields
  `valkeyPrimary`, `valkeyPrimarySince` and `valkeySentinelsReachable` of an earlier revision of
  this page, and R-OPS-001's reasons replace `unreachable`, `circuit_open` and `rejected`: an open
  circuit is `circuit: "open"`, not a reason.
- **Per installation** (`/system/info`, R-OPS-004):
  - `replicas.live`, `replicas.ready`, `replicas.versions`, and `replicas.roles.<role>` with
    `live`, `ready`, `degraded` and `nodes` for each role; this replaces `replicas.byRole`;
  - the `valkey` block with installation facts only: `mode`, `primaryName`, `sentinels` (the
    number configured), `tls`, `keyPrefix`, `keyspace` and `degradedReplicas`. `serverVersion` and
    each replica's client state are not in it; they live in the registry above. No Sentinel
    address and no credential appears in either answer;
  - the `backup` block: `expectedIntervalSeconds`, `lastSuccessAt`, `overdue` and `lastRunState`,
    read from `backup_run` (Q-API-205). `overdue` follows the rule of R-API-050 (1.5 × the
    expected interval), so this block, the backup summary of R-API-050, the UI and
    `QuaderBackupStale` agree.
- **Drain safety.** The screen decides whether a role is drain-safe from the items of
  `/system/replicas`: its ready replicas that are not `lost`, and their distinct nodes (R-UI-038).
  `replicas.roles.<role>.nodes` is the installation-wide summary for scripts and monitoring.

Acceptance criteria:

- With two `api` and two `worker` replicas running, `GET /api/v1/system/replicas` lists all four
  with their `roles` and nodes, and `GET /api/v1/system/info` reports `replicas.roles.api.live` and
  `replicas.roles.worker.live` as `2`; the system status screen (R-UI-038) renders from these
  answers, the task and job API, R-API-049 and R-API-050 without other endpoints.
- A replica started with the development role lists `"roles": ["all"]`.
- With Valkey stopped, every item lists `valkey` under `degraded`, with `valkey.state`
  `degraded` and `valkey.reason` `connection` or `timeout`, within `health.failure_threshold` ×
  `valkey.health_check_interval` plus `system.heartbeat_interval` plus 1 s; every item's `state`
  stays `ready`; and `/system/info` reports `valkey.degradedReplicas` equal to `replicas.live`.
- With three Sentinels configured and two of them stopped, every item's
  `valkey.sentinelsReachable` is 1 and `valkey.sentinelsConfigured` 3 within
  `valkey.sentinel.refresh_interval` plus `system.heartbeat_interval`, while `valkey.state` stays
  `available` and the `valkey` check `pass`, because the primary still answers.
- No answer of `/system/info` contains `serverVersion` under `valkey`, and the OpenAPI document
  contains none of `valkeyPrimary`, `valkeyPrimarySince`, `valkeySentinelsReachable` and
  `replicas.byRole`.

### R-API-040 · Garbage collection and storage summary
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: API-002, API-113, API-031, API-032

Semantics owned by [storage.md](storage.md); starting and stopping use the task and job endpoints
of R-OPS-019 (one path per function, Q-API-9 and R-API-020):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/system/tasks/gc/run`, `/api/v1/system/tasks/gc-full/run` | Start an incremental or a full collection run (`dryRun`); 202 with the job; 409 with the active job while any collection run is queued or running | `admin` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/jobs?kind=gc`, `?kind=gc-full`, `/api/v1/system/jobs/{id}` | Runs; each job's result carries the counts and reclaimed bytes defined by [storage.md](storage.md) | `system.read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/jobs/{id}/cancel` | Stop a run after the current batch | `admin` |
| GET | `/api/v1/storage/summary` | Blob and repository usage, the figures per connection (P1, R-STOR-028; built, `getStorageSummary`; `404` before the first run) | `settings:read`, the `storage.read` of [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/tasks/storage-summary/run` | Recompute; 202 with the job (P1; built) | `admin` |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/tasks/orphan-sweep/run`, `/api/v1/system/tasks/scrub/run` | Start an orphan sweep or an integrity scrub (P1, R-STOR-026, R-STOR-027) | `admin` |
| GET | `/api/v1/storage/damaged-blobs` | Damaged blobs and copies (`scope=blobs`, `scope=copies`), each with its copies and referencing items (P1, R-STOR-027, Q-API-386; built) | `settings:read`, the `storage.read` of [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) ([storage.md](storage.md) Q-STOR-267) |
| POST | `/api/v1/storage/damaged-blobs/{sha256}/recheck` | Read every copy of one blob whole now; a per-resource action, not a task (P1, R-STOR-027; built) | `settings:write` (`admin`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/storage-connections`, `/api/v1/system/storage-connections/{id}` | The object-store connections with state, fill, backlog and capabilities (P1, R-STOR-061, Q-API-385, Q-API-406; built, `listStorageConnections`, `getStorageConnection`) | `settings:read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/tasks/storage-reconcile/run` | Start a reconciliation run (P1, R-STOR-056; built); 202 with the job, 409 with the active one | `admin` |

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"dryRun":true}' "$QUADER_URL/api/v1/system/tasks/gc-full/run"`
  answers 202; `POST …/system/tasks/gc/run` while it runs answers 409 with the same job; after the
  job ends, `GET /api/v1/system/jobs?kind=gc-full` lists it with its result counts.

### R-API-042 · Build information
Priority: **P1** · Covers: API-107, API-156, API-157, API-158, API-159, API-160, API-162, API-163, API-165

Build information gets its own spec page, `builds.md` with prefix `R-BLD`, written before P1
build work starts (Q-API-5); it owns the record schema, the mapping of CI job names to
`{buildName}`, promotion and retention of runs, and uses the build permissions of R-AUTHZ-027 in
[authorization.md](authorization.md). Until it exists, this page reserves the surface so that the
paths do not move, and the MVP implements none of it. `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE` of
`/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/retention` are already specified by [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-043.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/builds` | Build names; `q`, `sort` | read on the build |
| GET | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs` | Runs, newest first | read on the build |
| PUT | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs/{number}` | Upload a build record; replacing an existing run needs `overwrite` | deploy on the build |
| GET | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs/{number}` | A run; `latest` as number alias; `compareTo={number}` adds a diff | read on the build |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs/{number}` | Delete; `deleteArtifacts=true` also deletes linked artifacts (202) | delete on the build |
| POST | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs/{number}/promote` | Set status, optionally copy or move artifacts and dependencies to a target repository, set properties; `dryRun` | deploy on the build, plus the permissions of copy and move |
| GET | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/runs/{number}/artifacts` | Artifacts with download URLs; optional `pattern` (repeat) | read on the build |
| GET, PUT, DELETE | `/api/v1/builds/{buildName}/retention` | Retention of runs ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-043): `GET` reads the stored parameters (404 when none); `PUT` stores them and applies them at once through a `build-retention` job, answering 202 with the job, or with `"wait": true` waiting up to `retention.build_retention_wait` and then answering 200 with the job result if it finished, otherwise 202; `DELETE` removes the parameters (204) and no run | `GET`: read on the build; `PUT`, `DELETE`: delete on the build |

Acceptance criteria:

- Uploading a build record for run `42` and then `GET …/runs/latest/artifacts` lists the record's
  artifacts with download URLs that resolve.

### R-API-043 · Retention and cleanup policies
Priority: **P1** · Covers: ADMAPI-085, ADMAPI-086, ADMAPI-088

Owned by [storage.md](storage.md): `/api/v1/retention/policies` (list, create),

### R-API-044 · Configuration as code
Priority: **P1** · Covers: ADMAPI-072, ADMAPI-073, ADMAPI-084

Owned by [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md):
`GET /api/v1/config/export`, `POST /api/v1/config/diff` (plan) and `POST /api/v1/config/apply`

### R-API-045 · Diagnostics
Priority: **P1** · Covers: ADMAPI-078, ADMAPI-080, ADMAPI-081

Owned by [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md):
`GET /api/v1/system/locks`; `GET /api/v1/system/log-levels`,
`PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/system/log-levels/override`; `/api/v1/system/support-bundles` (create,
list) with `/{id}`, `/{id}/download` and DELETE. Leases and the other advisory locks live in
PostgreSQL ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-017), so one query answers for the whole
cluster. The flight locks that collapse remote fetches live in Valkey (R-ARCH-033), last at most
`cluster.flight_lock_ttl` past their holder's last extension and carry only hashes, so the lock
list does not show them; their metrics (`quader_flight_lock_lost_total`,
`quader_flight_lock_bypass_total`) are the diagnostic. R-OPS-026 lists the PostgreSQL category
`fetch` as retired, and R-ARCH-017 keeps its number reserved.

Acceptance criteria:

- While a garbage-collection run holds its lease, `GET /api/v1/system/locks` shows it with the
  holding replica.

### R-API-046 · SCIM provisioning
Priority: **P1** · Covers: ADMAPI-035

Owned by [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md). The SCIM 2.0 service
