[RFC 7644](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7644)) lives under `/api/v1/scim/v2/`. It is the one
exception to R-API-003 (SCIM attribute names), R-API-009 (SCIM error bodies, RFC 7644 §3.12) and
R-API-010 (SCIM index paging).

Acceptance criteria:

- A SCIM client creates a user and a group with that member through `/api/v1/scim/v2/Users` and
  `/Groups`; `GET /api/v1/groups/{name}/members` lists the user.

### R-API-047 · Projects
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: ADMAPI-063, ADMAPI-064, ADMAPI-065, ADMAPI-067

Raised from P1 on 2026-11-02 with R-AUTHZ-026 (beta phase 5a).

Owned by [authorization.md](authorization.md) (R-AUTHZ-026; every repository belongs to exactly one project, users
and groups are members with a role, [Q-AUTHZ-206](authorization.md#q-authz-206--every-repository-belongs-to-exactly-one-project),
[Q-AUTHZ-207](authorization.md#q-authz-207--a-user-or-group-is-a-member-of-a-project-with-a-role-and-the-role-grants-the-projects-repositories),
[Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)):

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/projects?membership=` | Every project for `projects:read`; otherwise the caller's memberships, each with the caller's role, and the projects whose level admits the caller, without a role; `membership=true` lists the memberships only ([Q-AUTHZ-277](authorization.md#q-authz-277--a-project-is-seen-by-whom-its-level-admits-and-its-members-stay-with-its-members)); each item carries `visibility` | any caller; anonymous while `publicContent` is true |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects` | Create a project; `visibility` defaults to the installation's `defaultLevel` (R-API-056) | `projects:write` (`admin`); recent authentication for a level above `private` |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}` | Read, with `visibility` | `projects:read`, a member, or a caller the project's level admits |
| PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/visibility` | Set the project's level, `{"level": "internal"}`; lowering lowers the repositories above it (R-API-057) | `projects:write`; recent authentication |
| PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}` | Replace display name and description; `If-Match` required | `projects:write`, or Owner; recent authentication |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}` | Delete when empty (no repository, service account or CI mapping) | `projects:write`; recent authentication |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/members` | The members (users and groups) with their roles | `projects:read`, or a member |
| PUT | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/members/{principalRef}` | Add a member or change its role, `{"role": "developer"}` (`reader`, `developer`, `maintainer` or `owner`); 409 `last_owner` when it demotes the last Owner ([Q-AUTHZ-217](authorization.md#q-authz-217--the-last-owner-of-a-project-is-removed-or-demoted-only-by-an-administrator-of-quader)) | `projects:write`, or Owner; recent authentication |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/members/{principalRef}` | Remove a member; 409 `last_owner` for the last Owner | as `PUT` |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/principals?q=&kind=&limit=` | The users, groups and service accounts whose name or a word of it starts with `q`, with what a member's row shows, to name as members and in policies (R-API-077) | `identities:read`, or Owner |

The members operations cover the user and group membership operations of ADMAPI-064 and ADMAPI-065. What a project
holds is addressed below it and listed with its family: repositories, their sub-resources, the move and the upstream
tests (R-API-022 to R-API-030), service accounts and their tokens (R-API-031, R-API-032), policies (R-API-033) and CI
mappings (R-API-035). The instance-wide lists of repositories, permission policies and service accounts carry each
item's `project` and accept `project=` (webhooks and retention policies when they exist). `GET /api/v1/authz/me`
lists the caller's memberships with their roles (`projects`). Global custom roles and environments are P2 there
(see Deferred). Project writes, members and the move of a repository included, answer with `Quader-Authz-Epoch`
(R-API-052, R-AUTHZ-032).

Acceptance criteria:

- An Owner of `team-a` creates a policy in `POST /api/v1/projects/team-a/policies` (201) and gets 403 for
  `POST /api/v1/permission-policies` (a policy of no project).
- `GET /api/v1/projects` answers a member its own projects with its role, and the `auditor` every project. An internal user
  who is no member gets the `internal` and `public` projects without a role, and with `membership=true` none.
- An administrator creates project `team-a` and adds `user:alice` as `owner` (201); alice adds `group:team-a-devs` as
  `developer` (201), and removing herself while she is the only Owner answers 409 `last_owner`.

### R-API-048 · Package ownership surface
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

Package ownership (who may publish new versions of a package name) is owned by
[authorization.md](authorization.md):
`GET`, `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/packages/{packageName}/owners`,
`DELETE …/owners/{owner}` and `GET /api/v1/package-owners`. The package details screen
(R-UI-007) shows the owners of a package in a repository where the caller holds `read`, and offers
the owner changes to callers holding `manage`. Package names containing `/` (npm scopes) are
percent-encoded in `{packageName}` (`%40team-a%2Fui`); the router decodes the segment once.

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN" "$QUADER_URL/api/v1/projects/web/repositories/npm-local/packages/%40team-a%2Fui/owners"`
  answers 200 for a reader of `web/npm-local`.

### R-API-049 · Stored-secret key-ring status
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-016

The key ring that seals stored secrets is configured through mounted files (R-ARCH-021 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md)) and rotated in steps (R-HA-027 in
[ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md)). This requirement makes its state readable through the API, so
the UI, monitoring and an operator can check and finish a rotation without a shell in a pod, which
would expose the key files themselves (Q-API-8). `quader admin secrets status` and this endpoint
share one implementation in `internal/secrets`; this page owns the payload.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/system/encryption` | Key IDs, sealed-value counts per key ID, canary state, the key IDs every live replica holds, last re-encryption | `system.read` |
| POST | `/api/v1/system/tasks/secrets-reencrypt/run` | Start the re-encryption of R-ARCH-021 as the manual task `secrets-reencrypt` (no schedule; its job kind has the same name) through the task trigger of R-OPS-019 (Q-API-9); 202 with the job; 409 with the running job; 409 `key_ring_incompatible` while `ringsCompatible` is false | `admin` |

```json
{
  "answeredBy": "quader-api-6f9c7d8b5-x2v4q",
  "activeKeyId": "2026-10",
  "keys": [
    {"id": "2026-10", "active": true, "sealedValues": 14, "canary": "ok"},
    {"id": "2026-04", "active": false, "sealedValues": 3, "canary": "ok"}
  ],
  "replicas": [
    {"name": "quader-api-6f9c7d8b5-x2v4q", "role": "api", "activeKeyId": "2026-10", "keyIds": ["2026-04", "2026-10"]},
    {"name": "quader-worker-7d4b9c6f8-q8n2m", "role": "worker", "activeKeyId": "2026-10", "keyIds": ["2026-04", "2026-10"]}
  ],
  "ringsCompatible": true,
  "lastReencryption": {"jobId": "01933b2a-7c41-7d1e-9a52-3f0e4b8c2d11", "state": "succeeded", "finishedAt": "2026-10-28T12:40:02.118Z"}
}
```

- `activeKeyId` and `keys[].canary` are the answering replica's view, and `answeredBy` names that
  replica, as in R-OPS-004. Requests reach replicas at random, so during a rotation two refreshes
  can show different values; the UI therefore shows each replica's active key from `replicas` and
  labels the top-level values with `answeredBy`. `canary` is `ok`, `failed` or `absent` (no canary
  row for that key ID yet). `keys` lists the union of the answering
  replica's ring and every key ID that sealed values reference. `sealedValues` counts sealed values
  per key ID over every sealed column registered with `internal/secrets`, the same registry the
  re-encryption job walks.
- `replicas` comes from the replica registry (R-OPS-003 in
  [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)): each `web` and `worker`
  replica publishes its role, the key IDs of its ring and its active key ID with its heartbeat.
  Both roles open sealed values (`web` for upstream credentials on remote fetches, `worker` for
  webhook secrets and re-encryption), so both count. Lost replicas are left out. Backup and restore
  pods do not register (R-HA-003 in [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md)); a backup copies sealed
  values without the ring, and a restore checks the ring itself
  ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-020).
- `ringsCompatible` is true when every live replica's ring holds every key ID that is active on
  any live replica or referenced by a sealed value. False is the state in which a value sealed by
  one replica cannot be opened by another, for example when step 2 of R-HA-027 rolls out before
  step 1 reached every replica.
- The answer contains key IDs only: never key material, key fingerprints, ciphertext or plaintext.
- The re-encryption task refuses to start while `ringsCompatible` is false, because it would seal
  values that some replica cannot open. It needs no recent authentication: it changes no grant and
  reveals nothing. The request is audited like every write (R-API-019).
- The check is as fresh as the registry: a replica that started within the last heartbeat interval
  may not be listed yet. The start-up canary of R-ARCH-021 stays the hard guard; this endpoint and
  the task's refusal catch the mixed-ring state of a running cluster, which the canary cannot see.
- Monitoring reads the same state as metrics on the operations listener:
  `quader_secrets_sealed_values{key_id}` and `quader_secrets_key_rings_compatible` (0 or 1), defined
  by [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md).

Acceptance criteria:

- With replica A running on the old ring and replica B started afterwards with a new key active
  that A's ring lacks, `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` shows `ringsCompatible: false`, and
  `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/secrets-reencrypt/run` answers 409 `key_ring_incompatible`.
- After the rotation steps of R-HA-027 and a successful re-encryption run, `keys` reports
  `sealedValues: 0` for the old key ID, the same count that `quader admin secrets status` prints.
- No answer of the endpoint contains the base64 content of any key file.

### R-API-050 · Backup runs, status and stored backups
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-032

The backup job (INV-19) runs in the `backup` role as a Kubernetes CronJob; its runs, holds and
retention are [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) (R-BAK-009 to R-BAK-017). This
requirement owns the read-only API through which the UI (R-UI-038, R-UI-048) and scripts see them.
Every value comes from PostgreSQL (`backup_run`, `system_state`) and the replica's configuration;
`web` replicas hold no target credential and never read the target (R-BAK-015, Q-API-11).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/system/backups` | Runs, newest first; filters `operation` (`create`, `delete`, `verify`), `state`, `trigger`, `startedFrom`, `startedTo`; cursor-paged (R-API-010), `includeTotal` allowed | `settings:read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/backups/{runId}` | One run | `settings:read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/system/backups/summary` | Status of the backup job: last success, overdue, last failure, active run, stored backups and the retention that produced them, target, restore origin, manual-run command | `settings:read` |

No endpoint starts, deletes, verifies or restores a backup, in any priority (Q-API-10); a manual
run is `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/<name>`, which R-UI-048 shows. `{runId}` is a
server-generated UUID, so `summary` can never be a run; the route check of R-API-004 still lists it as a reserved name of `runId` (Q-API-204). `state`, `operation` and `trigger` are strings in the schema (Q-API-204). The `backup` block of
`/api/v1/system/info` (R-OPS-004, R-API-038) repeats the last success, the overdue mark and the
state of the newest run in short form, under the same overdue rule.

Run (an item of the list):

```json
{
  "id": "01933c4e-2f10-7b3a-9c1d-5e8f7a6b4c21",
  "operation": "create",
  "backupId": "20261028T020000Z-7f3a",
  "state": "copying",
  "trigger": "schedule",
  "pod": "quader-backup-29885880-x7k2q",
  "quaderVersion": "0.4.0",
  "target": "s3://quader-backups/quader",
  "startedAt": "2026-10-28T02:00:04.112Z",
  "heartbeatAt": "2026-10-28T02:41:19.870Z",
  "leaseExpired": false,
  "finishedAt": null,
  "snapshotAt": "2026-10-28T02:00:09.448Z",
  "progress": {"phase": "copying", "tablesDone": 41, "tablesTotal": 58, "blobsToCopy": 1204, "blobsCopied": 830, "bytesCopied": 9123456789},
  "result": null,
  "error": null
}
```

- The fields are the columns of `backup_run` (R-BAK-009) in the names of R-API-003. `target` is
  the column as recorded (bucket, prefix and endpoint host, never a credential). `pod` tells a run
  started by hand from a scheduled one, because a Job created with
  `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/…` carries the name its creator chose (R-BAK-012).
- `leaseExpired` is true for a run in an active state whose `lease_expires_at` has passed: its
  process has stopped, and the next run will mark it `abandoned` (R-BAK-010). The API never changes
  the row itself.
- `error` is the stored problem object; the UI translates its `code` (R-UI-042).

Summary:

```json
{
  "expectedIntervalSeconds": 86400,
  "lastSuccessAt": "2026-10-27T02:47:31.009Z",
  "overdue": false,
  "lastFailure": null,
  "active": {"id": "01933c4e-2f10-7b3a-9c1d-5e8f7a6b4c21", "operation": "create", "state": "copying", "startedAt": "2026-10-28T02:00:04.112Z", "leaseExpired": false},
  "target": "s3://quader-backups/quader",
  "retention": {"keepLast": 7, "keepWithinSeconds": 0},
  "storedBackups": {
    "asOf": "2026-10-27T02:47:31.009Z",
    "runId": "01933a1b-8c22-7e41-b0f3-2a6d9e4c7b10",
    "items": [
      {"backupId": "20261027T020000Z-1c9e", "snapshotAt": "2026-10-27T02:00:08.913Z", "quaderVersion": "0.4.0", "schemaStep": 42, "databaseBytes": 183500800, "blobCount": 51234, "blobBytes": 412316860416, "damaged": false}
    ]
  },
  "restoredFrom": null,
  "manualRun": {"namespace": "quader", "cronJob": "quader-backup"}
}
```

- `expectedIntervalSeconds` is `backup.expected_interval`, the value behind
  `quader_backup_expected_interval_seconds` and the alert `QuaderBackupStale` (R-BAK-014).
- `lastSuccessAt` is `finished_at` of the newest `completed` or `completed_with_warnings` create
  run. `overdue` is true when it is older than 1.5 × the expected interval, the condition on which
  `QuaderBackupStale` fires, so API, UI and alert agree. A mark at 1 × would flap on every
  schedule whose runs vary in length: a daily run that finishes a few minutes later than the day
  before is older than 24 h for those minutes. With no successful run at all, `lastSuccessAt` and
  `overdue` are `null`, and the UI shows "No backup yet" as a warning.
- `lastFailure` (`runId`, `at`, `code`) is the newest `failed` or `abandoned` create run, or an
  active create run whose lease has expired, when it is newer than the last success; `interrupted`
  runs never count, because a drain is not a failure. This is the same rule as
  `quader_backup_last_failure_timestamp_seconds` and `QuaderBackupFailed`.
- `storedBackups` and `retention` come from the newest create or delete run that listed the
  target: the complete backups it found after its own deletions, and the `keep_last` and
  `keep_within` it applied (Q-API-11; the run result's `retained` and `retention`, cross-page to
  R-BAK-016). `asOf` and `runId` name that run, so the view says how old it is. Backups written or
  removed outside Quader appear only after the next run; `quader backup list` reads the target
  itself (R-BAK-018). `null` until such a run exists. The run is the one with the newest finish
  among the 25 newest successful create and delete runs of each operation that recorded a
  `retention` (a create with `--no-prune` records none, Q-BAK-41).
- `leaseExpired` and `overdue` are judged on the database's clock (Q-API-206).
- `restoredFrom` is `system_state.restored_from` (`installationId`, `incarnation`, `backupId`,
  `snapshotAt`) after a restore (R-BAK-022), otherwise `null`.
- `manualRun` holds the namespace and the CronJob name that the chart renders into the
  configuration (`backup.manual_run`, cross-page), so the UI can show the exact command; each is
  `null` when unset.

```yaml
backup:
  manual_run:
    namespace: ""        # default (proposed): empty; the chart sets the release namespace, example: quader
    cronjob: ""          # default (proposed): empty; the chart sets <fullname>-backup, example: quader-backup
```

Acceptance criteria:

- During a run, `GET /api/v1/system/backups?state=copying` lists it with growing
  `progress.blobsCopied` (the criterion of R-BAK-009).
- With `backup.retention.keep_last: 1`, after two completed runs A and B, the summary's
  `storedBackups.items` lists B's backup only, and `storedBackups.runId` is B.
- A backup pod deleted with `--grace-period=0 --force` during `copying`: once its lease has passed,
  the run shows `leaseExpired: true`, and the summary's `lastFailure` names it, until a later run
  succeeds.
- A run ended `interrupted` by a drain, followed by a successful retry, never appears as
  `lastFailure`.
- With `backup.expected_interval: 1h` and a test clock, `overdue` is `false` 80 minutes after the
  last success and `true` at 91 minutes, the same moments at which a `promtool` test of
  `QuaderBackupStale` is silent and fires.
- `GET /api/v1/system/backups/summary` without `system.read` answers 403. No answer of these
  endpoints contains a value of the target's credentials (a test greps for the fixture's access
  key ID and secret).
- The OpenAPI document contains no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE operation under
  `/api/v1/system/backups`.

## Part C — UI

### R-UI-001 · Technology baseline and delivery
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-058

- Angular 22 (INV-1) in the workspace layout of R-ARCH-004: standalone components only, zoneless
  change detection (the default since v21), `OnPush` (the default since v22), strict TypeScript
  and strict templates, `HttpClient` on the fetch backend (the default since v22) except for
  uploads (R-UI-012). Checked on 2026-10-28 against v22 release coverage: `resource()` and
  `httpResource()`, Signal Forms and `@angular/aria` are stable or generally available in v22.
- Serving (R-ARCH-004): hashed assets with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`,
  `index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-cache` and the SPA fallback for every non-file path; the page of a package (R-UI-007) and the
  page of a file of a repository (R-UI-010) are such paths although their last segment can have a dot. A hashed asset is a file named
  `<name>-<8 characters of A–Z, a–z, 0–9, _ and ->.<extension>` in at most two plain directories below the locale
  ([Q-UI-140](#q-ui-140--which-file-names-of-the-ui-build-are-hashed)); `build:embed` fails a build whose files do not follow
  that rule. A hashed asset the replica's own build lacks, which during a rolling upgrade is one of the other release, is
  served from the shared asset store that every replica serving the UI publishes its build to ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md)
  R-HA-020, Q-HA-120), verified against its digest in every case
  ([Q-UI-143](#q-ui-143--a-file-of-the-shared-store-is-verified-whatever-storagedownloadverify-says)); an unknown one is a `404`, and one the store cannot be asked for is a `503` with `Retry-After`
  ([Q-UI-141](#q-ui-141--what-a-replica-answers-for-a-hashed-file-of-another-release)). Nothing else under `/ui/` is ever
  served from the store. This page adds:
  - the UI lives under `/ui/{locale}/` (R-UI-045); `/` redirects to `/ui/`, and `/ui/` as well as
    any `/ui/<route>` without a locale redirects to the same route under the preferred locale, so
    links such as `/ui/login?auto_sign_in=false` of [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)
    keep working;
  - `index.html` gets a per-response CSP nonce as the `ngCspNonce` attribute of the root element,
    which Angular applies to the styles it inserts;
  - the notices of the bundled software, `3rdpartylicenses.txt` in every locale directory
    (`/ui/<locale>/3rdpartylicenses.txt`, Q-UI-144): an unhashed text file, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, revalidated like
    `index.html`. The shared asset store takes only hashed files, so it never holds the notices, and every replica serves the
    notices of its own build.
- Headers for UI documents:
  `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>'; img-src 'self' data:<image origins>; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types angular angular#bundler`,
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`,
  `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`. `<image origins>` is empty by default. It holds the
  exact origins of `ui.readme.external_image_origins` (R-UI-008, Q-UI-6) and, when
  `server.content_base_url` is set (P1, R-ARCH-029 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)), that
  content origin, because README images that the renderer generates for package files are
  redirected there. Each origin is preceded by a space; no wildcard is ever emitted.
  `connect-src` stays `'self'` with or without a content origin, because the UI never reads package
  content with `fetch` or XHR (below). Without the `angular#unsafe-bypass` policy, a value marked
  trusted through `bypassSecurityTrust*` cannot reach a sink that Trusted Types guard
  ([Angular security guide](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)), and without
  `angular#components` the CDK cannot insert SVG markup. Sign-in navigates to
  `/auth/…` and the identity provider by top-level navigation, which `form-action` does not govern.
- The UI's own code and assets come from nothing but Quader's origin (fonts and icons self-hosted,
  no analytics, no CDN), so it works in air-gapped installations; the only foreign requests are
  README images from origins an operator listed (R-UI-008). From P1, with `server.content_base_url`
  set, package content opened or shown in the browser loads from Quader's content origin
  (R-ARCH-029); that origin is Quader's own, not a foreign one.
- Links to package content (R-ARCH-007, R-ARCH-029 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)):
  - The UI never assembles a `/files/` or `/api/<format>/` URL from strings. "Copy
    download URL" uses the `downloadUrl` of the item or the version file, and the UI's own downloads and file links use
    its `contentUrl`, which the session cookie authenticates on `api` (R-API-025, R-API-029, Q-UI-106); README images are the URLs the server's renderer generated through
    `LinkBuilder` (R-UI-008); registry and feed URLs come from the client setup answer
    (R-API-030). Moving content to a content origin (P1) therefore changes no UI code.
  - The UI never reads package content with `fetch` or XHR. Package content reaches the browser
    only as a navigation or an `img` load, so the content origin needs no CORS and `connect-src`
    stays `'self'`.
  - The upload of the deploy dialog (R-UI-012, P1) is not a content link but the API operation
    `PUT /files/{projectKey}/{repoKey}/{path}` of R-API-025. It always targets the UI's own origin, because the
    content origin serves only `GET` and `HEAD` (R-ARCH-029), and it is built in one place, the
    `files` client in `web/src/app/api/`, like every other API call.
- Component library (Q-UI-1, replaced by Q-UI-126): Quader's own controls, plain HTML elements with the classes of
  `web/src/styles/_controls.scss`, on the Angular CDK in the release line of the Angular major in use (22.x,
  pinned once in the lockfile with the rest of Angular) for the behaviour of dialogs, menus and overlays, plus
  `@angular/aria` for the widgets the CDK lacks (the tabs, the tree of an Ansible collection's documentation, Q-UI-241, and the listboxes of the
  member editor, R-UI-022). No other component suite is added, and `@angular/material` is not a dependency.
  Colours, type and measures are Quader's CSS custom properties (`web/src/styles/_tokens.scss`) for both themes.
  Icons come from a self-hosted icon font used through
  ligatures (`font-src 'self'`). The one exception is the icon of a package format, which is the logo of the
  format's owner where the owner's terms allow it: the owner's unchanged file under `web/public/formats/`, shown as an
  `<img>` (`img-src 'self'`) by `<quader-format-icon>` (Q-UI-225, Q-UI-226). SVG icon registration is not used,
  because it takes URLs only as `SafeResourceUrl` values from a security bypass (banned by
  R-UI-046) and inserts the SVG through the Trusted Types policy `angular#components`, which this
  CSP does not list.
- Supported browsers (UI-058): the last two major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on
  the desktop, and the current Firefox ESR. The list is published in the user documentation; other
  browsers are unsupported.
- Bundle budget: initial JavaScript at most 400 kB compressed (# default (proposed)); every feature
  is a lazily loaded route (R-ARCH-004).
- Light and dark theme through CSS custom properties, following `prefers-color-scheme` unless the
  user's preference (R-API-021) overrides it.
- Every npm dependency is pinned once in the lockfile; CI installs with `npm ci`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl -sI "$QUADER_URL/ui/en/"` shows the CSP with a nonce that differs between two requests.
- A Playwright test records every request of a full journey (with no image origins and no content
  origin configured) and finds none to a foreign origin and no `securitypolicyviolation` event.
- The same journey shows no `fetch` or XHR request to a `/files/` or `/api/<format>/` path other than
  the upload of R-UI-012.
- With `server.content_base_url: https://quader-content.example.net` (# example, P1), the CSP's
  `img-src` names `https://quader-content.example.net`, and a README with an image from its own
  package renders that image without a `securitypolicyviolation` event.
- `grep -rn "bypassSecurityTrust\|addSvgIcon" web/src` finds nothing.
- The production build fails when the initial bundle exceeds the budget.

### R-UI-002 · Application shell
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-001, UI-004

- Top bar (slim, on one fill with the side bar, Q-UI-127, in the colours of the design language, Q-UI-88): the
  mark and the product name, the search field of R-UI-095 in the middle (below 36 rem a search button,
  [Q-UI-403](#q-ui-403--below-36-rem-a-search-button-opens-the-field-as-a-sheet)), the **Admin** button (shown
  to a caller who has the admin area; it leads into it and looks the same inside it), the **Documentation** link, the
  **Downloads** button (R-UI-210, shown to a holder of `content:metadata-read`), the theme button and the user menu. The search field is shown to every signed-in caller, and to an anonymous one while something
  is `public` (R-UI-095); it offers suggestions before and while typing (R-UI-096, R-UI-097), and Enter without a picked
  suggestion opens the results page `/search?q=<text>` of the main area (R-UI-098). A search never leads into the admin area
  except by an instance administrator's choice of a suggestion marked **Admin area** (R-UI-099,
  [Q-UI-390](#q-ui-390--enter-in-the-top-bars-search-opens-a-results-page-of-the-main-area-no-search-leads-into-the-admin-area),
  the owner's rule in [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)). The **Documentation** link (R-UI-050) opens
  the manual page of the current screen, or the overview of the help area, which is titled "Documentation" like the link
  (owner, 2026-11-06; Q-UI-90). The theme button offers
  "Follow the system", "Light" and "Dark" as radio items (R-API-021); the user menu is a round 32 px avatar, the
  name in its accessible name and on top of the menu, and holds profile, client setup, language and sign-out. The
  avatar (owner, 2026-11-07: "Ich möchte, dass im Frontend eine Kopie von DiceBear mit dem Style Bottts genutzt wird, um
  Usern die noch kein Avatar hochgeladen haben, ein dynamisches zugeordnet bekommen. Wichtig ist mir hier, dass keine
  externen Quellen zur Laufzeit benötigt werden. Alles zu DiceBear muss sich zur Laufzeit bereits im web-Container
  befinden und von dort ausgeliefert werden."): a user without an uploaded avatar gets a generated robot in DiceBear's
  "Bottts" style, the same one for the same user everywhere and in every session, seeded with the user's ID
  ([Q-UI-166](#q-ui-166--the-avatar-is-seeded-with-the-id-of-the-principal)). DiceBear's core and the Bottts style are
  dependencies of the UI, bundled by its build and served by Quader with the rest of the UI; the browser renders the SVG
  itself and shows it as a data URI, and no request goes to DiceBear's HTTP service, a CDN or any other host at runtime
  ([Q-UI-167](#q-ui-167--the-robot-is-rendered-in-the-browser-from-the-bundled-bottts-style-and-loaded-as-a-lazy-chunk)). An
  uploaded avatar takes precedence over the robot (the avatar component takes an optional image URL; upload and removal
  are R-UI-051). The robot is decoration, as the letter was: `alt=""`, the name beside it names the
  button. The robot sits on the surface fill of the theme, so it reads in both colour schemes
  ([Q-UI-168](#q-ui-168--the-robot-keeps-the-badge-the-letter-had-on-the-themes-surface-fill)). The avatar is shown in the
  top bar, on the profile and on the administrator's user screen (R-UI-051); other screens get one when the reference's
  screen for them shows one and the owner asks for it. Files join the field's kinds when the items search of R-API-028
  exists (R-UI-015). The project is not
  chosen in the top bar but by the address and the project's side bar
  ([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)). A configurable server name is P2 on
  [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md).
- Navigation with three side bars, each shown while one of its routes is open (Q-UI-127, Q-UI-129): the **project**
  (`/projects/{project}/…`), the **start** (everything else outside the admin area: the list of your projects, the repositories of
  every project, the guides,
  the profile, the help, the security dashboard) and the **Admin area** (`/admin/…`, reached through the Admin button; shown
  when the caller may use one of its entries,
  [Q-UI-621](#q-ui-621--the-admin-button-is-shown-when-the-admin-area-has-an-entry-for-the-caller)). The project's side bar starts with the **project switcher**
  (the project's mark and name as a button; a panel with a search field, the recently visited projects and the matches,
  opened and closed like a disclosure, closed by Escape with the focus back on the button) and lists the project's
  screens: repositories, packages, vulnerabilities
  ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022), a folding group **Access** (members, permission
  policies, service accounts and CI identity, the last three for the holder of their capability and for the Owner of the
  project) and settings. A side bar is made of titled blocks, each a group of the navigation named by its context title (R-UI-168):
  the start side bar has the block **Your work** with Projects, Repositories (the repositories the caller can see in every project,
  R-UI-020) and Guides (R-UI-124) and the folding group **Recently opened**, the
  last five repositories the person opened (R-UI-167), and for the holder of `content:metadata-read` a second block **Security
  audit** with **Security dashboard** (R-UI-158); the admin area's one block is titled **Admin area**, a project's one block by
  its switcher. The guides also open from the user menu,
  and the client setup opens from its repository (R-UI-120). The sections are the routes of R-UI-003. Inside the admin area, the single entries
  (dashboard, upstream registries (R-UI-187), endpoints, Bastions) come first (projects and repositories are no entries of it: an
  administrator finds them where everyone does, in the main area,
  [Q-UI-1040](#q-ui-1040--projects-and-repositories-leave-the-admin-area-the-main-area-holds-what-they-held), the owner's T-25), and related screens are grouped under folding headings: identity (users, groups,
  service accounts, tokens, CI identity), access (permission policies, system roles), system (system status, audit
  log, advisory sources) and, last, settings (General, then Authentication, then Malware scanning while the malware scanning is on, then
  Signatures, the trust anchors and Quader's signing identity ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-036 and R-SIG-056), then Storage (R-UI-200);
  Q-UI-326, [Q-UI-870](#q-ui-870--malware-scanning-is-the-third-page-of-the-settings-group), read once per page load,
  [Q-UI-874](#q-ui-874--the-screens-outside-the-settings-page-read-the-switch-once-per-page-load)). Every entry has an icon, which is decoration: the label is the accessible name.
  Entries the caller may not use are hidden (R-UI-005); a group without a visible entry disappears.
- Layout and density (Q-UI-2, Q-UI-68, Q-UI-127): the navigation is a left side bar below the top bar, on the
  same fill, and the content is a panel set into them; the side bar is visible at viewport widths of 1024 CSS px and
  more, and a drawer opened from a menu button in the top bar below that width. Where it is pinned, "Collapse sidebar"
  at its foot hides it and the menu button of the top bar brings it back. A group is open until the viewer folds it, except
  **Recently opened**, which is folded until the viewer opens it (R-UI-167). The collapsed state and the
  folded and opened groups are kept in browser storage per signed-in principal (non-secret, R-UI-043) and are
  a convenience only. The active entry is marked by a tinted pill, a bar in the accent colour (blue, Q-UI-96)
  and bold text, never by colour alone. Tables, lists and form fields use compact density (the 32 px
  control height and the 16 px cell padding of Q-UI-128) on every screen; interactive targets stay at least 24 × 24 CSS px
  (R-UI-044). Screen layouts that switch between one and two columns use CSS container queries on
  the content area, so collapsing the side bar never breaks them.
- Breadcrumbs: a trail on a bar at the top of the content panel, 40 px high as the reference's (Q-UI-128), derived from the route configuration (R-UI-003) and
  not written by the screens: the area name (no link), the screen, and for a detail screen the
  object's name. The trail of a folder or a file of a repository ends at the repository, whose step stays a link; the page shows
  the folders itself (R-UI-010, Q-UI-510). A trail of one step is not shown.
- List screens: the repository, user, group, service account, token, permission policy, endpoint
  and audit log lists share one data table (bordered, growing the page with a head that scrolls with it, R-UI-215, sortable
  column headers with `aria-sort`, a "?" help tooltip on a column that needs one, loading, empty
  and error states with retry, "Load more") and one head above the table (R-UI-100): the search by name, **Filters** with the
  number of filters that are set, and the set filters as chips. **Filters** opens the filter drawer over the page (R-UI-101,
  [Q-UI-420](#q-ui-420--the-filters-of-a-list-open-in-a-drawer-from-the-right-over-the-page)): the filters open, one under the other, "Clear all", a close button, one apply button; the list keeps its width
  and its columns. A table keeps no room for a scrollbar its rows do not need, so it ends where the lines above it end
  ([Q-UI-427](#q-ui-427--a-table-keeps-no-room-for-a-scrollbar-its-rows-do-not-need)). A column is sortable only
  where the API sorts by it (`sort` of `GET /api/v1/users`, `groups`, `service-accounts`,
  `permission-policies`), or where the whole list is in the browser (endpoints); a filter appears
  only where the API takes it. The panel opens by itself while a filter is applied. The packages
  list (R-UI-006) uses the same two components. Where its columns do not fit a list stacks its rows (R-UI-174), and its head is one row of
  its sort buttons above them, so it sorts at every width ([Q-UI-391](#q-ui-391--a-stacked-list-keeps-its-sort-buttons-in-a-row-above-its-blocks)).
- User menu: profile and tokens, client setup, quick repository setup (P1; only when repositories
  may be created), language, theme, keyboard shortcuts on or off, sign out.
- The banner of `GET /api/v1/system/banner` above the content, and a notice when maintenance mode
  is active; banner text has URLs linked and nothing else interpreted; `role="region"` with an
  accessible name.
- The line of the imprint and the privacy notice at the end of the content panel, after the screen, and at the end of every screen
  that stands alone (R-UI-226); none while the installation has neither text.
- A "Skip to main content" link is the first focusable element.
- Before the session expires, a non-modal dialog warns and offers to sign in again (WCAG 2.2.1);
  timeouts are those of R-AUTH-011.

Acceptance criteria:

- A user without administrative capabilities sees no Admin button and no admin area; an administrator does.
- With the keyboard only, the first Tab focuses the skip link, and Enter moves focus to the main
  heading.
- At 1280 CSS px the side bar is visible without interaction; at 800 CSS px it is hidden and the
  header's menu button opens it as a drawer that traps focus until closed.
- Compacting the side bar at 1280 CSS px leaves only icons, every entry still has its label as
  accessible name, and the choice is still in force after a reload for the same user.
- On `/admin/users/alice` the trail reads "Admin area / Users / alice" and "Users" links to
  the list. On `/projects/web/repositories/npm-local` it reads "Projects / web / Repositories / npm-local", and no step
  links to a route that does not exist.
- Every signed-in user sees the search field (R-UI-095), and its results list only what the user may read.
- Typing `test` into the top bar's search field and pressing Enter without a picked suggestion opens `/search?q=test` in the
  main shell (no admin side bar, no admin breadcrumb); its rows link to `/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>` and
  `/projects/<project>`, and no link of the page leads into `/admin` (R-UI-098).
- The top bar shows a robot avatar for a signed-in user, the same image after a reload and for the same user on another
  replica or browser, and another image for another user; the image is a data URI, `alt=""` and hidden from assistive
  technology; while the shell renders, no request leaves the origin; the build fails if a script of the bundle names
  `api.dicebear.com` or the third-party notices lack DiceBear's licences.
