- **The table is the router's.** Every route the router opens a page on (a component, a redirect, or a guard that decides where a
  path leads) is a row, written with `{name}` for the router's `:name` and with the segments its matcher captures; a row that says
  "not built" names a route the router does not have. The UI's unit test "R-UI-003 every route of the router is a row of the route
  table, every row a route, and a row that says "not built" no route" ([app.route-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/app.route-table.spec.ts))
  loads every lazy area of the router and reads this table, and fails both ways; a route added to the router adds its row in the same
  change.
- Routes with slash-containing parameters (npm scoped names, file paths) use a router `UrlMatcher`
  that captures the remaining segments.
- A repository is named in a route by the project of the route and its key, and in a query parameter (`?repository=`)
  by the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`. The content routes live under `/projects/{project}/…`
  ([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)); `/projects/{project}`
  answers with the repositories (Q-UI-216), so that the step of the project in the breadcrumb links to a route that exists. A route
  that existed before the project was the context (`/packages`, `/browse`, `/vulnerabilities`, and since [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page) a project's `…/browse`,
  `/admin/repositories/{project}/{key}`, `/admin/projects/{project}`) is not found, and so is the admin area's `/admin/security`, since
  the security dashboard is the auditor's page `/security` (R-UI-158), and so are `/admin/projects` and `/admin/repositories` with
  every path below them, since the projects and the repositories are the main area's (`/projects`, `/repositories`, Q-UI-1040):
  no redirect leads from them.
- Route guards only shape navigation; the API decides (R-UI-005). When a screen's first API call
  answers 403, the screen shows a "no access" state with the missing permission and, for callers
  with `policies:read`, a link to the explainer.
- Every route sets a page title ("Packages – Quader") through a `TitleStrategy`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Opening `/ui/en/projects/web/packages/npm/@team-a/ui@1.3.0` in a fresh tab shows that version (R-UI-111).
- Copying the URL of a filtered packages list into another browser reproduces the filters.

### R-UI-004 · Sign-in, session and sign-out
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-006, AUTHN-037, AUTHN-038

The flow and its security properties are owned by
[identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md); the UI side:

- The UI never shows a username and password form for regular users (INV-7).
- On load the UI calls `GET /api/v1/auth/whoami`. Success starts the application. A 401 is told apart by its `code`, not by
  its status:
  - `session_expired`: the browser sent the cookie of a session that has ended, and this answer has cleared it
    ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-001, Q-AUTH-410). The UI navigates to
    `/login?returnTo=<current route>&ended=1` whatever `publicContent` says: the person believes they are signed in and is told,
    instead of running on silently as a visitor without their private projects (owner, 2026-11-19, W-21).
  - any other code (no session cookie): while `publicContent` is false the UI navigates to `/login?returnTo=<current route>`;
    while it is true (from `login-options`), the application runs anonymously with a "Sign in" button (R-UI-057).
- `ended=1` makes the sign-in screen show the fixed notice "Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue where you left
  off." above the sign-in methods; no other value shows anything, and the parameter carries no text. The screen takes the
  parameter out of the address as it opens (`replaceUrl`), so a reload does not claim the end again; `returnTo` stays. While
  `publicContent` is true the screen offers "Continue without signing in" as for every visitor, and it leads into a working
  visitor session, because the browser no longer holds the cookie (Q-UI-710, Q-UI-711).
- `/login` renders only from `GET /api/v1/auth/login-options`: one button per provider, each
  navigating (full page) to the provider's `startUrl` with `return_to` set to the UI route under the path of the page's
  resolved base (`document.baseURI`, so a relative `<base href>` counts as the browser resolves it): `/ui/en/…` and `/ui/de/…` in
  the builds per locale, `/ui/…` on the development server (UI-A-49). With
  `autoRedirect` set, the page navigates at once unless the URL carries `?auto_sign_in=false`, or carries `ended=1` while
  `publicContent` is true, where the person chooses between signing in and continuing without (Q-UI-712). The
  break-glass form appears when `localLogin` is true or the URL carries `?auto_sign_in=false`, and
  posts to the local login endpoint of the owning page. The screen stands alone, without the shell,
  in one column: the form first, then the providers below "or sign in with" (Q-UI-125).
  A login notice is P2 ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)).
- A 401 during use (expired or revoked session) opens a dialog "Your session has ended" with "Sign
  in again"; editors with unsaved changes first offer "Copy draft as JSON". "Sign in again" opens `/login?returnTo=<route>`
  without `ended=1`, since the dialog has said it. The dialog has told the person, so the next `whoami` of the tab that answers
  `session_expired` (and clears the cookie) makes a visitor, not the sign-in screen again: "Continue without signing in" from
  that screen leads into the visitor session at once (Q-UI-713). "Not now" leaves the page as it is; the next load of a page
  in the browser meets the cookie at `whoami` and takes the path above, with the notice. No second mechanism clears the cookie.
- Sign-out: `POST /auth/logout` with the CSRF header, then navigation to the returned
  `redirectTo`, or to `/logged-out`.
- `/logged-out` is where the post-logout redirect URI `<baseURL>/ui/logged-out` lands. R-AUTH-003
  and R-AUTH-013 register that URI at the identity provider, and the locale redirect of R-UI-001
  takes it to `/ui/{locale}/logged-out`. Because the URI is registered at the IdP, the route name
  is a contract: it does not follow the UI wording, whose visible text stays "Signed out". The
  page needs no session. A 401 from `whoami` on this route does not navigate to `/login`, and the
  page never sends the browser to an identity provider on its own; otherwise auto-redirect would
  sign the user straight back in while the IdP session is still alive. The page offers "Sign in
  again", which opens `/login`.
- Sign-out in one tab signs out every other tab of the same browser (`BroadcastChannel`).
- Command-line login approval (P1). The flows, the `cli_login` record and the texts are owned by
  R-AUTH-034 and R-AUTH-036 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md).
  Both screens need a session; without one the UI starts the sign-in with `return_to` set to the
  screen. Approve and deny send the CSRF header and need recent authentication (R-API-007).
  - `/cli-login/{publicId}` is the `loginUrl` that `npm login` opens. It renders
    `GET /api/v1/auth/cli-logins/{publicId}`: the client kind and registry URL; the requesting
    address, user agent and request time; the resulting token's lifetime and scope; the warning to
    approve only a login the user just started; a prominent warning when the browser's address
    differs from the requesting address; and every refused poll with its address, its time and
    the text of R-AUTH-034. While the screen is open it refreshes the record every 2 seconds, so a
    refusal before or after the decision appears without a reload; leaving the screen stops the
    refresh. "Approve" (with an optional narrower scope or shorter lifetime) and "Deny" are final.
  - `/device` is the `verification_uri` of the device flow; `verification_uri_complete` adds
    `?code=`. The screen takes the user code as R-AUTH-036 requires, then shows the same record
    plus the tool's `client_id`. When the tool asked for `self_rotatable=true`, the screen shows
    that request, explains that the token could then renew itself, and lets the approver decline
    it; the issued PAT records the outcome as `selfRotatable`.

Acceptance criteria:

- With one provider and auto-redirect, opening `/ui/en/packages` unauthenticated lands at the
  identity provider and, after login, back on `/ui/en/packages`.
- With a public project and the cookie of an ended session in the browser, opening `/ui/en/guides` lands on the sign-in screen
  with the notice "Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue where you left off." and the address
  `/ui/en/login?returnTo=%2Fguides`; "Continue without signing in" opens **Guides** as a visitor without an error, and no
  request sent after the answer of the first `whoami` carries the session cookie. The same browser without the cookie opens **Guides** directly.
  Tests: [auth-guard.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.spec.ts), [login.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/login/login.spec.ts),
  [session-store.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.spec.ts).
- Signing out in tab A shows `/logged-out` in tab B within two seconds.
- With one provider, auto-redirect on, nothing public and `rp_initiated_logout` false,
  signing out lands on `/ui/{locale}/logged-out` and stays there. The browser sends no request to
  the identity provider until the user selects "Sign in again".
- (P1) With `/ui/en/cli-login/{publicId}` open, a poll of the login's `doneUrl` from outside the
  starting network appears on the screen as a refused poll with its address within 4 seconds,
  without a reload.
- (P1) On `/ui/en/device`, approving a request with `self_rotatable=true` and declining the
  self-rotation issues a PAT whose `POST /api/v1/tokens/current/rotate` answers 403.

### R-UI-005 · Permission-driven rendering
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-005

- Authorization is enforced by the API alone; the UI adapts what it shows for convenience.
- Data: capabilities and project memberships with their roles from `GET /api/v1/authz/me` for navigation and global
  actions; per-control
  decisions from `POST /api/v1/authz/check` (up to 100 checks per call, batched per screen, cached
  for 60 seconds, dropped on any 403 and on sign-out).
- Primary actions on a screen that the caller lacks are shown disabled with the reason ("Needs
  deploy on npm-local"); menu entries the caller lacks are hidden. Lists show what the API returns.
- On a screen of a project the reason names whom to ask, the project's Owners by name ("Read only. Ask priya, an Owner of
  web-frontend, to change this."), and no capability (Q-UI-318); the administrator's screens name the capability ("Read only:
  changing this needs the permission `settings:write`").
- Self-lockout guards are shown before the API refuses them: the last administrator binding cannot
  be removed, a user cannot disable themselves, the last Owner of a project cannot be removed or demoted except by an
  administrator (R-UI-041).
- An authenticated user who can read nothing sees an empty state that names their identity and
  groups, so they can ask for access.

Acceptance criteria:

- A user without `deploy` on `npm-local` sees the deploy action disabled with its reason; forcing
  the request from the browser console answers 403.

### R-UI-006 · Packages list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-008, ART-048

- The list uses the shared data table and the shared head of a list of R-UI-100 (Q-UI-68): the search by name or description
  (`q`) is the head's field **Filter packages**, the other filters are the drawer's (R-UI-101), the sort control is a column
  header, "Load more" is the table's.
- Backed by R-API-029 (the start page of a project is its repositories, R-UI-052, Q-UI-216). Filters of the drawer: package type
  (multi-select), repository (multi-select), keyword, created period (last 7, 30, 90 days, custom; a custom end day is included).
  The filters that are set appear as removable chips beside **Filters** (Q-UI-422) and live in the URL.
- Table (Q-UI-314): the package (its name, with its description as the muted second line, never cut), its format (icon plus
  text, never icon alone; the icon is the format owner's logo where the owner's terms allow it, else the neutral package
  glyph, Q-UI-225), **Latest**, the latest version (the word of a repository's package table,
  [Q-UI-432](#q-ui-432--the-package-list-says-latest-as-the-package-table-of-a-repository-does)), updated (relative, with the
  absolute time in a `<time datetime>` element and its title, R-UI-103). The number of versions, of repositories, the downloads and the first publication are on the package's page (its
  Details). Sortable by the package and updated in the headers; the sort by first created stays the API's and a saved view's
  (`sort=createdAt`). Every sort is the server's (R-API-029).
- Paging with an explicit "Load more" button; no infinite scroll.
- Tabs: all packages; recently opened (last 10 opened, browser storage keyed by user, Q-UI-323); saved views
  (at most 8, browser storage; rename, delete, make default; a list opened without any query applies the
  default view once). Browser storage access is wrapped so that blocked storage only hides these tabs.
  The tab is the `tab` query parameter.
- Each row is a link, so it opens in a new tab with the usual browser gestures.
- Empty states: no packages at all (link to client setup); no match (clear filters).

Acceptance criteria:

- After publishing three npm packages and one NuGet package, `format=nuget` shows one row, and
  reloading the page keeps the filter.
- With browser storage disabled, the page works and the two browser-storage tabs are hidden.

### R-UI-007 · A package's page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-009, ART-049

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-7): a package's page is its versions. A version has a page of its own (R-UI-111).

- `/packages/{format}/{name…}` resolves through `GET /api/v1/packages/lookup`; the name keeps its slash
  as a path separator (`/packages/npm/@team-a/ui`) and is one breadcrumb step (Q-UI-73).
- Header: the name, the format (its icon of Q-UI-225 and its name), the package's description (the latest version's) as the muted
  sentence, the number of versions and the latest version as a link to its page. For an image the number counts its tags and says so
  ("204 tags · Latest 5.4.7"), while the table lists its images (R-UI-110, Q-UI-1130).
- Then the versions as one table (R-UI-110), then the README of the latest version under the heading "README of <version>"
  (R-UI-008; not requested when the latest version has none for the caller, R-UI-057). For the format `ansible`, whose README is
  the first page of its documentation (R-UI-060), a link "Documentation of <version>" to the version page's Documentation tab
  stands there instead.
- **Details** at the end of the page, closed (Q-UI-322): the repositories that hold the package (each a link to its page), its
  keywords, its downloads and when it was first published.
- No tabs, no version select and no pre-release switch: what the tabs **Metadata**, **Files** and **Repositories** showed belongs
  to one version and is on its page ([Q-UI-458](#q-ui-458--the-tabs-metadata-files-and-repositories-become-the-version-pages-details-and-files)).
- Opening the page records it in "recently opened" (Q-UI-323).
- **The same page for every class.** A package a remote repository cached shows the description, the README and, on its version's page, the
  facts a published one shows, in every format (R-API-029). Where the format's job describes a cached version after the fill (npm
  R-NPM-050, Debian R-DEB-037), a page opened in the seconds before shows the version without them and reads it again by itself
  (R-UI-213).
- Links taken from package metadata (npm `homepage`, `repository.url`, `bugs.url`; NuGet
  `projectUrl`, `licenseUrl`, the `repository` URL) MUST be rendered as links only when their
  scheme is `http` or `https`, with `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"`; any other value is shown
  as text. Package authors set these values, and Angular's URL sanitizer is a second layer, not
  the rule. They are on the version's page.

Acceptance criteria:

- For `@team-a/ui` with versions `1.3.0`, `1.4.0` and `1.5.0-beta.1`, the page lists all three, `1.5.0-beta.1` first with the
  marks `next` and **Pre-release**, `1.4.0` with `latest`; the header's latest version is `1.4.0`.
- The README of `1.4.0` follows the table; `left-pad`, whose version has none, shows none and requests none.
- A package whose `homepage` is `javascript:alert(1)` shows the value as text on its version's page, and no `a` element carries it.

### R-UI-008 · Sanitized README rendering
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-009

Rendering happens on the server (R-API-029), so one renderer and one sanitizer policy serve every
client.

- Markdown is CommonMark plus GitHub-style tables, strikethrough, autolinks and task lists. Raw HTML
  inside Markdown passes through the sanitizer.
- Sanitizer allowlist (normative minimum):

| Allowed | Rule |
|---|---|
| Elements | `h1`–`h6`, `p`, `br`, `hr`, `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `dl`, `dt`, `dd`, `pre`, `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `em`, `strong`, `del`, `ins`, `sup`, `sub`, `a`, `img`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td`, `details`, `summary`, and disabled task-list checkboxes |
| `href` on `a` | Schemes `http`, `https`, `mailto`, and in-page `#` fragments; relative links that cannot be resolved are reduced to their text; links get `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"` and no `target` |
| `img` | `src` per the image policy (Q-UI-6): an `https` image whose origin is listed in `ui.readme.external_image_origins` is kept (the UI document's `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` of R-UI-001 keeps the page URL, which names the package, from reaching that host); every other external image is replaced by a link "External image: <alt>"; `data:` sources dropped; sources that resolve to Quader's own origin, relative or absolute, dropped as well, except image URLs the renderer itself generates for files embedded in the package, so a README cannot make the viewer's browser send authenticated requests to package or file endpoints ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-008). The renderer builds those URLs only through `LinkBuilder` ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-007), never from strings, so from P1 a content origin (R-ARCH-029) receives them without a renderer change; `alt`, `width`, `height` |
| `id`, `name` | Kept only when prefixed `user-content-` (prevents DOM clobbering) |
| `class` | Only `language-*` on `code` |
| Table attributes | `align` with `left`, `center`, `right`; `colspan`, `rowspan` |
| `open` on `details` | Kept |

  Everything else is removed: `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `form`, `input` (except
  the checkboxes above), `svg`, `math`, `base`, `meta`, `link`, `style` attributes, event-handler
  attributes, and `javascript:`, `vbscript:` and `data:` URLs.
- Limits: source at most `ui.readme.max_source_bytes`, rendered HTML at most 1 MiB, rendering at most
  2 seconds; beyond that the README is truncated with a notice. These limits come on top of the
  limits for untrusted package content of R-ARCH-028.
- The client binds the HTML with `[innerHTML]`, so Angular's sanitizer runs a second time; the
  Trusted Types CSP of R-UI-001 is the third layer. That second layer removes every `id` and `name`
  and does not know `vbscript:`; the component therefore finishes the job after binding: it drops a link
  target that is not a fragment, `http`, `https` or `mailto`, drops an image whose source is neither
  `https` nor a path of this origin, sets `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"` and no `target` on every
  link that leaves Quader, and derives the anchor `user-content-<slug>` of every heading itself, with the
  rule of the server's renderer (lower case, punctuation removed, spaces to hyphens, a repeated name
  numbered `-1`, `-2`), so that the table-of-contents links the server wrote resolve (Q-UI-71). The server
  and the component implement one rule, JavaScript's `trim`, `\s` and `toLowerCase`, and test one corpus
  (Q-UI-76).
- In-page links to `#user-content-…` scroll within the README and never navigate (the document's
  `<base href>` would turn a bare fragment into a navigation to the UI root); code blocks scroll
  horizontally and take focus.
- Libraries (pinned once in `go.mod`): [goldmark](https://github.com/yuin/goldmark) for Markdown
  and [bluemonday](https://github.com/microcosm-cc/bluemonday) for sanitizing.
- External image origins (Q-UI-6) are exact `https` origins (scheme, host, optional port; no
  path, no wildcard), validated at start-up; an invalid entry stops start-up, and so does an entry that
  is an origin of this installation (`server.base_url`, `additional_base_urls`, an endpoint's `base_url`):
  an image from it would make the viewer's browser send authenticated requests to Quader. Images of files
  embedded in the package (rendered through `LinkBuilder`) are P1 (R-ARCH-029) and not built. The same list feeds
  the sanitizer and the CSP `img-src` of R-UI-001, so the two can never disagree. Because the
  rendered HTML depends on the list, the README cache of R-API-029 stores the list's hash and
  re-renders when it changes.
- Package images (P1, R-ARCH-029): with `server.content_base_url` set, a browser's request for an
  image the renderer generated is redirected to the content origin, which the CSP `img-src` of
  R-UI-001 then lists. The list of external image origins above is unaffected; the content origin
  is never entered there.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  readme:
    max_source_bytes: 512KiB          # default; 1KiB to 16MiB
    external_image_origins: []        # default: every external image becomes a link
    # external_image_origins: ["https://img.shields.io", "https://gitlab.example.com"]   # example
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A fixture corpus of XSS vectors (script tags, event-handler attributes, `javascript:` links, SVG
  with script, `<form>`, `<base>`, `<style>`, `id="__proto__"`) rendered by the server contains none
  of them in executable form; a Playwright test displays each fixture and observes no dialog, no
  request to a foreign origin and no CSP violation.
- A README with a badge image from `https://img.shields.io` shows "External image: build status" as
  a link while `external_image_origins` is empty; with that origin listed, the image loads, the
  UI's CSP names exactly that origin in `img-src`, and an image from an unlisted host in the same
  README is still a link.
- A README containing `![x](/api/npm/web/npm-remote/left-pad)` or
  `<img src="https://quader.example.com/files/web/generic-local/x.png">` renders without an `img`
  element for either source, and viewing it causes no request to those paths.

### R-UI-009 · Install command panel
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-010

*Revised on 2026-11-25 (the owner, W-30, [Q-UI-1240](#q-ui-1240--the-panel-of-a-versions-commands-is-a-tab-per-client-and-set-up-client-at-the-rows-end),
[Q-UI-1241](#q-ui-1241--a-versions-page-has-its-command-behind-the-verbs-button-in-its-head-the-box-is-gone)):* the panel is the
panel of the verb's button (R-UI-052, [client-command-menu.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.ts)), in a
repository's list and in the head of the version's page; no box of a command stands on any page.

- A tab per client of the format (Docker | Podman; npm | pnpm | Yarn Berry | Yarn Classic; .NET CLI | NuGet CLI | Visual Studio; curl | wget |
  PowerShell), in the order of the setup's clients, each named by the client's short name; a format of one client (APT, ansible-galaxy)
  shows the client's name as the row's label instead of a strip of one tab. At the end of the row **Set up client**, which opens the
  client setup of the repository with the chosen client (R-UI-126). A repository picker (a select **Repository** above the row) when
  the version exists in more than one repository a client can use (default: a virtual repository containing it, else the first local
  one); the command and the setup follow it.
- A repository the version is not `available` through (R-API-029: disabled, or a virtual one that reaches it only through disabled
  members) is never offered; a version that only disabled repositories hold gets one muted sentence instead of the command, naming
  them: "The repository web/npm-local is disabled: nobody can install this version until it is enabled again."
  ([Q-UI-965](#q-ui-965--a-disabled-repository-offers-no-download-address-or-command-and-says-why-once)).
- The command comes from the install snippet of R-API-030 with package and version, requested with
  `credentials=none` (the install command carries no credentials). A command of one line is an address field of R-UI-065
  with its joined copy button; a command of several lines is a code block with its copy button (Q-UI-320); either way a
  live region announces "Copied". The tabs list the clients of the format that the UI has instructions for (Q-UI-70).
- A client with several forms of installing the package (NuGet's, [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-037) has a select
  **Form** above its command, the server's first form by default
  ([Q-UI-1360](#q-ui-1360--many-forms-of-installing-a-package-the-clients-stay-the-tabs-a-select-form-stands-in-a-clients-tab)); the
  version's `kind` (a .NET tool, a template, an MSBuild SDK) decides which clients are tabs and which forms each answers.
- Every client's command is in the panel, the ones not chosen hidden, so the panel is as wide as its longest command (24 to 48 rem,
  never wider than the window less 16 px each side) and switching tabs moves nothing; a one-line command is read in full where there
  is room (Q-UI-455, revisits Q-UI-320). Where the row has no room for the tabs and **Set up client** (npm's four at 390 px), the
  button goes to a line of its own under the tabs, at its end.
- npm and NuGet install commands carry no credentials; **Set up client** opens the page of the chosen repository with the chosen
  client for configuring the client once.
- Commands longer than three lines are folded after the third with an expander: the fold cuts the rest, it does not scroll it, and an
  unfolded command, or a short one, is as tall as its lines wrap to (R-UI-215).

Examples: `npm install @team-a/ui@1.4.0`, `dotnet add package Contoso.Logging --version 2.3.1`,
`<PackageReference Include="Contoso.Logging" Version="2.3.1" />`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Copying the npm command for `@team-a/ui@1.4.0` and running it in a project configured by the
  client setup installs that version.
- Unit ([client-command-menu.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.spec.ts),
  [package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts), milliseconds): npm's panel has the tabs npm,
  pnpm, Yarn Berry, Yarn Classic and **Set up client** to `…/npm-local/setup?client=npm`; the tab Yarn Berry shows `yarn add
  @team-a/ui@1.4.0` and the setup with `client=yarn`, and the panel opens again on it; Debian's panel names APT and has no tablist; a
  version in `web/npm-all` and `web/npm-local` offers both, the virtual one first.
- Rendered (rule 11): at 1440 px the command `npm install image-convert-tools@4.0.1` is shown whole, and its field ends within a
  few characters of the command's end; the panel of every format at 390, 1,024 and 1,440 px, in English and German.

### R-UI-052 · Repository content page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

`/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}` is what a repository holds, on the logical level (Q-UI-216), and the one way to its
folders and files (`…/{key}/files/{path…}`, R-UI-010, [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page));
its settings moved to `…/settings`. One shell serves every format; what differs per format is a small table of words and columns,
not a screen per format ([content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts)).

- Header (the shared page header of R-UI-067): the key (the `h1`), one muted sentence (the repository's description, else what
  the class means), the format and the class as badges (and **Disabled** for a disabled repository); a repository of a system-only
  format has the badge **System** with its sentence as the tooltip, and its header's sentence is "Filled by this installation itself,
  on a schedule; nobody publishes to it." in place of its description, which is the product's and names the format the badge beside
  it names (Q-UI-1203); no address field: the client
  address is Set up client's (R-UI-169, [Q-UI-664](#q-ui-664--the-repositorys-header-leads-to-set-up-client-and-holds-no-address)).
  At the right, the page's actions: **Set up client** (R-UI-126; not for a disabled repository), **Settings** for a
  caller who can read the configuration (`repositories:read-config`, or the Owner of the project) and a `more_vert` menu with
  **Files** (every format but generic, whose content is its files, Q-UI-511) and **Vulnerabilities** (not for generic and virtual).
- Where the content is narrow, the actions go under the heading, the sentence and the badges, on one line.
- Tabs under the header, each with its address (`tab-nav`, links with `aria-current="page"`): the content (captioned Images,
  Packages or Files) at `…/repositories/{key}`; for a remote repository the tabs of [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-018
  (the owner's word of 2026-11-23, Q-CUR-1), **Upstream** and **Downloads**, for every signed-in reader (a visitor without a session
  has neither, [Q-CUR-150](remote-curation.md#q-cur-150--the-strip-holds-the-content-upstream-and-downloads-for-every-signed-in-reader-the-strip-counts-the-open-requests-itself));
  and **Details** at `…/repositories/{key}/details`, always the last, on a repository of every format and class that has details
  for its reader (the owner's word of 2026-11-24, [Q-UI-1067](#q-ui-1067--details-is-the-last-tab-of-a-repositorys-page-not-a-section-under-its-list)).
  One tab is no strip (Q-UI-652): a repository whose page would have only its content (a local generic repository) shows none, and
  the address of a tab the page does not have leads to its content. **Set up client** opens the repository's page Set up client
  (`…/repositories/<key>/setup`, R-UI-120); it is the page's one way to the setup (Q-UI-321).
- A package format (npm, NuGet, OCI, Debian, every format with a view adapter) lists its items from `GET /api/v1/packages` with
  `repository=<qualified name>` and `format=<format>`, the filter `q` (query, server-side, name and description; a field as wide as
  a name, Q-UI-520) and the sort `name` or `updatedAt`, paged with "Load more". The column **Vulnerabilities** appears only for a
  format whose versions are matched against advisories (`FormatDescriptor.vulnerabilityScanning`, a format with the vulnerability
  adapter, R-VULN-009, or the image scanning, R-VULN-033) and only when the answer carries grades (Q-UI-377); for a format that is not
  scanned a muted sentence says so (Debian today). It shows the grade of the item's latest version in this repository
  (`vulnerabilityGrade` from `include=vulnerabilities`, R-VULN-039, Q-VULN-154) as `<quader-grade>` (R-UI-094) and sorts by grade
  (`sort=grade`, worst first as `-grade`, in the browser, Q-UI-373). The versions list of an item is `…/versions?repository=…` with its
  `…/vulnerabilities?repository=…` report, one request each per opened item.
- The row of an item opens in place (`collapse-region`) to its ten newest versions, newest first by the format's order (R-API-029),
  under a head of their own, with no scroll and no "Load more"; where the item holds more, a link under them, **All 103 tags** or **All 33
  versions** (the count of the row), leads to the table of the package's versions (its page, or `…/-/versions` where the package's page is
  its newest version, R-UI-218), which lists every version with filter, sort and "Load more" (R-UI-110,
  R-UI-215, [Q-UI-1111](#q-ui-1111--an-opened-item-shows-its-ten-newest-versions-and-links-all-of-them)). For an image the ten are its
  newest images (`group=content`, one row per manifest, the owner's word of 2026-11-25,
  [Q-UI-1130](#q-ui-1130--an-image-is-one-row-with-its-tags-on-the-opened-item-and-on-the-packages-page)): the leading tag as the link,
  **Pre-release** where it is one, the image's other tags muted after it (at most four, then "+N more"), the signature badge (R-SIG-035),
  the digest (which the list by content always carries), size and pushed (or fetched) time of the leading tag, and **Pull** of the leading
  tag; the tags that are no version (`latest`, `sha-…`) lead an image only when no version tag names it, below the versions by their time.
  A page of the list by content may be short or empty with a cursor; the item reads on until it has its ten or the list ends, at most
  eight requests (R-API-010). For an image the link stands where the list goes on or a row leaves a tag out, and the tags stand as
  [Q-UI-1150](#q-ui-1150--an-images-tags-are-one-line-of-facts-after-the-leading-tag-and-a-line-each-in-a-block) says. While a version
  shown waits for its scan (queued, scanning), the item reads its versions and grades again every 3 s
  ([Q-UI-1151](#q-ui-1151--an-opened-item-reads-its-versions-again-every-3-s-while-one-it-shows-waits-for-its-scan)). For a package, its
  versions with size and published time. Each row with the grade of its version in this repository.
  No box of a command stands in the list. At the end of each version's row, and of each item's row for its latest version, a button
  with the format's client verb and a chevron (**Pull** for an image, **Install** for a package, **Download** for a file;
  [Q-UI-1066](#q-ui-1066--a-versions-commands-are-a-menu-hung-from-a-button-with-the-formats-client-verb)) opens a panel hung from the
  button, as GitLab's **Code** menu: a tab per client of the format, then free room and **Set up client** at the row's end, and under
  the row the chosen client's command as a read-only field with its joined copy button (a command of several lines as the snippet's
  window); a format of one client names it as the row's label (R-UI-009,
  [Q-UI-1240](#q-ui-1240--the-panel-of-a-versions-commands-is-a-tab-per-client-and-set-up-client-at-the-rows-end)). A command is the install
  snippet of R-API-030 for this repository and that client (`credentials=none`, so it never holds a token), asked when the menu
  opens: `docker pull`/`podman pull` with this installation's real address for OCI, the install command of the format elsewhere.
  The menu is a non-modal dialog named by the verb, the item and the version; it takes the focus, keeps Tab inside, and Escape, a
  click outside and the button close it with the focus back on the button; as wide as its longest command (24 to 48 rem, Q-UI-455) and never wider than the window less
  16 px each side. A system repository that answers no client and a disabled repository have no such button (Q-UI-898, Q-UI-965).
  The item's name links to the package's page (R-UI-007; for a format that leads with its documentation the page of its newest version,
  R-UI-218), a version's name to the version's page (R-UI-111). A long name wraps inside
  itself beside its chevron, and its row starts where its neighbours do (Q-UI-520).
- A generic repository's content is its files: the page is the root folder of R-UI-010, and a folder or a file is the page at
  `…/files/{path…}`. A package format's raw files are a detail on demand: **Files** in the header's menu opens their root (`…/files`)
  with a way back to the list and a sentence that says what they are (Q-UI-511).
- A virtual repository shows what it resolves: the same list, whose `repository` filter expands to its members (R-API-029). A remote repository
  lists what it holds: what the format has stored for it (a cached npm or NuGet version, for example); a note says that only what
  clients have fetched appears. An OCI remote lists the images and tags its cache holds, from the same list API as a local one
  (R-OCI-036, Q-OCI-215): the note says that only the cached tags appear (those clients pulled and those a mirror pass fetched), the
  column of the tag's time is **Fetched** and not Pushed, and an empty remote says that it has cached no images yet (Q-UI-217).
- The tab **Details** (Q-UI-1067) holds, each under its name, what the repository has of these: the raw file address, labelled
  **Address for downloads by path (curl, wget)** with its copy button (the API's `addresses` list the format's protocol address
  first and the raw file address after it where the two differ, R-REPO-002; the UI labels by that order and names no path of its own,
  R-ARCH-007; for the full document of R-REPO-010 the UI builds the two addresses from the catalog in that order), **Caches** with the
  upstream a remote repository caches (its URL), and **Resolves from** with the members a virtual repository resolves from, each
  linked to its content page as far as the caller may read them (the consumer view of R-REPO-010 has neither). The tab exists when the
  repository has one of them for its reader.
- An empty repository says what fills it and for whom, and offers no button: **Set up client** is the header's (R-UI-144,
  Q-UI-555). A caller who may publish reads "This repository holds no packages yet. Publish a package with your client; Set up
  client shows how." (push an image; upload files), anyone else who fills it, a remote repository that it fills as clients fetch
  through it; where the folder's toolbar offers **Upload files** (R-UI-011) the sentence names the upload, and a disabled
  repository says only that it is empty. Without a description the header's sentence says what the class means; for a
  local repository "Holds what is published to it."
- Opening the page records it in the recently opened repositories of the browser (R-UI-020), which the side bar's **Recently
  opened** shows (R-UI-167).

Acceptance criteria:

- `/projects/web` opens the repositories of the project; the sidebar lists Repositories first; the project switcher and the start page lead there.
- `/projects/web/repositories/<oci-key>` lists the images; opening one shows one row per manifest, led by its highest tag with the other
  tags muted after it, with digest, size and pushed time, and a row's
  **Pull** opens a panel with the tabs **Docker** and **Podman** and **Set up client**, each tab a copyable
  `docker pull <host>/web/<oci-key>/<image>:<tag>` or `podman pull …`; Escape closes it and the focus is on **Pull** again.
- `/projects/web/repositories/<oci-remote-key>`, after a pull through it, lists the pulled image with its tag, the digest and a **Fetched** time; before any pull it says
  that the repository has cached no images yet (R-OCI-036, Q-UI-217).
- `/projects/web/repositories/<npm-key>` lists the packages with the grade of their latest version, and a version's **Install**
  shows `npm install <name>@<version>` in its tab **npm**; a reader without `repositories:read-config` sees no Settings action.
- `/projects/web/repositories/<npm-key>` has the tabs **Packages** and **Details**; `…/details` shows the address for downloads by
  path, and a remote repository's strip reads **Packages**, **Upstream**, **Downloads**, **Details**.
- The Edit action of the repository list and the Settings action of the content page open `…/settings`, and leaving it with unsaved changes asks first.
- A generic repository shows its files; a folder's name leads to `…/files/<folder>` and a file's name to `…/files/<path>`.
- The client address and **Set up client** stand on one line of the header at 1440 px.

### R-UI-010 · Files of a repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-011, ART-040, ART-041

The folders and files of a repository are pages of the repository
([ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page), owner, 2026-11-18): there is no screen of their
own and no tree across the repositories of a project.

- Addresses ([Q-UI-510](#q-ui-510--a-folder-and-a-file-are-the-repositorys-page-at-files-and-their-path)): a folder or a file is
  `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/files/{path…}`, the path with its slashes; `…/files` alone is the root. For a generic
  repository the root is the repository's own address, which every link to it uses. The page of a folder or a file is named after
  it (the document title); the breadcrumb ends at the repository's key, which stays a link, so the path stands on the page once.
  The address is bookmarkable, and a reload shows the same folder or file.
- The page keeps the repository's header (R-UI-052). Below it, for a path that is not the root (and for a package format's root),
  the path, the one place that names the folders and the file ([Q-UI-521](#q-ui-521--the-path-of-a-folder-or-a-file-stands-once-and-its-middle-folders-collapse-where-it-is-narrow)): **Files**, then each folder as a link,
  the last segment the page itself (`aria-current`) with a quiet copy button for the path right after it. A separator stays with
  the segment before it, so no line starts with one; a long name wraps at its hyphens. Where the path's row is narrower than
  64 rem, the folders between **Files** and the last segment collapse into one button, **Show the folders in between**, whose
  menu lists them as links.
- A folder lists its children through `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/children` (R-API-025) as the shared
  data table: **Name** (the icon of a folder or of a file, one each, an archive included, on the name's first line; a long name
  wrapping beside it), **Size** (files),
  **Last change** as the shared relative time with the absolute time as its title (Q-UI-518), and for a file a quiet copy button for
  its download address (the repository's address for downloads by path and the file's path); in a generic repository a file's row has
  instead the verb's button **Download** with the panel of its address and every client's command (R-UI-218,
  [Q-UI-1335](#q-ui-1335--a-generic-files-row-has-download-with-its-panel-where-a-packages-row-has-its-verb)). A name is a link to the folder's or the
  file's page. Entries load in pages of `ui.browser.page_size` with **Load more**
  ([Q-UI-513](#q-ui-513--a-folder-loads-in-pages-of-200-and-its-filter-says-when-it-has-not-seen-every-entry)); the field **Filter
  files** narrows the loaded entries and says so while more are to load.
- A file's page ([Q-UI-514](#q-ui-514--a-files-page-is-its-name-download-its-address-and-its-facts-the-rest-is-details)): the file's
  name with its icon is the last segment of its path, and **Download** (through the content route, R-API-025) and, for a holder of
  `delete`, **Delete** stand at the end of that row; the name is not repeated as a heading (the section's `h2` is for assistive
  technology only). In a generic repository **Download** is the main act of a split button whose chevron opens the panel of the
  file's address and its clients' commands, each with the check of the download
  ([formats/generic.md](formats/generic.md) R-GENERIC-017, [Q-UI-1330](#q-ui-1330--a-generic-files-download-is-a-split-button-the-browser-download-first-the-clients-commands-behind-the-chevron));
  for a package format's raw file, below: the download address as an address field. Then
  the facts **Size**, **Media type** (a word a person knows where the product has one, the media type beside it,
  [Q-UI-1333](#q-ui-1333--a-files-media-type-reads-as-a-word-with-the-type-beside-it)), **Created**, **Last changed** (each with who, where known) and **SHA-256** (its short form, the
  full value as the title, a copy button); a missing or damaged content says so under **Content**. **Details**, closed: every checksum
  (SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1, MD5) with a copy button, the download statistics (**Downloads**, **Last download**, **Last downloader**,
  read when Details opens), the item as the API describes it and the equivalent `curl` requests (INV-17), which call the function `quader_curl`
  and so never name the token ([Q-UI-1336](#q-ui-1336--a-command-keeps-its-credential-off-the-command-line-where-the-client-can-and-says-so-where-it-cannot)). A file of a disabled
  repository, which answers every download 404 (R-REPO-005), has no **Download**, no download address and no download with `curl`;
  one muted sentence says why where the address stood, and its folder's rows have no address to copy and no image or version a
  button **Pull** or **Install** ([Q-UI-965](#q-ui-965--a-disabled-repository-offers-no-download-address-or-command-and-says-why-once)). Properties (P1, R-API-026)
  and Effective permissions (P1, R-API-034) are not built yet. The link from a file to its package version appears when the API
  reports one; it reports none today (`package` is always null).
- What a plain reader sees: the list, a folder, a file, Download and the copy buttons. Every operation of R-UI-011 is offered only to
  the caller who may use it there ([Q-UI-512](#q-ui-512--the-operations-stand-where-they-act-and-only-for-who-may-use-them)).
- Empty states: an empty folder ("This folder is empty."), an empty repository (R-UI-052), a filter that matches nothing, and a path
  that does not exist or that the caller may not read (the not-found notice of the API's answer).

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  browser:
    page_size: 200   # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With the keyboard only, a user opens a generic repository, reaches `releases/1.0/app.zip` through the folders' names, and
  downloads it.
- A folder with 1,000 files shows the first 200 and loads the rest with **Load more**.
- A reader sees no Upload files, New folder or Delete on any page of a repository.

### R-UI-011 · Item actions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-012, UI-016

| Action | Applies to | Where | Needs | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Download | File | the file's page | `read` | MVP |
| Copy the download address | File | the folder's list (each file) and the file's page | `read` | MVP |
| Copy path | Folder, file | the trail | `read` | MVP |
| Upload files, New folder | A folder (the root too) of a local repository of the raw-files family (R-API-025) | the folder's toolbar | `deploy` | P1 (built) |
| Delete | A file, a folder (not the root) of a local or remote repository | the file's page; **Delete folder** in the folder's **More actions for this folder** menu | `delete` | MVP |
| Client setup | Repository | the header (R-UI-052) | `read` | MVP |
| Copy, move | File, folder | the file's page, the folder's toolbar (R-UI-013) | R-API-027 | P1 (not built: R-STOR-019 is not built) |
| Edit properties | File, folder | the file's Details | `annotate` | P1 (not built) |
| Reindex | Repository | its settings (R-UI-087) | `manage` | P1 (built for Debian, **Rebuild all indexes**; the API also rebuilds Ansible, the other formats answer `405`) |
| Invalidate cache (scope metadata, negative or all, R-API-024) | Remote or virtual repository | its settings | `manage` | MVP (no control yet) |

- What the caller may do is one batched check at the page's path (R-UI-005: `deploy`, `overwrite`, `delete`), cached by the session.
  A disabled repository offers no operation. Every action is a button with a visible label; none is reached through right-click alone.
- Deleting a file asks for confirmation naming the path. Deleting a folder shows the number of items; above 100 items the user
  types the folder name to confirm. When the trash can is enabled (R-UI-014, not built), the dialog says the items go there for
  the retention period; today it says they are deleted for good. After a delete the page shows the folder above; a folder delete
  that runs as a job shows the job's progress there (R-UI-042), and the list reloads when the job has ended.

Acceptance criteria:

- Deleting a folder with 150 items requires typing its name; the folder above no longer lists it after the job succeeds.
- An Owner of the project sees **Upload files** and **New folder** above a folder of a generic local repository and **Delete folder**
  in the folder's menu; a reader of the same project sees none of them.

### R-UI-012 · Deploy dialog
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-013

- Opened by **Upload files** of a folder's toolbar (R-UI-011), in a local repository of the raw-files family where the caller
  holds `deploy`. npm, NuGet, OCI and Debian repositories take no raw upload (R-API-025) and offer none: their clients publish, and
  **Set up client** says how. An Ansible Galaxy repository takes none either; its collections are published on the screen with
  **Upload collection**, which runs the client's publish ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-061), in the same place of the
  toolbar ([Q-UI-1320](#q-ui-1320--upload-collection-stands-in-the-toolbar-of-the-collections-where-upload-files-stands)).
- Fields: target folder (prefilled with the page's folder, relative to the root; missing folders are created), files (a drop zone plus
  a "Choose files" button, so dragging is never required), overwrite (only with `overwrite`).
- The size limit `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` is checked before the upload starts; larger files are
  pointed to native clients or `curl`.
- Uploads use `PUT /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}` on the UI's own origin (R-API-025, Q-UI-106), built by the `files` client of `web/src/app/api/` (R-UI-001), never by the dialog. Because the fetch backend reports no upload
  progress, uploads go through an XHR-based `HttpClient` instance (`withXhr()`) to show progress.
  This is the only XHR use for content, and it writes; the UI never reads package content with
  `fetch` or XHR (R-UI-001).
- Files up to 256 MiB are hashed in the browser (Web Crypto SHA-256) and sent with `Repr-Digest`;
  larger files rely on the server's own digest.
- Several files upload one after another with per-file status; "Cancel" aborts the current one. Closing the dialog after an upload
  reloads the folder's list.
- An upload cut without an answer (a drain that reaches the shutdown deadline, R-API-051, Q-ARCH-18
  in [architecture.md](architecture.md)) has stored nothing ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-004).
  The dialog sends it once more from the start through the Service, from the `File` object it
  still holds; a raw deploy of identical content to the same path is idempotent. If the retry
  answers that the path exists, the dialog compares the item's SHA-256 with the digest it computed
  and reports success when they match.

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  deploy:
    max_upload_bytes: 100MiB      # default; 0 = unlimited
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Uploading a 10 MiB file shows progress and ends with the file in the folder's list; a file above the limit
  is refused before any request.

### R-UI-013 · Copy and move dialog
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-014

Not built: the operations of R-API-027 and R-STOR-019 do not exist yet, so the pages offer no **Copy** and no **Move**. When they are
built, the dialog is this ([Q-UI-515](#q-ui-515--a-copy-or-a-move-chooses-its-target-repository-from-a-list-and-its-folder-by-browsing-it)):

- Opened by **Copy** or **Move** of a file's page or of a folder's toolbar, for a holder of `read` (copy) or `delete` (move) on the
  source.
- Target repository: a select of the repositories the caller may deploy to (same format, or generic; local, or virtual with a
  default deployment target, R-STOR-019), the source's own repository first, the others grouped by project.
- Target folder: the folders of the chosen repository, browsed in the dialog one level at a time from its root (the children of
  R-API-025, folders only), and a path field that takes a typed path too; default: the source's folder. A live preview names the
  resulting full path (`<project>/<repo>/<path>`).
- Conflict handling (overwrite, with `overwrite`), **Dry run** showing the report of `/api/v1/content/copy` or `/move`, then **Copy**
  or **Move**. Large operations show job progress (R-UI-042).

Acceptance criteria:

- The preview shows `web/npm-release/@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz` before execution, and that is where the file ends up.

### R-UI-014 · Trash can
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-018

Not built: the trash can of R-STOR-022 and R-STOR-023 does not exist yet; a delete is final, and the delete dialog says so. When it
is built, it lives here ([Q-UI-516](#q-ui-516--the-trash-can-of-a-repository-is-a-page-of-the-repository-the-installations-is-the-administrators)):

- Each repository has its trash can as a page of the repository, `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/trash`, reached from **Trash
  can** in the header's menu, which is shown only to a caller who sees entries there (the visibility rule of R-STOR-022: `deploy` or
  `manage` on the original path). A plain reader never sees it.
- Table: path, deletion time and actor, time until purge; a filter by path. Restore dialog: the original location by default, or
  another repository and folder chosen as in R-UI-013, conflict handling (`/api/v1/trash-can/restorations`). Purge of selected
  entries with confirmation.
- The installation's trash can across every repository is a page of the admin area, `/admin/trash`, for administrators, with
  **Empty trash can**, which requires typing `empty`.

Acceptance criteria:

- A deleted file appears in its repository's trash can and downloads again after restore.

### R-UI-015 · Search
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-019, UI-020, SRCH-048, SRCH-058

- The header search is R-UI-095 to R-UI-099. What stays here is the file search: when R-API-028 is built, **Files** becomes a
  kind of the field's filter, and Enter under it opens the file search form below.
- File search form: name, path glob, checksum, property, repositories, date ranges, "not downloaded
  since"; each field maps to one parameter of R-API-028 and to the URL.
- Results table: path, repository, size, modified; actions "show in its folder" (the folder's page of R-UI-010), download,
  copy URL.
- From a folder of a repository's page, a search starts scoped to that repository and folder (a removable scope
  chip).

Acceptance criteria:

- Searching files by the SHA-256 of a known tarball, under the field's kind **Files**, lists it with a working "show in
  browser" link.
- With shortcuts off, typing `/` in the page body does not move focus.

### R-UI-016 · Client setup
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-021, UI-022, UI-023

- The client setup of a repository is the repository's page **Set up client** (R-UI-120 to R-UI-123): the owner's decision of
  2026-11-18 merged the setup page and the guide into one page that opens from the repository
  ([ADR-202](../decisions.md#adr-202--the-client-setup-and-the-guide-are-one-page-of-a-repository)). It asks only for the client,
  where the format has several.
- The clients are those of `GET /api/v1/formats`, in its order: curl, wget, PowerShell; npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry, Yarn Classic; .NET CLI, NuGet CLI,
  Visual Studio; Docker CLI with Buildx, Podman; APT; ansible-galaxy.
- The credential and the token (R-UI-122): by default the snippets read the token from the variable `QUADER_TOKEN` (R-API-030
  `credentials=env`) and no secret appears on the page; **Create a token** creates one in place; a token can be written into the
  snippets under **More options**, checked in the browser and sent nowhere.
- The browser replaces `{{token}}` in the component only; the composed text is never stored in a service, browser storage or
  the URL and is discarded when the route is left (R-UI-043).
- Each snippet is a window (R-UI-121, [Q-UI-801](#q-ui-801--a-snippets-window-is-an-editor-for-a-file-and-a-terminal-for-a-command-coloured-by-its-language)):
  a file is an editor window whose tab names the file and whose bar has **Download**, through a Blob URL that is revoked right
  after the click, and the copy button; a command is a terminal window with the copy button. The copy button copies the snippet
  unchanged.
- For npm, the Publish step also holds the GitLab CI snippet in its two labelled variants (R-UI-017), for who may publish.

Acceptance criteria:

- Playwright: on the page Set up client of `npm-all`, a token created in place and written into the snippets under More options
  gives a `.npmrc` with which `npm install @team-a/ui` in a `node:24` container succeeds.
- The default produces a `.npmrc` containing the literal `${QUADER_TOKEN}`.
- Pasting a token with a wrong checksum shows a validation error and sends no request.

### R-UI-017 · npm client instructions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-024

Snippets for `npm-all` at `https://quader.example.com` (# example). The registry URL keeps its
trailing slash; the credential key is the same URL without scheme, which is how npm matches
credentials to a registry ([npmrc](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/npmrc)); npm
expands `${…}` in `.npmrc`. The protocol behind the URLs is owned by
[formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md), which contributes these templates.

Project `.npmrc` for npm, pnpm and Yarn classic:

```ini
registry=https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
//quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${QUADER_TOKEN}
```

Scoped variant (only `@team-a` packages from Quader):

```ini
@team-a:registry=https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
//quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${QUADER_TOKEN}
```

User-level configuration through the CLI (the shell expands the variable, so the token is written
into `~/.npmrc`):

```shell
npm config set registry=https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/
npm config set "//quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/:_authToken=${QUADER_TOKEN}"
```

Yarn Berry `.yarnrc.yml` ([yarnrc](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc); Yarn expands
`${…}`):

```yaml
npmRegistryServer: "https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/"
npmAlwaysAuth: true
npmAuthToken: "${QUADER_TOKEN}"
```

| Client | Install | Publish (local repository, or virtual with default deployment target) |
|---|---|---|
| npm | `npm install <package>` | `npm publish --registry https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/`, or `"publishConfig": {"registry": "…/api/npm/web/npm-all/"}` in `package.json` (the guide) |
| pnpm | `pnpm add <package>` | `pnpm publish --registry https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/` |
| Yarn Berry | `yarn add <package>` | `npmPublishRegistry: "…/api/npm/web/npm-all/"` in `.yarnrc.yml`, then `yarn npm publish` |
| Yarn classic | `yarn add <package>` | `yarn publish --registry …/api/npm/web/npm-all/` |

The registry in the publish column is the repository the snippets are for (`npm-all` here, a virtual repository
with a deployment target, or a local repository), not the deployment target (Q-API-180).

GitLab CI publishing. The Publish tab shows the GitLab CI snippet of
[formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) R-NPM-041 in two variants, each labelled with the client versions
it serves, so the user picks by the client in the job image:

| Variant | Label | ID token | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native exchange | "npm 11.5.1 and later, pnpm 11 and 12, Yarn 4" | `NPM_ID_TOKEN` with `aud: "npm:<host>"` (here `npm:quader.example.com`); the client exchanges it itself (R-NPM-022) | P1, with R-NPM-022 |
| Generic exchange | "npm 10, pnpm 10 on npm 10, Yarn 1" | `QUADER_ID_TOKEN` with `aud` set to the base URL; a pipeline step exchanges it at `POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/token` ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-007), and the job revokes the token as its last step | MVP |

The dialog offers both variants for every installation and never chooses between them by the base
URL's path: `server.base_url` is an origin without a path (R-OPS-005 in
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)), so Quader owns the host root
that npm's native exchange posts to ([formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-1). Until R-NPM-022
ships, the native variant is not shown.

Acceptance criteria (CI end-to-end, `node:24` container, real token in `QUADER_TOKEN`):

- With the project `.npmrc`, `npm view <package> version` and `npm install <package>` succeed;
  `npm publish` of a fixture to `npm-local` succeeds.
- With `.yarnrc.yml`, `yarn add <package>` (Yarn Berry) succeeds; `pnpm add <package>` succeeds with
  the `.npmrc`.
- The generic-exchange variant, pasted into a GitLab CI job on a `node:22` image whose ID token a
  CI identity mapping accepts, publishes a fixture to `npm-local` and ends with the CI token
  revoked. From P1, the native variant does the same on `node:lts`.

### R-UI-018 · NuGet client instructions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-025

.NET CLI (`--store-password-in-clear-text` is required on Linux and macOS, where NuGet cannot
encrypt stored passwords):

```shell
dotnet nuget add source "https://quader.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" \
  --name quader --username quader --password "${QUADER_TOKEN}" --store-password-in-clear-text
```

The snippets of the UI write the credential part only for a repository that is not anonymously readable, and the fixed user
name `quader`; the exact shapes per client and shell are in [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-026 (Q-NUGET-49).

Repository `nuget.config`. `%VAR%` references work on every operating system, and `<clear />`
removes other sources, so every package resolves through Quader (the virtual repository includes a
nuget.org remote) and a same-named package on a public source cannot slip in
([nuget.config reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/reference/nuget-config-file)):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <packageSources>
    <clear />
    <add key="quader" value="https://quader.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" />
  </packageSources>
  <packageSourceCredentials>
    <quader>
      <add key="Username" value="quader" />
      <add key="ClearTextPassword" value="%QUADER_TOKEN%" />
    </quader>
  </packageSourceCredentials>
</configuration>
```

NuGet CLI: `nuget sources add -Name quader -Source "https://quader.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-all/v3/index.json" -Username quader -Password "<token>"`.
Visual Studio: add a package source with name and service-index URL in the NuGet package manager
options; at the credential prompt enter any user name and the token as password.

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `dotnet add package <id> --version <version>`; `dotnet restore` |
| Publish | `dotnet nuget push <id>.<version>.nupkg --source "https://quader.example.com/api/nuget/web/nuget-local/v3/index.json" --api-key "${QUADER_TOKEN}"` (the token travels as `X-NuGet-ApiKey`, INV-8; a `.snupkg` next to the package is pushed with it, [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md)) |

The username is not checked (INV-8); the snippets use the fixed name `quader`.

The UI's client table offers three clients for NuGet: `dotnet`, `nuget` (nuget.exe) and `visual-studio` (Q-UI-94). Visual Studio
has a configure and an install snippet and none for publishing.
PowerShellGet and Chocolatey instructions need NuGet v2, which is P2 (INV-14), and are not offered in
the MVP; the `dotnet` and `nuget.exe` commands also come in PowerShell syntax.

Acceptance criteria (CI end-to-end, .NET SDK container, real token in `QUADER_TOKEN`):

- With the generated `nuget.config`, `dotnet restore` of a fixture project that references a package
  from `nuget-local` and one from nuget.org succeeds.
- `dotnet nuget push` of a fixture package to `nuget-local` succeeds, and the package is listed by
  `GET /api/v1/packages?format=nuget`.

### R-UI-019 · Instructions for further formats
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-026

Each format that ships, in whichever phase, ships in that phase its snippet templates (R-API-030), its guide
(R-UI-049) for every class and client it supports, and acceptance commands for its native clients (for example
`docker login`, Maven `settings.xml` with `${env.QUADER_TOKEN}`, `pip` index configuration, `GOPROXY` with `.netrc`,
`helm repo add` and OCI registry login). The guide is not a later step: the conformance kit fails a format with
clients that lacks it (R-ARCH-010 check 8). The setup page and the guides area are data-driven: a new format needs no
new screen, and the guides area offers it as soon as `GET /api/v1/formats` lists it with clients; the setup page still
takes its clients from the UI's table and the translated snippet explanations (Q-UI-70).

Raised from P1 to MVP by the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the rule binds NuGet in M3 and every later
format. What stays P1 is the list of further formats itself; each brings its templates, its guide and its acceptance
commands when it ships.

Acceptance criteria: per format, on its page; the setup page lists a format as soon as its templates are registered and
the UI's table names its clients, the guides area as soon as the format registers clients; the kit refuses a format
whose guide misses a class or a client.

### R-UI-049 · Guides for every registry variant
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-10-31 (Q-UI-83): the UI offers documentation and setup help for every package registry
variant, which is a format × a repository class (local, remote, virtual) × a client (for npm: npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry,
Yarn Classic). A guide tells a developer, accurately for Quader as built, what the repository is and how the client
configures, signs in, installs, publishes, changes tags, unpublishes, audits and keeps lockfiles through it, what an
endpoint with exposure rules changes, and what each answer of the protocol means. The text is the format's
(R-ARCH-008 `Guide()`, kit check 8), rendered by the server (R-API-053); the UI adds no format knowledge.

- **Where** (owner, 2026-11-18: context instead of choices). The guide of a repository is the explanation of its page **Set up
  client**, below the snippets (R-UI-120, R-UI-121, R-UI-125), for the repository's class and the chosen client. The guide of a class
  without a repository is the same page at `/guides/{format}/{class}` (R-UI-124). The navigation entry **Guides** shows the formats
  as tiles and leads to a format's repositories (R-UI-124); nothing is chosen before a guide opens.
- **Content.** The sections the server sends, laid out by R-UI-125: what a repository of the class is and the endpoint's note open,
  the others closed under their headings; the section's HTML bound like a README (R-UI-008, the same component and its finishing
  pass); every code block with a copy button. The guide's text is the format's and English, marked `lang="en"`; the frame of the
  page is translated (Q-UI-86).
- **Addresses** are the server's (the base URL of the endpoint the page is served from, R-API-053), never the page's
  location (Q-UI-69).
- **Anonymous readers** of anonymously readable repositories get the guide without credential steps: snippets without
  an authentication line and no publishing, tag or unpublish sections.
- Accessibility as R-UI-044: headings in order, landmarks, every control reachable by keyboard.

Acceptance criteria:

- Playwright (`09-guides.spec.ts`): the side bar's Guides shows the formats as tiles; the npm tile lists the npm repositories with
  their class; **Set up client** of the virtual npm repository opens its page with the four npm clients in one control, the
  virtual repository's explanation below the snippets, and the configure snippet that the setup answers for "Read it from the
  variable QUADER_TOKEN"; axe finds no serious or critical violation (E2.13, Q-UI-87).
- For every class and client of npm the guide has the sections `what`, `configure`, `authenticate`, `install` and
  `troubleshooting` (kit check 8), and every code its troubleshooting table names is a code of the problem catalog,
  under the status Quader answers it with (`TestR_UI_049_TheTroubleshootingCodesAreQuaders`).

### R-UI-050 · Help area and the manual
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's requirement of 2026-11-01: a "?" at the top right behind which the user and administrator documentation of
Quader is found, delivered by the frontend. The text is the manual of R-API-054; the UI renders no Markdown.

- **Entry.** The Documentation link of the top bar (R-UI-002) links to the manual page of the current screen: the longest route
  prefix of `HELP_TOPICS` in [core/help-topics.ts](../../web/src/app/core/help-topics.ts) (for example `/admin/endpoints`
  to the administrator guide's endpoints page), or the overview `/help` where none matches (Q-UI-90). The lint
  (`web/scripts/check-rules.mjs`) fails when a page named there is not a file of `docs/manual/`.
- **Overview** (`/help`): both guides with every page's title and summary, each a link to the page, and a link to the
  guides of R-UI-049 for the commands of a package client. For a plain user (R-UI-067) the administrator guide is a closed
  section at the end (Q-UI-324).
- **Page** (`/help/<section>/<page>`): the contents of both guides beside the page with the current page marked
  (`aria-current`), the page title as the heading and the document title, "On this page" from the page's headings, the
  page's HTML bound like a README (R-UI-008, the same component and finishing pass), and links to the previous and the
  next page. A link of the text to another page stays a link and opens the page in the application (a modified click
  opens it in a new tab through the browser); a fragment in the address scrolls to its heading. The contents are a navigation column:
  they stick beside the page and scroll their own entries, at most as high as the panel's view (R-UI-215, Q-UI-1112). On narrow
  content the contents give way to a link back to the overview.
- The manual's text is English and marked `lang="en"`; the frame is translated (Q-UI-86). The area sits behind the same
  guard as the guides: signed-in callers, anonymous ones while `publicContent` is true.
- **Width** (Q-UI-97). The page takes the width of its column, which grows with the viewport; the prose keeps a measure
  of 80 characters, tables and code use the full width. A table sits in a container of its own that scrolls sideways
  when it is wider; its cells break at spaces only, code in a cell stays whole, and the first column has a minimum width.
- Accessibility as R-UI-044: one `h1`, landmarks for the contents, "On this page" and the page navigation.

Acceptance criteria:

- The Documentation link leads to `/help/admin/endpoints` on the endpoints screen, to `/help/user/files` on the page of a folder or a file of a repository,
  to `/help/admin/operations` on the jobs screen and to `/help` on the signed-out screen (`app.spec.ts`).
- The overview lists both guides with every page linked; a page shows its title, its headings, the contents and its
  neighbours; a link to another page navigates in the application to that page and heading, a link inside the page
  scrolls; an unknown page and a failed read show the error with a retry; axe finds no serious or critical violation
  ([help.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/help/help.spec.ts), `app.routes.spec.ts` for both routes).
- A table of the manual sits in a focusable `.readme-table` container, and wrapping twice does not nest
  ([package-readme.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-readme.spec.ts), help.spec.ts).

Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-030, REPO-007
