### R-UI-021 · Repository creation wizard and edit form
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- A page of format tiles, then one form for the chosen format (R-UI-080, R-UI-081); there are no steps. The format comes first
  because some features are technically impossible for some formats (Q-UI-112). The form holds the artifacts' visibility level
  (R-UI-055). A repository is created in its project: the form is the project's (`/projects/{project}/repositories/new/{format}`),
  and the project is given, shown as text and not chosen (Q-UI-1040; the admin area's form with a project to choose is gone with
  the admin area's list). It is read-only on the
  settings page, where a move to another project is its own action (R-UI-087). After the create the form opens the new
  repository's content page (R-UI-052); its settings are `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/settings` (R-UI-087).
- The format chooser (R-UI-080) is a page of tiles from `GET /api/v1/formats`, each with the format's icon (its owner's logo where
  the owner's terms allow it, else the neutral package glyph, Q-UI-225) and its name, under a search field ("Search by package
  type") that filters the tiles by name. Only the formats the installation has appear. A tile is a link to the form of its format
  ([Q-UI-340](#q-ui-340--a-new-repository-is-a-format-chooser-and-one-form-as-the-references-new-project)); Enter in the search
  field opens the one format that is left (Q-UI-115).
- The form's **Class** (R-UI-080) is a radio group of the three classes; the classes in the chosen format's `classes` in
  `GET /api/v1/formats` can be chosen. Those `classes` are generated from each format's `Descriptor().Classes`
  (R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-010 in [architecture.md](architecture.md)); the UI holds no list of classes
  per format of its own (FMT-001). A class the format lacks is shown disabled with one sentence of
  reason, and cannot be chosen (Q-UI-113). Another class keeps the identity fields and starts its own parts from that class's
  defaults; **Change format** returns to the chooser and starts afresh ([Q-UI-341](#q-ui-341--the-class-is-a-radio-group-of-the-form-preset-to-local)).
  A create that names a class the format lacks still fails on the server with 422.
- Settings forms render from the format's settings JSON Schema (R-ARCH-004, R-ARCH-008) into the
  format member of the repository document that is named after the format (`npm`, `nuget`;
  [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004), never into a generic
  `formatSettings` member. A format adds a panel only for interactions a schema cannot express.
  The form shows the members whose `x-quader-classes` contain the class, in **Advanced settings** of the
  creation form (R-UI-083) and in a closed section of the settings page (R-UI-087), and writes a setting only where it differs
  from the schema's default (Q-UI-78 to Q-UI-81).
- NuGet local repositories: the NuGet settings of the settings page show
  the effective `nuget.deleteMode`, `unlist` (the default) or `delete`, with one sentence on what
  `dotnet nuget delete` and `nuget delete` do in this repository: unlist the version, or delete it
  for good with a tombstone ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-007). Deletes through
  the UI and the management API are hard deletes whatever the mode (R-NUGET-007).
- A setting that is an array of strings is a **list control** (Q-UI-200): one entry per line, or, when its items are an enum, one
  checkbox per option; an empty list leaves the setting to its default. A string setting that may be longer than 1 KiB (a pasted key
  block) is an area. A read-only member of the document that is not in the schema (`deb.upstreamKeyFingerprints`) is shown by the
  format's own panel and never written back.
- Ansible Galaxy repositories ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-009, R-ANS-012, R-ANS-026): the operations `listAnsibleImportTasks`
  (`read`; the import tasks of a local repository, of the deployment target for a virtual one, 405 `not_applicable` for a remote one),
  `listAnsibleTombstones` and `clearAnsibleTombstone` (`manage`; local only, the clearing writes the journaled event
  `ansible.tombstone.cleared`) are in `api/openapi.yaml` and answer 501 `ansible_not_implemented` until the local class builds them; the
  `ansible` member of the repository document holds `authUrl` and `clientId` for remote repositories.
- Ansible Galaxy documentation ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-033 to R-ANS-037): the three operations above, and `listAnsibleImportTasks` gains the optional query parameters `package` and `version` (the Import log tab of a version, Q-UI-240).
- Debian (APT) repositories ([formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-030, Q-DEB-100 to Q-DEB-102): the settings page of a local
  or virtual repository has the closed sections **Signing keys** (the keys in every state with fingerprint in groups of four, state in words, type, origin, times and
  the public certificate; **Generate a next key**, **Import a key** with a write-only secret key and passphrase, **Promote**,
  **Remove**, **Reinstate** and **Confirm retirement**; a private key is never shown) and **Indexes** (the state of each suite and
  **Rebuild all indexes**, R-UI-087). The calls act at once and are not part of "Save changes"; the destructive ones ask first.
- Key: starts with the suggested key (R-REPO-063); check of the INV-5 pattern and of availability within the chosen project (a `GET`
  of `/api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}` answering 404), shown as R-UI-086 says; the same key may exist in
  another project.
- Remote: the group **Upstream** of the form and the open section **Upstream** of the settings page (R-UI-082, Q-UI-122): a button
  per well-known registry of the format (`upstreamPresets`, R-REPO-062), the upstream URL starting with the default preset's (a
  format without presets needs the URL), the authentication (none, username and password, bearer token) with a write-only password
  (Q-UI-123), **Test connection** (`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/upstream-tests`) with the result inline, in words (Q-UI-124),
  and in **Upstream details** the further hosts (`remote.extraHosts`), the metadata and negative cache periods with the format's
  defaults as values (`defaultMetadataTtlSeconds`, `defaultNotFoundTtlSeconds`) and, on the settings page, the offline switch
  (INV-11). A member is written only where it differs from its default (Q-UI-80); the rest of the `remote` section (limits,
  integrity, `sourceNetwork`, the other cache members) is set through the API.
- Virtual: the group **Members** of the form with the member picker and the deployment target (R-UI-081), and the section
  **Members** of the settings page (R-UI-022).
- From phase 6b, on remote repositories of a format whose upstream can be discovered (`mirror: true` in
  `GET /api/v1/formats`, from the format's registration; the UI holds no list of such formats): a **Mirror**
  section with the mode (`pullThrough` or `mirror`) and the members of `remote.mirror`
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050), first among them **Mirror only these packages** (`remote.mirror.include`, R-CUR-018, one name
  pattern per line; empty means every package the repository delivers, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-017), the warning or refusal `mirror_unbounded` at the
  mode with the sentence of R-REPO-052, and for an Owner without `repositories:write-config` the section read-only except
  **Pause** and **Turn off** (Q-REPO-142). The section is the group **Mirror** in **Advanced settings** of the creation form
  (R-UI-083) and the closed section **Mirror** of the settings page (R-UI-087, Q-UI-117); the members show in mode `mirror` and are written only where they differ from their defaults, and a create in
  mode `pullThrough` writes no `remote` member; the early notice at the mode applies the server's bound rule to the scope and the
  storage limit for the upstream URL entered and the server decides (Q-UI-118, Q-UI-122). On the settings page of a remote stored in mode `mirror`, the **Mirror**
  section shows, above the settings (Q-UI-119), the status of `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/mirror`: the state in words (off,
  paused, no bound, scheduled, running, waiting, bound reached, failing; green only for a scheduled mirror after a complete pass;
  **No bound** is a mirror of a well-known registry stored without its bound, which does not run, and plans no next pass,
  [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) Q-CUR-43), the pass
  in progress with its counts and its job, the last complete pass, the next pass, the last error, the rate-limit waits and the
  bound. While a pass is in progress (`running`, `waiting`) the status is read again every 5 s, every 30 s while none is (a pass the
  schedule starts shows without a reload, R-UI-213), and no longer once the section is closed or the page left. A caller who may change the repository (the permission of Save, Q-UI-120) has **Pause** and **Resume**, which `PATCH`
  `remote.mirror.paused` with `If-Match` and nothing else of the form (a 412 opens the conflict dialog of R-UI-042), and **Run a
  pass now** (`POST …/mirror/run`, and **Run a full pass** from its menu), which shows the queued job with a link to the jobs of
  the kind `mirror-pass`; `409 mirror_pass_running` shows the running job instead of an error, and `mirror_off`,
  `mirror_paused` and `mirror_unbounded` are shown in words (Q-UI-104, Q-UI-105, Q-UI-121). In the state **No bound** the run and its
  menu are disabled with the reason beside them, and the state's sentence tells only the holder of `repositories:write-config` to set
  a bound in the mirror settings, every other reader that an administrator of the installation can
  ([Q-UI-1061](#q-ui-1061--a-mirror-without-its-bound-offers-no-run-and-says-who-can-set-the-bound)).
- From M4b, on local and remote repositories of a format with the vulnerability adapter: the
  `vulnerabilities` member ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-002), and
  on the settings page a link to the repository's view of the vulnerability report (R-VULN-022).
- **Show as API request** at the end of the form: the JSON body and the equivalent `curl` command (INV-17).
- Create sends the `Idempotency-Key` generated when the form opened.
- Settings page (R-UI-087): one column of sections; key, class and format read-only; each section's save sends a PATCH of its
  members with `If-Match`; 412 opens the conflict dialog (R-UI-042) for that section; unsaved changes are guarded on navigation.
  The settings hold no section about setting up a client: the guide is on **Set up client** of the repository's header (R-UI-120).
- Server field errors (`errors[].pointer`) are shown at their fields and in an error summary.

Acceptance criteria:

- Creating `npm-remote` with the npm preset and "Test connection" succeeds; double-clicking "Create"
  creates one repository.
- Saving an edit after another administrator saved first opens the conflict dialog.
- With a test build that registers a format whose `Classes` lack `Virtual`, choosing that format
  does not offer the class `virtual`, or shows it disabled with the reason, and `local` can be
  chosen. Choosing the class `virtual` for npm, then **Change format** and that format, leaves Local chosen.
- The format chooser lists the installed formats as tiles, typing `nu` in the search field leaves the
  NuGet tile, and the tiles can be reached and opened with the keyboard alone.
- A remote npm repository in the form shows the Upstream group with the preset URL, authentication none and the periods with
  their defaults as values, and a create that changes none of them sends no `remote` member.
  A create with another URL, username and password and a metadata period sends
  `remote: {url, authMode: "basic", username, password: {value}, cache: {metadataTtlSeconds}}` and nothing else of `remote`;
  the value of the password is nowhere on the page, in the request shown under **Show as API request**, in browser storage or in a
  read of the repository, which shows `password: {set: true}`. On the settings page its field is empty and says that one is stored,
  and a save of another member does not touch it. "Test connection" posts the unsaved section and shows the answer: reachable and the credentials
  accepted, or the reason of an upstream that could not be reached.
- A remote npm repository in the form shows the Mirror group of **Advanced settings** in mode pull-through; choosing
  mirror shows its members with their defaults, and a create with only `intervalSeconds` changed
  sends `remote: {mode: "mirror", mirror: {intervalSeconds: …}}` and nothing else of `remote`.
  An Owner of the project without `repositories:write-config` sees the section read-only except Pause and Turn off.
- The Mirror section of a remote stored in mode `mirror` shows the state and the facts of `GET …/mirror`; **Pause** sends
  `{"remote": {"mirror": {"paused": true}}}` with the loaded `If-Match` and the state reads Paused, **Resume** reverts it, a
  caller who neither holds `repositories:write-config` nor is Owner of the project sees the status and no button, and **Run a
  pass now** answers with the job of its 202 or, after a 409 `mirror_pass_running`, with the running job. While the state is
  running or waiting the status is read every 5 s, otherwise every 30 s (R-UI-213), and no read follows once the section is closed.
- The settings page of `nuget-local` without a `nuget.deleteMode` shows "unlist"; after
  `PATCH /api/v1/projects/web/repositories/nuget-local` with `If-Match` and `{"nuget": {"deleteMode": "delete"}}`
  it shows "delete".
- Creating a local npm repository in the form with `latestGuard` turned off stores
  `{"npm": {"latestGuard": false}}`; turning it on again on the settings page removes the `npm` member,
  and the form offers no `latestGuard` for a virtual repository.

### R-UI-022 · Virtual repository member editor
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-032

- The editor is the section **Members** of the settings page (R-UI-087); its picker is also the group **Members** of the creation
  form (R-UI-081).
- Two lists: available (repositories of the virtual repository's own project and the same format, excluding the
  repository itself and anything that would create a cycle, then, in a group **Upstream registries**, the well-known repositories of
  the format that are not retired, each with its state where it is not `active` (R-UI-189); a virtual repository lists no repository
  of any other project, [Q-REPO-212](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-212--a-repository-is-addressed-inside-its-project-and-no-repository-is-shared),
  [Q-REPO-371](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-371--a-virtual-repository-lists-repositories-of-its-own-project-and-of-upstream))
  and selected (ordered). Buttons Add, Remove, Move up, Move down, Move to top work with
  keyboard and single pointer (WCAG 2.5.7); drag and drop is an optional extra. Both lists are
  listboxes of `@angular/aria` (R-UI-001, Q-UI-1).
- An "Effective resolution order" view flattens nested virtual repositories per
  [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md); `GET …/resolution?path=` explains a sample
  path.
- Default deployment target: picker over the selected local repositories, or none.
- A live region announces each change ("npm-remote moved to position 2 of 3").
- A cycle reported by the server (422 with pointer) is shown on the offending member.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the keyboard only, a user adds two members, reorders them and saves; the API shows that order.

Built as [Q-UI-210](#q-ui-210--the-member-editor-is-a-tab-with-its-own-save-offers-what-the-api-accepts-and-explains-the-saved-order); the journey is `R-UI-022` in [18-virtual-members.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/tests/18-virtual-members.spec.ts).

### R-UI-023 · Quick repository setup
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-033, REPO-008

Administrators and the project's Owners pick a project, formats and a prefix; the preview shows the keys that
`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/quick-setup` ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-015)
will create in the project (local, and virtual over the local one and the format's default well-known repository `upstream/<id>`,
with its state where it is not switched on), then creates them in one request and offers client setup for the virtual repository
([Q-REPO-385](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-385--quick-setup-lists-the-formats-default-well-known-repository-instead-of-creating-a-remote)).

Acceptance criteria:

- With `upstream/npmjs` switched on, quick setup for npm with prefix `team-a` creates `team-a-npm-local` and `team-a-npm`, and
  `npm install` through the virtual one fetches a public package; with it off, the preview says "upstream/npmjs is not switched on
  yet: the virtual repository serves your own packages until an administrator switches it on."

### R-UI-024 · Users and system roles
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-035, UI-036

- List: username, display name, email, origin (identity provider, administrator-created, SCIM,
  break-glass), status, the badge External (R-UI-056), last sign-in (relative, R-UI-103); the search by name or email in the
  list's head, the filters status, origin, group, administrator and external in its drawer (R-UI-100, R-UI-101); the user name
  column sorts (`sort=username`, `-username`).
- Detail ([Q-UI-223](#q-ui-223--the-user-the-endpoint-and-the-service-account-and-group-lists-follow-the-guide)): display name and email edited in place with "Save changes" (an administrator's correction lasts until the next login), ID and origin as
  read-only fields; identities (provider and subject, read-only and copyable); attributes from the identity
  provider, read-only and labelled as such; status with "Disable" (choice to revoke tokens) and
  "Enable"; group memberships (identity-provider-sourced read-only with a badge, manual ones
  editable); system roles through role bindings (R-API-033) with the last-administrator guard; the
  user's tokens (a quiet section **Tokens** like the page's others, opened when the user holds a token and never closed by itself, [Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows); **Revoke all
  tokens** a danger button in the page's section **Advanced**, last on the page) and sessions (list, end all); "Explain permissions" (P1); "Audit"
  (audit log filtered on this actor). The break-glass account shows its lock state and "Unlock".
- The group claim on the user page ([Q-UI-610](#q-ui-610--the-user-pages-notice-of-a-missing-group-claim-says-since-when-and-what-the-policy-does)): while the record carries `groupClaimMissing`, the
  section **Groups** opens with a warning that names the provider, the reason in words, the date and time since which its
  sign-ins carry no usable group claim, and what the policy does at each of them: `clear` removes the memberships synchronized
  from it, `keep` leaves them as they were. That is the current state, which the audit log records only when it changes
  (R-AUTH-008).
- **New user** pre-provisions a user linked to an identity-provider identity (R-API-031): the dialog **New user** creates the
  user's record in Quader with **Create user** ([Q-UI-573](#q-ui-573--the-button-that-makes-a-new-thing-says-new-thing-and-a-new-user-is-made-not-added)). No password
  fields exist.
- `/admin/roles` lists the fixed roles of `GET /api/v1/roles` with their bindings and offers bind
  and unbind; a binding's principal is chosen in the shared principal field (R-UI-150, R-UI-152).

Acceptance criteria:

- Disabling a user with "revoke tokens" makes that user's API calls with a token fail with 401 on
  every replica within 2 s (R-API-052), and the audit log shows the change.

### R-UI-025 · Groups
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-037

- List: name, description, origin, member count; the search by name in the list's head, the origin in its drawer (R-UI-100,

- Editor: name (rename allowed where the owner allows it), description, auto-join, members with

### R-UI-026 · Service accounts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- List and editor: project (none for an account of no project), name, description, owners (P1), groups (accounts of
  no project only: a project's account is never a group member), status with disable and enable. The list of the admin
  area is the instance-wide list with a project column; a project's screen (R-UI-041) lists the project's accounts.
  A name is unique within its project, or among the accounts of no project, and is shown as `sa:<projectKey>/<name>`
  or `sa:<name>` ([Q-AUTHZ-209](authorization.md#q-authz-209--a-projects-policies-and-service-accounts-are-named-within-the-project-administrators-keep-instance-wide-ones)).
- Tokens, a quiet section of the page opened when the account holds a token and never closed by itself
  ([Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows)):
  issue (scope and expiry as in R-UI-029, one-time display, recent authentication), list, revoke one, and revoke all in the
  page's section **Advanced**. The server lets the administrator role, and for a project's account the project's Owners, issue
  and rotate the tokens of a service account ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)
  R-AUTH-027, R-AUTH-030, [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026); the tab offers **Create token** and
  **Rotate** to those callers only (`authz/me` `roles` and `projects`), not to a holder of `identities:write` alone,
  who would get 403. An Owner's form offers no non-expiring lifetime, no `admin` and no `system` item. Revoking follows
  `tokens:revoke` or the role `owner`.
- The token form offers the binding to endpoints where the caller may read them (Q-UI-91). It offers **Administrator: everything on this installation**
  to a caller with the administrator role for an account of no project that holds the role itself (`ServiceAccount.isAdmin`); the choice sends
  `{"inherit": true, "admin": true}` ([Q-UI-220](#q-ui-220--the-form-of-a-service-account-token-offers-the-administrator-choice-for-an-account-that-holds-the-role)).
- The page is one column, as the style guide's settings pages are ([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)):
  the description and the ID at the top with **Save changes**, **Details** (status, the administrator role, created) and **Advanced** (disable or enable, delete) as sections.
- A hint explains when to use one: CI systems without OIDC exchange, long-running automation.

Acceptance criteria:

- A token issued on the Tokens tab authenticates `npm view` against a repository the service account
  may read.

### R-UI-027 · Permission policy list and editor
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-039, UI-040

- List: project (none for a policy of no project), name, description, principal summary ("3 groups, 1 CI mapping"),
  resources summary, actions; filters by principal (picker), repository and project. The list of the admin area is the
  instance-wide list; a project's screen (R-UI-041) lists the project's policies.
- Layout (Q-UI-4): one page for create and edit, no step-by-step wizard. The sections run down the
  left with an in-page table of contents; the preview panel is a right column while the
  content area is at least 59 rem wide, which sticks beside the form while it fits in the panel's view and never scrolls by itself
  (R-UI-215, [Q-UI-1112](#q-ui-1112--a-navigation-column-sticks-beside-the-page-with-a-scroll-of-its-own-any-other-side-column-sticks-only-while-it-fits)) (a container query on the content area; the window's 960 px
  left the form 110 px wide at 1,024 px with the side bar open, R-UI-171; 59 rem keeps the preview beside a form of at
  least 20 rem in a window of 1,280 px with the side bar open, where a threshold of the form's full width had folded it
  away) and a collapsible region above the save bar when it is narrower. The explainer (R-UI-028, P1) is its own screen, reached from the editor through "Test
  this policy" (saved policies only, once the explainer ships), which opens it in a new tab with the policy's first principal and
  repository filled in, so the draft in the editor stays untouched.
- Editor sections, following the policy model of
  [authorization.md](authorization.md): general (name on create only, description); principals
  (users, groups, service accounts) chosen per entry in the shared principal field (R-UI-150); a CI identity a stored entry names
  shows as a chip and is not offered (Q-UI-583); resources with a live "covers 4 repositories" preview, whose selectors take the form of the
  policy's context: `<projectGlob>/<keyGlob>[:<format>]` or a class for a policy of no project, bare keys, key globs
  and classes of the project for a project's policy ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-004,
  [Q-AUTHZ-216](authorization.md#q-authz-216--repository-selectors-name-the-project-in-instance-contexts-and-a-bare-key-inside-a-project)); include and exclude
  patterns of package names and paths with syntax help and a tester field ("Does `@team-a/ui` match?") in a closed section
  **Limit to package names or paths**, open when one of them holds a value (details on demand); actions with a one-line
  explanation each. Every section is the quiet disclosure of Q-UI-322.
- Preview panel fed by `POST /api/v1/authz/validate-policy` (debounced 500 ms): covered repositories,
  errors, warnings. An error of a field shows once the field holds a value or a save was tried, as next to the field, and names
  the field by its label ("Name: …"), never its JSON pointer. "Try it" answers from the draft alone; its **Explain** is a
  secondary button that says what is missing when a principal or a repository is not named yet; the answer adds what the repository's visibility level gives the principal
  (`internal` covers users who are not flagged external, service accounts and CI identities, never anonymous; R-AUTHZ-030,
  R-AUTHZ-035), and says so.
- The one-line help of the actions says what each covers; `manage` is the administration of content
  (package owners, the override of the shadowing check, namespace claims, cache operations), and
  the settings of a repository need the capability `repositories:write-config`.
- Save shows a diff against the loaded revision (principals, resources and actions added or removed),
  then sends PUT with `If-Match`; recent authentication is handled as in R-UI-042.
- Delegated managers (P1) see only the entries the API lets them change.

Acceptance criteria:

- Creating the policy of R-API-033's acceptance test through the editor yields the same stored
  document as creating it through the API.
- The diff before saving lists exactly the added principal when only one was added.

### R-UI-029 · Profile, personal tokens and sessions
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-053, AUTHN-039, AUTHN-040

- Profile (`GET /api/v1/users/me`): one column ([Q-UI-333](#q-ui-333--a-pages-sections-are-quiet-disclosures-tokens-too-open-while-there-is-a-token-the-profile-follows)): the avatar, the identity as read-only fields (from the identity
  provider), then the quiet sections **Preferences** (language, theme, keyboard shortcuts; R-API-021; open), **Groups** with
  source (open while the group claim notice stands) and **System roles**.
- Missing group claim (R-AUTH-008 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)):
  while the record carries `groupClaimMissing` (`{"provider", "reason", "since", "onMissingClaim"}`), a notice next to the
  groups names the provider and the reason (`absent`, `wrong_type` or `overage`). It says that the
  last login through that provider carried no usable group claim, so the groups synchronized from
  it may be missing (the default `clear` removes them) and the identity provider's group mapping
  needs an administrator. The notice is `role="status"` text, not a dialog, and disappears after a
  login that delivers the claim.
- What the profile does not have (settles UI-053's open point on password changes): no unlock step,
  because the session already proves the login (R-AUTH-017 in
  [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)); no password section, because
  users have no password in Quader (INV-7) and the break-glass password is changed by replacing its
  Kubernetes Secret (R-AUTH-014); no editable email or display name, because both come from the
  identity provider at every login (R-AUTH-016 maps the catalog's "profile updatable" option to
  this). Nobody changes a password through Quader. An administrator's correction of email or
  display name through `PATCH /api/v1/users/{username}` (R-API-031) lasts until the user's next
  login. SSH keys and linked accounts are P2 on the identity page and not shown.
- The profile's three pages (Profile, Personal tokens, Sessions) have the shared page header and are the tab strip of links
  under it; **Create token** and **End all other sessions** are the header's actions (Q-UI-307, UI-A-20). An empty token list
  says what is missing: "No active tokens." while the revoked and expired ones are hidden, "No tokens yet." with them (the
  administrator's list says "There is no active token yet." unfiltered and "No token matches." filtered, Q-UI-565).
- Personal tokens: list with the token (description and hint), the scope summary, the two sharing the room the others leave by
  their content ([Q-UI-563](#q-ui-563--a-column-is-as-wide-as-its-content-what-never-breaks-declares-no-width-and-the-columns-that-wrap-share-the-room)), expires
  and last used, and, from 64 rem of the list, created, each time relative (R-UI-103); the row ends with **Rotate** and
  **Revoke**, two quiet buttons with their words, or the state of a token that is no longer active
  ([Q-UI-332](#q-ui-332--a-token-list-shows-token-scope-expiry-last-use-and-its-action-created-and-created-via-give-way-first),
  [Q-UI-429](#q-ui-429--a-token-list-gives-the-scope-the-room-leaves-out-how-a-token-was-made-and-words-both-actions)); tokens
  expiring within 7 days are marked, and a token with `admin: true` whose owner does not hold the administrator role now says that
  its administrator rights are inactive. Create dialog: description (required), expiry (presets and a
  custom date, bounded by R-AUTH-040), scope (three choices, Q-UI-213: administrator rights, only for a caller who holds the
  administrator role; all repository permissions of the owner without administration, the preselected one; or restricted to
  repositories and actions; grammar of R-AUTH-024) and, for a caller with `endpoints:read`, the endpoints the token
  is bound to (Q-UI-91). Recent authentication applies. The result is shown once with a
  copy button and the notice that it cannot be shown again. Revoke and rotate with confirmation;
  rotate is P1 and, like creation, needs recent authentication (R-AUTH-030).
- Sessions (`/api/v1/users/me/sessions`): list with created, last seen, address, user agent and
  "this session"; end one, or end all others.

Acceptance criteria:

- A created token works in `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …" "$QUADER_URL/api/v1/auth/whoami"`;
  reopening the profile never shows it again; revoking it makes the same call answer 401 on every
  replica within 2 s (R-API-052).
- Ending all other sessions signs out a second browser.
- The profile page contains no password field, no unlock control and no editable email or display
  name; after the identity provider changes the user's email, the next login shows the new value.
- After a login whose ID token and userinfo carry no group claim, the profile shows the notice with
  the provider and `absent`; after a later login that carries the claim, the notice is gone.

### R-UI-030 · Token administration
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-041, TOK-026

- The page is titled **Tokens**, as its entry in the side bar (R-UI-145).
- All tokens (`tokens:read`): the token (description and hint, which names its type), owner, scope, expires, last used, and
  **Revoke** or the state of a token that is no longer active; below 64 rem of the list the rows stack ([Q-UI-332](#q-ui-332--a-token-list-shows-token-scope-expiry-last-use-and-its-action-created-and-created-via-give-way-first)); filters type,
  owner, state, expiring before, unused since; revoke single and selected
  with confirmation. An active token with `admin: true` whose owner does not hold the administrator role says that its
  administrator rights are inactive (`Token.ownerIsAdmin`, [Q-UI-221](#q-ui-221--the-token-administration-marks-administrator-tokens-whose-owner-no-longer-holds-the-role)).
  A caller without `identities:read` is not told the owner's role, and the row then says nothing about it
  ([Q-AUTH-428](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-428--the-administrator-role-of-a-token-owner-or-a-service-account-is-shown-only-to-a-holder-of-identitiesread-and-to-the-owner-itself)).
- CI tokens come from `/api/v1/ci/issuances` with job context (project, pipeline, job, mapping) and
  "Revoke matching" by project or pipeline.
- "Revoke by value": a field to paste a leaked token; the value is sent once to
  `POST /api/v1/tokens/revoke` and cleared. The screen says only what the answer supports (Q-UI-92):
  after a `200` (administrator) which token of which owner was revoked, after the empty `202`
  that the request was accepted and that the answer does not say whether the value was a token.

Acceptance criteria:

- Filtering "unused since 90 days" lists a token never used since its creation 91 days ago (test
  clock).

### R-UI-031 · Authentication settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-043

`/admin/settings/auth` (the sidebar's **Settings › Authentication**, Q-UI-326) renders `GET /api/v1/settings/auth`: **New users are external** (`newUsersExternal`, a checkbox with
the sentence "Users created from now on start as external users; existing users keep their flag.", R-AUTH-044), token default
and maximum lifetimes per token type, expiry notices, and the read-only status block (providers and discovery state, break-glass state, session
timeouts, client switches including Basic, the command-line login poll binding mode, SCIM state).
YAML-pinned and ceiling-bounded values show their source. Hiding unauthorized resources
(`authz.hide_existence`) is shown read-only. Save sends `PATCH` with `If-Match`; recent
authentication applies. The page is one column ([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)):
**New users are external** is open at the top, the token lifetimes and the read-only status are sections, and each group with a
save button sends the members of its own group only. Who may read without signing in is the visibility of the general settings
(R-UI-053).

The status block shows the two poll-binding warnings that the answer carries (R-AUTH-034,
R-AUTH-040 in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)) as warnings next to
the mode, each with icon and text:

- mode `off`: any poll of an approved `npm login` receives the token, wherever it comes from;
- mode not `off` while `server.trusted_proxies` is empty: behind an edge proxy every poll carries
  the proxy's address, so the binding cannot tell the user's network from anyone else's.

Acceptance criteria:

- Ticking **New users are external** and saving makes the next user who signs in for the first time an external user.
- With the default poll binding and an empty `server.trusted_proxies`, the screen shows the
  trusted-proxy warning; with `poll_binding.mode: off`, it shows the `off` warning.

### R-UI-032 · Sign-in protection and public content
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-038, UI-042

- Break-glass lockout state and threshold (read-only, R-AUTH-038) with "Unlock".
- A summary of what anyone can read without signing in: the `publicObjects` of `GET /api/v1/settings/visibility` (R-API-056),
  linked to the general settings' Visibility section (R-UI-053).
- Multi-factor authentication, password expiry and password rules belong to the identity provider
  (INV-7); the screen says so instead of offering controls.

Acceptance criteria:

- After the configured number of failed break-glass logins the account shows as locked, and
  "Unlock" unlocks it.

### R-UI-033 · General settings
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-044

`/admin/settings/general` (the sidebar's **Settings › General**, where `/admin/settings` leads, Q-UI-326) shows the public base URL and its source (`GET /api/v1/system/info`,
read-only field, R-OPS-005) at the top, then the visibility (R-UI-053), the banner and the maintenance mode as sections with a **Save changes** each
([Q-UI-222](#q-ui-222--which-settings-pages-are-one-column-now-and-what-a-sections-save-button-is-called)); the maintenance section opens by
itself while the mode is on. The banner is `/api/v1/system/banner` (enabled, severity, plain text) and the
maintenance mode `/api/v1/system/maintenance`. Server name, date format, logo and login notice are
P2 on [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md).

Acceptance criteria:

- An enabled banner appears on every screen for every user within one minute after saving.

Built as [Q-UI-211](#q-ui-211--general-settings-save-the-banner-and-the-mode-separately-ask-before-read-only-and-the-shell-reads-both-every-30-seconds); the journey is `R-UI-033` in [19-general-settings.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/tests/19-general-settings.spec.ts).

### R-UI-034 · Storage and proxy settings
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-045

`/admin/settings/storage` renders `/api/v1/settings/storage` (trash can and the other runtime
storage settings of [storage.md](storage.md)) and the global offline mode of
`/api/v1/system/proxy-offline` (confirmation: every remote repository stops fetching), and links to
outbound proxies and client certificates ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md)).
The UI-only limits (`ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes`, `ui.browser.page_size`) are shown read-only.

Acceptance criteria:

- With offline mode on, `npm view` of an uncached public package through `npm-remote` fails while
  cached packages still install.

### R-UI-035 · CI identity
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-049, CIOIDC-024

- Issuers: name, type, issuer URL, audiences, number of mappings, key status (last fetch or error)
  with "Refresh keys".
- Issuer editor per [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md); creation validates discovery and keys.
- Mappings per issuer in evaluation order, with conditions summary (`namespace_path in [4711]`,
  `ref_protected = true`), grants summary and maximum token lifetime.
- Mapping editor: conditions with suggestions of GitLab claim names (`project_path`,
  `namespace_path`, `ref`, `ref_type`, `ref_protected`, `environment`, `pipeline_source`,
  `user_login`, …); grants, where the policies and the groups are each a text field that suggests the names as they are typed,
  held and saying so while the list loads ([Q-UI-334](#q-ui-334--a-picker-is-one-control-from-the-start-held-while-its-list-loads-and-a-field-is-as-wide-as-its-kind-of-input));
  options; "Test with claims" opens the claim tester prefilled. Warnings returned on save are shown.
- Per mapping, "CI snippet" shows the text of `GET /api/v1/ci/issuers/{issuer}/snippets/gitlab-ci`
  (for a project's mapping `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/ci/issuers/{issuer}/snippets/gitlab-ci`, which an Owner of the
  project may read) for the chosen format (npm or NuGet) with a copy button. This covers the GitLab counterpart of
  CIOIDC-024 ([GitLab ID tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/secrets/id_token_authentication/)).
- Delegations (P1) and issuances (R-UI-030) are tabs of the issuer.
- An Owner of a project reaches the project's CI mappings from the project (the project route family of
  R-API-035): the mapping list and editor, the claim tester over the project's tier and the issuances of its mappings, with
  the issuers as a read-only choice (Q-CI-26). A mapping's name is unique within the project and the issuer, without a
  prefix, and shown as `ci:<issuer>/<projectKey>/<name>`
  ([Q-AUTHZ-214](authorization.md#q-authz-214--a-projects-ci-mappings-are-named-within-the-project-like-its-policies-and-service-accounts)).
  The editor offers the project's repositories as bare keys and its policies, and no groups. The
  screens and routes are those of [Q-UI-99](#q-ui-99--the-ci-screens-sit-under-identity-and-a-projects-ci-screens-are-the-same-components-under-the-project);
  the bulk revoke and the detail of an issuance are Q-UI-100; the bulk revoke is offered only while every applied filter is one
  the request carries, and the day filters are the local day (Q-UI-102).

Acceptance criteria:

- The snippet copied from the screen, used in a GitLab CI job of project `team-a/ui` on a protected
  branch against the test environment, publishes `@team-a/ui`.

### R-UI-036 · Claim tester
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- `/admin/ci/{issuer}/test`. Input: a text area accepting claims as JSON or a compact JWT.
- A pasted JWT is decoded in the browser (base64url header and payload, no signature check). The UI
  replaces the text with the pretty-printed claims, discards the token, and states that only the
  claims are used. If `exp` lies in the future, a warning says the token is still a valid credential
  until then.
- "Insert sample GitLab claims" fills a realistic payload (`iss`, `aud`, `sub` such as
  `project_path:team-a/app:ref_type:branch:ref:main`, `namespace_id`, `namespace_path`,
  `project_id`, `project_path`, `ref`, `ref_type`, `ref_protected`, `pipeline_source`,
  `environment`, `user_login`, `job_id`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`) that the user edits, as JSON or in a
  form view.
- "Evaluate" calls `POST /api/v1/ci/issuers/{issuer}/evaluate` and shows the decision trace of the
  owning page: the matched mapping or "No mapping matches; the exchange would fail", every
  candidate with each condition's expected and actual value and a pass or fail mark (icon plus
  text), the resulting grants with templates resolved, the token that would be issued.
- "Explain resulting permissions" opens the explainer (P1) with the mapping as principal.
- Claims are never put into browser storage and are gone when the route is left.

Acceptance criteria:

- Pasting a signed test ID token shows its claims, and the network log shows that only the claims
  JSON was sent.
- Changing `ref_protected` to `false` switches the result to no match and marks that condition.

### R-UI-037 · Audit log
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-023

- Table from `GET /api/v1/audit/rows` in five columns, one form at 1,440 and 1,024 px whatever the events hold and blocks only at
  390 px ([Q-UI-997](#q-ui-997--the-audit-log-keeps-five-columns-and-an-opened-event-stands-beside-it-only-where-both-keep-their-form)):
  time (relative, the moment in full as its title), actor (with the address the event came from under it), action (a short plain
  name of its own for every event type of the audit
  registry, in English and German, with the event name under it, which breaks after its dots only, [Q-UI-567](#q-ui-567--an-audit-actions-key-breaks-after-its-dots-only)); an unknown name is shown as sent), target (the actor and a
  repository's target wrap in their column and are never cut, UI-A-46; a resource the entry knows by name shows the name, any
  other its kind and its identifier on one line, [Q-UI-568](#q-ui-568--an-audit-target-the-entry-knows-by-name-shows-the-name-another-its-identifier-on-one-line);
  a repository's project by its mark and its name under it), outcome (a badge, **Success**, **Failure**, **Denied**,
  [Q-UI-564](#q-ui-564--a-status-word-starts-with-a-capital)); filters time range (presets and custom), actor, action, category,
  repository, the resource (its kind and its identifier,
  [Q-UI-998](#q-ui-998--the-audit-log-filters-by-the-resource-an-event-is-about-its-kind-and-its-identifier)),
  outcome (the list's drawer, R-UI-101; the head has no search by name, its end the time zone and the exports); "Load more". The log is always newest first and has no sort control. The action filter suggests every
  prefix of the registry's event types at every level (`ci.*`, `ci.issuer.*`) and every type with its name, from the registry.
- Detail panel with the full event and links to actor and target. It stands beside the log from 68 rem of content (1,440 px) and above
  it, at the log's width, where it is narrower; an event opened from the list takes the focus, so the page brings it into view (Q-UI-997).
  Beside the log it sticks while it fits in the panel's view and never scrolls by itself; **Close** gives the focus back to the row it was
  opened from (R-UI-215, Q-UI-1112).
  Where the panel is narrower than 25 rem (390 px) each fact's name stands above its value, so that the time of the event stays on one line
  ([Q-UI-972](#q-ui-972--a-narrow-audit-event-puts-each-facts-name-above-its-value)). The actor's kind and credential stand on a line
  under its name; the action's key under its name, or alone where the action has no name of its own, and a key breaks after a dot or an
  underscore only, in the panel and in the row (Q-UI-567); the slash between a repository and its path belongs to the path. The
  resource is its kind and its identifier, which a copy button copies (Q-UI-998). The details wrap their long lines in the panel, every
  string longer than 200 characters shortened to its start and its length, and a copy button copies them whole
  ([Q-UI-995](#q-ui-995--a-document-shortens-a-long-string-to-its-start-and-its-length-and-copies-whole-a-code-block-scrolls-a-few-screens-at-most)).
- **A download is one row** ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-055, the owner's decision of
  2026-11-26, [Q-UI-1395](#q-ui-1395--a-downloads-row-names-its-unit-in-the-target-and-opens-in-place)): a row of a download stands at
  its first item's time, how long it went on under it ("for 12 s"); its action is the action's name ("File downloaded"); its target the
  repository, the unit in bold with its version or tag muted beside it (an image pulled by its digest: the first item's digest cut to 12
  digits), and the number of its items and their bytes under them; a chevron before them opens it in place. A package's and a
  repository's name break after a slash, a dot or an at sign, never inside a word.
- **An opened download** ([Q-UI-1396](#q-ui-1396--an-opened-download-lists-its-first-ten-items-and-links-all-of-them)) lists its first
  ten items under its row, each with its clock time to the second (the moment its title), which opens the item's event in the
  panel, its path, a link to the file, its SHA-256 cut to 12 digits with the whole as its title and a copy button, and its size; where it holds more, **All N items** opens the log of that
  download's events. It grows the page by at most ten rows and never scrolls (R-UI-215), and it stays open while the log reads itself
  again (R-UI-213); a download that goes on grows in its row.
- **A push, a publish and a delete are one row too** ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-056,
  [Q-UI-1491](#q-ui-1491--a-row-of-several-events-names-the-act-not-its-first-events-action)): every row of several events names its act
  in one word instead of its first event's action, and no key under it: **Downloaded**, **Pushed** (OCI, NuGet), **Published** (npm,
  Ansible Galaxy, Debian), **Uploaded** (files that published no version), **Deleted**, **Writes allowed**, **Data keys handed**. Its
  target names the unit with its version or tag, or "3 versions" where it names several (the delete of a package), and the number of its
  items and the bytes of its files. Opened, an item that is no file names its action and its version, without a link (**Package version
  published 1.4.0**), with its digest where it names one
  ([Q-UI-1492](#q-ui-1492--an-opened-row-names-an-item-that-is-no-file-by-its-action-and-its-version)).
- **The log of one row** (`?group=<first event's ID>`,
  [Q-UI-1397](#q-ui-1397--the-log-of-one-download-lists-its-events-oldest-first-and-offers-no-export),
  [Q-UI-1493](#q-ui-1493--the-log-of-one-rows-events-is-group-and-its-chip-events-of)) lists every event of it from
  `GET /api/v1/audit/rows/{id}/events`, oldest first, one row each, with **Load more**; the head names it as the chip **Events of**,
  whose removal returns to the log; it offers no export, which takes the log's filters.
- **The German words** ([Q-UI-1490](#q-ui-1490--the-audit-log-holds-its-german-actions-by-the-acts-word-and-a-shorter-word-where-it-reads-right),
  [Q-UI-1494](#q-ui-1494--german-counts-a-rows-items-as-einträge-and-a-days-volume-as-gbtag)): the acts' words fit the action's 7.5 rem in
  both languages; "File downloaded" is "Heruntergeladen", "File deployed" "Bereitgestellt", the act "Data keys handed" "Datenschlüssel"; a row's items are "Einträge".
- Times in the user's locale with a UTC toggle (in the list the title of each relative time, in the panel the moment); export of the
  current filter as CSV or JSON Lines (`/api/v1/audit/events/export`), one line per event, a download's items each a line.

Acceptance criteria:

- Changing a policy and filtering the audit log by it shows the event with the before and after of
  the grants.
- Every event type the registry holds has a name in the audit log: a unit test walks the registry (the fixture
  `audit-actions.fixture.ts`, which a Go test writes from `internal/audit` and keeps current) and fails on a type without one.
- An event with the outcome `warning` ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) Q-AUTH-402) shows
  **warning** with the warning icon in the warning colour, never the red of a failure; the outcome filter offers it. The list
  decides by the outcome, not by the event type.
- Unit ([audit-log.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.spec.ts), the describe "R-OPS-055 a download is one row", the
  fake API's rows formed as the server forms them, milliseconds): a pull of 13 items is one row named by its image and tag with "13
  items", their bytes and "for 12 s"; an anonymous pull of the same image is a row of its own named by its first item's digest; an event
  before the unit has no chevron; the opened row lists ten items, its first item's path links the file and its digest's title is the
  whole digest, an item's time opens its event, **All 13 items** links the download's log; a fourteenth item read every 30 s grows the
  row, which stays open; the log of one download lists its 13 events with the chip and no export.
- Unit (`web`, [audit-log.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.spec.ts), the describe "R-OPS-056 a push, a publish and a
  delete are one row", milliseconds): a push of two layers, its tag and its version is one row **Pushed** named `acme/app 1.4.0` with
  "4 items" and the bytes of its three files, its writes a row **Writes allowed** beside it, an npm package's delete of three versions one
  row **Deleted** naming "3 versions"; opened, the push lists its files by their paths and its version as **Package version published
  1.4.0** without a link, its digest the version's file's.
- Rendered (rule 11, the screen `admin-audit-rows` of [screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts), in the German pass too, 1,440,
  1,024 and 390 px, light and dark): a push of an image of 24 tiny layers closed and opened beside its writes, a NuGet push, a delete of
  a version and of a package of three versions, three files uploaded into a folder, a pull of an image of 32 items opened, a pull by
  digest, an npm install of three packages, a pull still going on, a refusal, events of before, and the log of one pull's events; the
  layout checks find nothing in either language (Q-UI-1490).

### R-UI-038 · System status
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-008

The screen is MVP because every endpoint it renders from is MVP (the replica registry API of
R-OPS-003, R-OPS-004, the task and job API of R-OPS-019, R-API-049, R-API-050), and it is the only
UI view of the replicas per role, of Valkey, of the backup job, of the scheduled tasks and of the
key ring. It needs a little backend work beyond those endpoints: the registry's `node` and its
nested `valkey` view (R-OPS-003, adopted by R-API-038), the per-role counts and the `backup` block
of the system information (R-OPS-004), and the backup summary of R-API-050, which are MVP because
INV-12 makes roles, drains and Valkey MVP and INV-19 the backup job (Q-UI-7).

- **Admin dashboard** (Q-OPS-175, owner 2026-11-06): the first screen of the admin area at
  `/admin/dashboard`, where `/admin` and the Admin button of the top bar lead a holder of
  `settings:read`. One page of cards: the instance bar (overall state, version, base URL, ready
  replicas, a link to the status screen); the overall state is the worst statement of the status screen's header that is an
  error or a warning, in its words, else "All roles ready", and while replicas drain or start an informing "Replicas are being
  replaced" beside it (Q-UI-600 to Q-UI-602); one card per role with its ready and live replicas, the nodes where its ready
  replicas name them (no row where none does, Q-UI-604),
  requests and server errors per second, the worst p95 latency, requests in flight, CPU and memory
  against the limits, summed from the runtime snapshots of R-OPS-003 (lost replicas left out; a role
  without a replica says so); PostgreSQL, Valkey and the object store (one line per connection, R-UI-197) with their readiness check over
  the live replicas (connected with the slowest `durationMs`, or how many replicas fail), their facts
  of R-OPS-004, and the stored content of the overview; the counts of the overview with links to
  their screens and "New repository" for `repositories:write-config`; and the job queue with the
  active key and the state of the backup ([R-UI-165](#r-ui-165--the-dashboard-shows-the-state-of-the-backup)). It refreshes every
  15 seconds with a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2), like the status screen, and a failing overview leaves the rest readable with a retry.
- **The page** ([R-UI-164](#r-ui-164--system-status-jobs-and-backups-are-the-tabs-of-one-page)): `/admin/system` is the tab
  **Status** of the page **System status**, beside **Jobs** (`/admin/system/jobs`) and **Backups** (`/admin/system/backups`,
  R-UI-048); the header's **Pause automatic refresh** and **Refresh now** act on the tab that is shown.
- Cards from `GET /api/v1/system/info` and `/system/replicas`: version and revision (its first twelve characters, the full hash
  their title, [Q-UI-570](#q-ui-570--a-hash-in-running-text-is-its-short-form-with-the-whole-as-its-title)), with a link to the notices of the
  bundled software of the same build (Q-UI-144); base URL and
  source; the maintenance mode, as a row only while it is not `normal` (Q-OPS-156); database (server version, schema version against the supported ones);
  scheduled tasks (`/system/tasks`: next run, last outcome) with "Run now", which runs on a
  `worker` replica; recent jobs (`/system/jobs`) with cancel.
- **Jobs** (the tab `/admin/system/jobs`, and the recent jobs of the status screen, one table for both): kind, state (a badge,
  Q-UI-560), enqueued, progress, replica, result and cancel; the kind and the replica stay on one line, the result takes the
  room (Q-UI-563). The filters kind and state are the head of every list, **Filters** and its drawer with the chips of the set
  ones ([Q-UI-566](#q-ui-566--the-jobs-and-the-backup-runs-take-the-head-of-every-list)). The result cell of a job whose `error` is set shows its `code`, under it the `detail`
  as the server wrote it, untranslated and wrapping at any character, and "Attempt *n* of *m*" with *n* the error's `attempt`
  (the job's `attempt` when the error has none) and *m* the job's `maxAttempts`; an error without a detail shows its code
  alone. The result of a succeeded job is summarised as before (Q-UI-172).
- **Replicas by role** (Q-UI-7, Q-UI-107). One group per role in the order `api`, `packages`, `worker`, taken from the replica's `roles`
  (Q-ARCH-341); a replica of the development role `web` forms a group `web` while it is live; a replica with roles
  `["all"]` of the development role forms a group `all`, and while one is live it serves every role (R-HA-001), so a group
  `api`, `packages` or `worker` without a replica of its own is left out with its warnings (UI-A-45); within a group, one sub-group per pool of R-HA-062 and per
  endpoint pool, each with its own counts and drain safety,
  headed with the role's `live`, `ready` and `degraded` counts from `replicas.roles` of
  `/system/info`, each listing its replicas with name, node, version, state (`starting`, `ready`,
  `unready`, `draining`, `lost`), heartbeat age and Valkey view. `draining` and `starting` are neutral, `lost` is a warning and
  `unready` an error; a replica that went stale while draining signed off and is not listed by the server (R-OPS-003,
  Q-OPS-210 in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)), and the synthetic check `draining` is not
  named among the failing checks, because the state says it (Q-UI-600). Each group states whether the role
  is drain-safe right now: its `ready` replicas, not `lost`, run on at least two distinct nodes, so
  draining any one node leaves a ready replica (INV-12, R-HA-059). The group shows, with icon and
  text (the first two informing, as a property of the installation's size, Q-UI-603; the others as warnings):
  - "Fewer than two ready replicas": a node drain or the loss of one pod interrupts this role;
  - "All ready replicas on one node": a drain of that node interrupts this role (shown only when
    every replica reports a node);
  - for `worker`, "No live worker replica": jobs and scheduled tasks are queued but nothing runs
    them (R-API-015); for a pool, "No live replica in the pool `<pool>`", shown while every row of the pool is `lost` (Q-UI-108: the registry holds the pool's name and not its queues, and a pool whose rows were pruned is not known);
  - for `packages`, "No live packages replica": package clients and raw downloads get no answer from the edge, while the
    UI keeps working (Q-UI-107);
  - while replicas of two versions are live, an information notice naming both versions, because N
    and N-1 run side by side during every rolling upgrade (INV-3); it is not a warning.

  The screen says what it cannot see: disruption budgets, free capacity on other nodes and whether
  the remaining replicas carry the peak (the N + 1 rule of R-HA-059), because Quader holds no
  Kubernetes permissions (R-HA-033).
- **The scanner replicas** (from `GET /api/v1/system/scanners`, [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
  R-OPS-048, [Q-UI-897](#q-ui-897--a-scanner-replica-is-one-more-kind-of-row-one-table-for-the-system-page-and-the-settings-of-both-scannings)).
  After the roles, one more group `scanner` with its `live` and `ready` counts, and in it one sub-group per kind named with its tool,
  `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav` (Q-HA-372), each with its counts and a table in the form of the replicas': name, node,
  version, state with the reason beside it in words ("No database loaded yet" for `database`, "clamd does not answer", "Analyser does not
  run", "Certificate not loaded", "Spool not writable", "Still starting", else the code), **State changed** (the relative time of
  `stateSince`), heartbeat, and **Tool** in place of the Valkey view ("Trivy 0.67.2", "ClamAV 1.5.5"). A replica that is not ready is shown
  with its reason, a lost one as lost. A kind without a replica says why in a sentence instead of an empty table: none has reported
  (`reporting`, a warning), the scan listener cannot tell the kind (`unverified`), or no scanner of the kind is configured (`none`, naming
  the setting; the role `all` builds no image scanner, [architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-563). A failure of the read stands in the
  group's place and leaves the roles. The rows are the scanners' own statements, bound as text (H-1161 in
  [security/scanner-replicas.md](../security/scanner-replicas.md)). With the detection in the scanner
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-225) the trivy rows name the database the pod holds, here
  under the tool in **Tool** and in the fold of **Advisory sources** in a column **Database**
  ([Q-UI-915](#q-ui-915--an-image-scanners-database-is-a-badge-beside-its-tool-and-the-installations-statement-a-line-beside-the-counts)):
  the badge **Database in use** (a check, green) with "built" and the age of the build, **Older database** or **No database yet** (an
  hourglass, neutral), the digest its title. While ready pods of the kind do not hold the database
  in use, a line under the kind's heading informs "*n* of *m* ready replicas do not hold the database in use yet: the detections they are
  asked for wait until they have loaded it"; it is no warning of the header, because every new database leaves the pods on the one before
  for the seconds of its load. Built on 2026-11-21: [scanner-replicas.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/scanner/scanner-replicas.ts),
  `databaseLag` in [scanner-model.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/scanner/scanner-model.ts),
  [system-status.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.html).
- Readiness checks per replica, from the `checks` of `/system/replicas` (R-OPS-001, R-OPS-003; Q-OPS-2
  in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)), in two kinds that the
  screen never merges:
  - **failing**: a gating check fails (for example `database`, `schema` or `invalidation`) and the
    replica is `unready`; shown as an error with the check names;
  - **degraded**: the replica is `ready` while a reported check fails. Two checks can be in this
    state; `/readyz` answers `200` and lists them under `degraded`, and
    `quader_health_check_passing{name=…}` shows `0`:
    - `objectStore`, after the first readiness unless `health.require_object_store` is set: blob
      requests on that replica fail with a retryable `503`, everything else keeps working;
    - `valkey`, whenever Valkey is unreachable from that replica ([architecture.md](architecture.md)
      R-ARCH-031, [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) Q-HA-13): no request fails, but remote fetches
      are collapsed per replica only, the negative cache is per replica, rate limits fall back to
      per-replica shares of the budget (R-API-016), and changes reach that replica through the
      change-log poll instead of within milliseconds.

    Each is shown as a warning that names the check and says, in the words above, what it means.

  Both kinds use icon plus text, never colour alone (R-UI-044).
- **The page header** states the installation in one rule (`serviceStatus` in
  [system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts)), what is wrong first:
  - as an error: "No ready replica of the role `<roles>`" for a role the installation needs (`api`, `packages` and `worker`
    unless a live `all` replica serves them; `web`, `all` and an unknown role while one of its replicas is live) that has no
    ready replica (Q-UI-602); "Replicas unready" while a live replica fails a gating check after it was ready;
  - as a warning: "Lost without draining: `<names>`, last heartbeat `<time>`" while a replica is listed as lost (owner,
    2026-11-18, Q-UI-602); "Degraded" while a ready replica's reported check fails; "No ready replica of `<kind>`" for a kind of scanner
    whose replicas report themselves (`reporting`) and none of which is ready, its scans waiting (Q-UI-897);
  - else "All roles ready";
  - and after them, informing and neutral: "Replicas are being replaced (`n` draining, `m` starting), as during every update"
    while replicas drain or start (Q-UI-600), and "Not drain-safe" while a role it needs is not drain-safe (Q-UI-603). The
    notice of two versions side by side (below) belongs to the same update.
- **Valkey card**, from the `valkey` block of `/system/info` (installation facts: mode, primary
  name, configured Sentinels, TLS mode, key prefix and keyspace) and each replica's nested `valkey`
  view of `/system/replicas` (R-API-038): per replica its state with the reason in R-OPS-001's
  vocabulary, each reason translated, the circuit (an open circuit is shown as such), the primary
  address, the reachable against the configured Sentinels and the server version. The card
  summarises with icon and text:
  - "Available on every replica", or "Degraded on k of n replicas" with the reasons, where k is
    `valkey.degradedReplicas` and n is `replicas.live`;
  - "Replicas disagree about the primary" when replicas whose `valkey.state` is `available` report
    different `valkey.primary` addresses for longer than `valkey.sentinel.refresh_interval` plus
    one heartbeat: a replica bound to a demoted primary, the case R-ARCH-031's reconciliation
    bounds;
  - "Sentinels unreachable" when a replica's `valkey.sentinelsReachable` is below a majority of its
    `valkey.sentinelsConfigured`, the condition on which `QuaderValkeySentinelsDegraded` fires
    ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-007): no failover can happen while it lasts, so the next
    primary failure would leave Quader degraded until someone acts. The `valkey` check stays `pass`
    meanwhile, because the primary still answers (R-HA-056 step 6);
  - the time of the last primary change (the newest `valkey.lastPrimaryChangeAt` of the
    replicas);
  - the server version, or each version with its replicas when the replicas report different ones,
    as an information notice.
- **Backups card**, from `GET /api/v1/system/backups/summary` (R-API-050): the last success and its
  age, an "Overdue" mark under the rule of R-API-050 (1.5 × the expected interval), "No backup
  yet", the last failure when it is newer than the last success, the active run with its phase and
  progress, and a link to the backups screen (R-UI-048).
- **Vulnerability data card** (from M4b), from the `vulnerabilityData` block of `/system/info`
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-004,
  [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-024): per source and ecosystem its
  mode, state, age and consecutive failures, with icon and text for data that is stale, never
  imported completely or failing to sync, and a link to the sources screen (R-VULN-022).
- Jobs (`/admin/system/jobs`): the list of `GET /api/v1/system/jobs` with filters for `kind` and
  `state`. The state filter offers every job state of R-ARCH-016: `queued`, `running`,
  `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelling`, `cancelled`. A cancelled job shows `cancelling` until it
  stops at its next checkpoint (R-OPS-019), and "Cancel" is offered only for `queued` and
  `running` jobs.
- A "Stored-secret keys" card from `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` (R-API-049): the active key ID
  and the key IDs of each replica, sealed values per key ID, the canary state labelled with the
  replica that reported it, and whether the rings are compatible (icon plus text). A key ID that is no longer active but still seals values is marked
  "re-encryption pending" with "Re-encrypt now" for administrators (the task trigger of
  R-API-049), disabled with its reason while the rings are incompatible. The card names the next
  rotation step of R-HA-027 that the state allows, for example "No values left under 2026-04: its
  key file can be removed."
- Automatic refresh every 15 seconds with a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2).

Acceptance criteria:

- Stopping one of two replicas changes its status on the screen within 40 seconds without a reload.
- After a rotation to a new key, the card shows the old key ID as "re-encryption pending"; after
  "Re-encrypt now" finishes, it shows zero values under the old key ID and the removal hint.
- Blocking object storage after both replicas became ready shows both as degraded with
  `objectStore` within 40 seconds, and neither as unready (default `health.require_object_store`).
- Cancelling a running `gc-full` job lists it under the state filter `cancelling` until it stops,
  then under `cancelled`.
- With two `web` and two `worker` replicas, stopping Valkey shows every replica as degraded with
  `valkey` and the explanation within 40 seconds, the header reads "degraded", no replica is shown
  unready, and the Valkey card reads "Degraded on 4 of 4 replicas".
- `SENTINEL FAILOVER quader` updates the last primary change on the Valkey card within 40 seconds,
  and every replica reports the new primary.
- Scaling `worker` to 0 shows "No live worker replica" within `system.heartbeat_stale_after` plus
  15 seconds, and the header reads "No ready replica of the role worker". A test that pins both `api` replicas to one node shows
  "All ready replicas on one node" and "Not drain-safe" in the header, informing.
- During `kubectl rollout restart deploy/quader-api` with two `api` replicas, the header never reads an error or a warning: it
  reads "All roles ready" and, while a pod drains or starts, "Replicas are being replaced"; the draining pod's row says
  `draining` without failing checks; 30 s after the rollout returns no old pod is listed (R-OPS-003).
- After `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` of one of two `api` replicas, the header reads "Lost without draining:" with
  the pod's name and its last heartbeat as a warning, not as an error, once the row is 30 s stale; the row stays as `lost`.
  With both `api` replicas deleted so, the header reads "No ready replica of the role api" as an error until a new one is ready.
- An installation of one healthy replica of the role `all` reads "All roles ready" and an informing "Not drain-safe"; no
  warning and no error. The dashboard's card of the role shows no **Nodes** row outside Kubernetes (Q-UI-604).
- With `backup.expected_interval: 1h` and the last successful backup two hours old (test clock),
  the Backups card shows "Overdue"; at 80 minutes it does not.
- With two of three Sentinels stopped, the Valkey card shows "Sentinels unreachable" within
  40 seconds, while every replica's `valkey` check stays `pass` and the header does not read
  "degraded".

### R-UI-039 · Webhooks
Priority: **P1** · Covers: UI-046, UI-047, EVT-034

List; editor (key, URL, handler kind standard or templated, for templated handlers the method,
the body template and header templates of R-OPS-041 and named write-only secrets, otherwise the
signing secret with rotation; event types from `/api/v1/webhooks/event-types`, repository
selectors, outbound proxy, custom headers, enabled); "Test" with the receiver's status, latency
and body excerpt; status (`/{key}/status`); deliveries with request and response details and
"Redeliver". Project-scoped subscriptions and a project column come with EVT-022 (P2). Semantics:
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md).

Template validation (R-OPS-041, Q-OPS-11 there): a template is checked when the subscription is
saved or tested unsaved, and a refusal answers `422`. The editor shows each error at the template
field it belongs to (`errors[].pointer`, R-API-009) and in the error summary, with the server's
text, which names the rejected construct: `define`, `template` or `block`; a `range` inside
another `range`; a `range` over a literal, a function result or a variable; more than 16 `range`
actions in one template, header templates included; the `call` function; a reference to an
unknown secret; a template that fails to render against the sample event of a subscribed type.
The editor does not check templates itself, so its rules never drift from the server's.

Acceptance criteria:

- "Test" against a receiver that answers 500 shows the status and body excerpt.
- Saving a template with 17 `range` actions keeps the editor open and shows, at the template
  field, the error naming the 16-range cap; a template with `{{ define "x" }}` shows an error
  naming `define`.

### R-UI-055 · The visibility of a repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **One level in the main view.** The section **Visibility** of the repository's settings page (R-UI-087) is the block
  **Visibility**: one column, one radio group of Q-UI-228, **Visibility level**, and its own **Save changes**
  ([Q-UI-231](#q-ui-231--a-repository-sets-artifacts-and-wiki-in-one-block-of-its-access-tab-and-the-wizard-sets-the-artifacts),
  [Q-UI-770](#q-ui-770--the-wikis-own-level-is-a-fold-of-the-section-visibility-closed-while-the-wiki-has-the-repositorys-level),
  [Q-UI-772](#q-ui-772--the-one-group-is-named-visibility-level-for-every-format-and-the-wiki-is-bounded-by-the-repository)).
  The level is the artifacts': who can install, download and list the packages. An option above the project's level is disabled
  with "The project is internal, so this repository cannot be public." The block is the same for every format and every class.
- **The wiki's own level behind a fold.** For a format with wiki content (`wiki: true` in `GET /api/v1/formats`, R-AUTHZ-034) the
  block has the fold **Wiki visibility** under the group, the inline form of the shared disclosure (Q-UI-552); the other formats
  have none. It holds the sentence "The wiki is the README and the documentation of the packages. It has the repository's
  visibility level unless a lower one is chosen here." and the wiki's radio group, which the fold's toggle names on the screen (its
  legend, **Wiki visibility**, is for assistive technology). A wiki option above the visibility level is disabled with "The wiki
  cannot be more open than the repository."
  - The fold is closed while the wiki's level is the visibility level. The block opens it when the two differ, as stored or in
    the form, and when the server refused the wiki's level, so a differing level and its error are never behind a closed fold by
    themselves. The person may close it; a closed fold that holds an unsaved choice says "Unsaved changes" after its name.
  - **The wiki follows**
    ([Q-UI-771](#q-ui-771--a-wiki-without-a-level-of-its-own-follows-the-visibility-level-in-the-form)). While the wiki has no
    level of its own (it is stored at the visibility level, and no level was chosen in the fold in this edit) it takes the level
    chosen above, up and down, and the save sends both parts. A wiki with a level of its own keeps it: it is lowered where the
    visibility level falls below it, and gets it back when the level rises again before the save. Choosing the visibility
    level's own level for the wiki and saving makes it follow again.
- **The server's answer at its level**
  ([Q-UI-773](#q-ui-773--the-servers-answer-for-a-level-stands-under-that-levels-group)). A field problem at
  `/visibility/artifacts` or `/visibility/wiki` (422 with `visibility_above_project` or `visibility_wiki_above_artifacts`, 403
  `visibility_level_restricted`, R-API-057) stands under that level's group, in the error colour, as an alert that describes the
  group; the wiki's opens its fold. An answer that names no level (409 `public_not_allowed`) is the block's notice. The block
  sends only the parts that changed.
- The creation form holds the one group (R-UI-081, labelled **Visibility** among the form's fields), preset to the `visibility` of
  R-REPO-063 (the lower of the installation's default and the project's level); the wiki follows the artifacts at create.
- A warning `public_populates_remote` of the answer is shown as a warning at the block, with its sentence (R-AUTHZ-008).
- The repository list, the repository's header and the client setup dialog show the artifacts level's icon before the
  repository's name (Q-UI-230).
- Editable for the project's Owner and for `repositories:write-config`; read-only otherwise. A level the installation restricts is
  disabled for whoever may not choose it, after the project's reason, and kept where the part has it (R-UI-141).

Acceptance criteria:

- In the Public project `web`, the Owner of a repository whose levels are Internal sets **Visibility level** to Public: the wiki
  follows behind its closed fold. The Owner opens **Wiki visibility**, sets the wiki to Internal and saves; the repository list
  shows the Public icon, and an anonymous visitor's package page of a package in it has no README tab (R-UI-057). Opened again,
  the settings page shows the fold open (the journey `21-visibility`).
- In an Internal project the option Public of both groups is disabled with the reason.
- Unit tests (`repository-visibility.spec.ts`): one visible group and the closed fold for a format with a wiki, no fold for one
  without; the fold open by itself while the levels differ, also for a reader; the wiki bounded by the level with its reason; a
  wiki without a level of its own follows the level up, both parts are sent and the fold stays closed; a level chosen in the fold
  is the wiki's own, a closed fold with it says "Unsaved changes", and only the changed parts are sent; a wiki with its own level
  is lowered with the level and gets it back; a field problem stands under its level's group, the wiki's opens the fold, and an
  answer without a level is the block's notice; no serious axe violation with the fold open and with an error.
- Renders: `repository-settings-npm-local` (the fold closed, and opened in `sections`), `repository-settings-ansible` (levels that
  differ: open as the page opens), `repository-settings-generic` (no fold), `repository-settings-visibility-refused` (the
  server's answer under each group).

Built as Q-UI-231, Q-UI-236, Q-UI-237, Q-UI-770 to Q-UI-773: [repository-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-visibility.ts), [repository-create.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-create.ts) (the creation form since R-UI-080); test [repository-visibility.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-visibility.spec.ts).

(R-UI-055), a project's settings and the dialog that creates a project (R-UI-054), reads the caller's choices
(`GET /api/v1/visibility-choices`, R-API-076) and shows ([Q-UI-542](#q-ui-542--every-form-that-chooses-a-level-reads-the-callers-choices-and-gives-the-first-reason-of-r-authz-038),

### R-UI-057 · What the UI shows of the wiki and of public content
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- The package page (R-UI-007) shows the README tab only when `hasReadme` is true for the caller, and a format's documentation
  tabs only when their member is present ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034); it never requests the README for
