  and "Continue without signing in" there makes it one (R-UI-004, Q-UI-710).
- Such a visitor sees the vulnerabilities of what the public levels admit (the owner, 2026-11-26: "Natürlich soll die Hauptinstanz
  Vulnerabilities an öffentlich sichtbaren Repos anzeigen."): the grades of every list and of a version's facts, and the tab
  **Vulnerabilities** with the open findings, without the triage, and with no link into a screen that needs a session (R-UI-224,
  [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-280--an-anonymous-caller-reads-the-open-findings-of-what-the-levels-admit-and-the-public-state-of-a-check)).

Acceptance criteria:

- An anonymous visitor opens the package page of `@web/button` in `web/npm-public` (artifacts Public, wiki Internal): the
  versions and the install panel are shown, the README tab is not, and the browser made no request for the README.
- A signed-in internal user sees the README tab on the same page.
- An anonymous visitor of a graded version of a public repository sees its grade and the tab **Vulnerabilities** (R-UI-224).

### R-UI-041 · Projects
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-003, UI-050, UI-051

Raised from P1 on 2026-11-02 with R-AUTHZ-026 (beta phase 5a). Follows the project model of R-AUTHZ-026 in
[authorization.md](authorization.md): every repository belongs to exactly one project, and users and groups are members
with the role `reader`, `developer`, `maintainer` or `owner`
([Q-AUTHZ-206](authorization.md#q-authz-206--every-repository-belongs-to-exactly-one-project),
[Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)). The content
screens live inside the project, `/projects/{project}/…`
([Q-UI-129](#q-ui-129--the-project-is-the-context-of-the-content-chosen-from-your-projects)); this requirement fixes what
the model gives the screens:

- The project is chosen, not filtered: the start page (`/projects`) lists the caller's projects (`GET /api/v1/projects`: the
  memberships of `authz/me`, every project for a holder of `projects:read`) and then the projects whose level admits the caller
  (R-UI-054), and a caller with exactly one project starts in it; inside a project the project switcher at the top of the side bar changes it. There is no project filter in the top
  bar, and no list of a project's content is narrowed by a stored choice.
- Start page: the project (its mark, its display name and its key under it, R-UI-102), description, the visibility, the caller's
  role (for a member), the number of repositories and of members; the head's search by key or name and **Your projects** (R-UI-100).
  It is the one list of projects: the admin area has none (the owner's T-25,
  [Q-UI-1040](#q-ui-1040--projects-and-repositories-leave-the-admin-area-the-main-area-holds-what-they-held)). For a holder of
  `projects:read` the head also holds the check box **Show Owners and storage**, which adds the columns **Owners** (by name, the
  dash for none) and **Storage** (the logical size the project is charged, `logicalBytes`,
  [R-STOR-049](storage.md#r-stor-049--the-storage-of-a-project), the exact bytes as its title); the choice is kept for the viewer
  as an opened Details section is (Q-UI-967), and a plain user's list stays as it is
  ([Q-UI-1041](#q-ui-1041--the-owners-and-the-storage-are-columns-on-demand-of-the-start-page-for-the-holder-of-projectsread)).
- Create dialog (administrators, `projects:write`), opened by **New project** on the start page: key
  (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-+[a-z0-9]+)*$`, immutable), display name, description, the visibility level (R-UI-054), and the first Owner;
  repositories are created in the project afterwards. The display name and the description are edited in place on the project's
  settings, by administrators and the project's Owners (Q-UI-215). Delete is offered there to administrators only, and only for
  projects without repositories, service accounts and CI mappings.
- The project's settings show the logical size the project is charged (`logicalBytes`, in binary units, with the exact byte count as its
  tooltip), for every member and every holder of `projects:read`. The physical size of the object store is a figure of the admin
  dashboard only.
- Members screen (`/projects/{project}/members`, Q-UI-214, R-UI-142): the users and groups of the project with their roles, in the
  head and the table of every list, the number of members after the heading, read for every member; an Owner and an
  administrator add a member chosen in the shared principal field over the project's lookup (R-UI-150, Q-AUTHZ-182), change a role
  and remove a member. The last
  Owner cannot be removed or demoted except by an administrator: the action is shown disabled with the reason, and a
  `409 last_owner` from a concurrent change is reported as such
  ([Q-AUTHZ-217](authorization.md#q-authz-217--the-last-owner-of-a-project-is-removed-or-demoted-only-by-an-administrator-of-quader)).
- For an Owner of a project, also without any capability, the project's side bar holds the project's administration (as
  for the delegates of Q-AUTHZ-181): its repositories (create in the project, edit, delete and move to another project
  it owns; R-UI-020, R-UI-021), its policies (`/projects/{project}/policies`, named within the project; the editor offers the
  project's repositories as bare keys, key globs and classes, and names each entry's principal in the shared principal field over
  the project's lookup, R-UI-150), its service accounts
  (`/projects/{project}/service-accounts`, named within the project, shown as `sa:<projectKey>/<name>`, listed through the
  project's route `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/service-accounts`, which admits the Owner, as the policies are, never
  through the instance-wide list, which needs `identities:read`; the admin area's filter by project takes the same route; create, enable, disable and delete) and their tokens (issue, with the lifetime cap and without a `system` scope, and revoke), its CI
  mappings (`/projects/{project}/ci`, R-UI-035) and its settings (display name and description, edited in place, Q-UI-215). An Owner without a
  capability has no admin area (Q-UI-129). A member with another role sees the project's settings and members read-only. An
  action the caller's role does not allow is not offered; the policies, service accounts and CI identity are listed in the
  side bar only for the holder of their capability and for the Owner.
- The `auditor` and the other holders of `projects:read` see every project, its members and its screens read-only.
- The lists across projects (the repositories of every project under **Your work**, R-UI-020; the admin area's service accounts,
  permission policies and audit log) name the project of each item in a column and link to the project's screen; the project is
  also a filter of the repository and policy lists.
- The built-in project `upstream` is listed where its rule of [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-041 admits the caller,
  with the badge **Built-in** after its name and no role, members or Owners (R-UI-190).

Acceptance criteria:

- An administrator creates project `team-a` with `user:alice` as its first Owner; alice adds `group:team-a-devs` as
  `developer`; a member of that group finds `team-a` on the start page with the role `developer`, and the project's members
  read-only.
- alice, without any system role, has no admin area; in `team-a` she sees the project's side bar and none of the global
  screens; she creates a policy `npm-read` and a service account `partner` in `team-a`, and the account is shown as
  `sa:team-a/partner`.
- The remove action of alice's own membership is disabled while she is the only Owner.
- An administrator finds **New project** on the start page and no entry **Projects** in the admin area; ticking **Show Owners and
  storage** adds the columns Owners and Storage, which `sam` is not offered (Q-UI-1041).

### R-UI-042 · Errors, conflicts and feedback
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- One HTTP interceptor (R-ARCH-004 `core/http`) maps problem `code` values to translated messages and
  `errors[].pointer` to form controls. An unknown code, and an answer without a problem document, is said from its status in the
  reader's language; the server's English `detail`, the `requestId` with a copy button and every other fact of the answer stand under
  that sentence (R-UI-216, which replaced "Unknown codes show the English `detail`" on 2026-11-25).
- 412 `precondition_failed`: a conflict dialog "Changed by someone else since you opened it",
  showing their version against yours field by field, with "Reload (discard mine)", "Overwrite"
  (re-sends with the new ETag after showing the diff) and "Copy my changes". A field is named by the label the form gives it and its
  value shown as the form shows it: a list as its entries, a switch as On or Off, a choice as the option's text, an empty value as
  the en dash of an empty cell (Q-UI-561) or the form's own word for it, a secret never; a field the form does not show keeps its API
  name as the server's text ([Q-UI-1210](#q-ui-1210--the-conflict-dialog-names-a-field-by-the-forms-label-and-shows-a-value-as-the-form-does)).
  The review before an exposure rule's save (R-EP-017) shows its fields the same way.
- **Own permission changes** (INV-17, R-API-052, [authorization.md](authorization.md)
  R-AUTHZ-032). After a write that answers `Quader-Authz-Epoch` (a policy, a role binding, a project, its members, the
  move of a repository), the session store (R-UI-046) keeps the highest such epoch of the tab, and the
  interceptor sends it as `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` on every request that follows, so the next
  screen, the `authz/me` and `authz/check` refresh included, shows the change on whichever replica
  answers. The epoch lives in memory only, never in browser storage, and is cleared on 401 and on
  sign-out.
  - 412 `authz_epoch_unknown`: the UI drops that epoch at once (otherwise every later request
    would fail the same way), re-reads the changed object by its `ETag` (R-API-012), and tells the
    user that the change may not have been saved, showing the object as now stored; when the
    stored object matches the user's draft, as for a retried write below, the message says that
    the change is stored. A GET that met the `412` is sent again without the header; any other
    request is offered again with "Retry".
  - 503 `authz_stale`: a GET is retried once after `Retry-After`; any other request shows the 503
    notice below with "Retry".
- 401 `reauthentication_required`: a dialog explains why, keeps the draft of non-secret forms in
  session storage keyed by route, and starts the re-authentication flow of R-AUTH-011; after return
  the draft is restored and the action can be repeated. Forms holding secrets are not kept.
- 429: idempotent GETs retry once after `Retry-After`; otherwise a message with the wait time.
- The UI sends an `Idempotency-Key` on every request that accepts one (R-API-014): creates, job
  starts and job-starting deletes. The key is generated when the form or dialog opens and kept
  until it closes.
- A network error without an answer (for example a request cut at the end of a replica's drain,
  R-API-051) is retried once through the Service, which picks another replica: a GET as it is; a
  request that carries an `Idempotency-Key` with the same key (R-API-014), so it cannot create or
  start twice; a PUT or PATCH with the same `If-Match`. A retried write that answers 412 because
  its first attempt did commit is recognised by comparing the current resource with the user's
  draft: when they match, the UI reports success instead of opening the conflict dialog. A retried
  DELETE that answers 404 counts as done. Any other unsafe request (a POST action without an
  idempotency key, such as a revocation or a rotation) is not retried automatically: the UI says
  that the action may or may not have run, reloads the affected resource, and offers "Retry".
- 409 `idempotency_in_progress`: the UI waits `Retry-After` and sends the same request with the same
  key once more, which replays the first request's outcome.
- 409 `token_already_issued` on a retried token creation: the first attempt created a token whose
  secret was lost with its answer. The UI revokes it (`DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{tokenId}`), creates
  the token again with a new key, and shows only the new one, so no unseen token stays valid.
- 503: a page-level notice with "Retry"; in maintenance mode the notice shows the operator's
  message. Since R-UI-216 every failed read offers "Retry", and a failed read whose failure may pass reads again by itself.
- Confirmations use a polite live region (`role="status"`), errors `role="alert"`; notifications
  with actions stay until dismissed. Both are shown as the reference's toast at the bottom right of the window, the owner's place
  (2026-11-24: "Und diese dann bitte unten rechts einblenden, nicht links"), with the text, an optional action and a close button
  "×" named **Close**. One confirmation is shown at a time: a new one replaces the confirmation still on screen, and the region
  announces each; a notification with an action and an error keep their own toast. A confirmation without an action goes after
  8 seconds, which stop while the pointer or the focus is on it
  ([Q-UI-1063](#q-ui-1063--feedback-outside-forms-is-the-references-toast-at-the-bottom-right-one-confirmation-at-a-time)).
- Jobs show a progress component that polls the job (R-API-015) and announces progress at most every
  10 seconds.

Acceptance criteria:

- A forced 412 `precondition_failed` in a Playwright test opens the conflict dialog, and
  "Overwrite" stores the user's version.
- After saving a policy in the e2e profile `scatter`, the network log shows
  `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` with the epoch of the `PUT` on the requests that follow it. A test proxy
  that answers one of them `412` `authz_epoch_unknown` makes the UI show "may not have been saved",
  re-read the policy, and send no `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` on later requests until its next
  permission change; the conflict dialog does not open.
- An unknown `code` shows the request ID, the code and the server's `detail` as facts under the sentence of its status (R-UI-216).
- A test proxy resets the connection of the wizard's `POST /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories` after the server
  has committed it. The UI retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`, reports success, and exactly one
  repository exists. The same with a `PATCH` of the edit form reports success without the conflict
  dialog.
- The same proxy resets the connection of a token creation after the commit. The UI ends with one
  displayed token; `GET /api/v1/tokens` lists it and the first token as revoked.
- The same proxy resets a `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/disable`. The UI sends it once only and
  shows the user's state as reloaded afterwards.

### R-UI-043 · Secrets in the browser
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- Token values (created or pasted) live only in component-local signals. They never enter shared
  services, the URL, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, the browser history, console output
  or error reports, and are cleared when their dialog closes or the route changes.
- Secret inputs are `type="password"` with a reveal toggle, `autocomplete="off"` and
  `spellcheck="false"`; copying uses the Clipboard API on an explicit click only.
- Write-only fields (upstream passwords, webhook secrets) show whether a value is set and a "Replace"
  action; they are never prefilled.
- Configuration files with an embedded token are offered for download through a Blob URL that is
  revoked right after the click.
- API answers carry `Cache-Control: no-store` (R-API-017), which keeps secret-bearing answers out of
  the browser's caches.

Acceptance criteria:

- After creating a token and closing the dialog, a test inspects `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`,
  IndexedDB, the URL history and the console log and finds no `qdr_` value.

### R-UI-044 · Accessibility
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Every screen meets [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) level AA. Design rules that follow from
specific criteria:

| Criterion | Rule in Quader |
|---|---|
| 1.3.1 Info and relationships | Data tables are `<table>` with `<th scope>`; landmarks; one `h1` per screen, no skipped heading levels |
| 1.4.1 Use of color; 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 contrast | Status, decision and diff marks carry icon and text; contrast verified in both themes |
| 1.4.10 Reflow | Usable at 320 CSS px; a list stacks its rows where its columns do not fit (R-UI-174); a code block and a document's table scroll sideways inside their own region |
| 1.4.13 Content on hover or focus | Tooltips are dismissible and hoverable; no information exists only in a tooltip |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | Tree, member editor, reordering, file selection ("Choose files" button) and action menus work by keyboard |
| 2.1.4 Character key shortcuts | Single-key shortcuts (`/`, R-UI-095) are on by default and turned off in the profile (`keyboardShortcuts`, R-API-021); they never act while the focus is in a text field ([Q-UI-401](#q-ui-401--slash-focuses-the-field-and-is-on-by-default-the-preference-turns-it-off)) |
| 2.2.1 Timing adjustable; 2.2.2 Pause | Session expiry warning (R-UI-002); auto-refresh can be paused (R-UI-038) |
| 2.4.2 Page titled; 2.4.3 Focus order | Title per route; focus moves to the new `h1` on navigation to another screen and into dialogs on open, and returns to the trigger on close; a navigation that changes only the query or the fragment (a list's filter writing `?q=` while one types, a tab) leaves it where it is |
| 2.4.11 Focus not obscured | A list's head scrolls with the page and sticks over no row (R-UI-215); a side column that sticks stands beside the page's content; an editor's save bar sticks at the panel's lower edge |
| 2.5.7 Dragging movements | Every drag interaction has a button alternative (R-UI-022) |
| 2.5.8 Target size | Interactive targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px |
| 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 Errors | Field errors as text next to the field plus a summary at the top |
| 3.3.7 Redundant entry | The wizard never asks twice for what was entered in an earlier step |
| 3.3.8 Accessible authentication | No cognitive tests; pasting allowed in every token field; login happens at the identity provider |
| 4.1.2 Name, role, value; 4.1.3 Status messages | Custom widgets built on `@angular/aria` or the CDK accessibility patterns ([Angular Aria](https://angular.dev/guide/aria/overview)); status messages through live regions |

Process:

- Automated checks with axe-core in Playwright
  ([Playwright accessibility testing](https://playwright.dev/docs/accessibility-testing)) on every
  route, in both themes and both locales; violations of impact "serious" or "critical" fail the
  build, others are triaged.
- Before each release, a manual screen-reader pass (NVDA with Firefox, VoiceOver with Safari) of
  five journeys: sign in; find a package and copy its install command; client setup with a new
  token; create a remote repository; edit a policy.

Acceptance criteria:

- The axe run reports zero serious or critical violations on all routes.
- The five manual journeys are recorded as passed in the release checklist.

### R-UI-045 · Internationalization
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- English (source and default) and German ship with the MVP. Every UI text is translatable; no
  sentence is concatenated from fragments; counts use ICU plural and select messages ("1 Version",
  "3 Versionen").
- Mechanism (Q-UI-5): Angular's compile-time i18n (`@angular/localize`,
  [Angular i18n](https://angular.dev/guide/i18n)) with one build per locale, served at `/ui/en/` and
  `/ui/de/` (R-UI-001). No runtime translation library is used; switching the language reloads the
  route under the other locale.
- Locale choice: the user's preference (R-API-021), then `Accept-Language`, then
  `ui.default_locale`. Switching the language in the user menu stores the preference and reloads the
  same route under the other locale. The preference applies to a request for `/ui/` or a UI route
  without a locale from a browser that holds a valid session cookie; the redirect reads the cookie
  itself, read-only, because the authentication stage ignores it on `/ui/` (Q-API-184). A request without a
  session, with an ended one, or whose preference cannot be read follows `Accept-Language`.
- Dates, numbers, file sizes (binary units such as MiB with the locale's decimal separator) and
  relative times are formatted with Angular's locale data and `Intl`.
- API texts stay English; the UI translates problem codes (R-UI-042) and shows the English `detail`
  for unknown ones.
- Not translated: user content (READMEs, descriptions), identifiers, and snippet code, which is
  marked `translate="no"`.
- `<html lang>` matches the locale (WCAG 3.1.1). Layouts tolerate 35 % longer German text.
- A missing translation fails the build (`i18nMissingTranslation: error`).
- An English–German glossary of product terms (for example "permission policy" →
  "Berechtigungsrichtlinie"; "repository" stays "Repository") is kept with the translation files. A term keeps one
  grammatical gender in every text: "das Token"
  ([Q-UI-1052](#q-ui-1052--token-is-neuter-in-every-german-text)).

Configuration:

```yaml
ui:
  default_locale: en      # default (proposed)
  locales: [en, de]      # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A browser with `Accept-Language: de-DE` opening `/ui/` lands on `/ui/de/packages` with German
  texts and German number formatting.
- A user whose stored locale is `de`, signed in, opening `/ui/` with `Accept-Language: en` is
  redirected to `/ui/de/`; the same request without the session cookie, or with a cookie that is
  not a valid session, is redirected to `/ui/en/`.
- Removing one German translation unit makes the build fail.
- Unit test (`formal-german.spec.ts`): no German target uses "Token" as a masculine noun.

### R-UI-046 · State management with signals
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Builds on the workspace rules of R-ARCH-004 (standalone, zoneless, signals; generated types and
thin hand-written clients in `src/app/api/`):

- Signals are the reactive state primitive in components and services. RxJS is used only where
  Angular APIs emit observables (router events, `HttpClient` internals) and is converted with
  `toSignal` at that edge.
- Server state is read with `httpResource()` (stable since v22,
  [Angular guide](https://angular.dev/guide/http/http-resource)) keyed by signals (route parameters,
  filters), using request descriptors built by the clients in `src/app/api/`. Mutations call those
  clients from a feature service and then reload the affected resources. There is no global cache of
  server data.
- The clients use `HttpClient` with the types openapi-typescript generates (R-API-002, Q-API-1),
  so the interceptors (CSRF,
  problem mapping, request ID) apply to every call, and no component calls `/api/v1` directly.
- URL state (filters, sort, tab, version) lives in query parameters and reaches components as signal
  inputs through the router's component input binding; changing a filter navigates with
  `replaceUrl`.
- Shared state of a feature lives in an injectable store service exposing read-only signals and
  methods; no third-party state library in the MVP. A session store holds `whoami`, `authz/me`, the
  check cache and the authorization epoch of the tab's last own permission change (R-UI-042), and
  is reset on 401, on 403 for a cached decision, and on sign-out; a reset on 403 keeps the epoch,
  so the reload it causes still carries it. A permission change made in the tab also reloads
  `authz/me` and clears the check cache, with that epoch sent.
- Forms use Signal Forms (stable since v22,
  [Angular guide](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/overview)) with validators derived from the
  OpenAPI constraints (patterns, lengths) where the generator emits them.
- `computed` and `linkedSignal` derive state; `effect` is reserved for side effects at the boundary
  to non-Angular APIs (browser storage, focus, clipboard).
- Lint rules enforce: no `subscribe(` in components, no `NgZone`, no `bypassSecurityTrust*`, no direct
  `localStorage` access outside the storage wrapper.

Acceptance criteria:

- The lint configuration contains the four rules and CI fails on a violation.
- Changing a filter on the packages list issues exactly one API request and updates the URL.

### R-UI-047 · Testing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

| Tier | Tool | Scope | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest through Angular's unit-test builder | Pure logic: token substitution, JWT decoding, token checksum validation, pattern preview, problem mapping, stores | Every pull request |
| Component | Vitest browser mode with `TestBed`; API answers from the OpenAPI examples | Screens and widgets including keyboard behavior | Every pull request |
| Contract | TypeScript compile against the generated types; mock answers validated against the document | Drift between UI and API | Every pull request |
| End-to-end | Playwright against the chart-installed build in the local profile of [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-051: two `web` and two `worker` pods, PostgreSQL with a standby, Valkey with a replica and three Sentinels, an S3-compatible store (SeaweedFS), the backup CronJob, plus a test OIDC provider and a test CI token issuer | Journeys: sign-in, client setup followed by real `npm` and `dotnet` commands, repository wizard, policy edit, claim tester, token create and revoke, audit entry, system status and backups screens | Smoke on every pull request; full nightly, once in the `scatter` profile (three `web` replicas, round robin per request, R-ARCH-032), once with Valkey stopped, and once while the node drain of R-HA-059 variant A runs, where no journey may fail |
| Accessibility | axe-core in Playwright, plus the manual pass of R-UI-044 | Every route × theme × locale | Every pull request; manual per release |
| Internationalization | Build with missing-translation error; `make web-i18n-check` ([i18n-check.mjs](../../web/scripts/i18n-check.mjs)): the committed translation source equals a fresh `ng extract-i18n`, and the German file has every unit of it, no other, with its location notes and English source | Both locales | Every pull request |
| Security | README XSS corpus; any `securitypolicyviolation` event fails an end-to-end test | Renderer, CSP | Every pull request |
| Renders | `make ui-renders`: Playwright against the UI development profile with a seed through the API ([Q-UI-304](#q-ui-304--make-ui-renders-renders-the-working-tree-through-the-dev-server-signs-the-three-kinds-of-user-in-through-a-provider-of-the-profile-and-seeds-through-the-api)) | Every screen as each kind of user of R-UI-067, both schemes, 1440, 1024 and 390 px, every tab, the whole length; a screen with an error notice, a 4xx or 5xx of the app's own API or a console error fails | Locally, before a UI change is committed (rule 11 of the plan); no CI job |

- End-to-end tests prepare data through the API, not through the UI (INV-17), and run in Chromium on
  pull requests and, in the full run of Test and Release on the commit that closes the phase, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- Line coverage of services and pure logic at least 80 % (# default (proposed)).
- Test tool versions are pinned once in the lockfile and used by local runs and CI alike.

Acceptance criteria:

- The CI workflow runs every tier at the stated cadence, and a deliberately broken snippet template
  fails the end-to-end client-setup test.

The second half is proved by [Q-UI-212](#q-ui-212--a-broken-snippet-template-is-proved-to-fail-by-a-test-on-the-apis-renderer-beside-the-journey-that-holds-the-page-against-the-written-out-text).

### R-UI-048 · Backups
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: OPS-032

`/admin/system/backups`, the tab **Backups** of the page **System status** (R-UI-164), for callers with `settings:read` (as
R-API-050), renders R-API-050. It shows the backup job
of INV-19 and changes nothing: backups are started by the CronJob or by hand with `kubectl`,
configured through the chart and the configuration file, and restored by a Helm hook Job
([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-011, R-BAK-012; Q-API-10).

- **Status.** Last success with its age, the expected interval, "Overdue" (R-API-050's rule) or
  "No backup yet", and
  the last failure with its translated `code` when it is newer than the last success. A run in
  progress shows its phase (`starting`, `snapshot`, `copying`, `finalizing`, `pruning`), tables
  exported, blobs and bytes copied against the totals, its pod and its start time, refreshed with
  the status screen's interval and pause control (R-UI-038). A run whose lease has expired is
  shown as "stopped without finishing; the next run marks it abandoned".
- **Runs.** The list of `GET /api/v1/system/backups` with filters for operation and state (the head of every list, **Filters**
  and its drawer with the chips of the set ones, [Q-UI-566](#q-ui-566--the-jobs-and-the-backup-runs-take-the-head-of-every-list)) and
  "Load more": start, operation, pod, state, backup ID, snapshot time, duration, database bytes,
  blobs copied and warnings. State labels carry icon and text. `interrupted` reads "interrupted by
  a drain or eviction; the Job retries it" and is not shown as a failure (R-BAK-012). A detail panel
  shows the result and the error.
- **Stored backups.** The complete backups that the newest listing run found in the target, with
  backup ID, snapshot time, Quader version, schema step, database and blob sizes and a "damaged"
  mark, headed "as recorded by run <id> at <time>" and the note that `quader backup list` reads the
  target itself (Q-API-11). Next to it, read-only: the target, `keep_last` and `keep_within` as
  that run applied them, and the expected interval.
- **Start a backup now.** No button starts one. A panel shows the command with a copy button,
  filled from `manualRun`:
  `kubectl -n quader create job --from=cronjob/quader-backup quader-backup-manual-<timestamp>`
  (# example), with `<timestamp>` (Unix seconds) filled in by the browser when the panel opens.
  A Job name may have at most 63 characters
  ([Job](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/)), so the browser shortens
  the CronJob part when a long release name would exceed it. Without `manualRun`, the namespace
  and CronJob name appear as placeholders. The panel says that the run appears in the list once its
  pod has started, that it records `trigger: schedule` and is told apart by its pod name
  (R-BAK-012), and that one backup runs at a time (R-BAK-010).
- **Restore.** When `restoredFrom` is set, a notice names the backup ID and snapshot time this
  installation was restored from. Restoring is a Helm operation on an empty installation
  (R-BAK-020, R-BAK-021); the screen links to the operator documentation and offers no restore
  action.

Acceptance criteria:

- During a run, the screen shows phase `copying` and a growing count of copied blobs without a
  reload.
- A run ended `interrupted` by a drain, then completed by the Job's next pod, shows the first as
  interrupted, not failed, and the status shows no failure.
- After two runs with `keep_last: 1`, "Stored backups" lists one backup, recorded by the second
  run.
- The network log of a visit to the screen, including a click on the copy button, contains no
  request with a method other than GET or HEAD.
- With `manualRun.cronJob` set to a 52-character name, the copied command, run with `kubectl`,
  creates the Job, and its name has at most 63 characters.

### R-UI-051 · Avatar upload
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-07: "Upload jetzt mitbauen: nur PNG/JPEG/WebP, serverseitig neu kodiert, max. 1 MiB, als Blob
gespeichert, vom api-Pod ausgeliefert; Spec, Security-Seite und Tests dazu." The API is R-API-055; this requirement is the
screens. The robot that a user without an image gets is R-UI-002. The development agent decided what the owner did not say
(Q-UI-169 to Q-UI-171).

- **Where a user manages their own avatar.** The profile (R-UI-029) opens with a card **Public avatar**, the place the
  reference puts it: the current avatar at 96 px (the uploaded image, or the robot), a **Choose file…** button, **Remove
  avatar** while an image is set, and the help text: PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 1 MiB, at least 32 by 32 pixels, not animated,
  and that the server cuts the picture to a centred square and stores it again as a 256 by 256 pixel PNG, so there is no
  cropper. Choosing a file sends it at once (`PUT /api/v1/users/me/avatar`; the body is the file, `Content-Type` its type, the
  CSRF header as for every session write); there is no second save step (Q-UI-170). **Remove avatar** asks first, then
  sends `DELETE /api/v1/users/me/avatar`. Both give a status message.
- **Checks before sending.** The browser refuses, with the text of the matching server refusal and without a request, an empty
  file, a type other than `image/png`, `image/jpeg` and `image/webp`, a file over 1,048,576 bytes, a file the browser cannot
  decode, and an image under 32 pixels on a side or over 4,194,304 pixels in all (read with `createImageBitmap`). The server
  repeats every check and decides the format from the bytes; only it can tell an animated image (Q-UI-171).
- **The answers.** `415 unsupported_media_type`, `413 payload_too_large`, `400 malformed_request`, `422` with
  `errors[0].code` `animated_image`, `invalid_dimensions` or `undecodable_image`, and `503 server_busy` (which the UI does not
  retry: the user chooses again) each have a sentence in English and German next to the form (R-UI-042, R-UI-045); any other
  answer, `403` included, is the general error notice with the request ID. A refused upload changes nothing on screen.
- **The new URL.** The answer of the upload is the user record; its `avatarUrl` replaces the image everywhere in the page. The
  shell keeps the signed-in user's `avatarUrl` (it reads `GET /api/v1/users/me` once per signed-in principal, because
  `whoami` does not carry it), so the top bar changes without a reload, and a removal puts the robot back. A principal
  that is not a user or the break-glass account (a service account, a CI token) has no avatar and the shell does not ask. The
  old URL is `404` after a replacement and is never requested again. The seed of the robot stays the principal's ID.
- **Moderation.** On the administrator's user screen (R-UI-024) the **Attributes** show the user's avatar (48 px) and, for a
  holder of `identities:write` while an image is set, **Remove avatar**, which asks for a confirmation that names the user and then
  sends `DELETE /api/v1/users/{username}/avatar` (R-API-055). An administrator never sets another user's image.
- **Accessibility and security.** The avatar images are decoration (`alt=""`, hidden from assistive technology): the name is
  next to them. The file input is hidden and its button carries the name; a refusal is announced as an alert. The images
  are same-origin URLs, which the CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`) admits; the UI renders nothing from the uploaded bytes but an
  `<img>`.

Acceptance criteria:

- A signed-in user without an image sees the robot on the profile and in the top bar. After choosing a valid PNG, the top bar
  and the profile show the uploaded image without a reload, and a reload keeps it; **Remove avatar** and its confirmation
  bring the robot back.
- A GIF, an empty file, a file over 1 MiB and an image of 31 by 400 pixels are each refused with a sentence and no
  `PUT` leaves the browser; an animated WebP is refused with the sentence for `animated_image` after the server answers `422`.
- Every refusal code above has an English and a German sentence.
- An administrator with `identities:write` sees **Remove avatar** on the user screen of a user who has an image, after a
  confirmation the image is gone and the robot is shown; without the capability the button is not shown.
- While the profile and the top bar are used, no request leaves Quader's origin.

### R-UI-060 · The Documentation tab of an Ansible collection
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The package page (R-UI-007) of a version of the format `ansible` shows the tab **Documentation** instead of README when `metadata.docs.state` is not `none` or
the version has a README, and makes it the default tab then. The data is that of [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search);
the tab is wiki content and follows the wiki check of [R-ANS-037](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-037--the-documentation-is-wiki-content-which-routes-documents-and-fields-the-wiki-check-gates).

- **Layout** (Q-UI-241): two panes. Tree pane (`clamp(18rem, 30%, 26rem)`): the search field in its head ([Q-UI-243](#q-ui-243--the-search-field-filters-the-tree-through-the-server-and-keeps-the-counts)),
  below it the tree, rows of 32 px: **Documentation** (the README, the other Markdown files and **Changelog** as children; the changelog opens with its head, the member it was read from and, when cut, a note of its own, [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-053), **Modules (n)**, **Plugins (n)** (children by type, collapsed at first with
  their counts, opened when they hold the open page or a match) and **Roles (n)**, each group with its count as a neutral badge; an entry row shows its name, the short description
  as the tooltip; an entry without documentation is muted and labelled "no documentation". Page pane: the open page, as long as the page,
  scrolling with the page; a new page brings the pane's top into view. The tree pane is a navigation column that sticks beside it and
  scrolls its own entries, at most as high as the panel's view (R-UI-215, Q-UI-1112). Under 48 rem of content width one pane shows at a
  time with a back action, each as long as it is; **Back to the tree** brings the entry that was read into view where its group is open.
- **Addressing.** The open page is the query parameter `doc` of the package URL (`README.md`, `module/<name>`, `filter/<name>`, `role/<name>`, `file/<name>`); the search text is `q`;
  a link, a reload and the back button restore both. Changing the version or the repository resets `doc` and `q`. An unknown `doc` shows the first page and no error.
- **Requests.** The tree is one call of `getPackageVersionDocs` per version, repeated only for a search (300 ms after the last key, at least 2 characters); a page is one call of
  `getPackageVersionDocEntry` or `getPackageVersionDocFile`; nothing is requested for a tab that is not shown, and `include` of the version details is not used to learn the state.
- **Pages** are R-UI-061. **States**: `pending` shows "The documentation of this version is being fetched." and a refresh action; `unavailable` shows the reason in words
  (upstream error, too large, invalid document); `none` shows no tab. A search with no match shows "No entries match" in the pane, never an empty tree.

Acceptance criteria:

- The tab for `hans_fischer.common`-like data shows the groups Modules (8) and Plugins (24) with their counts, the README first, and keeps the counts while a search narrows the tree.
- A reload of `…?doc=module/check_host_reachable&q=host` shows the same page and the same narrowed tree.
- A version without a README and with state `none` has no Documentation tab and the page requests none of the operations.
- Keyboard: the tree is a `role="tree"` of links; arrow keys move, Enter opens, `aria-current="page"` marks the open entry; the search field has the label "Search the documentation" and Escape clears it.

### R-UI-061 · An entry page and a file page
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

An entry page (Q-UI-242) shows, in the order ansible-doc prints, a head (the full name `<ns>.<name>.<entry>` with a copy button, the short description, "added in", a `warn` badge for a
deprecated plugin) and the sections Synopsis, Parameters, Notes, Requirements, Attributes, See also, Examples, Return values and Authors, each only when it has content. **Parameters** is the shared data
table (no frame, hairlines) with two columns, as the documentation site has them ([Q-UI-1246](#q-ui-1246--an-entrys-parameters-and-return-values-are-two-columns-as-the-documentation-site-has-them)): Name (with aliases, the type and element type, Required as a text badge, and "added in" under it) and Description (the prose, then the choices or the default, then the configuration); **Return values** likewise (the name with its type; the description with Returned and Sample); a suboption row is indented 16 px per level
with a "suboptions of <name>" label for the screen reader, and a parameter with suboptions is collapsible (open at first, [Q-UI-252](#q-ui-252--the-parameters-of-a-page-are-open-at-every-level-at-first-each-parameter-with-suboptions-folds-on-its-own)). Defaults, choices and samples are text as written; the default among the choices is bold with "(default)". Examples and a sample of several lines are a `<pre>` in the code block
control of the README with a copy button, highlighted as YAML ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-050). The head lists the page's sections; each option and return value has its anchor, a button that copies its link, and its configuration
and "added in <collection> <version>" under its description; the parameters of a lookup, a filter or a test are split into Terms or Input, Positional and Keyword parameters ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md)
R-ANS-048 to R-ANS-050). A role without argument specs shows its README only; a role with them shows a section per entry point (its head, prose and the same option tables, anchors `parameter-<entry point>--<path>`), then its README under **README** ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-052). A page whose entry has `hasDocs` false shows the head and "This plugin has no documentation in its source." (generated) or "The upstream sent no
documentation for this plugin." (upstream). A muted line below says where the documentation comes from ("Generated by Quader from the archive, 2026-11-11 09:41" or "Taken from the upstream") and names
the repository when the version is in more than one. A file page is the README renderer's output (R-UI-008) for a Markdown file.

- **Safety.** The HTML an operation returns is bound with `[innerHTML]` as the README component binds it (Angular's sanitizer and Trusted Types stay on); **every other value of an entry is bound as text**, so a
  hostile default or sample cannot become markup. The lint rule that forbids `bypassSecurityTrust*` (R-UI-046) covers the new components.

Acceptance criteria:

- A module whose parameters nest three levels deep renders three indented levels; a parameter named `<img src=x onerror=1>` appears as that text.
- An entry with `hasDocs` false shows the head and the line, no empty sections.
- A role page shows the README HTML and no Parameters section.

### R-UI-062 · The Contents tab
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The tab **Contents** (shown with the Documentation tab, with the count as a neutral badge) is the flat list of what the version contains: a data table with the columns Name, Type and Short description, a type
filter (a select of the types present with their counts), sorted by type then name, one request (the tree of `getPackageVersionDocs`, shared with the Documentation tab so the two never disagree). A row whose entry has documentation links to
`?tab=documentation&doc=<type>/<name>`; one without is plain text. A version with 5,000 entries (the bound) shows the list in pages of 100 with "Load more".

Acceptance criteria:

- The table lists the 32 entries of the owner's collection with their types; selecting `module` shows 8 and the badge on the tab stays 32.
- A row with documentation opens the entry in the Documentation tab.

### R-UI-063 · The Import log tab and the other tabs of the reference
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The tab **Import log** is shown on a version held by a **local** repository (not for a remote or a virtual repository's remote member): the import task of that version, newest first, through `listAnsibleImportTasks` with the optional query
parameters `package` and `version` (Q-API-262), state as a badge, the time, a failed task's reason and code, and the messages as text (level, message; a
warning's and an error's level in their colour); the warnings of the import (R-ANS-062) and of the generator (R-ANS-034) are among them. The dialog
**Upload collection** shows the task of its publish the same way (R-ANS-061). It is readable by whoever reads the repository, as the task is (R-ANS-009), and is
**not** wiki content.

The other tabs and facts the reference shows are the page's existing ones; nothing is duplicated (Q-UI-240, Q-UI-245):

| Reference | Quader | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Install: description, license, install command, download, Requires Ansible | On the version's page (R-UI-111): the install panel (the command of R-API-030 with the real address), the licences in its facts, the Details tab (**Requires Ansible**, tags), the Files tab (the archive with its SHA-256 and download); the description in the header | R-UI-111, R-ANS-026 |
| Dependencies | A **Dependencies** section of the Details tab: the collections the version needs with their ranges, each a link to that package's page when the installation holds it (muted text otherwise) | Q-UI-245 |
| Distributions | The **Repositories** of the Details tab (the repositories that hold the version) | R-UI-111 |
| Docs site, Website, Issue tracker, Repo | The links of the Details tab: "Docs site" (`documentationUrl`, so named for this format), "Homepage", "Issue tracker" and "Source repository", shown as text links with the external-link marker and only for `http` and `https` | Q-UI-245 |
| Contents, Import log, Documentation | New tabs: R-UI-062, this requirement, R-UI-060 | |

Acceptance criteria:

- A local version shows its import task with the warning of a documentation bound; the same version through a virtual repository over it shows the task of its target, and a remote version has no Import log tab.
- A version with `dependencies` shows the Dependencies section with a link for a collection the installation holds; a link with another scheme than `http` or `https` is not rendered as a link.

### R-UI-064 · States, the wiki check, responsiveness and tests of the documentation screens
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The wiki check.** `metadata.docs` absent means no Documentation and no Contents tab and no request (Q-UI-244); a 404 or a refusal of an operation removes the tab without a message. The Import log and the other tabs are unaffected.
- **Responsiveness.** At 390 px the tree and the page are one pane at a time; at 1440 px both; the parameter table scrolls horizontally inside its region, never the page.
- **Accessibility and style.** Controls are the GitLab-style controls of Q-UI-126 (the tab group, the data table, the text input, the badges), the tree follows R-UI-007's keyboard rules, colours are the tokens of the design language (green only for positive status).
- **Tests.** Web unit tests: the tab choice from `metadata.docs` and `hasReadme`, the tree grouping and counts, the search debounce, minimum length, live region and empty state, the entry sections, text-only binding of hostile values, keyboard, the narrow layout. Browser journeys named in R-ANS-046 (local, remote, virtual, wiki), each asserting the first page's content.

Acceptance criteria: the tests above exist and run in `make web-test`; the journeys run in the e2e set `ansible`; `make web-lint` is green.

### R-UI-065 · One read-only address field with a joined copy button for every client address
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task of 2026-11-11 (T-20): the column **Client address** of the repository list cut the address with an ellipsis
(`https://quader.k8s-main.…`), so it could not be read. Every address that Quader shows for a client to put into its
configuration looks like the field **Clone with SSH** of the owner's GitLab: the whole address in a read-only, bordered field
in a monospace font, with the copy button joined to the field's right edge. It is one shared component,
`<quader-address-field>` ([ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#address-field)); no screen draws its own
`<code>` plus copy button for a client address. The development agent decided what the owner did not say (Q-UI-272 to Q-UI-274);
the widths are Q-UI-300 and Q-UI-301 since the owner's task of 2026-11-12 (T-21), which replaced Q-UI-270 and Q-UI-271 after
the list showed a field of a different width in every row and scrolled sideways.

- **The field.** A read-only `<input type="text">` holding the address, 32 px high, the text in `--quader-font-mono` at 0.875rem,
  a 1 px border in `--quader-control-border`, the fill of an editable control (`--quader-control-bg`), not the grey fill of a
  read-only value (Q-UI-274). The copy button sits in the same row, attached to the right edge: no gap, one border between
  them, the field's right corners and the button's left corners square, the outer corners rounded by `--quader-control-radius`.
  The button is the existing `btn btn-icon` copy button with the glyph `content_copy`.
- **Never cut.** The address is never cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped, and its `title` is not the only way to read it.
  Where the field is shorter than the address, the address scrolls inside the field (an input does so natively), and the
  copy button stays joined to it.
- **One width per place.** A field takes the width of its line, not of its address. No list has an address column: an address
  means nothing without its client, so a list of repositories offers **Set up client** in the row ([Q-UI-426](#q-ui-426--a-projects-repository-list-has-no-client-address-its-row-offers-set-up-client)),
  a project's and the list of every project alike (Q-UI-1042). A field alone on its line fills the line up to a measure
  of 70 characters, so stacked fields are one width too (Q-UI-301).
- **Selectable.** A click or focus in the field selects the whole address; the user can also select a part of it and copy
  with the keyboard. The address is the field's value, so the browser's find, drag and copy work as on any input (Q-UI-273).
- **Copy button.** `aria-label` and `title` name what is copied (**Copy client address**; in a list the label names the row,
  **Copy client address of npm-internal**). A click writes the address to the clipboard and the polite live region says
  **Copied to the clipboard.**; where the clipboard is not available an alert says so and the field stays selectable (the
  behaviour of `quader-copy-button`, which the component reuses). There is no other visual confirmation, and no green
  (owner rule).
- **Name.** The field has an accessible name: `aria-label` = the label of the place (**Client address**, in a list **Client
  address of npm-internal**).
- **Keyboard.** Tab reaches the field, then the button; Enter or Space on the button copies. The field takes the focus ring of
  the other controls; arrow keys, Home and End move inside it. Nothing traps the focus.
- **Colour schemes.** Light and dark both use the control tokens; the border has at least 3:1 against the surface in both
  (R-UI-044).
- **No address, no field.** An empty address renders nothing; the caller decides what stands in its place (a server without a
  configured base URL shows no address, R-REPO-002).
- **Scope (Q-UI-272, Q-UI-320).** The field holds one line to copy: an address (a URL, or a registry host with a path,
  `quader.k8s-main.wds18.de/docker-hub-remote`) or a command of one line (the install command of a package). A configuration
  file or a snippet of several lines keeps the code block with its copy button.

Acceptance criteria:

- Component unit tests: the field's value is the full address for `https://quader.k8s-main.wds18.de/api/npm/npm-internal/`,
  for `quader.k8s-main.wds18.de/docker-hub-remote` and for a 300-character address; the input is `readonly` and has an
  accessible name; no element of the component has `text-overflow: ellipsis`; the field sets no width of its own from its
  address; a field shorter than its address shows its start; a click on the button writes exactly the address to the clipboard
  and sets the status message; a failed write sets the alert; focus in the field selects all of its text; an empty address
  renders nothing; axe finds no violation.
- Rendered (rule 11 of the plan, `make ui-renders`): no repository list scrolls sideways at 1440, 1024 or 390 px, in both schemes,
  with the filter drawer open or closed (Q-UI-330, Q-UI-426).
- Every screen of R-UI-066 shows its address through the component, and no template of those screens gives a client address
  the class `ellipsis`.
- Playwright: a project's repository list holds no address field, and the row's **Set up client** opens the repository's page Set
  up client (`…/repositories/<key>/setup`); so does a row of the list of every project (`/repositories`).

### R-UI-066 · The screens that show a client address use the address field
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Each screen shows its client addresses through `<quader-address-field>` (R-UI-065):

| Screen | Place | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Repository list (R-UI-020), `/projects/{project}/repositories` and `/repositories` | No field: the row's **Set up client** opens the repository's page Set up client, where the address stands with the snippets that use it ([Q-UI-426](#q-ui-426--a-projects-repository-list-has-no-client-address-its-row-offers-set-up-client), Q-UI-1042) | The search results (`/search`) have neither a field nor Set up client (Q-UI-430) |
| Repository settings (R-UI-087), the settings view and the consumer view | No address ([R-UI-169](#r-ui-169--a-repositorys-address-stands-in-a-field-on-set-up-client-only)) | The address stands on Set up client |
| Repository content page (R-UI-052) | No field in the header, whose **Set up client** leads to the address (Q-UI-664); **Details**: each further address with its label | Q-UI-320: the address for downloads by path is not on Set up client |
| Start page (R-UI-166) and the side bar's **Recently opened** (R-UI-167) | No address | The owner's rule of W-20 |
| Set up client (R-UI-120) | The page header: the repository's address on this installation, or on the Bastion chosen under **More options** | The address has its context: the snippets that use it (W-4 of the owner's walk of 2026-11-18) |
| Endpoint page, the address of an exposure rule | No field: the row's copy button, whose name and tooltip carry the address ([Q-UI-331](#q-ui-331--an-endpoints-rules-are-the-shared-data-table-and-a-rules-client-address-is-the-rows-copy-button)) | The administrator manages the rules; the address is handed out with the button |

Not in scope: the text of a guide (server-rendered HTML, where an address is prose in `<code>`), the snippets and commands of
the setup page and the guides, a command of several lines (an install command of one line is a field, Q-UI-320), the
**Base URL** and **Hosts** columns and field of the
endpoint (configuration of an endpoint, not an address given to a client), and digests and fingerprints (a hash is not an
address).

Acceptance criteria:

- A unit test per row of the table that shows a field finds `quader-address-field` with the full address as its value; a row with
  no address finds none.
- A test that read an address from text content reads the field's value instead (an input's value is not text content).

### R-UI-067 · Three kinds of user: the plain user, the power user and the administrator
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task T-21 of 2026-11-12: "Easy access to the product for simple users. Optional details for power users and
admins." The UI serves three kinds of user. A kind is not a role of its own: it is read from the roles and capabilities the
caller already has (R-AUTHZ-010, R-AUTHZ-026, `GET /api/v1/authz/me` of R-UI-005), per project
([Q-UI-310](#q-ui-310--the-kind-of-user-is-read-from-the-roles-in-force-per-project-and-is-no-role-of-its-own)):

| Kind | Who | The job the screens serve first |
|---|---|---|
| **Plain user** | In the project of the screen at most the role `reader`, or a reader through the project's visibility level (R-UI-054); no system role | Find a repository or a package, copy its client address, set up the client, install |
| **Power user** | In the project of the screen the role `developer`, `maintainer` or `owner`; no system role | Publish, maintain the project's repositories and, as its Owner, its members, policies, accounts and settings |
| **Administrator** | A system role (`admin`, `repository-admin`, `security-admin`, `auditor`, `webhook-admin`); each opens the admin area with the screens of its capabilities | All of the above in every project, and the admin area |

One person can be a plain user in one project and a power user in another; outside a project (the start page, the client setup,
the guides) the highest kind of the caller's memberships counts.

- **The main view is the plain user's.** Every screen of the main path (the start page, a project's repository and package
  lists, the repository page, the package page, the client setup) shows first what the plain user's job needs, in the same
  layout for every kind. The decisions per screen are Q-UI-311 to Q-UI-316.
- **Details behind one disclosure.** What only power users and administrators need (configuration facts, statistics, owners and
  claims, internal names) is not in the main view: it sits in one closed section **Details** at the end of the screen's main view,
  the same quiet disclosure on every screen (Q-UI-322), which remembers per user and screen whether it was opened
  ([Q-UI-319](#q-ui-319--the-details-are-one-closed-section-per-screen-that-remembers-whether-the-user-opened-it)). Changes stay on
  the screen's **Settings**, which is offered only to who may change (R-UI-005).
- **Nothing in the way.** The plain user is not offered a read-only copy of a settings page, a sidebar entry of an administration
  screen, or a disabled control of an administrator's action
  ([Q-UI-317](#q-ui-317--the-plain-users-project-sidebar-holds-the-content-the-projects-members-and-settings-move-into-its-about-section)).
  Its main views name no internal terms: no capability names (`projects:write`), no stored-format names, no UUIDs, no request
  IDs outside an error notice ([Q-UI-318](#q-ui-318--the-plain-users-main-views-name-no-internal-terms-a-refusal-says-who-can-do-it)).
- **The power user's work in place.** The power user sees the main view of the plain user plus the actions of its role in the
  screen's header and row menus (publish, create, settings, delete) and the Details; the administrator in addition the admin area
  behind the top bar's Admin button.
- **Simple by default, details on demand** (the owner's rules of 2026-11-12,
  [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)). The power user's flows follow the same rule as the
  plain user's views: creating and configuring a repository asks only what the repository needs to work, for every format and
  class; access in it is the members and the visibility level (R-UI-055); every other setting (patterns, disabling, hiding
  existence, administrator notes, mirror and protocol tuning) is in a detail view or behind an advanced-settings section, never a
  step; a remote's connection is tested where its upstream is entered; a default is a field's value, a field is as wide as its
  input, a title names the format, and a field shows an error only after it was touched or on submit, in words and never as a
  pattern (the shared text and select fields hold the rule for every form: an error waits until the field was left once or a
  submit of its form was attempted, UI-A-42). The creation flow and the
  repository settings are planned on T-18's tree (T-21, "Creating and configuring a repository") and are not decided on this page;
  their defects are in the audit.

This page specifies the kinds and the decisions; the screens follow them in the fix waves of the audit of 2026-11-12,
each change rendered under rule 11 (R-UI-047, `make ui-renders`).

Acceptance criteria:

- `make ui-renders` renders every screen of the main path as `sam` (plain user), `priya` (power user) and `ada` (administrator)
  of its seed, and the pictures show for each kind what Q-UI-311 to Q-UI-319 say; the audit lists every difference until it is
  fixed.
- The plain user reaches a repository's client address from the start page in at most two steps and the client setup of that
  repository in at most three, without passing a settings page.
- No main view of the plain user shows a capability name, a UUID or a settings page it cannot change.

### R-UI-080 · A new repository: the format first, then one form that names it
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- **The format chooser.** `/projects/{project}/repositories/new` is a page titled **New
  repository**, with the sentence "Choose the package format. It decides what the repository can do." and the tiles of the
  installed formats from `GET /api/v1/formats` (the format's icon, Q-UI-225, and its display name) under the field **Search by
  package type** (Q-UI-115). A format that is system only (`systemOnly`, [formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001) is no
  tile, no part of the count "N of N formats" and found by no search: the installation creates its one repository itself
  ([Q-UI-1200](#q-ui-1200--a-system-only-format-is-left-out-of-every-choice-for-something-new-and-kept-wherever-something-is-found-or-shown)). A tile is a link to the form of its format; Enter in the search field opens the one format that is
  left. There is no Next button ([Q-UI-340](#q-ui-340--a-new-repository-is-a-format-chooser-and-one-form-as-the-references-new-project)).
- **The form.** `/projects/{project}/repositories/new/{format}` is one page titled
  **New <display name> repository** ("New OCI (Docker) repository", "New npm repository", Q-UI-353) with a link **Change format**
  back to the chooser. In this order (the project is given by the address and named in the line under the title, Q-UI-1040): **Class**,
  **Key**, **Description (optional)**, **Visibility**, the class's own group (**Upstream** for remote, **Members** for virtual),
  the closed section **Advanced settings** (R-UI-083), the disclosure **Show as API request**, then **Create repository** and
  **Cancel**. One column of at most 56 rem. In the admin area the project is a select, held while the projects load; a project
  the user chose stays chosen whatever the address binds later.
- **Class** is a radio group of the three classes, each with its sentence; a class the format does not implement is disabled with
  its reason (Q-UI-113). Preset: local. Another class keeps the project, an edited key, the description and the visibility, and
  starts its own group and the Advanced settings from the defaults of that class (R-REPO-063, [Q-UI-341](#q-ui-341--the-class-is-a-radio-group-of-the-form-preset-to-local)).
- **Change format** returns to the chooser; what was typed is not carried over, and the unsaved guard asks first when something was.
- An unknown format in the address shows the chooser with the notice "This installation has no format <name>.", the name as a value of
  running text (Q-UI-1213), and the chooser's trail, which ends at one step **New repository**
  ([Q-UI-1215](#q-ui-1215--a-resolved-title-that-repeats-the-step-before-it-adds-no-step)).
- A system-only format in the address (`/projects/{project}/repositories/new/clamav`) offers no form: the page is the chooser, titled
  **New repository**, under the note "This installation creates the repository of ClamAV definitions itself; it is not created here.",
  followed by "It is upstream/clamav." with the link to the repository's page where the reader sees a repository of the format (the
  first of `GET /api/v1/repositories?format=<format>`; nothing is said of one the reader does not see). The defaults of the form are not
  asked ([Q-UI-1201](#q-ui-1201--the-forms-address-of-a-system-only-format-shows-the-chooser-with-one-sentence-and-its-repository)).
- **Create repository** sends the document with the `Idempotency-Key` generated when the form opened (R-UI-042) and opens the new
  repository's content page (R-UI-052). **Show as API request** shows the body (a typed password as `<the password>`, R-UI-043)
  and the same request as `curl`. A form that asks for a recent sign-in keeps its draft without secrets, as before.

- **Show as API request** is the form's last closed section, under **Advanced settings** and with its chevron: the request body
  and the same request with curl ([Q-UI-552](#q-ui-552--every-fold-is-the-shared-disclosure-a-fold-inside-a-section-is-its-inline-form)).

Acceptance criteria:

- **New repository** on the repository list opens the chooser; typing `nu` leaves the NuGet tile; Enter opens a page whose
  `<h1>` is "New NuGet repository", with no step list and no Next button.
- With a test format whose classes lack `virtual`, the class Virtual is disabled with "<Format> does not implement the class
  Virtual." and Local is chosen.
- With ClamAV's definitions in the catalog, the chooser counts "6 of 6 formats", has no tile of it and "clam" finds nothing; its form's
  address shows the note with the link to `upstream/clamav` and no form (Vitest, `repository-format-chooser.spec.ts` and
  `repository-create.spec.ts`, milliseconds; rendered: `repository-new`, `repository-new-system-only`).
- Double-clicking **Create repository** creates one repository.

### R-UI-081 · The standard fields of each class
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031, UI-032

- **Every class:** **Key** (R-UI-086; it starts with the `suggestedKey` of R-REPO-063), **Description (optional)**, **Visibility**
  (the artifacts group of R-UI-055, preset to the `visibility` of R-REPO-063; the wiki follows the artifacts at create).
- **Remote:** the group **Upstream** of R-UI-082.
- **Virtual:** the group **Members**: the picker of R-UI-022 over the local and remote repositories of the project and the format,
  the ordered members with Add, Remove, Move up, Move down and Move to top, and **Deployment target**, a select of **None** and the
  local members, set to the first local member when the first one is added (Q-UI-347).
- Nothing else is in the main form: no administrator notes, no patterns, no switches, no format settings ([Q-UI-343](#q-ui-343--the-standard-flow-holds-what-a-repository-needs-to-work-and-no-format-setting)).
- When `getRepositoryDefaults` cannot be read (a refusal, or a server that does not answer it), the key starts empty and the
  **Visibility** group is left out: the create sends no `visibility`, and the server applies its default (R-REPO-004).

Acceptance criteria:

- Pressing **Create repository** on the form of a local generic repository without typing anything creates the repository of
  the suggested key, and its document holds the defaults of R-REPO-004.
- A virtual npm repository created with `npm-local` and `npm-remote` as members reads back `virtual.members` in that order and
  `virtual.deployTarget: "npm-local"` without the deployment target being touched.

### R-UI-082 · Well-known upstreams and Test connection where the upstream is entered
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031, RMT-004

- Above **Upstream URL**, the group **Well-known registries** has one button per entry of the format's `upstreamPresets`
  (R-REPO-062), in the format's order, labelled with its display name (`translate="no"`). A button sets the URL to its preset's.
  The button whose URL equals the field, compared as the server normalizes it, is pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`); any other URL
  presses none. A format without presets has no group, and its URL field starts empty and is required ([Q-UI-345](#q-ui-345--the-presets-are-buttons-with-names-and-the-pressed-one-follows-the-url)).
- After it, in the creation form, the group **Registries of this installation** has one button per registry preset of the installation
  for the format (`registryPresets` of R-REPO-063, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-076), in the
  administrator's order, labelled with its display name (`translate="no"`) and pressed by the same comparison. A button sets the URL
  to its preset's, and the further hosts follow it until they are edited, as they follow a well-known preset (the test of the connection
  sends them too); it never sets a credential, and the create names `extraHosts` for it
  ([Q-REPO-418](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-418--a-registry-preset-is-a-value-put-into-the-form-and-nothing-follows-it)). The
  settings page of a stored repository shows the well-known registries only
  ([Q-UI-907](#q-ui-907--the-registries-of-this-installation-are-a-group-of-their-own-after-the-well-known-ones-in-the-creation-form)).
  A format without well-known presets shows this group alone; its URL field still starts empty and is required, and the hint under it
  reads "Choose a registry of this installation or enter the address of another."
- The URL field starts with the default preset's URL. **Authentication** (None, Username and password, Bearer token), **Username**
  and **Password or token** follow (write-only, Q-UI-123). Under the password one muted line names where the credential goes: the
  URL's host and every further host that receives it ("The credential is sent to registry.gitlab.com and gitlab.com.").
- **Test connection** follows the credentials. It sends the unsaved section (`testUpstream`, R-REPO-024, R-REPO-064) and shows the
  server's `verdict` in words (Q-UI-124, [Q-REPO-488](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-488--the-upstream-tests-answer-carries-its-verdict),
  [Q-UI-1225](#q-ui-1225--a-test-says-the-servers-verdict-with-one-tone-table)); no screen derives a verdict from the status. Below
  the verdict stands what the test learned, without a click, and **Copy report**, in the one result of every connection test
  ([Q-UI-1226](#q-ui-1226--a-tests-result-shows-what-it-learned-in-one-shared-component-with-copy-report)). A result goes when a
  field of the section changes. When the answer is `foreign_host_denied` with a
  `tokenService`, the result names that host and offers **Allow <host>**, which adds it to the further hosts (receiving the credential
  when Authentication is not None) and runs the test again ([Q-UI-346](#q-ui-346--test-connection-names-a-token-service-that-is-not-allowed-and-offers-to-allow-it)).
- Inside the group, the region **Upstream details** (a toggle with `aria-expanded`, closed by default) holds **Further hosts** (one
  row per host pattern with a checkbox **Receives the credential**, **Add host**, **Remove**; it starts with the preset's hosts and
  follows the preset until it is edited), **Metadata cache period in seconds** and **Negative cache period in seconds**, the checkbox
  **Start the download when a version is asked for** (`remote.downloadOnProbe`, checked by default, R-REPO-065,
  [Q-UI-766](#q-ui-766--the-switch-of-the-background-download-is-a-checkbox-of-the-upstream-details)) with the hint "A client that asks
  for one version without downloading it, such as for an image's manifest, starts its download in the background, charged to that
  client's limits.", and, on the settings page only, **Offline**.
- A create writes what Q-UI-122 says, and `extraHosts` only when the list differs from the hosts the server stores for that URL
  without it (R-REPO-062). The settings page writes the section as Q-UI-122 says, with `extraHosts` always present.

Acceptance criteria:

- **New OCI (Docker) repository**, class Remote: the buttons Docker Hub, Quay, GitHub (ghcr.io) and GitLab; Docker Hub is pressed and
  the URL is `https://registry-1.docker.io/`. Pressing GitLab sets `https://registry.gitlab.com/` and shows `gitlab.com` under
  Further hosts as receiving the credential; the create sends `remote: {url: "https://registry.gitlab.com/"}`, and the stored
  document holds `extraHosts: [{pattern: "gitlab.com", sendCredentials: true}]`.
- Against a test registry whose token service is on a host the repository does not list, **Test connection** names that host and
  offers **Allow**; after it, the test runs again and the token service accepts the typed credential.
- **New npm repository**, class Remote: one button, pressed; the cache periods read 7200 and 1800; a create that changes nothing
  sends no `remote` member.
- With the installation's preset Harbor for OCI (`https://harbor.example.com/`, `harbor.example.com` receiving the credential), **New OCI
  (Docker) repository**, class Remote, shows **Registries of this installation** with Harbor after the four well-known buttons; pressing
  it presses Harbor alone, shows `harbor.example.com` under Further hosts, and the create sends `remote: {url: "https://harbor.example.com/",
  extraHosts: [{pattern: "harbor.example.com", sendCredentials: true}]}`.

### R-UI-083 · Details on demand
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- The form's section **Advanced settings** (`<quader-disclosure>`, closed) has the sentence "Notes, paths and the settings of
  the format. The defaults suit most repositories." (of a remote: "Notes, access details, the mirror and the settings of the format.
  The defaults suit most repositories.") and these groups, each under its own heading, where they apply:
  **Administrator notes**; **Paths** (include and exclude patterns, the pattern syntax; a local or a virtual repository only: a remote
  has none, its delivery rules decide what it delivers, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-002); **Access details** (Hide existence);
  **Mirror** (a remote of a format with `mirror`: the mode, and in mode mirror the members of `remote.mirror` and the format's own
  `mirror` member, such as `oci.mirror` or `deb.mirror`); **<Display name> settings** (the format's other schema members for the class;
  absent when there are none) ([Q-UI-344](#q-ui-344--where-the-details-go)).
- **Disabled** and **Offline** are not offered at creation; the settings page has them.
- The details of the upstream fold inside its group (R-UI-082), not in Advanced settings.
- A field error inside a closed region opens the region: on **Create repository** and from the link of the error summary.

Acceptance criteria:

- The form of a local npm repository shows **Advanced settings** closed; opened, it shows Administrator notes, Paths, Access details
  and npm settings with **latestGuard**, and no Disabled.
- An OCI remote in mode mirror shows the tags of `oci.mirror` in the Mirror group; every OCI remote shows **Platforms** (`oci.platforms`)
  under "OCI (Docker) settings" with `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` in the field, one per line
  ([Q-UI-767](#q-ui-767--the-platforms-of-an-oci-remote-stand-in-its-format-settings-for-both-modes)).
- A create refused with a field error at `/includePatterns/0` opens Advanced settings and puts the error at the include patterns.

### R-UI-084 · A default is the value of its field
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- A field whose setting has a static default shows the default as its value, editable: the key (`suggestedKey`), the class
  (local), the visibility, the URL (the default preset), the further hosts (the preset's), the cache periods, the members of
  `remote.mirror`, the deployment target (the first local member) and every member of the format's schema with a `default`,
  text and number fields included. The values come from `getRepositoryDefaults` (R-REPO-063) for the document's members and from
  `settingsSchema` for the format's member ([Q-UI-348](#q-ui-348--a-default-is-the-value-of-its-field)).
- A value equal to its default is not written (Q-UI-80). A field the user empties shows its default again when it is left.
- A field the person is in never changes under their hands
  ([Q-UI-702](#q-ui-702--a-default-that-arrives-while-its-field-has-the-focus-waits-until-the-field-is-left)): a default that
  `getRepositoryDefaults` answers while the key, a cache period or a number of the mirror group has the focus is shown when the
  field is left, and only if it still takes a default then (the key until it is edited, Q-UI-342; a period or a number while it
  holds no value of its own).
- A setting whose default is derived from other settings has no static value: a choice offers **Automatic** first (npm
  `audit.mode`, NuGet `vulnerabilityInfo`), a text stays empty with its description (Debian `label`, which is the key while unset).
- No "Default: …" hint line remains.

Acceptance criteria:

- An OCI remote shows 300 in both cache periods; in mode mirror, 3600 as the pass interval and 4 as the concurrent fetches; a
  local Debian repository shows the architectures `amd64` and `arm64` and the origin `quader`. A create that changes none of them
  writes none of them.
- The class Remote chosen and the key entered before the class's defaults are answered: the key keeps what it showed, a key typed
  there is created as typed, and a key left untouched shows `npm-remote` once it is left; the same for a cache period and the pass
  interval (`repository-create.spec.ts`).

### R-UI-085 · A field is as wide as its expected input
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- The six widths of the style guide's **Forms**, tokens in `_tokens.scss`, classes in `_controls.scss` and the input `width` of
  `<quader-text-field>` and `<quader-select-field>` ([Q-UI-334](#q-ui-334--a-picker-is-one-control-from-the-start-held-while-its-list-loads-and-a-field-is-as-wide-as-its-kind-of-input));
  which field of the repository forms takes which is [Q-UI-349](#q-ui-349--a-field-of-the-repository-forms-takes-the-width-of-its-kind-of-input-and-a-schema-member-the-width-of-its-type):

  | Class | Token | Width | For |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `field-w-number` | `--quader-field-width-number` | 6 rem | a count of up to six digits |
  | `field-w-duration` | `--quader-field-width-duration` | 8 rem | a period in seconds, up to eight digits |
  | `field-w-bytes` | `--quader-field-width-bytes` | 13 rem | a byte count, up to nineteen digits |
  | `field-w-version` | `--quader-field-width-version` | 16 rem | a version with the list of versions it offers: a bound of a range ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-010, R-CUR-026) |
  | `field-w-name` | `--quader-field-width-name` | 28 rem, half the column | a key, a name, a host, a description, every select and every picker |
  | `field-w-full` | — | the column | a URL, a note, a list, a key block |

- A field is never wider than its column; a narrower column shrinks it and its text scrolls inside it.
- Which field gets which: key, username, password, project, authentication, hide existence, discovery, deployment target, a host
  of Further hosts, description (one sentence, [Q-UI-551](#q-ui-551--a-description-is-as-wide-as-a-name)): `name`; upstream URL,
  administrator notes, patterns: `full`; the two cache periods, the pass and
  full-pass intervals: `duration`; concurrent fetches, versions per package: `number`; storage limit: `bytes`. A schema member:
  `integer` and `number` → `number`; a string with `format: uri` or `maxLength` above 128, and every list → `full`; any other
  string and every choice → `name`.
