Acceptance criteria:

- At the wide width of `make ui-renders`, the metadata cache period field is 8 rem wide and the URL field spans the column; at the
  narrow width no part of the form scrolls sideways.

### R-UI-086 · An error shows when it helps
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- A field's own error (its shape, a required value) appears only after the field was left with a value, or after **Create
  repository** or a section's **Save changes** was pressed; never on a field that was not touched, empty or prefilled
  ([Q-UI-350](#q-ui-350--an-error-appears-after-the-field-was-left-or-the-form-was-sent)).
- **Create repository** is enabled while nothing is being sent. Pressed with errors, it sends nothing, shows the error summary
  with a link per field and moves the focus to the summary.
- The key's availability is asked 400 ms after the last keystroke; "A repository with this key already exists in the project." is
  shown when the answer comes, because it answers what was typed. The suggested key is free when the form opens (R-REPO-063), and
  a key the person did not type is never asked: not while another class's suggestion loads either.
- An error says what to do: "Use 2 to 64 lower-case letters and digits, with ., _, __ or - between them." Server field errors
  appear at their fields whatever was touched.

Acceptance criteria:

- The opened form shows no error. Typing `A` into the key and leaving it shows the message; clearing the key and pressing **Create
  repository** shows the summary and sends no request.

### R-UI-087 · The repository's settings page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

The settings page follows the style guide's settings pages: one column of at most 56 rem, no tab group
([Q-UI-351](#q-ui-351--the-repository-settings-page-is-one-column-of-sections)). In this order, where they apply:

1. At the top, without a title: **Key** (a read-only field) and **Description (optional)**, with **Save changes**.
2. **Visibility**, open: the block of R-UI-055 with its own save: the one level, and for a format with wiki content the fold
   **Wiki visibility**, closed while the wiki has the repository's level.
3. **Upstream** (remote), open: R-UI-082 with its **Upstream details** region, which holds **Offline** here.
4. **Members** (virtual), open: the editor of R-UI-022 with its own save.
5. Closed: **Mirror** (status above the settings, R-UI-021, and the format's `mirror` member), **<Display name> settings**, **Access
   details** (include and exclude patterns, Hide existence; of a remote only Hide existence, R-CUR-002, and none on a well-known remote,
   whose Hide existence is the product's), **Administrator notes**, **Signatures** (the background fetch of a remote and
   the gate **Only artifacts with a verified signature can be downloaded from this repository**, [signatures.md](signatures.md)
   R-SIG-040 and R-SIG-074), **Download links** (every repository but a system repository: the repository's opt-out of
   signed links, disabled with its reason where it cannot act, R-UI-201, Q-UI-956), **Signing keys** and **Indexes** (Debian local and virtual), **Import tasks** and **Tombstones**
   (Ansible), **Details** (class, format, layout, project,
   client address, created, last changed, last activity), **API** (the stored document; each section's unsaved change as a request),
   **Advanced** ([Q-UI-352](#q-ui-352--disable-move-and-delete-are-in-advanced)): **Disable repository** or **Enable repository**,
   **Move to another project**, **Delete repository**.

- Each section's **Save changes** sends only its members as a merge patch with `If-Match`; a `412` opens the conflict dialog of
  R-UI-042 for that section; the other sections keep their unsaved edits.
- A closed section that holds an unsaved change says "Unsaved changes" after its title; leaving the page with one asks first.
- The open sections (Visibility, Upstream, Members) have a heading and no toggle. A closed section whose content is read from
  the server (Signing keys, Indexes, Import tasks, Tombstones) reads it when it is first opened; the mirror's status is
  read only while the section Mirror is open. The page's header names the repository with the icon of its level, and a disabled
  repository with the badge **Disabled**.
- The section Mirror shows an unset member of `remote.mirror` with the default of `getRepositoryDefaults` (R-REPO-063) for the
  repository's project and format, and a save leaves a member equal to it unwritten; the client keeps no copy of these defaults.
  A caller the server refuses them to sees the stored members only.
- A caller who may not change the repository sees the fields read-only and no save; the reduced view of a caller without
  `repositories:read-config` is unchanged.
- A repository of the project `upstream` shows what R-UI-190 says: the product's members read-only, the state, the level, the
  address and the account with a link to its page in the admin area, and the narrowing settings editable.

Acceptance criteria:

- The settings of a remote OCI repository show Key, Description, Visibility and Upstream open, every other section closed, and no
  tab. Saving a changed description sends `{"description": …}` and nothing else.
- With an unsaved include pattern in the closed Access details, the section says "Unsaved changes", and leaving the page asks.

### R-UI-201 · The repository's settings: the section Download links
Priority: **P1** · Covers: STOR-032

Built on 2026-11-23 (package 3): [repository-download-links.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-download-links.ts).

- **Where** ([Q-UI-955](#q-ui-955--the-repositorys-opt-out-is-a-closed-section-shown-only-where-a-link-can-happen), changed by
  [Q-UI-956](#q-ui-956--the-repositorys-section-stands-on-every-repository-disabled-with-its-reason-where-it-cannot-act)): a closed section
  **Download links** of the repository's settings page (R-UI-087), after **Signatures**; never part of a creation form, not even of its
  advanced settings. It stands on every repository but a system repository, of every format and class.
- **What it holds:** the checkbox **Downloads of this repository may go by signed links of the object store**, checked by default
  (`storage.downloadLinks`), with one line on why it acts or when, and its own **Save changes**, as every section of R-UI-087:
  - the format has a route whose clients all check a digest (`formats` of `GET /api/v1/download-links/switch`, R-STOR-014; today OCI and
    Ansible Galaxy, every class; npm no longer,
    [Q-STOR-354](storage.md#q-stor-354--yarn-4-installs-a-tarball-whose-object-was-altered-so-npms-tarball-route-declares-nothing)): the
    checkbox is usable whatever the installation's switch says. With the switch on it says "The installation delivers large downloads by
    link."; with the switch off "The installation does not hand downloads to links at the moment; your choice takes effect when an
    administrator switches them on.", so that an Owner opts a repository out before the switch goes on. A virtual repository adds "A
    member that does not allow it is delivered by Quader.";
  - not every client of the format checks a digest (the member is `not_applicable`): the checkbox is unchecked and disabled, with "Not
    every <Format> client checks the bytes it downloads against a digest, so Quader delivers every download of this repository itself."
    This is the one state that disables it.
  The switch is read once per page load; a switch that could not be read says nothing of the installation, and the API decides.
- German: **Download-Links**; **Downloads dieses Repositorys dürfen über signierte Links des Objektspeichers gehen**; "Ob große Downloads
  dieses Repositorys direkt aus dem Objektspeicher kommen dürfen." (the section's hint); "Die Installation liefert große Downloads per Link
  aus."; "Die Installation gibt derzeit keine Downloads an Links ab; Ihre Wahl wirkt, sobald ein Administrator sie einschaltet."; "Ein
  Mitglied, das es nicht erlaubt, wird von Quader ausgeliefert."; "Nicht jeder <Format>-Client prüft die heruntergeladenen Bytes gegen einen
  Digest, deshalb liefert Quader jeden Download dieses Repositorys selbst aus."
- A caller who may not change the repository sees the state as text: "Downloads of this repository may go by signed links of the object
  store." or "Quader delivers every download of this repository itself." („Downloads dieses Repositorys dürfen über signierte Links des
  Objektspeichers gehen.“, „Quader liefert jeden Download dieses Repositorys selbst aus.“).
- A save sends `{"storage": {"downloadLinks": <value>}}` with `If-Match`; the merge patch keeps `storage.maxUploadSize`. A well-known
  repository of `upstream` takes the administrator's write, as its other narrowing settings (R-REPO-069).

Acceptance criteria:

- Web unit (Vitest): the section stands closed after **Signatures**; on an OCI repository unchecking and saving sends
  `{"storage": {"downloadLinks": false}}` with `If-Match`; on a NuGet repository the checkbox is disabled with the sentence of a format not
  every client of which checks; with the installation's switch off it stays usable, says when the choice takes effect and saves; a virtual
  repository says what a member does; a caller who may not change it reads text (`repository-download-links.spec.ts`).

### R-UI-088 · A title and a heading name one thing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-031

- The form's title names the format (R-UI-080). Every section and group heading names one topic; no heading lists several.
- A label is the setting in sentence case, its unit included ("Metadata cache period in seconds"); a help text is one line. The
  key's help: "Part of the repository's address. It cannot be changed later."
- A format setting's label is the `title` of its member in the format's settings schema (Q-UI-79), which every member of every
  format's schema has ("Tags to mirror", not `tags`). A title or a description of a schema is read by users and names no
  requirement or decision ID.
- A format setting's description says what the setting does for the user and when to change it, in one or two sentences of plain
  words: no HTTP status, no error code, no configuration key or member name, no `null`, and a limit in words ("1 to 300 seconds,
  written like 30s"). The wording of the specification stays with the format's page of the specification and the member's
  description in the OpenAPI document (Q-UI-79).
- Each value of a setting's `enum` has a label of its own in the member's `x-quader-enum-titles`, which the select shows
  ("Delete for good", not `delete`); a choice without a static default still offers **Automatic** first (R-UI-084), and the
  description says what Automatic does.
- An object of a schema is a group under its own heading, in the type of the page's other group headings and without a frame
  (Q-UI-78): npm's **Security audit** reads like **Paths** in the creation form's Advanced settings.

Acceptance criteria:

- No heading of the form or of the settings page holds "and" between two topics.
- Every member of every format's settings schema has a `title`, and no title or description of the five schemas holds an `R-…`
  or `Q-…` ID.
- No title, description or value label of the five schemas holds an HTTP status, a dotted configuration key, an error code, a
  member name in camelCase or `null`, no description has more than two sentences, and every value of a member's `enum` has a
  label (`TestR_UI_088_EverySettingOfAFormatHasATitleAndPlainTexts`).
- The creation form of an npm remote shows **Security audit** as a heading in Advanced settings, with no frame around its fields,
  and its **Mode** offers Automatic, "From Quader's advisory data", "Forward to an advisory service" and "Off".

### R-UI-090 · The grade shield
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task of 2026-11-12 (T-21): "Vulnerabilities shall be shown as we realised it in cogpit." A version's grade
([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-038) is drawn as cogpit draws an image's: a crest with its letter.
`<quader-grade-shield>` ([grade-shield.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-shield.ts)) is the one drawing of it; no
screen draws its own.

- **The crest.** An inline SVG in a box of 100: two shallow arcs across the top that meet in a point at its middle, the sides
  straight down to half the height, then curving to a point at the bottom (cogpit's geometry). Its fill runs from 25 % lighter at
  the top to 25 % darker at the bottom of the grade's colour; S has a gold rim. N/A is flat and quiet.
- **The letter** is SVG text in the sans face at weight 700, 54 % of the side, centred at 46 % of the height (the point takes room
  below); "N/A" at 56 % of that size.
- **Sizes.** 20 px in a list, a header and a tab, the size of a format's icon in a list
  ([Q-UI-381](#q-ui-381--the-shield-in-a-list-is-20-px-the-size-of-a-format-icon)); 32 px on the card.
- **Colours** ([Q-UI-370](#q-ui-370--the-grades-take-cogpits-colours-and-s-a-and-b-are-the-greens-of-a-good-grade)): the tokens
  `--quader-grade-s` to `--quader-grade-e`, `--quader-grade-na`, the rim `--quader-grade-rim` and the letters' inks
  `--quader-grade-s-ink`, `--quader-grade-ink`, `--quader-grade-ink-on-dark`, `--quader-grade-na-ink`; S to E are the same in both
  schemes, N/A is the scheme's quiet grey. The letter keeps 4.5:1 on its fill (`palette.spec.ts`).
- **Never by colour alone.** The letter says the grade, and the grade's text stands beside the shield wherever it is shown; there
  the shield is decorative (`aria-hidden`). Alone, it is `role="img"` named **Grade E**
  ([Q-UI-371](#q-ui-371--the-shield-is-an-inline-svg-whose-letter-is-text-and-it-is-decorative-beside-its-text)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: for each grade the SVG carries the letter as text and the grade's class; `size` sets 20 or 32 px; with a label it is an
  image with that name, without one it is hidden from the accessibility tree; axe finds no serious violation.
- The contrast of every letter on its fill and of N/A's crest and letter is held by `palette.spec.ts`.

### R-UI-091 · The grade's text and rule
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The text** is the grade and the count that decides it, as R-VULN-038 words it: "E · 13 Critical", "C · OS end of life",
  "S · no known vulnerabilities", "N/A · Queued"; the letter at weight 600. **The rule** is the sentence of R-VULN-038's
  table; for S of an image "No known vulnerabilities, and the OS is supported".
- **N/A is never said bare** (the owner, 2026-11-25; [Q-UI-1120](#q-ui-1120--na-says-its-state-in-a-word-and-its-sentence-is-the-cells-description)).
  Beside the N/A shield stands the word of the grade's `state` (R-VULN-039), the server's, never a sentence of the server's: "Queued",
  "Scanning", "No scanner", "No database", "No advisory data", "Scan failed", "Scanning off", "Not matched", "Internal", "Not scanned",
  "Not an image" (German "Wartet", "Wird geprüft", "Kein Scanner", "Keine Datenbank", "Keine Advisory-Daten", "Prüfung fehlgeschlagen",
  "Prüfung aus", "Nicht abgeglichen", "Intern", "Nicht geprüft", "Kein Image"). The sentence of **Not scanned** (`format_not_scanned`)
  says the reason of the format where the screen knows the format (the owner, 2026-11-25,
  [Q-UI-1244](#q-ui-1244--not-checked-for-vulnerabilities-says-the-reason-of-the-format)): an Ansible collection has no public advisory source that lists it by version, Debian's advisories
  name source packages and releases and the matching is not built yet, a file has no package name and version an advisory could name.
  Its sentence, why and what comes ("Waits for its
  vulnerability scan since 25 Nov 2026, 08:31. It is scanned in turn, without anyone having to act."), is the cell's tooltip and
  accessible description, and the rule of the version page's card, which folds a failed or put-off scan's `stateCode` under
  **Technical details** ([technical-details.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/technical-details.ts), R-UI-214). One component says it in every
  list of every format (`<quader-grade>`), so a list's new rows take it as it is. `<quader-grade>` and `<quader-grade-card>` take
  `image` (the format is OCI), for the rule of S. A state an administrator must repair ("No scanner", "No database", "No advisory data",
  "Scan failed") stands in the warning's colour, in a list, on the version's line and on its card; a state that passes or was chosen
  stays neutral, by the one rule of both scans ([Q-UI-1214](#q-ui-1214--a-scans-state-is-a-warning-where-an-administrator-must-repair-something-and-neutral-otherwise)).
  **Revised on 2026-11-18 (owner, walk objection W-9): beside its shield the letter is not written a second time.** The shield
  carries the letter; the text beside it is the count that decides ("13 Critical", "OS end of life", "no known vulnerabilities",
  "not scanned"), in a list, on a version's row and facts line, and on the card. A screen reader still hears "Grade E · 13
  Critical": the letter and its separator are in the text, hidden from sight. Where no shield stands (a tooltip, the order of a
  sort) the text keeps its letter. The shield is centred on the line it stands in, whatever that line's height, and adds
  nothing to it; in a table cell a badge is too, so that the text of every cell of a row stands on one line (Q-UI-308).
- **Revised on 2026-11-18 (R-UI-143, Q-UI-556):** beside the shield, in every list and on a version's page, the text is the
  statement of R-UI-112, the total and the fixable findings; the deciding count ("13 Critical") and the rule are the tooltip's and
  the card's.
- `<quader-grade>` ([grade.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade.ts)) is the shield of 20 px and the text on one line,
  for a list cell, a header and a tab. Its tooltip (`[quaderTooltip]`) names every count, "13 Critical · 160 High · 113 Medium ·
  16 Low · 843 Unknown", and "OS end of life" when it is; the text stays the accessible name of the cell.
- The words are the UI's, translated (`vuln.grade.*`); the grade is the server's (R-VULN-039). `gradeText`, `gradeRule` and
  `gradeRank` ([grade-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-words.ts)) derive them from the grade, its counts and
  its end of life and never decide the grade again.

Acceptance criteria:

- A table test of the text, the rule and the rank over the boundaries of R-VULN-038 (0, 10 and 11 Low, 1, 5 and 6 Critical, the
  end of life, N/A) and of the order E · 13 > E · 6 > D · 4 > D · 2 > C · 120 > S > N/A.
- Unit: `<quader-grade>` shows the shield and the text, its tooltip names every count; axe finds no serious violation.
- Unit (Vitest, milliseconds): every `state`'s word and sentence, in English and in the German build; the cell's tooltip and accessible
  description; the card's code under **Technical details**.

### R-UI-092 · The severity bar
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

`<quader-severity-bar>` ([severity-bar.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/severity-bar.ts)) draws open findings by severity
as cogpit draws an image's:

- **Five segments** in one row, Critical, High, Medium, Low and Unknown, `none` counted in Low (Q-VULN-153); 22 px high, 4 px apart,
  rounded by `--quader-radius-s`; each segment's count inside it, centred, at 12 px and weight 700, in tabular figures.
- **Width by share** ([Q-UI-372](#q-ui-372--the-bars-segments-are-as-wide-as-their-share-with-room-for-their-number)): each
  segment first gets the room of its number and its padding, then the rest of the row is shared by the segments' shares of all
  findings, each share at least 7 %. A count is never cut and the row never scrolls sideways.
- **Colours: one scale for the bar, the trend and the badge**
  ([Q-UI-860](#q-ui-860--one-severity-scale-for-the-bar-the-trend-and-the-badge-the-bars-fills-with-a-mark-tone-of-the-same-hue)).
  The fills, the same in both schemes: `--quader-sev-critical` `#7f1d1d` (dark red), `--quader-sev-high` `#c9302a` (red),
  `--quader-sev-medium` `#e8a33d` (orange), `--quader-sev-low` `#f5d68e` (yellow); the count in `--quader-sev-ink-light` (white) on
  the first two and `--quader-sev-ink` `#1c1204` on the next two; Unknown hatched in diagonal stripes of `--quader-sev-unknown` and
  `--quader-sev-unknown-light`, its count in the text colour. A severity without findings is drawn faint (its fill at 28 % over the
  surface), and its 0 stays readable in the text colour (4.5:1; the muted tone would not be, `palette.spec.ts`). The same fills are
  the bands of the trend (R-VULN-022). Each severity has a **mark tone** of its fill's hue, deeper in the light scheme and brighter
  in the dark one, which keeps 3:1 against every surface it sits on: `--quader-sev-critical-mark` `#6c0b17` / `#d95853`,
  `--quader-sev-high-mark` `#9c1e18` / `#f6815b`, `--quader-sev-medium-mark` `#a15e04` / `#ffb755`, `--quader-sev-low-mark`
  `#a78314` / `#ffe8b0` (light / dark); it is the edge on top of the trend's band and the icon of the severity's badge. None is a
  neutral grey (`--quader-sev-none` `#737278` / `#89888d`) and Unknown's mark the muted grey (`--quader-sev-unknown-mark` `#626168` /
  `#a4a3a8`), so that neither reads as a step of the scale. No severity is green (R-UI-002), and none takes a status colour: a
  severity is no error.
- **Name.** The bar is `role="img"` with the name "Open findings: 13 Critical, 160 High, 113 Medium, 16 Low, 843 Unknown"; the
  numbers inside are hidden from the accessibility tree. With `[queries]` (the report's header and the grade card of the package
  page, R-UI-094) each segment is a link that applies its severity filter, named by its count and severity ("13 Critical"), in a
  list named "Open findings"; on the package page the link keeps the page's other query parameters (`merge`) and the segment of
  the filter in force is marked (`aria-current`).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: the five counts in order, None added to Low; a larger count gives a larger share and a zero count a faint segment that
  still shows 0; the Unknown segment is hatched; the accessible name lists every count; with links each segment links to its
  filter; axe finds no serious violation.
- Rendered: the counts 13, 160, 113, 16 and 843 fit their segments at 1440 and 390 px in both schemes.
- Unit (`palette.spec.ts`): every count keeps 4.5:1 on its fill; every mark tone, None and Unknown's mark keep 3:1 against the page,
  the raised surface, the card, the table head and the row under the pointer in both schemes; neighbouring severities (Critical,
  High, Medium, Low, None) stay at least 9 apart in CIEDE2000, the fills and the marks, under the deuteranopia and the protanopia
  simulations of Machado et al. (2009); a mark tone is within 12 degrees of its fill's hue in LCh.

### R-UI-093 · The grade card
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

`<quader-grade-card>` ([grade-card.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-card.ts)) is a version's grade in one
repository with its details, as cogpit's card:

- The shield of 32 px on the left, centred on the card's lines; on the right, one below the other: the text (weight 600), the rule
  (muted, 12 px), the severity bar of R-UI-092 and the line of facts (muted, 12 px). No frame: the card sits in its section.
- **The line of facts**, its parts separated by " · ": for an image **OS** and its name, **end of life** in the warning colour
  when it is, and **Scanned** with the time of its oldest scan ("Scanned 1 h ago (Nov 12, 2026, 12:31:51 PM)"); for every other
  format **Checked** with the time of the advisory data it was checked against ("Checked 3 min ago (…)", Q-VULN-156); the time is
  `<quader-time-ago>`, one relative time ("just now", "3 min ago", "1 h ago", "4 d ago") with the absolute time in brackets
  ([Q-UI-378](#q-ui-378--a-time-on-the-grade-card-is-one-relative-time-with-the-absolute-time-in-brackets-from-one-component));
  last, the link **Findings in web-frontend/images**, which opens the project's vulnerability report filtered by the repository,
  the package and the version (R-VULN-022) ([Q-UI-374](#q-ui-374--a-list-shows-the-shield-and-the-text-the-bar-and-the-facts-are-the-cards)).
- On the package page the card's bar filters the findings below it ([Q-UI-379](#q-ui-379--the-vulnerabilities-tab-pages-the-open-findings-of-a-version-from-the-findings-api-filtered-by-the-cards-bar)).
- **N/A** shows the shield, the text and the rule only: there are no counts to draw.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: an image's card with "OS alpine 3.24.1", the end of life and the scan time; a package's with the data's time; the link's
  query names the repository, the package and the version; N/A has no bar and no line of facts; axe finds no serious violation.

### R-UI-094 · Where the grade shows
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

Every screen that showed the highest severity of a version or a package shows its grade instead; the findings themselves keep
their severity (R-VULN-022). The list shows the grade; the bar and the facts are on the card (R-UI-067: details on demand,
[Q-UI-374](#q-ui-374--a-list-shows-the-shield-and-the-text-the-bar-and-the-facts-are-the-cards)).

| Screen | Place | What |
|---|---|---|
| Repository content (R-UI-052) | The column **Vulnerabilities** of the items | `<quader-grade>` of the item's latest version (`vulnerabilityGrade`, R-VULN-039): the total and the fixable findings, as the versions table says them (R-UI-143); the column sorts by grade ([Q-UI-373](#q-ui-373--the-list-sorts-by-grade-in-the-browser-over-the-whole-list-up-to-1000-entries)) |
| Repository content, the opened row | The column **Vulnerabilities** of the versions | `<quader-grade>` of each version in this repository |
| Package page (R-UI-007), the versions table (R-UI-110) | The column **Vulnerabilities** | `<quader-grade>` of each version: the grade, the total of its open findings and how many have a fix (R-UI-112) |
| Version page (R-UI-111) | The line of facts | `<quader-grade>` of the version (the worst of its repositories), a link to the tab **Vulnerabilities** ([Q-UI-375](#q-ui-375--the-package-page-shows-the-versions-grade-in-its-header-and-a-card-per-repository-on-its-tab), Q-UI-454) |
| Version page, tab **Vulnerabilities** (R-VULN-023) | Each repository's section | `<quader-grade-card>` above the block banner, its bar's segments the severity filter of the findings below (`severity` in the URL); then the open findings, 25 at a time from the findings API, worst first, with their number from the grade's counts ([Q-UI-379](#q-ui-379--the-vulnerabilities-tab-pages-the-open-findings-of-a-version-from-the-findings-api-filtered-by-the-cards-bar)) |
| Vulnerability report (R-VULN-022), a project's and the security dashboard | The header | `<quader-severity-bar [links]>` of the open findings in scope in place of the five severity counts; the counts **Malicious**, **Needs triage** and **Blocked versions** stay ([Q-UI-376](#q-ui-376--the-reports-header-shows-the-severity-bar-whose-segments-are-its-filter-links)) |

- A caller who gets no grades (an installation that does not scan, Q-VULN-158) sees no grade column, no card and no header grade,
  not a column of dashes ([Q-UI-377](#q-ui-377--a-list-without-grades-has-no-grade-column)). A visitor without a session gets the grades
  of what the public levels admit and sees every place of this table (R-UI-224).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: the repository content list shows `<quader-grade>` for each row and sorts by grade, worst first, on its second click; the
  opened row grades each version; the version page's grade links to the tab, the tab shows one card per repository and the
  package page's versions table a grade per version; the tab asks the findings API for 25 open findings of the version, worst first, says their
  number, and a segment of the card's bar narrows them to its severity; the report's header shows the bar with five filter links;
  without grades no column.
- Rendered (rule 11, `make ui-renders`): the repository content of `npm-internal`, `npm` and `images`, the package pages and the
  version pages of the npm packages and the image with the tab **Vulnerabilities**, and the vulnerability report of the project
  and of the admin area, as plain user, power user and administrator, light and dark, at 1440, 1024 and 390 px; the seed holds
  versions of the grades S, A, B, C, D, E and N/A.

### R-UI-095 · One search field in the top bar for every caller
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task T-22 (2026-11-12): "A sensible search, with suggestions and everything." The top bar's field (R-UI-002) is the one
search of the UI.

- **Who gets it.** Every signed-in caller, whatever its roles, and an anonymous caller while the UI runs without a session, which it
  does only while some repository's artifacts are `public` (`publicContent`, R-UI-004,
  [Q-UI-400](#q-ui-400--every-signed-in-caller-gets-the-field-and-an-anonymous-one-while-something-is-public)).
- **The field.** The placeholder "Search or go to…", with " (/)" while `/` is on; a `search` icon at its start; at its end the filter
  button (`filter_list`, accessible name "Filter: <kind>"); while a kind is chosen, a chip with the kind's name and a remove button at
  the field's start. The field fills the top bar's middle column up to 40 rem.
- **The filter** ([Q-UI-402](#q-ui-402--the-filter-is-a-menu-button-at-the-fields-end-and-the-chosen-kind-a-chip-at-its-start)). A
  menu of radio items: **All** (the default), **Repositories**, **Packages**, **Projects**, and for an instance administrator
  (R-UI-099), after a divider, **Users** and **Groups**, each marked **Admin area**. Backspace in an empty field, or the chip's remove
  button, returns to **All**. The kind lasts until the page is reloaded and is part of the results page's address (R-UI-098).
- **Keyboard** ([Q-UI-401](#q-ui-401--slash-focuses-the-field-and-is-on-by-default-the-preference-turns-it-off)). `/` moves the
  focus into the field while the preference `keyboardShortcuts` is on (R-API-021, on by default) and the focus is not in a text
  field, a text area, a select or an editable element; the key is not typed. Ctrl+K, and ⌘K on macOS, does the same whatever the
  preference. An anonymous caller has no preferences and gets Ctrl+K and ⌘K only.
- **Below 36 rem** ([Q-UI-403](#q-ui-403--below-36-rem-a-search-button-opens-the-field-as-a-sheet)). The field gives way to an icon
  button (`search`, accessible name "Search") among the top bar's actions. The button, `/` and Ctrl+K open the search as a sheet: a
  panel over the top bar's full width, `role="dialog"` named "Search", with the field and the filter at its top, a **Close** button,
  and the suggestions below it down to the bottom of the window. The focus stays in the sheet; **Close**, or Escape while no list is
  open, closes it and returns the focus to the button.
- The field asks the server for nothing before it has the focus (R-UI-096) and a text (R-UI-097).

Acceptance criteria:

- The plain user `sam` (`reader` of two projects, no system role) sees the field at 1440 px and the button at 390 px; an anonymous
  visitor of an installation with one public repository sees them too; with nothing public, an anonymous visitor sees the sign-in
  page and no field.
- With `keyboardShortcuts` on, `/` typed on the page body focuses the field and is not typed into it; typed into another text field
  it is typed there; with the preference off, `/` does nothing; Ctrl+K focuses the field either way.
- At 390 px the button opens the sheet with the focus in its field; Escape closes it and the focus is on the button again.

### R-UI-096 · What the opened field offers before anything is typed
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

When the field gets the focus without a text, a list opens under it, in this order
([Q-UI-404](#q-ui-404--the-empty-field-offers-the-references-parts-in-its-order-and-the-admin-pages-last)):

1. **Places**: Projects (`/projects`), Repositories (`/repositories`, Q-UI-1040), Guides (`/guides`), Profile (`/profile`), Personal tokens (`/profile/tokens`), and the entries
   of the start side bar's sections the caller has (Security dashboard, `/security`, for the holder of `content:metadata-read`,
   R-UI-158, [Q-UI-626](#q-ui-626--the-security-dashboard-is-a-place-and-a-page-of-the-main-area-in-the-search)), each with its
   side-bar icon; an anonymous caller gets Projects, Repositories and Guides.
2. **Frequently visited repositories**: up to five, each with its format's icon, the key, and "· <project key>" muted.
3. **View all my projects** (`/projects`).
4. **Frequently visited projects**: up to five, each with the project's letter mark (as the project switcher's), the display name,
   and "· <key>" muted.
5. For an instance administrator only (R-UI-099), after a divider: **Admin area**, with Dashboard, Users, Groups and
   Settings (the repositories are a place of the main area, Q-UI-1040), each the admin side bar's entry (icon and label, R-UI-002) where the administrator may use it, and each marked
   **Admin area**.

Groups 2 to 4 are not shown to an anonymous caller.

- **Where "frequently visited" is kept**
  ([Q-UI-405](#q-ui-405--frequently-visited-is-kept-in-the-browser-per-principal-by-visits-and-recency)). In browser storage
  (non-secret, R-UI-043), one key per signed-in principal ID, `quader.frequent.<principal ID>`: per repository its qualified name,
  per project its key, each with the number of visits and the time of the last one, at most 20 per kind. A visit is the opening of a
  repository's page or content page, or of a project's screen; it counts once per entry in 15 minutes, and every visit is the entry's
  last one. A repository's visit is recorded when the server answered its page with the repository, and not while the repository is
  being deleted; the entry of a repository that is gone (deleted or moved by the person, or not found by its own page) is removed
  from the store (R-UI-167). The order is the number of visits, halved for every 14 days since the last visit, then the last visit. The same store,
  ordered by the last visit, is the side bar's **Recently opened** (its newest five, read with one request of its own, R-UI-167) and the project switcher's
  recent list; the two stores of before are no longer read (no migration before the first stable release). A route under `/admin` is
  never recorded. With storage blocked, groups 2 and 4 are left out.
- **Only what the caller may still read**
  ([Q-UI-406](#q-ui-406--a-stored-entry-is-shown-after-the-server-confirms-that-the-caller-still-reads-it)). The stored repositories
  are shown after one `GET /api/v1/repositories?name=…` (R-API-063) has returned them, and only those it returned; the stored projects
  when the project list the UI reads once (Q-UI-129) holds them. An entry that is not returned is left out and stays stored. The
  request runs when the list first opens after sign-in, and again after the stored repositories or the caller's authorization epoch
  changed. The group joins the open list when the answer comes; an entry the reader already walked to stays active
  ([Q-UI-700](#q-ui-700--the-active-entry-follows-its-identity-when-the-list-changes)).

Acceptance criteria:

- `sam`, who opened `web-frontend/npm-vendor` three times and `platform/collections` once, sees them in that order; after he loses
  `read` on `platform`, `platform/collections` is not shown and its entry stays stored.
- `ada` (system role `admin`) sees the **Admin area** group last, each entry marked; `sam` and the power user `priya` see no such
  group.
- A second user signed in in the same browser sees none of `sam`'s entries; with storage blocked the list holds Places and **View
  all my projects** only.
- Opening the empty list sends at most the one request of the repositories.

### R-UI-097 · Live suggestions while typing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **When** ([Q-UI-408](#q-ui-408--one-request-per-settled-text-250-ms-after-the-last-key-an-anonymous-caller-waits-longer)). A
  signed-in caller's text of two or more characters is sent 250 ms after the last key; an anonymous caller's of three or more after
  500 ms, and at most four times in 4 s. One request per settled text, `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions` (R-API-060) with the kinds of
  the filter; a request a newer text supersedes is cancelled; the answers of the last ten texts are reused for 30 s while the list is
  open. Below the minimum the list shows R-UI-096.
- **Groups and order** ([Q-UI-407](#q-ui-407--the-main-areas-groups-come-first-and-the-admin-areas-last-five-in-each)).
  Repositories, Packages, Projects, Documentation (the entries of collections, R-ANS-058), Pages; then, for an instance administrator
  only and after a divider, Admin pages, Users and
  Groups, each group heading and each entry marked **Admin area** (R-UI-099). Five per group, three for Pages and Admin pages; with a
  kind chosen, that group alone with ten. A group without a match is left out. A group of the main area whose answer says `more` ends
  with **All repositories for "<text>"** (packages, projects), which opens the results page on that tab (R-UI-098).
- **An entry** shows: a repository the format's icon, the key and "· <project key>" muted; a package the format's icon, the name
  and "· <project key> / <repository key>" muted; a project the letter mark, the display name and "· <key>" muted; a page its
  side-bar icon and label; a user the avatar (R-UI-002), the display name or the username, "· <username>" muted and **Disabled**
  where it is; a group the `group` icon and the name. Keys and names carry `translate="no"`.
- **Where it leads**: a repository `/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>`; a package its page in the project of the answer's
  repository (`/projects/<project>/packages/<format>/<name>`); an entry of the documentation its collection's page with
  `?doc=<type>/<name>` (the `menu_book` icon, the entry's name, "· <type> · <collection> <version>" muted); a project `/projects/<key>`; a page its route; a user
  `/admin/users/<username>`; a group `/admin/groups/<name>`.
- **Pages** are matched in the browser, in the UI's language, by the project rule of R-API-062 over the labels of the Places of
  R-UI-096 and of Sessions (`/profile/sessions`) and Documentation (`/help`); **Admin pages** over the labels
  of the admin side bar's entries the administrator may use.
- **Highlighting** ([Q-UI-409](#q-ui-409--the-matched-text-is-bold-marked-by-the-client)). Every occurrence of each term of the text
  in the shown name is bold (weight 600), case-insensitively; overlapping marks merge. Nothing else is coloured.
- **States.** While a text's first answer is pending, the previous list stays with a quiet "Searching…" line. No match in any group:
  "Nothing you may read matches "<text>". Press Enter to search everything." A `429`: "Too many searches. Suggestions return in
  <n> s.", and no request is sent before its `Retry-After` has passed. Another error: "Suggestions are not available."; Enter still
  works.
- **Keyboard and ARIA** ([Q-UI-410](#q-ui-410--the-field-is-an-aria-combobox-with-a-grouped-listbox)), after the WAI-ARIA Authoring
  Practices' combobox with a listbox popup: the field is `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`,
  `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the popup is a `listbox` named "Suggestions" whose groups are `role="group"`
  named by their headings. The focus stays in the field. Down and Up move the active entry: Down from the field enters the list, Up
  from the first entry returns to the text, nothing wraps. Enter opens the active entry; Escape closes the list and, with the list
  closed, empties the field; Tab leaves the field and closes the list; Alt+Down opens the list without moving. After each answer a
  polite live region says how many suggestions are shown, or that none matches.
- **The active entry when the list changes**
  ([Q-UI-700](#q-ui-700--the-active-entry-follows-its-identity-when-the-list-changes)). Typing makes the text active. A list that
  changes without a key (a newer answer, the frequently visited repositories confirmed by the server) keeps the entry the reader
  walked to active wherever it now stands, under the same option id; where the new list does not hold it, or holds nothing, no entry
  is active and Enter does what it does without one (R-UI-098). An entry is the same when it opens the same target. A list never
  makes an entry active by itself.
- **Pointer and held keys** ([Q-UI-701](#q-ui-701--the-pointer-activates-an-entry-only-when-it-moves-and-a-held-enter-acts-once)).
  The pointer makes the entry under it active when it moves; a list that changes or scrolls under a resting pointer does not. A
  held Down goes on from where its entry stands in the newest list. A held Enter acts once: its repeats open nothing.

Acceptance criteria:

- `sam` types `vend`: after 250 ms one request `GET /api/v1/search/suggestions?q=vend&kind=repository,package,project&limit=5`;
  the list shows `npm-vendor · web-frontend` under Repositories with `vend` in bold.
- `ven`, `vend` and `vendo` typed within 200 ms send one request, for `vendo`.
- With the keyboard only: Down, Down, Enter opens the second entry; Escape closes the list and a second Escape empties the field.
- `sam` types `npm`, then `npm-`, and walks to `npm-all` before the answer of `npm-` comes: an answer that puts `npm-cache` first
  keeps `npm-all` active under the same `aria-activedescendant`, and Enter opens it; an answer without `npm-all`, or without any
  suggestion, leaves none active, and Enter opens `/search?q=npm-`. A `mousemove` at the pointer's old position over the moved
  list changes nothing (`search-field.spec.ts`).
- A `429` with `Retry-After: 3` shows the notice, and no request is sent for 3 s.
- axe reports no serious or critical violation with the list open, in both schemes.

### R-UI-098 · Enter opens the results page of the main area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Enter in the field with no active entry opens `/search?q=<text>&kind=<kind>`
([Q-UI-411](#q-ui-411--enter-without-a-picked-suggestion-opens-search-whose-tabs-read-the-three-lists)), a page of the main area with
the start side bar (R-UI-002); it never opens a route under `/admin` (R-UI-099). No entry is active as long as the reader has not
walked to one, and after a newer list dropped the one they walked to
([Q-UI-700](#q-ui-700--the-active-entry-follows-its-identity-when-the-list-changes)): Enter then opens this page, never an entry
the reader did not choose.

- **Header**: the `<h1>` **Search** and the description "What you may read that matches "<text>"." The top bar's field keeps the text
  while the page is open; the page has no field of its own.
- **Tabs**: **Repositories**, **Packages**, **Projects**, **Documentation**, without counts. `kind` chooses the tab; without it, or with `user` or
  `group`, the tab is the first group that had a suggestion when Enter was pressed, else **Repositories**. The tab is part of the
  address.
- **A tab is the list of its kind with `q`**, 25 rows at a time with **Load more** (R-API-010): Repositories, `GET
  /api/v1/repositories?q=`, built from the parts of the repository list
  ([Q-UI-430](#q-ui-430--the-searchs-repository-rows-are-built-from-the-parts-of-the-repository-list): the visibility icon, the key
  with its description, the project by its mark and its name, format and class; no address and no copy button, Q-UI-426);
  Packages, `GET /api/v1/packages?q=`, with the columns of Q-UI-314 and the project (its mark and name) and repository of each;
  Projects, `GET /api/v1/projects?q=`, with the start page's columns (Q-UI-311), the project's mark before its name;
  Documentation, `GET /api/v1/search/documentation?q=` ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-058): the entry with its type and
  short description, the collection (its name with its namespace as a link) and version, the project and the repository. A row leads to
  its object's page in the main area. The packages are sorted by relevance (R-ANS-057); a package's namespace links to the page of the
  name across every project, its tags to the search for them (R-UI-220).
- **Empty**: "Nothing you may read matches "<text>"." on the tab. A text of fewer than two characters shows "Type at least two
  characters." and asks nothing.
- The page has no users, groups or admin pages and no link into the admin area. It takes over the page of the stopgap that replaced
  `/admin/repositories?q=` ([Q-UI-415](#q-ui-415--the-stopgaps-results-page-becomes-r-ui-098s)).

Acceptance criteria:

- As `ada` (system role `admin`), `test` and Enter open `/search?q=test`; the page holds no link whose path starts with `/admin`.
- `/search?q=vend&kind=package` opened directly shows the Packages tab, and **Load more** after 25 rows.
- As `sam`, the Repositories tab lists only what `sam` may read; a repository of `platform` with `hideExistence: false` on which
  `sam` holds nothing is not listed.

### R-UI-099 · The search leads into the admin area only by an administrator's choice of a marked suggestion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner (2026-11-12, after typing "test" in the top bar and landing on the admin area's repository list with Enter): a search on
the main page must never end in the admin area, unless live suggestions are shown, some of them are explicitly marked as pages of the
admin area, and the user is an instance admin; then and only then may a search result lead there
([CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md#product-simple-by-default-details-on-demand)).

- **Instance administrator** ([Q-UI-412](#q-ui-412--an-instance-administrator-is-the-holder-of-the-system-role-admin)): a caller
  whose `GET /api/v1/authz/me` lists the system role `admin` in `roles`, directly or through a group. The other system roles, which
  open the admin area too (R-UI-067), get no admin suggestions and reach their screens through the Admin button.
- **Admin suggestions** are the admin pages, users and groups of R-UI-096 and R-UI-097, shown only to an instance administrator.
  Each shows the mark **Admin area**, the Admin button's icon `build` and the words, which are part of its accessible name ("Users,
  Admin area"); so does each of their group headings. They come after every group of the main area, behind a divider.
- **Only by an explicit choice**: a click on such a suggestion, or Enter while it is the active entry. Enter without an active
  entry, the results page, the filter, the frequently visited entries and every other way out of the field open a route of the main
  area. With the filter on Users or Groups, Enter without an active entry opens nothing and the live region says "Choose a user from
  the list." ("a group") ([Q-UI-413](#q-ui-413--under-a-users-or-groups-filter-enter-without-an-active-entry-opens-nothing)).
- **One gate.** The field opens every target through one function, which refuses a route under `/admin` unless the target is an
  admin suggestion and the caller is an instance administrator at that moment.
- The rule is navigation, not access control: what the admin area shows is decided by the API as before (R-UI-005).

Acceptance criteria:

- As `ada`: `users` shows **Users · Admin area** under Admin pages; Enter without an active entry opens `/search?q=users`; moving to
  that entry and Enter opens `/admin/users`.
- As the holder of `security-admin` alone: `users` shows no admin group, and Enter opens `/search?q=users`.
- A unit test drives every way out of the field (Enter with and without an active entry of each kind, a click on each kind, the
  **All … for** lines, the empty list's entries, the filter) as `ada`, `priya` and `sam` and asserts that only `ada`'s choice of a
  marked entry reaches `/admin`.

### R-UI-100 · The head of every list: the search by name, Filters and the filters that are set
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-6): a name was three steps
away (**Filters**, the section **Name or description**, **Search**), and what was filtered was not visible while the panel was
closed. Every list screen has one row above its table, built by one component, `<quader-list-head>`
([list-head.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/list-head.ts)):

- **The search by name** ([Q-UI-421](#q-ui-421--the-search-by-name-is-a-field-above-the-list-outside-the-drawer)): a field as wide
  as a name (R-UI-085), named and hinted by its job (**Filter repositories**, **Filter packages**, **Filter findings**, **Filter
  users**, **Filter groups**, **Filter service accounts**, **Filter projects**, **Filter members**). It filters as the list's name filter does, through
  the same query parameter or request member, 250 ms after the last key or at once on Enter. A list whose API has no search by name
  (the permission policies, the token administration, the audit log, the issued CI tokens) has no field.
- **Filters**, the button that opens the list's drawer (R-UI-101), with the number of filters that are set. A list whose only filter
  is the name (the service accounts, the start page's projects, a project's members) has no button and no drawer.
- **The filters that are set**, one chip each, to the right of the button
  ([Q-UI-422](#q-ui-422--a-set-filter-is-a-chip-beside-filters-and-what-does-not-fit-folds-into-n-more)): the filter's name muted,
  its value, and a button that removes that filter alone, named "Remove the filter Format: npm". Chips that do not fit beside the
  button fold into one **+N more** button that opens the drawer. The search text is the field's and no chip.
- **The list's own controls** at the row's end: the selection's action (**Revoke selected**, **Change status**), the bulk revoke of
  the issued CI tokens, the audit log's time zone and exports, the start page's **Your projects**.

Below 36 rem of content the field takes its own line and the button and the chips the next. A list's table keeps its whole width.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests of the list head: the field sends the trimmed text 250 ms after the last key and at once on Enter; a text the list
  applies from elsewhere replaces what the field shows; a chip names its filter and its value, and its button removes it.
- Each list's spec: the head stands before the table; an applied filter is a chip and the drawer stays closed; removing a chip
  changes only its filter.
- Rendered (`make ui-renders`): the head of every list in both schemes at 1440, 1024 and 390 px, with several filters set
  (`repositories-chips`, `packages-chips`, `vulnerabilities-chips`, `admin-users-chips`) and, at 390 px, more chips than fit.

### R-UI-101 · The filters open in a drawer over the page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner (W-6): the panel beside the list was "extremely ugly"; the list was rebuilt narrower when it opened. **Filters** opens a
drawer that slides in from the right over the page ([Q-UI-420](#q-ui-420--the-filters-of-a-list-open-in-a-drawer-from-the-right-over-the-page),
[ADR-200](../decisions.md#adr-200--a-lists-filters-open-in-a-drawer-the-apps-one-pattern-for-content-over-the-page)); the list
behind it keeps its width and its columns. One behaviour at every width.

- **The drawer** is a shared component, `<quader-drawer>` ([drawer.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/drawer.ts)): a modal dialog
  named by its heading **Filters**, at the window's right edge and its full height, 24 rem wide or the window's width. The focus
  moves to its heading and is trapped inside; Escape, its close button and a click beside it close it; the focus returns to
  **Filters**; the page behind it does not scroll. It slides in and out with the motion of every panel.
- **The filters stand open**, one under the other, each a labelled field or a group named by its legend
  ([Q-UI-423](#q-ui-423--the-drawers-filters-stand-open-apply-closes-it-and-closing-without-apply-keeps-what-the-list-shows)).
  **Clear all** in the drawer's head removes every filter of the drawer and keeps the search text; **Apply filters** at its foot
  applies the staged values at once and closes it. A drawer closed without **Apply filters** keeps the filters the list shows.
- `<quader-filter-panel>` ([filter-panel.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/filter-panel.ts)) is the drawer of a list's filters, and
  carries those of the packages, the repositories, the vulnerability report, the users, the groups, the permission policies, the
  token administration, the audit log and the issued CI tokens.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests of the drawer: closed until **Filters** opens it; a modal dialog named **Filters**, outside the screen's element;
  focus on its heading, back on **Filters** after the close button; Escape closes it without applying; **Apply filters** applies
  once and closes it; the open drawer passes axe.
- Playwright: the journeys that filter a list (the packages, the audit log, the issued CI tokens) open the drawer by **Filters**,
  set its fields and apply them with **Apply filters**.

### R-UI-102 · A project has its mark wherever it is listed, and an icon before a name stays on the name's first line
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner (W-1, W-3, 2026-11-18): the search's suggestions and the project switcher showed a project with its letter mark, the
project tables showed the name alone; and a long repository key broke away from its visibility icon, which stood alone on the first
line.

- **The project's mark** ([Q-UI-424](#q-ui-424--a-projects-mark-is-one-component-before-its-name-wherever-a-project-is-listed)),
  `<quader-project-mark>` ([project-mark.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/project-mark.ts)): the first letter of its display name
  (else its key), or for the built-in project `upstream` an arrow pointing up
  ([Q-UI-837](#q-ui-837--the-project-upstream-stands-first-in-a-list-of-projects-and-its-mark-is-an-arrow-pointing-up)), on a stone of Quader's mark, which turns into the mark's coloured stone while the pointer or the keyboard's focus
  is on its row, link or option; decorative. It stands before the name in every list of projects (the start page, the search's
  **Projects** tab, the project switcher's lists, at 32 px beside a name with its key under it) and
  wherever a row names its project (the list of every project's repositories, the search's repositories and packages, the permission
  policies, the audit log, at 20 px), there as `<quader-project-link>`: the mark and the project's display name, linked to it.
- **An icon before a name** ([Q-UI-425](#q-ui-425--an-icon-before-a-name-has-a-column-of-its-own-in-the-cell-and-a-long-name-breaks-inside-itself-beside-it)):
  the cell `.icon-name` gives the icon a column of its own and the name the rest, so the icon and the start of the name share the
  first line in every row; a name longer than its column breaks inside itself, after a hyphen where it has one. A description
  under the name stands in the name's column.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests: the search's repository rows and a project's repository rows hold the visibility icon and the key as the two columns
  of `.icon-name`; the search's project cell holds the mark; the start page's project rows hold the mark.
- Rendered: `repositories-long-keys`, `repositories` and `all-repositories` with `release-candidates-for-the-customer-portal-frontend`
  and the project **Customer portal release engineering and delivery** show the icon and the start of the name on one line.

### R-UI-103 · One way to write a time
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The walk of 2026-11-18 found three ways across lists: "4 minutes ago", "Nov 18, 2026" and "Nov 18, 2026, 8:17:21 AM"
([Q-UI-431](#q-ui-431--a-time-in-a-list-is-relative-with-the-absolute-time-as-its-title-a-log-writes-the-moment)):

- **A list of things** (packages, repositories, findings, users, tokens, the search results) writes a time relative to now in the
  build's language, "4 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 4 weeks", with its date and time ("Nov 18, 2026, 8:17:21 AM") as the title of
  the `<time>` element: `<quader-time-ago absolute="title">`. A column whose cells start with such a time is at least as wide as the
  widest relative time of the language (`relativeTimeWords`), so the list's form does not change with the ages of its rows
  ([Q-UI-1069](#q-ui-1069--a-column-of-relative-times-holds-the-widest-relative-time-of-its-language)).
- **A card or a page's facts** write the relative time with the absolute time in brackets (Q-UI-378): `<quader-time-ago>`.
- **A log** (the audit log, the issued CI tokens), where the moment is the content, writes the date and the time, `medium`.
- One wording of a relative time: `relativeTime` ([format-time.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/format-time.ts)); `timeAgo`
  ([time-ago.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/time-ago.ts)) is the same in the build's locale. A screen that calls either follows.
- No screen of a package or a repository writes a time with the date pipe or a helper of its own: the versions of a package and
  its **First published**, a version's facts and its repositories, the items of a repository and their versions, and the files of a
  folder use `<quader-time-ago>` in the form of their place (the merge of the four packages of the walk, 2026-11-18).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests: `relativeTime` and `timeAgo` give one wording ("now", "1 minute ago", "yesterday", "in 4 weeks"); the list form puts
  the absolute time into the title; `relativeTimeWords` holds the largest count of every unit in English and German.
### R-UI-110 · A package's versions as one table
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-7): "a click on a package shows its versions as a table", one row per version; the standard
case is a user who looks for one version of a dependency, or for the vulnerabilities of that version. What a row carries is the
owner's reference screen's; its look is Quader's own.

- **Its address** ([R-UI-218](#r-ui-218--a-package-leads-with-the-documentation-its-format-carries), [Q-UI-1242](#q-ui-1242--a-packages-address-is-its-newest-version-where-its-format-leads-with-its-documentation-its-table-is--versions)): the package's own address
  `/projects/{project}/packages/{format}/{name…}` for a format whose content is its list (OCI, Debian, generic files), and
  `…/{name…}/-/versions` for a format whose packages lead with their documentation (Ansible Galaxy, npm, NuGet), whose own address is the
  newest version's page; there the breadcrumb reads Packages › the package (a link to its address) › **Versions**. It loses nothing:
  the table, the README of the latest version below it and the details are the same at either address.
- The table holds every version the reader may read (`GET …/versions?sort=-version`, read once, every page), with the grades of
  the package report (`GET …/vulnerabilities`, R-VULN-039) and the distribution tags of the latest version's details. **For an image a row
  is an image, not a tag** (the owner's word of 2026-11-25, which changes his word of W-7 "one row per version" for OCI,
  [Q-UI-1130](#q-ui-1130--an-image-is-one-row-with-its-tags-on-the-opened-item-and-on-the-packages-page)): `group=content`, the leading tag
  as the version with every other tag of the image muted after it ("+ more" where the answer has more than 100), the signature badge on
  the row; the column is headed **Tag**, the field **Filter tags** also matches the other tags, and the count reads "M of N images".
- **Columns, in the owner's order** ([Q-UI-450](#q-ui-450--a-row-of-the-versions-table-is-the-version-its-size-its-vulnerabilities-and-two-times)):
  **Version** (a link to the version's page, R-UI-111; after it its npm tags as badges, `latest` first and the others by name, at most
  three and "+N more", each saying in its tooltip what it is, the badge and the words of the tab Upstream
  ([Q-UI-1190](#q-ui-1190--an-npm-tag-is-a-badge-on-the-row-of-the-version-it-names-with-a-tooltip-that-says-what-it-is),
  [Q-UI-1191](#q-ui-1191--a-version-shows-three-tags-and-n-more-whose-tooltip-names-the-others)), and the mark **Pre-release**), **Size** (R-API-080: a size that is not known is the shared no-value with a title that says why, a partial size has **≥** before it and a title that says what it counts), **Vulnerabilities** (R-UI-112; only when the answer carries a grade other than N/A: a format that is not scanned and a package of internal names are N/A in every row, Q-UI-377), **Published** (an image's
  **Pushed**, or **Fetched** where only remote repositories hold its newest version, [Q-UI-1314](#q-ui-1314--an-images-date-is-pushed-or-fetched-on-every-screen)),
  **Last download** (R-API-065, R-API-079; "Never" for a version no client downloaded, with a help text and a title, Q-API-342), under
  it the version's downloads ("410 downloads", [R-UI-222](#r-ui-222--every-table-of-versions-says-each-versions-downloads-and-an-images-digest)), and **Repositories** only when the versions differ in the
  repositories that hold them ([Q-UI-457](#q-ui-457--the-column-repositories-appears-only-when-the-versions-are-held-by-different-repositories)).
  An image's digest stands under its tags (R-UI-222).
- **Sort**: the highest version first by the format's precedence (the server's order); every column but Repositories sorts both
  ways in the browser over the whole list; equal keys keep the highest version first. The sort is the address's `sort`
  (`-published`, `vulnerabilities`, …), the default left out ([Q-UI-452](#q-ui-452--the-versions-are-searched-sorted-and-paged-in-the-browser-over-the-whole-list)).
- **Search**: a field **Filter versions** above the table, 18 rem wide, narrows the rows to those whose version or one of whose tags
  holds the typed text, case-insensitive, at once and without a request; the address's `q` follows without a new history entry,
  and "N of M versions" says how many match.
- **Pre-releases and tags** stand in the rows with their marks; there is no switch for pre-releases
  ([Q-UI-453](#q-ui-453--pre-releases-and-distribution-tags-are-marks-in-the-row-no-switch)).
- 50 rows show at first, **Load more** adds 50; a new search or sort starts at 50 again.
- A time is the shared helper's relative time with the absolute time as its title.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: of 120 versions the table shows 50, then 100 after **Load more**, and 50 again after a new search; `beta` narrows to the
  pre-release, `latest` to the version the tag points at; each column's sort orders the rows and is the address's; the grade cell
  of `E` with 1,145 findings and 112 with a fix reads "1,145 findings · 112 fixable" beside its shield (R-UI-091: the letter is
  the shield's and is not written again).
- Rendered (rule 11): the package pages of npm (`@acme/ui-kit`, the many-version `chart-render-kit` filtered and sorted by grade,
  `image-convert-tools`, the longest name), the image `portal/web`, the NuGet, Debian and Ansible packages of the seed, as plain
  user, power user and administrator; the image `tools/agent` of the remote `platform/image-cache`, whose tags show a known size, a
  partial one and one that is not known (W-24).

### R-UI-111 · A version has a page of its own
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: UI-009, ART-049

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-7): "a version has a page of its own with an address of its own": the grade card, the findings,
the install command, the files and the metadata of that one version. It can be linked and sent, and the list of findings has the
page's width. Not chosen by the owner: a row that opens inside the table, and a drawer.

- **Address**: `/projects/{project}/packages/{format}/{name…}@{version}`, the version after an `@` in the last segment
  (`/packages/npm/@team-a/ui@1.4.0`, `/packages/oci/portal/web@1.4.0`)
  ([Q-UI-451](#q-ui-451--a-versions-address-is-the-packages-with--and-the-version)). The breadcrumb reads
  Packages › the package (a link to its page) › the version. Every link to a version leads here: the versions table, the repository
  content page (R-UI-052), the finding and the advisory pages and the report (R-VULN-022). For a format whose packages lead with their
  documentation the package's own address is this page of its newest version ([R-UI-218](#r-ui-218--a-package-leads-with-the-documentation-its-format-carries)), and its breadcrumb ends at the
  package.
- **Header**: the package name and the version as the `h1` ("image-convert-tools 4.0.1"), the format, the npm tags that point at the
  version (every one, the badge of
  [Q-UI-1190](#q-ui-1190--an-npm-tag-is-a-badge-on-the-row-of-the-version-it-names-with-a-tooltip-that-says-what-it-is)) and the mark
  **Pre-release**, the package's description. At its right the page's acts (the place of the repository page's **Set up client**):
  for a format that leads with its documentation the switch between the versions ([Q-UI-1243](#q-ui-1243--the-switch-between-the-versions-is-a-menu-of-the-ten-newest-in-the-head-with-a-link-to-all)), then the button with the
  format's client verb (**Pull**, **Install**) whose panel is R-UI-009's ([Q-UI-1241](#q-ui-1241--a-versions-page-has-its-command-behind-the-verbs-button-in-its-head-the-box-is-gone)); a version of the ClamAV definitions
  has **Set up client** with freshclam instead (R-UI-194). Where no client can install the version (held only by disabled
  repositories, Q-UI-965, or only by system repositories, Q-UI-898, Q-UI-899) the head has no button, and the sentence why stands under
  the facts.
- **Facts**, one line with the style guide's separator: the grade with the total and the fixable findings (R-UI-112), a link to
  the tab Vulnerabilities; when it was published (an image's **Pushed** or **Fetched**, Q-UI-1314); its size (R-API-080); when a client
  last downloaded it (R-API-065, "never"); its downloads; its licences, a link to the licence's address where the version declares one.
  Under them the version's links in one row, and the note that it runs an install script ([R-UI-221](#r-ui-221--a-versions-general-properties-read-the-same-in-every-format)). Below them the
  banners **Unlisted.**, **Blocked in <repository>** and **Deprecated.**
- No box of a command before the tabs (the owner, 2026-11-25, [Q-UI-1241](#q-ui-1241--a-versions-page-has-its-command-behind-the-verbs-button-in-its-head-the-box-is-gone)): the command is the head's button.
- **Tabs** (`tab`): for a format that leads with its documentation its documentation first, the tab the page opens on where the version
  carries it ([R-UI-218](#r-ui-218--a-package-leads-with-the-documentation-its-format-carries), [Q-UI-1245](#q-ui-1245--a-version-without-documentation-opens-on-its-first-tab-with-content-and-its-readme-tab-says-so)); **Vulnerabilities** (R-VULN-023), the first tab of a version whose grade is
  not N/A otherwise; for the format `ansible`
  **Documentation** and **Contents** (R-UI-060, R-UI-062); **README** (R-UI-008, when `hasReadme`); **Files** (path with its size and
  its SHA-256's first twelve characters and copy button under it, the path the file's download where it offers one; the malware
  scan, the signature;
  [Q-UI-1002](#q-ui-1002--a-versions-files-keep-their-table-the-size-and-the-hash-stand-under-the-path),
  [Q-UI-1051](#q-ui-1051--a-versions-file-path-is-its-download)); **Details** (the format's metadata of R-API-029 in the order and the
  blocks of [R-UI-221](#r-ui-221--a-versions-general-properties-read-the-same-in-every-format): Debian's long description, the keywords, the dependencies, an image's digest, media type,
  artifact type, size and platforms, each platform with its size or "Not fetched" while the repository does not hold it (Q-OCI-221), a
  chart's facts, **Package details** with the facts only the format has (Debian's with the source package as a link to its binaries and
  the copyright file in a closed fold, [formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-038, R-DEB-039,
  [Q-UI-1272](#q-ui-1272--a-debian-packages-changelog-is-a-tab-its-copyright-a-fold-its-files-a-section-of-files)), the authors; then the
  repositories that hold the version, each a link to its page, with its class and when it was published there); **Changelog** of a Debian version after Details, and its
  installed files under the package files of **Files**; **Vulnerabilities** after Details for a version that
  is N/A; **Import log** of an Ansible collection in a local repository (R-UI-063)
  ([Q-UI-456](#q-ui-456--the-version-page-opens-on-its-vulnerabilities-when-it-is-graded)).
- A version the reader may not read, or that does not exist, is the not-found notice.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `@team-a/ui@1.4.0` reads "@team-a/ui 1.4.0" with `latest`, its facts, the head's **Install** whose panel shows
  `npm install @team-a/ui@1.4.0`, no box before the tabs, and the tabs README, Files, Details; graded B it opens on its README with
  Vulnerabilities second (npm leads with its documentation); the breadcrumb of `/projects/web/packages/npm/@team-a/ui@1.4.0` is
  Projects, web, Packages, @team-a/ui, 1.4.0.
- Rendered (rule 11): the version pages of npm (with and without a grade, with fixable findings, the longest name), the image tag,
  NuGet, Debian and Ansible as plain user, power user and administrator, every tab.

### R-UI-112 · A version's vulnerabilities in one statement
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-7): the row of a version shows its grade, the total of its findings and how many of them have a
fix. The page that opened before said **Vulnerabilities (1145)** in its tab and **E · 13 Critical** beside the version: two
numbers whose relation the reader had to know.

- `<quader-grade>` (R-UI-143; `<quader-version-grade>` until 2026-11-18) shows the shield, which carries the letter, and "1,145
  findings · 112 fixable" (the sum of `open` and `fixable` of the
  grade, R-VULN-040), "no findings" for S, "not scanned" for N/A; its tooltip names the rule of the letter and every count. The
  versions table and the version page's facts show it; the card of each repository on the tab keeps the rule and the bar
  ([Q-UI-454](#q-ui-454--a-version-says-its-grade-total-and-fixable-findings-once-the-tab-carries-no-count)).
- The tab **Vulnerabilities** carries no count.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: the grade E with 13 Critical, 160 High, 113 Medium, 16 Low and 843 Unknown of which 112 have a fix reads "1,145
  findings · 112 fixable" beside the shield E, and "Grade E · 1,145 findings · 112 fixable" as text; S "no findings"; N/A "not
  scanned"; the tab's label is "Vulnerabilities".

### R-UI-120 · Set up client is one page of a repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-2): the guides and the client setup become one page with a context; a guide opens from a
repository, where the format, the class and the repository are known, and asks for none of them
([ADR-202](../decisions.md#adr-202--the-client-setup-and-the-guide-are-one-page-of-a-repository)).

- Route `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/setup`, with the query parameters `client` (one of the format's clients) and
  `bastion` (R-BAS-007); the document title and the `h1` are **Set up client**, the breadcrumb is the project's trail with the
  repository's key and **Set up client** (Q-UI-480).
- The header names the context and asks for nothing: the repository (`<project>/<key>` with the icon of its level, a link to its
  page), the format and the class as the badges of the repository's own header (R-UI-052: the format with its icon, the class with
  its icon), and the address the snippets use as an address field (R-UI-065): the repository's on this installation, or its address
  on the Bastion chosen under **More options**.
- The client is one select **Client** with the format's clients of `GET /api/v1/formats` in their order, the one of `?client=`
  or the first chosen; a format with one client shows no control (Q-UI-482). Choosing a client replaces `?client=`.
- The page is reached from every **Set up client** (R-UI-126). It needs `read` on the repository: the API answers `404`
  otherwise, which the page shows as the error notice of a missing repository. A disabled repository shows a warning that it
  refuses every client.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`client-setup.spec.ts`): the page opened for `web/npm-all` names the repository, the format and the class, shows the
  address and has no control for the format, the repository or the class; npm offers its four clients in one select, generic none.

### R-UI-121 · The job first, the explanation after
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner chose the design on 2026-11-20 (W-27, [Q-UI-800](#q-ui-800--set-up-client-takes-variant-a-snippets-are-windows-the-page-has-pictures-and-less-text)):
"Variante A ist am besten und gefällt mir."

- The page reads from top to bottom: the header (R-UI-120), with a picture of the flow at its right end where the content is at
  least 55 rem wide (a window of about 1,200 px with the side bar); the client; the credential, one framed row with **More
  options**, closed, inside it (R-UI-122); the steps **1 Configure**, **2 Install** and, for who may publish, **3 Publish** (R-UI-123),
  joined by a rail from one number to the next, each a short heading with the snippets of the client setup's tab of that name
  (R-API-030); then the explanation under the heading **Guide** (R-UI-125). Below 36 rem of content the rail goes and the number
  stands before the heading.
- **Less text** ([Q-UI-804](#q-ui-804--a-snippet-says-only-what-its-window-does-not-and-a-second-way-of-a-step-is-a-fold)): a snippet
  has at most one short sentence, by its `id` (the UI's text, R-UI-045), and only what its window does not say already (the window
  names the file and shows the command; an install command has none). A name of a file, a setting or a command in it is code. A
  second way of a step (an image pull secret for a Kubernetes cluster, the same command in PowerShell or cmd, a `nuget.config`
  beside the command, a one-line `.list` file, a `requirements.yml`, the `~/.netrc` line of roles, the scoped variant) stands after
  the step's own snippets behind an inline fold titled with the way, a label of one line at 390 px in every locale (Q-UI-810). A
  snippet that only works with a credential (the pull secret,
  the token variable in PowerShell and cmd, the `~/.netrc` line) is not shown to an anonymous visitor.
- **A snippet is a window** ([Q-UI-801](#q-ui-801--a-snippets-window-is-an-editor-for-a-file-and-a-terminal-for-a-command-coloured-by-its-language)):
  a file (its `fileName`) is an editor window, its tab the file's name, its lines numbered, **Download** and the copy button in its
  bar; a command is a terminal window, its tab the command line (`shell`, `PowerShell`, `cmd`), each command after its prompt (`$`,
  `PS>`, `>`), none on a line that continues the one before, a here-document or a block. The window is light in the light scheme
  and dark in the dark one, with syntax colours keyed by the snippet's `language`, never by its format, so a new format adds no
  highlighter. The parts the server names as the reader's (`marks`, R-API-030) are marked: where the token goes as a chip, what
  the reader replaces tinted, dashed underneath and in italics, each with a title. A long line wraps with an indent of two
  characters under itself (Q-UI-486) and never inside a flag, a mark or a token's reference (up to 32 characters each); an address
  breaks after its slashes. Nothing in a window scrolls sideways at 390 px. The copy button copies the text exactly; the numbers
  and the prompts are no part of it. A window shows no window controls and no name or logo of an editor or a terminal product.
- The pictures (the flow, a window's tab line) may take the format's accent
  ([Q-UI-803](#q-ui-803--a-format-adds-one-accent-pair-for-its-pictures-a-format-without-one-takes-the-neutral-pair)); the
  page's own controls and text keep the app's palette.
- The snippets are `GET …/client-setup` for the repository and the client (`credentials=env`, `none` for an anonymous caller,
  `placeholder` while a token is to be written into them, R-UI-122); the explanation is the repository's guide (R-API-053) for the
  same client. With a Bastion chosen the snippets are the Bastion's and the page shows no explanation: the guide describes this
  installation, and a sentence says how to read it.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`client-setup.spec.ts`): the steps are Configure, Install, Publish in that order, each with its snippets; the
  explanation follows the last step; no contents box stands above the page; the npm configure snippet says "Save as `.npmrc` in your
  project." and the install command nothing; a file is an editor window with its name, **Download** and **Copy snippet**, a command a
  terminal window without **Download**; the pull secret of OCI is a closed fold **For a Kubernetes cluster**.
- Unit tests (`code-window.spec.ts`, `code-syntax.spec.ts`): the window's text is the snippet's exactly and the copy button copies
  it; the marks are laid over the colours wherever their text stands; a terminal prompts a command once; the wrap rule keeps a
  flag, a mark and a token's reference whole and breaks an address after its slashes; `clients.spec.ts`: every snippet id the API
  renders is known to the page, no sentence is longer than 20 words, every fold's label (a second way and **More options**) has at
  most 32 characters in English and in German, and every fold the page shows is one of them (Q-UI-810).
- Renders (rule 11): the screens `setup-*` at 1440, 1024 and 390 px, light and dark, as each kind of user, with no layout finding
  and nothing that scrolls sideways.

### R-UI-122 · The token without leaving the page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- A signed-in reader sees one framed row (Q-UI-800): a key, **Token** and "The snippets read it from `QUADER_TOKEN`.", **Create a
  token** beside them, the page's one confirm button, on the line of **Token** (R-UI-175), and **More options** inside the row
  (Q-UI-483). The button creates a personal token (R-API-032) described as "Client setup: <client>, <repository>, <date>",
  scoped to the repository with `read`, plus `read` and `deploy` on the setup answer's `publishTarget` when the reader ticks
  **It may also publish**, which is shown only while the answer names a target; it expires after `tokenTtlSeconds` of the setup
  answer (`ui.client_setup.token_ttl`). Recent authentication applies.
- The created token is shown once, with what it may do, in an address field with its copy button (R-UI-065), then "Run this, paste
  the token, press Enter. The shell keeps it out of its history." and the command `read -rs QUADER_TOKEN && export QUADER_TOKEN` in
  a terminal window `bash, zsh` with its own copy button: run in bash or zsh, it reads the pasted token into the variable without
  echo and without an entry in the shell's history. A line names the CI way: a masked variable of that name. The snippets keep the
  reference.
- **More options** holds **Token in the snippets**: **Read it from the variable QUADER_TOKEN** (the default) or **Write a token into
  the snippets**, a password field with a reveal toggle; the value is checked in the browser for its prefix, length, alphabet and
  CRC-32 (INV-8, R-AUTH-022), the check that failed is named, only a value that passes is written into the snippets, and it is
