  sent nowhere. Until one passes, the snippets show `{{token}}` and a note says so; a token written in stays marked where it
  stands. **More options** also holds **Install from** where a Bastion can be chosen (R-BAS-007, Q-BAS-96); it has no hint line.
- Secrets (R-UI-043): the created and the pasted token live in signals of the page only; another repository or another client
  discards both, leaving the page discards both; an answer of the creation that arrives after the repository or the client changed
  is revoked and never shown; a double click creates one token.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests: the request of **Create a token** has the description, the lifetime and the scope above; the value appears once, the
  snippets keep `${QUADER_TOKEN}`; the page has no link to the personal tokens; a pasted value with a wrong checksum is named and
  no request carries it.

### R-UI-123 · What each reader sees
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

| Reader | Steps | Credential | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A reader who may not publish (the plain user `sam`) | Configure, Install | The line with **Create a token**; **More options** | Without publishing and its upkeep (R-API-070) |
| A member who may publish (`deploy` on the target) | Configure, Install, Publish | As above, and **It may also publish** | With publishing |
| A caller who can read the configuration of a virtual repository without a deployment target | Configure, Install, and Publish with the reason and a link to the repository's settings | As above | Without publishing |
| An anonymous visitor of a repository whose artifacts are `public` | Configure, Install, without the snippets that need a credential (R-UI-121); the sign-in of an image says it is not needed to pull | "You are not signed in: the snippets hold no credentials."; no **More options** unless a Bastion can be chosen | Without credential steps and publishing |

A Bastion target has no Publish step; its banner says that a Bastion is read only (R-BAS-007). An anonymous visitor of a
repository that is not public gets the `404` of R-UI-120.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests: `web/npm-remote` has Configure and Install; an anonymous visitor gets `credentials=none`, no token line and no More
  options; an anonymous visitor of `web/oci-local` reads "Not needed to pull: this repository can be read without signing in." and
  no fold **For a Kubernetes cluster**; `web/npm-readonly` shows the reason to a holder of `repositories:read-config` and no Publish
  step to a reader.

### R-UI-124 · Guides: the formats as tiles, a format's repositories, the guide of a class
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **`/guides`** (the navigation entry **Guides**, also the user menu's): the heading **Guides**, one sentence, and the formats of
  `GET /api/v1/formats` that list clients as the tiles of R-UI-127, in the catalog's order; nothing else to choose (owner,
  2026-11-18). A signed-out visitor sees it while `publicContent` is true.
- **`/guides/{format}`** (Q-UI-481): the trail **Guides / <display name>** and the title the display name, never the key
  ([Q-UI-553](#q-ui-553--the-guides-trail-names-a-format-as-people-read-it)); the heading "<display name> repositories", a sentence, and the repositories of that format
  the reader may read and that are not disabled, virtual first (marked **Recommended**), then by name. The list is built from the
  parts of every repository list ([Q-UI-430](#q-ui-430--the-searchs-repository-rows-are-built-from-the-parts-of-the-repository-list),
  Q-UI-425, Q-UI-426): **Repository** (the visibility icon, the key as a link to the repository, the description as its muted second
  line), **Project** (its mark and its name, R-UI-102), **Class** (icon and name), and at the row's end **Set up client** in the
  form of a row's action (R-UI-126). The format is the page's, so it is no column. An empty list says that the reader can use no repository of the format. Below the list, **Without
  a repository**: one link per class the format has, to the guide of that class.
- **`/guides/{format}/{class}`**: the page of R-UI-120 without a repository. The header names the format and the class; the
  address shows `<project>` and `<repository>`, and the credential line says that they stand for the project and the key of the
  reader's repository; the snippets and the explanation are the guide of the class (R-API-053, R-API-070). No token is created
  and there is no **More options**: there is no repository to scope a token to.
- A format without clients, or a class the format does not have, says that there is no guide and links to `/guides`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`guides.spec.ts`): the tiles are the formats with clients and lead to `/guides/<format>`; the npm page lists the
  repositories virtual first in the columns and the name cell of the repository list, with **Set up client** to `…/setup`, and
  links the three class guides.

### R-UI-125 · The explanation reads like a page, not like a reference
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- Below the steps, under the heading **Guide** (`h2`): every section of the guide is a closed row titled with the section's heading
  (a `<quader-disclosure>` with an `h3`), in the server's topic order; the first one, what a repository of the class is,
  is closed too ([Q-UI-805](#q-ui-805--the-guide-is-a-list-of-closed-rows-under-one-heading), revising Q-UI-485). The headings are the
  contents: no contents box stands above the page.
- A line of the prose (paragraphs, lists, the prose's own headings) is at most 70 characters wide; a table or a code block may
  take the page's column, which is the settings measure (56 rem). Every column of a table wraps; where the page is narrower than
  40 rem a table's rows stand as blocks, the first cell on a line of its own, every other cell under it with its column's name
  before the value ([Q-UI-971](#q-ui-971--a-guides-table-stands-as-blocks-where-the-page-is-narrow)).
- Every code block of the prose has a copy button (**Copy code**). A line too long for its block wraps instead of being cut off.
  The copy buttons copy the text unchanged.
- The format's text carries `lang="en"`; the frame is translated (Q-UI-86).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`guides.spec.ts`): every section is a closed row in the server's order, the first one too, with no second fold; a
  code block of the prose has **Copy code**; `client-setup.spec.ts`: the heading **Guide**, the class's section first and closed.
- Renders (rule 11): `setup-long-key` and `setup-deb` (`debian-internal-packages-for-bookworm-and-trixie`) at 390 px show every
  address of their snippets whole.

### R-UI-126 · Set up client is one action with one target and one look per place
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- One label, **Set up client**, and one target: the repository's page of R-UI-120, where the client address stands (R-UI-169). It
  stands in the repository's header, first of its actions (not for a disabled repository; once on the page, also when the
  repository is empty, R-UI-144), in the rows of a project's
  list of repositories (W-4), in the install panel of a version (with the
  panel's client as `?client=`) and in the rows of the repositories behind a format's tile (R-UI-124). The repository's settings
  have no section that points to it (the development agent, 2026-11-18): the repository's own page carries it in its header.
- One look per place ([Q-UI-487](#q-ui-487--set-up-client-is-a-default-button-on-a-page-and-a-quiet-row-action-in-a-table-row)): the default button (`btn-default`) on a page and in a header; in a row of a table the
  quiet form of a row's action (`btn-tertiary`), whose accessible name ends with the repository's key. It is never blue.
- No link leads to `/setup`: `check-rules.mjs` fails the lint on a route literal of `/setup` or `/browse` in the application's
  code (`removed-routes-rule.mjs`, tested in `lint-rules.test.mjs`).
- The packages list of a project names no repository: its **Set up client** leads to the Guides (R-UI-124), where the reader

- The user menu and the search's pages (R-UI-097) have no entry for a client setup without a repository.

  repositories of a format: the label, the class (`btn-default` on a page, `btn-tertiary` in a row) and the target.
- The lint rule's test: a link to `/setup` or `/browse` fails, a repository's own `…/setup` passes.

Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- `quader-format-tiles` ([format-tiles.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/format-tiles.ts)): each format of the list as a tile with

### R-UI-142 · The members list is built like every other list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Seen by the development agent on the power user's screens of the owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (`members`): the filter field was as
wide as the page, a sort button **Account** with an arrow stood beside it instead of the head of every list, and a tab strip with
a single tab, **Members 2**, stood above it ([Q-UI-550](#q-ui-550--the-members-list-takes-the-head-and-the-table-of-every-list-and-its-count-moves-to-the-heading)).

- The list has the head of R-UI-100: the field **Filter members**, as wide as a name, which searches the display name and the user
  name. The list has no filter besides the name, so it has no **Filters** and no drawer.

  name or **Group** under it), **Source**, **Role** and the row's menu. **Account** and **Role** sort by their column headers;
  **Role** puts the strongest role first and then the accounts in order. The answer holds every member, so the search and the sort
  run in the browser and are exact. Where the columns do not fit the rows stack as every list's do (R-UI-174).

  (`count` of the page header).

Acceptance criteria:

  **Filters**, the table's sortable headers are Account and Role, a click on a header reverses or changes the order, and the search
  narrows the list.
- Rendered (rule 11): `members` as plain user, power user and administrator, light and dark, at 1440 and 390 px.

### R-UI-143 · A grade says the same thing in every list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Seen by the builder of the guides and the development agent on 2026-11-18: a repository's list of packages said the count that
decides the letter ("2 High" beside the shield C), the package's versions table "1,145 findings · 112 fixable" beside the shield; a

### R-UI-144 · An empty repository says what fills it, and for whom
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Seen by the builder of the guides on 2026-11-18: an empty repository showed **Set up client** twice, in its header and under the
sentence of its empty state ([Q-UI-555](#q-ui-555--an-empty-repository-shows-set-up-client-once-in-its-header-and-its-empty-state-says-what-fills-it-and-for-whom)).

- **Set up client** stands once, in the header beside the address (R-UI-126). The empty state of the repository's content and of
  the root of its files is a sentence and no button: what it does not hold yet, then what fills it, for this caller.
- A caller who may deploy to the repository (`deploy` of `POST /api/v1/authz/check` at its root) reads "This repository holds no
  packages yet. Publish a package with your client; Set up client shows how." (images: push; files: upload); in a generic repository
  where the toolbar offers **Upload files**, "This repository holds no files yet. Upload files here or with your client." Anyone else
  reads who fills it: "… Members who may publish to it fill it with their client." A remote repository fills by the fetches of every
  client: "This repository has cached no packages yet. It fills as clients fetch through it; Set up client shows how." (images: pull).
  A disabled repository says only what it does not hold: no client can use it, and its header has no **Set up client**.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`repository-content.spec.ts`, `repository-files.spec.ts`): an empty npm repository shows one **Set up client**, in the
  header; its empty state says the publisher's sentence to a caller who may deploy and the members' sentence to one who may not, with
  no link or button; an empty OCI remote says that it fills as clients pull through it; a disabled repository says only that it is
  empty.
- Rendered (rule 11): `repository-empty` as plain user, power user and administrator, light and dark, at 1440 and 390 px.

### R-UI-145 · Nothing in a list breaks where it must not
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

What the development agent saw on the 19 screens of the admin area before the owner's walk (2026-11-18,
"Station of the administrator"): a status whose icon
stood on one line and its word on the next in every row of the jobs; a replica's name, an action's key and a token's description
broken while the column beside them was half empty; a UUID broken across two lines where the row named the same person by name;
**Format** and **Class** 2 px below the other cells of their row; a dashboard card as wide as the page with a label 1,100 px from
its value; a version broken into three lines in a card whose right half was empty; a schema version touching its check mark; the
sentence under the endpoints' title smaller than on every other page; a page titled **Token administration** under the menu entry
**Tokens**. The rules, for every list of the app:

- **A status is one element** ([Q-UI-560](#q-ui-560--an-icon-in-a-table-cell-is-one-element-with-its-word)): its icon and its word
  in the badge (`.ok`, `.warn`, `.bad`, `.badge`), which never breaks; an icon before a text that may wrap is `.icon-name`. A lint
  rule refuses an icon that stands directly in a table cell. Its word starts with a capital
  ([Q-UI-564](#q-ui-564--a-status-word-starts-with-a-capital)).
- **An identifier stays whole** and **a column is as wide as its content**
  ([Q-UI-563](#q-ui-563--a-column-is-as-wide-as-its-content-what-never-breaks-declares-no-width-and-the-columns-that-wrap-share-the-room)):
  a row's header that is an identifier (`translate="no"`) and a cell of one stay on one line; a column whose values never break
  declares no width and is as wide as its longest value; the columns that wrap share what is left in proportion to their content,
  and only a list with one such column lets it `prefer` the room. An audit action's key breaks after its dots only
  ([Q-UI-567](#q-ui-567--an-audit-actions-key-breaks-after-its-dots-only)); a resource's identifier is cut on one line with its
  whole value as the title ([Q-UI-568](#q-ui-568--an-audit-target-the-entry-knows-by-name-shows-the-name-another-its-identifier-on-one-line));
  a hash in running text is its short form ([Q-UI-570](#q-ui-570--a-hash-in-running-text-is-its-short-form-with-the-whole-as-its-title)).
- **A format and a class stand on the line of their row**, and so does a row's control in every table
  ([Q-UI-562](#q-ui-562--a-format-and-a-class-are-centred-on-the-line-of-their-cell)): a group's **Remove** stood 5 px below the
  member's name.
- **A check box keeps its size** beside a label of several lines
  ([Q-UI-575](#q-ui-575--a-check-box-keeps-its-size-beside-a-long-label)): the CI issuer's **Public issuer** was smaller than the
  form's two other boxes.
- **A save bar closes the page** down to the panel's edge
  ([Q-UI-576](#q-ui-576--the-policy-editors-save-bar-closes-the-page-down-to-the-panels-edge)): a line of the policy form showed
  below **Create policy**.
- **A card's rows are built one way and a card is no wider than 30 rem**
  ([Q-UI-572](#q-ui-572--a-cards-rows-are-one-construction-and-a-card-is-at-most-30-rem-wide)).
- **The sentence under a title is the header's** ([Q-UI-569](#q-ui-569--the-sentence-under-a-title-is-the-headers-description)),
  and **a page's title is its entry's in the side bar** (**Tokens**, R-UI-030).

Acceptance criteria:

- `check-rules.mjs` fails on a template whose table cell holds an icon directly (`status-rule.mjs`, tested by
  `lint-rules.test.mjs`); the app passes it.
- Unit tests: the jobs' state, the audit outcome and a replica's state are badges whose word starts with a capital; the replica
  cell has no `.wrap`; the list of every project's repositories and the token lists pin no column; the audit key holds `<wbr>` after each
  dot only; a target known by name shows it with the identifier as the title; the system status shows the revision's twelve
  characters with the hash as the title and the schema version apart from its badge; the dashboard's CPU and Memory are rows of
  the card's list; the endpoints' sentence is the header's; a check box is a direct child of its `.check-row`.
- `layout-rules.spec.ts` reads the shared stylesheets and holds the rules of Q-UI-562, Q-UI-563, Q-UI-575 and Q-UI-576.
- Looked at in the running UI (not rendered by the builder, who had no render stack): the screens of the list in the report of
  the change.

Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

### R-UI-150 · A principal is chosen from a search that shows the people it found
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's W-12 (2026-11-18, at **System roles**, where a role was bound by typing `user:name`, `group:name` or `sa:name`): "a person
is chosen through a person search that shows the possible people, everywhere a person search plays a role". His reference is the
member field of his GitLab: one types "Swa", and under the field a row shows the avatar, the full name and under it the username of
the match ([Q-UI-580](#q-ui-580--one-shared-field-names-a-principal-everywhere-and-nobody-types-a-reference)).

- **One field**, `<quader-principal-field>` ([principal-field.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/principal-field.ts)), names a user, a
  group or a service account wherever the UI names one (R-UI-152). Nobody types a reference: the field holds the chosen principals as
  chips (avatar or the kind's icon, the name, a remove button) and hands the reference to its form.
- **While one types** it searches, from the second character and after a pause of 250 ms; an older answer that arrives late is
  dropped. Under the field it lists the matches, each a row with the avatar (the uploaded picture, else the generated robot of
  R-UI-002) or the kind's icon (a group, a service account), the display name or the name, and under it in the secondary type the
  `@username`, **Group**, **Service account** or **Service account of `<project>`**
  ([Q-UI-582](#q-ui-582--a-match-is-a-row-of-avatar-name-and-username-and-a-choice-is-a-chip)).
- **Inputs:** the kinds (users; users and groups; users, groups and service accounts; groups; users and service accounts), one choice or
  many, the project the principal is named in, the references already taken (not offered again), read-only.
- **Where the matches come from** decides who may search, and the field never widens it
  ([Q-UI-581](#q-ui-581--the-field-searches-what-its-caller-may-already-search)): with a project, the project's lookup
  (R-API-077, its Owner and `identities:read`); without one, the suggestions of the admin area's kinds (R-API-078, `identities:read`).
  The admin area offers the instance-wide service accounts, the accounts that a role, a group or a global policy can name; a filter by
  owner or actor offers every account. A disabled user is not offered.
- **Keyboard and assistive technology**, by the combobox pattern of WAI-ARIA with a listbox: the focus stays in the input,
  `aria-activedescendant` names the active row; ↓ and ↑ move it, Enter takes it (and never submits the form around the field while
  there is text), Escape closes the list and then empties the text, Backspace on an empty text removes the last chip of a field of
  many. A polite live region says how many matches there are, or the state below. The active match follows the rules of the search
  field ([Q-UI-700](#q-ui-700--the-active-entry-follows-its-identity-when-the-list-changes),
  [Q-UI-701](#q-ui-701--the-pointer-activates-an-entry-only-when-it-moves-and-a-held-enter-acts-once)): a newer answer keeps it
  where it still lists it and leaves none active where it does not; Enter without an active match takes the only match the list
  shows, and does nothing with several; the pointer activates a row when it moves; a held Enter acts once and never submits the
  form.
- **States** under the matches: "Searching…" until the first answer; "Nobody matches “Swa”. A person can be found after their first
  sign-in." when no user matches (for a field without users, "Nothing matches “…”."); "More match. Type more of the name." when the
  search left matches out; "The search failed. Change the text to try again." when it was refused or failed, with no stale row
  ([Q-UI-585](#q-ui-585--a-person-who-has-never-signed-in-is-not-found-and-the-field-says-so)).
- **A stored reference** the field cannot search is shown, never offered: a CI identity that a stored policy entry names reads
  **CI identity** with its reference and can be removed
  ([Q-UI-583](#q-ui-583--a-ci-identity-is-never-offered-a-stored-one-shows-as-a-chip)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`principal-field.spec.ts`): one character asks nothing; two ask once after the pause with the field's kinds; a match shows the
  avatar, the display name and `@username`, a group its icon and **Group**; a disabled user is not offered; ↓ sets
  `aria-activedescendant`, Enter takes the match (default prevented) and the chip replaces the input of a field of one; Escape closes
  and then empties; many choices are chips and Backspace removes the last; nothing found, more and a failed search say so; with a
  project the lookup answers with the field's kinds and the search API is not asked; the admin area offers instance-wide accounts and
  a filter every account; a taken reference is not offered; the open list passes axe.
- Unit, per place of R-UI-152 (`role-bindings.spec.ts`, `groups.spec.ts`, `policy-editor.spec.ts`, `policy-list-table.spec.ts`,
  `project-screens.spec.ts`, `project-members.spec.ts`, `projects.spec.ts`, `ci-editor-screens.spec.ts`, `audit-log.spec.ts`,
  `token-admin.spec.ts`, `user-list-table.spec.ts`, `users.spec.ts`): the principal is chosen from the search and the write or the
  filter carries the form the API takes.
- Rendered (rule 11): `admin-roles` and `admin-group` with the state `search` (the matches open under **Bind to** and **Add a member**),
  as administrator, light and dark, at 1440 and 390 px.

### R-UI-158 · The security dashboard is the auditor's page, under Your work
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-17): "beim Security
dashboard handelt es sich nicht um ein Admin Feature, sondern um ein Auditor-Feature. Für Auditoren oder Administratoren gehört es
unter Your Work als zweite Kategorie "Security Audit", darunter dann Security Dashboard. Sichtbar nur für Instanz-Auditoren und
Instanz-Administratoren."

- **Place** ([Q-UI-620](#q-ui-620--the-security-dashboard-is-security-of-the-main-area-under-the-second-context-title-security-audit)). The
  dashboard is `/security` of the main area, its finding `/security/findings/{id}` and its advisory
  `/security/advisories/{ecosystem}/{id}`. The start side bar has, after the block **Your work**, a second context title **Security
  audit**, written and placed as **Your work**, with the plain entries **Security dashboard**, **Malware** (`/security/malware`) and
  **Signatures** (`/security/signatures`) (R-UI-168; the owner's correction of
  the same evening: "Security-Audit hatte ich eigentlich als weiteren context-title erwartet"; the two later entries by his word of
  2026-11-23, [Q-UI-1005](#q-ui-1005--malware-and-signatures-are-entries-of-their-own-under-security-audit)). The entry of the page shown
  is the one whose address is the longest the page's address starts with. The trail reads "Security audit /
  Security dashboard" (the title a name without a link, R-UI-002's breadcrumbs), the page's title "Security dashboard". The admin area has no entry and no route for it: `/admin/security` is not found (R-UI-003). **Advisory sources** stays
  in the admin area's group System, because the sources are the installation's configuration.
- **Who** ([Q-AUTHZ-295](authorization.md#q-authz-295--the-security-dashboard-opens-for-the-holder-of-contentmetadata-read)). The
  title, the entry and the page are the holder's of `content:metadata-read`, the capability that lets the findings API read every
  project (R-VULN-019): the system roles `admin` and `auditor`. Everyone else sees neither the title nor the entry, and the address
  answers **Page not found** ([Q-UI-622](#q-ui-622--a-caller-without-the-capability-gets-page-not-found-at-security)). The role
  `security-admin` holds `vulnerabilities:triage` without `content:metadata-read` and has no dashboard: it triages on the screens of
  the projects whose repositories it may read.
- **Three pages** ([Q-UI-1005](#q-ui-1005--malware-and-signatures-are-entries-of-their-own-under-security-audit), the owner's decision,
  superseding Q-UI-871 and Q-UI-873): **Security dashboard** (`/security`) holds the vulnerability findings, without a strip of views;
  **Malware** (`/security/malware`, [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-025) and **Signatures** (`/security/signatures`,
  [signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-038, with the refused downloads of gated repositories and their releases of R-SIG-074) are pages of
  their own, each with its heading, title and trail ("Security audit / Malware"). Who sees an entry is who opens the dashboard.
- **On the page** (R-UI-005): the selection, **Change status** and the finding's status buttons for the holder of
  `vulnerabilities:triage`; **Advisory sources** for the holder of `settings:read`; nothing else leads into the admin area; a
  package opens in its project.
- **The Admin button** is shown to a caller who may use an entry of the admin area
  ([Q-UI-621](#q-ui-621--the-admin-button-is-shown-when-the-admin-area-has-an-entry-for-the-caller)). An auditor may (the admin
  dashboard through `settings:read`, the audit log, the users), so it keeps the button; a caller whose only capabilities are the
  dashboard's has none and is not led into an empty admin area.
- **The search** offers **Security dashboard** to the holder as a place before anything is typed (R-UI-096) and as a page while
  typing (R-UI-097), unmarked: it is a page of the main area, so R-UI-099 does not apply to it
  ([Q-UI-626](#q-ui-626--the-security-dashboard-is-a-place-and-a-page-of-the-main-area-in-the-search)).
- The manual's page is in the user guide (`docs/manual/user/security-dashboard.md`), and the "?" of the top bar opens it.

Acceptance criteria:

- As `auditor` (a member of no project): the side bar of `/projects` shows the title **Security audit** with **Security dashboard**; it opens
  `/security`, the trail is "Security audit / Security dashboard", the Admin button is shown and not current; a finding opens below
  `/security`. As `admin` the same. As a reader, an Owner and the holder of `security-admin`: no title, no suggestion, and
  `/security` shows **Page not found**. `/admin/security` is not found for everyone.
- A lint rule refuses a link to `/admin/security` in the UI's sources (`web/scripts/removed-routes-rule.mjs`).
- Unit tests: `app.spec.ts`, `app.routes.spec.ts`, `security-dashboard.spec.ts`, `admin-home.spec.ts`, `search-field.spec.ts`,
  `search-gate.spec.ts`; the journey `web/e2e/vuln/16-security-dashboard.spec.ts`.

### R-UI-159 · The security dashboard has one filter: the head of its list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-17): above the counts the page had a form of its own (**Advisory ID**, **Package starts with**,
**Project key**, **Search**, with example texts in the fields) that set filters of the list far below it, which has its own head.
The owner chose, from three options (one filter at the list's head; the form as the scope of the whole page; the form moved down to
the list), the first ("Option A").

- **The page** starts with its title, one line that says what the counts and the trend cover, the counts and the trend; then the
  list with the head of R-UI-100. There is no form above the counts and no field with an example as its text.
- **The search** of the list's head, "Search by advisory, alias, package or summary", takes the question "do I have CVE-X?" in
  one step ([Q-UI-623](#q-ui-623--a-whole-advisory-identifier-in-the-search-is-the-advisory-filter-any-other-text-the-text-search)):
  a whole advisory identifier is the `advisory` filter in its canonical spelling (the findings of that advisory and of every
  advisory that names it as an alias, through the index of Q-VULN-111), any other text is `q` (a part of the package name, the
  identifier, an alias or the summary, in any case; R-VULN-020). The field shows the identifier, and no chip repeats it. The
  advisory page's link to all of its findings lands there too.
- **The drawer** holds **Project** first, the projects the caller sees as a list to tick, each with its mark and name
  ([Q-UI-624](#q-ui-624--the-project-of-the-dashboards-drawer-is-ticked-from-the-projects-by-mark-and-name)), then the categories
  of a project's report but **Advisory**, which the search takes. A chip names the project by its name. `packagePrefix` is no filter
  of the UI any more; the API keeps it.
- **What the counts cover** ([Q-UI-625](#q-ui-625--the-counts-and-the-trend-follow-the-scope-filters-and-a-line-says-so)): the
  counts and the trend follow the project, repository and format filters, never the search or the other filters, and the line
  says which: "The counts and the trend cover every project." while none of the three is set, "… cover the projects,
  repositories and formats of the filters." while one is.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`security-dashboard.spec.ts`): no form and no example text above the list; the order title, line, counts, trend,
  list; `cve-2021-44906` sends `advisory=CVE-2021-44906`, `ghsa-XVCH-…` the GHSA identifier in its spelling, `minimist` and
  `CVE-2021` send `q`; the alias finds the finding; the drawer's projects by mark and name, ticked into `project=`; the project chip
  by name; the line with and without a scope filter; a reader sees no triage control.
- The journey `16-security-dashboard.spec.ts`: an alias pasted in lower case finds the finding of two projects, the project ticked in
  the drawer narrows the list and the counts, a text search narrows the list while the counts stay the project's.
- The integration test `TestR_VULN_020_List` finds a finding by an alias of its advisory through `q`.

### R-UI-163 · A row with one action names it, a row with several has a menu
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-18 (W-18, [Q-UI-640](#q-ui-640--a-row-with-one-action-names-it-a-row-with-several-has-a-menu)):
the practice of most lists is the rule of every list and every table of the app, in the main area and the admin area.

- **One action** of a row is its word as a quiet button (`btn btn-tertiary`), with the row's name for assistive technology
  after the word (**Revoke**, heard as "Revoke ci-deploy"). A destructive word has the same quiet form as every other row
  action; its confirmation dialog says what it destroys. Where the one action differs by permission, it is one word either way.
- **Two or more actions** are the row's menu: the `more_vert` button (`btn btn-tertiary btn-icon`) named **Actions for
  &lt;name&gt;**, its entries the actions in words. A menu never has one entry.
- **Beside the menu** at most one frequent action stands on its own: the copy button of a value (its icon, with its name and
  tooltip, [Q-UI-642](#q-ui-642--a-copy-button-stays-the-copy-icon-also-where-it-is-a-rows-one-action)), or **Set up client**
  in its quiet word form in a project's repository list ([Q-UI-487](#q-ui-487--set-up-client-is-a-default-button-on-a-page-and-a-quiet-row-action-in-a-table-row)).
  The menu may offer the same action again.
- **A switch and the act of a state stand in the cell of that state** (the owner's working paper W-28 of 2026-11-25,
  [Q-CUR-201](remote-curation.md#q-cur-201--a-versions-acts-stand-where-their-state-stands)): a list whose rows set a state by a switch
  shows the switch in that state's cell beside its badge, and an act that changes what one cell shows stands in that cell as its one
  word (the cache's **Download**, **Download for examination** or **Discard**; a reader's **Request** under the delivery). Such a row
  has no action cell and no menu, and no cell holds two words.
- **Opening the thing is its name**: the name in the first column is the link to the thing's page, and a row whose only action
  would open it has no action cell.
- **A credential's Revoke is never in a menu** ([Q-UI-641](#q-ui-641--a-credentials-revoke-is-never-in-a-menu-a-token-row-keeps-its-two-words)):
  a leaked token is revoked with one click. A row that offers it with one other action shows both words (a personal token's
  **Rotate** and **Revoke**), because a menu of one entry is not made.

Brought to the rule on 2026-11-18 ([Q-UI-643](#q-ui-643--how-the-lists-that-did-not-follow-the-rule-follow-it)): the CI
mappings (**Edit** or **View**, **Test** and **Delete** as words), the Debian signing keys (two buttons per key), the saved
views of the package list (three words), a project's members (a menu of one entry), an endpoint's rules (a menu of one entry for
a reader whose rule is not served), and the two rows whose one action was a default button (**Clear** of an Ansible tombstone,
**Run now** of a scheduled task).

Acceptance criteria:

- `check-rules.mjs` fails on a template whose table cell or list item shows two word actions at once
  (`row-actions-rule.mjs`, tested by `lint-rules.test.mjs`); the app passes it with one allowed file, the token table of
  Q-UI-641. `lint-rules.test.mjs` passes a cell with a switch, one word and a link; `layout-checks.spec.ts` passes a switch beside its
  badge on one line.
- Unit tests: a CI mapping's row offers **Edit**, **Test** and **Delete** in the menu **Actions for &lt;name&gt;** to a writer and
  **Test** as its word to a reader, and the name opens the mapping; a next Debian key offers **Promote** and **Remove** in its
  menu, a withheld one **Reinstate** and **Confirm retirement**, the primary and a retired key nothing; a saved view's menu offers
  **Rename**, **Make default** or **Remove default**, and **Delete**; a project member's row offers **Remove** as a word; an
  endpoint's rule offers no menu to a reader whose rule is not served; the tombstone's **Clear** and a task's **Run now** are
  quiet buttons.
- The journeys that act on a changed row open its menu (12, 13, 17).

### R-UI-164 · System status, Jobs and Backups are the tabs of one page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-18 (W-19, [Q-UI-650](#q-ui-650--jobs-and-backups-are-tabs-of-system-status)): the jobs and the
backups were reached only through two text links at the end of the long status screen, and the side bar marked **System
status** on both.

- **One page, four tabs.** The page **System status** has one header, the tab strip under it (`tab-nav`, links with
  `aria-current="page"`, as the profile's pages) with **Status**, **Jobs**, **Backups** and **Storage** (R-UI-196, Q-UI-930), and the
  tab's content below. Each tab has its own address: `/admin/system`, `/admin/system/jobs`, `/admin/system/backups`,
  `/admin/system/storage`; the browser's back button and a
  reload keep the tab. The title of the page stays **System status**; the document title and the breadcrumb end with the tab
  (**Admin area › System status › Jobs**), as the profile's pages do ([Q-UI-653](#q-ui-653--the-status-tab-loses-its-links-to-the-other-tabs-a-filter-belongs-to-its-tab)).
- **One pair of refresh controls** ([Q-UI-651](#q-ui-651--one-pair-of-refresh-controls-in-the-pages-header-acts-on-the-shown-tab)):
  **Pause automatic refresh** and **Refresh now** stand in the header and act on the tab that is shown; no tab has a second
  pair. A pause holds across the tabs while the page is open.
- **No links of their own.** The status tab's text links **Jobs** and **Backups** at its end and the link **All jobs** of its
  card **Recent jobs** are gone: the tabs are the way there. The links from the dashboard and the repository screens keep their
  addresses and land on the tab.
- **A filter belongs to its tab.** The jobs' `kind` and `state` and the runs' `operation` and `state` stay in the address of
  their tab; a tab's link carries none, so leaving the tab drops them, and the browser's back button brings them back.
- **Who sees which tab** ([Q-UI-652](#q-ui-652--the-tab-strip-is-shown-to-whoever-may-open-every-tab)): Status, Backups and Storage
  read operations that need `settings:read`; the jobs answer every signed-in caller with the jobs they started (R-API-015). A caller
  with `settings:read` sees the four tabs; a caller without it, who follows a link of a repository screen to the jobs, sees
  them without a strip of one tab. The API decides as before (R-UI-005).
- **The side bar** keeps the one entry **System status**, marked on the four tabs.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (the page as the router builds it): one `<h1>` **System status** on every tab, the three tabs with their
  addresses and the current one marked, one **Refresh now** and one pause button in the header, **Refresh now** reloads only
  the shown tab, the pause holds across a change of tab and stops each tab's timer, a filter in the jobs' address is dropped by
  another tab, the status tab has no link to `/admin/system/…` but the tabs, a caller without `settings:read` sees the jobs
  without a strip; no serious axe violation.
- The route map test: `/admin/system/jobs` and `/admin/system/backups` are titled **Jobs** and **Backups** and show the `<h1>`
  **System status**.
- The journeys 06 and 16 reach the jobs and the backups through their tabs.

### R-UI-165 · The dashboard shows the state of the backup
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Added by the development agent to W-19, for the owner to object ([Q-UI-654](#q-ui-654--the-dashboard-shows-the-state-of-the-backup)):
a missing or overdue backup is seen on the first screen of the admin area, without opening the backups.

- The dashboard's card **Operations** has the row **Last backup**: the time of the last success in the list's form ("3 hours
  ago", the date and time its title, Q-UI-431), with the warning badge **Overdue** beside it when the backup summary says so
  (R-API-050: older than 1.5 times the expected interval), or the warning badge **No backup yet** while no run has succeeded.
- The card's foot links **View backups** to the tab **Backups** (`/admin/system/backups`), beside **View jobs**.
- The row and the link read `GET /api/v1/system/backups/summary`, the operation the Backups tab shows its status from; no new
  field. A caller whose summary is refused, or an installation whose summary cannot be read, gets the card without the row and
  the link; the rest of the dashboard is unchanged. The summary is read again with the dashboard's refresh.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests: the row shows the time of the last success and links the Backups tab; "Overdue" and "No backup yet" are warning
  badges; a refused summary leaves the row and the link out; the dashboard has no serious axe violation.

page as the auditor: "Unter projects macht "recently opened" irgendwie keinen Sinn, sieht nicht aus. […] Unter projects will der

### R-UI-167 · Recently opened is a folding group of the side bar of Your work
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-18 (W-20, [Q-UI-660](#q-ui-660--recently-opened-is-a-folding-group-of-your-work-with-the-last-five-repositories)):
"Lass uns lieber "recently opened" im side-menu zentral anbieten, falls jemand das tatsächlich nochmal nachschlagen will."

- **Place.** The home side bar (the main area outside a project, R-UI-002) ends its block **Your work** with the folding group
  **Recently opened** (icon `history`), after **Projects** and **Guides**. A project's side bar and the admin area's have no such
  group: inside a project the project switcher offers the recently opened projects (Q-UI-129).
- **Entries.** The last five repositories the person opened, newest first, from the search's store (R-UI-096: the newest five of up
  to 20 by the last visit, in this browser, per principal). An entry is a link to the repository's page
  (`/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>`) that shows the project's small mark (Q-UI-424) and the repository's key on one line; a
  key too long for the line is cut with an ellipsis. Its `title` and its accessible name are "<key> in <project's display name>
  (<project>/<key>)" ([Q-UI-661](#q-ui-661--an-entry-of-recently-opened-is-the-projects-mark-and-the-repositorys-key)). No address,
  no button.
- **Folded at first.** The group is folded when the side bar is shown for the first time; afterwards it keeps what the viewer
  chose, in the side bar's stored layout (`quader.nav.<name>`, `opened`), as every other group keeps its folding (R-UI-002).
- **Only what the caller may still read**
  ([Q-UI-662](#q-ui-662--the-side-bar-confirms-the-remembered-repositories-once-per-session)). An entry is shown after one
  `GET /api/v1/repositories?name=…` (R-API-063) returned it; one it did not return is left out and stays stored. The answer is
  kept for the session, per principal and authorization epoch: the request runs when the home side bar is shown (pinned, or the
  drawer opened) and the newest five hold a name the session has not asked yet, and asks for those names alone. Navigating asks
  nothing; opening a further repository asks for that one name when the home side bar is shown next; a new authorization epoch
  asks again.
- **A repository that is gone leaves the group at once**
  ([Q-UI-769](#q-ui-769--a-repository-that-is-gone-is-removed-from-the-browsers-store-by-the-screen-that-learns-it)), without a
  request and without a new sign-in. Its entry is removed from the store, and with it from the group and from the search field's
  frequently visited repositories (R-UI-096), when
  - the person's deletion of it is accepted, on its settings page or in a list's row, also while the deletion's job still runs;
  - the person moves it to another project: the name it had is removed, and the page it moves to records the new one;
  - the repository's own page, its content page or its settings, is answered with 404.

  The stored repository that becomes one of the newest five is asked for alone when the home side bar is shown next, as a newly
  opened one is. A visit is recorded only when the server answered the page with the repository, and not for a repository that is
  being deleted, so a page that is not found never puts its name into the store.
- **Not shown** while no stored repository is confirmed, to an anonymous visitor, and where the browser's storage is not available
  (`FrequentPlaces.available()`).
- **Narrow and collapsed.** In the drawer below 1024 px the group is a group of the drawer as the others are; the collapsed side
  bar (**Collapse sidebar**, Q-UI-127) is hidden whole, so it hides the group with it.
- The store, its limit of 20 and the search field's use of it (R-UI-096) are unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`app.recent.spec.ts`): the group is the last entry of **Your work**, folded at first; one request for the newest
  five, a name it did not return is left out; an entry's link, mark, key, `title` and accessible name, no field, no button; the
  choice to open it is stored and holds on the next visit; navigating asks nothing again, a newly opened repository is asked alone;
  no group with nothing readable, nothing stored, storage blocked, or anonymous; none in a project's side bar or the admin area;
  in the drawer the request runs when the drawer opens; no serious axe violation. A repository removed from the store leaves the
  group before any answer, the group goes with its last entry, and the stored one that moves up is asked for alone.
- Unit tests of the screens that learn it: the settings page removes the repository when its deletion is accepted while the job
  runs, removes the old name after a move, removes a repository it does not find, and records no visit of one that is being deleted
  (`repository-detail.spec.ts`); the list removes a repository deleted from its row, and opening that row while the job runs
  records nothing (`repository-list.spec.ts`); the content page records the visit once the repository was read and removes one it
  does not find (`repository-content.spec.ts`); the store removes one repository and keeps the others and the projects
  (`frequent-places.spec.ts`).
- Render: `sidebar-recent` as `plain` and `power`, the group open, with the seed's long key.

### R-UI-168 · A side bar is made of titled blocks; Security audit is the second title of Your work's side bar
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's correction of 2026-11-18 (W-17): "Security-Audit hatte ich eigentlich als weiteren context-title erwartet."

- **The model** ([Q-UI-663](#q-ui-663--a-side-bar-is-a-list-of-titled-blocks)). A side bar (`NavArea`) is a list of titled blocks
  (`NavSection`: an id, a context title and its entries, items and folding groups). The home side bar has two: **Your work**
  (Projects, Repositories (Q-UI-1040), Guides, and the group **Recently opened** of R-UI-167) and **Security audit** (**Security dashboard**). The admin area
  has one, **Admin area**; a project's side bar has one, whose title is the project switcher. A block without an entry for the
  caller is left out with its title; an area without a block is left out.
- **The look.** Every context title is the same element in the same place: a `<p class="context-title">` in the accent colour of the
  navigation, at the text size and weight 600, with 8 px of padding and 4 px under it, its text 16 px from the side bar's edge, as
  the area's name always stood. A further block starts
  12 px under the last entry of the block before it. **Security dashboard** is a plain entry with its icon, no folding group and no
  chevron.
- **Accessibility.** Each block is a group of the navigation (`role="group"`) named by its title (`aria-labelledby="nav-<id>"`); a
  project's one block is named by the project's display name. The same in the drawer.
- **Who.** The block **Security audit** is shown to the holder of `content:metadata-read` (R-UI-158), the capability the route's
  guard asks for; without it neither the title nor the entry.
- The trail of the page stays "Security audit / Security dashboard" (R-UI-158); the search's place **Security dashboard** (Q-UI-626)
  and the rule of the Admin button (Q-UI-621) are unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests (`app.spec.ts`): as an auditor at `/security` the side bar's titles are **Your work** and **Security audit**, both
  `p.context-title`, each the name of its group; no group toggle and no chevron in the home side bar; the entries Projects, Repositories, Guides,
  Security dashboard; without the capability one title. `security-dashboard.spec.ts`: the block of the model, and none without
  the capability. The admin area's and a project's side bars keep their tests.
- The journey 16 finds **Security dashboard** in the group named **Security audit** and no button of that name.
- Render: `sidebar-auditor` as `auditor` (the drawer opened at 390 px), and `security` as `admin` and `auditor`; `sidebar-admin` as
  `admin`, the admin area's block without Projects and Repositories (Q-UI-1040).
