### R-UI-170 · An icon stands on the line of its label, and the renders find one that does not
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-18 (W-5, about W-3: "Can you not see something like this yourself?"): a repository's visibility icon
stood alone on the first line of its row and the key started on the second, and the render of that row had been looked at and
passed. The same defect was the jobs' state ("check_circle" above "Succeeded") before Q-UI-560.

- Wherever an icon stands before or after its label (a status, a button, a link, a format, a project's mark, a row's name), the
  icon and the first line of the label share a line ([Q-UI-425](#q-ui-425--an-icon-before-a-name-has-a-column-of-its-own-in-the-cell-and-a-long-name-breaks-inside-itself-beside-it),
  Q-UI-560). An icon its parent lays out above its text (a tile, an empty state, a column) is meant so. Sharing a line is not
  enough: where on that line it stands is R-UI-175.
- `make ui-renders` measures it in every picture and fails the screen on a finding (the check `icon-apart` of
  [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), [Q-UI-682](#q-ui-682--the-render-run-measures-the-layout-in-the-page-and-a-finding-fails-the-screen)),
  for every control as for every icon since R-UI-175: a check box under its label, a copy button under its hash. A control that a
  wrapping row of controls moved to its next line (a toolbar at 390 px) is not a finding; an icon, a mark, a status, a check box
  or a copy button moved away from its text is.

Acceptance criteria:

- The render run's report names no `icon-apart` finding; `failures.txt` would name the screen, the width, the element and its label.

### R-UI-171 · A short thing stays on one line
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

A status or a badge, a chip, a button's label, a tab, a table's header, a date or a time, a key or an identifier in a cell (an
element the app marks `translate="no"`), a number with its unit, a format, a class and a visibility level stand on one line
(R-UI-145, Q-UI-428, Q-UI-563). The toggle of an inline fold is a button, so its label stays on one line too; only the toggle
that is a section's heading wraps as the heading does (Q-UI-810). Not covered: a name that breaks inside itself beside its icon
(Q-UI-425), a key a list lets break after its hyphens (`th.wrap-name`, Q-UI-303), and the name of a row that stands as a block
(R-UI-174).

A value in running text, a host, a repository's key, a digest, a version, a path or a file name, is a `code` the template marks
`translate="no"`, and breaks at none of its hyphens and dots while it fits on a line of its own: it moves to the next line whole, and
breaks inside itself only where it is longer than the line ([Q-UI-1213](#q-ui-1213--a-value-in-running-text-is-one-code-that-moves-whole-to-the-next-line-while-it-fits-on-one)).
A sentence the code builds with a value splits at it (`aroundValue`), and a list of values stands as one (`<quader-value-list>`).

A word of a list's cell does not break inside itself: a column that wraps declares a least width that holds its words (the
audit log's project broke into "Platfor" / "m enginee" / "ring" beside a target that took the room). A token longer than any
column (an identifier, a path, a hash) may still break where it must (Q-UI-425). A status whose words are too long for a pill in a
narrow cell puts its verdict on the badge and the rest after it as muted text that wraps between its words, in a list's cell as
the cell's second line (the signatures' **Signed**
with "signer not trusted", Q-UI-1076). A list of facts (`dl.facts`) puts each term above its value below 36 rem of content, so a
value has the whole line and breaks inside itself only where it is longer than that line (Q-UI-1077).

A heading wraps between its words, after a hyphen, or at a soft hyphen, where the browser draws the hyphen; never between two letters
of a word (the German heading of the authentication settings read "Authentifizierungseinstellung" / "en" at 390 px). A German word
longer than 20 letters carries a soft hyphen at a joint of its compound, so that no run of letters is longer, and breaks there with a
hyphen wherever its line is too short (a heading, a label of the sidebar); a name in a heading (an element marked `translate="no"`)
longer than 16 characters is a token that may break where it must (Q-UI-425)
([Q-UI-1091](#q-ui-1091--a-long-german-word-carries-soft-hyphens-at-the-joints-of-its-compound-and-a-heading-never-breaks-inside-a-word)).

No line starts with a separator: a separator drawn before its item (the middle dot of `.dot-before` and of a line of facts) stands on
the line of what it follows, or a clip hides it at a line's start (`.dot-separated`); any other separator ends the item before it, as a
breadcrumb's slash does ([Q-UI-1173](#q-ui-1173--a-breadcrumbs-separator-ends-the-step-before-it)): "· found 1 hour ago" started a line
on the page Malware, "/ Set up client" the second line of a breadcrumb at 390 px.

Acceptance criteria:

- The render run's report names no `broken` finding (the check `broken` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts)), no
  `heading-broken` finding (a heading broken between two letters of a word) and no `separator-start` finding.
- Fixtures (`layout-checks.spec.ts`, three engines): a malware find's "· found 1 hour ago" wrapped to the start of a line is found; the
  same on one line, the place and the time a line each, and a wrapped line of facts whose first dots the clip hides pass. The web lint
  refuses a separator drawn by CSS in any other way (`separator-rule.mjs`, tested by `lint-rules.test.mjs`).
- Fixtures (`layout-checks.spec.ts`, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit): "Authentifizierungseinstellungen" in a heading of 358 px at the
  first heading's size is found; with a soft hyphen at its joint it breaks there and passes; a heading that wraps between its words and a
  long name pass.
- `make web-i18n-check` fails on a German text with a word of more than 20 letters without a soft hyphen (`longWords` of
  [i18n-check.mjs](../../web/scripts/i18n-check.mjs), tested by `lint-rules.test.mjs`).

### R-UI-172 · A row reads along one line, and its actions are built like its neighbours'
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The first line of every cell of a table's row and every control of a cell without text (an action cell, a check box's cell) have
the middle of the row's name's first line, within the tolerance of R-UI-175 (the walk measured 2 px for **Format** and
**Class**, 5 px for a group's **Remove**; Q-UI-308, Q-UI-562). Middles, not baselines: a 12 px word in a badge has the middle of
the 14 px name beside it and another baseline. A control in a cell stands at the line's top with margins that make it the line's
height, not on its baseline: **Set up client** beside the row's menu stood on the menu glyph's baseline, 3 px under the row's name
(found by the check, 2026-11-18). This holds for every table of the app, its head as well as its body, and for the first line of a
row that stands as a block (R-UI-174); a document's table (the manual, a guide, a README) is prose and not measured. A control in a
cell with text is measured against that text (R-UI-175). The action cells of one table are built one way in every row that has
one: a menu, a word or an icon, as R-UI-163 asks.

Acceptance criteria:

- The render run's report names no `row-offset` and no `row-actions` finding (the checks of the same names in
  [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts)).

### R-UI-173 · Nothing is cut while there is room beside it, and nothing scrolls sideways
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- A text cut with an ellipsis, and a field's value cut, is cut only where the box that holds it has no room for the rest.
- The page scrolls sideways at no width; from 1,024 px no region inside it scrolls sideways either (Q-UI-427, R-UI-085). A table is
  never wider than its place: where its columns do not fit, its rows stack (R-UI-174).
- A tab strip whose tabs are wider than its place keeps them on one line and scrolls sideways without a scrollbar; at an edge
  beyond which tabs lie a fade with a chevron says so and scrolls it by a click, and the current tab and a focused tab stand clear
  of the fades ([Q-UI-1074](#q-ui-1074--a-tab-strip-wider-than-its-place-scrolls-without-a-scrollbar-with-a-fade-and-a-chevron-at-the-edge)).
  Before it scrolls, a strip takes its tabs closer (8 px at each side of a label instead of 12), so that it scrolls only where they do
  not fit that way either: the seven tabs of an Ansible collection's version in German were 13 px wider than their place at 1,024 px
  ([Q-UI-1090](#q-ui-1090--a-tab-strip-takes-its-tabs-closer-before-it-scrolls)).
- Neither the window nor the shell's panel scrolls past the content. The panel and a table's room are the containing blocks of what
  is positioned inside them: a text for assistive technology only (`.visually-hidden`) in rows a region hid stood at its place, far
  below the window's end, and a package's 33 versions had 900 px of empty page under them (the check `empty-scroll`).
- A short text in a table's cell (a summary, a count with its unit) stands on one line where the other columns have the room for it
  and no row uses that room: a column whose width was set wider than every value of it gives the room back (the check `cramped`,
  [Q-UI-1060](#q-ui-1060--what-a-layout-check-can-hold-of-the-render-sets-blind-spots-and-what-stays-to-the-eye); W-5's grade
  "3 findings ·" over "0 fixable" at 1,024 px).
- The renders take a screen at a further width where a list changes its form between the run's three (the start page at 1,100 px,
  the list of every project's repositories at 1,100 and 1,280 px; `widths` of a screen in
  [screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts)).
- An overlay (a dialog, a drawer, a menu, a tooltip, a list that opens under its field) stands inside the window, and what it holds
  stands inside it: W-12's person-search list, 24 rem wide in a drawer of 21 rem, stood past the drawer's edge. From 1,024 px no region
  of an overlay scrolls sideways either (a table wider than its dialog). A state with an open overlay is rendered and measured in the
  window a person has, not in one grown to the page's length
  ([Q-UI-1171](#q-ui-1171--a-state-with-an-open-overlay-is-pictured-and-measured-in-the-window-a-person-has)).
- No text is cut by the box that holds it without an ellipsis: a line of a part of a line of facts that wrapped inside itself started
  under the clip that hides each line's first dot and lost its first letters ("ov 18, 2026"; the check `cut`,
  [Q-UI-1170](#q-ui-1170--the-render-checks-see-overlays-and-clipping-as-a-person-does-correcting-q-ui-1060)).

Acceptance criteria:

- The render run's report names no `clipped`, no `cramped`, no `sideways`, no `tab-scrollbar`, no `overlay-out` and no `cut` finding
  (the checks of the same names in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) and [render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts));
  `make ui-states` measures the dialogs' states by the same `overlay-out` and `sideways`.
- Fixtures (`layout-checks.spec.ts`, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit): the list 24 rem wide in a drawer of 21 rem is found, the list as
  wide as its field passes; a menu of 160 px at x 300 in a window of 390 px is found, flipped to x 214 it passes; a table of 900 px in a
  dialog's body is found at 1,024 px and not at 390 px, a code block that scrolls a long command there is allowed as in a page; the
  line of facts as it was before 2026-11-19 is found with its second line cut, the app's stylesheet passes; a text cut with an ellipsis
  or in a region that scrolls is not `cut`'s, the same text cut bare is.
- Unit (`tab-strip.spec.ts`): a strip whose tabs fit keeps their padding and shows no fade; one whose tabs fit only closer together
  takes them closer and shows none; a wider one shows a fade at each edge beyond which tabs lie and
  a click on it scrolls by the strip's width less the fades; the current tab and a focused tab are scrolled clear of the fades;
  the fades add no text, no tab stop and nothing for a screen reader. The web lint refuses a strip without `quaderTabStrip` and a component with one that does not
  import the directive (`tab-strip-rule.mjs`, tested by `lint-rules.test.mjs`).

### R-UI-174 · A list stacks its rows only where its columns do not fit, and a stacked row is dense
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

At 1,024 px with the side bar open every list of the app stood as blocks, one line per cell, because the shared table stacked
below 48 rem of its own width whatever its columns needed; a package's 33 versions were 5,136 px high there (seen in the builders'
renders, 2026-11-18).

- A data table stacks where its columns at their least widths (a wrapping column's declared `width`, a column that never breaks
  at its longest value) need more than its region has, and only there
  ([Q-UI-680](#q-ui-680--a-list-stacks-where-its-columns-at-their-least-widths-do-not-fit-measured-by-the-table-itself)).
  A column whose cells start with a relative time is at least as wide as the widest relative time of the build's language, so the
  list's form does not follow the ages of its rows
  ([Q-UI-1069](#q-ui-1069--a-column-of-relative-times-holds-the-widest-relative-time-of-its-language)).
- A stacked row is the name with its actions on the first line, then one line per field: its column's name in a column as wide as
  the list's longest name, at most two fifths of the list, and its value beside it, so a field stands at the same place in every
  block ([Q-UI-1050](#q-ui-1050--a-stacked-row-is-a-grid-of-names-and-values-one-field-a-line)). The column is never narrower than
  the longest word of the names, so a name wraps between its words and never inside one, and a list in a block of a stacked list (a
  package's versions opened in a repository's list) measures its own names
  ([Q-UI-1068](#q-ui-1068--a-stacked-rows-column-name-wraps-between-its-words-never-inside-one)). Every name stands on its value's
  first line; a value of two lines grows downwards ([Q-UI-762](#q-ui-762--the-cells-of-a-stacked-rows-line-stand-on-one-baseline)). A meter takes a line of its own: its column's name,
  the bar and its figure on one line, the state under the bar
  ([Q-UI-763](#q-ui-763--a-meter-in-a-stacked-row-is-a-line-of-its-own-name-bar-and-figure-on-one-line)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit test: the table stacks where its least width exceeds its region's and not where it fits, measured again when its rows
  change, and a stacked table measures the longest name its rows show for their column of names, never narrower than their longest
  word, also a list in a block of a stacked list; a column of relative times holds the widest wording (`data-table.spec.ts`).
- The render run's report names no `broken` column's name (a name broken inside a word), and no `stacked-fits`, no `stacked-place`,
  no `stacked-offset` and no `label-apart` finding: a stacked
  table whose columns would fit is a finding, and so is a field of a stacked list off the place of the list's other fields, two fields
  on one line of a block, and a stacked row's name off its value's line or off its neighbours' line.

### R-UI-175 · A control or an icon beside a text stands on the middle of that text's first line
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's walk of 2026-11-19 (W-23), with a picture of the images of a public remote: "Wieso ist denn wieder nur das Icon am
Anfang mittig und die Schrift ist wieder nicht richtig ausgerichtet." The button that opens a row stood 8 px below the line of the
image's name beside it and made the row 65 px high where its text needed 49; the check `icon-apart` passed it, because the
button and the name shared some height. The owner had objected to this class of defect before (R-UI-170, R-UI-172).

- Wherever a control or an icon stands beside a text it belongs to (in a table's row, in a row of a flex or grid box, in running
  text) its vertical middle is the middle of that text's first line, within 1 px
  ([Q-UI-722](#q-ui-722--the-tolerance-of-a-middle-is-1-px-what-the-rounding-of-a-centred-unit-leaves)). It does not make the
  line or the row taller than its text alone makes it, unless the control is the row's content (a toolbar, a row of buttons).
- A control is: a button, an icon button and a disclosure toggle; a link in the form of a button; a check box, a radio button, a
  switch; a select; an input of one line beside its label or value; a chip, a badge, a status (an icon and its word); an avatar,
  a project's mark, a format's or a visibility level's icon, a grade's shield; a copy button; a menu's trigger. An icon is a
  glyph of the icon font. A control that holds an icon is one control: the glyph of a button is the button.
- Its text is the nearest text in its row: beside it, or beside a box it stands in, up to the cell of a table or the box that lays
  out the row ([Q-UI-721](#q-ui-721--a-controls-text-is-the-nearest-text-of-its-row-found-through-the-boxes-that-lay-out-the-row)).
- The exceptions ([Q-UI-724](#q-ui-724--the-exceptions-are-layouts-not-places-above-or-below-a-field-under-its-label-a-picture-a-mark-after-its-text-a-framed-box-a-word-that-wraps)):
  a control laid out above or below its text on purpose (a tile, an empty state, a column of a form); a field with its label
  above it, and a control of several lines (a text area); a picture (an avatar, a project's mark, a grade's shield, `.picture`) at
  least 1.5 lines high beside a name with a second line under it (a person's user name, a project's key), centred on the two
  lines, or beside a card's text, centred on all of it; a mark after its text (a "new window" mark after a link), which may stand
  on the text's last line instead of its first; a control beside a framed box (a code block, a list box), which stands on the box;
  a control with a word of its own (a badge, a status, a chip), which may wrap to a line of its own as a word does.
- The shared rule that does it is one of the global styles
  ([Q-UI-720](#q-ui-720--a-control-is-centred-on-the-line-by-margins-of-half-the-difference-read-from-the-lines-height));
  a screen does not centre a control by hand.

Acceptance criteria:

- The render run's report names no `off-line`, `icon-apart` and `row-offset` finding (R-UI-176).
- The owner's row (`repository-oci` as the power user, the images of a repository) is 49 px high, its button's middle and its
  name's middle within 1 px.

### R-UI-176 · The checks of a control's line are proven on their own pages, and the render set shows every row with a control
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

A check that cannot fail on the defect it names guards nothing: the run after W-5 had no finding while the owner's row stood in
its pictures.

- The render checks measure R-UI-175 in every picture: `off-line` (a control or an icon beside its text, off its middle),
  `icon-apart` (one that shares no height with its line), `row-offset` (a table's row; R-UI-172), `joined` (a button joined to
  a field, an address or a command with its copy button, is as high as the field and is no control beside a text); each names
  the element, its text and the distance in px ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen)).
- The checks are tested on fixture pages of their own in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with the app's fonts, without the UI stack
  (`make ui-layout-test`, [Q-UI-723](#q-ui-723--the-checks-are-tested-on-fixture-pages-in-the-playwright-chromium-not-in-the-angular-test-runner),
  [Q-UI-1045](#q-ui-1045--the-layout-checks-fixtures-run-in-three-engines-and-chromium-sets-text-without-hinting); the screens are
  rendered in Chromium, which sets text without hinting so that the development machine and the runner measure the same widths): the
  owner's row must fail with the 8 px he saw, each exception of R-UI-175 must pass, and an offset of 1.5 px must fail. `make
  ui-renders` runs them before the screens.
- On demand the screens are rendered in Firefox or WebKit, the fixtures first in that engine
  ([Q-UI-1049](#q-ui-1049--the-renders-run-in-firefox-or-webkit-on-demand-into-a-folder-of-their-own)), and the screens marked for it
  in German against the dev server's German build
  ([Q-UI-1048](#q-ui-1048--a-german-pass-of-the-renders-for-the-screens-marked-for-it)), each run into a folder of its own.
- The shared patterns of the style guide are rendered with the app's own global stylesheet on the same pages and must pass, so the
  shared rule holds without a running UI
  ([Q-UI-725](#q-ui-725--the-guard-without-a-stack-renders-the-shared-patterns-with-the-global-stylesheet-and-a-lint-rule-refuses-the-off-line-declarations)). `make web-lint` refuses `vertical-align: middle` and `align-items: last baseline` in a style (the
  declarations that put every icon, badge and mark of the first run off its line), except a table cell's own alignment.
- Every kind of table or list row with a control is in the render set with at least one row (an expandable row, a row with a check
  box, a menu, a copy button, an avatar, a project's mark, a chip or a badge beside a name), so the checks see it
  ([Q-UI-726](#q-ui-726--the-render-set-opens-an-items-row-and-shows-the-public-remote-as-the-visitor-sees-it)).
- The states of the overlays that no walk opens are measured by the same function in a real browser without the stack (`make
  ui-states`, [Q-UI-1140](#q-ui-1140--the-states-of-the-overlays-are-measured-at-the-component-tier-in-the-unit-test-builders-browser-mode)):
  every dialog as it opens with long data, after a submit with invalid fields and with the shared error notice of a failure; the
  confirm dialog's shapes; the token's secret shown once; tooltips at the window's right edge. A state fails on any finding of the
  checks and of R-UI-215's one scroll per overlay, and a copy of a dialog whose button stands 8 px under its name must report
  `off-line` there, one with a block that scrolls inside its scrolling body `inner-scroll`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `make ui-layout-test` passes (`web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts`), its test names carry R-UI-175 and R-UI-176.
- `make ui-states` passes (`web/src/app/**/*.states.spec.ts`), the harness's test name carries R-UI-175 and R-UI-176.
- `make web-lint` passes; the rule's own test fails on both declarations (`web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs`).
- A full render run names no layout finding.

### R-UI-177 · Download limits in the admin area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

The owner's decisions of 2026-11-19 (W-26; [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md)). The admin area's side bar gains two entries
after **Tokens**, in its group Identity ([Q-UI-730](#q-ui-730--the-admin-area-has-two-entries-usage-and-download-limits),
[Q-UI-750](#q-ui-750--the-admin-areas-two-entries-stand-in-identity-after-tokens-the-projects-usage-in-access-after-service-accounts)): **Usage** (`/admin/usage`, R-UI-183)
for holders of `usage:read`, and **Download limits** (`/admin/limits`) for holders of `limits:read`. A caller without either sees
neither.

**Download limits** is one page with the shared page header (title "Download limits") and the tab strip of links under it:
**Rules** (`/admin/limits`), **Profiles** (`/admin/limits/profiles`, R-UI-178), **Projects** (`/admin/limits/projects`),
**Blocks** (`/admin/limits/blocks`).

- **The mode** stands under the header on every tab, as a status line with its word and one sentence: "Mode: **Audit**. Every limit
  is counted and shown; nothing is refused or slowed." or "Mode: **Enforce**. Limits refuse and slow requests." A holder of
  `limits:write` has the button **Switch to Enforce…** or **Switch to Audit…** beside it (R-UI-182). The words Audit and Enforce are
  the owner's and are not translated into other terms.
- **Rules** (the instance place): the rule table of R-UI-179 over `GET /api/v1/limits/assignments`, with **Add rule** in the head for
  a holder of `limits:write`. The built-in rules stand in the order of R-UI-179 with the other rules of their kind
  ([Q-UI-751](#q-ui-751--the-rule-table-lists-the-rules-in-the-order-resolution-tries-them-at-every-place)), each with the badge
  **Built-in**, their action **Change** and no **Delete**. Under the table one line: "Block time after too many refused requests: 15 minutes" with **Change** (a field in minutes,
  1 to 1,440, saved through `PATCH /api/v1/limits/settings`).
- **Projects** ([Q-UI-756](#q-ui-756--the-tab-projects-reads-every-projects-maximum-and-rule-counts-in-one-operation)): one row per project that has a maximum or a rule: the project (mark, display name, key), **Maximum** (the profile's
  name with "+ N changes" for overrides, or "None"), **Rules** (the number at the project and its repositories). For a holder of
  `limits:write` the maximum is the link that opens its dialog (**Set maximum** where there is none), with the profile select and
  the override fields of R-UI-179's dialog, and **Remove maximum** is the row's one action
  ([Q-UI-758](#q-ui-758--a-rule-opens-by-its-name-and-delete-is-the-rows-one-action)). The head's search finds a project by key or name; **Add maximum** opens the dialog with a project field
  first. Empty: "No project has a maximum. A project's Owner can set limits up to the instance's values." 
- **Blocks**: the active blocks, newest first (`GET /api/v1/limits/blocks`): the subject (as in R-UI-183's first column), the place,
  started, ends (a relative time, R-UI-103), the refused requests against the limit ("61 of 60 per hour"), and **Lift** for a holder
  of `limits:write` (a confirmation that names the subject). A filter switch **Show ended blocks** adds the blocks of the last 30
  days with their end or "Lifted by <name>". Empty: "Nothing is blocked."
- A holder of `limits:read` without `limits:write` (the auditor, the security administrator) sees every tab read-only, without the
  actions.

Acceptance criteria:

- The auditor opens **Download limits** and sees the mode, the five built-in rules and no **Add rule**; the administrator sees
  **Add rule** and **Switch to Enforce…**.

### R-UI-178 · The profile editor
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

`/admin/limits/profiles` lists the profiles (`GET /api/v1/limits/profiles`): name with the badge **Built-in**, description, the
eleven figures in one compact cell ("200/s · 1,000 burst · 50,000/h · cache 200 MB/s, 300 GB/h · upstream 50 MB/s, 30 GB/h, 2,000
req/h · 250 parallel transfers · 1,000 GB/day · 500 refused/h"; an unlimited figure is left out; Unlimited reads "Unlimited"), and **Used by**
("4 rules, 1 project maximum"). **New profile** in the head and a row's **Edit** open the editor; **Delete** is offered for an own
profile that nothing uses, else shown disabled with the reason ("Used by 3 rules").

The editor is a page (`/admin/limits/profiles/new`, `/admin/limits/profiles/{key}`), one column as the style guide's settings pages:

- **Name**, **Key** (on create only; filled from the name, editable, the pattern's help "Lower case letters, digits and hyphens"),
  **Description (optional)**.
- The figures in four groups, each a heading and its fields, each field as wide as its input (R-UI-087's rule; a field of seven
  digits and its unit): **Requests** (per second, burst, per hour), **From the cache** (MB per second, GB per hour), **From the
  upstream** (MB per second, GB per hour, upstream requests per hour), **Transfers** (in parallel, GB per day; the figure counts
  transfers, [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-041), **Refused requests**
  (per hour). The value is in the field (a default is a value in the field, [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md)); an empty field is unlimited, and the field
  says so as its placeholder "Unlimited". Units are decimal: 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes, 1 GB 1,000,000,000
  ([Q-UI-736](#q-ui-736--the-ui-shows-decimal-mb-and-gb-the-api-bytes)); the API's bytes are converted on load and on save, and a
  value that is not a whole number of bytes after conversion is rounded down.
- A help line per group, one sentence: what happens at the limit ("At the limit a request is answered 429 with the time to wait.",
  "Above the rate a download is slowed down; above the hourly amount the next download is refused before it starts.", "With the
  upstream budget used up, what is cached is still served.", "Each layer of an image and each package of an install is one
  transfer: a pull runs 3 to 6 at once, an npm, pnpm or Yarn install 8 to 64, a NuGet restore one per package. A further transfer
  waits up to 10 seconds, then is refused, or at once while a server holds many waiting transfers.", what one pull or install holds
  (R-LIM-041), the wait and the share of R-LIM-024), and under **From the
  cache** the note that a very low rate makes a large file take longer than some clients wait in total.
- Unlimited cannot be edited: its page shows the figures read-only with "Unlimited is always unlimited."
- **Save** sends `PUT` (or `POST`) with `If-Match`; a `412` opens the conflict dialog of R-UI-042.

Acceptance criteria:

- Changing Standard's "From the cache, GB per hour" from 300 to 250 sends `cachedBytesPerHour: 250000000000`.
- Emptying a field sends `null`, and the list shows the figure no more.

### R-UI-179 · The rule table and the rule dialog
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

One component (`<quader-limit-rules>`) lists the rules of a place and is used at the instance (R-UI-177), a project and a repository
(R-UI-180), so that the three places look and work the same.

- **Columns**: **Applies to** (the "who": for a user the avatar, the display name and under it `@username`; a group its icon and
  name; a technical token its key icon, its name and under it its account (`sa:web/partner`); a CI project the CI icon, the project
  path and under it the issuer; an address range in the monospace type; "Every signed-in user", "Every technical token", "Every CI
  job", "Every anonymous caller", "Every administrator"; a rule whose "who" was deleted "(deleted)" in the secondary type),
  and the rule's note as a muted line under it, [Q-UI-1001](#q-ui-1001--a-download-rules-note-stands-under-whom-it-applies-to)),
  **Profile** (the name, and "+ uncached 20 GB/h" for each override, at most two, then "+ N more"), and **Delete** as the
  row's one action; the name of the "who" opens the rule's dialog (**Change**) for a caller who may change it, and a built-in rule
  has no action ([Q-UI-758](#q-ui-758--a-rule-opens-by-its-name-and-delete-is-the-rows-one-action)). A capped rule whose figures are clamped now carries the warning badge **Above the maximum** with a tooltip
  that names the figures and what applies.
- **Order**: single callers and addresses, then groups, then the kinds, as resolution tries them (R-LIM-013); within each, by name.
- **The dialog** (**Add rule**, **Change**):
  - **Applies to**: a choice of **A user**, **A group**, **A technical token**, **A CI project**, **An address or range**, **Every
    caller of a kind**. A user, a group, a technical token and a CI project are chosen in the shared principal field (R-UI-150),
    which gains the kinds technical token and CI project, whose matches come from `GET /api/v1/limits/subjects` (a technical token's
    row: its key icon, its name, under it its account; a CI project's row: the project path, under it the issuer and the ID); at a
    project or repository the field searches through the project's lookup (R-API-077) and the subjects of the project. An address is
    a field of the width of an IPv6 prefix with the help "An address, or a range such as 198.51.100.0/24 or 2001:db8:1::/48". A kind
    is a select. On **Change** the "who" is read-only.
  - **Profile**: a select of the profiles by name, with the figures of the chosen one shown read-only under it in the compact form of
    R-UI-178.
  - **Change single figures**: a closed disclosure (details on demand) with the eleven fields of R-UI-178, each holding the chosen
    profile's value ([Q-UI-752](#q-ui-752--the-single-figures-of-a-rule-hold-the-profiles-values-a-changed-field-is-an-override));
    a field whose value the person changed is an override and has a link **Use the profile's value**. An empty field reads
    "Unlimited"; emptying a field of a limited figure overrides it to unlimited. A rule writes only the figures that differ from the
    profile.
  - **Note (optional)**.
  - At a project or a repository, for a caller without `limits:write`: a line under the profile names the cap, "You can set up to
    the instance's values for this caller, or up to the project's maximum (Technical)", and a `422 limit_above_maximum` marks each
    named field with its cap ("At most 30 GB per hour here").
- Empty table (a project or a repository): "No rule here. Callers get the instance's limits." The instance never has an empty
  table.

Acceptance criteria:

- The same rule table renders at `/admin/limits`, at a project's settings and at a repository's settings with the same columns.
- Adding a rule for the group `contractors` with Restricted and one override sends one `POST` with `who`, `profile` and the single
  override.

### R-UI-180 · The limits of a project and of a repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

Simple by default ([CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md), [Q-UI-731](#q-ui-731--at-a-project-and-a-repository-the-limits-are-a-closed-section-of-the-settings)):
the plain path of a project and of a repository shows nothing of the limits.

- **A project's settings** (`/projects/{project}/settings`) gain a closed section **Download limits** before **Advanced**, for an
  Owner and for holders of `limits:read`. Its title line says "2 rules" when the project has rules and "Maximum: Technical" when it
  has a maximum, else nothing. Open, it shows one sentence ("Rules here apply to the project's repositories that have no rules of
  their own."), the project's maximum as a read-only line ("Maximum given by an administrator: Technical" or "No maximum: you can
  set limits up to the instance's values."), and the rule table of R-UI-179 with **Add rule**. A link **Usage of this project**
  leads to R-UI-183 in the project's scope.
- **A repository's settings** (R-UI-087) gain a closed section **Download limits** after **Access details**. Its title line says the
  number of rules when there are any. Open, it shows the rule table of R-UI-179 for the repository and, for a remote repository, the
  group **Ceilings** with one sentence ("All callers of one kind together; a request must fit both its caller's limit and the
  ceiling.") and two rows, **All anonymous callers** and **All signed-in callers**, each with **GB per hour from the upstream** and
  **Upstream requests per hour** (empty: unlimited) and its own **Save changes**. A link **Usage of this repository** leads to
  R-UI-183 scoped to the repository.
- **A repository's service accounts**: a closed section **Service accounts** after **Download limits** (R-UI-181).
- A member who is no Owner sees neither section; a holder of `limits:read` sees them read-only.
- The project's side bar for an Owner gains **Usage** (`/projects/{project}/usage`) after **Service accounts**; it is listed only for
  an Owner and for holders of `usage:read`.

Acceptance criteria:

- An Owner opens a remote's settings: **Download limits** is closed and says nothing; opened, it shows "No rule here." and the
  ceilings empty. A reader of the project sees no such section.

### R-UI-181 · Technical tokens at the instance, a project and a repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

The owner's word is **technical token** (decisions 12 and 13): the service account carries the rights, each technical token below
it is named for the system that uses it and has a budget of its own
([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-045, R-AUTH-046,
[Q-UI-734](#q-ui-734--a-technical-token-is-a-named-row-of-its-service-accounts-page-with-its-limit-and-its-usage)).

- **The service account's page** (R-UI-026) at the instance (`/admin/service-accounts/{name}`), at a project
  (`/projects/{project}/service-accounts/{name}`) and at a repository (`/projects/{project}/repositories/{repo}/service-accounts/{name}`)
  calls its section **Technical tokens**, open while the account has one. Its list: **Token** (the name, under it the hint of its
  current secret with its expiry, "qdr_sat_kMbd · expires in 2 months" or "· never expires", **Expires soon** under it in the last
  days, and its description), **Limit** (the profile of the token's own rule, "+ N changes", or "Default (Technical)", and as the
  cell's second line the last 24 hours, "95,695 requests · 518.8 GB in 24 h" or "Not used in 24 h",
  [Q-UI-761](#q-ui-761--a-technical-tokens-last-24-hours-is-the-second-line-of-its-limit)), **Last used**, and the actions
  **Rotate** and **Revoke**; the limit itself opens its rule dialog, **Set limit** or **Change limit** with **Remove limit**
  in it ([Q-UI-759](#q-ui-759--a-technical-tokens-limit-opens-its-rule-dialog-and-the-row-keeps-rotate-and-revoke)). A token without
  a live secret is listed apart, without its limit, and shows **Expired** or **Revoked** and the action **Issue new secret**. Every
  row has a menu **Actions for <token>** beside its words, with **Edit description** (a dialog of the one field, saved with the token's
  `ETag`) and **Delete** (after the question every removal asks), for `identities:write` or an Owner of the account's project
  ([Q-UI-1007](#q-ui-1007--a-technical-tokens-description-is-edited-and-the-token-deleted-from-its-rows-menu)). At
  1,024 px and wider both lists are tables.
- **New technical token** (the section's head) opens the create dialog of R-UI-026 with **Name** first (required; help: "The system
  that uses this token, for example `nightly-mirror`. It cannot be changed."), then description, expiry, scope and endpoints as
  today. The secret is shown once, as today.
- **Set limit** opens the rule dialog of R-UI-179 with the "who" fixed to this token and the place of its account (the instance,
  the project, the repository); for a token with a rule it is **Change limit**, with **Remove limit** at the dialog's foot.
- The tokens with a live secret and the ended ones are two tables of the section, the ended ones under **Expired and revoked** with
  the column **Ended** (when and how the last secret ended) after **Token**, so that the action cells of a table are built one
  way (R-UI-163, [Q-UI-740](#q-ui-740--the-ended-technical-tokens-are-a-table-of-their-own)).
- **Rotate** is offered to the administrator role; an Owner revokes and issues a new secret
  ([Q-AUTH-419](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-419--an-owner-of-the-project-does-not-rotate-the-secret-of-a-technical-token-it-issues-a-new-one)).
  **Revoke** revokes the token's live secrets; the token stays, ended.
- **Issue new secret** opens the create dialog without the name; the result is shown once.
- **A repository's service accounts**: the repository's settings section **Service accounts** (R-UI-180) lists the repository's
  accounts (name as `sa:<project>/<repo>/<name>`, description, the actions it holds, state, technical tokens) with **New service
  account**: a dialog with **Name**, **Description (optional)** and **Rights on this repository**, one checkbox per action (Read,
  Annotate, Deploy, Overwrite, Delete, Manage) with the one-line help of R-UI-027; Read is ticked. A row opens the account's page,
  whose top holds the rights as the same checkboxes with **Save changes**.
- **The admin area's Service accounts** list gains the column **Level** (Instance, Project, Repository) and shows the repository of a
  repository's account beside its project; the filter by project includes its repositories' accounts.
- **The admin area's Tokens** (R-UI-030) shows a technical token's secret as "<token name> · <hint>" with the account as its owner.
- An Owner sees the create, renew, revoke and limit actions on the accounts of its project and of its repositories; a holder of
  `identities:write` alone does not see **New technical token** (R-UI-026's rule stays).

Acceptance criteria:

- An Owner creates the repository account `ci` on `web/npm-local` with Read and Deploy, issues the technical token `release`, and
  the token publishes to `web/npm-local`; rotating it keeps the row and its last 24 hours.

### R-UI-182 · The mode switch
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

**Switch to Enforce…** ([Q-UI-733](#q-ui-733--the-mode-switch-shows-what-the-last-24-hours-would-have-been-before-it-is-flipped)) opens a
dialog titled "Switch to Enforce" that shows, before anything changes, what the last 24 hours would have been in Enforce
(`GET /api/v1/limits/mode-preview`):

- one sentence each, with the numbers: "12 callers would have been limited.", "3,400 requests would have been refused.", "25
  downloads would have been slowed down.", "1 caller would have been blocked."; under it the figures that would have refused most
  (the three of `byFigure` with the most events) and the kinds of caller (`byKind`), each linked to the overview filtered by
  **Would have been limited**;
- when nothing would have been limited: "In the last 24 hours no caller would have been limited.";
- the consequence in one line: "From now on, limits refuse and slow requests on every replica within seconds."
- **Switch to Enforce** (primary) sends `PATCH /api/v1/limits/settings {"mode": "enforce"}` with `If-Match`, after recent
  authentication (R-API-007, R-UI-042); **Cancel**.

**Switch to Audit…** is the step that removes protection: an instance starts in Enforce, and in Audit no request limit holds on
the protocol paths ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-026, [Q-LIM-4](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-4--in-audit-nothing-on-a-protocol-path-is-refused-or-slowed-the-package-classes-of-r-api-016-included)). It opens a
dialog with one sentence, "In Audit nothing is refused or slowed on the package and registry addresses, not even by the request
limits; every limit is counted and shown as "Would have been limited".", and **Switch to Audit**. After either switch the status line of R-UI-177 changes and a notice confirms it.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the preview's fixture of 12 callers, the dialog shows "12 callers would have been limited." and its link opens the overview
  with the state filter set.

### R-UI-183 · The usage overview
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

`/admin/usage` (instance scope, `usage:read`) and `/projects/{project}/usage` (project scope, an Owner and `usage:read`), with
`?repository=<repo>` for one repository ("who pulls most here"). The page's title is "Usage", in a project "Usage of <project
display name>", for a repository "Usage of <repository key>".

- **Head** (R-UI-100): the search by name or address; **Filters** (the drawer of R-UI-101) with **Kind** (Users, Technical tokens,
  CI, Anonymous addresses, System), **State** (Close to the limit, Limit reached or Would have been limited, Blocked) and, in the instance
  scope, **Project**; the period as a segmented control **Last hour**, **Last 24 hours**, **Last 30 days**; **Export CSV** as a quiet
  button (`…/usage/export` with the same filters).
- **Two views as links over the table**: **Close to the limit** and **Limit reached** (in Audit **Would have been limited**), each the state
  filter set, beside **All callers**. The filters, the period, the search and the sort are the page address's parameters, so a link
  opens the overview filtered ([Q-UI-755](#q-ui-755--the-usage-overview-keeps-its-filters-in-the-address-the-instances-project-filter-narrows-the-instances-list)).
- **In Audit mode** a line under the head says "Mode: Audit. Limits are counted, not applied." and every state reads "Would have been
  limited" instead of "Limit reached".
- **Columns**: **Caller** (as R-UI-179's first column; an anonymous address in the monospace type, a CI project by path, "System" for
  the system; a blocked subject with the badge **Blocked**), **Requests**, **From the cache**, **From the upstream**, **Upstream
  requests**, **Refused**, and **Now** (the meter, [Q-UI-732](#q-ui-732--the-meter-shows-the-tightest-hour-or-day-figure-now-not-the-periods)):
  a bar of the utilisation of the tightest hour or day figure with its percentage, and its state as text under it (**Close to the
  limit** from 70 %, **Limit reached** or **Would have been limited**, **Unlimited**, nothing for normal); the bar's colour follows the
  design tokens for warning and danger, never green (green only for a positive status). The figure beside the bar is the
  percentage, and the tooltip names the figure and the place ("From the cache per hour at the instance: 82 % of the limit"): a list
  row carries the ratio, not the amounts ([Q-UI-757](#q-ui-757--the-overviews-meter-says-the-percentage-the-callers-page-the-amounts));
  the caller's page shows the amounts ("246 GB of 300 GB").
- Every numeric column sorts (the head's sort control and the column header); bytes in decimal units with one decimal ("1.2 GB"),
  the exact count in the tooltip.
- A row opens the subject's detail (R-UI-184).
- From 80 rem of the list every column shows; below, **Upstream requests** and **Refused** give way first, then the row stacks
  (R-UI-174, [Q-UI-760](#q-ui-760--the-usage-overviews-upstream-requests-and-refused-give-way-below-80-rem)).
- **Empty states**: no usage in the period, "No downloads in the last 24 hours."; a filter that matches nothing, "No caller matches.";
  in a project scope without protocol traffic, "Nobody downloaded from this project in the last 24 hours."
- **What each kind of user sees** (R-UI-067): an administrator and an auditor the instance scope with addresses; a project Owner its
  project's scope with the names and addresses of the callers of its repositories; nobody else reaches the page (the route's guard
  sends them to their own usage, R-UI-185).

Acceptance criteria:

- The overview with 60 seeded subjects sorts by **From the cache** descending; **Close to the limit** lists exactly the subjects with
  a ratio from 0.7 below 1 and no limit event.
- A project Owner's overview lists an anonymous address that pulled from its public remote, and no subject that only used another
  project.

### R-UI-184 · A caller's usage, and which limit applies
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

`/admin/usage/{kind}/{id}` and `/projects/{project}/usage/{kind}/{id}` (`GET …/usage/subjects/{kind}/{id}`). The title names the
caller, not its reference: a user's display name ("Priya Raman"), a technical token's name ("deploy-prod"), a CI project's path
("acme/web"), an address ("198.51.100.23"); the breadcrumb's last step is the same words
([Q-UI-765](#q-ui-765--a-callers-page-is-titled-with-the-callers-name-and-its-reference-stands-under-it)).

- **Top**: under the title the caller's kind and its reference (a user's `@priya`, a CI project's issuer), for a technical token a
  link to its account; a client certificate's kind alone, since its title is the certificate's subject and **By credential** tells
  two certificates apart by their serial; when blocked, a notice
  "Blocked until 10:55 after 61 refused requests in an hour" with **Lift block** for a caller who may lift it.
- **Limits**: one block per budget key (the instance, and each project or repository whose rule applies to it): its place, the rule
  that applies and why in one sentence, read from the explanation ("Rule for the group contractors at web/npm-remote, profile
  Restricted, one figure changed"), and every figure as a row: the figure's name, a meter of used against limit for the windowed
  figures (**Requests per hour**, **From the cache per hour**, **From the upstream per hour**, **Upstream requests per hour**,
  **Volume per day**, **Parallel transfers**, **Refused per hour**), and the rates as text (**Requests per second**, **From the cache
  per second**, **From the upstream per second**); an unlimited figure reads "Unlimited".
- **Which limit applies**: a quiet button **Explain for a repository**, which opens a panel with a repository field (the repositories
  of the scope) and shows the steps of R-LIM-035 as an ordered list ("Repository web/npm-remote: no rule for alice. Groups: rule for
  contractors applies."), the effective figures, a clamp ("Above the project's maximum: 30 GB applies") and the ceiling of a remote.
- **Last 24 hours**: the five-minute history as three small charts over one time line, requests, from the cache and from the
  upstream, each with its own axis and one series in the data colour; the points with refused requests or limit events are marked
  over the requests in the warning colour, named in the legend
  ([Q-UI-754](#q-ui-754--the-history-is-three-small-charts-of-one-axis-each-not-one-chart-of-three-series)). A pointer over a chart, or
  the arrow keys on it, reads one point out in words; a table of the same points stands behind **Show as table** for keyboard and
  screen-reader users; the colours follow the design tokens.
- **By repository** (for the period of the head): repository, requests, from the cache, from the upstream, upstream requests,
  refused; sortable.
- **By credential** (a user and a certificate subject): a user's **Browser session** and each personal token by its description and
  hint; a certificate subject's certificates, each **Client certificate** with its serial, so that a renewed certificate stands
  beside the one it replaced ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-027); with requests, from the cache and from the
  upstream.
- The period control of R-UI-183 stands in the head and changes **By repository** and **By credential**; the limits and the 24 hours
  stay "now".

Acceptance criteria:

- For a user who downloaded through a session and two tokens, **By credential** lists three rows whose sum equals the totals.
- **Explain for a repository** for Alice at `web/npm-remote` lists the steps of R-LIM-013's first worked example.

### R-UI-185 · A user's own usage on the profile
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

The profile's tab strip (R-UI-029) gains **Usage** (`/profile/usage`, [Q-UI-735](#q-ui-735--a-users-own-usage-is-a-tab-of-the-profile))
for every signed-in user (`GET /api/v1/users/me/usage`):

- the caller's own limits per budget key, as R-UI-184's **Limits**, with the sentence "Your limits come from <rule>." instead of the
  administrator's wording;
- **Which limit applies** as R-UI-184, over `GET /api/v1/users/me/limits` and the repositories the user can read;
- **Last 24 hours**, **By repository** and **By credential** as R-UI-184;
- a blocked user sees the block's notice without an action;
- in Audit mode the line "Limits are counted, not applied yet." and every state as "Would have been limited".
- Empty: "You have not downloaded anything in the last 24 hours."

Acceptance criteria:

- A user whose personal token was refused with `download_limit_reached` opens the link of the refusal's `detail` and sees
  **From the cache per hour** at 100 % with "Limit reached".

### R-UI-186 · What a limited caller sees in the UI
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

- The UI's own calls go to the management API, which the figures do not limit (R-API-016); its downloads (a file's **Download**, a
  package version's download) go to `/files/` or a protocol path and can be refused.
- A download refused with one of the codes of [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-020 shows a notice, not an error
  page: "Your download limit of 300 GB per hour is used up. Try again in 14 minutes.", written in the reader's language from the
  problem's members `figure`, `limit` and `retryAfterSeconds` (the problem's `detail` where it lacks them), with the link **See
  your usage** to `/profile/usage`; a `caller_blocked` says "Downloads are paused for you until 10:55 after too many refused
  requests."; a `too_many_parallel_transfers` says "You have 250 transfers running, the most you may have at once; each layer of an
  image and each package of an install is one." (R-LIM-041). A caller without a session (a visitor) gets the same text without the link. The UI learns of the refusal by asking for
  the download's first byte before the browser downloads
  ([Q-UI-753](#q-ui-753--a-download-of-the-ui-asks-for-its-first-byte-before-the-browser-downloads-it)).
- A slowed download is not announced: the browser's download shows its rate.

Acceptance criteria:

- A file download refused with `too_many_parallel_transfers` shows the notice with the problem's text and the link, and the page
  stays as it was.

### R-UI-187 · Upstream registries in the admin area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-20 ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md)
[Q-REPO-370](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-370--a-built-in-project-upstream-holds-the-products-well-known-repositories)): a page of
its own in the admin area on which an administrator switches each well-known repository on or off and sets its visibility, with one
action that switches all on and one that sets the visibility of all
([Q-UI-830](#q-ui-830--upstream-registries-is-one-list-grouped-by-format-with-a-switch-and-a-level-in-each-row)).

- **Where.** The admin area's single entry **Upstream registries** after **Repositories** (R-UI-002), icon `cloud_download`
  ([Q-UI-838](#q-ui-838--upstream-registries-takes-the-icon-cloud_download-of-the-admin-areas-side-bar)), route `/admin/upstream`, for a caller with `repositories:read-config`; the page reads
  `listUpstreamRepositories` (R-API-083).
- **Header.** Title **Upstream registries**, with the number of preset repositories as its badge; the sentence "The public
  registries this installation offers to every project. Each is off until you switch it on." The primary action **Switch all on**
  (`btn btn-confirm`), the second **Set visibility of all** (`btn btn-default`); both only for `repositories:write-config`, and
  **Switch all on** disabled with the reason "Every registry is on." when nothing is off.
- **The list**: the head of every list with **Filter registries** (by display name and key, R-UI-100); one table whose rows are grouped
  by format in catalog order, each group headed by a row with the format's icon and display name (`<quader-format-icon>`, R-UI-145).
  Columns:
  1. **Registry**: the display name (the link to R-UI-188) and, muted under it, `upstream/<key>` as a name.
  2. **On**: a switch (`role="switch"`, `aria-checked`, the shared `<quader-switch>`, its accessible name "Switch on Docker Hub") with

     (R-UI-141). A row whose repository is `private` and on says under its name,

  4. **Listed by**: the number of virtual repositories that list it (`num`), or the en dash.
  5. One action, **Details** (R-UI-163), which opens R-UI-188.
  A note under the name, muted, where it applies: "Address differs from Quader's"; "The account was removed when Quader's address moved

- **Registries of this installation.** Below the table, the section of R-UI-195 with the presets an administrator keeps for the form
  of a new remote repository.
- **System repositories.** Below them a second table, **System repositories** (the name of the project's page, [Q-UI-900](#q-ui-900--the-admin-page-of-the-upstream-registries-names-the-same-two-system-repositories)), holds the system repositories: `scanner-trivy` with the
  display name "Image scanning database", the state as a badge, **In use** (`ok`) "In use by the image scanning" or **Not in use**,
  the level as text (Private, with the lock icon) and **Details**; no switch and no select
  ([Q-UI-834](#q-ui-834--the-system-repositories-stand-in-a-table-of-their-own-without-a-switch)). `clamav`
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-075) stands below it the same way, with the display name "ClamAV
  definitions" and "In use by the malware scan" ([Q-UI-883](#q-ui-883--a-system-repository-names-the-work-it-serves-and-a-local-one-has-no-address-and-no-account)),
  and it is the one row of the table with a switch: **ClamAV definition updates**, the shared `<quader-switch>` with its accessible name
  "ClamAV definition updates" and **On** or **Off** after it, and, while on, the level as text; read-only callers see the word only
  ([Q-UI-903](#q-ui-903--clamav-definition-updates-is-a-switch-in-the-row-and-a-section-of-the-registrys-page)). Switching it on opens a

  Public: anyone who reaches this address can download them, without a credential." with **Switch on** (the request asks for a recent
  sign-in where the session needs one); switching off asks "Stop serving the ClamAV definitions? ClamAV installations that update from

  line "Docker Hub is on." Switching off a repository that virtual repositories list asks first: "Switch off Docker Hub? 3 virtual

  and `listedByProjects` of the list's item, [Q-API-363](#q-api-363--the-item-counts-the-listing-virtual-repositories-and-their-projects-and-an-answer-about-one-repository-names-them)).
- **Switch all on** opens a dialog: "Switch on 11 registries? Each is Internal once it is on: everyone signed in who is not marked external,
  people and their pipelines and service accounts, can pull through it, directly and through every virtual repository that lists it.
  Quader contacts each registry when a client asks for something it has not stored." with the names of the registries it switches on, and **Switch all on**. It never offers Public (owner).
- **Set visibility of all** opens a dialog with the radio group of the levels (`<quader-visibility-level>`, Q-UI-228) and **Set
  visibility**. **Public** in either place, the dialog or a row's select, asks first with the sentence the owner asked for:
  "Public: anyone on the internet can pull through this installation, on its bandwidth and on its upstream allowance (Docker Hub's pull
  limit, for example)." with **Make public**; the request then asks for a recent sign-in where the session needs one (R-API-007).
- **Errors and conflicts** follow R-UI-042; `public_not_allowed` and `visibility_level_restricted` stand at the row's select.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, `upstream-registries.spec.ts`, about 2 s; the screens rendered under rule 11 of promt.md, light and
dark, wide and narrow, with the twelve presets and one retired fixture):

- The page shows the groups OCI (Docker), npm, NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy with their rows, and `scanner-trivy` under **Used by
  Quader**; an auditor sees no switch, no select, no header actions.
- Switching Docker Hub on sends `PUT …/upstream-repositories/docker-hub/state` with `{"state": "on"}`; switching off `npmjs`, which one
  virtual repository lists, asks first.
- **Switch all on** names the registries that are off and sends `switch-on-all`; choosing Public in a row asks with the sentence above.

### R-UI-189 · A well-known repository as a member of a virtual repository
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **The picker** (R-UI-022, R-UI-081's group **Members**): under the project's repositories, the group **Upstream registries** lists the
  well-known repositories of the virtual repository's format that are not retired: the display name, `upstream/<key>` as a name, and a
  `warn` badge **Not switched on** or **Switched off** where the repository is not active
  ([Q-UI-832](#q-ui-832--the-picker-offers-the-upstream-registries-of-the-format-as-a-group-of-their-own)). A team may pick one that is
  off; the save then shows the warning `member_inactive` in words.
- **A placeholder** in the selected list keeps its place and shows its state: the badge (**Not switched on**, **Switched off**, **No
  longer offered**) and one muted sentence under it ([Q-UI-833](#q-ui-833--a-placeholder-keeps-its-place-with-a-badge-and-one-sentence)):
  "Skipped until an administrator of Quader switches it on." / "Skipped: an administrator of Quader switched it off." / "Skipped: Quader
  no longer offers it. Remove it." An active member whose level is `private` says "Private: the readers of this virtual repository do
  not read through it unless a global policy names them."
- **The section's head** says how many members take no part, when any: "1 member takes no part: upstream/npmjs." The "Effective
  resolution order" view marks placeholders as skipped.
- **Where the states come from.** A caller with `repositories:read-config` reads the states above from `listUpstreamRepositories`.
  Whoever may write the member list, the creation form and the editor of a caller who may change the repository (an Owner of its
  project or a holder of `repositories:write-config`), reads the state and the level of each preset of the format that is not
  retired from `listFormatUpstreamRepositories` ([Q-API-364](#q-api-364--a-writer-of-a-virtual-repository-reads-the-state-and-the-level-of-a-formats-well-known-repositories-through-an-operation-of-its-own)); a member that names none of them is **No longer offered**.
  A caller who reads the member list but may not change it, and one that read refuses, is offered the format's upstream presets and
  learns of each only what the repository list answers: one it reads that is disabled is **Off** ("Skipped until an administrator of
  Quader switches it on."), one it does not read shows no state ([Q-UI-840](#q-ui-840--a-reader-who-may-not-change-a-virtual-repository-learns-a-registrys-state-from-what-it-reads)).
- **Explain a path** names a placeholder by its state, from `upstreamState` of the resolution explanation, in the words of its badge:
  "Not switched on, so not asked", "Switched off, so not asked", "No longer offered, so not asked".
- The repository's header and the members list show nothing else of it; the client setup of the virtual repository is unchanged.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, the member editor's spec, about 1 s; journey `R-UI-022` unchanged): the picker of an npm virtual repository
lists `npm-local` and, in **Upstream registries**, `npm public registry` with `upstream/npmjs` and **Not switched on**; adding it and
saving sends `members: ["npm-local", "upstream/npmjs"]`; the selected list shows the badge and the sentence.

### R-UI-190 · The project `upstream` in the main area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **Lists.** The project is listed where R-AUTHZ-041 admits the caller, by its mark and display name **Upstream** with the badge
  **Built-in** after the name, its key, its description (the UI's localized sentence, not the stored English one,
  [Q-UI-895](#q-ui-895--the-built-in-projects-description-is-a-localized-text-of-the-ui)), the number of repositories the caller reads and no role or members
  ([Q-UI-835](#q-ui-835--the-project-upstream-is-a-project-with-the-badge-built-in-and-no-administration)); with the columns of
  an administrator (R-UI-041) it has no Owners. It stands first in every list of projects it is in, above the other
  projects whatever the list is sorted by (a filter that does not match it takes it out), and its mark carries an arrow pointing
  up where every other project's carries its initial
  ([Q-UI-837](#q-ui-837--the-project-upstream-stands-first-in-a-list-of-projects-and-its-mark-is-an-arrow-pointing-up)). It shows no
  level of its own: its Visibility cell is the en dash, heard as "Each registry has its own visibility.", and no level icon stands
  beside its name in the lists, the switcher or a header ([Q-UI-844](#q-ui-844--the-project-upstream-shows-no-level-of-its-own-each-registry-has-one)).
- **Its side bar**: the switcher, **Repositories**, **Packages**, **Vulnerabilities**; no **Access** group (it has no members,
  policies, service accounts or CI mappings) and no **Settings** entry. Its repository list is the project list of R-UI-020 with the
  state of each repository as a badge (**Off**, **No longer offered**) for a caller with `repositories:read-config`; a caller without
  it sees only what it reads. Its system repositories stand below the list in a closed section of their own (R-UI-192).
- **A repository's content page** (R-UI-052) of a retired registry says **No longer offered** in place of **Disabled**, and under its
  header the sentence of R-UI-188's retired page, for a caller with `repositories:read-config` (read with `getUpstreamRepository` while the
  repository is disabled); any other caller sees **Disabled**, as for every disabled repository (Q-UI-840).
- **A repository's settings page** (R-UI-087): Key and Description read-only; **Visibility** and **Upstream** read-only, each with the
  line "Managed in Admin area › Upstream registries." linked to R-UI-188 for an administrator; **Visibility** has no fold **Wiki
  visibility**, because the repository's one level covers its packages and its documentation and the repository document refuses a
  change of either (`422 managed_by_product` at `/visibility`, R-REPO-069); no **Access details** (a remote has no include and exclude
  patterns, its delivery rules narrow it, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-002, and Hide existence is the product's);
  the vulnerability settings, **Offline** and the cache-fill action editable for `repositories:write-config`; no
  **Mirror**, no **Disable repository**, no **Move to another project**, no **Delete repository**. `scanner-trivy` shows everything
  read-only, its level as one statement in place of the group of levels, "Its visibility is always Private: only Quader's image
  scanning reads it.", without the line "Managed in …", which stays under **Upstream**, where its address is managed; `clamav`
  the same with "Its visibility is Private while ClamAV definition updates is off.", or its level while it is on, with the line "Managed in
  Admin area › Upstream registries." (Q-UI-883, Q-UI-903). The format's settings are read-only, **Hide existence** and **Service accounts** are absent, **Administrator notes**
  stays editable; the vulnerability settings and the cache-fill action have no field on the settings page of any repository and
  are set through the API ([Q-UI-842](#q-ui-842--the-settings-page-of-a-well-known-repository-reads-what-the-product-holds-and-edits-what-an-administrator-narrows)).
- **Set up client** of a preset repository is the page of R-UI-120, as for any remote. A system repository has none: no screen offers
  **Set up client** for it, neither its row, its page, the guides nor a package's install panel (the owner's
  [Q-UI-891](#q-ui-891--the-system-repositories-of-upstream-stand-apart-below-the-list-closed-and-without-set-up-client),
  [Q-UI-896](#q-ui-896--no-screen-offers-a-client-action-for-a-system-repository-one-function-decides-the-link)). Its page `…/setup`, opened
  by its address, says for `scanner-trivy` "Quader's image scanning reads its database through this repository. Clients cannot use it."
  and shows no snippet; for `clamav` while ClamAV definition updates is off "Quader's malware scan keeps its signature database in this

- **Search, Recently opened and the guides** list well-known repositories like any repository the caller reads, with the project's

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, about 1 s; rendered under rule 11): the project list shows **Upstream** with **Built-in**, first, above a
project whose name and key sort before it, also when the list is sorted the other way, and its mark holds an arrow and no letter; its side bar
has no **Access** and no **Settings**; the settings page of `upstream/npmjs` for an administrator shows **Upstream** read-only with the

### R-UI-192 · The system repositories of the project `upstream` stand apart on its page
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-21 ([Q-UI-891](#q-ui-891--the-system-repositories-of-upstream-stand-apart-below-the-list-closed-and-without-set-up-client)).

- **The list** of the project's page **Repositories** (`/projects/upstream/repositories`, R-UI-020) holds the preset repositories only.
  A system repository (`scanner-trivy`, `clamav`; R-REPO-066) is none of its rows, on any of its pages.
- **Below it**, set apart by room of its own over a hairline, the section **System repositories** (German "System-Repositories",
  [Q-UI-892](#q-ui-892--the-section-is-named-system-repositories)): the one collapsible section of every screen (`<quader-disclosure>`,
  Q-UI-322) with the number of its repositories after its heading as the neutral badge of a count, and one muted sentence under it,
  "Quader writes these repositories itself. Its scanners read them, and an administrator can offer the ClamAV definitions to your ClamAV
  installations." It is closed at every
  visit; nothing of its state is stored. Opened, it holds a table of the list's columns (Repository, Format, Class and the row's
  actions) with the system repositories the caller reads, by key.
- **No Set up client**, but for `clamav` while ClamAV definition updates is on (R-UI-190). A row's menu offers what the API lets the
  caller do with the repository: **Settings** (to whoever reads the configuration, as every row), **Files** (the management API lists its
  items), for `clamav` **Versions** (its packages, R-UI-194) and, for `scanner-trivy`, **Vulnerabilities** (the report, which the product
  leaves empty: the repository's scanning is off, R-REPO-070). No **Delete**, neither of the repository (R-UI-190) nor of a file of
  `clamav` ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-075), and nothing else a client does.
- **Who sees it.** The section stands only for a caller who reads a system repository. `scanner-trivy` is always Private, `clamav`
  Private while ClamAV definition updates is off; a plain user sees the list alone, and, once the definitions are on at a level the user
  reads, the section with `clamav` as its one row. The rows are read by name once per visit
  ([Q-UI-893](#q-ui-893--the-section-reads-its-rows-by-name-once-per-visit-and-filters-them-in-the-browser)); a read that fails shows
  its error and **Retry** inside the section.
- **The filter** of the list's head (the search and the drawer's format, class and state) covers both tables
  ([Q-UI-894](#q-ui-894--the-filter-covers-both-tables-and-opens-the-section-where-it-matches-one-of-its-rows)): the heading counts
  the section's matches; a filter that matches one of its rows opens it, one that matches none closes it, at 0; without a filter it is
  closed. The reader's own toggle holds until the filters change.
- **The project's description** under the title is the UI's localized sentence
  ([Q-UI-895](#q-ui-895--the-built-in-projects-description-is-a-localized-text-of-the-ui)).
- **Nowhere a client action.** No screen offers **Set up client** for a system repository, and its content page offers no upload, no
  new folder and no sentence about what clients fetch or publish
  ([Q-UI-896](#q-ui-896--no-screen-offers-a-client-action-for-a-system-repository-one-function-decides-the-link)).

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, `system-repositories.spec.ts`, about 0.4 s, and the R-UI-192 cases of `repository-content.spec.ts` and
`core/upstream-project.spec.ts`; rendered under rule 11, `repositories-upstream` as the administrator closed, opened and searched, and
`repositories-upstream-plain`):

- The page of `upstream` lists `debian`, `docker-hub` and `npmjs` with **Set up client** each and no system repository; below it
  **System repositories 2**, closed, with the sentence; opened, `clamav` and `scanner-trivy` with the same columns, no **Set up
  client**; the row menu of `scanner-trivy` is **Settings**, **Files**, **Vulnerabilities**, of `clamav` **Settings**, **Files**,
  **Versions**; with ClamAV definition updates on, the row of `clamav` has **Set up client**.
- `?q=TRIVY` shows "No repository matches." above and the section open with **1**; `?format=oci` opens it with `scanner-trivy`;
  `?q=docker` leaves it closed with **0**; the rows are asked for once, by name.
- A caller who reads no system repository gets no section; `setupCommands` of `upstream/scanner-trivy` is null; the page of
  `upstream/scanner-trivy` has no **Set up client** and says "This repository has cached no images yet.", that of
