### R-UI-194 · The ClamAV definitions: databases, versions and what each holds
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's words of 2026-11-21: "wir ziehen alle verfügbaren Metadaten aus dem ClamAV-Definitionen"
([formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-003, R-CLAMAV-007;
[Q-UI-904](#q-ui-904--the-definitions-show-as-the-repositorys-packages-the-version-in-use-first)).

- **Where.** The repository's page of `upstream/clamav` (`/projects/upstream/repositories/clamav`, where every repository lists its packages,
  R-UI-052; R-UI-111's screens for a database and a version), opened
  from **Versions** of R-UI-188 and R-UI-192, for whoever reads the repository: an auditor and an administrator always, every reader of its
  level while ClamAV definition updates is on.
- **The list**: three rows, `bytecode`, `daily`, `main`, each with the version in use, its build time and its age ("under a day", "1 day",
  "8 days"); a `daily` built more than 7 days ago carries the `warn` badge **Outdated** with "ClamAV warns about a database older than 7
  days." in its tooltip and as the row's note, and `main` and `bytecode`, which ClamAV rebuilds rarely, show their age without a badge
  and without the sentence ([Q-UI-912](#q-ui-912--only-daily-is-outdated-by-its-age-as-clamav-warns-only-about-daily)); the age and
  its badge are one line that never breaks ([Q-UI-1064](#q-ui-1064--an-age-and-its-badge-are-one-value-that-never-breaks)). Above
  the list one muted line names the set in use (`main-63.daily-28190.bytecode-339`) and, where it differs, the set before it. The rows are
  read with the versions' state (`include=state`) and the details of the one version in use of each database
  ([Q-UI-910](#q-ui-910--the-databases-and-their-versions-read-the-state-from-the-version-list-and-the-build-time-from-the-version-in-use)).
- **A database's page**: its versions newest first, the version in use first with the badge **In use** (`ok`), then **Previous**,
  **Superseded** and, muted, **Files removed** for the history (R-MAL-034); per version the build time and age, the signatures, the
  functionality level with "ClamAV 0.103 or later" *(example)*, the builder, and **Verification** ("ClamAV's signature verified", "Not
  verified: from the repository ops/clamav-db", "Unsigned container") with the header's MD5 and the computed one in a closed fold.
- **A version's Files tab**: the container and its detached signature with size, SHA-256 and **Download** (a reader downloads a stored
  container through `/files/` while the switch is on; an auditor through the content route), no **Delete**; the **Detached signature** fact
  (present, its number of signatures, "Quader passes it on; ClamAV checks it"); and **Members**: a table of the container's member files
  (name, size, lines, SHA-256 in a closed fold), sorted by name, with the sentence "The signature count of the header is the total; lines
  of a member are not always signatures." A version whose members were not read says so.
- **No install panel** while the switch is off (the sentence of R-UI-193 says why); while it is on, the panel shows, instead of a command per
  version, the sentence "A ClamAV installation always takes the version in use: point freshclam at Quader once, and it updates by itself."
  and **Set up client**, which leads to the client setup of R-CLAMAV-006
  ([Q-UI-911](#q-ui-911--the-install-panel-of-a-definitions-version-leads-to-the-client-setup)). A database's page shows its versions'
  state as the badge after the version, the version in use first while the table keeps its default order; the build time and the other
  facts of a version are on the version's page.
- The texts of a header (the builder, the build time's text) are shown as text, never as markup.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, the package screens' specs with a fixture of the three databases, about 1 s; rendered under rule 11, light and
dark, wide and narrow, with a daily in use, a previous one, a history row, a main 9 days old, a bytecode 8 days old, and the list once
more with a daily 8 days old): the list's rows, the **Outdated** badge on a daily past 7 days and not at 7 days or less, never on main or
bytecode; the page's badges in order; the members table and the sentence; no **Delete** on a file.

### R-UI-193 · A system repository is set apart wherever it is shown, and nothing offers what it refuses
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's word of 2026-11-21 to what the builder of R-UI-192 had reported and left: "Vom Builder gemeldet, nicht geändert: direkt
nacharbeiten. Das ist alles wichtig und muss umgesetzt werden." A system repository of the project `upstream` (`scanner-trivy`,
`clamav`; R-REPO-066) answers every client's request, every download by path and every deploy with 404, for every caller
(R-REPO-070, R-REPO-075); the management API reads it. The UI knows the two by their qualified names (`isSystemRepository`,
`isSystemRepositoryName` of `upstream-project.ts`, Q-UI-893).

- **No address, download or command** ([Q-UI-898](#q-ui-898--nothing-offers-what-a-system-repository-refuses-no-address-no-download-no-command)):
  the admin area's row has no copy button and its menu no **Copy client address**; its content page's tab **Details** has no address for
  downloads by path; a file's row in its folders has no copy button (and the folder's table no column for it); the page of one of its
  files has no **Download**, no download address and no **Download with curl** (the item's own request with curl stays, which the
  management API answers); no row of one of its images or tags has the button **Pull** (Q-UI-1066); a package's install panel
  never offers it, and a version's **Files** tab offers no **Download** for a file it holds.
- **Why, once** ([Q-UI-899](#q-ui-899--where-a-download-or-a-command-is-left-out-one-sentence-names-the-work-that-reads-it)): where the
  download address of a file stood, and in the install panel of a version that only system repositories hold, one muted sentence:
  "Only Quader's malware scan reads this file while ClamAV definition updates is off; clients cannot download it." (`clamav`), "Only
  Quader's image scanning reads this
  version; clients cannot install it." (`scanner-trivy`), and the other two of the same form.
- **One name** ([Q-UI-900](#q-ui-900--the-admin-page-of-the-upstream-registries-names-the-same-two-system-repositories)): the admin
  area's page **Upstream registries** heads its second table **System repositories**, as the project's page heads its section, in
  German "System-Repositories".
- **Not offered where a repository is picked to work with** ([Q-UI-901](#q-ui-901--a-system-repository-is-not-offered-where-a-repository-is-picked-to-work-with)):
  the guides' list of a format, the repository select of the exposure rule editor, the repository filters of the security dashboard
  (the findings and the view **Malware**), and the repository suggestions of **Explain for a repository**. A filter whose address names
  one keeps it as an option, so that the reader can take it off.
- **Still found, and marked** ([Q-UI-902](#q-ui-902--where-a-system-repository-is-listed-among-others-it-carries-the-badge-system)): the
  list of every project's repositories (`/repositories`), the top bar's suggestions (also its frequently visited repositories) and the tab **Repositories** of
  the search's results show them with the neutral badge **System** after the key, part of a suggestion's spoken name ("scanner-trivy ·
  upstream, System"). The project's own section has its heading and no badge in its rows. Where a row's class cell says **System**
  (a repository of a system-only format, `upstream/clamav`), that cell is its mark and the key carries no second badge (Q-UI-1203).
- **While ClamAV definition updates is on** ([Q-UI-908](#q-ui-908--upstreamclamav-answers-its-clients-while-its-switch-is-on-and-every-screen-treats-it-so)):
  `upstream/clamav` answers its clients (R-REPO-075), and every screen treats it as a repository the reader reads: its row and its page offer
  **Set up client**, its page and its files their addresses and **Download**, the install panel the sentence of R-UI-194, and its setup page
  the client setup of R-CLAMAV-006. What stays: the badge **System**, its section of the project's page, no upload, no new folder and no
  **Delete** of a file (Q-REPO-416). The UI asks the switch of `upstream/clamav` only (`SystemClients`): a caller with
  `repositories:read-config` from the admin area's item, anyone else by reading the repository at all, which is private and fixed while
  the switch is off. `scanner-trivy` answers no client in any state.
- **Left as they are**: **Recently opened** in the side bar lists a system repository like any other repository the reader opened (a
  visit is a visit); the row menus and the content page keep **Files**, **Settings** and, for `scanner-trivy`, **Vulnerabilities**
  (R-UI-192); a project's package list lists what a system repository holds.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, about 1 s together: the R-UI-193 cases of `core/upstream-project.spec.ts`, `system-repositories.spec.ts`,
`repository-content.spec.ts`, `version-command.spec.ts`, `package-version.spec.ts`, `guides.spec.ts`, `endpoints.spec.ts`,
`security-dashboard.spec.ts`, `malware-finds.spec.ts`, `usage.spec.ts`, `search-field.spec.ts`, `search-results.spec.ts`, and the
Q-UI-900 case of `upstream-registries.spec.ts`; rendered under rule 11: `all-repositories-upstream`, `files-system`, `admin-upstream`,
`search-system`, `search-field-system`):

- The admin list of `upstream` shows `scanner-trivy` and `clamav` with **System**, no copy button, and the menu of
  `scanner-trivy` **Settings**, **Files**, **Vulnerabilities**; `npmjs` keeps its copy button and **Copy client address**.
- The page of `upstream/clamav/main/63/main.cvd` while ClamAV definition updates is off has no **Delete** (Q-REPO-416) and no **Download**,
  no address field, the sentence, and in
  **Details** one curl command, the item's; its folder's table has the columns Name, Size and Last change.
- With ClamAV definition updates on (Q-UI-908), the row of `clamav` in the project's section has **Set up client**, its setup page is the
  client setup of R-CLAMAV-006, and a stored container of one of its versions has **Download**; `scanner-trivy` still has none of them.
- The opened row of an image of `scanner-trivy` has its tags and no command, and the client setup is never asked; its **Details** has no
  address field.
- A version that only `upstream/scanner-trivy` holds: the install panel says the sentence and asks for no snippet, **Files** has no
  **Download**; one held by `upstream/scanner-trivy` and `web/npm-local` installs through `web/npm-local` without a picker.
- The guides of npm list `upstream/npmjs` and not `scanner-trivy`, each row with **Set up client**; the rule editor offers
  `upstream/docker-hub` and not `upstream/scanner-trivy`; the dashboard's drawer offers it only with `?repository=upstream/scanner-trivy`;
  the view **Malware** offers `web/files-internal` alone; **Explain for a repository** suggests `web/npm-remote` alone.
- The suggestion of `upstream/scanner-trivy` is heard "scanner-trivy · upstream, System" and `web/scanner-trivy` without it; the results
  mark `scanner-trivy` and not `npmjs`; the admin page's second heading is **System repositories**.

### R-UI-195 · The registries of this installation in the admin area
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-20 ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-076): an administrator keeps the
installation's own registries, which the form of a new remote repository offers as buttons in every project (R-UI-082).

- **Where.** On the page **Upstream registries** (R-UI-187), below the table of the public registries and above **System
  repositories**, the section **Registries of this installation** (`<h2>`) with the sentence "Your organization's own registries. The
  form of a new remote repository offers them as buttons in every project, after the well-known registries. A preset holds no
  credential: each project enters its own." The page reads `getRegistryPresets` beside `listUpstreamRepositories`; the header's count
  and the filter of the page stay the public registries'
  ([Q-UI-906](#q-ui-906--the-registries-of-this-installation-are-kept-in-a-section-of-the-page-upstream-registries)).
- **The table**: rows grouped by format in catalog order, each group headed by the format's icon and display name as in the table
  above. Columns: **Registry** (the display name, and the URL muted under it as a name), **Further hosts** (each pattern as a name,
  followed by the muted words "receives the credential" where it does; the en dash for none) and, for a writer, the row's menu
  ("Actions for Harbor") with **Edit** and **Remove** (R-UI-163).
- **Add registry** (`btn btn-default`) under the sentence, for a holder of `repositories:write-config`.
- **Empty.** "No registry of this installation yet." and, for a writer, "Add one to offer it as a button in every project."
- **The dialog** of **Add registry** ("Add a registry") and of **Edit** ("Edit Harbor"): **Format** (a select of the formats with the
  remote class by display name; the first on Add), **Name** (as wide as a name), **Upstream URL** (full width) and **Further hosts** (the
  editor of R-UI-082: a row per pattern with **Receives the credential**, **Remove**, **Add host**) with the hint "Name the registry's
  token service here and let it receive the credential, so that the credential a project enters reaches it." No credential field.
  **Save** sends the whole list with the entry added or replaced, with `If-Match` (`setRegistryPresets`, R-API-084). A field error of the
  entry (`/presets/<n>/…`) stands at its field in the dialog, which stays open; a `412` shows the conflict of R-UI-042 and reads the
  list again; any other refusal stands in the dialog.
- **Remove** asks "Remove Harbor? Remote repositories created from it keep their address and hosts." with **Remove**, then sends the
  list without it.
- After a save the section shows the list the server answered and a `role="status"` line "Harbor is saved." or "Harbor is removed."

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, `registry-presets.spec.ts`, about 1 s; rendered under rule 11 of promt.md, light and dark, wide and narrow,
with presets of two formats and the empty state):

- With Harbor (OCI) and Verdaccio (npm) stored, the section shows the groups npm and OCI (Docker) with one row each; an auditor sees no
  **Add registry** and no row menu.
- Adding a registry sends `PUT /api/v1/settings/registry-presets` with `If-Match` and the list with the new entry last; a `422` at
  `/presets/2/url` shows its message under **Upstream URL** of the dialog.
- **Remove** of Harbor asks first and sends the list without it.

### R-UI-196 · The object-store connections on the tab Storage of System status
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision 9 of 2026-11-22: the admin area shows each connection with its state, fill and backlog and does not change it
([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-050 to R-STOR-061). *Built* (package F of the several connections):
[storage-page.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/storage/storage-page.ts), its template and
[storage-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/storage/storage-model.ts), with the decisions Q-UI-933 and Q-UI-935.

- **Where** ([Q-UI-930](#q-ui-930--the-connections-are-a-fourth-tab-storage-of-system-status)): a fourth tab **Storage**
  (`/admin/system/storage`) of the page **System status** (R-UI-164), for holders of `settings:read`; the header's refresh controls act
  on it as on the others. It reads `listStorageConnections` (R-STOR-061) and, for its last section, `GET /api/v1/storage/damaged-blobs`.
- **The sentence under the tab strip**: "Where Quader keeps your artifacts. Connections are set in the deployment's configuration
  (`config.storage.connections`); this page only shows them." with the link **How to add or remove a connection** to the operator
  manual's page.
- **The table**, one row per connection in its order ([Q-UI-931](#q-ui-931--a-connection-is-one-row-with-its-state-in-words-and-two-figures)):
  - **Connection**: the `id` as a name, and muted under it the endpoint's host and `bucket/prefix`;
  - **State** as a badge in words: **Active** (no colour), **Filling** (an hourglass, neutral) with "*n* % of the blobs", **Draining**
    (neutral) with the copies left, **Drained**, **Detached** (warning) with "*n* blobs only here" and, while its circuit is open on a
    replica, **Unreachable** (error) with "on *m* of *n* replicas", above the state; a connection configured on only some replicas shows
    "Configured on *m* of *n* replicas" (information, a line with its icon). What a drained or a detached connection asks for ("can be
    removed from the configuration", "not in the configuration of any replica") stands once, in the line over the table that names
    what needs an act ([Q-UI-933](#q-ui-933--what-a-connection-asks-for-stands-once-over-the-table-and-a-states-words-beside-its-badge));
    a share is rounded down, so a connection that lacks a blob never shows 100 %;
  - **Fill**: present copies of all blobs as a percentage and the bytes ("100 %, 1.7 TiB"), from the latest storage summary, whose age
    a line under the table gives;
  - **Backlog**: the queue ("12 blobs, oldest 4 minutes"), or the en dash when empty; "behind for over an hour" in the warning colour when
    the alert of R-STOR-056 would fire;
  - **Damaged copies**: missing and corrupt, the en dash for none;
  - **Scrub**: "*n* % read" with "within 30 days" (the connection's period) as the cell's muted second line, and "behind" in the
    warning colour when copies are overdue;
  - **Encrypted**: **No** (stage 1 knows no other value).
- **Details on demand.** A row's name opens a fold below it with the connection's non-secret settings as read (the credential source,
  `force_path_style`, the checksum modes, `batch_delete`, `storage_class`, `sse_mode`, `scrub_period`, `scrub_bytes_per_second`), its
  capabilities found by the start check ("Payload checksums enforced", "Copies keep and replace metadata", "Server-side copy from
  *other*"), `filledAt`, `lastFullPassAt`, and nothing that could be changed here.
- **Blobs no connection holds whole**: below the table, a closed section of details with their number, the first 20 of `scope=blobs`
  with digest (shortened, the full one in the title), state, the copies' states per connection and the first referencing item as a link
  to it; "No damaged blob." when the list is empty; with more, "The list shows the first 20." and the command
  `quader admin storage verify` to see them all (the page of the list carries no count of the rest); the line over the table names their
  number, so the plain view says that they need an act
  ([Q-UI-935](#q-ui-935--the-damaged-blobs-and-the-storages-tasks-are-closed-sections-and-the-line-over-the-table-names-what-needs-an-act)).
  A holder of `settings:write` sees **Check again** per row (`POST …/damaged-blobs/{sha256}/recheck`), which shows the copies' states it
  answered.
- **The last runs of the storage's tasks**: a second closed section with `storage-reconcile`, `scrub`, `orphan-sweep` and
  `storage-summary`, each with its last run and its next, linked to its jobs (Q-UI-935).
- **One connection** shows one row; the columns that only matter with several (Backlog, the fold's server-side copies) show the en dash.
- **Narrow screens**: below 48 rem the row becomes a card with the same labels; nothing scrolls sideways.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, `storage-connections.spec.ts`, about 1 s; rendered under rule 11 of promt.md, light and dark, wide and
narrow, with one connection, with two of which one is filling and one unreachable on one replica, and with a detached one):

- Two connections, `default` active and `secondary` filling at 50 %, render two rows in order with **Active** and **Filling** "50 % of
  the blobs"; a queue of 12 blobs whose oldest is 4 minutes shows "12 blobs, oldest 4 minutes".
- A connection with `replicas.circuitOpen: 1` of 3 shows **Unreachable** "on 1 of 3 replicas"; a detached one shows the warning with its
  count.
- A caller without `settings:read` does not see the tab (R-UI-164's rule); the page offers no control that changes a connection.

### R-UI-197 · The object store on the dashboard, one line per connection
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

*Built* (package F): [dashboard.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/dashboard.ts) and its template, with the decision Q-UI-934.
