### R-UI-210 · The Downloads button in the top bar
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-24, 08:20 (task T-26; his picture of a desktop application's download panel, taken as the pattern only): a button with
a download icon at the top right opens the downloads. What a download from an upstream is, and the API behind the button, are
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-049 to R-OPS-052.

*Built* (T-26 package B): [upstream-downloads-button.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/upstream-downloads-button.ts) in
[app.html](../../web/src/app/app.html), the client [upstream-downloads-api.ts](../../web/src/app/api/upstream-downloads-api.ts), the window's
visibility [page-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/core/page-visibility.ts).

- **Who sees it** ([Q-OPS-423](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-423--the-holders-of-contentmetadata-read-see-the-downloads-of-every-repository-and-nobody-else)):
  a signed-in caller who holds `content:metadata-read` (`session.has(...)`), the administrator and the auditor, in the main area and in
  the admin area alike. Nobody else sees the button, nothing of it is rendered for them, and nothing is asked for them.
- **Where** ([Q-UI-1070](#q-ui-1070--the-downloads-button-stands-between-documentation-and-the-theme-and-counts-what-runs)): in the
  top bar's actions, between **Documentation** and the theme button; an icon button (`btn btn-icon topbar-icon`), the icon `download`.
- **The indicator.** While downloads run, a small badge on the icon's upper end corner carries their number (`running`; "99+" above
  99): downloads, each the unit a person asked for (an image with all its files, a version's package, a queue row's run;
  [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-049), never their files, in the information colour of the badges (`--quader-badge-info-bg`, `-fg`), readable in both schemes. No motion. With nothing
  running, there is no badge.
- **Its name.** "Downloads" when nothing runs, "Downloads, 3 running" while some run (German "Downloads" and "Downloads, 3 laufen"), as
  its accessible name and its title; `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` while the panel is open, `aria-controls` the panel's id.
  The badge is hidden from assistive technology: the name carries the count.
- **The refresh while the panel is closed:** `GET /api/v1/system/upstream-downloads/summary` at once, then every 10 s, only while the
  window is visible (`document.visibilityState`), and at once when it becomes visible again or the panel closes. While the panel is open,
  its list sets the count. A `403` hides the button until another principal signs in; any other failure keeps the last count and the
  next tick reads again. No announcement to assistive technology
  ([Q-UI-1073](#q-ui-1073--the-panel-refreshes-by-polling-while-it-is-seen-and-announces-nothing)).
- **Narrow screens:** the button keeps its place; the top bar's labels already drop below 48 rem, and this button has none.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, [upstream-downloads-button.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/upstream-downloads-button.spec.ts),
about 0.1 s): a session without `content:metadata-read` renders no button and asks nothing; with it, a count of 0 shows no badge and the
name "Downloads"; 3 shows "3" and "Downloads, 3 running"; 140 shows "99+"; the count is read every 10 s while the window is seen, not
while it is hidden, and at once when it is seen again; a failed read keeps the count, a `403` hides the button.

### R-UI-211 · The Downloads panel: what runs
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

*Built* (T-26 package B): [upstream-downloads-panel.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/upstream-downloads-panel.ts) with its
template, its words in [download-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/download-words.ts), the drawer's input `width`
([drawer.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/drawer.ts)), the times in [duration-text.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/duration-text.ts).

- **The panel** ([Q-UI-1071](#q-ui-1071--the-downloads-open-in-the-drawer-from-the-right)): the button opens Quader's drawer from the
  right (Q-UI-420), `min(30rem, 100vw)` wide, titled **Downloads**, with its close button named **Close downloads**; under the title one
  muted sentence: "What Quader is loading from the upstreams of remote repositories, and the last 100 finished downloads." Escape, the
  close button and a click beside it close it; the focus returns to the button. A link inside it (a repository, **Show in queue**,
  **About this list**) closes it as it leads away.
- **The filter.** A field **Filter downloads** (as wide as a name, R-UI-085) filters both sections at once, in the browser, by name,
  version, the first file's path and repository `project/key` (case-insensitive, part of the text). A section's heading says "Running (1 of 145)" while
  the filter is set, and a section with rows of which none matches says "No download matches the filter."
- **The section Waiting for an upstream (n)**, first while the list's `waiting` holds a queue
  ([Q-UI-1101](#q-ui-1101--the-top-bars-panel-says-the-queues-a-limit-holds-above-running), [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md)
  R-CUR-011): one row per repository whose download queue an upstream's rate limit holds, the warning's hourglass before one sentence,
  "206 downloads of upstream/docker-hub wait: Docker Hub limits requests; Quader asks again at 06:47." ("… limits requests until 08:12."
  where the upstream named the time; "1 download of … waits: …"), and under it the format's name and **Show in queue** to the
  repository's tab Downloads. The filter narrows it by the repository and the upstream's name. German: "Warten auf einen Upstream",
  "206 Downloads von upstream/docker-hub warten: Docker Hub begrenzt die Anfragen; Quader fragt um 06:47 erneut an.".
- **The section Running (n)** (`runningCount`), first without a held queue. One row per running download, the oldest first, as the API orders them; the
  rows keep their place across refreshes (tracked by `id`). A download is the unit a person asked for: an image with its manifests,
  configs, layers and attestations, a version's package, a queue row's run (R-OPS-049); its files are never listed, counted on the row
  or shown one by one ([Q-UI-1380](#q-ui-1380--a-row-is-one-download-and-never-lists-its-files-the-file-that-failed-stands-in-the-badges-title)):
  - Line 1: the format's icon (`<quader-format-icon>`) on the middle of the name's first line (R-UI-175), the **name** (wrapping inside
    itself, R-UI-145) and the version muted beside it. A version that is an image's digest (an image pulled by its digest) is cut to its
    algorithm and 12 hex digits (`sha256:1a2b3c4d5e6f`); an image whose tag is not known yet shows its name alone; a download of no
    package shows its first file as the name (the last path segment, a digest cut likewise). The name with the whole version is the
    line's title (the first file's path for a download of no package).
  - Line 2, with a total: one progress bar across the row for the whole download (`<progress>` named "Progress of <name> <version>",
    value and max in bytes): a queue row's run has the sizes it named, a download of one file its length. Without a total (a client's
    pull of an image, R-OPS-049): no bar.
  - Line 3, muted and small: "128.4 MiB of 286.9 MiB · 12.3 MiB/s · 42 s" (`formatSize`; the speed in the same unit per second; the
    time as `elapsedText`: "< 1 s", "42 s", "1 min 12 s", "1 h 5 min"). Without a total: "128.4 MiB · 12.3 MiB/s · 42 s". Without a speed
    yet (the first second): the en dash in its place.
  - Line 4, muted and small: the format's name (R-UI-006), the repository `project/key` as a link to the repository's page, and the
    origin in words ([Q-UI-1072](#q-ui-1072--a-row-says-what-what-it-took-and-who-caused-it-a-queued-one-links-the-queue)):
    - **Client · sam**, or **Client** when `by` is null;
    - for the queue: the person (**priya**, else **A person**), **Bulk**, **Sync** (a run of a download kept in sync, R-CUR-027),
      **Probe**, **Request**, **Allow** (the queue's words, R-CUR-018);
    - **Mirror pass**;
    - **Vulnerability database**.

    A queued row ends with the link **Show in queue** to the repository's tab Downloads, filtered by the name
    (`…/repositories/{key}/downloads?name=<name>`; the tab reads `name` from its address, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md)
    R-CUR-018).
  - More than the API listed: one line under the rows, "and 140 more running", with no link.
- **Empty:** "No download from an upstream is running." Before the first answer: "Loading the downloads."
- **Refresh while open:** the whole list at once, then every `pollSeconds` (2 s) while the panel is open and the window visible; closing
  the panel stops it, and is how a reader stops the moving content (WCAG 2.2.2). A failed refresh shows one line, "The list could not be
  refreshed; Quader tries again.", over the sections and keeps the last rows; a `403` closes the panel and hides the button.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, [upstream-downloads-panel.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/upstream-downloads-panel.spec.ts),
about 0.5 s with R-UI-212's cases): a running download with a total shows the bar and "of"; one without a total shows no bar and its
bytes; an image pulled by its digest shows `sha256:` and 12 digits, its whole digest in the title, and no file of it; each origin shows its words; a queued row links its queue with `?name=`;
the filter narrows both sections and says "1 of 5"; `runningCount` above the listed rows shows "and n more running"; the poll is 2 s while
open, keeps the rows when it fails, and stops when the panel closes. The tab Downloads' spec: `?name=` filters the queue and **Show every
download** clears it.

### R-UI-212 · The Downloads panel: what finished, and Hide all
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

*Built* (T-26 package B): the same files as R-UI-211; the manual's section
[Downloads from upstreams](../manual/admin/operations.md#downloads-from-upstreams).

- **The section Finished (n)**, under Running, newest first, at most 100. Each row:
  - Line 1: as a running row; with an outcome other than `completed`, a badge after the name: **Failed** (error, with its icon) with
    the failure's class in the queue's words (R-CUR-011; "Failed: Network") and as its title the failure's code and the file it failed
    at ("connection_reset at the file library/ubuntu/_blobs/sha256:…"; the code alone where the failure names no file), **Cancelled**
    (neutral), **Interrupted** (warning, with its icon; its title says "A replica stopped while this download ran.").
  - Line 2, muted and small: "286.9 MiB · 1 min 12 s · 4.0 MiB/s": the size, the duration and the average. A duration below one second
    reads "< 1 s", and the average is left out then.
  - Line 3, muted and small: the format's name, the repository link, the origin as in R-UI-211, and the end as
    `<quader-time-ago absolute="title">` ("4 minutes ago", R-UI-103). A queued row links its queue as in R-UI-211.
- **Hide all** ([Q-UI-1072](#q-ui-1072--a-row-says-what-what-it-took-and-who-caused-it-a-queued-one-links-the-queue)):
  - A small quiet button **Hide all** in the section's heading hides, on this device only, the finished downloads listed at that moment:
    it keeps the newest `finishedAt` of the list in the browser's local storage (`BrowserStorage`, key
    `quader.upstream-downloads.hidden-before`).
  - The section then shows the downloads that end later, and one line: "Hidden on this device: 100. **Show again**". **Show again**
    removes the mark.
  - Where local storage cannot be written, the button is not shown. Nothing is removed on the server, and nothing is audited.
- **Empty:** "No download has finished yet." When everything is hidden: the line above only.
- **The foot of the panel:** a link **About this list** to the manual's page (`/help/admin/operations#downloads-from-upstreams`).
- **Words** (German build, formal): Laufend, Abgeschlossen, Downloads filtern, Alle ausblenden, "Auf diesem Gerät ausgeblendet: 100.",
  Wieder anzeigen, In der Warteschlange ansehen, Fehlgeschlagen, Abgebrochen, Unterbrochen, Mirror-Durchlauf, Schwachstellendatenbank,
  Über diese Liste, "connection_reset bei der Datei …", "Ein Replikat hat angehalten, während dieser Download lief.", "und 140 weitere laufen", "Kein Download aus einem Upstream läuft.", "Noch kein Download ist abgeschlossen.",
  "Kein Download passt zum Filter.", "Die Liste konnte nicht aktualisiert werden; Quader versucht es erneut.". The queue's existing words
  are reused.
- **Rendered** under rule 11 of promt.md (`topbar-downloads`, `topbar-downloads-admin-area`, `topbar-downloads-panel` in English and
  German, `topbar-downloads-none`; [upstream-downloads.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/upstream-downloads.ts) answers both endpoints in the
  browser): light and dark, 1,440, 1,024 and 390 px; the button with no download, with 3 and with 140; the panel with six running rows
  (an npm tarball with a total, a mirror's Debian package without one, the owner's image downloaded ahead by a person as one row with
  the total its run named, a client's pull of an image without a total, a 120-character npm scope name of a bulk, the scanner database)
  and "and 140 more running", a finished list of 100 with every outcome (the owner's image failed at one of its 23 files, a client's pull
  of an image of 9 files), the filter set, everything hidden, the refresh error, both sections empty.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, in [upstream-downloads-panel.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/upstream-downloads-panel.spec.ts)):
each outcome shows its badge and words, a failure the file it failed at in the badge's title; a duration of 0.4 s reads "< 1 s" without an
average; **Hide all** stores the newest end and
hides those rows, a later download shows, **Show again** brings them back; without storage there is no **Hide all**; the empty states
read as above and the foot links the manual.

### R-UI-213 · No view needs a reload
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-24, 11:05, whole: "Ich hoffe das unsere Frontend bereits automatisch updates fetched und von mir zu keinem Zeitpunkt
erwartet wird dass ich F5 drücke um eine Ansicht zu aktualisieren." Nobody presses F5 to see what the server changed: every view that
shows state the server changes without the viewer's own act reads it again by itself.

*Built*: [live-refresh.ts](../../web/src/app/core/live-refresh.ts) (`live()`, `refreshResource()`), `PagedResource.refresh()` in
[paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts) with `PagedList.resumed()`, the window's visibility
[page-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/core/page-visibility.ts); how a view becomes live is on the developer page
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#live-views-r-ui-213).

- **When a view reads again** ([Q-UI-1075](#q-ui-1075--a-view-is-live-by-one-shared-poll-that-reads-in-place-and-only-while-it-is-seen)):
  every interval the view names while the window is seen (`document.visibilityState`) and the view is shown; at once when the window
  is seen again after it was hidden, or a paused refresh is resumed; never while hidden or paused. The view's own first read stays its
  own; reads never overlap. The intervals:
  - **fast, 3 s** (`LIVE_FAST_MS`) while something on the view runs: a scan that has not answered, a download that waits or runs;
    the existing fast reads keep their own (a job 2 s, the jobs list and a mirror pass 5 s, a Debian suite's build 3 s); those
    keep the rule of the window too: a job's progress (`JobProgress`) and the tab Downloads (R-CUR-018) read nothing while the
    window is hidden and read at once when it is seen again (both read on in a hidden window until 2026-11-25: the tab Downloads
    24 reads a minute with a running queue, a running job 30);
  - **30 s** (`LIVE_SLOW_MS`) for a list that a client's push or pull, a scan, the queue or another person's act changes: a list of
    events or findings others write never waits longer (the audit log, the security dashboard's findings, Q-UI-1216);
  - **60 s** (`LIVE_IDLE_MS`) for a page or a summary that changes in minutes: a version's page, a package's page, the tab Upstream,
    the security dashboards' summary, trend and sources, the ClamAV databases;
  - the pages of System status keep their 15 s with **Pause automatic refresh** (R-UI-164, WCAG 2.2.2), now only while seen.
- **Back-off.** A read that fails doubles the wait before the next (3 s, 6 s, 12 s …; 30 s, 60 s …), up to 5 minutes
  (`LIVE_MAX_BACKOFF_MS`) or the view's own interval where that is longer; a read that answers restores the interval.
- **In place, without flicker.** A read replaces what it read only when its answer is there: a list keeps its rows (tracked by their
  key), a row the person opened stays open, an open menu, the focus and the scroll stay, **Load more** continues after what was read
  again, and a field the person types in is never reset. A failed read keeps what is shown and shows no error; the next read tries
  again. A list the person extended with **Load more** is read again as far as it is shown. An answer that arrives after the view's
  query changed is dropped. A view whose own first read failed shows its notice, which reads it again by itself while the window is
  seen (R-UI-216, [Q-UI-1184](#q-ui-1184--a-failed-read-is-offered-again-and-a-failure-that-may-pass-is-read-again-by-itself)). A version's page keeps the tab it opened on when a finished scan adds the tab Vulnerabilities in front.
- **No announcement storm.** A read again sets no live region; a region that already announces (a job's progress, R-UI-042) keeps its
  own limit, and text that did not change is not written again.
- **After the person's own act** (a download started, an allow or a block, a release, a rescan, a run of a pass), the affected view
  reads at once, as each act already did (the tab Upstream after a write, a version's page after a release, the mirror after **Run a
  pass now**); a live read that runs meanwhile is followed by the act's own.
- **Forms are not live.** A settings page, an editor or a dialog holds what the person types; a change another person saved meanwhile
  meets the conflict dialog on save (412, R-UI-042).
- **A build the window was not loaded from**
  ([Q-UI-1370](#q-ui-1370--a-link-to-a-screen-whose-script-is-gone-loads-its-address-from-the-server-and-a-failed-navigation-is-said)):
  a link to a screen whose script the server no longer holds loads the link's address from the server, so the reader arrives where the
  link led, on the build that is served; a navigation that fails for another reason says so with what was said of it. No click does
  nothing.
- **What is live** (the audit of 2026-11-24). Every other screen shows what only a person changes through the UI (members, roles,
  policies, groups, users, service accounts, CI issuers and mappings, endpoints and their rules, limits, settings, upstream registries,
  the guides, the manual, the search's results), and shows another person's change at the next navigation.

  | Screen | Interval | What changes it |
  |---|---|---|
  | A repository's content: its packages or images; the versions of a row opened in it | 30 s; an open row's versions when its row says it changed | a push, a pull through a remote, a grade |
  | A generic repository's folder | 30 s | an upload, a delete by a client |
  | A version's page: files, malware scan, signatures, vulnerabilities, the tab Signatures | 3 s while a scan or check has not answered, 60 s after | the scanners, the checks |
  | A package's page | 60 s: its summary and grades; its versions when the summary changed | a push, a download, a grade |
  | The tab Upstream: the strip's counts, the list's rows, the requests panel | 60 s; the panel when the counts change | a download, a request, an allow |
  | A package opened in the tab Upstream | 3 s while one of its versions downloads, 60 s after | the queue |
  | The tab Downloads | 5 s while a row waits or runs or a bulk shown expands or waits, 30 s otherwise and while a rate limit holds the queue with nothing running ([Q-UI-1102](#q-ui-1102--the-tab-downloads-is-live-by-the-shared-poll-5-s-while-something-moves-30-s-otherwise)) | the queue, a client's failed fetch |
  | The label "Downloads · 2 failed" of a remote's strip, on every tab but Downloads | 30 s ([Q-UI-1103](#q-ui-1103--the-strips-label-reads-the-queues-counts-itself-on-every-other-tab-every-30-s)) | the queue |
  | The top bar's Downloads | as built (R-UI-210, R-UI-211) | the downloads, the queues an upstream's rate limit holds |
  | The ClamAV databases | 60 s: the list of databases; the versions and the set when it changed | the updater |
  | Vulnerabilities (summary, trend, findings), Advisory sources | 60 s | a scan, a sync |
  | Malware finds | 30 s | a scan |
  | Signature findings, refused downloads | 60 s | a check, a refused download |
  | Packages, Repositories (lists) | 60 s | a push, a size, a disabled repository |
  | Audit log | 30 s, the range moved to now | every act |
  | Mirror status, a Debian repository's indexes | 5 s and 3 s while a pass or a build runs, 30 s after | the schedule, a push |
  | Jobs | 5 s while one runs, 30 s while none does | the job runner |
  | System status, Backups, Storage, the admin dashboard | 15 s, pausable | the replicas |
  | An Ansible repository's import tasks, a version's import log | 30 s | a publish |
  | CI issuances, tokens (profile, administration) | 60 s | an exchange, a token's use |
  | Usage (own, a subject's, the overview's first page), Bastions | 60 s | downloads, a Bastion's state |
  | The banner and the maintenance mode | 30 s, only while seen | an administrator's save |

- **What it costs the server**, per open tab and minute: an idle view one or two requests (a list one; a version's page, a package's
  page and the tab Upstream two, and one more per package opened in the tab Upstream); while something runs, 20 a minute per fast
  view (a version's page with a pending scan reads the version and its report: 40). The top bar adds the banner and the mode (four a
  minute) and, for an administrator, the Downloads summary (six). A hidden tab costs nothing. A list read again costs as many pages as
  it shows ([H-1847](#h-1847--a-live-list-reads-its-rows-again-there-is-no-answer-of-what-changed)). Measured in a browser on
  2026-11-25 ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#what-an-open-tab-asks-of-the-server-measured)): a seen list or package page 6 to 7
  calls a minute with the top bar, a version's page whose scan waits 37 to 41, the administrators' dashboard and System status 27 to
  28 (their six reads every 15 s), every measured screen none while hidden.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, with fake timers in milliseconds): [live-refresh.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/live-refresh.spec.ts),
about 0.7 s: a view reads every interval while seen, not while hidden, at once when seen again; failed reads double the wait up to
the bound and an answer restores it; the interval follows what the view runs (fast, none, slow); no read while not shown or paused,
one at once when shown again; the person's act reads at once and starts the wait anew; a read keeps the rows, the open row, the focus
and the typed text and continues **Load more**; a failed read keeps the rows without an error; a read of a list whose query changed
meanwhile is dropped; a resource read again keeps its value, keeps it on a failure and drops a stale answer. One case per kind of
screen, each about 0.1 s: a version's page reads every 3 s while a file's malware scan has not answered and every minute after, and a
finished scan keeps the open tab ([package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts)); a
repository's images read again in place with a pushed image, an open row and its new tag
([repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts)); an open upstream package
every 3 s while a version downloads ([remote-upstream.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream/remote-upstream.spec.ts));
the ClamAV databases' cheap read first ([clamav-databases.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/clamav-databases.spec.ts));
the audit log's moving range ([audit-log.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.spec.ts)); the jobs in place, at 5 s and
30 s, and paused, and a running job's progress not read while hidden and read at once when seen again
([system-jobs.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-jobs.spec.ts)); the tab Downloads not read while hidden and at once
when seen again ([remote-downloads.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.spec.ts)); the banner
not read while hidden ([banner-store.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/banner-store.spec.ts)).

### R-UI-214 · A screen speaks its own language, never the server's sentence
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

On 2026-11-24 the German dashboard of the vulnerabilities said under its trend "A finding counts under its current severity, …": the
server sent the sentence and the screen showed it as it came. It was the third English server sentence inside a German page that day,
after the hint under the upstream search ([Q-CUR-166](remote-curation.md#q-cur-166--the-hint-under-the-upstream-search-is-a-code-the-screen-says-in-its-language))
and a failed bulk's detail ([Q-CUR-169](remote-curation.md#q-cur-169--a-download-failure-is-said-in-the-screens-language-from-its-code-the-servers-english-sentence-folds-under-it)),
and the audit of that day found thirteen more screens that did the same. A screen says everything in the reader's language; what the
server knows, it sends as a code with its parameters
([Q-UI-1080](#q-ui-1080--a-server-sends-a-code-the-screen-says-it-and-a-raw-text-folds-under-technical-details)).

- **A code, said by the screen.** Where the server's text is one of a closed set of cases (a warning, a note, a reason, a state), the
  API answers its code (an enum of the OpenAPI document) and the parameters the sentence names, and the screen writes the sentence
  with `$localize`, one case per code. An API field may keep an English `detail` beside the code for a reader of the API (as a
  problem's `detail`, R-UI-042); the screen does not show it as its words. A fixed sentence with no case to tell is no field of the
  API at all (the trend's `basis` is gone, R-VULN-021).
- **A raw text, folded.** Where the server's text is a diagnosis that no code covers (an error as a handler or a host returned it, a
  verifier's note, a format's note), or the English sentence beside a code, the screen says what happened in its own sentence, from
  the code where there is one, and shows the server's text only under **Technical details**, with its code where the screen said one
  ([technical-details.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/technical-details.ts), one component for every screen): closed, marked
  `lang="en"` and not translated, for whoever has to report it.
- **What stays as it came.** What a person typed (descriptions, notes, reasons of a release or a block, a banner's message), what an
  upstream wrote (a package's description, an advisory's summary), names and identifiers, and the texts that are English by decision
  and marked `lang="en"`: the manual (R-UI-050), a format's guide (Q-UI-86) and a format's settings schema (Q-UI-79). What a person
  or an upstream wrote is marked `translate="no"` (a package's description in its page's header, an upstream's hit and package, a
  request's note and a decline's reason; since the German pass of 2026-11-25 also a repository's description in its page's header,
  a package's description in a repository's list, the descriptions of a project, a repository and a package among the search's
  hits and in the project list, a download limit profile's description, an advisory's summary among the findings, and a
  package's README), so that the German pass tells it from a server's sentence. The built-in project's description is the UI's own
  and is not marked; a built-in limit profile's name and description are stored and editable, English as the installation first
  writes them ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) H-1861). A problem whose code the screen
  does not know is said from its status; its English `detail` is a fact of the notice, marked `lang="en" translate="no"`, with the
  request ID (R-UI-216).
- **The audit of 2026-11-24** (every binding of a server's text in `web/src/app`, against its source). Each screen exists once for
  every format and class that has it; the preview, the connection test, the mirror and the signatures serve every format through the
  same component:

  | Screen | Server field (source) | Now |
  |---|---|---|
  | Security dashboard, **Trend** | `VulnerabilityTrend.basis` (`report.TrendBasis`) | the field is gone; the screen's sentence (R-VULN-021) |
  | Tab **Upstream**, the preview of a download ahead | `RemoteDownloadPreview.note` (`preview` of `remote_downloads_api.go`, five sentences) | a code of five, said by the screen (`previewNoteText`) |
  | A repository's settings, a save's warnings; **Set visibility**; the upstream registries' toasts | `RepositoryWarning.detail` (`internal/repository`, eleven codes) | `code` is an enum, said by the screen (`repositoryWarningText`) |
  | A remote's **Test connection**; an upstream registry's test | `UpstreamTestResult.error.message` (`internal/proxy/upstream`) | the code (twelve) said by the screen (`upstreamTestErrorText`); the message and the code folded |
  | A CI mapping's save, **Test with claims** | `CiWarning.detail` (`internal/ci/claims`, ten codes) | `code` is an enum with `names`, said by the screen (`ciWarningText`) |
  | **Test with claims**, the result and the mappings looked at | `CiEvaluateResult.failure`/`detail`, `CiTraceEntry.detail` (`internal/ci`) | the failure said by the screen (`ciFailureText`); the detail and the reason folded |
  | A CI issuer's **Keys** and the issuers' list | `CiKeyStatus.lastError` (`FetchError.Error`: class, status, host) | the class and the status said by the screen (`ciKeyErrorText`); the line folded on **Keys** |
  | **Jobs** (System), a job's result | `JobError.detail` (the handler's error, five codes) | the code said by the screen (`jobErrorText`); the detail and the code folded |
  | **Malware scanning**, the signature database's failure | `MalwareDatabaseError.detail` | the title from the code as before; the detail and the code folded |
  | **Advisory sources**, a source's last error | `VulnerabilitySourceState.lastError.detail` | the title from the code, "The last run failed." for an unknown one; the detail and the code folded |
  | **Signatures** (settings), the public root's last failure | `SignatureTrustRoot.lastError` | the screen's sentence; the text folded |
  | A remote's **Mirror** tab, the last error and the last pass | `MirrorErrors.lastCode` (seven codes, now an enum) and `lastMessage`, `MirrorPassSummary.discoveryNote` (a format's note) | the code said by the screen (`mirrorErrorText`); the message with the code, and the note, folded |
  | A version's signatures, a file's signatures | `SignatureEntry.detail` (a verifier's note) | inside the entry's **Technical details** as **Verifier's note** |
  | **System status**, Valkey: the replica's row and the card | `ValkeyView.reason` (the client's free text, which names addresses and replies) | the new `reasonCode` (the nine codes `/readyz?verbose=1` shows) said by the screen (`valkeyReasonText`); the text folded in the replica's row |
  | Tab **Downloads**, a failed row and a failed bulk | `RemoteDownloadFailure.detail` | said from the code by the download queue (Q-CUR-169); the sentence folded by the same component |
  | An Ansible Galaxy import's log | `AnsibleImportTask.messages[].message` | a log as the Galaxy import API answers it to `ansible-galaxy`, kept and marked English (`lang="en"`) |

- **Held.** A lint rule refuses a template that interpolates a member the API gives to its English sentences (`detail`, `basis`,
  `message`, `lastMessage`, `lastError`, `discoveryNote`, …), with a short list of reasoned exceptions
  ([server-text-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/server-text-rule.mjs)); the German render pass reports a shown text of six words or more
  with three English function words in a German page, outside code and outside a text marked `lang="en"` or `translate="no"`
  (`english` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts)).

Acceptance criteria: `TestR_UI_214_EveryCodeASentenceStandsForIsInTheAPIsEnum` (unit, `internal/api/v1`, microseconds): every
repository warning, CI warning, preview note, mirror error code and Valkey reason code the server sends is a value of the API's enum.
"R-UI-214 every code the server sends has a sentence of the screen, and a German one in the German build" and "R-UI-214 technical
details are folded, English, not translated, and show the text as it came with its code"
([server-texts.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/server-texts.spec.ts), about 0.1 s): 87 codes of nine kinds each give a sentence,
none the API's, and a German one in the German build. The lint rule's two cases in `lint-rules.test.mjs` and the `english` check's
two fixtures in `layout-checks.spec.ts` (each under a second). The integration areas `npm` and `ansibleremote` (a preview's code),
`ci` (a dry run's warning names its scope items).

### R-UI-215 · One scrollbar per page
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-25, 06:50, on the tab Images of a remote OCI repository with an opened image of about a hundred tags, whole: "Ich
sehe auf dieser Seite 3 scrollbars neben einander. Das sieht echt scheiße aus und sollte vermieden werden. Optimal wäre wenn es wirklich
nur eine Scrollbar pro Seite gibt, die äußerste. Alles andere ist zu vermeiden. Bei kleinen Tabellen, ist evtl mal eine zweite
Scrollbar in Ordnung, aber nicht bei einer Tabelle die eh schon allein den gesamten Bildschirm füllt." The three were the opened image's
list, the list's own region and the page; the list's head stood above the opened image's rows, whose columns are others. The cause was
one rule for every list: the data table scrolled by itself under a height cap so that its head stayed in view (Q-UI-68, Q-UI-427),
which [Q-UI-1110](#q-ui-1110--the-page-is-the-one-thing-that-scrolls-a-lists-head-scrolls-with-it) reverses.

- **A page has one scrollbar, its own.** The content panel (`main`) scrolls, the window does not, and nothing inside the page scrolls
  upwards and downwards by itself. A list of any length grows the page, and its head scrolls with it; the data table is no tab stop
  and no region of its own, named by its caption.
- **An opened row shows a bounded part of its list** and links to the whole: an item of a repository's content its ten newest versions
  under a head of their own and **All N tags** or **All N versions** to the package's page (R-UI-052,
  [Q-UI-1111](#q-ui-1111--an-opened-item-shows-its-ten-newest-versions-and-links-all-of-them)). An upstream package opened in a row of
  the tab Upstream grows the page with **Load more**: an upstream version has no page of its own.
- **What keeps a scroll of its own**, each one by the development agent's choice that the owner may refuse
  ([Q-UI-1110](#q-ui-1110--the-page-is-the-one-thing-that-scrolls-a-lists-head-scrolls-with-it),
  [Q-UI-1112](#q-ui-1112--a-navigation-column-sticks-beside-the-page-with-a-scroll-of-its-own-any-other-side-column-sticks-only-while-it-fits)):
  - a boxed list of at most 24 rem with a frame above and below, inside no other box that scrolls: the trend's table of the
    vulnerabilities (18 rem) and the usage history's table (24 rem), which stand in for charts at a fixed height, and the list box of a
    virtual repository's members (8 to 20 rem), whose active option moves inside it;
  - a navigation column that sticks beside the page, at most as high as the panel's view: the manual's contents (R-UI-050) and the
    tree of a collection's documentation (R-UI-060), in their two-column forms;
  - an overlay (a dialog's body, a drawer's body, a menu, a field's suggestions), one scroll per overlay: a box inside it is as tall as
    its content (the packages drawer's repositories, an issued token's grants and claims);
  - a field that takes typed text.
- **A side column that is no navigation** (a policy's preview, R-UI-027; an opened audit event, R-UI-037) sticks beside the page only
  while it fits in the panel's view, and never scrolls by itself; taller, it scrolls with the page. Closing an audit event gives the focus
  back to the row it was opened from.
- **A box shows its content whole or folds it**: a folded command cuts after its third line behind its expander and never scrolls
  (R-UI-009); the CI snippet of a mapping is as tall as its lines. A box may scroll sideways where its lines are kept as they are
  copied (a code block, a document's table); that is R-UI-173's.
- **Held** by the render check `inner-scroll` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts)
  ([Q-UI-1113](#q-ui-1113--the-render-check-inner-scroll-measures-every-box-that-scrolls-by-itself-in-the-windows-first-height)),
  measured in the window's first height, before the render grows it.

Acceptance criteria: the render run names no `inner-scroll` finding. `make ui-layout-test`, the describe "one scrollbar per page
(R-UI-215)" of [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts), six fixtures in three engines, each under a second:
the owner's picture is found twice (the list's region and the opened image's region inside it); the same lists with the app's
stylesheet pass; a framed box of 18 rem passes and is found at 30 rem, without its frame and inside another box that scrolls; a
navigation column that sticks passes and a side column that is no navigation is found; an overlay's one scroll passes and a block that
scrolls inside it is found; a text area passes. Unit (Vitest, about 0.1 s each): an opened image lists its ten newest tags under its own
head and links all thirteen, and an item of ten or fewer has no link
([repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts)); the data table is no tab
stop and no region ([data-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.spec.ts)); a side column sticks only while it fits
([sticky-when-fits.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/sticky-when-fits.spec.ts)); closing an audit event gives the focus back to its
row ([audit-log.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.spec.ts)); a new documentation page brings its pane's top into
view and **Back to the tree** the entry ([ansible-docs.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/ansible-docs.spec.ts)); an opened
command has no cap ([client-command.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command.spec.ts)).

### R-UI-216 · A failure shows every fact of its answer
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-25, on a repository's page while the backend restarted behind the dev server's proxy, where two red notices stood one
above the other and each said only "HTTP 502": "wenn das Frontend Fehler anzeigt ist mir das ein bisschen dünn, ich will im Frontend alle
Infos die verfügbar sind angezeigt bekommen." The two were the shell's notice of the session's read (`whoami`) and the page's notice of
the repository's read, both 502 without a body; an answer that was no problem document had become the message `HTTP <status>`, and the
notice showed nothing else.

*Built*: [error-notice.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.ts) (`quader-error-notice`, every screen's), the facts of a failed
answer on `ApiError.answer` ([problem.ts](../../web/src/app/api/problem.ts),
[Q-UI-1180](#q-ui-1180--a-failure-carries-the-facts-of-its-answer-on-its-apierror)), made by `apiErrorOf` of
[failure.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/failure.ts) for the interceptors and the upload's own client, the words and the report in
[failure-report.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-report.ts), the groups in [failure-groups.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-groups.ts),
the toast's **Details** in [failure-dialog.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-dialog.ts); how a screen uses it is on
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#errors-in-screens-r-ui-216).

- **A sentence for every failure** ([Q-UI-1181](#q-ui-1181--every-failure-is-said-in-the-readers-language-from-its-code-else-from-its-status)),
  in the reader's language, with or without a problem document: the code's sentence where the screen knows the code (R-UI-042), else
  the status's: no answer (0); the server did not answer through the gateway in front of it (502, 504); the server is not ready (503);
  not signed in (401), no permission (403), does not exist (404), waited too long (408), too large (413), too many requests (429); the
  server failed (another 5xx); the server refused the request (another 4xx); an answer that could not be read; a failure of the page's
  own code. Never the bare status as the only words. The sentence is the notice's alert; the facts below it are not announced.
- **The facts of the answer, visible without a click**
  ([Q-UI-1182](#q-ui-1182--the-facts-stand-under-the-sentence-what-can-be-long-is-folded)), each only where the answer had it: the
  status with its reason phrase (`502 Bad Gateway`, from RFC 9110's table: HTTP/2 carries none), or **No answer**; the call (method,
  path and query); the time of the failure; the request ID with a copy button (the problem's, else the answer's `X-Request-Id`, which
  the server sets on every answer, `requestlog.go`); the problem's code; the server's own sentence (`detail`, else `title`), English and
  marked `lang="en" translate="no"`; Retry-After; that the page sent the call twice (R-UI-042's one retry); the failures of the call in
  a row.
- **What can be long, under Technical details** (R-UI-214's fold): the body of an answer that is no problem document, as text and at
  most 4,000 characters with a note of its whole length; its content type; the headers a script may read; the field problems of a
  refusal (pointer, code, sentence); the problem's `type`, `instance` and other members; the message of a failure of the page's code.
- **Copy report** ([Q-UI-1183](#q-ui-1183--copy-report-copies-the-whole-notice-as-plain-text)) copies the sentence, every fact and the
  folded part as plain text, the time in the reader's form and in UTC.
- **Retry for every failed read, and the read again by itself**
  ([Q-UI-1184](#q-ui-1184--a-failed-read-is-offered-again-and-a-failure-that-may-pass-is-read-again-by-itself)): **Retry** stands for
  every failed read (GET, HEAD) and for a write that got no answer, a gateway's or a starting server's (0, 502, 503, 504), where the
  screen binds `(retry)`. A failed read whose failure may pass (0, 408, 429, 5xx, an unreadable answer) reads its view again by itself
  while the window is seen: after 3 s, then twice as long after each further failure of the call, up to 5 minutes (R-UI-213's back-off),
  never before Retry-After; at once when the window is seen again; never while it is hidden. The notice says when it tries ("This page
  tries again by itself in 6 seconds.") and stays in place while it does, on every screen: a failed read's failure is cleared by the
  read's answer, never by its start, in one form ([Q-UI-1195](#q-ui-1195--a-failed-reads-failure-is-cleared-by-its-answer-in-one-form-and-a-rule-refuses-the-other)):
  `failureOf` of [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts) for a `resource()`, `PagedResource` for a list, and
  a read of its own that sets its failure after the answer; a list shows no "Loading." under the notice, and the notice says "Trying
  again." while a read runs, after the person's Retry too
  ([Q-UI-1197](#q-ui-1197--the-notice-says-trying-again-after-the-persons-retry-too-and-a-list-shows-no-loading-under-it)). A refusal
  (403, 404, 422) is not read again by itself; **a write is never repeated by itself**.
- **A page comes back whole** ([Q-UI-1196](#q-ui-1196--the-pages-retry-reads-its-other-failed-reads-with-it-and-a-read-that-would-show-a-wrong-fact-shows-its-failure)):
  the notice's Retry, the person's and its own, reads again every read of the page that failed with it (the formats, the server's
  address, the caller's rights, a section's own read), so that the page after the recovery is the page of a fresh load. A read whose
  failure would show a wrong fact while it lasts ("not scanned", "no members", "none", "off", the robot for an uploaded avatar) shows
  its failure as what it is, in a notice of its own where its fact stands, which joins the page's notice when the cause is the same; a
  read the page works without lets a failure that may pass through instead of answering "none", and a store of the whole app that read
  once reads again after one by itself
  ([Q-UI-1199](#q-ui-1199--a-read-the-page-works-without-lets-a-failure-that-may-pass-through-and-a-store-reads-again-after-one)).
- **One cause, one notice** ([Q-UI-1185](#q-ui-1185--notices-of-one-cause-in-one-place-are-one-notice-by-themselves)): notices shown
  at once in one place (the page, or one overlay) whose failures have the same status, code and server's sentence are one notice, the
  first in the page's order, which names every call and whose Retry reads every view; the others show nothing. Every
  `quader-error-notice` joins by itself, so every page that stacks notices has it, the owner's case first: the shell's and the
  repository's 502 are one notice with two calls.
- **Every screen and every format**: the change is in `ApiError`, the interceptors and the shared notice, which 197 places use. A compact
  place says the sentence and opens the whole notice ([Q-UI-1187](#q-ui-1187--a-compact-place-says-the-sentence-and-opens-the-whole-notice)):
  a failure's toast with **Details**, a failed upload's row with **Details**, a failed finding of a bulk triage with the sentence and
  its status and code. A form's error summary keeps its field list and folds the answer's report under Technical details
  ([Q-UI-1189](#q-ui-1189--a-forms-error-summary-folds-the-answers-report)).
- **Security** ([Q-UI-1186](#q-ui-1186--a-failures-facts-leave-out-every-credential-and-show-a-foreign-body-as-text),
  [data-and-secret-flow.md](../security/data-and-secret-flow.md#a-failed-answer-in-the-browser)): no request header, no request body,
  no cookie is shown or copied; a query parameter that carries a credential is named without its value; the credential headers of an
  answer are left out; a foreign body is text, never markup; the body of a successful answer that could not be read is never kept.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, milliseconds each): [error-notice.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.spec.ts), eleven cases,
about 0.3 s: a 502 without a body says its sentence and shows the status, the call and the time and no empty row; a gateway's error page
is folded as text, never as markup, with its headers and the note that it was cut; a 503 shows its code, the server's sentence marked
English, Retry-After, the request ID with Copy, the call sent twice and the failures in a row; a refusal lists its field problems; two
calls of one cause are one notice naming both, whose Retry reads both; two causes stay two; Copy report holds the sentence, the facts and
the folded part; a failed read reads again after 3 s and a write never; nothing is read while the window is hidden and at once when it is
seen again; the wait doubles up to 5 minutes and a refusal is not read again; a notice without a bound retry offers none; the person's
Retry keeps the notice saying "Trying again." until the read fails again (twelve cases, about 0.3 s).
[paged-resource.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.spec.ts) (two cases, about 0.06 s): a failed resource keeps its
failure while it reads again and its Retry reads the page's other failed reads with it and not one that answered; a list keeps its
failure while it starts again and clears it with the first page. [lint-rules.test.mjs](../../web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs): the rule
of [read-failure-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/read-failure-rule.mjs) refuses a failure made by hand and a retry that clears its failure
before the answer, of a notice and of a data table.
[interceptors.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/interceptors.spec.ts) (three cases) and
[failure.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/failure.spec.ts) (five): the facts of a 502 with a credential parameter, the failures
in a row and their end, a problem in a Blob, the redaction of the query and of the headers, an unreadable answer without its body, a
failure of the page that is no lost connection. [problem-messages.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/problem-messages.spec.ts): a
sentence for every status without a problem document, one second singular. The pages' reads that came back wrong (Q-UI-1196), one case
each where the screen's spec existed: [virtual-members.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/virtual-members.spec.ts) (the
candidates), [groups.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/groups/groups.spec.ts) (the policies naming a group),
[package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts) (the scanning report),
[session-store.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.spec.ts) (the session's failure kept while it is read again),
[server-address.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/server-address.spec.ts) (the address's failure thrown, never "none configured"),
[deb-signing-keys.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/deb-signing-keys.spec.ts) ("Trying again." in place after Retry). [repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts):
the repository's page comes back by itself with the formats that failed beside it. The notice's eight states in a browser
([error-notice.states.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.states.spec.ts), `make ui-states`) and the render walk
`repository-failures` in English and German ([failures.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/failures.ts),
[Q-UI-1188](#q-ui-1188--the-notices-states-are-measured-in-make-ui-states-and-its-words-in-the-render-sets-german-pass)).

### R-UI-217 · Every load shows the spinner the owner picked
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-25, at an opened upstream package that only read "Reading the package from the upstream.", whole: "Es gibt
verschiedene Stellen in unserem Frontend, die remote Inhalte nachladen und dafür einige Zeit brauchen. Ich hätte gerne dass das Laden
immer von einem Spinner begleitet wird. Den Spinner will ich mir aber aussuchen". Of four candidates he chose the bricks of the
product's mark: "Quader spinner sieht gut aus, aber bitte 3 reihen Steine und damit viereckig." Later the same day, at the tab Upstream
of `upstream/galaxy`, where the results' box said only "Loading.": "Hier auch loading ohne Spinner. Finde selbstständig alle Stellen die
einen Spinner brauchen. Tipp: der OIDC Login ebenso", and at a search for "common" that took 5.9 s: "Hier suche nach upstream repos in
ansibil galaxy, spinner". The search had shown the level's 38,655 packages as its hits and said that nothing matched, until its 392 hits
arrived.

*Built*: [spinner.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/spinner.ts) (`quader-spinner`), [loading.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/loading.ts)
(`quader-loading`), [busy.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/busy.ts) (`[quaderBusy]`, `busyActInterceptor`), the look and the delay in
[_spinner.scss](../../web/src/styles/_spinner.scss), the first paint in [index.html](../../web/src/index.html); how a screen uses them is on
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#loads-and-the-spinner-r-ui-217).

- **The spinner is the mark** ([Q-UI-1229](#q-ui-1229--the-spinner-is-the-mark-three-rows-of-six-stones-lit-clockwise-in-sandstone)): its
  square of three rows, six stones, drawn inline from the mark's geometry. At rest each stone has the quiet neutral
  `--quader-spinner-stone`; one after another, clockwise from the top left, a stone lights up in the mark's sandstone
  (`--quader-mark-accent`) and fades back, a round in 1.8 s. Three sizes: on a line of text (16 px, centred on the line by R-UI-175), in a
  button (its icon's 16 px) and for a page or a large area (48 px, the next size above 40 px at which every stone and joint falls on whole
  pixels). It is decoration for assistive technology (`aria-hidden`); the sentence beside it is the place's one status. Sandstone is no
  state colour of the product and the spinner is the one place it moves.
- **The sentence stays and says what loads.** The spinner stands before the sentence ("Loading the members.", "Reading the package from
  the upstream."); a list says it in its table's place (`loadingText` of the data table); "Loading." stays only where nothing more is
  known. A place that had no sentence has one (the dashboard's parts, the security dashboard's summary, the first screen, the sign-out).
- **A load that answers within 300 ms shows nothing** ([Q-UI-1230](#q-ui-1230--a-load-shows-after-300-ms-by-the-stylesheet-in-the-place-its-content-will-take)):
  the sentence and the spinner keep their place from the start and become visible after the delay, so nothing moves when they appear.
- **Reduced motion** ([Q-UI-1237](#q-ui-1237--under-reduced-motion-no-light-travels-the-first-stone-stays-lit-and-the-mark-breathes)): no
  light travels; the first stone stays lit and the mark breathes slowly.
- **What shows one**: a first load of a page, a tab, a section, a dialog that reads before it shows, an opened row; a load after the
  person's act (a search, a filter, a level, a page, **Load more** where its rows arrive); a field whose choices load (the spinner inside
  the select or the field, its one option or its placeholder saying what loads); a search's suggestions ("Searching…"); an act that waits
  for the server (its button, [Q-UI-1235](#q-ui-1235--a-busy-button-spins-where-the-person-pressed-by-its-flag-or-by-the-writes-its-press-started));
  a switch whose answer is open (in place of its word); the first paint before the app starts and until its first screen stands
  ([Q-UI-1236](#q-ui-1236--the-first-paint-holds-the-spinner-until-the-first-screen-stands)); the sign-in's redirect to the provider; the
  sign-out.
- **What shows none**: a live view's read again of what it shows (R-UI-213,
  [Q-UI-1238](#q-ui-1238--a-live-views-read-again-shows-no-spinner)); a count on a tab's label or a badge that appears when known; an
  avatar's image.
- **A new question shows its load, never the answer of the question before**
  ([Q-UI-1234](#q-ui-1234--a-new-question-shows-its-load-never-the-answer-of-the-question-before)): while a read that answers another
  search, level, filter or page runs, the area shows the spinner and the sentence; a count line and an empty sentence belong to the
  answer and are not shown under the new question's words. The data table shows its load whenever it loads and holds no row, so "loaded
  and empty" while it loads cannot show the empty sentence. A list of suggestions as one types keeps the matches of the text before
  while it reads, with the spinner on its status line: they still name real people and things.
- **Held** by the lint rule of [busy-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/busy-rule.mjs)
  ([Q-UI-1239](#q-ui-1239--a-lint-rule-refuses-a-load-without-the-spinner-by-its-sentence-its-list-its-button-and-a-spin-of-its-own)) and the
  render walk `loading-states` ([loading.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/loading.ts)), which holds calls open to picture the loads.

Acceptance criteria (Vitest, milliseconds each): [spinner.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/spinner.spec.ts), six cases, about
0.1 s: the stones lit clockwise from the top left; `index.html`'s first paint draws the same stones in the same order with its sentence in
both languages; the spinner is decoration, the sentence the one status, the delay and reduced motion the stylesheet's; a busy button with
a flag keeps its label and spins only where it was pressed; one without a flag spins while the write its press started is open, refuses a
second press, and spins for no read of a live view and no write that something else started; a switch whose answer is open shows the
spinner in place of its word. [data-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.spec.ts): a list that loads a new question
shows its load and never its empty sentence, and **Load more** spins where its rows arrive.
[remote-upstream.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream/remote-upstream.spec.ts): the owner's case, a search started
after a level's page with its answer held, shows its load, neither the level's total as hits nor the empty sentence, and its button is
held. [remote-downloads.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.spec.ts): an empty queue read again by
itself keeps its empty sentence and shows no load. [lint-rules.test.mjs](../../web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs), two cases. The states `download-preview-loading` and
`limits-rule-profiles-loading` of `make ui-states`.
### R-UI-218 · A package leads with the documentation its format carries
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-25, at the package list of `upstream/galaxy`: "Wenn man auf eine Collection klickt, sollte man meiner Meinung nach
direkt in der Doku der neusten Version landen. Das wäre das normale Verhalten in Ansible Galaxy." And: "Ansible-Collections haben die
spezifische Eigenschaft einer Dokumenation die hervorzuheben ist. Wir versuchen im Raum 'Ansible' die Galaxy vollständig und ebenbürdig
zu ersetzen." Asked whether npm and NuGet packages open the same way (about 21:00): "Ja sollen sie, wenn die dafür notwendigen
Metainformationen vorhanden sind, soll sie von uns verwendet und dargestellt werden. Das gilt immer: Doku die mit zum Format gehört und
regelmäßig vorhanden ist, soll auch bei uns umgesetzt werden. Schau zum Beispiel bei Ansible Galaxy: hier wird erst die Doku eingeblendet
(neuste Version) und man von dort aus in den Versionen zurück blättern wenn gewünscht."

*Built*: `leadsWithDocumentation` of [content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts), the routes of
[packages.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/packages.routes.ts), `versionsCommands` of
[package-links.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-links.ts),
[package-version.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.ts),
[version-switch.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-switch.ts).

- **The rule.** Documentation that belongs to a format and is regularly present is what a package of that format opens on. The format
  says so with `leadsWithDocumentation` of its content shape, not a screen with the format's name: on for Ansible Galaxy (a collection's
  documentation, R-UI-060), npm and NuGet (a version's README, R-UI-008); off for OCI, Debian and generic files, whose content is their
  list of tags, versions or files. A format joins by one line.
- **Addresses** ([Q-UI-1242](#q-ui-1242--a-packages-address-is-its-newest-version-where-its-format-leads-with-its-documentation-its-table-is--versions)): `/projects/{project}/packages/{format}/{name…}` of such a format is the page of the package's
  newest version (R-UI-111): `latestVersion` of R-API-029, the highest that is no pre-release, or the highest pre-release where none is
  stable, as the lists' column **Latest** says. `…/{name…}@{version}` is a version's page as for every format; `…/{name…}/-/versions` is
  the table of every version (R-UI-110), which the package's own address shows for the other formats. Every link to a package by its
  name (a repository's list, **Packages**, search hits and suggestions, the breadcrumb, a collection's dependency, **Recently opened**)
  leads to the package's address, so to its newest version's documentation; a link that means every version (an opened row's
  **All 33 versions**, the switch's last item) leads to the table.
- **The documentation first** ([Q-UI-1245](#q-ui-1245--a-version-without-documentation-opens-on-its-first-tab-with-content-and-its-readme-tab-says-so)): the tab of the documentation is the first of the version's page (**Documentation**
  and **Contents** of a collection, **README** of an npm and a NuGet package), and the page opens on it. Where the version carries none,
  the page opens on its first tab with content, and an npm or NuGet version's tab **README** stays and says "This version has no README
  to show."; a collection without documentation (a role archive) opens on the tab it has.
- **The switch between the versions** ([Q-UI-1243](#q-ui-1243--the-switch-between-the-versions-is-a-menu-of-the-ten-newest-in-the-head-with-a-link-to-all)) in the head of the version's page, before the verb's button: a button that
  names the version shown, whose menu lists the ten newest versions by the format's order, the one shown marked as the current page,
  the newest marked **Latest**, a pre-release marked **Pre-release**, and under them **All 30 versions**, the table. A version switched
  to opens on the tab of the address, the page of a collection's documentation (`doc`) and the address's fragment (an option's
  `#parameter-…`), so a reader of the documentation reads the other version's. While the ten are first read the menu shows the spinner
  (R-UI-217).
- **Deep links** keep their query and fragment on every address: the package's own address with `?tab=documentation&doc=module/<name>#parameter-<path>`
  shows that page of the newest version at that anchor; `…@{version}` with the same opens that version; `…/-/versions` keeps `q`, `sort`
  and a fragment.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts),
  [app.routes.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/app.routes.spec.ts), milliseconds): `/projects/web/packages/npm/@team-a/ui` shows "@team-a/ui
  1.4.0" with the breadcrumb Projects, web, Packages, @team-a/ui; `…/-/versions` is the table, titled **Versions**, the breadcrumb's
  package a link to `…/npm/@team-a/ui`; an image's own address is its table and `…/-/versions` names no image's table; the switch lists
  1.5.0-beta.1 (**Pre-release**), 1.4.0 (**Latest**, the current page), 1.3.0 and **All 3 versions**, and keeps `?tab=details`; a
  version without a README opens on **Files**, its README tab saying so; a graded npm version opens on its README;
  `/projects/web/packages/ansible/acme.tools?tab=documentation&doc=module%2Fcheck_host_reachable#parameter-host` shows that page of
  1.2.0 with the address, query and fragment unchanged, and the switch's 1.0.0 is the same address with `@1.0.0`; `acme.tools@1.0.0` with
  the same query and fragment opens 1.0.0.
- Journeys: `08-packages` (the name opens the newest version on its README, the switch leads to the table), `21-visibility` (a visitor
  without the wiki lands on **Files**), `ansible-docs` (a collection opens on **Documentation**).
- Rendered (rule 11): the npm, NuGet and Ansible Galaxy packages as their names open them, with the switch open and the command panel
  open, a package of thirty versions, one of pre-releases only, a version in three repositories, a long README, the tables at
  `…/-/versions`, in English and German, light and dark, at 390, 1,024 and 1,440 px.

### R-UI-221 · A version's general properties read the same in every format
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-25, walking the product with Docker and Ansible: "Du musst dir solche Angaben von mir echt selbstständig merken und
auch auf andere Registries anwenden. Ich habe nicht die Zeit dir das 30mal zu erklären." And: "Ich finde es wichtig, dass du
selbstständig generalle Eigenschaften unser Registry identifizierst und auch spezifische Eigenschaften identifizierst." And: "wenn die
dafür notwendigen Metainformationen vorhanden sind, soll sie von uns verwendet und dargestellt werden." A general property is shown by
one block, with the same words, at the same place, in every format that has it; a property only one format has stands in that format's
section **Package details**.

*Built*: [version-facts.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-facts.ts) (the blocks),
[version-metadata.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-metadata.ts) (what each format feeds them),
[package-version.html](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.html); the server's members of R-API-029 (`keywords`, npm's
`fileCount`, `unpackedSize`, `hasInstallScript`, `types`, `publisher`, `bundleDependencies`, `optionalPeers`).

| Property | Where it stands | npm | NuGet | OCI | Debian | Ansible Galaxy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Description | the head, under the name; Debian's long description first in Details | yes | yes | annotations, labels | short and long | yes |
| Licence | the facts line; its address the licence's link | yes | expression; `licenseUrl` the link; a licence file a link to its text (R-NUGET-038) | annotation, label | the copyright file's | yes |
| Links | one row under the facts line ([Q-UI-1313](#q-ui-1313--a-versions-links-are-one-row-under-its-facts-in-every-format)) | homepage, source, issues | homepage, source, branch, commit (R-NUGET-038) | url, documentation, source | homepage | homepage, docs site, source, issues |
| Install script | a note under the links, where a person decides to install ([Q-UI-1363](#q-ui-1363--what-a-build-a-compile-or-an-install-runs-is-said-in-the-note-of-an-install-script)) | `hasInstallScript` | build logic, analyzers, PowerShell scripts, with their files ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-039) | none | not read ([formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) H-2170) | none: an install runs nothing |
| Keywords | Details, first: chips to the packages of the format with the keyword ([Q-UI-1312](#q-ui-1312--keywords-and-tags-are-one-block-of-chips-that-open-the-package-list)) | `keywords` | `tags` | none | none (the source package groups) | `tags` |
| Dependencies | Details, after the keywords: one block ([Q-UI-1311](#q-ui-1311--every-formats-dependencies-are-one-block-a-group-per-kind-in-the-formats-words)) | five fields | per target framework | a chart's | nine relation fields | one list |
| Package details | Details, after the dependencies and an image's facts | runtimes, types, unpacked size, files, install script, publisher | title, minimum client, package types, language, copyright, licence acceptance, development dependency, target frameworks as chips, the dependencies' frameworks, symbols; the release notes a section of their own (R-NUGET-038) | annotations and labels | control fields, source package, copyright file | Ansible versions |
| Authors | Details, after Package details | yes | yes | annotation, label | (Maintainer in Package details) | yes |
| Size | the facts line, in the unit a person reads ([Q-UI-1316](#q-ui-1316--a-size-is-said-in-the-unit-a-person-reads-wherever-it-stands)) | yes | yes | yes | yes, Installed size in Package details | yes |
| Dates, downloads | the facts line; the table of versions ([R-UI-222](#r-ui-222--every-table-of-versions-says-each-versions-downloads-and-an-images-digest)) | yes | yes | Pushed or Fetched | yes | yes |

- **The dependencies** are one block in every format ([Q-UI-1311](#q-ui-1311--every-formats-dependencies-are-one-block-a-group-per-kind-in-the-formats-words)):
  under the heading **Dependencies** a group per kind named by the format's own word (npm's `dependencies`, `peerDependencies`,
  `optionalDependencies`, `bundleDependencies`, `devDependencies`; NuGet's target framework, **All frameworks** for a group without one,
  "No dependencies." for an empty group; Debian's relation fields as `apt show` names them), no group heading where the format has one
  list (an Ansible collection, a Helm chart); a dependency on a line of its own, its alternatives side by side with "or" between them,
  the name a link to its page where this installation holds the package and the reader may read it (one lookup per name, at most 60 per
  version, in npm, NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy), else text; its range or constraint muted after it; npm's optional peer marked
  **optional**.
- **The keywords** (`keywords` of the version, R-API-029: npm's `keywords`, NuGet's `tags`, a collection's `tags`) are chips under
  **Keywords**, each the package list of the project filtered by the format and the keyword (`…/packages?format=npm&keyword=react`), every
  one of them; they are the chip of every list, hit and namespace page (`<quader-package-tags>`, R-ANS-057), which a list shows five of
  and which leads to the same address; the package's table keeps them, as chips, in its closed **Details**.
- **The links** stand in one row under the facts line in every format (homepage, documentation or the docs site, source repository, issue
  tracker), each opening the other site; an address that is not http or https is its label and the text. A licence's address is no
  link of the row: the licence on the facts line is its link.
- **An install script** (npm's `hasInstallScript`, what Quader read of the tarball, R-NPM-007) is said under the links: "Runs a script
  of the package when it is installed", and in npm's Package details. NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy: see the table.
- Every value of a package's metadata is text; an address becomes a link only when it is http or https (R-UI-007).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts), milliseconds): an npm version shows its
  keywords as chips to `…/packages?format=npm&keyword=…`, its dependencies in the groups of its fields with an optional peer marked, a
  held dependency as a link, its links in the row under the facts, the install script's note and its Package details; a NuGet version
  its groups per framework and an empty one's "No dependencies.", its licence linked to its address; a Debian version its Installed size
  in MiB; [version-metadata.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-metadata.spec.ts): each format's feeding.
- Unit (Go, `TestR_UI_221_NPMPackageDetailsFacts`, milliseconds): npm's members of the section; integration
  (`TestR_API_029_VersionDetails`, a changed assertion): `keywords` and the tarball's facts of a published version.
- Rendered (rule 11): the tab Details of a package of every format whose metadata fills every block (`package-version-*-details`), in
  English and German, light and dark, at 390, 1,024 and 1,440 px.

### R-UI-224 · A visitor without a session reads the open findings of a public repository
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-26: "Natürlich soll die Hauptinstanz Vulnerabilities an öffentlich sichtbaren Repos anzeigen. Ja, dann ändert sich
das Verhalten der Hauptinstanz." His purpose: "Damit wollen wir Vertrauen in die ausgelieferten Images schaffen." The API answers such a
visitor the grades and the open findings of what the public levels admit ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-280--an-anonymous-caller-reads-the-open-findings-of-what-the-levels-admit-and-the-public-state-of-a-check)); the
screens show them, in both languages, and offer nothing a visitor cannot use.

- **Grades.** Every place of R-UI-094 shows the grade to a visitor without a session as to a signed-in reader: the column
  **Vulnerabilities** of a repository's content and of its opened item's versions, the versions table of a package page, a version's
  facts. A version that is not checked says so in public words: **Not checked yet** ("This version has not been checked for
  vulnerabilities yet."), **Not checked** ("This version is not checked for vulnerabilities."), or the format's own reason where the
  format is not scanned (Q-UI-1244) and **Not an image**; neither public state is a warning, and neither is read again faster than a
  view's idle interval ([Q-UI-1413](#q-ui-1413--the-public-states-are-neutral-words-without-a-time-and-a-page-reads-them-at-its-idle-interval)).
- **The tab Vulnerabilities.** Per repository the grade card (R-UI-093) without its link to the project's report, the block with its
  reason, and the open findings of the version report itself, at most 1,000 per repository, 25 at a time, the worst first, narrowed by
  the card's bar in the browser ([Q-UI-1410](#q-ui-1410--a-visitor-without-a-session-reads-the-findings-of-the-version-report-itself)).
  A repository whose grade counts more says "1,000 of 1,234 open findings shown, the worst first.". An image at the end of life of its
  OS whose grade is C without a High finding says why on the card: "OS end of life: no more security updates, the scan may miss
  vulnerabilities" (R-VULN-038).
- **A row.** The severity with its score, the identifier as a link to the advisory's page, the markers **Malicious** and **Known
  exploited**, the aliases, the summary, an image's components ("In xz 5.6.0-r0 → 5.6.1-r2") and the fixed versions; no status
  ([Q-UI-1411](#q-ui-1411--a-visitor-without-a-session-reads-a-finding-without-its-status-and-reaches-its-advisory-not-its-detail)).
- **The advisory page.** The advisory, and the versions it affects that the visitor may read, without their status and without the
  link to a finding; a list cut at 1,000 says so without the link into the report.
- **Nothing that needs a session.** No triage, rescan or block, no link to a finding's detail or to the project's report: the project's
  side bar has no **Vulnerabilities** for the visitor, and the breadcrumb's step of it is a name
  ([Q-UI-1412](#q-ui-1412--what-needs-a-session-is-left-out-for-a-visitor-without-one-and-the-views-are-told-not-asked)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([anonymous-vulnerabilities.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/anonymous-vulnerabilities.spec.ts),
  [grade-words.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-words.spec.ts),
  [breadcrumbs.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/breadcrumbs.spec.ts), milliseconds): a visitor's tab lists the report's findings with
  their aliases and an image's components, each linking to its advisory, without a status, asks no findings API and offers no link
  into the report; "30 of 1,500 open findings shown"; the bar narrows in the browser; a blocked version's finding links to its
  advisory; the public states' words in English and German; the advisory page without status and links; the side bar and the trail.
- Rendered (rule 11): `anonymous-version-findings` (with the advisory page and a plain user's view of the same version),
  `anonymous-version-clean`, `anonymous-version-image-pending`, `anonymous-version-image-eol`, `anonymous-version-ansible`,
  `anonymous-repository-grades`, `anonymous-package-grades`, in both schemes, at 1,440, 1,024 and 390 px, the marked ones in German.

### R-UI-240 · A Bastion's card: its limits, its throughput and its state
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The screen of the owner's decisions of 2026-11-26 on a Bastion (W-34; [bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-093, R-BAS-097,
[usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-044, R-LIM-046): a Bastion is configured on its card at the main installation
([bastion.md](bastion.md#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation) Q-BAS-323). Simple by default, details on
demand ([Q-UI-1480](#q-ui-1480--a-bastions-card-shows-the-preset-the-mode-and-the-throughput-everything-else-is-behind-details)).

- **The plain path**, a section **Limits** on every card (R-BAS-007), after the card's actions and the handover's section:
  - **Preset**: a segmented control **Internet**, **Partner network**, **Internal**, with one sentence under it for the chosen one
    ("Strict limits for callers from the internet; administrators too." / "The installation's own profiles for known partners." / "No
    limits, everything counted."), and **Custom** shown, not offered, once a kind rule or a flood figure differs. A change opens the dialog
    of [Q-UI-1481](#q-ui-1481--a-preset-is-applied-after-a-dialog-that-names-what-it-replaces).
  - **Mode**: the line "Mode: Enforce" or "Mode: Audit. Limits are counted, not applied at this Bastion." with **Switch to Audit…** or
    **Switch to Enforce…**, the dialogs of R-UI-182 for this Bastion, after recent authentication.
  - **Maximum throughput to this Bastion**: a number field in MB/s, as wide as five digits, holding "Unlimited" as its value until a number
    is set (a default is a value in the field), with **Save changes**.
- **Details** (a closed disclosure): the flood figures per address (anonymous, signed-in and pages: requests per second, burst, misses a
  minute; the failed-authentication timeout; the blocks; the exempt networks), the slots to the main installation, the anonymous ceiling,
  the throughput's anonymous share and GB per hour per class, the egress addresses (R-UI-243), and the link **Rules of this Bastion** to
  R-UI-241. W-35's switches **Web interface** and **Documentation** stand in the same section with that package's sentences.
- **The state, live** (R-UI-213's `live()`, from the replicas' reported status, R-LIM-045): per card one line "Cache 14.0 of 20.0 GB ·
  97 % hits · 9.0 GB protected · 41 MB/s from the main installation", the throughput against its cap where one is set as a meter (warning
  and danger colours, never green), and "4 callers limited now · 1 address blocked" linking to R-UI-241's **Blocks**. "No report in the
  last 5 minutes" where no replica reported.
- **The edge warning**: where a configured per-address request figure lies above the edge figure a replica reported (R-BAS-093), the line
  "The ingress of this Bastion refuses more than 1,000 requests a second per address before these figures apply." stands under the flood
  figures, in the warning colour.
- **Who sees what** (R-UI-067): a holder of `limits:write` changes the limits, the mode and the throughput; a holder of `endpoints:write` the
  switches and the egress addresses (Q-BAS-325); a reader sees the values as text, as Q-UI-960 says of a card's switch.
- Every change sends `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` with the card's `ETag`; a `412` or a refusal stands under the field with every fact of
  its answer (R-UI-216), and the field keeps the server's value.

*Not built* (package E12, after E8, E10 and E13). Today a card shows the registration's facts, its contacts, its tokens and the handover's
switch only (R-BAS-007, R-BAS-071).

Acceptance criteria:

- Vitest (`bastions.spec.ts`, about 1 s): a new registration shows Internet, "Mode: Enforce" and "Unlimited"; **Details** is closed; a
  holder of `endpoints:write` alone sees the limits as text; the edge warning for a reported figure below the configured one; the state
  line from a status fixture and "No report in the last 5 minutes" without one.
- Rendered (rule 11): the card in both schemes, wide and narrow, with Internet, Custom and an Audit mode, the details open and closed.
