| (c) Proxy images through Quader | Quader fetches and serves the image with size and type limits | Viewer addresses stay inside | Quader fetches URLs chosen by README authors from inside the network: a server-side request forgery surface controlled by package authors |
| (d) Block by default; operator allowlist of exact origins mirrored into the CSP | `ui.readme.external_image_origins` lists trusted origins; the sanitizer keeps images from them and the CSP allows exactly them | Air-gapped and cautious installations lose nothing; others enable exactly the hosts they trust; the browser enforces the same list | One configuration key; badges of public packages from unlisted hosts still show as links |

**Choice:** (d) — external images are blocked by default, and an operator can list exact `https` origins whose images are shown; the same list drives the sanitizer and the CSP `img-src`.

**Rationale:** The useful case for README images in a company registry is internal: badges and diagrams from the company's own GitLab or badge service. (d) serves that case without (b)'s leak of viewer addresses and package names to every host a package author picks, and without (c)'s request-forgery surface. Feeding the sanitizer and the CSP from one list means a sanitizer bug cannot load an image from an unlisted host, and the cross-origin request carries no page URL because UI documents use `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`. The previous recommendation, allowing every `https` image as an operator option, is dropped as too coarse. The development agent revisits this if operators ask for path-level restrictions, which CSP source expressions could express.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-008: the `img` rule, the origin-validation and cache bullet, the configuration key `ui.readme.external_image_origins` replacing `external_images`, and the acceptance criterion; R-UI-001: `img-src` takes the listed origins and the foreign-request rule names the exception; R-API-029: the README cache stores the hash of the list; the security notes describe the rule.

### Q-UI-7 · Roles, drain readiness and Valkey on the system status screen

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Since 2026-10-28 every installation runs separate `web` and `worker` Deployments, needs at least two replicas per role on different nodes for a drain without outage, and runs on Valkey with Sentinel, which can degrade Quader without making a replica unready (INV-2, INV-12). The status screen of R-UI-038 showed a flat list of replicas and treated `objectStore` as the only degraded check. The question is what the screen shows about roles, drains and Valkey, and from which data.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Readiness checks only | Each replica shows its checks, `valkey` among the degraded ones | No new data | Nobody sees from the UI that a role has one ready replica left, that both `web` pods share a node, or that replicas disagree about the Valkey primary |
| (b) Registry-based role and Valkey view | The registry carries role, node (downward API `spec.nodeName`) and each replica's Valkey view (its `valkey` check, the primary it uses, the Sentinels it reaches); the screen groups by role, states drain safety per role and summarises Valkey | Shows the two conditions of a safe drain that Quader can observe, and the Valkey states an operator must act on, from data the replicas already have; the catalog's status screen lists a node per service instance (OPS-008) | Two more registry columns per heartbeat; the screen cannot see disruption budgets or free capacity |
| (c) Read Kubernetes objects | The replicas read Deployments, PodDisruptionBudgets and nodes through the Kubernetes API | Desired replicas, PDB state and node capacity | Needs a ServiceAccount token and read RBAC, which R-HA-033 rules out, for data that `kubectl` and the cluster's monitoring already show |
| (d) Leave it to dashboards | The screen links to Prometheus and Grafana | Nothing to build in the UI | Installations without dashboards see nothing, and the status screen keeps claiming "all ready" while a role is one pod from an outage |

**Choice:** (b) — the replica registry gains the node name and the number of Sentinels each replica reaches, next to the Valkey primary and check it already records, and the status screen groups replicas by role, states drain safety per role, and summarises Valkey from the replicas' views.

**Rationale:** The owner requires a drain without outage "when the setup is designed for it", and the screen is where an operator without cluster access sees whether it currently is. Two of the conditions are visible to Quader: at least two ready replicas per role, and on different nodes. The node name costs one environment variable from the downward API (`spec.nodeName` is offered as an environment variable only, [downward API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/downward-api/), checked 2026-10-28), and every replica already computes its Valkey state, circuit, Sentinel reachability and primary for the metrics of R-HA-057. Showing the primary each replica uses exposes the one Valkey fault that metrics aggregated with `max` hide: a replica still bound to a demoted primary. (c) needs Kubernetes permissions that Quader deliberately lacks, and (d) leaves the UI silent about the requirement the owner stressed. The screen states what it cannot see (budgets, capacity, the N + 1 rule). The development agent revisits this if Quader ever gets read access to the Kubernetes API for another reason, which would let the screen show desired replicas and budgets too.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (replicas by role with drain safety, the `valkey` degraded check, the Valkey card, the Backups card, the header's "not drain-safe", new acceptance criteria, and the MVP note that names the added registry fields), R-API-038 (the registry and system-information fields the screen reads, adopted unchanged from [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003 and R-OPS-004, which own their shapes: per replica `roles` (`["all"]` for the development role), `state`, `node`, `checks`, `degraded` and the nested `valkey` view with `state`, `reason` in R-OPS-001's vocabulary, `circuit`, `primary`, `sentinelsReachable`, `sentinelsConfigured`, `serverVersion` and `lastPrimaryChangeAt`; per installation `replicas.roles.<role>` with `live`, `ready`, `degraded` and `nodes`, the `valkey` block of installation facts and the `backup` block). An earlier revision of this block named flat fields (`valkeyPrimary`, `valkeyPrimarySince`, `valkeySentinelsReachable`), `replicas.byRole` and other reason names; the choice is unchanged, only the field shapes follow their owner. Cross-page: [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003 (column `node` and the `valkey` view column); [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-030 (the chart sets `QUADER_NODE_NAME` from `spec.nodeName` for `web` and `worker` pods), R-HA-057 (`quader_valkey_sentinels_reachable` counts the Sentinels that answer a periodic probe of all configured ones) and Q-HA-12 (the status screen now needs these registry fields and the backup summary, so "adds no backend work" no longer holds).

### Q-API-13 · Problem member name, problem type, status of validation errors and error codes

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Absolute problem type on the public base URL | `type` is `https://<base url>/api/v1/problems/<code>` | Resolves to a page of the installation | Differs for every installation and for every alias of the host; cannot be compared across installations |
| (b) Relative reference `/api/v1/problems/<code>` served by Quader from the embedded code registry (chosen) | `type` is the same on every installation; `GET /api/v1/problems/{code}` describes it | Identical everywhere; resolves on every base URL | Served by Quader only |
| (c) `about:blank` with the code as a member | The RFC 9457 default | No catalog to serve | No description of the code for clients |

Request-ID member (chosen with the API conventions, `requestId`): (a) `request_id` in snake case, as the logs
name it; (b) `requestId` in camel case, as the rest of the API's JSON (R-API-003) (chosen). The member carries
the value of the `X-Request-Id` header.

Status of a validation failure: (a) 400 for every `invalid` error; (b) 400 for a request that cannot be parsed
or that names an unknown field, and 422 when the body parsed and the fields are invalid (chosen).

Codes (chosen): `malformed_request` for the 400 of an unparsable request (not `invalid_request`, which is the
OAuth form of [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-008); `server_busy` for a replica at its concurrency
bound (not `too_many_requests_in_flight`); `database_timeout` for a statement that exceeded its limit, `503` with
`Retry-After` (R-ARCH-019).

**Choice:** (b) for the type, `requestId` for the member, the 400/422 split, and the three codes above.

**Rationale:** A client matches on `code` and on `type` across installations, so both must be the same
everywhere, and the API's JSON is camel case in every other member. The split keeps a parse error apart from a
field error without a second status family. The development agent would revisit the codes before any of them
is released, because a code is never renamed within an API major version (R-ARCH-025).

**Applied in the spec:** R-ARCH-023 names `requestId` (it said `request_id`, which contradicted R-API-009 and the
API's JSON); R-API-009 already states the type, the status split and the extension members. `malformed_request` is
in R-API-009's generic table; `server_busy` and `database_timeout` are named by their owning pages
([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-005 and R-ARCH-019, R-API-014). Decision record:
[ADR-126](../decisions.md#adr-126--problem-details-with-a-relative-type-a-requestid-member-and-named-error-codes).

### Q-API-14 · Stand-in for `system.read` until authentication ships

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

**Superseded in M1** by [Q-AUTHZ-16](authorization.md#q-authz-16--the-dev-profile-bridge-systembootstrap_anonymous_read-in-the-new-engine)
and [Q-AUTHZ-71](authorization.md#q-authz-71--the-bootstrap-bridge-opens-two-operations-not-a-capability): the switch was not removed
with authentication; it stays a development-profile bridge in front of the authorization engine and opens only the system
information and the replica list to anonymous callers on the default endpoint.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No anonymous read; the development profile reads the replica list with a credential | No credential can be valid before M1 | No exposure | The development profile and its load test have no credential to read with |
| (b) `system.bootstrap_anonymous_read`, default `false`; `true` only where configured (chosen) | Anonymous callers read `/api/v1/system/info` and `/api/v1/system/replicas`. A presented `Authorization` header gets `401` (`bootstrapAuthenticate`). Startup refuses `true` with an `https` `server.base_url` other than localhost. | Off by default; the dev profile and its load test work; the refusal keeps it away from a public origin | Anyone who reaches the client listener of a development installation reads the replica list |
| (c) A fixed development principal that holds every permission | A stand-in identity in code | Works with every route | The stand-in becomes the authorization model by accident |

**Choice:** (b). The key is removed with the identity work at M1.

**Rationale:** The replica list and the installation facts are operator data, but the M0 dev profile must show them
to a load test. The refusal of the `https` origin keeps the switch away from anything that is not a development
installation, and the warning in the log says so at each start. The development agent would revisit the key when
M1 ships, where it is deleted rather than kept.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-038 states the M0 stand-in and its refusal (paragraph under the endpoint table).

### Q-UI-8 · Bundle budget, CSP nonce and inline code

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No budget | The build reports sizes only | No failing build | The initial bundle grows unnoticed |
| (b) Raw-size guard in `angular.json`: warning at 800 kB, error at 1500 kB (chosen as the first line) | Angular's budget on the build output | Fails on a gross regression with no extra tooling | Raw sizes say little about what a browser downloads |
| (c) Compressed budget of what `index.html` loads, checked by `web/scripts/check-budget.mjs` (400 kB, chosen as the rule of R-UI-001) | The script reads `index.html`, follows the files it loads and sums their gzip size; `build:embed` runs it after the build | The number of R-UI-001 is what is enforced | A script to keep in step with Angular's output names |

Nonce: `index.html` carries the literal `QUADER_CSP_NONCE` on the root element as `ngCspNonce`; the server replaces it with the
per-response nonce of the CSP. Inline code: critical-CSS inlining and font inlining are off in `angular.json` (`inlineCritical: false`,
`fonts.inline: false`), so no inline code needs the nonce.

**Choice:** (b) and (c) together, and the nonce with inlining off, as stated.

**Rationale:** The guard catches a gross regression at once; the compressed budget is the number that R-UI-001 states
for the user's download. Turning inlining off keeps the strict CSP of R-UI-001 without a hash for each inline block.
The development agent would revisit the raw guard if Angular's budgets change their meaning, and the compressed budget
when a route is loaded lazily and no longer part of the initial bundle.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-001 states the 400 kB compressed budget (unchanged); the mechanism is the choice of this block.

### Q-UI-9 · Test tiers of the web UI at M0

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every tier of R-UI-047 at M0, including browser mode, contract tests and Playwright | The full table from the first commit | Nothing deferred | The M0 shell has no journeys to test in a browser, so the tiers would test nothing yet |
| (b) Unit and component tiers at M0 on jsdom through Angular's `unit-test` builder; browser mode, contract, Playwright and axe with the M1 screens (chosen) | The M0 table has two tiers | The tiers that exist test real logic; the rest arrive with the screens they test | R-UI-047's table describes M1 and later for the rest |
| (c) Unit tests only | Nothing else at M0 | Smallest | No component test of the shell |

**Rationale:** Browser-based tests need screens. Writing them against the M0 shell would test placeholders and cost
the build time that the coverage evidence needs. The development agent would revisit this when the first screen
of M1 lands, which is when the browser tiers and axe start.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-047 is unchanged; its table describes the full target, and this block states the M0 subset.

### Q-UI-11 · Accessibility tooling and its scope at M1

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Playwright with `@axe-core/playwright` only | The tier of R-UI-044 and R-UI-047 | Real layout, contrast, both themes | Needs browser binaries and a running server in CI; the e2e work package owns that harness, so the shell would wait for it |
| (b) axe-core inside the Vitest component tier on jsdom (chosen for M1), Playwright later | `axe.run` on the rendered component, serious and critical impacts fail the spec; one spec renders every routed screen | Runs in `make web-test` and in every pull request now; pinned in `web/package-lock.json` | jsdom has no layout: `color-contrast`, the document-level rules and keyboard journeys are not evaluated |
| (c) Both from now | (a) and (b) | Complete | The cost of (a) without its harness |

**Choice:** (b). `axe-core` 4.14.0 is a dev dependency, `web/src/app/testing/axe.ts` runs it with `color-contrast` off, and
`app.routes.spec.ts` renders every M1 route and fails on a serious or critical violation. The same spec proves the tooling is live by asserting
that a page with an unnamed button and an image without text is reported. `<html lang>` is checked in the built output, where Angular sets it per locale.

**Rationale:** The shell and the placeholders have structure but no content worth a browser run, and a check that runs on every pull request beats one that
waits for a harness. What jsdom cannot see stays on the Playwright tier of R-UI-047: contrast in both themes (the status colours are
`light-dark()` pairs chosen for 4.5:1 and are not machine-verified yet), focus order across a real navigation, reflow at 320 CSS px, both locales.
The development agent would revisit this when the e2e work package has its Playwright harness; the jsdom run then stays as the fast tier.

**Revisited (Q-UI-66):** the harness exists. `@axe-core/playwright` runs on every screen a journey of `web/e2e` visits, with `color-contrast` and the
document-level rules on, in light and dark, English and German, and fails on a serious or critical violation; the jsdom run stays as the fast tier, as
planned. What jsdom could not see was real: it hid two violations that every screen had (Q-UI-67). The contrast of the status colours in both themes is now
machine-verified on the screens the journeys visit.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-044 and R-UI-047 are unchanged; this block states the M1 subset. Q-UI-9 said axe starts with the first M1 screen: it does, in the form chosen here.

### Q-UI-12 · HTTP layer, service interfaces and endpoints that are not in the OpenAPI document yet

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Wait for the wave-2 operations before writing any client | No code against missing endpoints | No guessed shapes | The cross-cutting mechanisms (session, errors, retries) cannot be tested, and the screens wait |
| (b) One `ApiClient` on `HttpClient` plus an abstract service class per endpoint family with an HTTP implementation and an in-memory fake (chosen) | `api/*-api.ts` declares the interface, the hand-typed DTO where the document lacks the operation, and the HTTP implementation; `provideApiServices()` binds them in `appConfig`; specs bind the fakes of `api/testing/fakes.ts` | Screens code against a stable interface; swapping a hand-typed DTO for the generated type changes one file | Hand-typed shapes can drift until the generator covers them |
| (c) A generated service layer | Generated clients | No hand-written shape | Excluded by R-ARCH-004 / R-UI-046 |

**Choice:** (b). Interceptors, outermost first: problem mapping and session consequences, the one automatic retry, then the request conventions.
CSRF is Angular's XSRF support configured with the cookie `__Host-qdr_csrf` and the header `X-CSRF-Token` (R-AUTH-012). The retry layer follows R-UI-042
literally and retries at most once per request: a GET after a network error, `429`, or `503 authz_stale`; a request with an idempotency key after a network
error or `409 idempotency_in_progress`; a PUT or PATCH with its `If-Match` and a DELETE after a network error; a GET without `Quader-Authz-Min-Epoch` after
`412 authz_epoch_unknown`. A DELETE that answers `404` after a retry counts as done; an `ApiError` carries `afterRetry` so that an editor can compare the stored resource with its
draft before it opens the conflict dialog. The client has no wildcard overload for `If-Match` (R-API-012). Endpoints typed by hand for now:
`auth/whoami`, `auth/login-options`, `auth/local/login`, `auth/logout`, `authz/me`, `authz/check`, `users/me/preferences` and `system/encryption`, with the shapes
that R-AUTH-009, R-API-021, R-AUTHZ-023 and R-API-049 print.

**Rationale:** The screens of waves 2 and 3 become content. Where an owning requirement leaves a shape open (`authz/me`, the logout answer, the job returned by the task
trigger) the DTO states the minimum the UI reads and is marked in its file. The development agent would revisit this as each operation reaches `api/openapi.yaml`:
the hand-typed DTO is replaced by the generated schema and the contract tier of R-UI-047 starts to compile against it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042, R-UI-046 and R-API-010 to R-API-014 are unchanged; this block records how the UI implements them.

### Q-UI-13 · Choices on the system status screen and the navigation

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Which cards exist before their endpoints do | Build only what the API serves; build all with fakes; build none | Installation, database, replicas by role, readiness checks and the Valkey card render from `system/info` and `system/replicas`. The stored-secret keys card renders from the typed `EncryptionApi` and shows its own error while the endpoint is absent. Scheduled tasks, jobs and backups have no card yet; the jobs and backups routes are placeholders linked from the screen |
| "Replicas disagree about the primary" needs the bound `valkey.sentinel.refresh_interval` plus one heartbeat | Read the bound from configuration; use a fixed bound | A fixed 30 seconds (`PRIMARY_DISAGREEMENT_GRACE_MS`), measured over the screen's own refreshes; the UI cannot read the configuration |
| Who sees "Re-encrypt now" | `admin` role; any holder of `settings:write` | The action needs `admin` (R-API-049) and `authz/me` lists capabilities, not roles; the UI offers it to holders of `content:bypass`, which only `admin` bundles (R-AUTHZ-010). The API refuses anyone else |
| When the Administration area appears | Any capability; a named list | Any capability in `authz/me` (R-UI-002). Each entry additionally needs its own: repositories `repositories:read-config`, users, groups and service accounts `identities:read`, permission policies `policies:read`, system roles `roles:read`, tokens `tokens:read`, endpoints `endpoints:read`, audit log `audit:read`, system status and settings `settings:read` |

**Choice:** the status screen renders the cards the API serves (completed by Q-UI-19), replicas that disagree about the primary get a fixed grace of 30 s, "Re-encrypt now" is offered to holders of `content:bypass`, and the Administration area appears for any capability, each entry with its own.

**Rationale:** Each choice follows the nearest requirement and stays removable: the grace constant and the capability map are one line each. The development agent would revisit the
re-encryption gate when `authz/me` also reports roles.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 and R-UI-002 are unchanged; this block records the interpretation.

### Q-UI-14 · Forms of the repository and endpoint screens: signals and native controls

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Signal Forms with validators derived from the OpenAPI constraints | The plan of `docs/developer/web-ui.md` | One mechanism for every form | The package is new in Angular 22, and the OpenAPI constraints that matter here (key pattern, rule-name pattern) are one regular expression each; the real validation is the server's and arrives as `errors[].pointer` |
| (b) Plain signals and native controls (chosen) | One `signal` per form, `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>` and checkboxes styled by the tokens, labels with `for`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` set from the server's field problems | Matches the sign-in form; every control is a labelled native element, which axe and screen readers handle without a layer; field errors, the error summary and the dirty check are small helpers (`shared/field-errors.ts`, `shared/unsaved-guard.ts`) | Each form wires its own `(input)` handlers |
| (c) Material form fields everywhere | `mat-form-field` around each control | The look of the sign-in form | Density `-2` and long forms with textareas and repeated fields get heavy; no gain in behaviour |

**Choice:** (b). Server field errors (`ApiError.fieldErrors`) are shown at the control and in an alert summary whose entries focus the control (R-UI-044, WCAG 3.3.1, 3.3.3); an editor with unsaved changes asks before it is left (`unsavedChangesGuard`); a form that meets `reauthentication_required` keeps its non-secret draft in session storage by route and takes it back once (`shared/drafts.ts`, R-UI-042).

**Rationale:** The forms of this work package are a handful of text fields and switches; a form library would add a concept without removing a line of the server-error mapping, which is the part that matters. The development agent would revisit this when a screen needs cross-field validation on the client (the policy editor) and would then move all forms at once.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021, R-UI-042 and R-UI-044 are unchanged. `docs/developer/web-ui.md` no longer announces Signal Forms for the first form.

### Q-UI-15 · Settings of `ui.*` that the browser cannot read

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

R-UI-010 names `ui.browser.page_size` (200) and R-UI-012 names `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` (100 MiB). No management API member returns the configuration, so the screens cannot read them.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Add the two values to `GET /api/v1/system/info` | The UI reads them | The configured value wins | Backend work in the UI wave |
| (b) Constants with the documented defaults (chosen) | `BROWSER_PAGE_SIZE = 200`, `UPLOAD_LIMIT_BYTES = 100 MiB` | Works today; the server still decides (its own upload limit answers `413`, the cursor accepts any page size up to 10,000) | A changed `ui.*` value does not reach the screen |
| (c) A build-time value | Baked into the bundle | Single source | The same bundle serves every installation |

**Choice:** (b). The constants sit next to their use (`features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts` since [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page), `api/files-api.ts`). The upload dialog refuses a larger file before any request, as R-UI-012 requires.

**Rationale:** The defaults are the proposed ones, and a mismatch costs a refused request, never a wrong write. The development agent would revisit this when the first operator sets `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes`; the likely fix is (a), as two more members of `system/info`.

**Applied in the spec:** none. Listed as a gap in the report of this work package.

### Q-UI-16 · Upload: an XHR client of its own, create-only unless "Replace" is ticked

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| How progress is reported | `fetch` upload streams; a second `HttpClient` on XHR (`withXhr()`) | A second `HttpClient`, created once from the root environment injector in `api/files-api.ts`, with XSRF protection and without the Quader interceptors (they cover `/api/v1/` and `/auth/` only). It maps a failure to `ApiError` and ends the session on a 401. It is the only XHR use and it only writes (R-UI-001, R-UI-012) |
| What a path that already exists does | Always replace; replace only when asked | The request carries `If-None-Match: *` unless the user ticks "Replace files that already exist", offered only to a caller who holds `overwrite` there (one batched `authz/check`). Without the tick a duplicate is a `412` with a sentence that names the switch |
| Hashing | Never; always; up to 256 MiB | Up to 256 MiB the browser computes SHA-256 and sends `Repr-Digest` (R-UI-012). A file that cannot be read for hashing is still sent |
| A cut upload | Fail; retry once | One retry from the start with the `File` in hand after a request that got no answer. If the retry answers `412` (the first attempt did commit), the dialog reads the item and counts the upload as done when the stored SHA-256 equals the one it computed |

**Choice:** a second `HttpClient` on XHR for the progress, `If-None-Match: *` unless the caller ticks "Replace files that already exist", SHA-256 in `Repr-Digest` up to 256 MiB, and one retry of a cut upload.

**Rationale:** Each choice is the literal reading of R-UI-012 and R-ARCH-014; the create-only default makes an accidental overwrite impossible without the permission and the switch. The development agent would revisit the second client when `fetch` upload streaming reports progress in all supported browsers.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-012 is unchanged (the dialog is P1; the file tree offered it because the API has the operation; since [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page) a folder of a repository's page does).

### Q-UI-17 · File tree: `@angular/aria` tree, actions in a toolbar

Status: **Superseded by [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page)** (owner, 2026-11-18): the file tree is gone; a repository's folders and files are its pages
(R-UI-010) and their actions stand on them (Q-UI-512). The text below is the record of the superseded decision.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| The tree widget | Own implementation; `@angular/aria` tree (R-UI-010, Q-UI-1) | `ngTree`, `ngTreeItem` and `ngTreeItemGroup` with explicit selection: Enter or a click selects and navigates; the arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead are the pattern's. The group of a folder is created lazily by the pattern and filled when the folder is first expanded |
| "Load more" | A button below the tree; a tree item | A tree item at the end of the group of a folder (reachable by keyboard); activating it loads the next page and leaves the selection where it was. Pages are `BROWSER_PAGE_SIZE` entries |
| Where the actions live | A button on every node; a toolbar above the details | A toolbar above the details of the selection (R-UI-011 asks for an actions button and the keyboard, "never right-click alone"); the context-menu key and Shift+F10 on the tree move focus to the toolbar. A button inside a tree item would nest interactive content in a `treeitem` |
| Deleting a folder | Count by listing; a count endpoint | `children?recursive=true` walked until more than 100 entries are seen; above 100 the dialog asks for the folder name, and `202` shows the job's progress |
| Filters and the open tab | Component state; query parameters | Key text, class, format, sort and the details tab are query parameters (R-UI-003) |

**Rationale:** The tree pattern gives roles and keyboard handling that an own widget would have to re-prove against R-UI-044. The development agent would revisit the toolbar when the tree grows per-node actions that a toolbar cannot reach (P1 copy and move).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010 and R-UI-011 are unchanged. A virtual repository's members and the cache label of a remote repository are not shown: no such repository exists in M1.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Columns of the list | The spec's "created"; what the summary view carries | `GET /api/v1/repositories` answers the summary view with `lastActivityAt` and the client addresses but no creation time, and `view=full` has no addresses. The list shows **last activity** instead of "created" and sorts by key only; the detail page shows creation and last change. The two missing members (creation time on the summary, sort by creation) are reported to the backend |
| Settings forms | Rendered from a JSON Schema per format (R-UI-021); hand-built | The forms are hand-built for the members that apply to the generic format (R-REPO-004, R-GENERIC-008): description, notes, include and exclude patterns, disabled, require authentication, hide existence. *Superseded for the format member by [Q-UI-78](#q-ui-78--the-repository-settings-form-renders-the-subset-of-json-schema-the-formats-use): the `npm` member is rendered from `settingsSchema` (Q-ARCH-229).* |
| Classes in the wizard | A list in the UI; derived | The union of the `classes` of all formats; the format step offers the formats that contain the chosen class. Today that is `local` and the generic format |
| Edit | `PUT`; `PATCH` | A JSON merge patch of the changed members only (`shared/merge-patch.ts`) with the loaded `ETag`; no change disables "Save". A `412` re-reads the repository: equal to the draft after a retried write is a success, otherwise the conflict dialog; "Overwrite" sends the draft's difference against the newly stored version with the new `ETag` |
| Delete | Immediate; type the key | The key is typed; `202` is followed by the job progress component until the job ends, and the row disappears when it succeeded. A `repository_referenced` answer repeats the dialog with the "detach" choice |
| Key availability | `GET` of the key | A `404` after a 400 ms pause means free; any other answer says the check was inconclusive and the server decides at the create |

**Choice:** the list shows last activity instead of the creation time, the forms are hand-built for the generic format's members (the format member since rendered from its schema, Q-UI-78), the wizard offers the union of the formats' classes, an edit is a merge patch with the loaded `ETag`, a delete needs the typed key, and a `404` means a free key.

**Rationale:** The list cannot show what the API does not give, and a request per row would defeat the paging. The development agent would revisit the columns once the summary view has `createdAt`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020 reads "created" and "sort by creation"; this block records why the list shows last activity until the API changes.

### Q-UI-19 · Endpoint screens, audit log and the completed status screen

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Dimensions of the rule editor | One form for all formats; by the format's pattern subject | By `patternSubject` of the repository's format: `path` shows path patterns, `name` shows package names, versions (range, include, exclude, pre-releases) and tags. The descriptor has no "has tags" flag, so tags appear for every name format and the server answers `dimension_not_supported` at the pointer where a format has none |
| The save of an existing rule | Save at once; diff first | A diff dialog (stored against draft, field by field) precedes `PUT` with `If-Match` (R-EP-017); a create sends the `Idempotency-Key` generated when the page opened |
| Preview | On every change; debounced | `check-exposure` 500 ms after the last change with the draft as `rule` (`draft` as the name when none is typed yet), the test paths or the package and versions as input. A stale answer is dropped |
| Client address of a rule | Always shown; only when served | `baseUrl` plus the format's `protocolBasePath`; flagged "This endpoint does not serve this address" when the endpoint's surface lacks the family of the address (`files` or `packages`) |
| Mode `all` | Silent; a banner | A banner on the endpoint, the editor and the preview (R-EP-017) |
| Audit action labels | The event name; a label | A translated label for each event name of the registry, the name in code next to it; an unknown name is shown as sent. Filters, the open event and the time zone are query parameters; the export links carry the filter and, when the range is a preset, its resolved bounds |
| Job progress | Poll fast; poll with an announcement limit | A shared component polls every 2 s and gives assistive technology a new text at most every 10 s and on the final state (R-UI-042) |
| Status screen | Cards without endpoints; all cards | This work package completes the cards of Q-UI-13's first row: the key card shows the replicas' key rings, the replica that lacks a key ID, the canary with the replica that reported it, the last re-encryption and the next rotation step; the scheduled tasks card runs a task with an `Idempotency-Key`; recent jobs offer "Cancel" for queued and running jobs; `/admin/system/jobs` filters by kind and state and refreshes with a pause control. Backups stay a placeholder (R-UI-048) |

**Choice:** the rule editor follows the format's pattern subject, a rule's save shows a diff first, the preview runs 500 ms after the last change, a client address the endpoint does not serve is flagged, mode `all` shows a banner, audit actions get translated labels, job progress is polled every 2 s and announced at most every 10 s, and every card of the status screen but backups is completed.

**Rationale:** Each row is the literal requirement where the API allows it and the narrowest reading where it does not. The development agent would revisit the tag handling when the descriptor reports its dimensions.

**Applied in the spec:** R-EP-017, R-UI-037 and R-UI-038 are unchanged; this block supersedes the first row of Q-UI-13.

### Q-UI-22 · Users, groups and service accounts are edited without a version tag

Status: **Reversed** by [Q-API-42](#q-api-42--one-mechanism-for-a-missing-if-match-and-one-stale-error) and [Q-AUTH-50](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-50--users-groups-and-service-accounts-carry-a-revision-so-does-the-authentication-settings-row) (originally decided by the development agent; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough). The decision below was taken because the API gave these resources no tag; it now does.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Merge patch of the changed members, last writer wins on those members (was chosen) | The documented behaviour of the operations (R-API-013); the screens send only what the user changed | Two administrators editing different fields do not conflict; matches the API | Two edits of the same field overwrite silently |
| (b) Require `ETag` and `If-Match` and the conflict dialog (now chosen) | The API returns tags for these resources | Uniform with policies and settings | Needed the API to return tags |
| (c) Read-only screens | No edits | No conflicts | Not the requirement |

**Choice (current):** (b). The user, group and service account screens keep the `ETag` of the loaded record, and `PATCH` sends it as `If-Match` (`ApiClient.patch`, the same call as for repositories and policies); the screens that already used a tag (authentication settings, preferences, policies) are unchanged. A 412 opens the conflict dialog through `ConflictResolver.save` ([conflict-dialog.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/conflict-dialog.ts)): it reads the record again and shows only the members of the patch, stored now against the user's. "Overwrite" sends the same merge patch with the tag read at that moment, "Reload" adopts the stored record, closing the dialog writes nothing. A 412 on a retried write whose stored members already equal the patch is a success (the first attempt committed). The answer's `ETag` is the tag of the next write. Membership changes (`PATCH /users/{username}/groups`, `/groups/{name}/members`), disable, enable and unlock carry no tag (R-API-012 exempts the deltas); after an action the screen reads the record and its tag again. `ApiClient.patchMerge` is removed, so every merge patch carries `If-Match` and the retry layer of R-UI-042 may repeat it.

**Rationale:** the API now requires the header (a missing one is 428), so the screen cannot omit it, and a tag the user loaded is what makes two edits of the same field visible. The development agent revisits this if a screen edits a member that the tag does not cover.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042's conflict dialog applies to users, groups, service accounts, preferences, authentication settings, policies, repositories and exposure rules. The token tables show a warning for a token whose binding names an endpoint that is not configured (`unknownEndpoints`, R-EP-011, Q-EP-24).

### Q-UI-24 · Where a new token value is shown, and a lost one

The API decides in every case |

### Q-UI-66 · The browser tier: Playwright in the web workspace, one worker, no retries, the journeys in file order

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Decision | Options | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| Where the suite and its tools live | A `web/e2e` project with its own `package.json`; devDependencies of the Angular workspace (`web/package.json`) | The Angular workspace's `package.json`: one lockfile pins `@playwright/test` 1.64.1, `@axe-core/playwright` 4.14.0 (its `axe-core ~4.14.0` is the version of the jsdom tier) and `@types/node`; the browser build is `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, which resolves to the locked version, so there is one version per tool |
| How the browser trusts the dev CA | Install the CA into the browser profile or the system store; `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list` for the leaf; `ignoreHTTPSErrors` with a verified handshake first | `ignoreHTTPSErrors`, after `global-setup.ts` has opened a verified TLS connection to the edge and to the IdP against the dev CA (name checked). A system store needs administrator rights, an SPKI list breaks when the leaf rotates (E0.15 renews it under load), and the handshake keeps the check the CA exists for |
| How the browser reaches the IdP's Service name | A hosts entry (administrator rights); a proxy; `--host-resolver-rules` | `--host-resolver-rules=MAP quader-keycloak.quader.svc <port-forward>`: the page keeps the issuer's name, the redirect URI and the certificate check are the real ones, and the host stays untouched |
| Concurrency and retries | Parallel workers with retries; one worker, no retries | One worker, in file order, no retries. The journeys share one installation and the per-address limits of R-AUTH-038; the audit journey reads the actions of those before it; a retry that turns red into green hides a finding |
| What an assertion of "scattered" is | Count requests in the proxy; the `X-Quader-Replica` of the responses the page saw | The responses the page saw: at least two replicas per journey. Which replica a single call reaches is not asserted: the calls of a screen repeat in a fixed number, so one of them can reach the same replica on every load (measured on the status screen). Nothing is inferred from server metrics |
| Test data | Through the UI; through the API | Through the API with the administrator token (INV-17), `beforeAll` and `afterAll` per journey; the UI is used for what the journey tests. `global-setup.ts` removes alice and bob, the JIT users of an earlier run, like E1.1 |
| Reporting | The list only; plus a JSON report | List, HTML (`.out/playwright/report`, uploaded by CI) and, when `TestE1_11Journeys` runs it, JSON, which the Go test turns into one subtest per journey named by its title, so the `go test -json` report says which journey failed |
| Browsers | Chromium, Firefox and WebKit | Chromium. R-UI-047 asks for all three in the full run on the commit that closes the phase; that run is not set up (the self-hosted runner would install two more browsers, and the journeys have no engine-specific behavior yet) |

**Choice:** Playwright in the Angular workspace, a verified TLS handshake before `ignoreHTTPSErrors`, `--host-resolver-rules` for the IdP's name, one worker in file order without retries, scattering read from the replicas of the responses the page saw, test data through the API, a JSON report turned into a subtest per journey, and Chromium only.

**Rationale:** The choices keep the tier cheap to run on the e2e job that already exists and the verdict unambiguous: a failing journey, an axe violation
or a CSP violation fails `TestE1_11Journeys`. The development agent would revisit Firefox and WebKit at the end of the milestone, and the single worker if the
journeys grow past what the 90-minute budget of the e2e job leaves.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-047 is unchanged; this block states how its end-to-end, accessibility and security tiers are met at M1: seven journeys, Chromium, axe on
every visited screen, `securitypolicyviolation` watched on every page. Not covered at M1: Firefox and WebKit, the client-setup journey with real `npm` and
`dotnet`, the claim tester and the backups screen (no such screens yet), reflow at 320 CSS px and focus order across navigations.

### Q-UI-67 · What the browser tier's axe run found, and how it was fixed

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Finding | Options | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| The label of every `mat-form-field` was `display: none`: the density of -2 sets `--mat-form-field-filled-label-display: none`. Sighted users saw empty boxes; axe reported `label` and `select-name` as critical | Leave the density; give each field an `aria-label` and a visible placeholder; set the token to `block` once | Set `--mat-form-field-filled-label-display: block` on `html` in `main.scss`: the label becomes the floating label and every field of every screen is fixed at once; per-field fixes would repeat in each form |
| The user menu button had `aria-label="User menu"` while its visible text is the user's name (WCAG 2.5.3, axe `label-content-name-mismatch`, serious, on every screen) | Keep the `aria-label` and add the name to it; drop the `aria-label` and add the words as visually hidden text | Drop the `aria-label`; the name is the visible user name followed by a visually hidden "User menu" (same message id `shell.user-menu`, so the German unit stays valid) |
| The upload dialog's title, label and hint failed `color-contrast` when axe ran while the dialog was still fading in | Raise the colours; wait for the animation | Wait: `expectAccessible` awaits the finite animations of the document before axe runs. The colours were not wrong (the same dialog passes after the transition) |

**Choice:** the labels of the form fields shown again by one token in `main.scss`, the user menu named by its visible user name with a hidden "User menu", and axe run after the dialog's animation ends.

**Rationale:** The first two were present on every screen and invisible to the jsdom tier; they are the reason the browser tier was worth building.
The third was a false alarm of timing, not a defect. The development agent would revisit the token if a form needs the compact label-less look again.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-044 is unchanged; the fixes are in [main.scss](../../web/src/styles/main.scss) and [app.html](../../web/src/app/app.html).
