### Q-UI-106 · How the UI's downloads and uploads reach `api` after the cut

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: ADR-155 asked whether the UI calls a `packages` or `files` route with the session cookie, and if it does, that the
call is served through `api`. Verified in [web/src](../../web/src/app): the upload and the folder creation are
`PUT /files/{repo}/{path}` with the session cookie and the CSRF header ([files-api.ts](../../web/src/app/api/files-api.ts),
`upload`, `createFolder`), and the Download buttons of the browse screen (since [ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page) the file's page) and the package page navigate to the `downloadUrl`
of the item or the version file ([repository-file.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts),
[package-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-detail.html)), which is a `/files/` URL or a package
protocol URL such as `/api/npm/npm-local/@team-a/ui/-/ui-1.4.0.tgz`. After the cut the edge sends those paths to `packages`,
which evaluates no session cookie (R-EP-010).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Session-only content routes on `api`, `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}`, running the `/files/` transfer through the same item store; `contentUrl` on items and version files (chosen) | The UI downloads and uploads through `api`; clients keep `downloadUrl` | No session reaches `packages`; one transfer implementation; token clients cannot move bulk traffic to `api` (a request without the session answers `404`); the UI still builds no content URL itself | A second path for the same transfer to test; `api` pods need a spool for the UI's uploads; a protocol URL opened in the browser asks for a credential, because the cookie no longer counts there |
| (b) Signed short-lived download links that `packages` checks | `api` issues a signature for the session's principal, `packages` verifies it | Downloads stay on `packages` | A credential type of its own with expiry, replay and revocation rules; uploads still need a path through `api` |
| (c) The edge routes requests that carry the session cookie to `api` | A header or cookie match at the edge | No URL change | Not portable (an implementation-specific match in the Gateway API, none in a plain Ingress); a misrouted request falls through to `packages` silently |
| (d) `packages` evaluates sessions on `/files/` and package downloads | The old behaviour on those paths | No change | Puts the session store into `packages`, which ADR-155 excludes |

**Choice:** (a). An upload through the content route is bounded by `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` on the server (it was a check
in the browser only), which sizes the `api` spool (R-HA-029, R-HA-035).

**Rationale:** the trust cut stays a property of the roles, the transfer stays one implementation, and the rule that the UI
assembles no content URL holds because the API hands it `contentUrl`. The development agent would revisit this when the content
origin of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-029 (P1) is built: package content shown in the browser then loads from that
origin, and `contentUrl` points where that requirement says.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-025 (the routes and their rules), R-API-029 (`contentUrl`), the links to package content of the
UI baseline, R-UI-012 (uploads); [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010; [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001 (what
`api` builds); [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-029, R-HA-035 (the `api` spool).

### Q-UI-107 · How the status screen groups replicas after the cut

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-038 groups replicas by role (`web`, `worker`) and states drain safety per group (Q-UI-7). After the cut there are
three roles, pools of each, endpoint pools, and during the upgrade across the cut the role `web` beside the new ones.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A group per role (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, and `web` or `all` while one is live), a sub-group per pool with its own counts and drain safety (chosen) | Roles first, pools inside | Drain safety is a property of a Deployment, which a pool is; the upgrade window shows both shapes | A longer screen with many pools |
| (b) A flat group per Deployment | Every pool its own group | Simple | Hides which pools belong to one role; the role's totals are lost |
| (c) Groups per role only, pools as a column | Short | Compact | A pool with one ready replica on one node looks drain-safe inside a healthy role |

**Choice:** (a). The screen is served by `api`, so it is never shown with no live `api` replica; it warns when no `packages`
replica is live, which the UI could otherwise not notice.

**Rationale:** the N + 1 rule of R-HA-059 holds per role and pool; the screen shows it where it holds. The development agent
would revisit this if installations run so many pools that the screen needs a filter.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the groups and their notices); [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
Q-OPS-161 (the role values).

### Q-API-194 · The role members of the replica descriptions are additive, because the role enums are frozen

Status: **Superseded by [Q-ARCH-341](architecture.md#q-arch-341--code-shaped-only-by-the-compatibility-rules-is-cleaned-up-the-cluster-minimum-version-stays)** (owner, 2026-11-06): the three enums list the real roles and `roleName` is gone. The text below is the record of the superseded decision.

Context: Q-OPS-161 makes the registry's role the `--role` name (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`, `all`). Three enums of the
released contract list roles: `answeredBy.role` of the system information, `Replica.roles` and `EncryptionReplica.role`, each
closed at `web`, `worker` and `all`. R-ARCH-025 fails the compatibility check for a value added to a closed response enum
(oasdiff `response-property-enum-value-added`), and for an enum made extensible (`response-property-became-not-enum`); both were
run against the last release (`make compat-check`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The three enums keep their meaning as a role class, and the exact role is a new member `roleName` (chosen) | `roles` of an `api` or `packages` replica reads `["web"]`; `roleName` reads `api` or `packages`; `Replica.pool` is new too | Additive, so a client written against the last release keeps working and meets no unknown value; `replicas.roles` is a map and takes the exact names | Two members describe one fact; a reader of the registry's JSON example must know that `roles` is the class |
| (b) Add `api` and `packages` to the three enums | The document lists the values of Q-OPS-161 | One member | Fails R-ARCH-025 until the next breaking version of the API |
| (c) Make the enums extensible | `x-extensible-enum` | Future values need no break | The change itself is `response-property-became-not-enum`, which also fails |
| (d) Report `api` and `packages` as `web` and add nothing | No new member | Smallest change | The status screen cannot group by role, the point of Q-UI-107 |

**Choice:** (a). The class is `web` for every role that serves client endpoints (`api`, `packages`, the bridge `web`), `worker`
for `worker` and `all` for the development role (`roleClass` in [internal/api/v1/roles.go](../../internal/api/v1/roles.go));
the handlers set both members when they read the replica source, so the composition root needs no change for the role members.
`pool` is filled by the source (`internal/app/facts.go`), which holds the registry's value.

**Rationale:** the same precedent as Q-API-191 and Q-VULN-74: keep the closed enum, state the new fact in a new member. The
development agent would revisit this at the next breaking version of the API, where one member `role` with the five values is
the cleaner shape.

**Applied in the spec:** R-OPS-003 (the example, the class and `roleName`, the acceptance criterion), R-OPS-004 (`answeredBy`,
`replicas.roles`), R-UI-038 (the groups read `roleName`), R-API-038's acceptance criteria. Code: `api/openapi.yaml`
(`roleName` on `answeredBy`, `Replica` and `EncryptionReplica`; `Replica.pool`), `internal/api/v1/roles.go`,
`internal/api/v1/handlers.go` (`Summarise` keys by `roleName`), `internal/api/v1/encryption_api.go`. Tests:
`TestR_OPS_003_EveryReplicaIsListedWithItsOwnRole`, `TestR_OPS_004_SummaryPerRoleOfTheCut`, `TestR_OPS_004_RingsOfEveryRole`.

### Q-API-195 · The content routes are the files transfer behind a session check, and the UI's upload limit is a configuration key

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-API-025 and Q-UI-106 add `GET`, `HEAD` and `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{repoKey}/content/{path}` for the session cookie,
which reaches only `api`. Verified in the code: `PackageFile.path` is the `path` of the live file item of the version
(`PackageViewFiles`) and `PackageFile`'s repository is the one that holds it, so `contentUrl` is built from the pair like
`downloadUrl`; the CSRF check of a session (`session.Store.CheckCSRF`) reads the token header and the origin and never the body, so a
`PUT` that streams its body is checked like one that decodes JSON; `files.Service` reads stored items only and contacts no
upstream, so a path that is not stored answers `404` also in a remote repository. `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` did not exist as
a configuration key although R-UI-012 names it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One handler: the files handler serves both prefixes through `serve`, and the content routes add the session check and the upload limit (chosen) | `rawfiles.Handler.Content(limit)` registers three routes; the document lists them as operations tagged `files`, kept out of the generated interface because a path of several segments is no generated route | The decision of every request, `Range`, digests, content headers, blocking and statistics are the code of `/files/`, so a caller without `read` gets the same `404`; the document and the route table are compared in both directions | Folder index links and the directory index are those of `/files/` |
| (b) A second implementation in `internal/api/v1` | Generated routes with a query parameter for the path | Fits the generator | A second transfer path that can drift from the first; the path of an item in a query parameter is not what `contentUrl` promises |
| (c) Accept tokens on the content routes too | One route family for everything | Simpler for scripts | Token clients would put their bulk traffic on `api`, which Q-UI-106 keeps off it |

**Choice:** (a). A request whose credential is not the session cookie answers the `404` of an unknown path before the repository
is looked up or an index begun. The routes offer no `DELETE`. A path that ServeMux would redirect (an empty, `.` or `..` segment) is
redirected like on every route of `/api/v1/`; `/files/` answers it `400 invalid_path` because it registers an uncleaned handler for its
whole prefix, and the content routes cannot (the prefix is `/api/v1/repositories/`), which the UI never meets because it encodes
every segment. A `PUT` above `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` (default `100MiB`, `0` unlimited) answers `413` through a body reader that
fails at the first read of a declared length above the limit and when a body of unknown length crosses it; the deploy reads the body
only after it decided the caller, so a caller who may not deploy is refused first. The key is the new `ui.deploy` section of
[internal/config/ui.go](../../internal/config/ui.go).

**Rationale:** one transfer path is the property that keeps the two routes equal in authorization. The development agent would
revisit the redirect if a client of the content routes other than the UI appears, and the limit if installations want a per-repository
value (the repository's own `storage.maxUploadSize` still applies underneath).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-025 (the content row and bullet), R-API-029 (`contentUrl`), R-UI-012. Code:
[internal/api/rawfiles/content.go](../../internal/api/rawfiles/content.go), `internal/api/edge/links.go` (`ContentPath`,
`ItemView.ContentURL`), `internal/api/v1/document.go` (`ContentOperations`), `internal/api/v1/packages_api.go`. Tests:
`TestContentRoutes`, `TestContentRoutesAgreeWithTheDocument`, `TestSplitContentPath`, `TestDescribeItem`,
`TestR_API_029_PackageFileContentURL`.

### Q-API-196 · The mirror's state is the first of seven that holds, and a pass whose job waits in the queue is waiting

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-REPO-056 names seven states and says what the three of a pass in progress mean, but a row can satisfy several at once (a
paused mirror whose pass is in progress, a failing mirror whose bound is reached). Verified in the code: a job is `queued`,
`running`, `cancelling` or ended ([internal/jobs](../../internal/jobs/job.go)); a pass that a drain released is the same job
`queued` again with its attempt unchanged (R-REPO-053), and an exclusive enqueue finds a `cancelling` job as active.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Derive the state from the row, the configuration and the job in this order: `off`, `paused`, `failing`, `bound_reached`, `running`, `waiting`, `scheduled`; `running` is a job that is `running` or `cancelling`, any other job or none is `waiting` (chosen) | `mirrorStateOf` in [mirror_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/mirror_api.go) | One answer per row on every replica, no column the engine must keep in step; what an operator must act on (off, paused, failing, the bound) hides nothing behind a pass that is only running | A paused mirror with a running pass shows `paused` while the pass finishes its package |
| (b) `paused` and `failing` only when no pass is in progress | The pass shows first | The UI shows progress while a pause takes effect | A failing mirror that still has a pass in progress shows `running`: the alarm hides |
| (c) The engine writes the state into a column | One source | Cheap to read | A second state that the configuration (mode, pause) changes without the engine knowing; a stale value after a PATCH until the next dispatch |

**Choice:** (a). The pass and its counts are in the document whatever the state is, so a client that wants the progress of a paused
mirror reads `pass`.

**Rationale:** the state is the question "what does this mirror need from me", and the operator-facing conditions come before the
progress. The development agent would revisit the order if the Mirror tab needs "pausing" as a state of its own, which would be a
new member and not a new value of the closed enum (Q-API-191).

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the states). Code: `mirrorStateOf`.

### Q-API-197 · The pass names its job as a job reference, the summary of the last pass has one schema with the stored one, and a summary that cannot be read is none

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-REPO-056 shows `pass.job` as `{id, href}` and the last complete pass as a document of eleven members; Q-API-193
named the schemas `MirrorPass` and `MirrorCompletePass`. The engine stores the summary as `mirror_state.last_pass`, a JSON
document ([migration 00040](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00040_mirror.sql)); the migration does not say its members.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `pass.job` is the existing `JobReference` (`id`, `kind`, `state`, `href`), `null` once the job row is removed; the schema of the last pass is `MirrorPassSummary`, its members are the eleven of the example and the engine stores exactly them in `last_pass`; a summary that is missing, `null` or not a document with an `outcome` shows as `null` (chosen) | One schema for what the job API already returns; the UI links the job and reads its state without a second request | The client sees `kind` and `state` too: two members more than the example | The status never fails for a stored document it only shows |
| (b) A schema of two members | Exactly the example | A second job-reference schema | The UI cannot tell a running job from a queued one without reading it |
| (c) The id only | Smallest | — | The `href` is the contract of R-API-015 |
| (d) Answer 500 for a summary that cannot be read | Loud | The engine's mistake is seen | A status that cannot be read hides the failing mirror that the operator opens it for |

**Choice:** (a). The name of the schema is `MirrorPassSummary`, which replaces the name `MirrorCompletePass` of Q-API-193; nothing
was published under it. `docs/developer/mirror.md` states the members of `last_pass` for the engine.

**Rationale:** the job reference is the one way the API names a job (R-API-015), and the Mirror tab needs the state of the job to
tell a pass that runs from one that waits. The development agent would revisit (d) if the engine's tests do not pin the stored
shape; a decoder that falls silent is only as good as that test.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the example), Q-API-193 (the name). Code: `buildMirrorStatus`, `decodeLastPass`.

### Q-API-198 · The run enqueues first, so that the exclusive key answers whether a pass is queued or running, and writes the request after it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the run must answer 409 `mirror_pass_running` naming the job, record the request in `mirror_state.pass_requested_*`, enqueue
the pass and write `mirror.pass_requested`, atomically. Verified in the code: `jobs.Queue.Enqueue` inserts under the dedup key and,
when an exclusive job of the key is queued, running or cancelling, returns that job with `Created: false`; the refusal outcomes below
500 of an operation behind an `Idempotency-Key` are stored and replayed, so their transaction commits.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) In one transaction: enqueue; when the job exists, answer 409 with it and write nothing; else record the request and the event (chosen) | `enqueueMirrorPass` | The key decides, so two concurrent requests cannot both create a job; a refusal that commits under an idempotency key has written nothing | The job exists before its request is recorded (both commit or neither) |
| (b) Look for a queued or running job first, then enqueue | A query of the job table | Reads like the spec | A race between the look and the insert; a second statement that repeats the key's logic |
| (c) Record the request first, then enqueue | Spec order | — | A 409 behind an idempotency key commits the request of a pass that was not started |

**Choice:** (a). The other refusals (class, mode, pause) are answered before the transaction from the repository read of PostgreSQL
(Q-REPO-164), so they write nothing either.

**Rationale:** the exclusive dedup key is already the definition of "one pass per repository at a time" (R-REPO-053), and the API
asks it instead of reimplementing it. The development agent would revisit (b) only if the job queue stopped returning the existing job.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the run). Code: `enqueueMirrorPass`.

### Q-API-199 · The two operations decide their permission in the handler, a refused reader is hidden by the decision on read, and a project administrator runs on the manage it holds

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by [Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)**: the project right is the role, not a switch; the Maintainer and the Owner of the repository's project hold `manage` through their role and run a pass, the Owner reads the status, and `project_switch_off` and `projectAdmin: manageRepositories` are gone.

Context: R-REPO-056 admits for the status `repositories:read-config`, `manage` or an administrator of the repository's project, and for the
run `repositories:write-config`, `manage` or an administrator of the project with `manageRepositories`. The declaration forms
(R-API-008) express one capability, or one repository action; Q-OPS-155 decides such a disjunction in the handler under the
declaration `authenticated`. Verified in the code: the decision point answers a refused `manage` with 403 whatever else the caller
holds, and 404 only for a refused `read` ([internal/authz/decide.go](../../internal/authz/decide.go), `refusal`, R-AUTHZ-016); a
project administrator holds `manage` on every repository of its project, whatever the project's switches say (Q-AUTHZ-183,
`grantedBy`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Decide in the handler: the capability, the project right, then `manage`; a caller refused on `manage` who cannot read the repository and is not a configuration reader is answered by the decision on `read`, 404 when the repository hides its existence; a configuration reader is answered 403 (chosen) | `requireMirrorReader`, `requireMirrorWriter` | Every row of the table is one branch; a `manage` holder without `read` is no stranger; the answer for a hidden repository is the bytes of a missing one | A caller refused on `manage` costs two decisions, which the denial dedup window of R-OPS-015 keeps from doubling the events |
| (b) Declare `repositories:write-config` with `projectAdmin: manageRepositories`, as the upstream test does | The shared step decides | Nothing to write | The table's `manage` is lost: a team lead with `manage` on one remote could not run its pass |
| (c) Require the project's switch from a project administrator even though it holds `manage` | A second check on top of the decision | The switch means the same for a run as for a write | The decision point already gave `manage`; to ask the grant's source (`project:<key>`) would couple the API to how a grant came about, and the run changes no configuration |

**Choice:** (a). A project administrator with `manageRepositories` off may therefore run a pass; the 403 `project_switch_off` of an
update does not occur on the run. The switch gates what changes a configuration (R-AUTHZ-026), and the run changes none: it asks the
engine for what the settings already allow.

**Rationale:** the table of R-REPO-056 is the union of three rights, and the engine already makes the third include the second for
project administrators. The development agent would revisit (c) if the owner wants a run, which causes background download volume,
to need the project's switch (gap [H-531](../security/delegated-administration.md#h-531--a-run-can-be-requested-as-often-as-a-pass-ends)).
The cache entry list (R-REPO-032) decides the same disjunction with the decision on `manage` alone and so answers 403, not 404, where
the caller cannot read the repository; it is not changed here.

**Applied in the spec:** R-REPO-056 (the permissions), R-API-022. Code: `requireMirrorReader`, `requireMirrorWriter`, `hiddenOr`;
[delegated-administration.md](../security/delegated-administration.md).

### Q-API-200 · The format descriptor's `mirror` is a required boolean read from the catalog

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-021 lets the wizard offer the mirror only for a format whose remote can discover; the catalog fact is `Entry.Mirror`
(set by `formats.Register` from the optional lister interface, ADR-152). The descriptor of `GET /api/v1/formats` is built from
`formats.Descriptor`, which does not carry the fact.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A required boolean `mirror` in `FormatDescriptor`, read from `catalog.Default()` by the format's name; false for a format the catalog does not know (chosen) | `mirrorFact` | One source for the repository model and the UI: the model refuses `mode: mirror` by the same fact, so the wizard offers exactly what the save accepts; an addition to a response, which the compatibility check allows (R-ARCH-025) | A client that validates strictly and has no `mirror` member in its copy of the schema |
| (b) An optional member, absent when false | Smaller document | — | Every other member of the descriptor is required; the UI would test for presence |
| (c) A new member of `Descriptor` | The format declares it | — | A second statement of a fact that the registration derives, which can drift from it |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the UI must not hold a list of mirrorable formats (R-UI-021), and a fact that the model enforces is the one to offer.
The development agent would revisit (c) never: the fact is derived from the adapter's interface so that it cannot be declared
without being implemented.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021, R-API-022. Code: `ListFormats`, `mirrorFact`.

### Q-UI-108 · A pool without a live replica is named by its pool, because the registry does not say which queues it claims

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-038 asks for "No live replica claims the queues `<queues>`" for a worker pool. The replica registry holds the pool
name (`pool`) and no queue list, and a pool without any registry row is not known to the screen at all.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The warning names the pool: "No live replica in the pool `<pool>`" (chosen) | Shown while every row of the pool is `lost` | Needs no new data; the operator knows the pool and its queues from the values | Does not repeat the queues; a pool whose rows were pruned (24 h) shows nothing |
| (b) Add the pool's queues to the registry and the API | A column and a member | The text of the requirement | A migration and a contract change for a message; the registry would hold configuration |
| (c) No pool warning | Only the role-level warnings | Nothing to build | An empty pool, the case that matters, would go unnoticed for 24 h |

**Choice:** (a). The warning appears on the sub-group of a pool whose replicas are all lost; the role-level notices of `worker`
and `packages` (no live replica) are unchanged.

**Rationale:** the loss of a pool's last replica is visible for as long as its row exists, which is what the screen can know. The
development agent would revisit this if the API gets the pool's queues for another reason.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the pool notice). Code: `web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts` (`roleGroups`).
Tests: the specs `system-status-model.spec.ts` and `system-status.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-109 · The Download links use `contentUrl`; "Copy download URL" keeps the protocol URL

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-UI-106 lets the session cookie download and upload through the content routes of `api`. The file browser and the
package screen show a Download link and the browser a copy button for the address.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The link is the `contentUrl` of the item or version file; the copy button copies `downloadUrl` (chosen) | Two addresses, each for who uses it | The link works with the session on `api`; the copied address is what a token client can use on `packages` | None found |
| (b) Both use `contentUrl` | One address | Simple | A copied relative route that a token cannot use |
| (c) Both keep `downloadUrl` | No change | None | The link would need the session cookie on `packages`, which ignores it (R-ARCH-001) |

**Choice:** (a). The upload and the folder creation of the deploy dialog build their URL in one place, `contentPath` of
`web/src/app/api/files-api.ts` (R-UI-001); a file above `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` is refused by the dialog before it starts and
by the server with `413`.

**Rationale:** the UI never assembles a protocol URL (R-UI-001). The development agent would revisit this when a content origin
(R-ARCH-029) serves the downloads.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-012, R-UI-001's links rule, R-API-029. Code: `web/src/app/api/files-api.ts`,
`features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts` (was `features/browse/browse.html`), `features/packages/package-detail.html`. Tests: `files-api.spec.ts`, `repository-files.spec.ts`,
`package-detail.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-110 · The status screen groups by the replica's role and shows a role it does not know after the known ones

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the registry names one role per replica (`roles`, Q-ARCH-341); the screen keeps a group for a role it does not know.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The group of a replica is its role; a role other than `api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`, `all` is a group after them (chosen) | The screen hides nothing | A further role, or a registry of a newer release, never disappears from the screen | The screen has no text for such a role beyond its name |
| (b) Group by the class in `roles` | No new member needed | Works with the old data | `api` and `packages` would be one group `web`, which Q-UI-107 rejects |
| (c) Drop unknown roles | Only the known groups | Tidy | A running replica would be missing from the screen |

**Choice:** (a). The groups `api`, `packages` and `worker` always exist; `web` and `all` only while a replica reports them. A
sub-group heading is shown when a role has a pool, or more than one sub-group.

**Rationale:** an operator must see every replica the registry lists. The development agent would revisit this when a fourth role
exists.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038. Code: `system-status-model.ts` (`roleOf`, `roleGroups`). Tests: `system-status-model.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-111 · During the upgrade across the cut the UI falls back to `/files/` against a replica of the old shape

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
**Ended** on 2026-11-19 by [Q-HA-315](ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-315--the-charts-upgrade-bridge-across-the-cut-is-removed-the-binary-keeps-the-role-web-for-development-and-tests): no replica of the old shape can answer a Quader UI, so a
download link takes `contentUrl` only; the repeat of an upload on `/files/` was gone before.

Context: in the first step of the upgrade across the cut (R-HA-064) a UI bundle from a new pod can reach a `web` replica of the
previous release, which has no content route (Q-UI-106) and lists no `contentUrl`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Links take `contentUrl`, else `downloadUrl`; an upload or a new folder repeats its PUT once on `/files/` when the content route answers 404 `not_found` (chosen) | The old replica serves `/files/` with the session cookie | No step of the upgrade breaks the browser journey | One more request on that 404 |
| (b) No fallback | The UI uses the content routes only | Simpler | Uploads fail and Download links vanish until step 2 |
| (c) Pin the UI to the old routes until step 2 | A value switches the routes | Exact | A setting that exists for one upgrade |

**Choice:** (a). Only the unknown-path code `not_found` triggers the repeat; `repository_not_found`, 401, 403, 409 and 413 are
answered as they are, so the fallback never turns a refusal into a second attempt.

**Rationale:** the upgrade must keep the UI working in both steps. The development agent would remove the fallback once no supported
upgrade starts from the shape before the cut (R-ARCH-025).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-064 (the browser journey). Code: `web/src/app/api/files-api.ts` (`putWithFallback`), `repository-file.ts`
(was `browse.html`), `package-detail.ts` (`fileHref`). Tests: `files-api.spec.ts`, `repository-files.spec.ts`, `package-detail.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-112 · The repository wizard asks for the format first

Status: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-05.

Context: the wizard started with the class (local, remote, virtual) and offered the formats of that class second. Some features
are technically impossible for some formats (a format may lack a class, may have no settings for a class, and only some formats
can mirror a remote), so what the later steps offer depends on the format, not the other way round.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Class first, then the formats that implement it (as before) | The first question is what kind of repository | Familiar from the first prototype | The format decides what is possible afterwards, so the first answer limits nothing and the second is limited by it |
| (b) Format first, then the classes of that format (chosen) | The first question is which package type the repository serves | The choice that limits everything after it is the first one; the class step can say what the format cannot do | A user who thought in classes first answers a different first question |

**Choice:** (b), by the owner.

**Rationale:** some features are technically impossible for some formats, so the format is the first choice.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the steps, the class step's rule and its acceptance criteria). Code:
`web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-wizard.ts` and `.html`. R-UI-023 (quick setup) is unaffected.

### Q-UI-113 · A class the chosen format does not implement is shown disabled, with the reason

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Hide it | The class step lists only the format's classes | Nothing to explain | A user who looks for a virtual repository of a format without it cannot tell whether Quader lacks the feature or the format does |
| (b) Show it disabled with one sentence (chosen) | The card stays, cannot be chosen, and says "NuGet does not implement the class Virtual." | It teaches what the format cannot do, which is the reason the format comes first; the sentence is the description of the disabled radio, so assistive technology reads it | Three cards where one would do |
| (c) Show it enabled and refuse at the end | The server's 422 decides | No client logic | The user finds out at the last step |

**Choice:** (b). The reason names the format and the class and is the same sentence for every format; the descriptor says which
classes exist, not why one is missing, so the UI does not invent a cause.

**Rationale:** (a) removes the one piece of information the reordered wizard is able to give. The development agent would revisit
this when a descriptor carries a reason per missing class; the sentence then uses it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-wizard.html` (the class step), `repository-wizard.ts` (`supports`,
`unsupportedReason`). Test: `repository-wizard.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-114 · The format tiles are a listbox of `@angular/aria`; the icon is the one of the package list

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Native radio inputs in cards, as the class step | `input type=radio` in a label | Native arrow keys in every direction, no library | The grid is a picker of one of many with a filter; a radio group announces every tile as a group member even while filtered |
| (b) A single-choice listbox of `@angular/aria` (chosen) | `ngListbox` with `ngOption` per tile, explicit selection, horizontal orientation, one tab stop | The WAI-ARIA pattern for choosing one of many, filtered; R-UI-001 names the listbox for such widgets; a tile is not a form control | Arrow keys move along the row (Left and Right, on to the next row), not up and down; typeahead, Home and End work |
| (c) Buttons with `aria-pressed` | A toggle per tile | Simplest markup | One tab stop per tile (a long tab path), no arrow navigation |

**Choice:** (b), with `selectionMode="explicit"` so that moving over a tile does not change the format (a change resets
settings, Q-UI-116), and a click on the chosen tile keeps the choice. The icon is `formatIcon` (`shared/format-icon.ts`), the one the
package list shows in its type column: `extension` for NuGet and the neutral `inventory_2` for every other format; the UI holds no
list of formats (FMT-001). The name is the descriptor's `displayName`. *Since [Q-UI-225](#q-ui-225--a-format-shows-its-owners-logo-where-the-owners-terms-allow-it-else-the-neutral-glyph)
the icon is the owner's logo where its terms allow it (Debian, NuGet, OCI) and `inventory_2` elsewhere, rendered by
`<quader-format-icon>`; it is still the same function as the list's.*

**Rationale:** the wizard now has a picker of one of many that a filter shortens, which is the listbox pattern. Keyboard users move
with Left and Right, Home, End and typeahead, and the filter shortens the path. The development agent would revisit (a) if the
owner or a screen-reader user finds the missing Up and Down arrows a loss; the tiles then become radios in a CSS grid.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-wizard.html`, `repository-wizard.scss`, `shared/format-icon.ts`. Tests:
`repository-wizard.spec.ts` (the keyboard and selection specs).

**Revisited by [Q-UI-340](#q-ui-340--a-new-repository-is-a-format-chooser-and-one-form-as-the-references-new-project) (2026-11-12):** the tiles are links on a chooser page, one tab stop each, and Enter opens a format; the listbox and its explicit selection go with the steps. The icon stays the one of the package list.

### Q-UI-115 · The search field filters the tiles by name, in the browser

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Case-insensitive substring of the display name or the name, in the browser, with a live count (chosen) | `GET /api/v1/formats` is loaded once | The catalog is a few formats; instant; no request per key | None for the size |

### Q-UI-116 · Changing the format resets what no longer applies

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Reset everything after the format | Class, key and settings are cleared | Nothing stale | Typing the key and the description again for a format change |
| (b) Keep what still applies: the class if the new format has it, the key, description and access settings; clear the format settings and the mirror section (chosen) | The shared members of the document stay | Settings of one format are meaningless for another; the generic members are the same | A user who changed the format may not notice the cleared settings |
| (c) Keep everything | Settings travel along | Least work | A `latestGuard` of npm would be sent for NuGet |

**Choice:** (b). The class is cleared only when the new format lacks it, so the class step reopens empty.

**Rationale:** the format member and the mirror section are defined by the format's schema and flag; every other member of the
document is format-independent. The development agent would revisit (a) if the owner finds the partial keep surprising.

Within the form, another class keeps the identity fields ([Q-UI-341](#q-ui-341--the-class-is-a-radio-group-of-the-form-preset-to-local)).

### Q-UI-117 · The Mirror section: where it sits, what it writes, who may change it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Where | The class-specific step and a tab of the edit form; a step of its own | The class-specific step of the wizard (under the access settings and the format's settings), and a tab **Mirror** on the edit form of a remote of a format with `mirror: true`. The status of Q-UI-104 is a later addition to the same tab |
| What shows | Always every member; the members in mode `mirror` only | The mode always; the members in mode `mirror` only, so the default view is two cards |
| What a create writes | Every member; what differs from the default | Nothing in mode `pullThrough`; in mode `mirror` the mode and the members that differ from their defaults (R-REPO-050) |
| What an edit patches | A diff that may drop `remote`; a structural diff | The mode and the mirror object are always part of the compared document, so a merge patch carries only the changed members and a member set back to its default is cleared with `null`; the rest of `remote` (the URL, the credentials) is never part of the patch |
| Project administrator | Hide; read-only | The caller without `repositories:write-config` sees the section read-only except **Paused** and **Turn off** (the mode back to `pullThrough`), and cannot choose mode `mirror` (Q-REPO-142; the server answers `422 mirror_restricted` for anything else) |

**Choice:** the Mirror section in the remote's class step and edit form (moved since by Q-UI-344), its members shown in mode `mirror` only, a create that writes what differs from the defaults, an edit that patches the mode and the mirror object structurally, and a section read-only but for **Paused** and **Turn off** to a caller without `repositories:write-config`.

**Rationale:** a member written only where it differs follows Q-UI-80 and keeps a stored document equal to what the user decided;
the structural diff is what makes a patch of one member safe on a document whose other `remote` members the form does not edit. The
development agent would revisit the "members in mode `mirror` only" view if operators ask to prepare the settings before turning the
mode on.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `mirror-settings.ts`, `repository-model.ts` (`remoteOf`, `mirrorOf`), `repository-wizard.*`,
`repository-detail.*`. Tests: `mirror-settings.spec.ts`.

**Revisited by [Q-UI-344](#q-ui-344--where-the-details-go) (2026-11-12):** where the section sits: the group **Mirror** in **Advanced settings** of the creation form, with the format's own `mirror` member, and a closed section **Mirror** of the settings page. What it shows, writes and patches, and who may change it, stay.

### Q-UI-118 · The unbounded-mirror notice is an early warning with the server's rule

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No client check; show the server's `mirror_unbounded` after the save | Only the server speaks | One rule in one place | The user learns after the last step |
| (b) A notice under the mode that applies the bound rule of R-REPO-052 to the entered include patterns and the storage limit, while the server still decides (chosen) | `refused` (the format's well-known upstream) or `warned` (any other), in the words of the server | The user sees the refusal before it happens and what removes it | The rule is written twice (`Bounding` in `internal/mirror/discover`, `boundsMirror` in `mirror-settings.ts`) |

**Choice:** (b). The wizard has no upstream field, so a create takes the format's default upstream and the notice treats it as the
well-known one; the edit form compares the stored URL with the format's `defaultUpstreamUrl`. The server's answer at `/remote/mode`
is shown at the mode as well.

**Rationale:** an operator who chooses mirror for the public npm registry should not discover the bound requirement from a 422. The
development agent would revisit the duplicate rule if the catalog serves the rule's inputs.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `mirror-settings.ts` (`boundsMirror`, `unbounded`). Test: `mirror-settings.spec.ts`.

**Revisited by [Q-REPO-323](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-323--every-preset-is-a-well-known-upstream-for-the-mirror-bound) (2026-11-12):** `refused` applies to the URL of every preset of the format (`upstreamPresets`), the URL entered or, while it is empty, the default preset's; any other upstream is `warned`.

### Q-UI-119 · The status sits above the settings on the Mirror tab and is read only while the tab is open

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One tab: the status above the settings; the panel exists while the tab is open and reads the status every 5 s while a pass is in progress (chosen) | `GET …/mirror` when the tab opens, again every 5 s in the states `running` and `waiting`, after a pause, a resume, a run and a save, and never in the other tabs | What is going on comes first, the settings that explain it follow; no request for a tab nobody looks at; a finished pass stops the polling | A status that changes more slowly than 5 s is up to 5 s old |
| (b) The status below the settings | The same on one tab | The settings stay at the top where an administrator who edits expects them | The state, the one thing an operator comes for, is under a screen of fields |
| (c) A tab of its own for the status | Two tabs | Each tab is short | Two tabs for one repository's mirror, and the form's tab and the status's tab say different things about one state |
| (d) No polling; a **Refresh** button | The status is read when asked | No requests | An operator who watches a pass reloads by hand |

**Choice:** (a). The panel shows when the repository is stored in mode `mirror`; a form that has only just chosen the mode says that the status comes after the save.
The interval is the 5 s of the jobs screen (`JOBS_REFRESH_MS`); the polling stops with the panel because the panel is created by the tab (`matTabContent`).

**Rationale:** the status answers "is it working", the settings answer "why". The development agent would revisit (b) if administrators report
that they scroll past the status to reach the settings, and the interval if the status read becomes expensive on installations with many open tabs.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the bullet and the acceptance criterion). Code: `mirror-status.ts`, `repository-detail.html`. Tests: `mirror-status.spec.ts` (polling start, stop, refresh), `mirror-tab.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-120 · Pause, resume and run follow the permission of Save; the status follows the one of the form

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by [Q-AUTHZ-208](authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)**: the buttons show for whoever may save the repository, `repositories:write-config` or the role `owner` in its project; `manageRepositories` is gone, and an Owner without `repositories:write-config` keeps the read-only Mirror section of Q-REPO-142.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The buttons show for whoever may save the repository (`repositories:write-config`, or `manageRepositories` of its project, R-AUTHZ-026); the status shows for whoever sees the form (chosen) | `SessionStore.canWriteRepositories(project)` decides Pause, Resume and the run buttons | It is the permission of the API for a patch and for the run ("as an update", R-REPO-056); the UI already knows it, and a project administrator, who holds `manage` on the project's repositories, gets the buttons (Q-API-199) | A grant of `manage` on one repository through a policy, without the capability, is not known to the UI: such a caller sees no button and uses the API |
| (b) Show the buttons to everyone and let the server answer 403 | No decision in the UI | Never wrong about a grant the UI cannot see | A button that fails for most readers |
| (c) Ask the server first (a probe) | An extra request per screen | Exact | A request to learn what a refusal teaches |

**Choice:** (a). The status needs `repositories:read-config`, `manage` or the administration of the project, and the edit form shows the document to exactly those callers, so a
caller who sees the tab may read the status; a 403 or 400 of the status is shown in the panel as the error it is.
A project administrator pauses and resumes (the server's `mirror_restricted` lets `paused` through, Q-REPO-142), and the Mirror section stays read-only for them except **Paused** and **Turn off** (Q-UI-117).

**Rationale:** the same rule as every other write on the form keeps the screen consistent. The development agent would revisit it when the session
carries the per-repository grants of the caller (R-AUTHZ-010), which would let (a) see a `manage` grant.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `repository-detail.html` (`canChange`). Tests: `mirror-tab.spec.ts` (three callers), `mirror-status.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-121 · Pause is a patch of its member alone; a run answers with the job or with the reason

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Pause** and **Resume** patch `remote.mirror.paused` with the loaded `If-Match` and keep the other unsaved edits; a 412 settles like a save; **Run** shows the job and treats its 409s as answers (chosen) | The document's revision protects the pause (Q-UI-105); the form keeps its draft | The button does what a script does (INV-17); an edit in progress is not lost, nor saved by accident | The form's own **Paused** checkbox and the button are two ways to one member; both read the same stored value after the button |
| (b) Pause saves the whole form | One save | One code path | A click on Pause saves unfinished edits |
| (c) Pause as the form's checkbox only | No button | One way | The status panel shows the state but cannot act on it |

**Choice:** (a). After the patch the stored document is the new baseline and only the `paused` member of the form follows it. A 412 reads the stored
document: when it already says what the user asked (another administrator paused, or a retried write committed) nothing more happens; otherwise the conflict dialog of
R-UI-042 shows the difference and **Overwrite** sends the pause with the new `ETag`, **Reload** takes the stored document. **Run a pass now** posts `{"full": false}`
with a fresh `Idempotency-Key` and **Run a full pass** `{"full": true}`. The 202's job and the `job` of a `409 mirror_pass_running` are shown the same way: the sentence
("A pass is queued." or "A pass is already queued or running.") with its id and state and a link to the jobs screen filtered by the kind `mirror-pass`, because that screen has
no route per job. `mirror_off`, `mirror_paused` and `not_applicable` are shown in words at the buttons; every other failure is an error notice. The panel reads the status again after each.

**Rationale:** a refusal that the server's own state explains is information, not a failure. The development agent would revisit the link when the jobs screen gets a route per job (it would
open that job) and the double path for pause if the checkbox is dropped from the section.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021, R-REPO-056 (the UI line). Code: `repository-detail.ts` (`setMirrorPaused`, `takeStored`, `handlePauseError`), `mirror-status.ts` (`run`, `runError`). Tests: `mirror-tab.spec.ts` (pause, resume, 412 three ways), `mirror-status.spec.ts` (202, each 409, 400).

### Q-UI-122 · The upstream settings: where they sit, what the URL field holds, what is written

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Question | Options | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| Where | In the access step with the format's settings; a step of its own; the General tab | The class-specific step of the wizard, above the format's settings (so the Mirror section, which depends on the URL, follows it), and a tab **Upstream** on the edit form, for every remote repository whether its format can mirror or not |
| What the URL field holds | Empty with the preset as a placeholder; the preset as the value | The wizard starts with the preset as the value, so "Test connection" and the review show what is used; an empty field means the preset; a format without a preset starts empty and needs the address (the server answers `422` at `/remote/url` otherwise) |
| What a create writes | Everything; what differs from the preset and the defaults | The URL only when it names another upstream than the preset (compared as the server normalizes it), the authentication members only for an authentication other than none, a period only when it differs from the format's default, `availability` only when offline; nothing at all of `remote` when none applies (Q-UI-80) |
| What an edit patches | Whole objects; members | The URL always as entered, so a patch never depends on how the server reads a removed URL; `cache` and `availability` are always present as objects on both sides of the merge patch, so a member set back to its default is `null` inside the object and the members the form does not edit (`storeArtifacts`, `failureThreshold`, ...) are never nulled |
| The mirror's bound notice | The format's well-known upstream; the URL entered | The URL entered, or the preset while it is empty (Q-UI-118 compared the stored URL or assumed the preset) |

**Choice:** the upstream settings above the format's settings (moved since by Q-UI-344 and Q-UI-345), the preset as the URL field's value, a create that writes only what differs from the preset and the defaults, an edit that sends the URL as entered and `cache` and `availability` as whole objects, and the mirror's bound notice from the URL entered.

**Rationale:** a remote of a private registry, the case that needs a URL and a credential, is what a mirror is most used for; the form shows what the repository will do. The development agent would revisit the
split of the wizard's step if it grows past what one page carries once the extra hosts, the limits and the integrity members get fields.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `upstream-settings.ts`, `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamOf`, `initialUpstream`, `remoteOf`), `repository-wizard.*`, `repository-detail.*`, `mirror-settings.ts` (`upstreamUrl`). Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`.

**Revisited by [Q-UI-344](#q-ui-344--where-the-details-go) and [Q-UI-345](#q-ui-345--the-presets-are-buttons-with-names-and-the-pressed-one-follows-the-url) (2026-11-12):** where the upstream sits: the group **Upstream** of the creation form and an open section of the settings page, with the preset buttons above the URL, **Test connection** under the credentials and the periods, the further hosts and Offline folded into **Upstream details**. The URL field starts with the default preset's URL; what a create writes and what an edit patches stay, and the settings page also writes `extraHosts`.

### Q-UI-123 · The password is write-only: typed, sealed by the server, never read into a field or shown

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field starts empty; typing sends `{"value": ...}`; an empty field keeps what is stored; **Remove the stored password** sends `null`; the request shown on screen carries a placeholder; no draft stores it (chosen) | R-REPO-033 as the API states it: a read shows `{"set": true}` or the reference, never the value | A secret exists in the page only while it is typed; a save of another member cannot blank it | An administrator cannot see what is stored, which is the point |
| (b) Send `{"set": true}` back with every save | The document as read, sent back | Symmetric with the API's wording | The form would carry a member that is not a setting of the user's |
| (c) Show a masked placeholder in the field | Dots for the stored value | The user sees that there is one | A placeholder that looks like a value can be saved as a new password |

**Choice:** (a). A stored `secretRef` reads as a reference: the hint says so and the field replaces it only when a password is typed. The request body and the `curl` of the review and of the **API** tab show
`<the password>` instead of the value; the drafts kept across a sign-in (R-UI-042) never hold it; and **Test connection** uses only a typed password, because an unsaved test cannot refer to a stored one
(`{"set": true}` is `422 invalid_secret` there), which the page says.

**Rationale:** R-UI-043 keeps secrets out of storage and logs; the API already gives the shape. The development agent would revisit the removal
checkbox if the API grows an operation to rotate the stored secret.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021 (the criterion). Code: `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamOf`, `maskSecrets`), `upstream-settings.ts`, the draft handling of `repository-detail.ts` and `repository-wizard.ts`. Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-124 · Test connection probes the unsaved section and shows the answer in words

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `POST /api/v1/upstream-tests` with the format and the section as the form would write it, with the URL it would use; the result inline, in words, and gone when a setting changes (chosen) | What the repository would do, before it exists | Works in the wizard, where nothing is saved; the same call on the edit form shows the unsaved state | The edit form's test cannot use the stored password |
| (b) The saved repository's test (`POST …/upstream-test`) on the edit form | The stored section, with the stored secret | Uses the stored password | Cannot test a change before it is saved; a second code path |
| (c) A test only after the create | One path | Simple | The wizard cannot tell the user that the URL is wrong |

**Choice:** (a). The verdict is a sentence ("The upstream answered.", "The upstream answered and refused the credentials.", "The upstream could not be reached.", "The upstream answered with an error.")
with an icon, and green only for an answer with an accepted or no credential and a status below 400; the facts follow: the HTTP status, whether the credentials were accepted, the duration, the certificate
(subject, valid until) and the reason with its code (`dns_error`, `tls_untrusted`, `egress_denied`, `offline`, ...). The offline switch is part of what is tested, so an offline repository's test says `offline`, as the server does.
A refused test (403, 422) is an error notice.

**Rationale:** the section is what the user is about to save; the test of the saved one is the API's. The development agent would revisit (b) for the edit form when the API's unsaved test accepts `{"set": true}` of a stored repository.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: `upstream-settings.ts` (`test`, `outcome`), `repository-model.ts` (`upstreamTestBody`). Tests: `upstream-settings.spec.ts`, journey `14-mirror.spec.ts` (F-54).

### Q-UI-125 · The sign-in screen stands alone, and ?auto_sign_in=false waives the automatic sign-in

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

The sign-in screen showed the navigation sidebar of the shell, none of whose entries can be used without a session, and it
did so only when it was reached from a guarded route: opened directly at `/ui/login`, the shell stayed hidden, because the
session was never asked for. The owner asked for a sign-in page without the menu, laid out as one column (a form, then the
providers below "or sign in with"), for the automatic sign-in at the provider to be a chart setting, and for a URL parameter
that waives it even when it is on.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/login` and `/logged-out` carry `data: { bare: true }`; the root component renders none of the shell around such a screen, and none at all before the first navigation has ended (chosen) | The screen alone, in the middle of the page | The same screen whether opened directly or reached from a guard; nothing that cannot be used is shown | Two forms of the frame in one template |
| (b) Hide only the sidebar while no session is known | Top bar stays | Smaller change | The top bar's theme and sign-in controls are as useless before a sign-in; the direct/guarded difference stays |
| (c) A second root component for the screens without a session | Clean split | No condition in the shell | Two bootstraps or a router-level layout switch; the outlet moves and a screen is created twice |

**Choice:** (a). The router outlet stays in one place, so a screen is created once; a navigation that is cancelled (a
guard's redirect) does not decide the frame, the one that ends does. With anonymous access on, an anonymous visitor keeps
the sidebar on every other screen, because there its entries work.

The sign-in screen is one column of at most 25rem: the wordmark, the heading, the break-glass form when it is offered
(labels above the fields, a primary "Sign in" across the column), then the providers. Below the form a provider is a
neutral button with its display name under a divider "or sign in with"; without the form each provider is a primary
button "Sign in with <name>". "Continue without signing in" closes the column when anonymous access is on.

`?auto_sign_in=false` replaces `?local=1` with the same meaning: no redirect to the single provider of `autoRedirect`, and
the break-glass form shown whether or not `auth.break_glass.show_on_login_page` offers it. Only the value `false` waives
the redirect. `?local=1` is not kept as a second name: the installations so far are the owner's, and two parameters for
one switch would both have to be documented and tested. The automatic sign-in itself is `auth.login_page.auto_redirect`
(R-AUTH-009), which the chart already passed through; `values.yaml` now shows it as
`config.auth.login_page.auto_redirect`, and `values.schema.json` types it as a boolean, so Helm refuses another value
instead of a replica failing at start-up.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004 above, R-AUTH-009 and R-AUTH-014 in
[identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md). Code: `app.ts` (`bare`, `shell`), `app.html`,
`app.routes.ts`, `features/login/login.ts`, `features/login/logged-out.ts`, `_shell.scss` (`.bare`, `.bare-panel`),
`deploy/helm/quader/values.yaml`, `values.schema.json`. Tests: `app.spec.ts`, `login.spec.ts`, journey `01-sign-in.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-126 · Quader's own controls in place of Angular Material

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.** Built: the sign-in screens, the shell and the admin dashboard first, then
every other screen, the dialogs, tabs, checkboxes, menus and the tooltip, and the Material theme last
([Q-UI-153](#q-ui-153--the-last-material-controls-become-small-shared-pieces-on-the-cdk-and-angulararia)); `@angular/material`
is no dependency of `web/` any more.

The owner asked to leave the look of Angular Material for the design language of the sign-in page he showed: flat
controls, labels above the fields, a primary button in the accent, neutral grey secondary buttons. Measured on
2026-11-06: the forms were already native (147 `input`, `select` and `textarea` elements with Quader's own classes against
4 `mat-form-field`); Material remained in the buttons (253 uses in 81 files), the dialogs (28 files), the checkboxes (12),
the tabs (5), the menus (3), the tooltip (2), and the top bar and sidebar. `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` were
already dependencies.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Replace Material: Quader's own classes for the controls (`_controls.scss`), the behaviour of the composite widgets from the CDK (dialog, menu, overlay) and `@angular/aria` (tabs), screen by screen; `@angular/material` leaves `package.json` at the end (chosen) | The look is Quader's alone | Full control of the look; no ripple, state layer or MDC structure to fight; a smaller bundle; focus trap, keyboard handling and ARIA still come from the Angular team's packages | Every template with a Material control changes; the dialogs move to the CDK's API |
| (b) Restyle Material through its tokens and overrides | Templates stay | Fewer changes | The ink bar, the state layers and the dialog structure stay visible; every Material release can move the overrides; `main.scss` already carries many |
| (c) Only the sign-in screen and the shell | Small | Quick | Two design languages side by side until the rest is decided |

**Choice:** (a), in this order: the control styles and the sign-in screens first, then the buttons of every screen, the
shell (top bar, sidebar, menus, tooltip), the dialogs, the tabs and checkboxes, and last the Material theme, whose
`--mat-sys-*` tokens give way to Quader's. The colours stay those of Q-UI-88 and Q-UI-96 (cogpit's blue as the accent,
green for a positive status only); the controls take them from tokens of their own (`--quader-control-*`,
`--quader-accent-fill`, `--quader-btn-*`), so they no longer depend on Material.

The controls: one height (32 px) and radius (6 px) for buttons and fields; buttons `btn-confirm` (the accent), `btn-default`
(white with a hairline in the light scheme, filled grey in the dark one), `btn-tertiary` (text only), `btn-danger`,
`btn-icon`, with `btn-block` and `btn-sm`; text fields, selects and areas with a 1px outline of 3.2:1 and 3.4:1 (WCAG
1.4.11) and a semibold label above; native checkboxes and radios in the accent; a solid focus outline for every control.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-044 (contrast and focus unchanged), R-UI-046; R-UI-001's component-library bullet and the
density sentence of R-UI-002 name the result. Code: `_tokens.scss`, `_controls.scss`, `_dialog.scss`, `shared/ui/`; every
screen. Documented in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#controls) and
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#controls).

### Q-UI-127 · The admin area has a sidebar of its own behind an Admin button, and the shell takes the reference's frame

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

The owner asked for the administration to be separated from the rest of the navigation, entered through an Admin button
of the top bar that only its users see, and for the shell to take the structure and look of the reference he showed:
a top bar and a sidebar on one fill, the content as a panel set into them, the breadcrumb trail on top of the panel, and
a sidebar that collapses away instead of shrinking to icons.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two areas, one sidebar each: `/admin/…` shows the admin area's entries under the title "Admin area", every other route the content's; an Admin button in the top bar for every caller with `SessionStore.hasAdminArea()` (chosen) | The two kinds of work apart | The sidebar holds what belongs to the task at hand; the admin entries no longer push the content's down; the same rule as before decides who sees the admin area | One more click from a content screen into an admin screen |
| (b) Both areas in one sidebar, the admin area folded | One sidebar | No extra click | The separation the owner asked for is not there |
| (c) A separate admin application | Clean split | Independent | Two shells to maintain, a reload between them |

**Choice:** (a). The button reads "Admin" with a wrench icon and leads to `/admin`, whose guard opens the first admin
screen the caller may use (repositories, or projects for a project administrator); the logo leads back to the start page.
Who sees the button is who saw the Administration area before (any capability, or the administration of a project,
Q-AUTHZ-181), so nothing new is shown or hidden.

The owner's corrections of 2026-11-06, after the first draft: the Admin button keeps the reference's default button, at the
controls' full height and in the neutral fill, inside the admin area as well (the draft had made it small and tinted it in
the accent while the area was open; `aria-current` alone marks that now). And the link to the manual reads
"Documentation" next to its icon, not a bare "?". Below 768 CSS px both labels give way to their icons and remain the
links' accessible names. The breadcrumb bar is as high as the reference's: 40 px with its hairline, as measured on the
owner's instance (the owner had asked for 48 px "like GitLab"; 48 px is the reference's top bar, Q-UI-128).

The frame: one fill for the top bar and the sidebar (since Q-UI-128 the reference's `#ececef` and `#28272d`; light grey
`#f1f4f8` before, where the frame had been navy), the content as a panel on the page's fill with rounded corners, and the
breadcrumb trail as a bar on top of it. The top bar holds the mark and the name, the repository search in
the middle, then the project filter, the Admin button, the Documentation link, theme and the user's round badge; the name is in the badge's
accessible name and on top of its menu. The sidebar's title is the area's name; its entries are pills, the current one
tinted in the blue with its text in a deep or pale step of it and heavier (Q-UI-128; a bar in the accent before). "Collapse sidebar" at its foot hides it where it is pinned (the choice is
stored per principal, as the folded groups are), and "Open navigation" in the top bar brings it back; below 1024 CSS px it
is a drawer over the content with a backdrop, closed by Escape, the backdrop or a link. This replaces the icon rail of
Q-UI-68. The top bar, the sidebar and the menus are no longer Angular Material's (Q-UI-126): the menus are the CDK's
(`cdkMenu`, radio items for the theme and the project filter), the drawer traps the focus with `cdkTrapFocus`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002. Code: `app.html`, `app.ts`, `core/navigation.ts` (`areaOf`, `area`),
`core/nav-state.ts` (`collapsed`), `_shell.scss`, `_tokens.scss` (`--quader-nav-*`, `--quader-search-*`,
`--quader-mark-*`, ADR-199), `shared/brand/quader-mark.ts`. Tests: `app.spec.ts`, `app.projects.spec.ts`, `palette.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-128 · The reference's type, colours and measures

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.**

Context: in the review of the shell the owner found the Admin button harder to read than the reference's and asked for
the reference's colours, then, in its admin area: "Ich will dass du das Design (auch Schriftgröße) von hier übernimmst".
The reference is his own GitLab (19.0.1), which he opened in a browser window the development agent could read. Asked
whether that raises a legal problem: the values (colours, sizes, radii) are taken and written into Quader's own tokens;
GitLab's design tokens and component library are MIT-licensed (`@gitlab/ui`), its font is OFL-1.1, and no code, name or
logo of GitLab enters Quader.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The reference's values in Quader's tokens: colours of both schemes, the type, the measures of the frame, controls, cards and lists; a pair that misses WCAG AA is moved in its own hue (chosen) | Quader looks like the reference's admin area | One look across the owner's tools; values measured, not guessed; R-UI-044 holds | Quader's own colour (cogpit's blue, Q-UI-96) goes |
| (b) Only the type and measures, cogpit's colours kept | Half the reference | Quader keeps a colour of its own | Not what the owner asked |
| (c) GitLab's stylesheet or component library itself | Its CSS in Quader | Exact | Its CSS carries GitLab's class names and EE parts under GitLab's own licence; a second component system next to Q-UI-126 |

**Choice:** (a). The font, one decision of its own (owner, 2026-11-06): the reference's "GitLab Sans" is Inter with the
`cv05` form of the lower-case l; Quader ships Inter (`@fontsource-variable/inter`, OFL-1.1) with `cv05` switched on, so
the look is the reference's without its name in Quader (the options were GitLab Sans itself, or the system font as before).

What was measured, and where it went (the values per scheme are in [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#the-two-schemes)):

- Type: 14 px on 21 px at weight 400 for text and controls, 12 px for small text, sidebar entries at 425 and the current
  one at 500, headings at 600 with -0.01em tracking: page titles in the heading-1 size (24 to 30 px by the window's
  width), section titles in heading-2 (21 to 25 px).
- Frame: `#ececef` / `#28272d` around panels of the page's fill, 16 px round, 8 px from the window's right and bottom
  edge, no border; the sidebar 240 px wide, its title in the current entry's text colour, entries 28 px high and 8 px
  round with a 16 px icon in a 24 px box, the current one tinted in the blue (`#1f75cb` at 16 % / `#68a8e8` at 25 %) with
  its text `#0a335c` / `#cae0f7`; the breadcrumb bar 40 px with a hairline, its text 12 px; the search field 12 px round.
- Controls: 32 px, 8 px round, label weight 400; the default button white with a grey hairline / `#89888d` at 40 % without
  one, which makes the Admin button on the dark frame 7.0:1 where it was a fill barely set off from the frame; the confirm
  button `#1f75cb` / `#63a6e9`; menus white / `#28272d`, 8 px round.
- Cards: a strong fill (`#ececef` / `#3a383f`) 12 px round with 4 px inside, the title on it, the content on the page's
  fill 8 px round, rows with 12 px above and below and a hairline between.
- Lists (measured on the reference's Admin → Users): page titles at 30 px confirmed; tables without a frame on the page's
  fill, 16 px in every cell, the head at weight 600 in the heading colour between two hairlines, a hairline under every
  row; tabs with the current label at weight 600 over a 2 px line in the focus ring's blue (`#1f75cb` / `#428fdc`).
  Material's buttons and tabs, which most screens still use (Q-UI-126), are themed to these measures.
- Statuses (owner, 2026-11-06: "Status auf GitLab Standard umstellen"): a status is the reference's badge, a pill 20 px
  high with 12 px text and a 12 px icon, pale with deep text in the light scheme and full with near-black text in the
  dark one (success, warning, danger, info, neutral); every status of Quader (an icon and a word with `.ok`, `.warn` or
  `.bad`) is drawn as one, and the outlined tags of the screens became neutral badges. The content width stays the
  panel's (owner, the same day), where the reference centres a 1280 px column.
- Top bar, compared side by side with the reference at 100 % zoom: the Admin button 88 × 32 px with 14 px text, the
  avatar 32 px, 8 px between the actions.
- Links (owner, 2026-11-06, one decision of its own): underlined in running text, so a link there is not told apart by
  colour alone (R-UI-044, WCAG 1.4.1: the link blue is 1.5:1 against the text); in a table or a key-value list, where the
  column or the row says what is a link, underlined only under the pointer and on focus, as the reference shows them.
  The other options were the underline everywhere (as before) and nowhere (as the reference, which fails 1.4.1 in
  running text).
- Moved for WCAG AA (R-UI-044): the accent as text and focus ring is `#2f68b4` / `#66a8ea` (the confirm blue is 4.0:1 and
  4.49:1 on a filled field); the search field's outline is `#858489` / `#737278` (the reference's hairlines are 1.7:1
  against the frame, WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

- Icons (owner, 2026-11-06): Material Icons in the outlined variant, line icons like the reference's (the same font package
  and ligature names; the reference's own icon set was not taken, it is part of its identity).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (the breadcrumb bar). Code: `web/angular.json` (the font), `_icons.scss` (the outlined icons), `main.scss` (Material's
palette and type, the body, the page title), `_tokens.scss`, `_controls.scss`, `_shell.scss`,
`features/system/dashboard.scss`, `_list-screens.scss` (the data table), `features/audit/audit-log.scss` (the link button
in its table), the badges in `_controls.scss` (the screens' own tag styles removed). Tests: `palette.spec.ts` (the new surfaces: the
default button on the frame, the hover of the top bar and the menus, the search field, the card; the tab line; each
badge's text and icon on its pill; the positive badge is the one other green).

### Q-UI-129 · The project is the context of the content, chosen from your projects

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-06**, proposed to the owner with the membership of
[Q-AUTHZ-207](authorization.md#q-authz-207--a-user-or-group-is-a-member-of-a-project-with-a-role-and-the-role-grants-the-projects-repositories),
which he chose. Built (T-7).

Context: every repository belongs to exactly one project and is addressed inside it (Q-AUTHZ-206, Q-REPO-212), and a user is a
member of few projects, typically one to five; the platform team and the administrators see many. Today the project is a
filter of the top bar (R-UI-041), offered to administrators and project administrators only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The project as context (chosen) | The start page lists your projects; a project's screens live under `/projects/<key>/…` with a sidebar of the project (packages, browse, repositories, members, settings) and a project switcher at its top (recently visited, search); the top bar's project filter goes; the admin area keeps its lists over all projects | The address and the sidebar say which project you are in, as the reference shows a project; few projects make a short start page | Every content route moves under the project |
| (b) The project as a filter, as today, for everybody | The content screens stay global and filter by the chosen project | Fewer route changes | A repository's address contains its project (Q-REPO-212), the screens would not; the filter hides where you are |
| (c) A project picker at sign-in | One project per session | Simple | Switching projects means signing in again or a mode; most users work in more than one |

**Choice:** (a). A user with exactly one project starts in it; with several, on the list. A repository, package or file is
always shown inside its project; the admin area's lists name the project in a column.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (the side bars, the project switcher), R-UI-003 (the route table), R-UI-020, R-UI-021,
R-UI-041 (the start page, no project filter); the preference `projectFilter` of R-API-021 is removed (API, OpenAPI, column). Code:
`web/src/app/core/project-context.ts` (the project of the URL, the projects of the caller, the recent ones),
`core/navigation.ts` (`projectEntries`), `features/projects/` (`project-context.routes.ts`, `projects-home.ts`,
`project-switcher.ts`, `project-settings.ts`, `project-members-page.ts`, `project-list-pages.ts`), the content routes
below `/projects/:project`, `GET /api/v1/packages?project=`. Tests: `app.projects.spec.ts`, `app.routes.spec.ts`,
`core/breadcrumbs.spec.ts`; journeys 02, 03, 08, 09, 10, 12, 13 and 15 of `web/e2e`.

### Q-UI-130 · The auditor has an instance-wide vulnerability dashboard, under Your work

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06** (what) and **on 2026-11-18** (where and for whom, W-17: under **Your work** as the
