### Q-UI-700 · The active entry follows its identity when the list changes

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: finding F-131. The search field kept the active entry as a position. A newer answer that replaced the list while the
reader walked the old one (the text typed, its answer still on its way, Down pressed meanwhile) or the frequently visited
repositories that join the empty list once the server confirmed them (Q-UI-406) left the highlight on another entry than the one
the reader walked to. Enter opens the highlighted entry, so nothing opened unseen, but it was not the entry the reader chose. The
principal field (R-UI-150) dropped the active match with every answer, also where the answer still listed it. The WAI-ARIA
Authoring Practices name no rule for a list that changes without a key; their examples reset the active option when the text
changes, which both fields already do.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep the position | As built in the search field | Nothing to build | The highlight moves to an entry nobody walked to; Enter opens it |
| (b) No entry is active after every new list | As built in the principal field | Simple; nothing is active that was not walked to | A list that only gains entries (the frequently visited group, a match added) throws the reader back to the text |
| (c) The same entry stays active wherever the new list holds it; where it does not, no entry is active and the text is (chosen) | The entry's identity: what it opens (a repository by project and key, a package by ID, a page by route, an **All … for** line by kind and text, a principal by reference) | The reader stays where they were; nothing is active that they did not walk to; Enter does what it does without an active entry (the results page in the search, R-UI-098; the only match in the principal field, R-UI-150) | An entry that vanished leaves the reader at the text, one Down from the first entry |
| (d) As (c), and the neighbour of a vanished entry becomes active | The nearest entry | The reader stays in the list | The neighbour is an entry nobody walked to, and Enter opens it |

**Choice:** (c), in both comboboxes through one helper, `ActiveOption`
([active-option.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/active-option.ts)). An option's DOM id is derived from the entry's identity, not
its position, so `aria-activedescendant` keeps naming the entry when it moves and a screen reader does not announce a move as a new
entry; the polite live region says the new count (R-UI-097). A list that becomes empty leaves nothing active, and Down does
nothing in it. A held Down that meets a new list goes on from where its entry now stands.

**Rationale:** the active entry is the reader's choice in progress; only the reader moves it. The development agent revisits (d)
if readers of the walk lose their place where an answer drops the entry they stood on.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-097, R-UI-098, R-UI-150. Code: [active-option.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/active-option.ts),
[search-field.ts](../../web/src/app/features/search/search-field.ts),
[principal-field.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/principal-field.ts).

### Q-UI-701 · The pointer activates an entry only when it moves, and a held Enter acts once

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: F-131 has two more ways to an entry nobody walked to. A browser sends `mousemove` at the old position when the content
under a resting pointer changes or scrolls, so a new list, or the list scrolled to the keyboard's entry, gave the active entry to
whatever came to lie under the pointer. A held Enter repeats: after the first press opened an entry and emptied the field, a repeat
opened the results page of an empty text, and in the principal field a repeat could submit the form around it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) As built: every `mousemove` activates, every Enter acts | — | Nothing to build | The two ways above |
| (b) A `mousemove` at the position of the one before is ignored; a repeated `keydown` of Enter (`repeat`) does nothing but prevent its default (chosen) | Movement is the pointer's intent; a repeat is no new press | The keyboard's entry stays until the pointer really moves; one press, one action | A pointer that moves by less than a pixel does not count |
| (c) The pointer never activates; it only clicks | Keyboard alone moves the highlight | No conflict at all | The row under the pointer and the highlight disagree, and the pointer's hover is what a person expects to see |

**Choice:** (b), in `ActiveOption.pointer` and `heldEnter` of [active-option.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/active-option.ts),
for both comboboxes. **Rationale:** what the person did is what moves the highlight; what the page did is not. The development agent
revisits it if a pointer device reports the same position for a real move.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-097, R-UI-150.

### Q-UI-420 · The filters of a list open in a drawer from the right over the page

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)** for the drawer; the development agent built it from the options below; the owner
reviews the build at the walkthrough.

Context: W-6 of the walk of 2026-11-18. The filter panel stood beside a list where the list kept 71 rem and between its button and
the list where it did not ([Q-UI-327](#q-ui-327--the-filter-panel-sits-beside-a-list-only-where-the-list-keeps-71-rem-and-a-tables-columns-share-its-rows-width-without-the-scrollbar)),
and the list was rebuilt narrower when it opened. The owner: "extremely ugly"; "shall we try a drawer?". The app had no drawer for
content; the only one was the navigation's at narrow widths.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A drawer from the right over the page, the CDK dialog at the window's edge, as a shared component `<quader-drawer>` (chosen) | One behaviour at every width; the list keeps its width | The owner's choice; focus trap, Escape, focus return, the page that does not scroll and the modal role come from the CDK the dialogs already use; one component for the next content over the page | The drawer covers the right of the list while it is open; the set filters are read in the chips (Q-UI-422) |
| (b) The navigation's drawer, reused | One drawer in the app | Nothing new | It is the shell's, from the left, without a dialog role or a focus trap |
| (c) Keep the panel beside the list (Q-UI-327) | Two layouts | Filters and list side by side | The owner's verdict |

**Choice:** (a), [ADR-200](../decisions.md#adr-200--a-lists-filters-open-in-a-drawer-the-apps-one-pattern-for-content-over-the-page).
The drawer is 24 rem wide (the window's width below that), a backdrop dims the page, and it slides in and out with the panels' motion.
**Rationale:** the owner chose the drawer; building it on the CDK dialog gives every rule of R-UI-044 for free and the app one way to
put content over a page. The development agent revisits the width if a list's filters need more than 24 rem.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-100, R-UI-101; Q-UI-327 replaced. Code: [drawer.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/drawer.ts),
[filter-panel.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/filter-panel.ts), `.quader-drawer` in [_dialog.scss](../../web/src/styles/_dialog.scss).

### Q-UI-421 · The search by name is a field above the list, outside the drawer

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)**, on the development agent's proposal, for the field outside the drawer; its behaviour is
decided by the development agent from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field filters 250 ms after the last key and at once on Enter, through the list's own name filter, the text trimmed (chosen) | As the repository page's **Filter packages** | One behaviour for the two fields the owner compared; no button; a paged list asks once per settled text | A request per settled text on a paged list |
| (b) Enter only | No request while typing | Fewer requests | Unlike the repository page's field the owner named |
| (c) The field filters the loaded rows in the browser | Instant | No request | A paged list filters only what is loaded, which the style guide forbids |

**Choice:** (a). The field is as wide as a name (28 rem, R-UI-085), its placeholder and accessible name the job ("Filter
repositories"). A list whose API has no search by name has no field; a list whose only filter is the name has no drawer and no
**Filters**. The search text is not a chip; **Clear all** of the drawer keeps it, **Clear all filters** under an empty result clears
it too. **Rationale:** the owner asked for the field the repository page has; its behaviour is that field's. The development agent
revisits the delay if the paged lists load too often.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-100. Code: [list-head.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/list-head.ts).

### Q-UI-422 · A set filter is a chip beside Filters, and what does not fit folds into +N more

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)** that the set filters show beside **Filters** while the drawer is closed; the form is
decided by the development agent from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One chip per set filter, its name muted and its value, with a button that removes that filter; the chips that do not fit beside the button fold into one **+N more**, which opens the drawer (chosen) | One row at every width | Every filter is visible and removable in one click where it fits; the row never grows; the drawer shows every filter open | Measuring the row in the browser; at 390 px only one or two chips stand |
| (b) The chips wrap onto further lines | Every chip always visible | No measuring | Five filters at 390 px are four lines above the list |
| (c) One summary chip ("3 filters") | Short | One element | The owner asked for the filters, "hinted or in full"; a summary names none |

**Choice:** (a). A chip never breaks; it stays in the row's order; a value is the reader's word (**OCI (Docker)**, **High**,
**Last 7 days**). The removing button is named "Remove the filter Format: npm"; **+N more** is named "Show all 5 filters".
**Rationale:** it is the owner's "hinted or in full" in one rule: in full where the room is, hinted where it is not. The development
agent revisits (b) if the walkthrough shows that users miss the folded chips.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-100. Code: `ListHead.fit` in [list-head.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/list-head.ts).

### Q-UI-423 · The drawer's filters stand open; Apply closes it, and closing without Apply keeps what the list shows

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The filters stand open, one under the other, each a labelled field or a group with its legend; **Apply filters** applies and closes the drawer; a drawer closed otherwise forgets its staged values (chosen) | No folding in the drawer | A filter is one step away; the drawer is a short form; what the chips say is what the list shows | A long drawer for the vulnerability report (nine filters), which scrolls inside |
| (b) Closed sections, as in the panel | Folding | A short drawer | A click per filter, the cost the owner named |
| (c) Every change applies at once | No button | One step less | A paged list reloads on every checkbox |

**Choice:** (a). **Clear all** in the drawer's head removes the drawer's filters at once and keeps the search text. **Rationale:**
the sections cost a click each, and a drawer has the window's height for its filters. The development agent revisits (c) for a list
that is complete in the browser.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-101. Code: [filter-panel.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/filter-panel.ts); each list's `restage`.

### Q-UI-424 · A project's mark is one component, before its name wherever a project is listed

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)** for the mark in every list of projects; the component, its sizes and the rows that
name a project are decided by the development agent from the options below; the owner reviews them at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One component, `<quader-project-mark>`, its letter drawn by the stylesheet; 32 px beside a name with its key under it, 20 px beside a name of one line; a row that names its project shows `<quader-project-link>`, the mark and the display name (chosen) | One mark | The switcher, the suggestions and every list show the same mark; the letter is not part of the link's name (axe `label-content-name-mismatch`) | A row shows the project's display name, which may be longer than its key |
| (b) The mark in the lists of projects only, a row's project by its key | Fewer marks | Short cells | The owner: "wherever a row names its project" |

**Choice:** (a). The project column of the admin area's repository list and of the search's repositories and packages is 11 rem, so
**Platform engineering** stands beside its mark on one line; a longer name breaks inside itself beside the mark (Q-UI-425). The
switcher's button and its lists use the same component. **Rationale:** one icon of a project makes a project recognisable in every
place. The development agent revisits the 11 rem if a project's name is usually longer.

**The mark's colours (decided by the owner, 2026-11-18):** "ich hätte gerne, dass diese Projekticons weiß sind und bei Hover über
der Zeile bernsteinfarben aufleuchten wie die Farbe von unserem Icon." The mark is a stone of Quader's own mark
(`--quader-mark-stone`: near white in the dark scheme) with the letter in `--quader-mark-letter`; while the pointer is on the
row, the link, the button or the option that holds it, or the keyboard's focus is in it, it is the mark's coloured stone
(`--quader-mark-accent`), with the change over the motion duration of the tokens (none under reduced motion). Decided by the
development agent: in the light scheme the stone is the mark's dark stone, not white, because a white tile does not stand out
from a white page; the letter is the other scheme's stone and holds 3:1 on both grounds (`palette.spec.ts`). The accent fill
it had before made every list of projects a column of blue tiles beside blue links.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-102. Code: [project-mark.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/project-mark.ts).

### Q-UI-425 · An icon before a name has a column of its own in the cell, and a long name breaks inside itself beside it

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)** for the result (W-3); the pattern is decided by the development agent from the options
below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The cell `.icon-name`: a grid of the icon's column and the name's, the name breaking after a hyphen and, where a part is longer than its column, anywhere (chosen) | One pattern for every list | The icon and the start of the name share the first line in every row; a description stands under the name, aligned with it | A broken key reads in parts |
| (b) Keep the key on one line | No break | Whole keys | The list scrolls sideways at 1440 px (Q-UI-303) |
| (c) Cut it with an ellipsis | One line | Even rows | A name that cannot be read |

**Choice:** (a), for every list that puts an icon before a name: the repository lists, the search's repositories, the lists of
projects and a row's project. It replaces `th.wrap-name` there; lists without an icon keep it. **Rationale:** the owner's row had the
icon alone on the first line because icon and link were loose siblings; a column for each cannot do that. The development agent
revisits nothing here.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-102; Q-UI-303 revised. Code: `.icon-name` in [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss).

### Q-UI-426 · A project's repository list has no client address; its row offers Set up client

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-18)** that the address leaves the list (W-4: "useless at this place; without a guide or a
context it is worthless"); the columns and the row's action are decided by the development agent from the options below; the owner
reviews them at the walkthrough.

Context: this reverses the part of [Q-UI-330](#q-ui-330--a-list-takes-its-columns-from-the-job-of-its-kind-of-user-the-important-properties-are-columns-and-the-address-takes-no-more-than-its-share)
that kept the address field in a project's list, and the list rows of R-UI-065, Q-UI-300 and Q-UI-301. The address stays where its
context is: the repository's page and the client setup.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Repository** (the visibility icon, the key, the description as its muted second line), **Format**, **Class**, and at the row's end **Set up client** as a quiet button beside the menu (chosen) | The name cell of every repository list | One name cell for the project's list, the admin area's and the search's; the repository takes the room the address left; the setup is one click from the row | The description is read under the key, not down a column |
| (b) The description as a column of its own (the development agent's first proposal) | Five columns | The description scanned down a column | Prose squeezed into a narrow column at 1024 px; the project's list would differ from the admin area's and the search's |
| (c) No row action | The menu only | Simple | The address had been the row's reason to be copied; the setup is where that job went |

**Choice:** (a). **Set up client** opens the repository's page Set up client (`…/repositories/<key>/setup`, R-UI-120; revised
when the Guides package was merged, 2026-11-18, which removed `/setup`), its accessible name ends with the key; it keeps the quiet
form of a row's action ([Q-UI-487](#q-ui-487--set-up-client-is-a-default-button-on-a-page-and-a-quiet-row-action-in-a-table-row)). The search's repository rows lose their copy button for the same reason (Q-UI-430). The admin area's list
keeps its quiet copy button and its menu's **Copy client address**: an administrator hands addresses out, and the owner's objection
named the project's list. With no address column left in a list, the address share (`fill`, `--quader-address-share`,
`--quader-address-chars`, `--quader-list-others`, `td.address-cell`) and the render report's check of address widths go.
**Rationale:** the owner's verdict; a repository's address is copied where its client is set up. The development agent revisits the
admin area's copy button with the guides that open from a repository (W-2).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-065, R-UI-066; Q-UI-300, Q-UI-301, Q-UI-330 revised. Code:
[repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html),
[data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts).

### Q-UI-427 · A table keeps no room for a scrollbar its rows do not need

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Revised in part by [Q-UI-1110](#q-ui-1110--the-page-is-the-one-thing-that-scrolls-a-lists-head-scrolls-with-it)**: no table scrolls by itself any more, so the "Against" of (a) is gone; no gutter is reserved, as chosen.

Context: every table ended 15 px before the right edge that the head of the list, the tab line and the separators above it reach
(`home`, `repository-npm-local`, `packages`, `profile-tokens`, `search-results`). The cause, one for all: the data table's scroll
region kept the room of its scrollbar (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`) whether its rows scrolled or not, so that the address column's
share could be taken of the rows' width (Q-UI-327).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No reserved gutter (chosen) | The table reaches the edge | Every table ends where the lines above it end; nothing measures the rows' width any more (Q-UI-426) | A table whose rows scroll has its scrollbar at that edge, over the last 15 px of the table |
| (b) Keep the gutter, pull the lines above in | Same edge | The scrollbar has its room | Every head, tab line and separator of every list changes |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the gutter served the address share, which is gone. The development agent revisits nothing here.

**Applied in the spec:** Q-UI-327 replaced. Code: `.table-scroll` in [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss).

### Q-UI-428 · The report's cells keep a qualified name, a fixed version and a time on one line

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: in the vulnerability report every row was three lines high because cells broke: **Fixed in** read "None / yet", the
repository `web-frontend/` / `npm-vendor`, and the time of detection "2 minutes / ago" (Q-UI-380 let these break).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The qualified name, each fixed version, "None yet" and the time are whole; a list of fixed versions breaks between versions (chosen) | Short rows | A row is as high as its summary; nothing reads broken | The identifier's column, with its summary, gets less room |
| (b) Restructure the report | Other columns | Room | Not decided by the owner (the report by package and version is open) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a name or a short phrase is never broken (the style guide); the summary is the prose that may wrap.
The development agent revisits the identifier's 10 rem (Q-UI-392) if a triager's list at 1280 px scrolls sideways.

**Applied in the spec:** Q-UI-380 revised. Code: [vulnerability-report.html](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.html),
[_vulnerabilities.scss](../../web/src/styles/_vulnerabilities.scss).

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: on the profile's tokens the cell **Scope** broke into four lines ("All repository permissions of the owner, without
administration") while the column **Token** was mostly empty; **Created via** said `ui`, a technical fact in the plain user's main
view; the row's actions were an icon without a label (rotate) and a word (**Revoke**).

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Scope** takes the room the others leave, **Token** keeps 10 rem; **Created via** is no column; **Rotate** and **Revoke** are two quiet buttons with their words (chosen) | Five columns that decide and **Created** (`narrow`) | The scope reads in two lines at 1440 px; nothing technical in the main view; one pattern for the two actions | How a token was made is read in the audit log only |
| (b) **Created via** behind a disclosure per row | Kept | The fact stays in the list | A pattern no other list has (Q-UI-332 (c)) |
| (c) The actions in a menu | One button | Room | The plain user's one frequent action behind a menu |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the scope decides whether a token stays; how it was made does not. The development agent revisits
**Created via** if administrators miss it in the token administration.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-029; Q-UI-332 revised. Code: [token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/token-table.ts).

**Revised by [Q-UI-563](#q-ui-563--a-column-is-as-wide-as-its-content-what-never-breaks-declares-no-width-and-the-columns-that-wrap-share-the-room)
(2026-11-18):** the scope no longer takes all the room: the token and the scope share it by their content, so the administrator's
long token descriptions no longer break into three lines beside a short scope.

**Kept by [Q-UI-641](#q-ui-641--a-credentials-revoke-is-never-in-a-menu-a-token-row-keeps-its-two-words) (2026-11-18):** the two
words are the one allowed case of two words in a row under the rule of R-UI-163.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: three ways to write a time across lists: "4 minutes ago" (the packages), "Nov 18, 2026" (the packages of a repository, the
tokens, the admin area's last activity), "Nov 18, 2026, 8:17:21 AM" (the files of a repository, the users' last sign-in); and two

| (b) The date everywhere | One form | Stable pictures | "When did this change" needs arithmetic |
| (c) The date and time everywhere | One form | Exact | Wide cells, the cause of broken rows |

absolute="title">` is a list's cell. The lists of this change use it; a screen that formats a time with the date pipe follows when it

**First published** as a fact), the version page (its line of facts with the absolute time in brackets, its repositories as a list),
the items of a repository and their versions (they wrote "Nov 18, 2026" and "Nov 18, 2026, 8:17:21 AM") and the files of a folder. **Rationale:** one rule a reader learns once. The development agent revisits the log's form if the owner wants
relative times there too.

### Q-UI-451 · A version's address is the package's with `@` and the version

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That the
version has an address of its own is the owner's (2026-11-18).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `…/packages/{format}/{name…}@{version}` (chosen) | `@team-a/ui@1.4.0`, `portal/web@1.4.0` | Reads as an npm install spec; one segment more for nobody; no format's names hold an `@` after their first character and no format's versions hold one, so the last `@` of the last segment separates them | An image is written `name:tag` by its clients, here `name@tag`, where OCI writes a digest |
| (b) `…/{name…}/-/{version}` | npm's tarball separator | No character of a name can be confused | A segment that means nothing to a reader |
| (c) `…/{name…}/versions/{version}` | A word | Readable | An image name may have a segment `versions`; the split is ambiguous |
| (d) Today's `?version=` | A query parameter | No route change | Not an address of the version's own: the owner asked for one |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** readable, sendable, unambiguous for every format Quader has. No redirect from `?version=`
(pre-alpha, no backward compatibility). The development agent revisits it when a format's names or versions may hold an `@`.
**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-003, R-UI-111; [package-links.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-links.ts),
[packages.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/packages.routes.ts).

### Q-UI-452 · The versions are searched, sorted and paged in the browser over the whole list

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The page reads every version once (pages of 500), the grades in one request; search, sort and paging in the browser (chosen) | One list in memory | Every column sorts, including grade and last fetched, which the server does not; the search answers at each key; finding one version among hundreds needs no round trip | A package of thousands of tags reads them all before the table shows |
| (b) Server-side search and sort | New list parameters | Scales to any count | A sort by grade or last fetched the API does not have; a request per key |
| (c) Search only, no sort | The field alone | Simple | The second question, "which versions are worst", has no answer |

**Choice:** (a). The table shows 50 rows and **Load more** adds 50. **Rationale:** the server already computes the whole list for
each page of it (R-API-029), so one sweep costs less than paging it. The development agent revisits it when a package with more
than 5,000 versions takes longer than a second to show. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-110.

### Q-UI-453 · Pre-releases and distribution tags are marks in the row; no switch

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every version is a row; a pre-release carries the mark **pre-release**, a version a tag points at the tag as a badge, `latest` first (chosen) | Marks | One list; the search finds `rc` and `latest`; the owner's objection to the checkbox | A package with many nightly pre-releases has many rows |
| (b) Pre-releases behind a switch, as before | The old checkbox | Shorter list | The control the owner found in the way; a version searched for may be hidden |
| (c) A column **Tags** | Its own column | Aligned | Empty in most rows of every format but npm |

[Q-UI-1130](#q-ui-1130--an-image-is-one-row-with-its-tags-on-the-opened-item-and-on-the-packages-page): an image's row is the image, led by

### Q-API-295 · A version's last download and its downloads are the fetches of it by the format's rule, read with the version rows

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That a
row says when the version was last fetched is the owner's (2026-11-18); that it is the last fetch of the version by a client and
the downloads count those, for every format and class, is the owner's (2026-11-19, W-24). Revised on 2026-11-19: until then (a) read
the lead item alone, which left a remote OCI tag (no lead item) at "Never", a Debian version at the downloads of its first
architecture, and a local OCI tag pulled by digest at none.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The statistics of the version's lead item alone | One join | Cheap | Wrong where the lead is not what clients fetch: a remote OCI tag has none, a Debian version has a file per architecture, a pull by digest is no download of the tag item |
| (b) The statistics of the version's fetch items, by the rule its format declares (`VersionFetch`: lead file, any file, document by name or digest), summed and the latest taken in a lateral subquery of `PackageViewVersions` and `PackageViewList` (chosen) | Read from what is stored | No new table; one statement for the whole list; each format names what its clients fetch | The rule of the document is a match by bytes under the package's path, which a format declares and the core states once |
| (c) A statistics row per version, written at each download | A table of its own | Cheap to read | The serve path must know the version of each item (an OCI manifest's tags), a write on the download path, a second copy of what the item statistics hold |

**Choice:** (b). **Rationale:** the item statistics of R-STOR-015 hold every download; what differs per format is which of them belong
to a version, and that is the format's knowledge, declared once in the contract (Q-API-340). The development agent revisits (c) if a
format's fetch cannot be named by items of the repository. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-065, R-API-079, R-API-029.

### Q-API-340 · The format contract declares what a fetch of a version is

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That the rule
holds for every format, built and future, is the owner's (2026-11-19: "Alles was wir hier für OCI besprechen gilt auch für alle anderen
Registries die bereits gebaut sind und für zukünftige Registries").

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A required declaration in the descriptor, `Descriptor.VersionFetch` (`FetchLeadFile`, `FetchAnyFile`, `FetchDocument`); `Validate` refuses a format with a package view without one; a test of `formats/all` pins each format's rule (chosen) | One fact per format | A future format cannot register without deciding it; the statements read the rule as data | The contract version rises (5, ADR-205) |
| (b) An optional method of the view adapter that returns the fetch items | Code per format | Any rule | An optional method is forgotten; the list's per-package count would need a second pass |
| (c) The core's own rule (the lead item, else every linked file) | Nothing per format | No contract change | Counts the provenance bundle and the `.nuspec` as downloads, and still misses a pull by digest |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the three rules cover the six formats, and a declaration that `Register` checks is the one thing a new
format cannot skip. The development agent revisits (b) when a format's fetch is not one of the three. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-079,
[architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, [decisions.md](../decisions.md) ADR-205.

### Q-API-341 · `sizeBytes` is null when the size is not known, and `sizePartial` marks a size of the parts held

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That a size that
is not known is shown as not known, not as 0 B, is the owner's (2026-11-19).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `sizeBytes` nullable, `sizePartial` boolean, both required (chosen) | Two members | The natural JSON of "not known"; a client that reads a number cannot mistake a partial sum for the whole | A client must handle `null` |
| (b) `sizeBytes` absent when not known | One member less | Smaller | Optional members are easy to miss; the generated types make it `undefined` |
| (c) A size object `{bytes, partial, known}` | One member | Self-describing | Breaks every reader of `sizeBytes` for one format's case |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-080, R-API-029; `api/openapi.yaml` (`PackageVersionSummary`, `PackageVersion`).

### Q-API-344 · The management API keeps its classes; on the protocol paths only package_write stays, in Enforce

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The model
is the owner's (W-26, 2026-11-19); the border is the development agent's. Revised on 2026-11-19 by the owner's
[Q-LIM-4](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-4--in-audit-nothing-on-a-protocol-path-is-refused-or-slowed-the-package-classes-of-r-api-016-included) (b): in Audit nothing on a protocol path is refused or slowed.

Context: the owner's figures count every request to a repository. R-API-016 had classes for `/api/v1/`, `/files/` and
`/api/<format>/` and none for `/v2/` (finding F-155), keyed by the token ID first, so every personal token had a budget of its own,
against the owner's rule that a PAT counts against its user.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/api/v1/` keeps `read`, `write`, `anonymous`; the package classes cover every protocol path, keyed by the subject, `package_read` and `package_anonymous` only in mode `audit`, `package_write` always | The figures of [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) take over the protocol paths in `enforce` | No installation loses its request limit by updating | Contradicts the owner's Q-LIM-4: the classes refuse in Audit |
| (b) `/api/v1/` keeps `read`, `write`, `anonymous`; `package_read` and `package_anonymous` are removed; `package_write` stays for unsafe methods on every protocol path, keyed by the subject, in mode `enforce` only (chosen) | The figures alone limit reads in `enforce`; nothing limits a protocol path in `audit` | One mechanism for reads; the key follows the owner's rule; Audit refuses nothing, as the owner holds | In `audit` nothing bounds protocol requests (H-1015); the default mode is therefore `enforce` |
| (c) Keep the package classes in both modes beside the figures | — | — | Two limits on every request in `enforce`, with different keys and numbers; refusals in Audit |

**Choice:** (b), since Q-LIM-4 (first (a)). **Rationale:** [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-3, Q-LIM-4 and
Q-LIM-27.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-016 (the border, the class table, the configuration, the acceptance criteria), R-API-082.

### Q-API-354 · A PUT that creates takes no If-Match, and requires it when it replaces

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `PUT /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/limits/maximum` sets a project's first maximum or replaces it (R-LIM-033, 201 or 200).
R-API-012 requires `If-Match` on every PUT of a resource that carries a revision `ETag`, and `If-Match: *` passes only when the
resource exists (RFC 9110 section 13.1.1). A first maximum has no `ETag` a client could have loaded: the operation as built answered
428 without the header and could never be called correctly for a create (the render seed and the maximum dialog both send none).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The create takes no `If-Match`; a replace requires it (428 without, 412 for a stale one); an `If-Match` sent where nothing exists answers 412 (chosen) | The operation declares the optional `If-Match` and documents 201 and 428 | RFC 9110's semantics of `If-Match` on a missing resource; a concurrent second create meets the stored version 0 rule and answers 412 | One more form of declaration besides required and exempt |
| (b) A create sends `If-Match: *` | — | One rule | `*` means "exists" in RFC 9110 and fails on a missing resource |
| (c) A separate `POST` creates | — | The general create | A second operation for one singleton |

**Choice:** (a). The declaration test of R-API-012 knows the form (`ifMatchOnReplace` in
[ifmatch_test.go](../../internal/api/v1/ifmatch_test.go)). **Applied in the spec:** R-LIM-033 of
[usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md). Code: [limits_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/limits_api.go) `SetLimitProjectMaximum`.

| (a) Without `project`, `projectRole: owner` admits a caller that may administer at least one project it is an Owner of; the handler decides on the project the request names (chosen) | The reader role already meant "a member of any project" without a project source | One declaration form, the same rule for both roles; the handler keeps the narrow check | The shared step admits an Owner the handler may still refuse |
| (b) The operations declare `authenticated` and decide everything in the handler | — | No change of the shared step | The capability's audit of a refusal is lost; the declaration test of R-API-008 no longer reads who may call |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-008. Code: `projectRoleAdmits` in
[authorize.go](../../internal/api/v1/authorize.go), tested in `TestR_AUTHZ_026_TheDeclarationOfAProjectRole`.

### Q-API-356 · A project without a maximum is read as 200 with `maximum` null

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/limits/maximum` answered 404 for a project without a maximum (R-LIM-033). That is the
ordinary state of a project, and the project's settings read it on every load, so every page load showed a failed request in the
browser (the full render run of 2026-11-19, `project-settings` as Owner and administrator). The API's other optional singleton, the

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The read answers 200 with `{"project": …, "maximum": null}` and no `ETag` while none is set, the maximum and its `ETag` once set; 404 stays the answer for a project that does not exist (chosen) | `LimitProjectMaximumState`; the client's `maximum()` returns null for it; the first maximum is set without `If-Match` (Q-API-354) | The ordinary state is an ordinary answer, as the banner's; "none" and "no project" are told apart | The read's body wraps the maximum the `PUT` answers bare |
| (b) The page learns it from an answer it already has | The instance's projects list (`GET /api/v1/limits/projects`) carries it | No read | That list is for `limits:read` at the instance, not for an Owner; the dialog still needs the `ETag` |
| (c) Keep 404 and allow it in the renders | — | No change | A failed request on every load of a project's settings |

**Choice:** (a). The project's settings and the tab **Projects** read it through the one client method. **Applied in the spec:**
R-LIM-033 of [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md). Code: `GetLimitProjectMaximum` in
[limits_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/limits_api.go), `LimitsApi.maximum` in [limits-api.ts](../../web/src/app/api/limits-api.ts),
tested in `TestR_LIM_033_AProjectsFirstMaximumTakesNoIfMatch`.

### Q-API-357 · A registry request without a credential that is answered with the challenge is not charged either

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the download limits count the registry's paths below `/v2/` since R-LIM-005, and a new instance enforces them (Q-LIM-4).
Every registry client sends its first request without a credential to learn the token endpoint from the `401` (R-OCI-004): the
version check `GET /v2/`, and with some clients every request. The rule of Q-API-290 read only the `/api/<format>/` addresses, so
these requests were charged to the client address under the profile Anonymous and answered `429` at its limit. Seen in Test and
Release 44625189982 (2026-11-19): the OCI conformance suite, one address, got `429` for 31 first attempts and failed; a build farm
behind one address is the same case. A client that receives `429` where it expects the challenge does not sign in.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The rule of Q-API-290 for the registry: the version check `/v2/` and a path below `/v2/<project>/<key>/` of a repository the index holds with artifacts that are not `public` are not charged when they carry no credential (chosen) | `ChallengedByLevels` reads both address forms | One rule for every format (the owner's rule that a decision taken at one format holds for all); costs a decision in memory, as Q-API-290 measured | An address can send unbounded challenged requests, bounded by stage 4 only, as on `/api/<format>/` |
| (b) Charge them, with a higher request figure for Anonymous | — | No exemption | No number separates a build farm's first attempts from abuse; the client still fails at the limit |
| (c) Answer the challenge at the limit instead of `429` | — | The client signs in | A second meaning of a refusal; the request is still counted against callers who read without a credential |

**Choice:** (a). Charged as before: a repository the index does not hold (its decision may ask PostgreSQL), a repository with
`public` artifacts (the request is served), the token endpoint `/v2/_token` (its own limits) and the catalog `/v2/_catalog`.
**Applied in the spec:** R-LIM-005 of [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md). Code: `ChallengedByLevels` in
[ratelimit.go](../../internal/api/v1/ratelimit.go), tested in `TestR_API_016_ChallengedByLevels` and by the OCI conformance suite
of the integration tests.

### Q-API-360 · The well-known repositories have operations of their own beside the repository document

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

(owner, 2026-11-20). The repository document already has `disabled`, `visibility`, `remote.url` and the account members.

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/api/v1/upstream-repositories` with an item per repository and operations for the state, the level, the address and the account, and two bulk operations; the document stays readable and takes the narrowing settings (chosen) | R-API-083 | Each operation carries its own rule: the override flag and the reset, the account's host rule for every caller, the bulk in one transaction, the product's address beside the stored one | Two ways into one row: the operations and the merge patch of the narrowing settings |
| (b) Everything through the document of `/api/v1/projects/upstream/repositories/{key}` and two bulk sub-paths there | One document | Fewer operations | A merge patch of `remote.url` cannot say "reset to the product's"; the item the page needs (state, product address, `listedBy`) is not the document |

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One transaction; the answer lists the repositories it changed and a `bulkId` that every event carries (chosen) | All or nothing | A refused level (restricted, no anonymous door) leaves nothing half done; one audit filter finds the bulk | One slow repository holds the transaction (a dozen rows, not slow) |
| (b) Best effort per repository, one result each | As `batch-delete` | Partial progress | A half-switched installation after an error |

**Choice:** (a). `Idempotency-Key` is accepted, so a retried request after a lost answer does not run twice.

**Rationale:** the set is small and bounded by the catalog; an administrator expects "all" to mean all. The development agent would
revisit this if a catalog grows past a few hundred presets.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-083; [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-068, R-REPO-073.

### Q-API-362 · A caller without `repositories:read-config` gets 403 on an item of the well-known repositories, as on the collection

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-REPO-073 asked for 403 on `listUpstreamRepositories` and 404 on `getUpstreamRepository` for a caller without the read
capability, "as for a hidden resource" (R-AUTHZ-016), and R-API-083 declares both operations with `repositories:read-config`. A
permission declaration is decided by the shared authorization step before the handler runs, and its refusal is 403
([authorize.go](../../internal/api/v1/authorize.go)): the two statements cannot both hold.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The declaration decides: 403 on the collection and on an item (chosen) | `x-quader-permission: {permission: repositories:read-config}` on both reads | The shared step enforces what the document declares, and the declaration test of R-API-008 sees the capability; the keys of the project `upstream` are the product's and the same in every installation, so a 404 would hide nothing | The item's refusal differs from the 404 of a repository hidden from its caller |
| (b) 404 on an item: `{authenticated: true}` and the capability checked in the handler | As R-AUTHZ-016 for a hidden resource | One answer for every unseen item | The declaration no longer names the capability the operation needs; the handler repeats the shared step's work for a resource whose existence is public |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** R-AUTHZ-016 hides that a resource exists from a caller who could learn something from it; which well-known repositories
exist is written in the catalog of every release and in this specification. The development agent would revisit this if a well-known
repository ever has a key that only one installation has (T-21b's own registries, should they ever join the project).

**Applied in the spec:** [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073 (the permission bullet and the acceptance
criteria); R-API-083 (unchanged: the declarations were already these).

### Q-API-363 · The item counts the listing virtual repositories and their projects, and an answer about one repository names them

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the question before a switch-off reads "3 virtual repositories in 2 projects list it" (R-UI-187), and the details of a
well-known repository list them "by qualified name, as links, as far as the caller reads them, and the number of the others"
(R-UI-188). The item of R-REPO-073 carried `listedBy`, a number and nothing else, so the page could say neither.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `listedBy` and `listedByProjects` on every item; `listedByNames` on every answer but `listUpstreamRepositories` (chosen) | The list counts; `getUpstreamRepository`, the writes and the bulk answers also name, in byte order, at most 100 | The list stays three queries whatever the number of repositories (the rows, their facts, one count that also counts projects); a write's answer replaces the item the details show, so a switch-off from there keeps the names without a second read | One bounded query more per repository a write answers |
| (b) The names on `getUpstreamRepository` only | As (a), the writes answering the numbers | The fewest queries | The details page loses the names after a write of its own, or reads the item again |
| (c) The names on every item, the list included | One shape everywhere | No absent member | The list's cost grows with the virtual repositories of every team, for a page that shows numbers |
| (d) An operation of its own, `GET /api/v1/upstream-repositories/{key}/listed-by` | — | The item keeps its shape | One more operation and one more request for one bounded list |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the names are those `repository.disabled` records already (Q-REPO-383), from the same query and with the same bound,
so `listedBy` minus their number is the number of the others. "As far as the caller reads them" holds for every name: each operation
of R-API-083 needs `repositories:read-config`, which reads the configuration of every repository of the instance. The development
agent would revisit the bound if a page ever needs more than 100 names; a page then reads the virtual repositories through the
repository search.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-083; [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073 (the item).

### Q-API-364 · A writer of a virtual repository reads the state and the level of a format's well-known repositories through an operation of its own

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the member picker of a virtual repository lists every well-known repository of its format that is not retired, with the
badge **Not switched on** or **Switched off**, and an active member at `private` says its own sentence (R-UI-189). Its caller is the
Owner of a team's project, who holds no `repositories:read-config`; no read answered them the state or the level. Whoever writes a
member list learns both already: listing `upstream/<key>` answers the warning `member_inactive` on the save and `upstreamState` in
the resolution explanation, and the explanation's `no-read` tells whether the caller reads the member (R-REPO-072).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/upstream-repositories` with a schema of its own, for whoever holds `repositories:write-config` and the Owner of any project (chosen) | `UpstreamRepositorySummary`: `key`, `name`, `displayName`, `state`, `visibility`; nothing of the address, the account or who lists it | The callers are the ones who write a member list, and they learn nothing they could not learn by listing a key; the declaration form exists (`{permission, projectRole: owner}` without a project, [Q-API-355](#q-api-355--projectrole-owner-without-a-project-admits-an-owner-of-any-project)); under the format no reserved key of the project `upstream` is added (R-API-004) | One operation more |
| (a') The same operation for every signed-in caller | `{authenticated: true}` | The simplest declaration | A reader, a user flagged external, a service account or a CI token would learn the state and the level of repositories they can neither list nor read |
| (b) The repository summaries of the project `upstream` shown to every signed-in caller, with the state | — | No operation more | Changes what a repository list hides, in the path every project uses |
| (c) The UI's fallback stays | — | Nothing to build | Contradicts R-UI-189: "Not switched on" and "Switched off" are not told apart, and a repository the caller does not read is not shown |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the read answers exactly the callers who could find each answer out by writing a member list, and nothing those callers
could not find out; that a preset exists was public already (`GET /api/v1/formats` lists the presets of every format). An anonymous
caller gets `401`, a signed-in caller who holds neither the capability nor an Owner's role `403`. A system repository is never a
member (R-REPO-070) and a retired one is not offered (R-REPO-071), so neither is listed. The development agent would revisit the
callers if a role other than the Owner's ever writes a member list.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-083; [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073; [authorization.md](authorization.md)
R-AUTHZ-041 (who reads the state); [security/visibility.md](../security/visibility.md).

### Q-API-274 · Package names: a whole-name prefix on a C-collation B-tree and word prefixes on a GIN tsvector, without pg_trgm

### Q-API-283 · The package statements take the name prefix as two bounds and are planned for their text

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-API-064 as planned read statement A with `LIKE <escaped q>%` and left the plans to PostgreSQL. Quader's connections
prepare their statements (`QueryExecModeCacheStatement`), and PostgreSQL may switch a prepared statement to a generic plan after
its fifth run. The `EXPLAIN` of the integration area `search` showed statement B's generic plan walking `packages_name_lower` over
every package for a rare word, and a generic plan cannot derive index bounds from a `LIKE` parameter at all.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Statement A as the range `low <= lower(name) < high` computed in Go; both statements after `SET LOCAL plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan` in their transaction (chosen) | Every run planned for its text; the range is a value pair, not a pattern | The planner picks the GIN for a rare word and the ordered B-tree walk for a common one; no escaping; the range serves a generic plan too | One statement more per request (a `SET LOCAL`), and a plan per run |
| (b) The planned `LIKE` and the default plan cache | As written | Nothing new | A generic plan reads every package for a rare word, after five requests |
| (c) Statement B as a subquery that takes the first 200 matches unordered, then orders them | No plan setting | Bounded read in any plan | Which 200 matches are read is not defined; the generic plan still chose a walk over the primary key |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the bound of R-API-064 must hold on the fifth request as on the first, and only a plan for the text
can choose the cheaper of the two indexes. The development agent revisits it if a request of the suggestions shows up as slow in
the planner's time.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-064 (the package row, the bullets on operators and on planning, the statement count);
[search.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/search.sql) `SearchCustomPlans`, `SearchPackagesByPrefix`.

### Q-UI-485 · The explanation follows the snippets: what the class is stands open, the rest is folded under its headings

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
**Revised by [Q-UI-805](#q-ui-805--the-guide-is-a-list-of-closed-rows-under-one-heading)** (2026-11-20): the owner's variant A closes
the first section too.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) After the steps: the introduction of the sections `what` and `endpoint` open (the rest of each under **More about this**), every other section a closed disclosure titled with its heading, in topic order (chosen) | The headings are the contents | The owner's order (the job, then what the class is and the troubleshooting); one scan of short headings; headings in order | A section the reader needs is one click away |
| (b) Each section under its step (configure and authenticate under Configure, …) | Explanation beside its snippets | Close to the snippet it explains | The steps grow long again; a disclosure inside a step breaks the heading order |
| (c) The whole guide open after the snippets, with a contents list | Today's text, moved | Nothing hidden | The dense prose the owner rejected, only lower |

**Choice:** (a). The first render showed npm's open section "What a virtual repository is" at 25 lines of dense prose below two
snippets, the largest element of the page; its introduction is three lines. **Rationale:** what only some readers need is behind a
disclosure (CLAUDE.md), and the class's introduction is what every reader of the explanation came for. The development agent revisits it if readers open the same folded section on most
visits: that section then stands open.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-125, R-UI-049.

### Q-UI-486 · A long line of a snippet wraps, and its continuation is indented

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a key like `release-candidates-for-the-customer-portal-frontend` makes every address line of a snippet longer than the
block at 1024 px and far longer at 390 px.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Wrap; a wrapped line continues two characters further right; copy copies the text as it is (chosen) | Every character visible | Nothing is cut off, at no width; a wrapped line does not look like a new line of an `.npmrc` | A wrapped URL is broken visually |
| (b) The block scrolls sideways (today) | Lines stay whole | The text looks like the file | At 390 px the end of an address is hidden and only a scrollbar hints at it |
| (c) Wrap without indentation | Every character visible | Simple | A wrapped line reads as two lines of the file |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a command the reader cannot see whole cannot be checked before it is run. The development agent
revisits it if a format's snippets depend on visible column alignment.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-125.

### Q-UI-487 · Set up client is a default button on a page and a quiet row action in a table row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The
owner asked on 2026-11-18 for one label and one look. Revised when the four packages of the walk were merged (2026-11-18): the
first choice, the default button everywhere, met two other looks built at the same time, the blue button beside the address in the
repository's header (Q-UI-517) and the quiet text action in a project's repository list (Q-UI-426).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `btn-default` everywhere, the rows of a table too (the first choice) | One look | The same in every place | A grey button in every row of a list draws more than the row's name; the style guide gives a row's actions the quiet form |
| (b) The confirm button everywhere | One look | Prominent | A column of blue buttons in every list; the blue is the commit of a form or a dialog |
| (c) Blue in the repository's header, grey elsewhere | Two looks | Prominent where it is the page's job | The two looks the owner objected to |
| (d) `btn-default` on a page and in a header (the repository's header, an empty state, the start page's recent repositories, the install panel, the packages list's header); in a row of a table the quiet form of a row's action, `btn-tertiary`, its accessible name ending with the key (a project's repository list, the repositories behind a format's tile) (chosen) | One look per place | A row's action looks like every row's action ([ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#buttons-and-dialogs): quiet for anything repeated down a list); the rows stay calm; nowhere blue | Two forms of one action, by where it stands |

**Choice:** (d). No **Set up client** is blue: it opens a page and commits nothing. **Rationale:** the owner objected to one action
looking different on two screens of one kind (the grey button of the packages list against the blue one of a repository); a page and
a table row are two kinds of place, and each keeps the form the style guide gives it. The development agent revisits it if readers
miss the row's action in a list.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-126, R-UI-052, R-UI-124; Q-UI-426, Q-UI-517 and Q-UI-514 revised. Code: `row-setup` in
[repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html) and
