[repository-content.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.html).

### Q-UI-488 · The format tiles take the page's width

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: seen in the first render of the four packages together (2026-11-18): the tiles stood in a grid of at most 56 rem, so at
1440 px the six installed formats showed as five tiles and one on a second row, with the right half of the page empty, on Guides and
on the format chooser of a new repository.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The grid takes the page's width, a tile at least 9.5 rem; empty tracks keep a tile at that width when there are few formats (chosen) | As many tiles in a row as fit | Six formats in one row at 1440 px; no rule that knows the number of formats | At 1024 px with the side bar open four and two |
| (b) Balance the rows: as many columns as make the rows equal | Three and three | No lone tile at any width | The tiles stay narrower than the page for no reason; a count of columns per number of formats |
| (c) As before | — | — | The lone tile |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the tiles are the page's only content, so they may use its width; the room the cap kept empty was the
defect. The development agent revisits it if a seventh format leaves one tile alone at 1440 px.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-127. Code: [format-tiles.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/format-tiles.ts).

### Q-API-310 · The guide's snippets travel beside its sections, and a reader's guide holds what the reader can do

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a section of topic `configure` or `install` carried the snippets of its tab, the publish snippets none (npm's publish
section named no tab). The merged page shows every snippet first and the prose below.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `Guide.snippets` with every tab; sections without snippets; `GuideSection.Snippets` leaves the format contract; the guide of a repository leaves out publishing for a reader who may not publish (chosen) | One list of snippets, one list of sections | The page lays them out as it needs; no snippet twice; the publish snippets are there; the format declares less | A breaking change of the answer and of the contract (no compatibility before the first stable release) |
| (b) Keep the sections' snippets; the page ignores them | No API change | Nothing moves | The page receives the configure snippets twice and the publish snippets never |
| (c) Put the guide's sections into the client setup's answer | One request | One answer for the page | The install panel's answer would carry prose; two jobs in one operation |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the page decides the layout, so the answer carries the parts, not a layout. The development agent
revisits it if a format needs a snippet that only one section explains.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-053, R-API-070; [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008 (the contract) and kit check 8.

### Q-API-330 · The forms read the levels a caller may choose from an operation every signed-in caller may call

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The brief
of W-11 ruled out making the forms call an administrator's endpoint.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `GET /api/v1/visibility-choices` for every signed-in caller (chosen) | The default, the restricted levels, whether the caller may choose them, whether `public` is available | One read that answers exactly what a form needs, also the `publicAvailable` the repository forms never had; the project dialogs stop reading `settings:read` | One more operation |
| (b) Members of `GET /api/v1/authz/me` | The caller's capabilities already travel there | No new operation; the session store holds it | The session store keeps it for the session, so a change of the settings shows only after a new sign-in; `authz/me` describes the caller, not the installation |
| (c) Open `GET /api/v1/settings/visibility` to every signed-in caller | One operation | Nothing new | It lists every public object of the installation, an administrator's summary |

**Choice:** (a), with the permission `authenticated` and listed among the reads a token whose scope does not inherit its owner's
rights may call (`ownerRightsReads` in [owner_rights_test.go](../../internal/api/v1/owner_rights_test.go)).

**Rationale:** a form opens, reads what it may offer and offers it; (a) is that read and nothing else. The development agent would
revisit this if more per-caller form rules appear, which could join one "form rules" read.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-076, R-UI-141.

### Q-API-331 · `restrictedLevels` is a set that a merge patch replaces whole

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An array of levels; a merge patch replaces it; duplicates count once; answered in the order of the levels (chosen) | RFC 7396 for arrays | The settings stay one merge-patch document with one `ETag`; a client sends what the checkboxes show | Two administrators who tick different boxes at once: the `If-Match` of R-API-012 refuses the second |
| (b) An object of three booleans | `{"private": false, "internal": false, "public": true}` | Each member patchable alone | A shape no other level member has |
| (c) Operations to add and remove one level | `PUT`/`DELETE …/restricted-levels/{level}` | Fine-grained | Two operations for three checkboxes, and the default's rule spans both members |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the UI saves the section in one patch (R-UI-140), and the rule against the default needs both members in one write.
The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-075; `VisibilitySettingsPatch` in `api/openapi.yaml`.

### Q-API-332 · One audit event carries both settings before and after

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `settings.visibility.changed` with `defaultLevel` and `restrictedLevels` in `before` and `after` (chosen) | One event per write | A reader of the audit log sees the whole state on each side; a patch of both members is one event | An event whose default did not change carries it anyway |
| (b) An event per member | `settings.visibility.restricted_changed` beside the existing one | Narrow events | One write, two events; a filter for "who changed the visibility settings" needs both types |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the settings are one document with one version; its audit event describes the document. The development agent records
no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-056, R-API-075; [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-036.

### Q-API-335 · The admin area's fields search through the suggestions, which gain service accounts and the avatar

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-12. Outside a project every field that names a principal is on a screen of the admin area (R-UI-152), whose caller holds
`identities:read` (every role that holds `roles:write`, `identities:write`, `policies:write`, `ci:write`, `tokens:read` or `audit:read`
holds it too, R-AUTHZ-010). The field needs, per text, the users with display name and avatar, the groups and the service accounts.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The suggestions of R-API-060 with the kind `service_account` and the user's `avatarUrl` (chosen) | One request per settled text for every kind the field asks | One read with ranks over the username and the display name; the permission and its 403 before any lookup exist; a fixed number of statements | The suggestions now serve two fields |
| (b) The identity lists with `q` (`/users`, `/groups`, `/service-accounts`) | Up to three requests per text | No change of the API | The user list matches the e-mail address and not the display name, so "Swa" finds people by their mail domain and misses "Swantje"; full records with the e-mail address travel for a row that shows none |
| (c) A new operation for the admin area's principal search | A dedicated read | Its own shape | A second ranking of users and groups beside R-API-062 |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the suggestions already answer "which users and groups match this text" to exactly the callers of
these screens; adding the service accounts and the avatar is the whole gap. The development agent revisits it if a field outside the
admin area must name a principal without a project (none does today).

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-078, R-API-060, R-API-061, R-API-062, R-API-064, R-UI-150.

### Q-API-336 · The project lookup answers the row's display name and avatar, finds the project's service accounts and matches words

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The rule
that no caller gains a search it did not have before is the development agent's correction of 2026-11-18 to its first brief for W-12,
which had opened the search to every internal user.

Context: inside a project the field searches the lookup of Q-AUTHZ-182, which answered the kind and the name of users and groups whose
name starts with the text. The owner's row needs the display name and the avatar, and "Swa" must find "Swantje Wagner", whose
username may be `s.wagner`. A project policy names the project's service accounts too, which the lookup did not offer.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Extend the lookup: a user's display name, ID and avatar path; words of the display name and of the names match; the project's own service accounts, the instance-wide ones for `identities:read`; no disabled principal, no break-glass account, no auto-join group (chosen) | Same callers, minimum, limit and rate limit | The row the owner asked for from the read an Owner already has; the accounts the Owner already lists; nothing offered that the write would refuse | Display names become readable by prefix to every Owner (H-392, widened) |
| (b) Keep kind and name only | As before | No widening | A row of usernames, not the owner's row; no service account |
| (c) An open search for every internal user | GitLab's model | Every member could suggest | A new enumeration surface; withdrawn |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the Owner already names these principals with this read; showing their faces and names is what makes
the choice reliable, and the e-mail address, status, origin and sign-in times stay with `identities:read`. The development agent
revisits it when the identity provider's directory can answer the lookup.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-077; [authorization.md](authorization.md) Q-AUTHZ-182 and H-392 revised.

### Q-UI-510 · A folder and a file are the repository's page at `files` and their path

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The
direction, files on the repository's page and no Browse, is the owner's (2026-11-18, W-8,
[ADR-203](../decisions.md#adr-203--browse-goes-a-repositorys-files-live-on-its-page)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `…/repositories/{key}/files/{path…}` for a folder and a file alike (chosen) | One matcher route below the repository; `files` alone is the root | A file has an address of its own that reads as its path; a name that ends in a file extension stays a page of the app (the dev server's proxy rule for such paths, [proxy.conf.mjs](../../web/proxy.conf.mjs)) | A word in the address that the path could also hold (a folder named `files` is `…/files/files`) |
| (b) The query parameter `?path=` on the repository's address, as the generic list had it | No new route | Nothing to match | A file has no address that reads as one; the breadcrumb cannot name the folders; the old list's behaviour of opening folders in place had no way back but the trail |
| (c) GitLab's `…/-/tree/{path}` and `…/-/blob/{path}` | Two routes, folder and file told apart by the address | The kind is known before the item is read | Two addresses whose difference the user has to know; a link to a path whose kind changed (a file replaced by a folder) breaks |

**Choice:** (a). The page reads the item at the path once (`GET …/items?path=`) and shows a folder or a file by its kind. A generic
repository's root is its own address (`…/repositories/{key}`), which every link to the root uses; `…/files` without a path shows the
same root and is what a package format's **Files** opens. The document title is the last segment of the path (or **Files** at the
root). **The path stands on the page once** (revised on the coordinator's review of the renders, 2026-11-18): the breadcrumb ends
at the repository, whose step stays a link (`data.belowTrail` of the route, `Breadcrumbs.belowTrail`), and the page's path below
the header carries the folders and, on a file's page, the file ([Q-UI-521](#q-ui-521--the-path-of-a-folder-or-a-file-stands-once-and-its-middle-folders-collapse-where-it-is-narrow)). The first build added one breadcrumb
step per folder as well, so a folder deep in the path stood twice on the screen and a file's name three times, and at 390 px the
two took eleven lines before any content.

**Rationale:** the owner's direction makes a file a place inside its repository; its address should say so. One way back up
through the folders is enough: the page's own path, next to the content it names. The development agent revisits (c) if a link to a path is often opened as the wrong kind.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-003 (the route table), R-UI-010, R-UI-052. Code: [repositories.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repositories.routes.ts)
(`filesMatcher`, `filesTitle`), [breadcrumbs.ts](../../web/src/app/core/breadcrumbs.ts), [project-links.ts](../../web/src/app/core/project-links.ts)
(`filesCommands`), [help-topics.ts](../../web/src/app/core/help-topics.ts). Tests: `filesMatcher` in [misc.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/misc.spec.ts),
the route map of [app.routes.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/app.routes.spec.ts), [breadcrumbs.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/breadcrumbs.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-511 · A package format's raw files are a page behind **Files** in the header menu

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: npm, NuGet, OCI, Debian and Ansible list packages as their content; their raw files (tarballs, `.nupkg`, manifests and
blobs, pool files) are how Quader stores them. A user rarely needs them; an administrator who cleans up or a support case does.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Files** in the header's `more_vert` menu, opening `…/files` with a way back to the list (chosen) | Details on demand, in the place Browse files had | The main view stays the packages; one click for who needs the files; the same page and operations as a generic repository's | A menu item is found only by who looks for it |
| (b) A tab **Files** beside the list | Visible | Found at once | A tab in every reader's main view for what readers do not need; R-UI-052 has no tabs (Q-UI-321) |
| (c) A section **Files** at the end of the page | On the page | No new address | A second long list on one page; the files of a large repository load for every reader |

**Choice:** (a). The page of a package format's files says in one muted sentence that these are the raw files as Quader stores them,
with a back link named after the list (**Packages**, **Images**). A virtual repository's **Files** lists only what it stores itself
(the generated index files of a Debian or Ansible virtual repository, Q-STOR-180) and says that its members' files are on their pages.
The repository list's row menu offers **Files** too, for every format (for a generic repository it leads to the same root as the key).

**Rationale:** "simple by default, details on demand" (CLAUDE.md): the files are a detail of a package format. The development agent
revisits (b) if users of a format look for its files often enough that the menu is a detour.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052, R-UI-010. Code: [repository-content.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.html),
[repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html). Test: "R-UI-052 a package format keeps its packages as the page" in
[repository-files.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-512 · The operations stand where they act, and only for who may use them

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A folder's operations in its toolbar (**Upload files**, **New folder**, and **Delete folder** in its menu), a file's on its page (**Download**, **Delete**), each shown only after the permission check at the page's path (chosen) | Actions on the object the page shows | The reader's page has no control it cannot use; one way to each job; no per-row menu to scan | A file is deleted from its page, one click further than from a row |
| (b) A menu on every row with the operations of that entry | Browse's toolbar per row | Delete without opening the file | A permission check per row (or offered actions that fail); a menu on every row of a list of 200 |
| (c) The operations for everyone, refused by the server | Simple code | Nothing hidden | A reader sees buttons that answer 403 (R-UI-005 says hide) |

**Choice:** (a). The page asks the batched permission check of R-UI-005 once per path for `deploy`, `overwrite` and `delete`.
**Upload files** and **New folder** appear in a local repository whose format is served below the files path (the raw-files
family of R-API-025; today the generic format) for a holder of `deploy`; **Delete** and **Delete folder** for a holder of `delete`,
never on the root, never in a virtual repository. **Delete folder** is the item of the folder's menu (**More actions for this
folder**), not a button beside the upload: deleting a folder is rare and destroys, uploading is the Owner's common job (revised on
the coordinator's review of the renders, 2026-11-18). A file's **Delete** stays beside **Download**, the file's own two actions. A disabled repository offers none of them. The upload opens the deploy dialog of
R-UI-012 with the page's folder; an empty repository's empty state then names the upload and offers no second button.

**Rationale:** the owner's rule (W-8): each operation for the roles that may use it, and the plain reader sees a list with nothing
in the way. The development agent revisits (b) if deleting many single files from a folder turns out to be a common job.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010, R-UI-011, R-UI-012, R-UI-052. Code: `permissions` in
[repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts),
[repository-files.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts),
[repository-file.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts). Tests: `R-UI-011` in
[repository-files.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-513 · A folder loads in pages of 200, and its filter says when it has not seen every entry

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a folder can hold thousands of entries (a release folder, an icon set). The children API pages by cursor (R-API-025) and
has no name filter.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Pages of `ui.browser.page_size` (200) with **Load more**; the filter narrows what is loaded and says so while more are to load (chosen) | The list and its filter in the browser | No API change; one request per page; the reader knows when the filter has not seen everything | Finding one name in 5,000 entries takes **Load more** first |
| (b) A name filter on the children API | Server-side | Finds any name at once | An API, a query and an index change for a filter the file search of R-API-028 is meant to answer |
| (c) Load every page up front | Complete | The filter sees everything | A folder of 50,000 entries is 250 requests before the first row |

**Choice:** (a). Below the toolbar a note reads "The filter searches the 400 entries loaded so far. Load more to search the rest."
while a filter is typed and the list has more. **Rationale:** a folder is browsed by its order; a search by name across a large
folder is the file search's job (R-UI-015, R-API-028, P1). The development agent revisits (b) when the file search is built or if a
folder of many entries is a common place to look a name up.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010. Code: `FILES_PAGE` in
[repository-files.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts). Test: "R-UI-010 a folder with 450 entries shows the first 200" in
[repository-files.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-514 · A file's page is its name, Download, its address and its facts; the rest is Details

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The name once, as the last segment of the path with its icon and the actions at the end of that row; the download address, five facts and **SHA-256**; every checksum, the statistics and the API in a closed **Details** (chosen) | Simple by default | The reader's job (fetch the file, check it) is on the page at once | The other checksums are one click away |
| (b) Browse's three tabs General, Statistics and API | As before | Nothing to decide | Tabs for facts that fit on one page; the statistics are a request every time a file is opened |
| (c) A drawer over the list | The list stays visible | Context | No address of its own; narrow for the API's JSON |

**Choice:** (a). The name is not repeated as a heading under the path (revised on the coordinator's review of the renders,

**Download** is a default button, not the primary: the repository's header holds **Set up client** (a default button too since

`<quader-time-ago>` (Q-UI-378), the form of a detail page. **Rationale:** the facts a reader needs are few; the checksums beyond
SHA-256 and the API's view are for who checks a file. The development agent revisits it if users ask for the other checksums often.

### Q-UI-515 · A copy or a move chooses its target repository from a list and its folder by browsing it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Not built:
the copy and move of R-STOR-019 do not exist.

Context: Browse's tree reached every repository of the project, so a copy into another repository could have been a drag in it.
Without the tree (ADR-203) the dialog has to offer the target.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A select of the repositories the caller may deploy to (same format or generic, local or virtual with a deployment target), the source's first, the others grouped by project; then the target's folders browsed in the dialog one level at a time, with a path field and a live preview (chosen) | Two steps in one dialog | Every target the server would accept and no other; deep folders reachable without typing; a typed path still works | A dialog that lists folders; the list of repositories is read once per dialog |
| (b) A path field only, `<project>/<repo>/<path>` | One field | Simple | The user has to know the target's exact key and folder |
| (c) A tree of every repository and folder in the dialog | Browse inside a dialog | Familiar | The tree the owner removed, in a smaller box |

**Choice:** (a). The list of targets is the repository list filtered by format and class; whether the caller holds `deploy` is the
batched check of R-UI-005 (the dry run of R-STOR-019 decides finally). **Rationale:** it keeps the one thing the tree did that a
copy needs, reaching a folder, without bringing the tree back. The development agent revisits (b) if users mostly copy into one
known place.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-013, R-UI-011.

| (c) Only `/trash`, the installation's (R-UI-014 before ADR-203) | One page | Simple | Far from the repository; a project's Owner sees entries of every project they may deploy to, mixed |

### Q-UI-520 · A long name wraps beside its icon or chevron, and a filter field is as wide as a name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: seen in the walk of 2026-11-18 on the repository's page: the row of the package
`customer-portal-api-client-generated-from-the-openapi-document` started about 10 px left of its neighbours, chevron and name alike
(the chevron, a flex item, shrank beside the long name); the field **Filter packages** was as wide as the page (1,128 px); a file
row's icon touched its name and sat higher than it, while a folder row had a gap and one line (the folder was a `button`, the file a
link, with different line boxes). The owner's first objection, W-3, was the same kind of defect. Found in the first renders of
this change (coordinator, 2026-11-18): an archive (`*.tar.gz`, `*.tgz`) had the icon `folder_zip`, whose outline is a folder's, in a
list where folders and files stand together.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The icon or chevron keeps its size (`flex: none`) and stands on the name's first line; the name takes the rest and wraps inside itself (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`); a folder and a file are the same link element; the filter field takes the width of a name field (28 rem), down to 12 rem; one icon for every file (`description`) and one for every folder (`folder`) (chosen) | One layout per row | A long name never moves a row's start or leaves its icon; the field fits its input | A very long name takes more lines |
| (b) Cut a long name with an ellipsis | One line | Rows of one height | The name the reader needs is cut (W-3 asks for the start beside the icon, not a cut) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the owner's W-3: the icon and the start of the name on one line, a name that is too long breaks
inside itself beside the icon. The rule of the style guide: a field is as wide as its expected input.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010, R-UI-052. Code: `.name-cell`, `.entry` and `.filter` in
[repository-lists.scss](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-lists.scss).

### Q-UI-521 · The path of a folder or a file stands once, and its middle folders collapse where it is narrow

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Asked for by
the coordinator's review of the renders (2026-11-18): the path stood on the screen twice, a deep one took eleven lines at 390 px,
three lines started with the separator, and the copy button floated beside the middle of the block.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Below 64 rem of the path's row, **Files**, one button for the folders in between, and the last segment; from 64 rem every folder (chosen) | A container query on the row; the button (`more_horiz`, **Show the folders in between**) opens a menu of the folders as links | Two lines at most for the seed's deep path on a phone; every folder in view where there is room; one way up to each folder at every width | At 1024 px with the side bar the folders are one click away |
| (b) Every folder at every width | No control | Nothing hidden | The deep path of the seed takes six lines at 390 px |
| (c) The middle folders collapse at every width | One layout | Short everywhere | The wide screen hides what it has room for |

**Choice:** (a). Each separator is generated after its segment (`::after`), so a line ends with it and never starts with it; a
segment wraps at its hyphens and breaks inside a word only when nothing else fits. The copy button of the path follows the last
segment. On a file's page the last segment is the file with its icon, and the file's actions stand at the end of the row (Q-UI-514).
**Rationale:** the path is the page's answer to "where am I"; its last segment matters most, and the folders in between are a
way back up, which the menu keeps. The development agent revisits the 64 rem threshold if the path is often collapsed on wide
screens.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010. Code: the path in [repository-content.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.html)
(`between`, `here`) and `.files-head`, `.files-trail` in [repository-content.scss](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.scss).
Tests: "R-UI-010 a folder deep in the path shows its path once" in [repository-files.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.spec.ts); the render
`files-deep` with its walk.

### Q-UI-542 · Every form that chooses a level reads the caller's choices and gives the first reason of R-AUTHZ-038

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| (b) Show every reason that applies | Two or three sentences under one option | Complete | A disabled option with a list of reasons; the second one is never the one the server answers |

### Q-UI-770 · The wiki's own level is a fold of the section Visibility, closed while the wiki has the repository's level

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's product rule of 2026-11-12: access in the standard flow is the members and the visibility level, nothing
else, and a setting only an expert needs lives behind a disclosure. The section **Visibility** of a repository's settings showed
two groups of three options, **Artifacts** and **Wiki** (Q-UI-231), for every format with wiki content (npm, NuGet, Ansible
Galaxy today). The wiki's level is the expert's: a new repository has it at the artifacts' level, and most never change it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The fold **Wiki visibility** inside the open section, under the one group: the inline form of the shared disclosure, as **Upstream details** inside **Upstream**; closed while the wiki's level is the repository's, opened by the block while the two differ or the server refused the wiki's level; the person may close it, and a closed fold with an unsaved choice says "Unsaved changes" (chosen) | `<quader-disclosure [inline]="true">` in `repository-visibility.ts`, its state a signal that follows "differs or refused" | One level in the main view; the wiki's level stays where visibility is set, in the same block with the same save, so "at most the repository's level" is seen beside it; a differing level is never hidden; the app's pattern for a section's further details | One more line in the section for a format with a wiki |
| (b) A closed section **Wiki visibility** of the page, among **Access details** and the others | A `<quader-disclosure>` with a save of its own | Out of the standard section whole | Two saves for two levels that bound each other; a differing wiki level is a screen further down; lowering the level would change a field in another section |
| (c) The wiki's level inside **Access details** | With the patterns and Hide existence | No new fold | That section saves the document's members with its own patch; the levels are not part of that form (Q-UI-237); a differing level could not open it without opening the patterns too |
| (d) Always open, under the first group | Today's block with a smaller second group | Nothing hidden | The standard flow keeps a second access setting, which the rule excludes |

**Choice:** (a). The fold has no hint line: its sentence stands inside it, so the closed fold is one line. **Rationale:** the
rule asks for one level in the standard flow and for the detail on demand; the two levels are one decision of the server (one
patch, rules that bind them), so they stay one block. Opening by itself is what keeps the simple view honest: whoever sees a
closed fold knows that the wiki has the level above. The development agent revisits (b) if further parts get levels of their own
and the fold grows into a form.

The project's settings and the admin area's general settings were checked for the same two groups: a project has one level (its
group is **Visibility level** in a closed section **Visibility**), and the general settings hold **Default project visibility**
and **Restricted visibility levels**, the two settings the owner named for that section (W-11, Q-UI-540), which are not a second
level of one thing. Neither shows artifacts and wiki, so neither changes.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-055, R-UI-087. Code: [repository-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-visibility.ts).

### Q-UI-771 · A wiki without a level of its own follows the visibility level, in the form

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: with the wiki's group in view, choosing an artifacts level below the wiki's lowered the wiki, and raising the artifacts
left the wiki where it was. Behind a closed fold that rule makes the one visible level say less than it shows: an Owner who
raises a repository from Internal to Public would keep an Internal wiki without having seen it, and the fold would open on a
difference nobody chose. The document stores two levels (`visibility.artifacts`, `visibility.wiki`, R-REPO-004), and a create
stores the wiki at the artifacts' level.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) In the form, a wiki whose stored level is the artifacts' and for which no level was chosen in this edit takes the level chosen above, up and down, and both parts are sent; a wiki with a level of its own keeps it, is lowered where the level falls below it and gets it back when the level rises again before the save; choosing the repository's level for it and saving makes it follow again (chosen) | The wiki's value in the form is derived: the level, or the lower of its own and the level | The one level means the whole repository for whoever never opens the fold; "follows" needs no stored flag, because equal levels are what a new repository has; nothing is lost by lowering and raising within an edit | An expert who set both levels equal on purpose gets a wiki that moves with the level; the API alone still leaves a part that is not named as it is |
| (b) Today's rule: the wiki is only lowered | Raising the level leaves the wiki | No part changes that the person did not touch | The fold opens after every raise, on a difference the person did not choose; a Public repository whose README is not public, by default |
| (c) The server stores "follows" (a wiki level that may be absent) | A change of the document, the schema and the rules of R-AUTHZ-033 | The API follows too | A change of the stored format and of every reader of the wiki's level for a rule the form can hold; nothing in the product reads "follows" but this form |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the simple path must be complete: one level, one meaning. The form is where the two levels are
set by a person, and equal levels are the state every repository starts in. The development agent revisits (c) when an API
client or a second screen needs to know whether a wiki follows, and (b) if the walk shows wikis opened to the public by a
raise that was meant for the packages alone.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-055. Code: `wikiFollows` and `wiki` of [repository-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-visibility.ts).

**Visibility**; the reason under a wiki option read "The wiki cannot be more open than the artifacts.", which is also the text of

(chosen) | `label`, `labelHidden` of the level control; two texts | One name for the same choice at a project and at a repository; no word in the main view that needs the model explained; the fold's toggle is the one visible name of its group | The creation form keeps **Visibility**, the name of a field among its fields |

valid.", whatever the field problem said. The server names the level in `errors[]` (`/visibility/artifacts`, `/visibility/wiki`:

development agent would change. `members` had a filter field as wide as the page, a sort button **Account** and an arrow beside
it, and a tab strip with a single tab, **Members 2** (Q-UI-214 took the reference's tab and sort). Every other list has the head of
R-UI-100 and sorts by its column headers. The members API answers one list: a project has no pending invitations and no access
requests, and groups are members of the same list, so the page has one view.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The head of R-UI-100 with the search alone, the shared data table sorted by **Account** and **Role** in its headers, no tab strip, the count as a badge after the heading (chosen) | **Members 2** as the page's `h1` | One list pattern in the app; the count stays where the eye starts | A count in a heading is new; the page header gains `count` |
| (b) The same, with a drawer of two filters (role, user or group) | **Filters** beside the field | A long list narrows by role | Sorting by **Role** already groups the roles; a drawer for two choices is an expert's detail in a plain list |
| (c) The count in the table's caption | Nothing beside the heading | No new element | The caption is for assistive technology; a sighted reader loses the count |
| (d) Keep the tab strip | As before | The reference's look | A tab strip of one is not a view, and it is the objection |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the members list is a list like the others and should read like them; the tab of the reference
carried a count, and the heading is the place a reader looks first. The development agent revisits (b) if a project's list grows
past a page, and a tab strip when the page gets a second view (invitations, access requests).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-142, R-UI-041; Q-UI-214 revised. Code: [project-members.ts](../../web/src/app/features/projects/project-members.ts),
[project-members-page.ts](../../web/src/app/features/projects/project-members-page.ts), `count` of
[page-header.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/page-header.ts).

### Q-UI-551 · A description is as wide as a name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's walk of 2026-11-18, `new-<format>-<class>`: the description was a text area as wide as the form (56 rem) for
one sentence. The rule is that a field is as wide as its expected input (R-UI-085); the style guide gave every description the
column (Q-UI-334, Q-UI-335). The fields above it, **Project** and **Key**, are 28 rem.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every description takes `name`, 28 rem, wherever it is entered or shown (chosen) | About 60 characters a line; a text area of two rows holds a sentence of 120 | Lines up with the key and the project above it, so the form's right edge stays even; one rule for every form | A long description scrolls inside its field |
| (b) A sixth width for a sentence (40 rem) | A token of its own | A longer line | A width that no other field shares makes the column ragged; Q-UI-335 revisits a width by the next one, not a new one |
| (c) Keep the column | As before | Room for anything | The objection |

**Choice:** (a), for the creation form and the settings of a repository, the creation dialog and the settings of a project, a group,
a service account, a permission policy, a CI mapping and a CI issuer, a Bastion and its tokens, and a personal token. The administrator
notes stay the column: they are a note, not a sentence. **Rationale:** the description is one sentence that names the thing, as long
as a few names. The development agent revisits it if the renders show common descriptions cut.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-085 (its table); ui-style-guide.md (Forms). Code: `field-w-name` on `#f-description` in

[repository-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-detail.html), `width="name"` on every

### Q-UI-553 · The guides' trail names a format as people read it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: seen by the builder of the guides on 2026-11-18: the trail read `Guides / oci` where every other place says **OCI
(Docker)**; the step was the route's parameter. The page's title was the key too.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The route `:format` resolves the format's display name from the catalog (`crumbLabel`), and the trail and the title show it; the key where the catalog does not know it (chosen) | `Guides / OCI (Docker)`, the tab "OCI (Docker) – Quader" | One name for a format in every place; the resolver runs once, the page below reads it | One request of the catalog before the page |
| (b) A map of keys to names in the UI | No request | Instant | A second list of the formats beside the catalog, which every new format must extend |

**Choice:** (a). `data.crumbParam` of a path route takes a resolved `crumbLabel` of the same route instead of the parameter's value.
**Rationale:** the catalog names the formats (`GET /api/v1/formats`, `displayName`); the UI should not keep a copy. No revisit condition.

### Q-UI-554 · Where the header is narrow, the page's actions share the line of Set up client

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
**Superseded by [Q-UI-664](#q-ui-664--the-repositorys-header-leads-to-set-up-client-and-holds-no-address)** (2026-11-18): without
the address field, **Set up client** is one of the page's actions, which go under the heading on one line by the page header's
own wrapping; the rules of the client row are gone. The text below is the record of the superseded decision.

Context: seen by the builder of the guides on 2026-11-18, a repository's page at 390 px: the header's parts wrapped one by one,
the address field, **Set up client**, then the page's actions on a line of their own; for a reader, whose only action is the menu,
the menu button stood alone on a line. The header is two blocks (the main column with the client row, and the actions), and the
actions block wraps below the main one where the two do not fit beside each other (below about 33 rem).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Below 36 rem of the content, a header with a client row is one flow: the heading, the sentence, the facts and the address field each a line, then **Set up client** and the page's actions (as one unit) on the next (chosen) | At 390 px: Set up client, Settings and the menu on one line, about 250 of 358 px | No button alone; the address keeps the whole width; the order of the focus is the wide layout's | A CSS rule that dissolves the header's two blocks there (`display: contents`) |
| (b) The actions beside the heading at the top right | The style guide's place of a page's actions | Familiar | The heading, a long key, keeps 230 px at 390 px and breaks into more lines |
| (c) The menu inside the client row at every width | Always together | No width rule | The menu leaves the action corner where the wide layout has it |

**Choice:** (a), for every header with a client row (the repository's page). A header without one keeps its two blocks; a page
whose actions are buttons with labels does not leave one alone. **Rationale:** the line under the address is the line of the
actions; the defect is a line with one icon on it. The development agent revisits the threshold if the actions grow.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052; Q-UI-517. Code: the container query at the end of the styles of
[page-header.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/page-header.ts).

### Q-UI-555 · An empty repository shows Set up client once, in its header, and its empty state says what fills it and for whom

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: seen by the builder of the guides on 2026-11-18: an empty repository showed **Set up client** in its header, beside the
address, and again under the sentence of its empty state (Q-UI-309). The sentence said "Publish a package with your client." to
every reader, also to one who may not publish, and to a remote repository, which nobody publishes to.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The header's button stays; the empty state is a sentence: what the repository does not hold yet, then what fills it for this caller, naming **Set up client** where that is the way (chosen) | One button, one sentence per reader | The action stands where it stands on every page of the repository; the reader learns whether the next step is theirs | One permission check more on the page of a package format (`deploy`, cached 60 s) |
| (b) The empty state keeps the button, the header loses it while the repository is empty | The action under the sentence | The empty state of Q-UI-309 as it is | The header changes with the content, and the address loses its button |
| (c) Both stay | As before | Two ways | The objection |

**Choice:** (a). A caller who may deploy reads "Publish a package with your client; Set up client shows how." (push an image,
upload files); in a generic repository whose toolbar offers **Upload files**, "Upload files here or with your client."; anyone else
"Members who may publish to it fill it with their client."; a remote repository "It fills as clients fetch through it; Set up client
shows how." to everyone; a disabled repository only what it does not hold. **Rationale:** the empty state's action is the header's
here, so the empty state's job is to say what to do with it and whether it is the reader's to do. The development agent revisits
(b) if readers miss the action at an empty repository.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-144, R-UI-052, R-UI-126; Q-UI-309 and Q-UI-217 revised. Code: `emptyContentText` in
[content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts), `fill` in
[repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts).

### Q-UI-556 · A repository's list of packages says a grade as the versions table does

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. What the
versions table says is the owner's (2026-11-18, W-7).

Context: the list of a repository's packages said the count that decides the letter, "2 High" beside the shield C (R-UI-091,
Q-UI-374); the versions table of a package, which a reader opens from that list, says "1,145 findings · 112 fixable" beside the
shield (R-UI-112, Q-UI-454). Two statements of one thing on two lists read one after the other. The list's grade carries the same
`open` and `fixable` as a version's (R-VULN-040), so either statement can stand in both.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every list says the versions table's statement: the total and the fixable, "OS end of life" for an image whose OS is; the deciding count and the rule are the tooltip's and the card's; one component, `<quader-grade>` (chosen) | The repository's list, its opened rows, the versions table and a version's facts say the same | The owner chose the total and the fixable for the version a reader looks for; a reader compares one number across the two lists | The list no longer says why the letter is C; the tooltip does |
| (b) The versions table goes back to the deciding count | "2 High" everywhere | The letter's reason in every row | Against the owner's W-7 |
| (c) Each list keeps its statement | As before | No change | The objection |

**Choice:** (a). `<quader-version-grade>` is merged into `<quader-grade>`; the deciding count ("13 Critical") stays on the card of
a version's page with the rule and the bar (R-UI-093). An image whose OS is at its end of life says so after its counts, because
that, not its findings, can be what made it C. The letter stays on the shield only (R-UI-091, revised 2026-11-18). **Rationale:** a
grade is one statement wherever a reader meets it, and the owner chose its words for the version. The development agent revisits it
if readers ask why a row is C without hovering.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-143, R-UI-091, R-UI-094, R-UI-112; Q-UI-374 and Q-UI-454 revised. Code:
[grade.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade.ts), `gradeSummaryParts` in
[grade-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/vulnerability/grade-words.ts).

### Q-UI-560 · An icon in a table cell is one element with its word

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: on `system/jobs` the state's icon stood on one line and its word ("succeeded") on the next, in every row; the audit log's
outcome, the advisory sources' state, the system status's replica, key and Valkey states and the rule editor's verdicts were
built the same way: an icon with a status class, then the word as a text node or a sibling span, directly in the cell. The lists
that used the badge (`<span class="ok"><icon/>Active</span>`) never broke.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every status in a cell is the badge; an icon before a text that may wrap is `.icon-name`; a lint rule refuses an icon that stands directly in a cell (chosen) | One construction, held by the lint | It cannot recur on a new screen; the badge is the reference's status | The badge is a pill, so a status that was plain coloured text gains a fill |
| (b) A shared table rule that keeps a cell with an icon on one line | CSS only | No template changes | A cell with an icon and a sentence never wraps; the cause stays in the templates |
| (c) Fix the jobs screen | Local | Small | The other screens keep the defect |

**Choice:** (a). `status-rule.mjs` (run by `check-rules.mjs`, tested in `lint-rules.test.mjs`) refuses a `material-icons` element
that is a direct child of a `<td>` or a `<th>`, unless it is an image of its own (`role="img"` with its name). **Rationale:** the
defect was a construction, so the construction is what is ruled out. The development agent revisits the rule if it refuses a
construction that cannot break.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-145, R-UI-037, R-UI-038. Code: [status-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/status-rule.mjs), the jobs, the
audit log, the advisory sources, the system status, the endpoints and their rule editor, the triage dialog, the CI issuers and
issuances.

| (b) Icons of 16 px in a cell | Smaller | No margin | The icon is the format's logo; 16 px is the badge's |

### Q-UI-563 · A column is as wide as its content; what never breaks declares no width, and the columns that wrap share the room

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a column that `prefer`s takes every pixel the others leave, and every other column is pinned to its least width
(Q-UI-330). That broke a value in a pinned column while the preferred one was half empty: the administrator's token
**Client setup: npm, web-frontend/npm-vendor, 2026-11-18** in three lines of 10 rem beside a scope of 280 px for "Repository grants:
1"; the project **Customer portal release engineering and delivery** in three lines of 11 rem; a job's replica "ms2022.local-" /
"39645" in 7 rem beside a result of half the page. A least width declared for a column whose values never break was a guess for
one screen: wider than its values, it took room the wrapping columns needed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A column whose values never break (a format, a class, a level, a time, a status, an identifier, the actions) declares no width and is as wide as its longest value; a column whose values wrap declares its least; only a list with one wrapping column lets it `prefer`; a row's header that is an identifier (`translate="no"`) stays on one line like a cell of one (chosen) | The table's own layout by content | No value is broken while room is free; no width is a guess | Where the wrapping columns need more than there is, the room is shared, so both break into two lines rather than one into three |
| (b) Bigger least widths for the broken columns | Numbers | Small change | A number for one screen's data; the next long name breaks again |
| (c) Ellipsis for every long value | One line | Even rows | A name cut where it was readable |

**Choice:** (a). The admin area's repositories: the repository and the project wrap (13 and 11 rem least, the project 12 rem
since the renders' look of 2026-11-18 found it in three lines at 1,280 px, the repository 12 rem since the format **ClamAV
definitions** made the format column 27 px wider on 2026-11-21 and the list needed 963 px at 1,280 px where its region has 953
beside a scrollbar) and share the room,
the rest is as wide as its values; inside a project the repository is the one that wraps and prefers. The token lists: the
token and the scope share the room (Q-UI-429 revised), the times and the actions as wide as their values. The jobs: the result is
the one that wraps and prefers; the kind and the replica stay whole. Where a value can be longer than any column, it is cut on one
line with its whole value as its title (Q-UI-568) or shortened (Q-UI-570). The sum of the least widths that the stacking of
Q-UI-306 is reasoned on counts a column without a width at its longest value. **Rationale:** the browser divides a table by its
content when nothing pins it, which is what the defects asked for. The development agent revisits a list whose wrapping columns
still break into three lines at 1440 px.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-145, R-UI-029, R-UI-038; Q-UI-330 and Q-UI-429 revised. Code: `columns` of
[repository-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.ts),
[token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/token-table.ts), [job-table.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/job-table.ts);
the identifier rule in [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss).
