### Q-UI-600 · A replica that drains or starts informs: the header says that replicas are being replaced

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-13 (owner, 2026-11-18). The header of the status screen read "Replicas unready" and the dashboard "A role is not
ready" as soon as one replica was not `ready`. During every rolling update a pod is `draining` for the drain delay and longer and
its successor `starting` for its start-up, so every update turned both red. A draining replica also listed "Failing checks:
draining", the synthetic check that fails on purpose from `SIGTERM` on.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Draining and starting replicas are left out of the header | The header looks at `ready` and `unready` only | Quiet | An administrator who opens the screen during an update does not learn why the counts move |
| (b) They inform: "Replicas are being replaced (`n` draining, `m` starting), as during every update", neutral, after the main statement (chosen) | The header still reads "All roles ready" while every role has a ready replica | Says what happens, in the neutral form, with the counts; the version notice below it names the two versions of the update | One more line during an update |
| (c) A warning while replicas drain | Yellow during every update | Draws the eye | An intended, routine change in the colour of a fault, which the owner objected to |

**Choice:** (b). The states `draining` and `starting` are neutral in the table; the synthetic check `draining` is not listed among a
replica's failing checks; the dashboard says "Replicas are being replaced" as an informing badge beside "All roles ready". The main
statement says "All roles ready" rather than "All ready", because it is true while a replica drains. A replica that stays
`starting` with another ready replica of its role informs too; its failing checks stay in its row. **Rationale:** a replica that
drains or starts is the normal path of an update, a restart and a change of scale; the header should name it without alarm, and
the role rule of [Q-UI-602](#q-ui-602--a-replica-lost-without-draining-is-a-warning-red-is-a-role-without-a-ready-replica) still
turns it red when no replica of a role is ready. The development agent revisits it if a replica that never leaves `starting` goes
unnoticed; a bound on the time in `starting` would then be an error of its own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the header, the replica states, the dashboard's overall state, acceptance criteria). Code:
`serviceStatus` and `failingChecks` in [system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts),
[system-status.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.html), [dashboard.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/dashboard.html).

### Q-UI-601 · The header says what is wrong first, each statement with its own level, and the dashboard the worst of them

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the header had three states in one colour each, "all ready", "degraded" and "replicas unready", and appended "not
drain-safe". With W-13 it has to tell an error (a role without a ready replica), a warning (a lost replica, a degraded check) and
what only informs (an update, the drain safety) apart, and it can hold several at once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One state, the worst | As before, with more states | Short | Hides the second fault while the first lasts; a lost replica during an update would hide the update |
| (b) Every statement that holds, worst first, each with its icon and level; "All roles ready" when none is an error or a warning; the dashboard shows the worst and the update (chosen) | One rule, `serviceStatus`, for both screens | The administrator reads every fault at once; both screens agree because they call one function | The header can be two lines at 390 px |
| (c) A list of statements in a card | Each its own row | Room for detail | A card for a sentence or two, above the cards that hold the detail |

**Choice:** (b). `serviceStatus` returns the conditions with their levels (`error`, `warning`, `info`) and the overall level; the
status screen renders all of them, the dashboard's instance bar the worst error or warning (or "All roles ready") and the
informing "Replicas are being replaced". **Rationale:** one function decides what both screens say, so they cannot disagree, and
the levels follow the design language's icon and colour per state (R-UI-044). The development agent revisits it if the header grows
past two lines in practice.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038. Code: [system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts),
[system-status.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.html), [dashboard.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/dashboard.ts).

### Q-UI-602 · A replica lost without draining is a warning; red is a role without a ready replica

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-18** — option (a).

Context: W-13. A replica that ends without a drain (a crash, a kill, the loss of its node) leaves its row, which is listed as
`lost` until the prune 24 h later (R-OPS-003). The header read "Replicas unready" in red for those 24 h, also when the role had been
replaced long since and every role had its ready replicas. The development agent proposed a warning; the owner chose it from three
options on 2026-11-18.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A warning (chosen by the owner) | While its role has a ready replica, the header and the dashboard say "Lost without draining", with the name and the last heartbeat, as a warning; the row stays in the table as `lost` until the prune | The administrator sees that it happened and when, without a fault that is no longer one | A replica that crashes every few hours shows as a warning, not as an error |
| (b) Red, as before | A lost row turns the header red | Hard to miss | Red for 24 h after a crash that Kubernetes repaired in seconds; red stops meaning "act now" |
| (c) Not in the header at all | Only the row says `lost` | Quiet | A crash is seen only by someone who reads the table |

**Choice:** (a), the owner's. Red is for a role the installation needs that has no ready replica: `api`, `packages` and `worker`
unless a live `all` replica serves them, and `web`, `all` or an unknown role while one of its replicas is live; a role whose only
replicas are lost, draining or starting has none. A role that only a lost row names (the bridge `web` after its upgrade, a removed
pool's Deployment) is not needed, so its lost row is a warning. What was red for other reasons stays red: a live replica that fails a
gating check after it was ready, an unsupported schema, incompatible key rings, a failing dependency check on the dashboard. The
rule for a lost replica is the constant `LOST_REPLICA_LEVEL` in
[system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts), one place to change it.
**Rationale:** the owner's: an update or a repaired crash is no fault. A role without a ready replica is one, and that includes a
`worker` or `packages` role scaled to zero, which the role group already names ("No live worker replica", Q-UI-107) and which the
header did not colour before.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the header, the replica states, acceptance criteria); R-OPS-003 and
[Q-OPS-210](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-210--a-row-that-went-stale-while-draining-has-signed-off-the-list-leaves-it-out-and-the-prune-deletes-it)
in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) say which rows are lost. Code: `serviceStatus` and
`LOST_REPLICA_LEVEL` in [system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts).

### Q-UI-603 · Not being drain-safe informs: it is a property of the installation's size

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-13. An installation with one replica of the role `all`, or of any role, is not drain-safe by its size: the header read
"Not drain-safe" with the warning icon, and the role group "Fewer than two ready replicas" as a warning, on a healthy installation.
The incident that makes a large installation lose its drain safety, a lost replica, has its own warning now (Q-UI-602).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A warning, as before | Yellow on every small installation | Draws the eye before a drain | A healthy single-replica installation looks like a fault at first sight |
| (b) Informing: the header's "Not drain-safe" and the group's "Fewer than two ready replicas" and "All ready replicas on one node" with the information icon, neutral (chosen) | The words stay; the level changes | The administrator who plans a drain still reads it; a small installation is not shown as broken | A large installation that lost a replica shows the loss as a warning and the drain safety only as information |
| (c) Not in the header | Only the role group says it | Quiet header | The runbook's drain step reads it from the header |

**Choice:** (b). "No live replica in the pool" stays a warning. **Rationale:** a property of the size that the administrator chose
is information; the faults that change it are warned about where they happen. The development agent revisits it if the chart
gains a way to say the intended replica count, which would make "fewer than intended" a warning of its own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038. Code: `serviceStatus` in
[system-status-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status-model.ts),
[system-status.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.html).

### Q-UI-604 · The dashboard leaves the Nodes row out where no replica names its node

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-13. The dashboard's card of the role `all` read "Nodes 0" beside "1 of 1 ready" on the owner's stack. The node is
`QUADER_NODE_NAME` from the downward API (R-OPS-003); outside Kubernetes no replica names one, so the count of distinct nodes was
0.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A dash | "Nodes –" | The row is always there | A row that never has a value outside Kubernetes |
| (b) No row where none of the role's ready replicas names its node (chosen) | `roleLoad` reports `nodes` as null then | Shows only what is known | The card's rows differ between installations |
| (c) The API reports null | `replicas.roles.<role>.nodes` null outside Kubernetes | The API says it too | The screens do not read it; R-OPS-004 keeps the count, documented as 0 outside Kubernetes |

**Choice:** (b). **Rationale:** a figure that cannot be known is left out rather than shown as a value. The development agent
revisits it if an installation outside Kubernetes ever gets a node name.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038 (the dashboard's role card); R-OPS-004 (`nodes` is 0 outside Kubernetes). Code: `roleLoad` in
[dashboard-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/dashboard-model.ts), [dashboard.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/dashboard.html).

### Q-UI-610 · The user page's notice of a missing group claim says since when and what the policy does

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: since the owner's W-14 (2026-11-18, Q-AUTH-400) the audit log records a missing group claim when it changes, so an
administrator who reads the entry weeks later needs the current state elsewhere. The user page showed it already, in the section
**Groups**: "The last sign-in through corp carried no usable group claim (absent), so groups synchronized from it may be
missing." It said neither since when nor that with `keep` nothing goes missing.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The notice stays in **Groups**, which opens while it stands, and names the provider, the reason in words, since when, and what the policy does at each sign-in (chosen) | One sentence more | It sits beside the memberships it concerns; one place | One state per user is shown, the identity whose state began last |
| (b) A line per identity under **Identities** | The state of each provider | Two providers each show their state | The API would carry the state per identity; the memberships it concerns are a section further down |
| (c) Both | — | — | Two places for one fact |

**Choice:** (a). The section opens by itself while the notice stands, as on the profile. The reason reads "no group claim",
"a group claim of the wrong type" or "too many groups for the token"; the time is the date and time of the locale.

**Rationale:** one fact has one place, and the one that existed is beside the groups the state affects. The development agent
would revisit it when a user with two providers whose claims are both missing is seen in practice.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-024. Code: [user-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/users/user-detail.html).

### Q-UI-580 · One shared field names a principal everywhere, and nobody types a reference

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-18** (W-12: "a person is chosen through a person search that shows the possible people,
everywhere a person search plays a role"); the shape of the field was decided by the development agent — selected from the options
below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the UI named principals three ways: text fields that took `user:name`, `group:name` or `sa:name` (system roles, the policy
editor's entries and **Try it**, the filters of the policies and the tokens), a field that took a bare name (a group's members, a user's
groups, the audit log's actor, the users list's group), and a search box with the matches as buttons (`quader-principal-picker`: the
project dialog, the project member dialog, the project policy editor). The CI mapping editor offered the groups in the browser's
`datalist`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One shared field, `<quader-principal-field>`, a combobox that searches while one types and lists the matches under it; the picker and every typed reference go (chosen) | Kinds, one or many, the project, by inputs | One control and one way to name a principal in the whole app; nobody needs the reference syntax | Every place changes at once |
| (b) The text fields keep their syntax and get suggestions | A `datalist` per field | Little change | The syntax stays in the UI; a `datalist` cannot show an avatar |
| (c) A button that opens a dialog with a search | "Choose a person" | Room for a long list | A second step for the common case; GitLab's field, the owner's reference, has none |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the owner asked for one behaviour everywhere; one component makes that a property of the app rather
than of each screen. The development agent revisits it if a place needs to name more principals than a field of chips holds.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-150, R-UI-152. Code: [principal-field.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/principal-field.ts).

### Q-UI-581 · The field searches what its caller may already search

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The rule
that no caller gains a search it did not have is the development agent's correction of 2026-11-18 to its first brief, which had
opened the search to every internal user as on the owner's GitLab.

Context: the places of R-UI-152 are of two kinds. In a project (its members, its policies) the caller is the project's Owner, who
has the lookup of Q-AUTHZ-182 and not `identities:read`. Everywhere else the caller is on a screen of the admin area and holds
`identities:read`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The project's lookup with `project`, the admin area's suggestions without (chosen) | The field picks its source by its input | No new enumeration surface: each caller searches what it could list before; the answers hold no e-mail address | Two sources with two limits (20 and 10 per kind) |
| (b) An open principal search for every internal user | As on GitLab | One source; a member could name people anywhere | A new way to enumerate every user's name and username for every internal user; withdrawn |
| (c) Pass a search function into each field | As the picker did | Each screen decides | The same two sources written again at every place |

**Choice:** (a). A refused search (a token whose scope lacks the capability) shows the failure and never falls back to another source.
**Rationale:** the owner asked for a person search where one is needed, not for a wider directory; every place that needs one already
has a read. The development agent revisits it if a place appears where a caller with neither must name a person; that place is then
reported, not widened.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-150, R-API-077, R-API-078.

### Q-UI-582 · A match is a row of avatar, name and username, and a choice is a chip

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The row is
the owner's (W-12).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A row of two lines, the avatar or the kind's icon in a 32 px circle, the name, the `@username` or the kind under it; a choice is a chip in the field, a field of one hides its input while it holds a choice (chosen) | As the members list's account cell (R-UI-142) | The owner's reference; the same look as the lists that show people | Two lines per match |
| (b) One line, "Name · @username", as the top bar's suggestions | Compact | Ten matches fit | Not the owner's reference |
| (c) The matches as buttons under the field | The old picker | Simple | No keyboard path through the matches; no avatar |

**Choice:** (a); the search starts at the second character (both sources refuse one), after 250 ms. **Rationale:** the owner showed
the row he wants; the members list already draws it. The development agent revisits the two lines if a long list of matches needs
to fit at 390 px.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-150, R-UI-151.

### Q-UI-583 · A CI identity is never offered; a stored one shows as a chip

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a policy entry may name a CI identity mapping (`ci:<issuer>/<mapping>`). The old editor took it as typed text. A CI mapping
receives its grants on its own page, which names its policies (R-UI-035), so a policy that names the mapping says the same thing a
second time.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field offers users, groups and service accounts; a stored `ci:` entry shows as a chip **CI identity** with its reference and can be removed (chosen) | The mapping's page grants | No typed reference; one place grants a mapping | A new policy entry for a mapping needs the mapping's page or the API |
| (b) A fourth kind, CI mappings, in the search | Searchable | Complete | A search over the CI tiers with its own permission rule for one rare case |
| (c) A text field for CI references beside the field | As before | Complete | The syntax returns |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the mapping editor is where a CI identity gets its rights; the policy editor stays a list of people,
groups and accounts. The development agent revisits it if CI entries in policies turn out to be common.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-150, R-UI-027.

### Q-UI-584 · A filter by person keeps the reference in the field and sends what its API takes

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the filters by person in a list's drawer take different forms in their APIs: the policies a reference, the tokens a username
or `sa:<name>` (and `me`), the audit log an actor's name or ID, the users list a group's name.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field holds the reference; each screen sends its API's form; the chip says the name (chosen) | `owner=sam`, `actor=sam`, `group=web-team` | No API changes for a filter; the chip reads as a name | Each screen converts |
| (b) Every API takes a reference | One form | Uniform | Changes three list operations for no reader's gain |

**Choice:** (a). The token filter's `me` goes from the UI: an administrator finds itself in the search. The audit log's actor filter
offers users and every service account; a link that names the actor by name shows it as a user's chip. **Rationale:** the person who
filters sees a name; what the API takes is the screen's business. The development agent revisits it if a filter must name a CI
token's mapping or the system as the actor.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-152.

### Q-UI-585 · A person who has never signed in is not found, and the field says so

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a user exists once it signed in through the identity provider (just in time), was provisioned by SCIM, or was created by an
administrator ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-007, R-AUTH-039, R-AUTH-016; R-API-031). The search finds users only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The empty state says "A person can be found after their first sign-in." (chosen) | One sentence | Says the product's answer where the person is missing | Does not offer the administrator's **Add user** |
| (b) Invite by e-mail from the field | A new flow | GitLab has it | Out of scope of W-12; no invitation exists |
| (c) Say nothing | "Nothing matches" | Short | The Owner does not learn why a colleague is missing |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the sign-in is how nearly every person becomes a user; an administrator's pre-provisioning is an
admin task with its own screen. Open: an invitation of a person who has never signed in (not built).

**Revisited on 2026-11-20 by the owner:** (a) stays for now. The invitation is to be one by e-mail, option (b), built later
with the sending of mail that Quader does not have yet; a pending membership without mail was offered and not chosen.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-150.

### Q-UI-620 · The security dashboard is `/security` of the main area, under the second context title Security audit

Status: **Decided by the owner, 2026-11-18** (W-17: under **Your work** as a second category **Security audit**, with **Security
dashboard** under it, for instance auditors and administrators; corrected the same evening: "Security-Audit hatte ich eigentlich
als weiteren context-title erwartet"); the address **decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the
owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the dashboard was the admin area's entry *Security* at `/admin/security`. The start side bar (**Your work**) has two
single entries, Projects and Guides. The development agent first built **Security audit** as a folding group inside the block of
**Your work**, because an area of `NAV_AREAS` ([navigation.ts](../../web/src/app/core/navigation.ts)) had one title and the folding
group was the shell's means for a section; it had briefed "a second section under Your work" where the owner meant a second
context title. The owner corrected it: **Security audit** is a context title like **Your work**, with **Security dashboard** as a
plain entry under it (R-UI-168; the model is [Q-UI-663](#q-ui-663--a-side-bar-is-a-list-of-titled-blocks)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/security`, the entry **Security dashboard** under the context title **Security audit** of the start side bar (chosen) | The routes `/security`, `/security/findings/{id}`, `/security/advisories/{ecosystem}/{id}`; the block carries the capability on its entry, so it disappears with its last entry | One short address that names the page; the title is written and placed as **Your work** | — |
| (b) `/audit/security` | The section's name in the address | Room for more pages of the section | `/admin/audit` is the audit log; two "audit" addresses for two things; longer |
| (c) A folding group **Security audit** inside **Your work** (built first, corrected by the owner) | A `NavGroup` with one entry | No change of the model | Not what the owner asked for: a section with one entry that folds, inside another section |

**Choice:** (a). The title is a name, not a page, so the trail reads "Security audit / Security dashboard" with the title unlinked,
as "Admin area" is. **Advisory sources** stays in the admin area's group System: it is the installation's configuration, and its
link on the dashboard is shown to the holder of `settings:read` only. **Rationale:** the owner placed the page and its title; the
address follows the side bar's other places (`/projects`, `/guides`, `/search`), which are one word below the root. The development
agent revisits the address when the section gets a second page.

[vuln-context.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vuln-context.ts), the lint rule

### Q-UI-621 · The Admin button is shown when the admin area has an entry for the caller

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner (W-17) wants the dashboard to be no admin feature, and an auditor who is no administrator must not be led into
the admin area by the page. The Admin button was shown for any capability (`SessionStore.hasAdminArea`). The auditor holds
`settings:read`, `audit:read`, `identities:read` and more, so the admin area has pages for it; a caller whose capabilities are
only those of the dashboard (`content:metadata-read`, `vulnerabilities:triage`) would have had a button into an admin area with no
entry since the dashboard left it. No system role is such a caller today; `webhook-admin` (`webhooks:read`, `webhooks:write`), for
whose screens the admin area has no entry yet, is one.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The button follows the admin side bar: shown when the caller may use one of its entries (chosen) | `Navigation.hasAdminArea`, computed from the entries the caller may use | The button never leads into an empty area; one source of truth, the side bar | An entry added to the admin area must name its capability, as every entry does |
| (b) Any capability, as before | No change | Nothing moves | A button into an empty area for a caller with the dashboard's capabilities alone |
| (c) Hide the button for the role `auditor` | A role name in the UI | Simple | The UI decides by role names, not by capabilities (R-UI-005); an auditor uses the audit log and the users of the admin area |

**Choice:** (a). The auditor keeps the button, because it may use the admin dashboard, the audit log, the identities and more;
on the security dashboard the button is not current, and nothing else on the page but **Advisory sources** (for `settings:read`)
leads into the admin area. **Rationale:** the button is the way into the area, so it exists when the area has something for the
caller. The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-158, R-UI-002. Code: [navigation.ts](../../web/src/app/core/navigation.ts) (`hasAdminArea`),
[app.html](../../web/src/app/app.html); `SessionStore.hasAdminArea` is gone.

### Q-UI-622 · A caller without the capability gets Page not found at `/security`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner wants the page visible only to instance auditors and administrators. The findings API answers every
authenticated caller with what that caller may read (R-VULN-019), so without a guard a reader who types `/security` would see the
findings of its own projects under the heading "Security dashboard" and a line that claims every project. The app's routes had no
guard by capability: the API decides and a screen shows its 403 (R-UI-003).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A guard by capability that shows **Page not found** at the address asked for (chosen) | `capabilityGuard('content:metadata-read')` in [auth-guard.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.ts) answers a `RedirectCommand` to the not-found route with `skipLocationChange`; a session that could not be read passes, so the screen shows the failure | The page never claims a scope the caller does not have; a caller without the right learns nothing about a page it cannot use, as with any address the app does not offer it | A route guard that does more than shape navigation, for one route |
| (b) No guard; the screen shows a "no access" notice when the caller lacks the capability | The notice of R-UI-003 | No guard | The screen asks the session instead of the API; the notice names a page the caller is not meant to know |
| (c) Redirect to the start page | The router's way of a guard | The caller lands somewhere useful | A link that silently goes elsewhere; nothing says why |

**Choice:** (a). The API decides what is read in any case; the guard only keeps the page from describing a scope the caller does
not have. Inside the app the address bar keeps the page the caller came from, because a navigation that is redirected without a
location change does not write its own address; a link opened from outside shows its address with **Page not found** (the
router's documented behaviour; not looked at in a browser).
**Rationale:** the owner's rule is a rule of visibility, and the findings API cannot refuse a page it serves to everyone. The
development agent revisits the guard if a second route needs one, to make it a route's data instead of a function.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-158, R-UI-003. Code: [auth-guard.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.ts),
[app.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/app.routes.ts).

### Q-UI-623 · A whole advisory identifier in the search is the advisory filter, any other text the text search

Status: **Decided by the owner, 2026-11-18** (one filter, at the list's head: the form above the counts goes); how the one field
answers "do I have CVE-X?" **decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: the form's **Advisory ID** sent `advisory`, which finds the findings of an advisory by its identifier or any alias, exactly,
and starts at the advisory rows (Q-VULN-111: 23 to 54 ms at 100,000 findings, where the walk over the sort index took 1.47 s). The
list's search sends `q`, which matches a part of the package name, the identifier, the summary and, in the statement since before this
change, every alias of the advisory, in any case (`VulnFindingsList` in
[vuln_api.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/vuln_api.sql); the API's description said only "the package name, the advisory
identifier or the summary"). `q` reads the caller's whole scope when it matches few findings.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field sends a whole identifier as `advisory` in its canonical spelling, any other text as `q` (chosen) | `advisoryIdOf` ([vuln-context.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vuln-context.ts)): `CVE-yyyy-n…`, `GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`, `MAL-`, `OSV-`, `PYSEC-`, `GO-`, `RUSTSEC-` with a year and a number; the field shows the identifier, no chip repeats it | Pasting a CVE finds the finding by its alias through the index, as fast as the form's field; a part of an identifier still finds by text; one field | The field writes the identifier's case anew (`cve-…` becomes `CVE-…`) after it is applied |
| (b) Everything as `q` | The list's search as in a project | No rule in the client | The question the dashboard exists for reads every finding at scale (Q-VULN-111's 1.47 s) |
| (c) Keep **Advisory** as a field of the drawer | The drawer's exact filter | The exact filter stays visible | Three steps for the page's main question; two places to type an identifier |

**Choice:** (a). The drawer of the dashboard has no **Advisory**; a project's report keeps its **Advisory** in the drawer and its
search as `q`, because its screens are outside this change (W-17). The API's description of `q` and R-VULN-020 now name the aliases,
and `TestR_VULN_020_List` finds a finding by an alias through `q`. The form's **Package starts with** goes without a successor in
the UI: `q` finds a part of a package name and the drawer's **Package** the exact name; the API keeps `packagePrefix`. **Rationale:**
one field for the owner's question, at the speed the form had. The development agent revisits the project's report, to give it the
same field, when the owner walks the vulnerability screens of a project.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-159; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-020, R-VULN-022. Code:
[vulnerability-report.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.ts) (`searchFor`),
[vuln-context.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vuln-context.ts), [openapi.yaml](../../api/openapi.yaml) (`q`).

### Q-UI-640 · A row with one action names it, a row with several has a menu

Status: **Decided by the owner, 2026-11-18** (W-18, "Option A" from three).

Context: the lists had two forms. The repositories, a project's members, the files of a repository and an endpoint's rules put
the row's actions into a menu; the projects of the admin area (**Edit**), the tokens and a Bastion's tokens (**Revoke**), the system
roles (**Unbind**), a group's members and a user's groups (**Remove**), the CI issuances (**Details**) and the sessions of the
profile (**End**) showed their one action as a quiet word. Two lists did neither: the CI mappings showed **Edit** (or **View**),
**Test** and **Delete** as words side by side, and the Debian signing keys two buttons per key.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The practice as the rule: one action is its word as a quiet button, two or more are the row's menu, with at most one frequent action beside the menu as an icon (chosen by the owner) | The two deviating lists move to the menu | A single action named by its word is faster and clearer than a menu with one entry; a leaked token's **Revoke** does not hide behind a menu | Two forms of row action in the app, by the number of actions |
| (b) A menu everywhere | Every row has `more_vert` | One form | One click more for the only action of a row; **Revoke** of a leaked token behind a menu |
| (c) Icons everywhere | Every action an icon with a tooltip | Compact | An icon has to be learned; most actions (**Unbind**, **Promote**, **Test**) have no icon a reader knows |

**Choice:** (a), the owner's. **Rationale:** the owner's, in the words above. The rule is
[R-UI-163](#r-ui-163--a-row-with-one-action-names-it-a-row-with-several-has-a-menu); the development agent filled in what the
owner did not say: a credential's **Revoke** (Q-UI-641), the copy button (Q-UI-642) and how each deviating list moved
(Q-UI-643).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-163; R-UI-146 (the row actions are no longer open). The style guide's
[Lists](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#lists).

### Q-UI-641 · A credential's Revoke is never in a menu; a token row keeps its two words

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's reason for Q-UI-640 is that a leaked token's **Revoke** must not hide behind a menu. The personal tokens of
the profile and a service account's tokens for an administrator offer two actions per token, **Rotate** and **Revoke**
([Q-UI-429](#q-ui-429--a-token-list-gives-the-scope-the-room-leaves-out-how-a-token-was-made-and-words-both-actions)), which the
rule's "two or more are a menu" would put behind `more_vert`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Revoke** of a credential is never in a menu; where its row has one other action, both stay words (chosen) | The token rows as they are | The owner's reason holds in every token list; no menu of one entry | The one place where two words stand side by side, named in the rule and allowed in its lint check |
| (b) Both in the menu | The rule without an exception | One form | **Revoke** of a leaked personal token behind a menu, against the reason of the rule |
| (c) **Revoke** as a word, **Rotate** as an icon beside it | Both visible | Compact | The icon without a label that Q-UI-429 removed; a rotation icon is not known |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the rule exists for the reason the owner gave; applying it to the personal tokens would break that

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-163; Q-UI-429 stays. Code: [token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/token-table.ts), the
allow-list of [check-rules.mjs](../../web/scripts/check-rules.mjs).

### Q-UI-643 · How the lists that did not follow the rule follow it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the survey of every table and list of 2026-11-18 found six that broke the rule. Which actions go where is the question for
two of them: the CI mappings, whose name already opened the mapping that **Edit** and **View** opened too, and the Debian signing
keys, whose withheld key offered **Confirm retirement** as a red button.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Opening is the name; the rest by the rule (chosen) | A mapping: the menu **Edit**, **Test**, **Delete** for a writer, the word **Test** for a reader (**View** was the name's link); a next key: the menu **Promote**, **Remove**; a withheld key: the menu **Reinstate**, **Confirm retirement**, each asking first as before | Every list in one form; a reader's row is not a menu of one; the endpoint rules' menu also offers **Edit** beside the name | **Confirm retirement** loses its red: the confirmation dialog carries the warning |
| (b) **Edit** or **View** stays a word, the other actions in a menu beside it | A word and a menu | Edit one click away | Two forms in one cell; the word repeats the name's link |
| (c) Keep a red **Confirm retirement** beside the menu | A destructive word in the row | The danger is seen | A second form of a destructive row action; the rule's one frequent action beside the menu is the copy, not a rare erasure |

**Choice:** (a). The other four lists move without a choice: the saved views of the package list put **Rename**, **Make
default** (or **Remove default**) and **Delete** into the menu; a project's member offers **Remove** as a word, as a group's member
does; an endpoint's rule has no menu where it would hold only **Edit** (a reader whose rule is not served); **Clear** of an Ansible
tombstone and **Run now** of a scheduled task are quiet buttons. **Rationale:** the name is the way to the thing in every list,
so an action that only opens it repeats the name. The development agent revisits (c) if an operator retires a withheld key by
mistake.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-163. Code: [mapping-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/mapping-list.ts),
[deb-signing-keys.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/deb-signing-keys.ts),
[package-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-list.html),
[project-members.ts](../../web/src/app/features/projects/project-members.ts),
[endpoint-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/endpoints/endpoint-detail.html),
[ansible-tombstones.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/ansible-tombstones.ts),
[tasks-card.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/tasks-card.ts).

### Q-UI-651 · One pair of refresh controls in the page's header acts on the shown tab

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the three pages each had **Pause automatic refresh** and **Refresh now** in a header of their own.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The page is a route of its own around the tabs' routes: its header holds the pair, the shown tab registers what **Refresh now** reloads and reads the pause for its timer; the pause holds across the tabs while the page is open (chosen) | `SystemPage` with `SystemRefresh`, the tabs below its `router-outlet` | One header that does not move when the tab changes; one pause for the page, as the user meant it | A tab depends on the page's service |
| (b) Each tab keeps its own header with the pair, the strip under each | The profile's construction | Each tab stands alone | The header is drawn again on every change of tab; three pauses that forget each other |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the user pauses the page, not one tab, and a header that stays in place is the tabbed page
the owner asked for. The development agent revisits it if a tab needs a control of its own in the header.

### Q-UI-654 · The dashboard shows the state of the backup

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

clicks from the first screen of the admin area.

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A row **Last backup** in the card **Operations**: the last success as a relative time, **Overdue** or **No backup yet** as warning badges, and **View backups** in the card's foot (chosen) | One request more, `GET /system/backups/summary`, the Backups tab's own | A missing backup is seen on the first screen; no new API field; the card already holds the job queue | One more row in a card of four |

### Q-UI-661 · An entry of Recently opened is the project's mark and the repository's key

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the side bar is 15 rem wide (`--quader-nav-width`). A nested entry's label starts 36 px into the entry, inside the
navigation's 8 px of padding, so an entry has about 184 px for its text at 14 px, and about 156 px beside a mark of 20 px: some 20
characters of a key. The seed's keys run from `npm` to
`customer-portal-api-client-generated-from-the-openapi-document`; a project key is up to 32 characters.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The project's small mark (Q-UI-424, 20 px), then the key; the title and the accessible name "<key> in <project name> (<project>/<key>)" (chosen) | 28 px for the project, the rest for the key | The key, which names the repository, gets the room; the project is recognised by the same mark as in every list, and lights up under the pointer | Two projects with the same initial and the same key look alike until the pointer rests on them |
| (b) `project/key` as the text | The qualified name | Unambiguous at a glance | The project key takes half of the line: `web-frontend/npm-vend…` |
| (c) The key, and the project's name on a second line | Two lines per entry | Both readable | Twice the height of every other entry of the side bar |

**Choice:** (a). The key is one line with an ellipsis where it does not fit (`.recent-key`); the accessible name starts with the
visible key, so speech input finds it by what is shown. **Rationale:** the side bar names places by one short word; the mark is the
project's sign everywhere, and the full name is one hover away. The development agent revisits (b) if keys repeat across projects in
the walk.

### Q-UI-662 · The side bar confirms the remembered repositories once per session

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the store keeps qualified names in the browser (R-UI-096); a repository can be deleted, moved or closed to the caller
since. The start page asked `GET /api/v1/repositories?name=…` for its five each time it loaded and left out what was not returned
(Q-UI-406). The side bar is on every page of the main area; a request per navigation would be one request per click.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One request for the names the session has not asked yet, when the home side bar is shown; the answers kept per principal and authorization epoch (chosen) | The first page of the main area asks for five names; afterwards only a repository opened since is asked, alone | No dead link; nearly no traffic; the group is complete when it is opened | A repository deleted in the same session stays listed until the next epoch or reload; its page then says it is not found |
| (b) One request when the group is opened | Nothing asked while folded | Less traffic for whoever never opens it | The group's existence ("not shown while there is none") cannot be decided folded; a list that changes as it opens |
| (c) The start page's way: one request per page that shows the side bar | Always current | Simple | One request per navigation |
| (d) No request: the store as it is | Instant | No traffic | A dead link for a repository the caller lost (Q-UI-406 (b)) |

**Choice:** (a). The request runs in an effect of the shell while the side bar shows the home area (pinned, or the drawer opened) and
the newest five hold an unasked name; a failed request leaves the names out until the store or the epoch changes. **Rationale:**
Q-UI-406's guarantee with the least traffic a part of every page deserves. The development agent revisits (b) if the request shows
in the measurements of the main area.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-167, R-UI-096 (Q-UI-406 holds). Code: [recent-repositories.ts](../../web/src/app/core/recent-repositories.ts),
[app.ts](../../web/src/app/app.ts).

**Revisited by [Q-UI-769](#q-ui-769--a-repository-that-is-gone-is-removed-from-the-browsers-store-by-the-screen-that-learns-it)**
(W-20): what stood against (a) is closed for a repository the person deletes or moves, and for one whose own page is not found; the
one request per session stays.

### Q-UI-769 · A repository that is gone is removed from the browser's store by the screen that learns it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the gap Q-UI-662 (a) left, from the plan (W-20): a repository deleted during a session stayed in **Recently opened** until
the next sign-in or change of permissions, and its entry led to "not found". The group asks the server once per session
(Q-UI-662), and that stays: no request per navigation. The same store feeds the search field's frequently visited repositories
(R-UI-096), which showed the deleted repository as long. The content page recorded a visit as soon as it had its address, before
the server answered, so the page of a repository that does not exist put its name into the store.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The screen that learns that a repository is gone removes its name from the store (`FrequentPlaces.forgetRepository`): the settings page and the list when the person's deletion is accepted, the settings page after a move, the content page and the settings page when the repository's document is answered with 404; a visit is recorded only after the server answered with the repository, and not for one that is being deleted (chosen) | One write to the browser's store where the fact is already known | No request; the side bar and the search follow at once, because both read the store; the next stored repository moves up into the five; a page that is not found leaves nothing behind | A repository somebody else deleted stays listed until the person opens it once; a repository that was only closed to the person and answers 404 loses its count of visits |
| (b) Keep the name stored and mark it unreadable in the session's answers | The side bar's answers get a third state | The count of visits survives | The search field keeps its own answers and would need the same; the name keeps one of the five places, so the group shows four; the mark is gone after a reload, the dead entry is back |
| (c) Ask the server again after a deletion and after a 404 | One more `GET /api/v1/repositories?name=…` | The server's word | A request for what the screen already knows; while the deletion's job runs the server still lists the repository |
| (d) Ask on every navigation (Q-UI-662 (c)) | Always current | Also finds what others deleted | One request per click, which Q-UI-662 ruled out |

**Choice:** (a). The deletion counts when the server accepted it, not when its job ended: the person typed the key to confirm it,
and the page that would hear the job's end may be left by then. **Rationale:** the fact is known in the browser at the moment it
happens, the store is the one source of both readers, and removing the name is what `forgetProject` already does for a deleted
project. The development agent revisits (d) in a cheaper form (an event from the server, or a check when the group is opened) if
repositories deleted by other people show as dead entries in the walk.

What it leaves: a repository that another person or an API client deleted stays in the group until its entry is opened once, which
answers "not found" and removes it, or until the authorization epoch changes. The page **Set up client** removes nothing when it
does not find its repository. A project the person deletes already leaves the project switcher and the search (the screen removes
it and reads the projects again); a project somebody else deleted stays in the switcher's recent list and among the search's
frequently visited projects until the list of projects is read again (the next load of the app, or a project the person creates,
changes or deletes). A name the server did not list
when the session asked, and that exists again later, stays out of the group until the next epoch.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-167, R-UI-096. Code: [frequent-places.ts](../../web/src/app/core/frequent-places.ts),
[repository-detail.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-detail.ts),
[repository-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.ts),
[repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts).

| (a) No field in the header; **Set up client** first of the header's actions, before **Settings** and the menu; the settings show no address (chosen) | One button where a field and a button were | The owner's rule; the header is the title, the facts and the actions, as every page's; the special narrow flow goes | Copying the address is one click further: Set up client, then copy |

### Q-UI-680 · A list stacks where its columns at their least widths do not fit, measured by the table itself

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Follows
the plan's words for W-5: "the threshold follows the table's columns".

Context: every data table stacked its rows below 49 rem of its frame (Q-UI-306, Q-UI-330), and the administrator's token list below
65 rem (`stackWide`, Q-UI-332). At 1,024 px with the side bar open a list has about 44 rem, so every list of the app stood as
blocks there, also a folder's three columns. A list whose columns needed more than 49 rem was wider than its place above it: the
start page's projects at 1,100 px, its **Members** out of sight. Since Q-UI-563 a column that never breaks declares no width, so
no number in the stylesheet can know what a list needs.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The table measures itself: its least width (each wrapping column at its declared `width` or its longest word, each column that never breaks at its longest value) against the room of its scroll region, again when its width or its rows change; it sets `stacked` where the room is less (chosen) | A `ResizeObserver` on a ruler of no height across the list, the measurement in the same task | The threshold is the list's own, also for a column without a width and for the rows a page loads later; no number to maintain | Script in the layout: the table is laid out twice when it is measured |
| (b) A threshold per list, summed from its columns' declared widths, in a container query per list | CSS only | No measurement | A column that never breaks has no declared width (Q-UI-563), so the sum is a guess again; a container query cannot read a property, so every list needs a rule of its own |
| (c) Keep 48 rem and lower it for short lists | Numbers | Small | The same defect at the next list; a list that needs 60 rem still overflows |

**Choice:** (a), in [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts) (`measure`): the table is given no width, so it
lays out at its least, then its width back; a stacked table leaves its blocks for that measurement and goes back in the same task,
so nothing is painted between. `stackWide` is gone. The observed elements are a ruler of no height and the scroll region, and
only a change of a width measures, so the change of the frame's height that the stacking makes starts no second round of the
observer. The region is observed because a scrollbar beside the rows narrows it while the ruler keeps its width: the admin area's
repositories at 1,280 px, with the window grown and shrunk back, stood 10 px wider than their region (2026-11-21). **Rationale:** what a list needs is a property of its
columns and its rows, and only the browser knows it. The development agent revisits the measurement if a list with hundreds of
rows makes a resize slow.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-174; Q-UI-306, Q-UI-308, Q-UI-330 and Q-UI-332 revised in their stacking threshold. Code:
[data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts), [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) (Stacked
rows).

### Q-UI-681 · A stacked row puts its cells side by side

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Follows
the plan's words for W-5: "the stacked form is denser than a line per cell". **Superseded by
[Q-UI-1050](#q-ui-1050--a-stacked-row-is-a-grid-of-names-and-values-one-field-a-line)**: side by side, a field stood at another place
in every block.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The name and the actions on the first line, then the other cells side by side, each its column's name and its value, as many to a line as fit; a long value takes a line and breaks inside itself (chosen) | A flex row with a break after the first line | Three or four short facts on one line at 390 px; the same markup, the head kept for assistive technology | Facts of different rows do not stand under each other |
| (b) One line per cell, as before | Q-UI-306 | Every fact at the same place | 33 versions 5,136 px high |
| (c) Two columns of facts | A grid | Facts under each other | A short fact takes half the row; a long one breaks into a narrow column |

**Choice:** (a). The facts are 20 px apart, their names muted (`data-label`), an empty cell left out. **Rationale:** a stacked row
is read, not compared; what makes it long is the line each short fact took. The development agent revisits (c) if a stacked list
is used to compare rows.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-174; Q-UI-306 revised. Code: [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss).

### Q-UI-682 · The render run measures the layout in the page, and a finding fails the screen

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Follows
the owner's W-5: "Can you not see something like this yourself?"

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Each picture's page is measured once by a script of rules (an icon apart from its label, a short thing in two lines, a row off its line, a cut text with room, sideways scroll, a stacked table that fits); a finding fails the screen with its element, its text, the width and the scheme; a finding that is right is allowed by a written reason beside the checks (chosen) | `layoutFindings` in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), one `page.evaluate` per state, in the light scheme | Exact and cheap; the same rules as the style guide's, each with its check; the run stays green only where the pictures pass them | Only what a rule names is found |
| (b) Compare each picture with an approved one | Pixel diff | Finds any change | Every intended change is a diff; the defects of W-3 were in approved pictures |
| (c) The development agent looks harder | No tool | Nothing to build | The defects were looked at and passed |

**Choice:** (a). The checks and their blind spots are listed in [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen); each
rule is a requirement (R-UI-170 to R-UI-174). The dark scheme has the light one's layout and is not measured again. **Rationale:**
the defects the owner found had a measurable form; a rule that measures it finds it in every picture, where an eye finds it in
the one it looks at. The development agent revisits a check whose allowed list grows longer than its findings.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-170 to R-UI-174. Code: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts),
[render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts), [sheet.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/sheet.ts).

### Q-UI-683 · An address field is as wide as its address, at least the measure, at most its line

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the render's check `clipped` found the address on Set up client cut after 70 characters with 500 px free beside it
(`setup-deb`, `setup-long-key` at 1,440 px: the seed's addresses of 89 and 96 characters). Since W-20 that header is the one place

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field is as wide as its address with its button, at least `--quader-address-measure` and at most its line, measured in characters of the field's font as the command field is (chosen) | `--quader-address-chars` on the field | A long address is read whole where there is room; fields of one stack keep one width while their addresses are shorter than the measure | A stack with one long address has one wider field |
| (b) Keep the measure as the cap | Q-UI-301 | Every field one width | The address cut beside empty room, which the owner objected to in W-5's kind |
| (c) The field always fills its line | No measure | Simple | A short address in a field far wider than it (R-UI-085) |
