### Q-UI-686 · The UI development profile gives an anonymous address the budget of a signed-in reader

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the anonymous screens of `make ui-renders` (`projects-anonymous`, `search-field`, `guides`, the setup of a public
repository) got 429 for `whoami`, the banner, the projects and the login options in every run: the anonymous visitors of the three
workers share the address 127.0.0.1, and the class `anonymous` (5 a second, burst 20, per address, R-API-016) is spent when three
of them open a page at once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The profile's `api.rate_limits.anonymous` is 50 a second with a burst of 200, the default of `read` (chosen) | One setting of [up.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/up.sh), beside the profile's `read` | Deterministic for any number of workers; no product default changes | The profile does not show an anonymous visitor's 429; the limiter's own tests do |
| (b) The anonymous screens in one serial project | Playwright | The profile keeps the default | One visitor's page already makes eight to ten calls; a walk of many states depends on timing |
| (c) A forwarded address of its own per worker (`X-Forwarded-For`) | Realistic visitors | The default stays | Depends on the proxy's and the trusted proxies' handling; one heavy walk can still spend its budget |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the renders show the screens, not the limiter; the profile already lifts `read` for the same
reason. The development agent revisits (c) if the renders are to show the 429 of an anonymous visitor.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-173 (a run that ends green). Code: [up.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/up.sh); documented in
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#local-ui-development).

### Q-UI-710 · An ended session at load goes to the sign-in screen with a notice, also while there is public content

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-19** ("Option A", W-21: the sign-in screen with the notice that the session has ended,
from three: that screen, on as a visitor without a word, the server counting a dead cookie as no credential). How the UI tells the
case apart is **decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `authGuard` loaded the session and took every 401 of `whoami` for "not signed in"; with `publicContent` true it started a
visitor that still sent the dead cookie, and every request answered `session_expired` ([identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)
Q-AUTH-410). The answer of `whoami` now clears the cookie, so the browser is a visitor from its next request on; the UI has to say
what happened before it lets the person on.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The session store reads the problem's `code`: `session_expired` is the state `ended`, which the guard sends to `/login?returnTo=<route>&ended=1`; every other 401 is `anonymous` as before (chosen) | One new state, one new branch of the guard | The status stays what R-AUTH-002 fixes; the code is the contract that already tells an ended session from none; `ended` is loaded again on the next navigation, which is then a visitor's | None found |
| (b) The guard runs on as a visitor and shows a notice in the shell | A banner "Your session has ended" above the public screens | No detour | Against the owner's choice; a person looking for a private project sees an empty list under a banner |
| (c) Any 401 with a cookie goes to the sign-in screen | The UI cannot see the cookie (`HttpOnly`) | None | Not buildable |

**Choice:** (a). The shell shows nothing for the state `ended`; the guard has left for the sign-in screen, which stands without the
shell (Q-UI-125). **Rationale:** the code was there and is the stable contract; the state keeps the decision in one place. The
development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004, R-UI-057. Code: [session-store.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.ts) (`SessionState`
`ended`), [auth-guard.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.ts). Tests: [auth-guard.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.spec.ts),
[session-store.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-711 · The sign-in screen learns the reason from `ended=1` and takes it out of the address

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the guard and the sign-in screen are separate routes, and the screen is also opened from links (the top bar's **Sign in**,
**Signed out**, a bookmark). Whatever tells the screen the reason can be put into a link from outside; the screen must not show a
text the link chooses, and a reload of the screen should not keep claiming an ended session.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A query parameter `ended=1` that selects a fixed notice; the screen keeps the notice for the visit and replaces the address without it (chosen) | As `reauth=1` of the re-authentication | Visible and testable; a link can show nothing but the one fixed sentence; a reload shows the screen without the notice | One more navigation (`replaceUrl`) as the screen opens |
| (b) The router's navigation state (`history.state`) | Not in the address | A link from outside cannot set it | Survives a reload in the browser's history entry, so the notice comes back on every reload; harder to test |
| (c) The session store's state | The screen reads `SessionStore.state()` | No parameter | Lost on a reload of the sign-in screen, which is fine, but the screen then depends on how it was reached in the same tab only, and a guard in another tab cannot pass it |

**Choice:** (a). Only the value `1` shows the notice; any other value shows nothing. The notice is the plain status line of the
re-authentication notice (`<p role="status">`), with the words of the dialog of R-UI-004: "Your session has ended. Sign in again to
continue where you left off." **Rationale:** the pattern exists (`reauth=1`), and the worst a forged link can do is say a session
ended. The development agent would revisit this if the notice is used to mislead in practice, then with (b).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004. Code: [login.ts](../../web/src/app/features/login/login.ts) (`ended`, `sessionEnded`). Tests:
[login.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/login/login.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-712 · An ended session waives the automatic sign-in only where there is a choice

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: with `autoRedirect` set, the sign-in screen leaves for the provider at once (R-AUTH-009); an identity provider with a live
session of its own signs the person in silently. The owner's choice offers, while there is public content, to continue without
signing in, which an immediate redirect would never show.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ended=1` waives `autoRedirect` while `publicContent` is true, and only then (chosen) | With public content: the notice, the providers and "Continue without signing in"; without it: the redirect as before | The choice is shown where there is one; where there is none, the operator's "send everyone straight there" stays and the person is signed in again without a click | Without public content the notice is not seen (the screen shows "Redirecting to the identity provider." for a moment) |
| (b) `ended=1` always waives it | The notice everywhere | The person always reads why | One click more on every installation with one provider and nothing public, for nothing to choose |
| (c) It never waives it | As before | No special case | The choice of the owner's option is never offered on an installation with `autoRedirect` |

**Choice:** (a). The break-glass form does not appear for `ended=1`; that stays `?auto_sign_in=false` (Q-UI-125).
**Rationale:** the notice exists to support a choice; where the operator removed the choice, the shortest way back in is the right
one. The development agent would revisit this if people on such installations report not knowing why they passed the provider.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004. Code: [login.ts](../../web/src/app/features/login/login.ts). Tests:
[login.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/login/login.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-713 · After the dialog of an end during use, the ended cookie makes a visitor

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a session that ends while the application is open shows the dialog "Your session has ended" (R-UI-004); its **Sign in
again** opens the sign-in screen. Only `whoami` clears the cookie (Q-AUTH-410), and the dialog does not call it, so the cookie is
still there when the person chooses "Continue without signing in" on that screen: the guard's `whoami` then answers
`session_expired`, and without a rule the person would land on the sign-in screen a second time, now with the notice.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The dialog's flag (`SessionStore.ended`) marks the end as told; the next load that meets `session_expired` is `anonymous`, and the flag is consumed (chosen) | One condition in the store | One landing on the sign-in screen, as on the load path; nothing new on the server | A rule that depends on what the tab has shown |
| (b) The dialog calls `whoami` to clear the cookie | The cookie goes at once | No second landing | A second way of clearing in the UI, a request from a dialog, and the window of H-1004 once more |
| (c) Accept the second landing | No change | Simplest | The person has read the notice twice and pressed "Continue without signing in" twice |

**Choice:** (a). "Not now" keeps the page as it is (R-UI-004): the guard does not run on a navigation inside the application,
and the next load of a page in the browser meets the cookie at `whoami`, which is the load path of Q-UI-710 with its notice; no
second mechanism clears the cookie. **Rationale:** the condition is the fact the dialog created; the load path covers the rest.
The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-004. Code: [session-store.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.ts) (`doLoad`, `markEnded`).
Tests: [auth-guard.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/auth-guard.spec.ts), [session-store.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/core/session-store.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-720 · A control is centred on the line by margins of half the difference, read from the line's height

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Follows
the owner's W-23 of 2026-11-19 ("ein für alle mal absichern").

Context: the first full run with the checks of Q-UI-721 (331 screens, 2,876 findings) grouped into seven causes of defects: an
icon of a line of text placed by `vertical-align: middle` or at a top-aligned row's top (1,482: a visibility level's icon, a
notice's, a status's; the middle of `vertical-align: middle` is the lower-case letters', 1.5 to 1.7 px under the line's); the
actions beside a heading (394: a page's and a file's actions, 2 px above the heading's line); a 32 px control at a row's top
beside a name (303: the owner's row, a path's copy button and menu, a digest's copy button); a badge or a status at
`vertical-align: middle` (79); a stacked row's actions at the block's top (62); a mark on the last baseline (57); a picture of the
wrong size or alignment (20). Each place that had centred a control did it with a constant of its own line (`1rem` in a list's
cell, `1.5 × 14 px` in a settings table, `1lh` of the project's mark), so the owner's row, whose button stood one box deeper than
the cell's rule reached, had none.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One line rule: every box hands the height of its line to what it holds (`--quader-line`, a registered length set to `1lh` on every element), a control or an icon takes its parent's instead of its own, and is centred by `margin-block: calc((var(--quader-line) - <its height>) / 2)` at the line's top; the icons of running text, the badges and statuses, the mark and the check boxes carry it, a 32 px control carries it as `on-line` and in a cell (chosen) | [_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss) | One formula for every line (16 px in a cell, 21 px in a paragraph, 28 px in a path); the control makes the line no taller; a long text keeps the control on its first line | A registered property on every element; a 32 px control beside a text needs the class |
| (b) `align-items: center` in every row | Flex | Simple | Centres on the whole text: the control leaves the first line as soon as the text wraps, and a 32 px control makes a line of 21 px 32 px high |
| (c) Keep a constant per place | As before | Nothing to change | The defect of the owner's row: the next place without its constant |

**Choice:** (a). A box of controls beside a heading takes the heading's line as its height (a page's actions) or as its line (a
file's actions). `vertical-align: middle` and `align-items: last baseline` are refused by a lint rule (Q-UI-725). A badge is 20 px
whatever it holds, so the rule centres a box of known height. A picture beside a name and its second line uses its own size: the
project switcher shows the medium mark, as Q-UI-424 says. **Rationale:** what was wrong in every cause was the line a control was
centred on, and only the box around it knows that line; a registered length computes `1lh` where it is set and inherits the
pixels (its first value must not depend on anything: with `1.3125rem` the browser dropped the property, which the guard of
Q-UI-725 found). The development agent revisits the class `on-line` if a 32 px control beside a text is found without it more
than once.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-175; R-UI-172 (the table's controls read the same line). Code:
[_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss), [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss),
[_catalog-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_catalog-screens.scss), [page-header.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/page-header.ts),
and the screens of each cause. Tests: [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) (the shared patterns).

### Q-UI-721 · A control's text is the nearest text of its row, found through the boxes that lay out the row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Follows
the owner's W-23 of 2026-11-19: "Kannst du das bitte einmal für das gesamte Frontend überprüfen und ein für alle mal absichern".

Context: `icon-apart` looked for an icon's label among the icon's own siblings, so the glyph inside the button that opens a row
was compared with nothing (its only sibling was itself), and the button with nothing either: the name beside it was the sibling of
the button, not of the glyph. `row-offset` compared the texts of a row's cells with each other, and they stood on one line.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The outermost control or icon is the unit (the glyph of a button is the button); its text is the next sibling with visible text outside every unit, else the previous one, else the same among its parent's siblings, and so on up to the table's cell or eight boxes; the box that lays out the two decides whether they are a row: a flex row (one of its lines unless it wraps), a grid's row (they share height), running text (inline boxes; the line may break); a flex column, a grid's other row or a block above or below ends the search as "laid out so on purpose" (chosen) | `textOfUnit` in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) | Finds the owner's row (the name's box is the button's next sibling), a copy button after a hash in a box of its own, a status in a cell beside its word; decides "row" by the layout the browser applied, not by a list of classes | A text that stands beside a control without belonging to it (a page's title beside its buttons) is compared too |
| (b) A list of row classes (`.name-cell`, `.icon-name`, `.check-row`, …) whose children are compared | Selectors | Exact for the listed rows | The next screen's row has a class nobody listed; the owner's row was the case nobody listed |
| (c) Every control against every text it shares height with | Geometry only | No structure needed | Compares a toolbar's button with the paragraph whose last line it touches; columns of a grid side by side are "beside" each other |

**Choice:** (a). The table's row is the check `row-offset`'s (R-UI-172): the search ends at the cell, a control in a cell with text
is measured against that text, and a cell with no text (an action cell, a check box's cell) by its controls against the row's name.
Hidden content is not measured: a box without size, `visibility: hidden` (a closed collapse region), `[hidden]`, a text for
assistive technology only, and what is positioned out of the flow (a field's magnifier). **Rationale:** what is a row is decided by
the layout the browser applied, which is exactly what the person sees; a list of classes is what failed. A text that stands in the
same row as a control without belonging to it stands on the same line by the same rule, so (a)'s "against" is no defect. The
development agent revisits (a) if a finding pairs a control with a text of another row.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-170, R-UI-175, R-UI-176. Code: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts). Tests:
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-722 · The tolerance of a middle is 1 px, what the rounding of a centred unit leaves

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the middle of a text is the middle of its glyphs' box (the font's ascent and descent), which is the middle of its line when
the line is centred on it. Chromium rounds the ascent and the descent of a font to whole pixels and lays boxes out in 1/64 px: the
name of the owner's row stands 0.5 px above its line's middle (Inter at 14 px on a line of 16 px). Measured in
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) on 60 units centred by the rule (the text sizes 12, 13, 14
and 16 px, the lines 1rem, 1.25rem and 1.5, units of 16 to 32 px): the largest distance of a centred unit's middle from its text's
middle is 0.75 px. Measured on defects: a badge or an icon at `vertical-align: middle` stands 1.7 px low (the middle of the
lower-case letters, not of the line), a mark on the last baseline 3.5 px high, the owner's button 8.5 px low.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 1 px (chosen) | `LINE_TOLERANCE` | Above every centred unit measured (0.75 px), below every defect measured (1.7 px) | A defect of exactly 1 px is not found |
| (b) 1.5 px, the old tolerance of `row-offset` between fonts | | Fewer findings | Passes nothing that (a) does not, but brings no unit closer; the 1.7 px of `vertical-align: middle` is only 0.2 px away |
| (c) 0.5 px | | Strictest | The rounding alone reaches 0.75 px: correct rows would fail |

**Choice:** (a), for the middles of every check (`off-line`, `icon-apart` measures no middle, `row-offset`); the baselines of
`row-offset` are no longer compared (R-UI-172). **Rationale:** the tolerance is the measured rounding, rounded up; every defect of
this kind the owner or the checks found is larger. The development agent revisits the value if the fonts or their sizes change (the
test logs the largest distance on every run).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-172, R-UI-175. Code: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) (`LINE_TOLERANCE`). Tests:
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) (the sweep, and 1.5 px found, 0.5 px not).

### Q-UI-723 · The checks are tested on fixture pages in the Playwright Chromium, not in the Angular test runner

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The
fixtures run in Firefox and WebKit too since [Q-UI-1045](#q-ui-1045--the-layout-checks-fixtures-run-in-three-engines-and-chromium-sets-text-without-hinting).

Context: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) had no test of its own; a check was proven only by a full render run, which
needs the stack and takes about 20 minutes, and the run that passed the owner's row proved nothing about it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A Playwright project of its own (`web/e2e/playwright.layout.config.ts`, `make ui-layout-test`): each test sets a page's content (a few elements, the app's fonts from `node_modules`), runs `layoutFindings` and names the findings it must have; `make ui-renders` runs it first (chosen) | The Chromium the renders use | Real layout, real fonts; two seconds; no stack, no seed; the same function the renders run | A browser to install (`npx playwright install chromium`), as for the renders |
| (b) The Angular test runner (Vitest) | `ng test` | Runs with `make web-test` | jsdom lays nothing out: every box is 0×0, a check measures nothing; Vitest's browser mode is not installed |
| (c) A render screen of fixtures in the app | A route of the app | In the run | Ships test pages in the product; proves the check only inside a full run |

**Choice:** (a). The owner's row as he measured it (65 px, the button's middle 32 px, the name's 24 px) is the first fixture and
must fail; each exception of R-UI-175 is a fixture that must pass. **Rationale:** a check is code with a failure mode of its own; it
needs a test that fails without it, and only a browser lays out. The development agent revisits a CI step for it with the
owner's decision on the renders in CI.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-176. Code: [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts),
[playwright.layout.config.ts](../../web/e2e/playwright.layout.config.ts), the `Makefile` target `ui-layout-test`,
[renders.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/renders.sh).

### Q-UI-724 · The exceptions are layouts, not places: above or below, a field under its label, a picture, a mark after its text, a framed box, a word that wraps

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The owner
asked for few exceptions, stated exactly (W-23).

Context: the first full run with the checks of Q-UI-721 named 2,876 findings; 479 of them were layouts the style guide asks for,
not defects: a copy button beside a code block or Add and Remove beside a list box (346; the control stands at the box's frame),
a grade's shield as a card's figure (66), a badge that wrapped under a date like a word (67).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Six, each decided by the layout, none by a screen: a control laid out above or below its text (a flex column, a grid's other row, a block of its own: a tile, an empty state), or in a column of controls without a text (Add, Remove and the moves between two lists, a toolbar of its own); a field with its label above it, and a control of several lines (a text area is no unit); a picture (an avatar, a project's mark, a grade's shield, a `.picture`) at least 1.5 lines high, centred on the first two lines of its text (Q-UI-424: the medium mark beside a name and its key) or on all of it, its buttons included (a card's figure); a mark after its text, which may stand on the text's last line (a "new window" mark after a link of two lines); a control beside a framed box (a block with a border, or a fill and padding, at the control's height: a code block, a list of members), which stands on the box and is not measured; a control with a word of its own (a badge, a status, a chip), which may wrap to a line of its own (chosen) | `textOfUnit`, `PICTURE`, `framed`, `ATTACHED` in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) | Each is a layout the style guide asks for; none lets a button beside a name through: a button is never a picture, and a name is no framed box | A control beside a box with a border is not measured at all, also where it stands off the box |
| (b) The same and a list of allowed screens | `allowed` | | Hides the next defect of its kind on that screen |
| (c) No exceptions | | | An empty state's large icon above its sentence, every field under its label, every copy button of a snippet would be findings |

**Choice:** (a). A control that a wrapping row moved to its next line (a toolbar at 390 px) is not a finding either: wrapping is how a
row of controls fits; an icon, a mark, a check box or a copy button that a wrapping row moved away from its text is (`icon-apart`).
**Rationale:** the exceptions are layouts, not places, so a new screen gets the same rule without an entry, and `allowed` stays
without an entry for these checks. The development agent revisits the picture exception if a 32 px button is ever drawn as a
picture, and the framed box if a control beside a box is found off it by eye.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-175. Code: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts). Tests:
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) (the exceptions' fixtures).

### Q-UI-725 · The guard without a stack renders the shared patterns with the global stylesheet, and a lint rule refuses the off-line declarations

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the renders find a control off its line on a screen they show, after 20 minutes and with the stack; a change of a shared
rule should fail before that. The causes of the first run had two forms a static rule can see: the declarations
`vertical-align: middle` and `align-items: last baseline`; and a control at a row's top without the line rule, which depends on the
row's layout.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two guards: the shared patterns of the style guide (a list's row, a settings table, an icon of a line, a badge in a heading, a check box, a link's mark, a project's mark) built from the global classes and rendered with `web/src/styles` compiled, on the fixture pages of Q-UI-723, must have no finding; and a lint rule refuses `vertical-align: middle` and `align-items: last baseline` in every style of `web/src`, except `vertical-align` on a table's cell, which aligns the cell's content (chosen) | `make ui-layout-test`, `make web-lint`; seconds | The patterns guard the shared rule in a browser (they found its first version void: a `rem` as a registered property's first value drops the property); the lint rule catches the commonest cause where no screen shows it (nine places after the screens' fixes, all changed) | A component's own rows are not in the patterns; a top-aligned row without the line rule is not seen statically |
| (b) A template rule: a `.btn` in a flex row with a text, without `on-line` | Static | No browser | Whether a row is a row and its items stand at its top is a property of the styles, often of another file: false alarms or misses |
| (c) Only the renders | | | 20 minutes and the stack per check |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** each guard is honest about what it sees: the lint rule refuses two declarations that are never the
line's middle, the patterns prove the shared rule in a browser. The development agent revisits (b) if a defect of a top-aligned row
recurs in a component.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-176. Code: [line-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/line-rule.mjs), [check-rules.mjs](../../web/scripts/check-rules.mjs),
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts). Tests: [lint-rules.test.mjs](../../web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs).

### Q-UI-753 · A download of the UI asks for its first byte before the browser downloads it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the UI's downloads are links the browser follows (`<a download>`); a 429 then ends as a failed download in the browser,
and the page learns nothing (R-UI-186 asks for a notice).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A click first sends `GET` with `Range: bytes=0-0`; a 429 shows the notice, any other answer lets the browser download (chosen) | — | The probe passes the same admission (R-LIM-021, a `206` is a download), so the refusal is known before anything is saved; the browser keeps its own download with its progress | One request more and one byte per download; a budget used up between the two requests ends as the browser's failed download |
| (b) Fetch the whole file into the page and hand it to the browser | — | One request | A large file is held in memory, and the browser shows no progress until it is complete |
| (c) A hidden frame | — | One request | A problem answer forbids framing (`frame-ancestors 'none'`): the page reads nothing |

**Choice:** (a). Revisit when a refusal can reach the page another way. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-186. Code:
[download-link.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/download-link.ts).

| (b) One chart of bytes (two series) and one of requests | — | Two charts | Two series told apart by colour alone in the dark scheme |
| (c) One chart, two axes | — | Compact | A second axis is read against the wrong series |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-184. Code: [usage-history.ts](../../web/src/app/features/usage/usage-history.ts).

development agent's look at the renders of 2026-11-19). Measured as the table measures itself (its columns at their least widths,
the renders of 2026-11-19, an administrator's list with **Rotate** and **Revoke**): with the last 24 hours under the limit the list
still needed 728 px (**Token** 160 at 8 rem, **Limit** 157, **Expires** 109, **Last used** 127, the actions 175) and had 872 px at
1440 px and 688 px at 1024 px.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Limit** holds the limit on the row's line and the last 24 hours as its second line ("95,695 requests · 518.8 GB in 24 h", "Not used in 24 h", whole from 50 rem of the list, broken between requests and bytes below); the secret's expiry stands beside its hint in **Token** ("qdr_sat_kMbd · expires in 2 months", **Expires soon** under it); the ended tokens' list shows no limit (chosen) | Measured: 651 px at 1024 px, up to 721 px at 1440 px; the ended list 603 px (**Token** 192, **Ended**, **Last used** 127, **Issue new secret** 175); both are tables at 1440 and 1024 px, blocks at 390 px | Two columns less; the limit and what it limits read together, and so do a secret and its end; the ended list keeps when and how a token ended | No column **Expires** to scan; an ended token's rule shows again only with its new secret |
| (b) **Limit** with its second line and **Token** at 8 rem, the column **Expires** kept | — | The column of R-UI-026's token lists | 728 px: blocks at 1024 px |
| (c) A column **Last 24 hours** of its own and the section as wide as the page | — | Every figure a column | The page's column is the house's measure for a detail page; still blocks at 1024 px |
| (d) Drop **Last used** from the list | — | Room | The one figure that says whether a system still uses its token |

**Choice:** (a). An ended token downloads nothing; its rule stays and shows in the active list when **Issue new secret** gives it a
secret again (Q-UI-740). **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-181. Code:
[technical-token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/features/service-accounts/technical-token-table.ts),
[technical-tokens.ts](../../web/src/app/features/service-accounts/technical-tokens.ts),
[technical-token-limit.ts](../../web/src/app/features/limits/technical-token-limit.ts).

### Q-UI-762 · The cells of a stacked row's line stand on one baseline

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a stacked row (R-UI-174) centred its cells on each line of the block. An ended token's **Ended** holds the time and under it
**Expired** or **Revoked**; centred against **Limit** and **Last used** of one line, its name stood half a line above theirs at 1440
px, and at 390 px it floated beside them (the development agent's look at the renders of 2026-11-19). The render checks did not see
it: `row-offset` measures a stacked row's first line only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The cells of a block stand on one baseline, the first line of each; a value of two lines grows downwards; two checks in the renders, `stacked-offset` (the names of one line on one middle) and `label-apart` (a value under its name) (chosen) | One rule in `_list-screens.scss` for every list | Every block of every list, and the next cell of two lines is found by the renders and by a fixture with the app's stylesheet | A field's frame in a block stands on the baseline as before (R-UI-175) |
| (b) Cells at the line's top | — | Simple | A cell whose first line is taller (a field, a link button) puts its name lower than its neighbours' |
| (c) The ended token's time and state on one line | — | This one cell | The next cell of two lines repeats it |

**Choice:** (a). `label-apart` finds a value only where its first piece (its first word, or its first box that does not break) would
fit beside its name: a media type that does not break and a link of its own box wider than the room start on the next line by right
(the full render run of 2026-11-19 had them, and a CI issuer's audience and an import's messages that did not have to). The name is
measured by a span of its text in its place: a mark of no width beside it wrapped in a flex cell and misreported a visibility level.
**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-174. Code: [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss),
[layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), fixtures in [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-240 · An Ansible package has a Documentation tab and a Contents tab; the README tab is its first page

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: task T-19. The owner's galaxy_ng shows, per collection version: Install (description, license, install command, download, requires Ansible), Documentation (search and tree), Contents, Import log, Dependencies, Distributions, and the links Docs site, Website, Issue tracker, Repo. Quader's package page (R-UI-007) already has an install panel, a Metadata tab (authors, license, `requires_ansible`, dependencies, links), Files, Repositories and All versions.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) For the format `ansible`: tabs **Documentation** (replaces README), **Contents**, Metadata, Files, Repositories, All versions, and **Import log** on a local repository (chosen) | Install = the install panel, Dependencies = a section of Metadata with links to the packages, Distributions = the Repositories tab, the links = the Metadata tab | Nothing exists twice; the page keeps the layout of the other formats; the new tabs are exactly what Quader lacks | Dependencies is not a tab of its own, which the reference has |
| (b) Mirror the reference's tab names one by one | Install, Documentation, Contents, Import log, Dependencies, Distributions | Familiar | An Install tab duplicates the sticky install panel; Distributions duplicates Repositories; the layout of R-UI-007 is a decision of the owner (Q-UI-3) |
| (c) Documentation only | No Contents tab | Smaller | The flat list "what is in this collection" is one click in the reference and cheap here (the tree's data) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the tabs of the reference that hold information Quader does not show yet are Documentation, Contents and the Import log; the rest are shown already, by the
install panel, the Metadata tab and the Repositories tab. **Documentation** is shown when `metadata.docs.state` is not `none` or the version has a README, and is the default tab
then (as README is elsewhere); its first page is the README. **Contents** is a data table (name, type, short description, a link to the page where `hasDocs`), a type filter, and
the count in its tab as a neutral badge; shown with the Documentation tab. **Import log** (local only) lists the import task of this version through `listAnsibleImportTasks`, extended by the optional query
parameters `package` and `version` (the tasks are readable by whoever reads the repository, R-ANS-009), newest first, state as a badge and the messages as text. All tabs are `<quader-tab-group>`
lazy tabs in GitLab's strip (design-language.md, Controls). A `404` of the documentation operations removes the tab without an error message (Q-UI-244). Dependencies is a section of the Metadata tab and the links of the reference are its links ([Q-UI-245](#q-ui-245--dependencies-and-the-links-of-the-reference-are-sections-of-the-metadata-tab-not-tabs-the-documentation-link-is-called-docs-site)). Revisit at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-007 (the tab list for the format), R-UI-060 to R-UI-064, [R-ANS-026](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-026--package-screens-and-the-deploy-dialog), [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-241 · The Documentation tab is the file browser's two panes: a tree with a search field, and the page

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Revised in part by [Q-UI-1112](#q-ui-1112--a-navigation-column-sticks-beside-the-page-with-a-scroll-of-its-own-any-other-side-column-sticks-only-while-it-fits)** (R-UI-215): the panes no longer scroll each on its own; the page pane scrolls with the page, and the tree sticks beside it with a scroll of its own.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two panes as the file browser (Q-UI-98): the tree pane (`clamp(18rem, 30%, 26rem)`) with the search field in its head, the page pane taking the rest (chosen) | The pattern of design-language.md "two panes" | Already built, specified and in the GitLab style (the wiki sidebar has this shape); each pane scrolls on its own; narrow widths show one pane with a back button | A tab inside a page that has its own two columns (tabs left, install panel right, R-UI-007): the content column is narrower |
| (b) A tree above the page | One column | Simple | The page scrolls away from the tree on long module pages |
| (c) A separate route for the documentation | `/packages/ansible/<name>/docs` | Full width | The page leaves the package page; the version selector and the install panel are lost |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the pattern exists and the owner chose it for hierarchies (design-language.md). The tree's rows are 32 px: the first row is **Documentation** (the README, the other
Markdown files below it as children), then the groups **Modules (8)**, **Plugins (24)** (children by type, each type collapsed at first with its count, expanded when it holds the current page or a search match) and **Roles (n)**, as the reference's
tree is, each group with its count as a neutral badge; an entry is a row with its name (the short description as the tooltip); an entry with `hasDocs` false is muted and labelled "no documentation". The selected row is
`--quader-accent-container`. The page is addressed by the query parameter `doc` of the package URL (`doc=README.md`, `doc=module/check_host_reachable`, `doc=file/install.md`), so a link, reload and back button work, and the tree follows it.
Under 48 rem of content width one pane shows at a time. The tree is a `role="tree"` of links (`aria-current="page"` on the open one), reachable by keyboard; it takes the width of the content container query, not of the viewport (the package
page is two columns from 960 px). Revisit if the owner finds the tab too narrow beside the install panel (then the install panel moves above the tabs for this tab).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-007, [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-242 · An entry page shows the plugin's documentation in the order ansible-doc prints it, from the structured answer

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A page head (full name with a copy button, short description, "added in", a deprecation notice), then the sections Synopsis, Parameters, Notes, Requirements, Attributes, See also, Examples, Return values, Authors, each only when it has content (chosen) | The structure of the answer of R-ANS-036 | Familiar to anyone who has read ansible-doc; a section appears only with content; prose is the server's sanitized HTML | A table with nested rows for suboptions is wide |
| (b) The raw `doc_strings` as formatted JSON | Whatever came | Trivial | Not documentation |
| (c) Tabs inside the page (Parameters, Examples, Return) | Fewer scrolls | Compact | A page of 59 KB (nmcli) in four tabs hides what the search matched |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** Parameters is the shared data table (no frame, hairlines): the columns are Name (with `aliases`), Type (and `elements`), Required (a text badge), Default, Choices and Description; a suboption row is
indented by its depth (16 px per level, a "suboptions of <name>" label for the screen reader) and a parameter with suboptions is collapsible with a chevron (open at first, Q-UI-252). Defaults, choices and samples are
text (typed JSON shown as written, a boolean as `true`/`false`). Examples and a sample are a `<pre>` in the same code block control as the README's, scrolling horizontally, with a copy button; there is no highlighting. A deprecated plugin
shows a `warn` badge. A role shows its README only. A page whose entry has `hasDocs` false shows the head and the line "This plugin has no documentation in its source." (generated) or "The upstream sent no documentation for this plugin." (upstream).
Below the page, one muted line says where the documentation comes from ("Generated by Quader from the archive, 2026-11-11 09:41" or "Taken from the upstream") and names the repository when the version is in more than one. States: `pending`
("The documentation of this version is being fetched.", with a refresh action), `unavailable` (the reason in words), `none` (no tab). Revisit at the walkthrough.

**Applied in the spec:** [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-243 · The search field filters the tree through the server and keeps the counts

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field in the tree pane head sends `q` to `getPackageVersionDocs` after 300 ms of silence and at least 2 characters; the tree shows the matching entries, the groups keep their counts and the head says "5 of 32" (chosen) | R-ANS-036 | Matches descriptions and parameter names the tree does not carry; one matching implementation; the counts of the reference's tree do not jump | A request per search |
| (b) Filter the loaded tree in the browser by name | No request | Instant | Names only; a second matching rule |
| (c) A search page | Results as a list | Room for snippets | Leaves the tab |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the search "inside the documentation" has to find a parameter by what it does, which only the server has. The field is a `text-input` with a search icon and an `aria-label` "Search the documentation"; Escape clears it; the
matches are a live region ("5 of 32 entries"); a search with no match shows "No entries match" in the pane, not an empty tree; the open page stays open while one searches; the query is the URL parameter `q`. Groups with no match are
hidden, groups with matches are expanded. Matching text is not highlighted on the page (no client-side matching). Revisit if the owner wants snippets.

**Applied in the spec:** [R-ANS-036](formats/ansible.md#r-ans-036--the-documentation-operations-of-the-screens-their-rendering-and-the-search).

### Q-UI-248 · The tree of the Documentation tab is the navigation tree of the keyboard library: a row is a link, a group is not selectable

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `@angular/aria`'s tree in navigation mode: a page is an `<a>` with `routerLink` and `aria-current="page"`, a group is a row that is not selectable and opens or closes on a click or the arrow keys (chosen) | R-UI-060 | The roving tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, type-ahead and the expand keys come from the library the file browser already uses; a row is a real link, so a modified click opens a new tab; `aria-current` is what R-UI-060 asks for | The treeitem role replaces the link role of the anchor, as the library's navigation mode does |
| (b) The same tree in selection mode, rows as `aria-selected` options | As the file browser | One pattern | A row is no link; `aria-current` is not set; a copied link needs the address bar |
| (c) A hand-written tree | Own key handling | No library coupling | A second tree implementation to keep accessible |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** R-UI-060 names links and `aria-current`; the library has a mode for exactly that, and the file browser's styles (`_browse.scss`) take `[aria-current='page']` as the selected row beside `[aria-selected='true']`. Revisit if the library drops the mode.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-060.

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the page announces the documentation in `metadata.docs` (Q-API-263), so the tab list needs no probe; the tree is requested lazily and the Refresh action of the state `pending` reads it again. Revisit if the documentation changes while a page is open.

### Q-API-290 · `package_anonymous` does not charge a request the decision point challenges

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The class
`package_anonymous` is removed by the owner's [Q-LIM-4](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-4--in-audit-nothing-on-a-protocol-path-is-refused-or-slowed-the-package-classes-of-r-api-016-included) (2026-11-19); the rule holds for the request figures of
[usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-005.

Context: with the visibility levels the authentication stage passes every request without a credential as the anonymous
subject, and the decision point answers the challenge where no `public` level admits it (R-AUTHZ-033). The challenge thereby
moved behind the rate limits of step 7: before, with anonymous access off, step 6 refused such a request before any class
counted it. A NuGet client sends each request without its configured credentials first and repeats it with them after the 401
(R-NUGET-012). The .NET SDK 10.0.403 (NuGet 7.9.0) of the acceptance suite does so for every resource, not only the service
index: in `e2e (nuget)` of 2026-11-12 (Test and Release 43282191873) each of the 308 paths the three restore sessions read
before the refusals began drew a 401 before its 200. Every first attempt was charged to `package_anonymous` of the client's address (20 per second, burst 100 by
default): each client of the cold restore of the reference solution (E3.2) had its first 100 to 104 attempts answered with the
challenge within 3 s and the next 344 to 405 with 429, and `dotnet restore` failed with NU1301; the single restore of R-REPO-055
through a mirror got 100 challenges, then 370 refusals. No request with the token was refused.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Step 7 asks the installed grant index: a request without a credential on a repository the index holds with artifacts that are not `public` is not charged (chosen) | `RateLimitOptions.Challenged`, `ChallengedByLevels` | One map lookup; the decision point still decides; a client with credentials pays only with its token, as before the levels; a `public` repository's anonymous reads keep their class | A request without a credential on such a repository is bounded only by step 4 (`max_in_flight`, the memory guard), as it was when step 6 refused it; it costs the path parse, the route match and one decision on the index, no database read; the stage reads the installed index, so a request whose decision runs on a newer one (a repository raised to `public` a moment ago) can pass once uncharged |
| (b) Give the charge back when the answer is the challenge | A decrement of the window's counter after the decision | Exact accounting of what was served | A path back into the limiter, in Valkey and in the fallback buckets; attempts in flight at once still count until their answers, so a client with more than `burst` of them is still refused |
| (c) Answer a request without a credential over its budget with the challenge instead of 429 | The client with credentials sends them | No index read in step 7 | A client without credentials on a `public` repository gets 401 instead of 429 and no `Retry-After`; the first attempts still fill the bucket that the address's anonymous readers share |
| (d) Raise the budget of `package_anonymous` | Configuration | No code | Any budget is exceeded by a larger solution or by CI jobs behind one address; it also raises what a caller without credentials gets on a `public` repository |
| (e) Step 6 challenges a request without a credential on a repository whose artifacts are not `public` | The stage reads the index | The challenge is where it was before the levels | A second place that decides what the anonymous subject reads, beside the decision point (R-AUTHZ-003); the refusal audit of the decision point is skipped |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the class of a request without a credential exists for callers who read without one; a first
attempt that the protocol repeats with credentials reads nothing, and its repetition is charged to the token. The rule is
conservative: what the index cannot answer (no repository in the path, a raw-file path, no installed index) is charged, and a
virtual repository whose own artifacts are `public` is charged even where a member is not. A key the index does not hold is
charged as well: its request looks the key up in PostgreSQL before the decision (R-ARCH-011 step 2), and without the charge a
caller without a credential could send one such query per invented key with no bound but step 4. `/files/` keeps charging its
`anonymous` class: its decisions are made while the service resolves the path, not in one check before any work, and no client
of the generic format in the e2e sets sends its credentials only after a 401. The development agent would revisit this if
challenged requests without a credential become a load that step 4 does not bound well enough, or if a raw-file client needs the
same rule.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-016 (the class table, the rule below it, the fields, two acceptance criteria);
[formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-012. Code: [ratelimit.go](../../internal/api/v1/ratelimit.go) (`Challenged`,
`ChallengedByLevels`), [wire_api.go](../../internal/app/wire_api.go). Tests: `TestRateLimitStage`,
`TestR_API_016_ChallengedByLevels`; `e2e (nuget)` `TestNuGetCollapse`, `TestNuGetMirror_R_REPO_055_ClientsFirst`.

mitzumachen. ... Zu viel Schrift." The page's own controls and text stay in the app's palette; "Bilder haben keine Einschränkungen

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) Variant A, calm: today's order and column; a snippet a window; a picture of the flow in the header and a rail along the steps; the credential one framed row; the sentences cut to what the window does not say; the guide a list of closed rows under **Guide** (chosen) | The page the owner knows, lighter | Nothing moves that readers learnt; the words up to the end of step 2 fell from 72 to 38 (npm) and from 157 to 45 (OCI) in the mockup | Less of a picture than the others |
| (b) Variant B, illustrated: a picture per step, the guide in a drawer | Pictures lead | The most inviting | The guide off the page, against ADR-202 |

### Q-UI-801 · A snippet's window is an editor for a file and a terminal for a command, coloured by its language

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: variant A (Q-UI-800) draws a file as an editor window and a command as a terminal window, with syntax colours. Something
has to decide which a snippet is, how it is coloured and how its long lines wrap, for every format, including those to come.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The window's kind from `fileName` (a file or a command), the colours from `language`, a small tokenizer of Quader's own per language, `powershell` and `cmd` sent as themselves (chosen) | The server's facts decide | A new format adds no highlighter and no case; the prompt of PowerShell and cmd is right; no dependency | The tokenizer knows the handful of shapes the templates write, not the whole of each language |
| (b) A highlighting library | Full grammars | Exact for any text | A dependency and its weight in the bundle for six short shapes |
| (c) Colours per format | Each format styles its snippets | Freedom | A new format adds code to the UI; two formats of one language look different |

**Choice:** (a). The window is `<quader-code-window>` ([code-window.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/code/code-window.ts)), the
tokenizer, the marks, the prompts and the wrap rule are pure functions of [code-syntax.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/code/code-syntax.ts).
A wrapped line keeps the indent of Q-UI-486; a flag, a mark and a token's reference of up to 32 characters never break, a longer
one (a token of 57 characters written into the snippet) may, so a window never scrolls sideways at 390 px; an address breaks after
its slashes. The colours are tokens `--quader-code-*` with a light and a dark value; palette.spec.ts holds each text colour at 4.5:1
on the window. The install panel's command of several lines is the same window (one look for a snippet); one of one line stays the
address field of Q-UI-320. Q-API-191 is superseded.

**Rationale:** the facts that decide a window are the server's, so the page stays format-free (FMT-001). The development agent
revisits it if a snippet's language needs more than its shapes (a long script), when a library may pay for itself.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-016, R-UI-121, R-API-030 (the languages). Code: [code-window.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/code/code-window.ts),
[code-syntax.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/code/code-syntax.ts), [client-command-menu.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.ts),
[packages_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/packages_api.go) `clientSnippet`, [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss).

### Q-UI-802 · The server names the reader's parts of a snippet, and an image has one word

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the window marks what the reader replaces and where the token goes. The mockup found them by pattern, and its OCI pull said
`<package>` where the push said `myapp:1.0`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The answer names them: `marks` of `{text, kind}` per snippet, from the token reference the credential mode wrote, the core's placeholders and the examples a template declares; the OCI pull shows the push's `myapp:1.0` when no package is asked (chosen) | The format declares, the UI shows | No guess; examples without brackets are found; a new format declares its own | A field in the answer and two in the format contract |
| (b) The UI guesses by pattern (`<…>`, `${…}`) | No API change | Cheap | Marks the tags of a `nuget.config`, misses `./acme-tools-1.0.0.tar.gz` |
| (c) The OCI push says `<package>` too | One word, no API change | Cheap | A shell reads `<package>` as a redirection; the push would not work as pasted even after a name was typed into one of two places |

**Choice:** (a), recorded as [ADR-208](../decisions.md#adr-208--a-setup-snippet-names-the-parts-that-are-the-readers-and-a-template-declares-its-examples).
The page writes a pasted token into the marks too, so it stays marked where it stands.

**Rationale:** the cheapest correct way: the template that writes an example is the one place that knows it is one. The development
agent revisits it if a mark's text also stands where it is not the reader's.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-030, R-UI-121. Code: [setup_snippets.go](../../internal/api/v1/setup_snippets.go) `snippetMarks`,
[oci/setup.go](../../internal/formats/oci/setup.go), [client-setup.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/client-setup.ts) `fillSnippet`.

### Q-UI-803 · A format adds one accent pair for its pictures; a format without one takes the neutral pair

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner wants one design for every format; the mockup coloured npm's pictures coral and OCI's sky blue.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One pair per format in the UI's catalog of format facts (`formatAccent` beside `formatIcon`), each a token of `_tokens.scss` with a light and a dark value, a neutral pair for any other format (chosen) | A fact of the format, in the pictures only | A format adds one line and one token; a new format looks right without one | The UI names the formats it has accents for, as it does for their logos |
| (b) The accent in the format's Go descriptor, sent by `GET /api/v1/formats` | The format owns it entirely | No UI change for a new format | A colour in the API; its contrast is outside palette.spec.ts |
| (c) No accent | One look | Simplest | The flow of every format looks the same, which the mockup the owner chose did not |

**Choice:** (a). npm coral `#e5535f` / `#f0717b`, OCI sky `#2f9fd6` / `#4db5e8` (the mockup's), NuGet violet `#7a5ad8` / `#a58ff2`,
Debian raspberry `#b8336a` / `#e9799f`, Ansible teal `#17998b` / `#45c7b7` (past the hue of the positive green), generic amber
`#c98a12` / `#e8b04a`; neutral `#8f97ad` / `#a9b1c4`. The accent fills the parcels and the glyph of the flow (a stack of layers for
OCI, a parcel for every other format) and the line over a window's tab; it is decoration, never text, never a control. No logo of
npm, Ansible Galaxy or Docker (Q-UI-225 to Q-UI-227).

**Rationale:** a picture may carry colour (the owner); a token keeps it reviewable in one place. The development agent revisits a
pair the owner objects to, and the place if formats come with brand colours of their own owners' terms.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-121. Code: [format-accent.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/format-accent.ts),
[_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss), [setup-flow-art.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/setup-flow-art.ts).

### Q-UI-804 · A snippet says only what its window does not, and a second way of a step is a fold

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the designer cut npm's and OCI's sentences ("Save as .npmrc in your project.", no sentence for an install). Every other
format and client was left to the builder, by the same rule.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One short sentence per snippet id, none where the window says it all; a second way of a step behind an inline fold after the step's own snippets; the sentence of an image's sign-in depends on the reader (chosen) | Less text, the plain path in view | One rule for every format: the words from the title to the end of step 2 fall by half or more | A fact the old sentence carried is now in the guide (why `ansible.cfg` holds no token, how a key rotation reaches a machine) |
| (b) Keep today's sentences, shorter | Less change | Every fact stays | Still two lines over every window |
| (c) No sentences at all | The windows alone | The least text | A file's place (next to the solution, in the home directory) is not in the window |

**Choice:** (a). The folds: **For a Kubernetes cluster** (OCI), **In PowerShell** and **In cmd** (NuGet, Ansible), **As a
nuget.config file** (.NET CLI, NuGet CLI), **As a one-line .list file** and **Remote without upstream keys** (APT; at first **For a
remote repository without upstream keys**, which broke into two lines at 390 px, [Q-UI-810](#q-ui-810--a-folds-label-is-a-buttons-label-at-most-32-characters-in-every-locale)),
**To install roles** and **With a requirements.yml** (Ansible), **For one scope only** (npm). A snippet that only works with
a credential is not shown to an anonymous visitor, and an anonymous visitor of a public image reads "Not needed to pull: this
repository can be read without signing in." instead of being asked to sign in. Measured from the `h1` to the end of step 2 without
code, as the mockup counted, as the power user: see the table in [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#set-up-client-and-the-guides).

**Rationale:** what the window shows needs no sentence; what a plain user needs is the first way, what an expert needs is a fold
away (CLAUDE.md). The development agent revisits a sentence readers miss.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-121, R-UI-123. Code: [clients.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/clients.ts) `snippetText`.

### Q-UI-805 · The guide is a list of closed rows under one heading

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Variant A
(Q-UI-800) closes the first section too.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The heading **Guide** (`h2`) and every section a closed disclosure with an `h3` title, in the server's order (chosen) | One list | The owner's variant; the headings in order under one heading | What the class is is one click away |
| (b) The first section open as before (Q-UI-485) | Unchanged | The class explained at once | Not what the owner chose |

**Choice:** (a). The disclosure takes a heading level (`level`, 2 by default). A closed disclosure took the room of its body's
padding (12 px, 8 px inline): the padding now belongs to an element inside the folded one, so a closed section, here and on every
screen, takes no room beyond its heading. **More about this** is gone with the open sections.

**Rationale:** the owner's choice of variant A; the level keeps the outline of the page right for a screen reader. The development
agent revisits it if readers open the first row on most visits.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-125. Code: [guide-view.ts](../../web/src/app/features/guides/guide-view.ts),
[disclosure.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/disclosure.ts).

### Q-UI-810 · A fold's label is a button's label: at most 32 characters, in every locale

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the render run on a new database (Test and Release 44715970992) found the fold **For a remote repository without upstream
keys** of the Debian setup page in two lines at 390 px, for each kind of user (R-UI-171). The step is 350 px wide there, the chevron
and its gap take 24 px; Inter at 14 px, weight 600, set the 45 characters at 315 px on a Mac and wider than 326 px on the runner. The
finding named it "… upstream keys container": the check read the comment Angular leaves for a block (`<!--container-->`) as text.
The German labels are longer, and no render shows them.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The toggle stays a button of one line; every fold label of Set up client (`setup.fold.*`, `setup.more`) has at most 32 characters in English and in German, held by `clients.spec.ts`, which reads the German targets from `messages.de.xlf`; the APT label becomes **Remote without upstream keys** (28) / **Remote ohne Upstream-Schlüssel** (30) (chosen) | Short labels | The rule of the render guard holds where it cannot look (German, a format the seed has no repository of); a millisecond test | A count of characters stands for a width |
| (b) The inline toggle wraps as a section's heading toggle does | One more exception in `broken` | Any label fits | A two-line button beside a chevron reads as a paragraph; the style guide lets only a heading wrap, and the guard would lose the case |
| (c) Measure every label in the app's font in the unit tier | The width itself | Exact | The unit tier renders in jsdom, without layout or fonts; only the renders measure, and only in English |

**Choice:** (a). The bound: 326 px of room (292 px for **More options** in the credential's row); the labels of the page set at 5.9 to
7.7 px a character on a Mac, the runner wider, so 32 characters at 7.7 px and a tenth more are 271 px, and a label breaks the bound only
where it averages more than 9.1 px a character, which only runs of capitals and of "m" and "w" do. The layout check names an element by
its text and its elements' text, without a comment (`textOf` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), a fixture in
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts)); the guard itself is unchanged.

**Rationale:** the cheapest test that sees both locales and every format; a fold is a control, and a control's label of one line is
the rule the other buttons keep. The development agent revisits the bound if a label of 32 characters is measured in two lines, or if
a third locale or a narrower place for a fold comes.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-121, R-UI-171, Q-UI-804. Code: [clients.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/clients.ts),
[clients.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/clients.spec.ts), [messages.de.xlf](../../web/src/locale/messages.de.xlf),
[layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts).

### Q-UI-840 · A reader who may not change a virtual repository learns a registry's state from what it reads

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the member editor of R-UI-189 shows the state of each registry of the format, in the picker and on a placeholder. A holder
of `repositories:read-config` reads the states from `listUpstreamRepositories`, and whoever may write the member list reads them with
the levels from `listFormatUpstreamRepositories` ([Q-API-364](#q-api-364--a-writer-of-a-virtual-repository-reads-the-state-and-the-level-of-a-formats-well-known-repositories-through-an-operation-of-its-own)). The settings page also shows the member list, read-only, to a
member of the project below the Owner, who holds neither; the repository list answers such a caller `disabled` only for a registry it
reads.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The format's presets are the registries offered; a read one that is disabled is **Off**, an unread one has no state; a member naming no preset is **No longer offered** (chosen) | What the API answers a reader, said as far as it goes | No request a reader is refused; nothing claimed the caller cannot know | "Not switched on" and "Switched off" read the same for a reader |
| (b) Ask `listFormatUpstreamRepositories` for every caller and say nothing on its `403` | One source | Exact for a writer, as (a) is | A refused request on every view of a reader's settings page |
| (c) Admit every reader of a virtual repository to the read of a format | Exact for everyone | The three words exact for a reader too | The API's decision, which chose the writers (Q-API-364 (a')): a reader would learn the state and the level of registries it can neither list nor read |

**Choice:** (a), also for a writer whose read of the format answers an error.

**Rationale:** the screen says what the caller's reads show and no more; a reader changes nothing about a member, so the two states
that tell an administrator's two actions apart are not what it needs. The development agent would revisit this if the read of a
format ever admits the readers of a virtual repository.

### Q-UI-843 · The form of a new repository starts at the class of its address

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-191's link leads to "the form of a virtual repository of the same format". The creation form starts at local
(Q-UI-341) and had no way to be opened at another class.

### Q-UI-898 · Nothing offers what a system repository refuses: no address, no download, no command

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below, carrying the owner's "Das ist alles wichtig und muss
umgesetzt werden" (2026-11-21) to every place the builder of R-UI-192 had reported; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: verified in the code. Every protocol request to a system repository answers 404 as for a repository that does not exist
(`target.resolved` of [files.go](../../internal/files/files.go) for `/files/`, and the content route of the UI shares it through `Stat`,
[content.go](../../internal/api/rawfiles/content.go)); the client setup answers snippets for it all the same
([packages_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/packages_api.go) `clientSetup` has no test for it), and the API answers its addresses, an item's
`downloadUrl` and `contentUrl` and a version file's two members as for any repository. So the admin area's copy button, a file's
**Download**, its download address and its curl command, the folder's copy buttons, the address for downloads by path of its **Details**,
the pull command of an opened image and the install panel of its versions all handed out something that fails.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The UI leaves each of them out for a system repository, decided by its qualified name (`isSystemRepository`, `isSystemRepositoryName`) in the component that holds the name (chosen) | R-UI-193 | One test, the one of Q-UI-896 and Q-UI-893, in every place; nothing asked of the server that fails; the API stays one shape for every repository, as it is for a disabled one, whose addresses it answers and whose clients it refuses | The browser repeats a fact the server knows |
| (b) The server leaves the addresses, `downloadUrl`, `contentUrl` and the snippets out for a system repository | The API answers what works | One source; a script against the API meets no dead address either | Two required members of `PackageFile` become optional for every repository; the client setup needs an answer for "no client"; the badge of Q-UI-902 and the lists of Q-UI-901 still need the key test, so the UI keeps it anyway |
| (c) Only the four places the builder named | — | Smaller | The folder's copy buttons, the address of **Details**, the opened row's command and a version's **Download** would still lead to 404 |

**Choice:** (a). A column that would be empty for every row goes with its content: the folder's actions, the opened row's actions and a
version's **Download** when no file of it can be downloaded (the style guide's rule of a column without data). The admin area's row keeps
its menu alone; the layout check that counts the ways the action cells of one table are built allows exactly that pair on the admin
area's repository list (`allowed` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), matched by its measured detail).

**Rationale:** the rule of Q-UI-896 is a fact of the repository, and every client action is one more place of the same fact. The
development agent would revisit (b) if the repository list ever carries the repository's kind (Q-UI-893's condition), which also makes the
key test unnecessary. **Kept on 2026-11-23** (the reading of the open findings): that the API still answers the addresses, the files'
`downloadUrl` and `contentUrl` and the client setup of a system repository is this choice's consequence, not a defect, and the condition
has not occurred: `RepositorySummary` and `Repository` carry no kind, only the admin area's `UpstreamRepository` does
([openapi.yaml](../../api/openapi.yaml)). Since [Q-UI-908](#q-ui-908--upstreamclamav-answers-its-clients-while-its-switch-is-on-and-every-screen-treats-it-so)
`upstream/clamav` answers clients while its switch is on, and there the addresses the API answers work while it is.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-193. Code: [repository-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.ts),
[repository-file.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts),
[repository-files.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts),
[repository-item-versions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-item-versions.ts),
[version-command.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-command.ts), [package-version.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.ts).
