### Q-UI-860 · One severity scale for the bar, the trend and the badge: the bar's fills with a mark tone of the same hue

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-20** ("Option C" of three candidates a designer drew).

Context: on the vulnerability report one severity had up to three colours. The trend came first (Q-VULN-53): its six series were
marks against the page at 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), in tones of the first reference screens (Q-UI-88), Low a teal and Unknown a violet
(`--quader-chart-*`). The severity bar came later in cogpit's colours (R-UI-092, Q-UI-370), whose Medium and Low fills do not reach
3:1 against the page; the bar does not need them to, because it carries its counts as text, so the trend kept its own palette
(Q-UI-376). And the badge of a finding took the page's status colours, so Critical and High were the same error red, and Low,
None and Unknown the same muted grey. Low was pale yellow in the bar, teal in the chart and grey in a list. The owner asked for
one scale. A designer drew three candidates as a static page of the report's top, the findings, the grade card, the tokens with
their measured contrasts and the colour-vision simulations, light and dark, with today's for comparison.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A, warm by tone | The bar's warm hues, each one tone that is fill, band and icon at once: crimson, red, orange, gold, lifted in the dark scheme | One tone per severity; a single token each | Every tone must hold 3:1 on the card, so in the light scheme Medium becomes a brown orange and Low a mustard: the bar changes; in the dark scheme High is a soft coral |
| (b) B, teal Low | The trend's scale taken into the bar: crimson, orange, amber and a teal Low, one tone each | The step from Medium to Low is a change of hue family that survives every colour-vision deficiency | Low leaves the warm family and reads as calm or informational, 20 degrees from the link blue and beside the green good grades; the bar changes most |
| (c) C, the bar's fills with marks (chosen) | The bar stays exactly as it is, both schemes; the trend's bands take the same fills and draw an edge of 1.5 px on top in a mark tone of the same hue, deeper in the light scheme and brighter in the dark one; the badge's icon is that tone, its word the text colour; Unknown is the bar's grey hatch everywhere, None a neutral grey; the usage screens get a token of their own | The bar the owner knows stays; one hue per severity everywhere; every mark holds 3:1 on the page, the card, the table head and a hovered row; neighbours stay at least 9 apart (CIEDE2000) under deuteranopia and protanopia | Two tones and two tokens per severity; the chart needs a second path per series for the edges; in the dark scheme the deep Critical band is lit only by its edge |

**Choice:** (c). The values are the designer's generator's, unchanged: the fills `#7f1d1d`, `#c9302a`, `#e8a33d`, `#f5d68e`; the marks
Critical `#6c0b17` / `#d95853`, High `#9c1e18` / `#f6815b`, Medium `#a15e04` / `#ffb755`, Low `#a78314` / `#ffe8b0` (light / dark);
None `#737278` / `#89888d`; Unknown's mark `#626168` / `#a4a3a8`; the usage teal `#347da0` / `#5cb3d6`, today's. The tightest pairs:
the light Low mark on the card 3.02:1 and the dark Critical mark on the card 3.01:1; the closest neighbours the light marks of Medium
and Low under deuteranopia (9.1) and the dark marks of High and Medium under deuteranopia (9.5). The grade shield
(`--quader-grade-*`) is another scale and stays.

**Rationale:** the owner's decision. The development agent records no revisit condition; the choice is the owner's. What the
development agent decided in building it is Q-UI-861 and Q-UI-862.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-092, R-VULN-022, Q-UI-376, Q-VULN-53. Code: [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss),
[_vulnerabilities.scss](../../web/src/styles/_vulnerabilities.scss), [report-trend.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/report-trend.ts),
[vuln-parts.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vuln-parts.ts), [palette.spec.ts](../../web/src/styles/palette.spec.ts);
[design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md#vulnerability-grades).

### Q-UI-861 · A band's edge is drawn on every day its severity has a finding, on the band's true top

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the designer left open how a severity with findings stays visible when its band is very thin. At 390 px the chart is about
half its scale: a band of two findings among 1,000 is 0.34 viewBox units high, under a pixel. The totals on the axis must stay true.
The exact numbers are the table's (**Show as table**) and the text alternative's (the last day); the chart has no tooltip (Q-VULN-53
chose none).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The edge is a line on the band's true top on every day the severity has at least one finding, 1.5 CSS px whatever the scale (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`); the edges are drawn after every band, the worst last (chosen) | Each band's height is its count; a day with a finding has its line, a day without has none | The heights and the totals stay exact; a band of one finding is still a line of 1.5 px; where two edges meet, the worse severity is on top | The line reaches 0.75 px into the band above it, and for Critical 0.75 px below the axis; where two neighbouring bands are both thinner than the line, the less severe one's edge is hidden (the table has both) |
| (b) A least height for a band with findings, 1.5 px, pushing the bands above it up | A thin band is always an area | Visible as a fill, not only as a line | The column overshoots its total: with six thin bands up to 9 px, and the axis no longer reads true |
| (c) A least height taken from the band above | The column's total stays | Visible as a fill | The neighbour's height is wrong instead; a count is drawn larger than it is |

**Choice:** (a). None has an edge too, in its own grey: on a band of its size it cannot be seen, and it keeps a thin None band
visible (the mockup drew None without an edge). Rendered at 390 px with two Critical among about 400 for 300 days: in the light scheme
the crimson mark is a clear line on the axis that starts on the first day with a Critical finding; in the dark scheme it is one
pixel row of `#d95853` between High's fill above (about 1.4:1) and the page below (4.6:1), visible and faint, the weak point the
designer named for the dark Critical band.

**Rationale:** the axis and the heights are the chart's statement, and they stay true; visibility is bought with a line, not with
a false area. The development agent revisits it if a reader reports a thin band that could not be seen.

**Applied in the spec:** R-VULN-022. Code: `trendGeometry` and the `edges` of [report-trend.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/report-trend.ts),
[vulnerability-report.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-862 · At 365 days the columns touch and are not parted by a hairline

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the mockup drew 90 days only. At 365 days a column is 1.63 viewBox units wide and the columns touch (the gap of one unit is
left out below four). Rendered with 365 days of data, each column still had the hairline of 0.25 units in the raised surface's colour
that parts the columns of 30 and 90 days: about a sixth of every column was the page's colour, every band was striped, the pale
Low read as near white in the light scheme and as stripes in the dark one, and white seams stood where the counts jumped.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep the hairline | As 30 and 90 days | Nothing changes | The bands are no longer the bar's fills: what the owner's choice is about is lost at 365 days |
| (b) Columns that touch drop the hairline (chosen) | `trendGeometry` says `touching`; the chart leaves the hairline out | The bands are the bar's fills; each band's edges, one per day, join into one stepped line | A single day is no longer told apart in the picture; the table carries every day |
| (c) A week per column at 365 days | 52 columns with gaps | Columns that part | The chart draws other numbers than the table; more code; a thin Critical day disappears into its week |

**Choice:** (b). The edges stay per day, so a day with a Critical finding still has its line.

**Rationale:** the smallest change that keeps the bands in the scale's colours; 30 and 90 days are unchanged. The development agent
revisits it if a longer range than 365 days comes (the API answers up to 400).

**Applied in the spec:** R-VULN-022. Code: [report-trend.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/report-trend.ts),
[_vulnerabilities.scss](../../web/src/styles/_vulnerabilities.scss).

### Q-API-380 · The sources item of the image database names the class of its repository

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-VULN-045 shows the commands that fill the database's repository for a local repository only. The sources item named the
repository and the reference (`aquasec/trivy-db:2`), not what kind of repository it is, and the screen is read with `settings:read`, which
does not read a repository's document.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A member `repositoryClass`, `local` or `remote`, on the item of `trivy`, `null` elsewhere and for a repository that does not resolve (chosen) | The report reads the repository by its name when it answers | The screen decides on the answer it has; a reader without `repositories:read-config` sees the commands too | One more member, which says that a repository of that name exists to a holder of `settings:read`, who already sees its name |
| (b) The screen reads the repository's document | No API change | Exact | Needs `repositories:read-config`; without it the commands would vanish |
| (c) The commands for every repository of the setting | No class needed | Simple | `upstream/scanner-trivy` is a remote that answers every push 404; the commands would not work and would mislead |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the screen shows what the installation can do, and the class decides it. The development agent would
revisit this if the sources item gains a link of its own to the repository's page.

**Applied in the spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-021, R-VULN-045. Code:
[sources.go](../../internal/vuln/report/sources.go), the schema `VulnerabilitySourceState` of [openapi.yaml](../../api/openapi.yaml).

### Q-UI-890 · The image database is a row of the sources table, its repository in the mode's column, its fetch a button of the runs

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Builds
Q-UI-850.

Context: the sources table showed every source as `OSV` or `CISA KEV` (the row of `trivy` read "OSV OCI" in mode `off`), and the runs had a
button per task of OSV and KEV only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The row is **Image database**, "for the image scanning" under it; the mode column holds the repository's qualified name (a link with `repositories:read-config`) and the image and tag under it; **Fetch the image database now** joins the runs, disabled with the setting `vulnerabilities.images.enabled` named while the image scanning is off; a failure's title names the repository; the commands of a local repository sit in a closed fold under the table (chosen) | One table, one column richer for one row | The repository is where the mode of the other rows is, so the table keeps its widths; the run an administrator needs after fixing the repository is one click; the fold keeps the plain screen plain | The mode column holds a name instead of a word for one row |
| (b) A section of its own under the table | A card for the database | Room for more | The database's state, age and failures would no longer be read beside the others' |
| (c) The repository in the source column | The name under **Image database** | The mode column stays words | The source column is the table's row header, which a screen reader reads with every cell; a link in it is read twice |

**Choice:** (a). The commands name `mirror.gcr.io` for `aquasec/trivy-db` and `ghcr.io` for `aquasecurity/trivy-db`, the registries that
publish under those names, with this installation's host and the repository's qualified name filled in. The repository's name may break
after its slash and nowhere else: the findings list keeps a qualified name on one line (Q-UI-428), but here one line made the least width
of the table pass 1440 px and every row stacked, and a break at the hyphen of `scanner-trivy`, which the browser chose before, splits a key.
While any source shows the error of its last run, the failures column holds 16 rem: squeezed between the others it had put the title under
the count (the layout check's `row-offset`) and the detail into a ribbon of three words a line. With the 16 rem the rows stack at 1440 px,
as R-UI-174 makes a table do whose columns do not fit, and read as sentences; without a failure the screen is a table at 1440 px. **Rationale:** the screen of every
source's health reads one more source the same way. The development agent would revisit this if a second source of the image scanning comes.

**Applied in the spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022, R-VULN-045. Code:
[vulnerability-sources.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-sources.ts).

### Q-UI-952 · The test is a link the administrator opens from a client of his network

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-242](../decisions.md#adr-242--delivery-by-signed-links-of-the-object-store-one-switch-of-the-installation-where-a-link-costs-nothing).

Context: the product's rule for remote repositories is a test of the connection where the upstream is entered. Here the question is
whether the clients reach the object store at the public address, and the clients' network is not Quader's: a public address in front
of a store inside the cluster is often not reachable from the cluster itself.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Test link** answers a link to a small probe, signed against the address as typed, with the `curl` command; the administrator opens it or runs it on a client machine (chosen) | No request from Quader to the address | Tests the network that matters, from the browser or any client; shows the store's own answer, a refused signature included | The page cannot say by itself whether it worked |
| (b) Quader fetches the link itself and reports the answer | A server-side test | A result on the page | Quader's network answers for the clients' network; an outbound request to an address an administrator types |
| (c) No test | | | The one precondition that fails most (clients that cannot reach the store) is found by the first failed pull |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the store's support of the overrides is proven on its own by the link check of every start (storage.md
Q-STOR-294); what remains is reachability, which only a client can show. **Applied in the spec:** [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-074,
R-UI-200.

| (a) Every connection has its field and **Test link**; an encrypted connection's field says that it is where a Bastion reaches the store and that for now a Bastion gets such files through the main installation, only its sentence of `encrypted` stands under it, and its test's sentence names a Bastion's network; the test's sentence of a plain connection names the clients' or a Bastion's network (chosen) | What R-STOR-096 asks, said as it is today | The address a handover will name can be set and tested before the data keys land; no sentence claims a client's link or a direct read there; a Bastion's operator reads which network to test from | The page offers an address that serves nothing until package 4, and says so |
| (b) The test link without the field, against the endpoint | | No field that serves nothing yet | The test is signed against the address as typed; an address in front of the store could not be tested |
| (c) Nothing until package 4 | | | R-STOR-096 and R-BAS-078 stay unbuilt; the Bastions screen's link leads to a page that cannot test an encrypted connection |

**Choice:** (a). The other reasons of an encrypted connection (`not_https`, `quader_host`, `link_check_failed`) are about clients' links,
which it never serves, so they are not shown under its field; an address a save or a test refuses still shows its error there. When
package 4 lands, the field's last sentence ("For now a Bastion gets the files of an encrypted connection through the main installation.")
goes. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-200 (changed); code: `connections` and `fieldReasons` of
[storage-settings.ts](../../web/src/app/features/settings/storage-settings.ts), [storage-settings.html](../../web/src/app/features/settings/storage-settings.html).
*Amended on 2026-11-23 by [Q-UI-990](#q-ui-990--with-the-data-keys-handed-an-encrypted-connections-field-says-how-a-bastion-reads-it-and-why-it-cannot)*,
when package 4 landed: the field says how a Bastion reads such a connection, and why a Bastion cannot stands under it.

### Q-UI-959 · A Bastion card's tables keep one form at the wide and the middle width; what most rows share stands under the row's name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** after the coordinator's look at the renders of the handover's surface (2026-11-23) —
selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a card of the Bastions screen ([bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-007) had a table of the last contact with six columns (replica,
time, client address, release, interface version, reported base URL) and one of the tokens with five, none with a declared least width, and
absolute dates. The data table stacks its rows where its columns at their least widths do not fit (Q-UI-680), and a column without a
declared width is as wide as its longest value: at 1440 px a card whose replicas report a base URL of 38 characters stacked its rows while
the next card, with a shorter URL, kept its table and broke its dates onto two lines (a date and a time are never broken, Q-UI-428); at
1024 px every date of the tokens broke. The owner's Bastion reports a base URL of 35 characters and pod names of 31. A card's list is
1,094 px wide at a window of 1440 px, 678 px at 1024 px and 316 px at 390 px (measured on the renders' stack); the six columns need about
1,030 px at the least widths their headers ask.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Last contact in three columns (**Replica**, **Time**, **Reported base URL**) and the tokens in four (**Token**, **Expires**, **Last used**, the action), each with a declared least width; under a replica's name its client address, release and interface version, under a token's description its hint and its creation, as the reference's list of runners shows a runner's version and address under its name; every time relative with its date and time as its title (Q-UI-431); the base URL and the description take the room the others leave; a name breaks after its hyphens, an address and a URL after their colons, dots and slashes (chosen) | The same form at 1440 and 1024 px for every card, stacked rows at 390 px only | The form follows the card's width alone: the tables need 632 and 642 px whatever they hold; no date breaks; a pod name of 63 characters and a base URL of 51 break inside their own columns; the **?** of **Replica** names what stands under the name | The address, the release and the interface version are no column to scan down |
| (b) All six columns where the list is 64 rem wide or more, the address, the release and the interface version under the name below it (the data table's `narrow`) | A column each where room allows | Nothing moves at 1440 px | Two forms between 1440 and 1024 px; a list of 1,024 to 1,030 px would stack; the German header **Schnittstellenversion** needs more |
| (c) The columns as they were, with declared least widths | | Least change | Six columns do not fit 678 px: every card stacks at 1024 px |

**Choice:** (a). The least widths: **Replica** 16 rem (a pod name of 31 characters stays on one line), **Time** 7.5 rem, **Reported base
URL** 10 rem; **Token** 9 rem, **Expires** 11 rem (its mark **Expires in 29 days** included), **Last used** 7.5 rem. **Applied in the
spec:** [bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-007 (amended); code: `contactColumns`, `tokenColumns` and `breakParts` of
[bastion-card.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-card.ts).

### Q-UI-990 · With the data keys handed, an encrypted connection's field says how a Bastion reads it and why it cannot

Status: **Decided by the builder** in the join of the handover's data keys (package 4 of
[developer/bastion-handover.md](../developer/bastion-handover.md)) with its surface (package 5) — selected from the options below; the owner
reviews it. It amends [Q-UI-958](#q-ui-958--an-encrypted-connection-has-its-address-and-its-test-link-for-a-bastion-and-says-what-it-serves-today),
whose field said that "for now" a Bastion gets such files through the main installation and showed only the sentence `encrypted` under it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

Context: since package 4 a Bastion whose direct reads are on reads a file of an encrypted connection from the object store with a link and
that file's key ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095), where no plain copy can serve. No client ever gets a link to an encrypted connection
(R-STOR-088), so the reasons of its clients' links (`reasons`, a store that ignores an override among them) still say nothing about it;
why a Bastion cannot read it is its `handoverReasons` (R-STOR-096: the address, the first part of the link check), as for a plain
connection on the Bastions screen ([bastion.md](bastion.md) Q-BAS-300).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The field says that no client gets a link to it and that a Bastion with direct reads reads each file there with a link and that file's key; under it the sentence `encrypted`, now "… Quader delivers its content to clients itself.", and the sentence of each of its `handoverReasons`, an address under a host of Quader in words of a Bastion ("A Bastion refuses a link there.") (chosen) | What stays true beside what is new | The Bastions screen's link leads to the field that says why its line stands; nothing tells an administrator that the files of a usable encrypted connection still pass the main installation | One sentence more to translate |
| (b) Only the field's last sentence goes, as Q-UI-958 said | The smallest change | | An encrypted connection a Bastion cannot read shows no reason where the card sends the administrator |
| (c) Its clients' `reasons` as a plain connection's | One rule | | A store that ignores an override would stand under a connection whose Bastion reads it, and `quader_host` would speak of image clients, which never get its link |

**Choice:** (a). The test link's sentence of an encrypted connection ("… on a machine of a Bastion's network …") stays as it is: it was
true before and is now. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-200 (its texts); code: `fieldReasons`, `reasonText` and `bastionReasonText` of
[storage-settings.ts](../../web/src/app/features/settings/storage-settings.ts), `@@links.address.hint-encrypted` in
[storage-settings.html](../../web/src/app/features/settings/storage-settings.html).

### Q-UI-876 · The words and the marks of a verdict

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

the render's check found it. The dashboard's list tells the two kinds of "could not be checked" apart, because its filter does: **Not

carries the member, so a version of an installation without the scanning has none. In German a release is "zum Download zulassen",
its noun "Zulassung", withdrawing it "zurückziehen", a find "Malware-Befund", as the glossary has them ("freigeben" renders exposure). **Applied in the spec:** [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-024, R-MAL-025. Code:
[malware-status.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/malware/malware-status.ts), [malware-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/malware/malware-words.ts).

### Q-API-381 · The scanner replicas are an operation of their own, `GET /api/v1/system/scanners`, with the kinds beside them

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Part of the
owner's order of 2026-11-21 that the screens name every scanner pod and its tool
([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-223).

Context: three screens show the scanner replicas: the System page, **Settings › Malware scanning** and **Advisory sources**, each read with
`settings:read`. A scanner's row has none of what a replica's row carries (the view of Valkey, the key ring, the leases, the runtime), and
the screens must say why a kind has no row: the role `all` runs no scanner pod, no scanner is configured, or the scan listener cannot tell
the kind.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One operation of its own: `kinds` from the answering replica's configuration, each with `replicas` (`reporting`, `unverified`, `inProcess`, `none`), and `items` (chosen) | One shape, one handler, read by the three screens | No reader of `/system/replicas` (the dashboard, the key rings, the support bundle) has to learn to leave a scanner out; the screens say why a kind is empty from the server's words, not from a guess of the role | One more read on the System page every 15 s |
| (b) Rows of `/system/replicas` with the role `scanner` and the members of a replica made optional | One list | The System page reads one answer | Every member of a replica becomes optional for every reader, and every count of replicas has to leave scanners out |
| (c) A member in each screen's own answer (the malware settings, the sources) | No new operation | One read per screen | Three shapes of one thing, and the System page still needs one |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a scanner replica is not a replica of the registry and has a shape of its own; one operation keeps both
lists true. The permission is the one of the three screens, `settings:read`, so the auditor reads the rows as every other fact of them; no
new permission. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038; [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048. Code:
[scanners_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/scanners_api.go), [wire_scanner_report.go](../../internal/app/wire_scanner_report.go), the schemas
`ScannerList`, `ScannerKind`, `ScannerReplica` of [openapi.yaml](../../api/openapi.yaml), whose `ReplicaState` both lists share.

### Q-UI-912 · Only `daily` is outdated by its age, as ClamAV warns only about `daily`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. R-UI-194 marked
every database **Outdated** from 7 days on; the renders showed `main` and `bytecode` flagged on the first day, because ClamAV rebuilds them
rarely, a false alarm an administrator would see at once.

What ClamAV does, read in its source at the tag `clamav-1.5.5`, `libclamav/cvd.c`, function `cli_cvdload` (lines 559 to 576): only when
the loaded file's name contains `daily.` (`strstr(filename, "daily.")`) does the engine compare the container's build time with the clock,
warn "The virus database is older than 7 days!" when the difference is more than 604,800 seconds, and take that container's version and
build time as the engine's database version. No other database's age is checked.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Outdated** and its sentence on `daily` alone, past 604,800 seconds as the engine counts; `main` and `bytecode` show their age only (chosen) | The rule of ClamAV's engine | The badge says what the administrator's ClamAV would say, and nothing it would not | A `main` that the network stopped publishing would not be marked; ClamAV does not mark it either |
| (b) Every database from 7 days on, as before | One rule for three rows | — | Two false alarms in normal operation |
| (c) The set's newest build time, once above the list | One badge | — | The newest is `daily`'s anyway, and the row that is old would not carry it |

**Choice:** (a). The version's page follows the same rule. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-194; [formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md)
R-CLAMAV-003. Code: [clamav-definitions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/clamav-definitions.ts) `isOutdated`.

[malware-settings.html](../../web/src/app/features/settings/malware-settings.html).

### Q-UI-915 · An image scanner's database is a badge beside its tool, and the installation's statement a line beside the counts

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. With the
detection in the scanner each pod of `vuln-scanner-trivy` holds a copy of the advisory database, and its row says which (R-OPS-048,
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-225): `database.version` the digest of the database its loader
wrote last, `database.builtAt` set only while that is the database in use, `database` `null` before the first load
([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-049, Q-VULN-213). The specification named the three states and the
screens, not the words, the place or the icon. An administrator should read per pod whether it holds the database in use and since
when that was built, an older one, or none yet, and for the installation whether every ready pod holds the database in use.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A badge, **Database in use** with a check in green, **Older database** and **No database yet** with an hourglass, neutral; "built" with the age of the build beside the first; the digest as the badge's title. On the System page under the tool in the column **Tool** (whose help then says what the words mean), in the fold of **Advisory sources** a column **Database** as ClamAV's rows have on the malware settings. For the installation an informing line under the kind's heading on the System page while ready pods do not hold the database in use, and on **Advisory sources** a third part of the summary, "all on the database in use" or "*n* not yet on the database in use" (chosen) | A badge as every state of the screens, the age as the updater's daily (Q-UI-913) | At a glance per row and per installation; green only for the positive state and every state a word; the System page's table keeps its columns at 1440 px | Two places for one value on two screens: under the tool on the System page, a column on the settings fold |
| (b) A column **Database** on both screens | One place | The same on both | Measured on the render profile at 1440 px: the System page's trivy table needs 1,192 px against 1,128 and stands as blocks, while the ClamAV table under it stays a table |
| (c) The database as a line under the state | The reason's place | No column more | A second thing in the state's cell, against the one meaning of the state (the pod is ready although it holds an older database) |
| (d) ClamAV's form: the version and its date, no badge | One look for both kinds | Nothing new | A digest of 64 hex digits says nothing to a reader, and "older" would be a missing date, a state by absence |
| (e) An older database as a warning, and a header warning of the System page | Loud | A stuck pod is seen | Every new database (up to four a day) leaves every pod on the one before for the 10 to 30 s of its load: the warning would flash on a healthy installation |

**Choice:** (a). An older database is neutral, as "Replicas are being replaced" is: the list cannot tell a pod that is loading from one
whose loader fails, and the first is the normal case after every new database; the help says both and where the reason stands (the log
of the pod's container `database`). The badge names the database in every state, because under the tool it has no column header to lean
on. The digest is no text of the cell: twelve hex digits beside the badge made the column too wide for the System page and say nothing
at a glance; the title keeps it for whoever compares two pods. Lost and starting pods are not counted for the installation; a starting
pod shows its own badge. The System page shows nothing while every ready pod holds the database in use, as its other notices do; the
summary of **Advisory sources** says it in words, and leaves the part out while no pod is ready. ClamAV's rows keep their column on the
settings pages and get none on the System page: the worker does not wait for a malware scanner's database. **Rationale:** the database is
a second property of a ready pod, so it gets its own badge beside the state and not in it, and on the System page it stands with the
tool that reads it. The development agent would revisit this when the list reports since when a pod has held a database that is not in
use: a pod that lags for minutes then becomes a warning, which needs that time in the API (Q-OPS-225 reports none) and is not built.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-038, Q-UI-897; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022;
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048. Code: [scanner-replicas.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/scanner/scanner-replicas.ts)
(the badge, the column and the line under the tool), [scanner-model.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/scanner/scanner-model.ts) (`podDatabase`,
`databaseLag`), [system-status.html](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.html) (the line under the heading),
[vulnerability-sources.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-sources.ts) (the summary).

### Q-UI-965 · A disabled repository offers no download, address or command, and says why once

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, closing the open finding "A disabled repository's file page offers
Download, which answers 404"; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: verified in the code. `/files/` and the content route of the UI refuse a disabled repository with 404 `repository_disabled`
for every caller (`target.resolved` of [files.go](../../internal/files/files.go), strict); the management API reads it. The file's
page offered **Download**, its download address and **Download with curl**, a folder's rows their address to copy and an opened image
its pull command, all of which failed. The page knew the repository was disabled only from the full document: the reader's view
(R-REPO-010) did not say it, so a reader was also offered **Set up client**.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Leave each of them out, as for a system repository (Q-UI-898), with one muted sentence where the address stood: "The repository is disabled: nobody can download this file until it is enabled again."; the reader's view carries `disabled` (chosen) | R-UI-010, R-REPO-010 | One rule for a repository that answers no client, whatever the reason; the reader learns why once, where the address would be; the header's badge **disabled** and the absent **Set up client** reach the reader too | Two places (the sentence and the badge) say one fact |
| (b) **Download** stays, disabled, with the reason beside it | The style guide's "a disabled option stays visible and says why" | The reader sees what is missing | A control nobody on this page can use, on every file of the repository; the address and the curl command would need the same |
| (c) Leave them out without a sentence | — | Shortest | A file page without the thing every other one has, unexplained but for the badge |

**Choice:** (a). The item's own request with curl stays: the management API answers it. Every reader's page knows the state, since the
reader's view of `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}` carries `disabled`.

The same rule holds on a version's page, which is reached through the package list without the repository's page. The details of the
version say for each repository that holds it whether a client gets the version through it (`available`, R-API-029): not through a
disabled repository, and not through a virtual one whose members that hold the version are all disabled, since resolution leaves a
disabled member out (R-REPO-019). The install panel offers only the others (R-UI-009); a version that only disabled repositories hold
gets the sentence in the panel, naming them: "The repository web/npm-local is disabled: nobody can install this version until it is
enabled again." The **Files** tab offers no **Download** for a file whose copy is a disabled repository's, and no column where no file
has one.

**Rationale:** the rule of Q-UI-898 is "nothing offers what the repository refuses", and a disabled repository refuses exactly what a
system repository refuses. The development agent would revisit it if a disabled repository's downloads become possible for some
callers (an administrator's `content:bypass`, Q-AUTHZ-162, applies to deletes only today).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-010. Code:
[repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts),
[repository-file.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts),
[repository-files.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts),
[repository-item-versions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-item-versions.ts), `ConsumerView` of
[document.go](../../internal/repository/document.go); on a version's page
[version-command.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-command.ts),
[package-version.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.ts) and `addAvailable` of
[packages_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/packages_api.go).

### Q-UI-966 · The state of the advisory data and the coverage are details; a banner only for who can act

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, closing the open finding of UI-A-16 (the T-21 audit); the owner reviews it
at the walkthrough.

Context: a plain user of a project's **Vulnerabilities** read two warnings about the advisory imports (an administrator's task, whose
link to the sources only a holder of `settings:read` was shown) and the coverage line "internal names only, … waiting for advisory
data, … not covered" (R-UI-067: the plain user's main view names no internal terms and offers nothing it cannot act on).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The banners for a holder of `settings:read`, who reaches the advisory sources from them; every other reader finds the same lines in a closed section **About these counts** under the counts, whose heading carries the note *Advisory data not current* while one applies; the coverage line stands in that section for everyone (chosen) | R-VULN-022, R-UI-067 | Who can act is warned; who cannot still learns, one click away, that the counts may miss findings, and sees it from the note without opening; one section for one kind of fact on every screen of the report | An administrator opens the section for the coverage |
| (b) Nothing for a reader without `settings:read` | — | Plainest | A reader takes the counts of stale data at face value |
| (c) The banners for everyone, as before | — | Everyone warned alike | A warning nobody reading it can act on, and the plain user's main view grows by two boxes (UI-A-16) |

**Choice:** (a). The section remembers whether the viewer opened it (Q-UI-967).

**Rationale:** a warning belongs to whoever can do something about it; for everyone else it is a fact about the counts, a detail on
demand. The development agent would revisit it if readers misread the counts because the note is too quiet.

**Applied in the spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022, R-UI-067. Code:
[report-summary.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/report-summary.ts).

### Q-UI-967 · A Details section is remembered per user, screen and section in the browser's local storage

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, building what Q-UI-319 decided and R-UI-067 asks ("remembers per user
and screen whether it was opened"); the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Per signed-in user, per screen and section (`file.details`, `repository.details`), in the browser's local storage; only an open section is kept, closed is the default (chosen) | `DisclosureMemory` | What R-UI-067 and Q-UI-319 say; a power user opens the file's Details once and finds it open on every file; two people on one browser keep their own, as the side bar does (NavState); the page works when the storage is blocked or cleared | Kept per browser, not per account |
| (b) Per object (each repository, each file its own) | One entry per thing | Exact | Grows with every page visited; a reader opens Details again on every new file |
| (c) In the user's preferences on the server | `PUT /users/me/preferences` | Follows the account across browsers | A write to the API for every click on a heading; a convenience of one browser becomes stored state |
| (d) The session's storage | Per tab | Nothing left behind | Lost with the tab, so opened again on every visit, which is what Q-UI-319 wanted to end |

**Choice:** (a), for every closed section headed **Details** (the repository page, a file, a package, the settings of a repository and

settings page and the folds inside a section are not remembered: they open as their screen says. The renders open every screen as a

**Rationale:** R-UI-067 names the unit (user and screen) and Q-UI-319 the place (the browser); a section is the finest grain a reader
notices. The development agent would revisit (c) if the owner wants it to follow the account.

### Q-UI-969 · The signatures' lists keep one form: a table at 1,440 and 1,024 px, blocks at 390 px

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, closing the open finding "Three narrow lists of the signatures' screens
stand as blocks even at 1,440 px", by the rule of the Bastion cards' tables
([Q-UI-959](#q-ui-959--a-bastion-cards-tables-keep-one-form-at-the-wide-and-the-middle-width-what-most-rows-share-stands-under-the-rows-name)),
which this decision applies to the signatures' lists; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: measured on the renders' data: the security dashboard's view of signatures needed 1,171 px at its columns' least widths against
1,113 at 1,440 px; a project's trust anchors 884 against 872; at 1,024 px every list of the signatures' screens, the admin page's
installation anchors, project anchors and blocked signers too, needed 880 to 1,171 px against about 690. So a list turned into blocks by
what it held, at a width where its neighbours were tables (R-UI-174 stacks where the columns do not fit).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One form per width whatever the list holds: a table whose columns fit at 1,440 and 1,024 px, the secondary facts as lines under the row's name where columns do not fit, blocks only at 390 px; a time in a list relative with the date as its title (Q-UI-431) (chosen) | Anchors: **Trust anchor** (the kind and the source or the project under it), **Expires**, **Signatures**, **State**, the action; blocked signers: **Signer** (the reason under it), **Signatures**, **Blocked**, the action; findings: **Artifact** (the path, the reason and the repositories under it; the name breaks after its dots and slashes), **Kind**, **Signer**, **Found** | A reader finds the same list at the same width; the least widths fit with room (602 to 682 px at 1,024) | The facts under a name are read, not scanned down a column |
| (b) Stack where the columns do not fit, as before (R-UI-174) | — | Every fact a column where there is room | The form changes with the data: one long name turns a list into blocks at 1,440 px |
| (c) A region that scrolls sideways | — | Every column kept | Refused from 1,024 px by the renders' checks |

**Choice:** (a). The list keeps R-UI-174's measurement: it stands as blocks where even these columns do not fit, which on the renders'
data is 390 px only.

**Rationale:** the Bastions screen's rule, so that the screens of the admin area and the dashboard read alike. The development agent
would revisit a list whose secondary line grows past three lines. The rule is Q-UI-959's; the renders hold a screen's lists to it
where the screen names them in `tables` (the signatures' screens; the Bastion cards are measured by their own walk).

How a cell of these lists breaks, after the renders at 1,024 px showed a signer's URL broken "…heads/le" / "gacy-build" and a
finding's title "acme.logging.abstractions 2." / "0.0-preview.1": a name and its version break between the two first, and the version
stays whole while it fits on a line; a name, a path or an identity that is a URL or a distinguished name breaks after `/`, `.`, `@` and
`,`, and not inside a word, a hyphenated one ("legacy-build", "dmz-frankfurt") included. A piece breaks inside itself only where it
is longer than the line. One helper cuts the pieces for the Bastion cards' addresses, the audit log's keys and the signatures' lists,
and one component shows them each whole while it fits (`breakParts` and `PartsText` of

### Q-UI-995 · A document shortens a long string to its start and its length and copies whole; a code block scrolls a few screens at most

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, building what the development agent decided for the open finding "The layout
checks stopped once at the admin area's Storage page" (W9); the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a Debian remote's stored document carries the archive's keyring in its preset, one line of about 77,000 characters; the section
**API** of its settings printed it in a code block about 602,000 px wide at 1,024 and 1,440 px. The renders' check allowed every code
block to scroll sideways, so the block went unnoticed for three days (2026-11-20 to 2026-11-23). The same document stands in the creation
form's **Show as API request**, a file's API description, an opened audit event's details and a backup run's result.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A string longer than 200 characters shows its first 64 and its length, "-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----… (77,012 characters)"; a copy button beside the block copies the whole text, and a muted line says so where something was shortened; the check allows a code block to scroll up to 4,000 px and fails a wider one (chosen) | `<quader-document-block>`, `atMost` of the layout check | The document reads as a document; nothing is lost to whoever copies it; the next such value fails its screen | The shown text is no longer what a selection copies |
| (b) The block wraps its lines | — | Every character visible | A keyring of 77,000 characters is a page of base64 between the settings |
| (c) The keyring left out of the document | — | Short | The document is no longer the stored one |

**Choice:** (a), on every page that prints a stored or an API document: a repository's stored document and the requests that save a
change (settings), the request body and the curl command of the creation form, a file's description, an audit event's details (which
also wrap, Q-UI-997) and a backup run's result. A command (curl) is built around the shortened body for the eye and around the whole one
for the copy. A setting the form cannot edit (`format-settings`, "Set it through the API") keeps its value as it is: no format has a
long one.

**Rationale:** a reader of the document wants its shape and the values a person can read; a value of 77,000 characters is copied, not
read. The bound of the check keeps the exemption for what it was made for, a long command or URL. The development agent would revisit
the limit of 200 characters if a value a reader needs (a long URL with its query) is cut.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-037, R-UI-087, R-UI-170. Code: [document-block.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/document-block.ts),
`allowed` and `CODE_BLOCK_SCROLL` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts).

"Mir ist noch aufgefallen, dass du malware und Signatures auf das Security-Dashbaord als Reiter gebracht hast. Ich hätte es lieber als
seperate Menüpunkte unter Security Audit."

Context: the security dashboard had three views, **Vulnerabilities** (`/security`), **Malware** (`/security/malware`) and **Signatures**
(`/security/signatures`), as a strip of links under the page's title (Q-UI-873); the side bar's **Security audit** had the one entry
**Security dashboard**.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The side bar's **Security audit** has three entries, **Security dashboard**, **Malware** and **Signatures**; each page has its own heading, title and trail ("Security audit / Malware"); the dashboard holds the vulnerability findings without a strip of one link; the pages keep their addresses, which were each view's own already, so no address goes and none redirects (chosen by the owner) | Q-UI-620's context title | What the owner asked for; each list is a page of its own, as Q-UI-871 (b) weighed | The side bar grows by two entries for whoever holds the dashboard's capability |
| (b) The strip of views stays | Q-UI-873 | — | Against the owner's word |

**Choice:** (a). Who sees an entry is who saw the view: the holder of `content:metadata-read` (Q-AUTHZ-295); nothing about permissions
changes, and an entry the caller may not open is not shown. The entry of the page shown is the one whose address is the longest that the
page's address starts with, so **Security dashboard** is not marked current on **Malware**, and a finding (`/security/findings/…`) keeps
**Security dashboard** current. The search offers the two pages as places as it offers every entry of the side bar (R-UI-096); the
settings of the malware scanning and of the signatures lead to them by their names.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-158, the route table; [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-025; [signatures.md](signatures.md)
R-SIG-038. Code: `security-audit` of [navigation.ts](../../web/src/app/core/navigation.ts),
[security.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/security.routes.ts), `currentRoute` of [app.ts](../../web/src/app/app.ts).

### Q-UI-1006 · Every page names a principal by the username, and every other kind with its kind as a word

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23, settling option (a) of
[Q-UI-1004](#q-ui-1004--a-page-names-a-person-without-a-principals-syntax) that waited; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the pages print who did something from a principal's reference (`user:priya`, `sa:ci-build`, `group:gh-ops`): a file's creator
and last downloader, a release of the malware or the signature gate, a role binding's principal and granter, a lifted block of the
download limits, the general settings' read-only mode, a signing key's upload, the storage settings' last change. Some printed the
reference as it is, some stripped `user:` and left every other kind in its syntax. An answer carries the reference alone; the people
lists carry display names because their readers may read the members.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Each answer that names a principal carries its display name too | One resolver of the server | A person named as the member lists name people | Every reader of the object, an anonymous reader of a public repository too, learns the names of who wrote it: who may read a person's name changes |
| (b) The page resolves references through a lookup | A new operation | No answer changes | A call per name, and a lookup of anyone's name for every reader |
| (c) One helper for every page: a user by the username without the kind ("by priya"), a service account, a group, a Bastion and a CI job with their kind as a word ("service account ci-build", "Servicekonto ci-build"); the reference stays the title (chosen) | `personName` | No new decision about who may read what; one form on every page; nothing printed in a reference's syntax | The username, not the display name |

**Choice:** (c). `check-rules.mjs` refuses a template that interpolates a principal's field (`releasedBy`, `grantedBy`, `lastDownloader`,
a stamp's `by` and the like) without the helper.

**Rationale:** who may read a person's name is unchanged, which (a) and (b) would change; the username is what the person signs in
with and what a search for a person matches. The development agent would revisit (a) if the owner wants display names on these pages.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-010. Code: [person-name.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/person-name.ts).

### Q-UI-1007 · A technical token's description is edited and the token deleted from its row's menu

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-23 as the coordinator of the screens' second round decided it (G5-51); the
owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the API changes a technical token's description and deletes the token (R-AUTH-045), the client had both operations, and no
screen called them: an administrator had to use the API. A token's row has **Rotate** and **Revoke** as words, which a credential keeps
([Q-UI-641](#q-ui-641--a-credentials-revoke-is-never-in-a-menu-a-token-row-keeps-its-two-words)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A menu **Actions for <token>** at the row's end, beside the words, with **Edit description** (a dialog of the one field, read with the token's `ETag` as it opens and saved with it) and **Delete** (the confirmation every removal uses, "Delete this technical token?") (chosen) | R-UI-163's menu | Both reach the screen without a third word in the row; a change somebody made meanwhile is refused, not overwritten | The secret's actions and the token's own stand in two places of one row |
| (b) The description edited in place in the row | — | No dialog | A field in every row of a list, against R-UI-163's one way per job |
| (c) A page of its own per technical token | A route | Room for more | A page for one field |

**Choice:** (a). The menu shows to whoever may change the token: `identities:write`, or the role Owner of the account's project; the
server decides in any case. **Rationale:** the token's own changes are rare and belong to the row of the token, behind its menu;
the frequent actions of its secret stay its words. The development agent sees no case for revisiting this.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-181. Code: [technical-token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/features/service-accounts/technical-token-table.ts),

### Q-UI-1031 · The UI development profile runs in instances, one per builder, and instance 1 is the main checkout's

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below (D5 of the triage of 2026-11-23); the
owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Amends [Q-UI-686](#q-ui-686--the-ui-development-profile-gives-an-anonymous-address-the-budget-of-a-signed-in-reader)'s
profile only in where it runs.

Context: the profile was one compose project per machine (`quader-ui-dev`, fixed ports) whose state belonged to the checkout. A
builder's worktree that ran `make ui-renders` (which always runs `up.sh`) recreated the running containers with its own certificates
under whoever was looking at the stack (2026-11-20), and the dev server on 4200 served the other checkout's UI. A builder whose change
needed its own backend copied the compose file by hand (web-ui.md, "Nothing automates this"); nothing gave a builder a new database
(F-053, F-207, F-208).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Instances `UI_INSTANCE=1..8`: project `quader-ui-dev<n>`, state `.dev/ui-dev-<n>`, every port plus `(n - 1) * 100`; instance 1 exactly the former names and ports, and refused in a git worktree (chosen) | [instance.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/instance.sh), read by every script of the profile; the integration stack's shape | A builder renders against a stack of its own, a new database the default of a new instance; instance 1's configuration hash is unchanged, so a running stack is not recreated | A builder names its instance; eight at most (instance 9's dev server would be on 5000, macOS's AirPlay receiver) |
| (b) One state directory per machine (the main checkout's, through `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) | Every worktree uses the one stack | No new names | A worktree still restarts the stack and serves its UI on the owner's port |
| (c) Make the render seed independent of what the database holds | | No second stack | Unbounded: every migration and seed row is a new way to differ |

**Choice:** (a). `renders.sh` points the render configuration at the instance (`UI_RENDERS_EDGE`, `UI_RENDERS_STATE`,
`UI_RENDERS_POSTGRES`); [web.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/web.sh) starts the dev server on the instance's port with its certificate and
its quader (`make ui-dev-web`). The variables carry no `QUADER_` prefix: a quader process refuses every `QUADER_` variable that is not
a setting. Verified on the development machine on 2026-11-23: instance 1 refused from a worktree before anything ran; instance 2 from
a worktree up, seeded and rendered (`login` and `projects`, four pictures, 0 failed) and removed with `PURGE`, while instance 1's
three containers (same ids, up three days) and its processes on 4200, 19080, 19081 and 19090 (same pids) did not change; the compose
configuration hashes of instance 1 equal those of the former file.

**Applied in the spec:** none (development tooling). Code: [deploy/ui-dev/](../../deploy/ui-dev/), the `ui-*` targets of the
[Makefile](../../Makefile). Elsewhere: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#instances-one-per-builder),
[build-and-test.md](../developer/build-and-test.md#instances-and-their-ports).

### Q-UI-1044 · An instance of the UI development profile is claimed, not chosen

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
Amends [Q-UI-1031](#q-ui-1031--the-ui-development-profile-runs-in-instances-one-per-builder-and-instance-1-is-the-main-checkouts).

Context: under Q-UI-1031 a builder named its instance. On 2026-11-23 two builders chose instance 6 a minute apart, and the second
started its containers with its own certificates over the first's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A claim per instance, the file `<main>/.dev/ui-dev-claims/<n>` with the claiming checkout's path, read and written under an flock(2) lock; a worktree without `UI_INSTANCE` takes the instance it claims or the first free one; a number another existing checkout claims is refused; a claim whose checkout is gone is taken over after its compose project's containers and volumes are removed; an instance that runs without a claim is never picked and is refused when named, `down.sh` may still end it; `make ui-dev-down PURGE=1` ends a claim (chosen) | [instance.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/instance.sh) | Nobody chooses, so two cannot choose alike; a removed worktree frees its instance | A claim outlives a worktree that is removed while its stack runs, until the next claim finds it gone |
| (b) A lock held for as long as a process runs, as the integration stack's | — | Released by the kernel | The stack outlives every process of the profile; `up.sh` ends while its containers run |
| (c) An instance derived from the worktree's name | — | No file | Eight instances and any number of worktrees: two names map to one number |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the stack is state that outlives a process, so its owner is written down; the lock only makes the
reading and writing of that note one step. The development agent would revisit it if builders ever run on more than one machine
against one Docker daemon.

**Applied in the spec:** none (development tooling). Code: [instance.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/instance.sh), [down.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/down.sh);
held by `TestUIDevInstancesAreClaimedNotChosen` ([checkoutprofiles_test.go](../../internal/tools/ciworkflows/checkoutprofiles_test.go)).
Elsewhere: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#instances-one-per-builder).

### Q-UI-1045 · The layout checks' fixtures run in three engines, and Chromium sets text without hinting

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
Amends [Q-UI-723](#q-ui-723--the-checks-are-tested-on-fixture-pages-in-the-playwright-chromium-not-in-the-angular-test-runner).
A first form (the fixtures in three engines with two of them marked as failing in Firefox) landed and was taken back the same day:
the marks held on the development machine and not on the runner, whose Firefox found what the development machine's did not.

Context: two things measured differently on the development machine (macOS) and on the runner (Linux). (1) `label-apart` compared
the top of a value's first line with the bottom of its column's name; the box of a line of text is the font's content area, which
outgrows a line of 1rem by a pixel or two, by a different amount per engine and platform (Firefox on macOS measured the name 18 px
high, Chromium 17), so the same layout was "under the name" in one engine and not in the other. (2) The walk passed the audit log's
table on the development machine that fell to blocks on the runner: measured on 2026-11-23 with the app's font, Chromium on Linux
hints the glyphs and rounds every advance to a whole pixel, which set a bold line 366 px wide that macOS set 355.5 px wide (3 %);
Firefox and WebKit measured the same on both to a twentieth of a pixel, and the scrollbar is 15 px in Chromium on both once
`--hide-scrollbars` is not given.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The checks measure what they name in a way that holds in every engine (`label-apart`: the value's middle below the name's bottom), the fixtures run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with no mark for one engine, and Chromium runs with `--font-render-hinting=none` in the fixtures and the renders (chosen) | `layout.ts`, the two configurations, `CHROMIUM_TEXT` of `paths.ts`, the job installs Firefox and WebKit | One measurement on both machines; a builder's render is what the runner renders | The renders show Chromium's text without hinting, as macOS sets it, where a reader on Linux sees it hinted |
| (b) Marks per engine and machine | — | — | What the first form did; they hold until a machine changes |
| (c) A reserve in every check for the runner's wider text | — | No flag | A margin that only covers what was measured once, and hides an offset the check exists to find |

**Choice:** (a). Measured on the development machine and in the Linux image of the pinned Playwright (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright`,
arm64): the 150 fixture tests pass in all three engines on both; without the flag Chromium on Linux measured the four sample lines
2 to 13 px wider, with it within 0.05 px of macOS. The runner is amd64 with the browsers `playwright-install.sh` installs: its first
`UI layout checks` shows it, and only the pipeline can.

**Rationale:** the walk judges the layout a reader sees from the widths of text, and a width that depends on the machine makes the
judgment the machine's. The development agent would revisit it if the owner wants the renders to show Linux's hinted text, which
then needs a Linux browser on the development machine too.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-176. Code: [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) (`label-apart`),
[playwright.layout.config.ts](../../web/e2e/playwright.layout.config.ts), [playwright.renders.config.ts](../../web/e2e/playwright.renders.config.ts),
[paths.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/paths.ts), the job `ui-layout` of [release.yml](../../.github/workflows/release.yml).

### Q-UI-1047 · The UI development profile keeps the release's Sigstore root, and the walk answers a refreshed one

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the backend of the UI development profile (`deploy/ui-dev`) sent nine requests to `tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev` at every start:
the task `signature-trust-root` refreshes the public Sigstore root (R-SIG-017), verified from the TUF root the release embeds. The render
seed reaches no public registry since W13; this was the last request of the profile to the internet. What the section **Public Sigstore
root** of Settings › Signatures showed depended on it: the CDN's version when it was newer than the release's snapshot, the snapshot
otherwise, a failure without a network.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `signatures.trust_root.refresh: false` in the profile; its root is the snapshot the release embeds (`internal/signatures/shipped/data`, the repository's own data); the walk `signatureSettings` answers a refreshed root in the browser, without a failure and with one (chosen) | The stack's answer is the release's snapshot | No request leaves the machine; the section shows the same at every start; every state of the section is rendered: the snapshot (the stack's), refreshed, refreshed with a failure | The refreshed states are answers of the walk, not of the task |
| (b) A TUF repository of the profile's own, served on the machine, with `trust_root.url` pointing at it | The task runs | The task's own path | A repository the profile signs cannot be verified from the embedded TUF root; it needs a key that names another TUF root, a product setting that only the profile would use and that widens what an operator can make the installation trust |
| (c) A copy of the public repository's metadata (the release's `tuf/`) served on the machine | The task verifies the real chain | No new setting | The timestamp of that metadata expires days after the snapshot, so every later start records a failure, the state the profile should not show by default |

**Choice:** (a). The walk's section was closed after its reload and showed neither answered state before; it now opens it. **Rationale:**
the trust root that ships with the release is a real state an installation without internet has, and the screen's other states are
answered as the walk answers every state the stack cannot produce. The development agent would revisit it if the task's own path needs a
render, which a test of the task (`internal/signatures/shipped/tuftest`) covers today.

**Applied in the spec:** none (the development profile). Code: [config.sh](../../deploy/ui-dev/config.sh), `signatureSettings` of
[screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts). Elsewhere: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#local-ui-development).

### Q-UI-1048 · A German pass of the renders, for the screens marked for it

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `make ui-renders` renders in English: the dev server of the profile builds one locale (`development` holds `localize: ["en"]`),
and every walk finds its controls by English words. German pages were looked at only by hand in the embedded build, and Set up client's
German page was never rendered (section 12 of the plan). The checks of a German word's length exist only for the folds' labels
(Q-UI-810).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `UI_RENDERS_LOCALE=de`: the dev server builds the German locale (the configurations `de` of `web/angular.json`), the run renders the screens marked `de: true` into `.out/ui-renders-de`, and their walks find controls by their place, not their words (chosen) | A pass of chosen screens | The same seed, profile and checks as the English renders; a screen joins with one flag; no second source of words | A screen joins only once its walk is free of English words |
| (b) Every screen in German | The whole walk twice | Every German page seen | Most walks click by English names (a rewrite of 2,800 lines), and the run doubles the pipeline's longest job |
| (c) Render against the embedded build (`/ui/de/`) | The production build | The build that ships | A production build per render and a backend restart; the backend serves the build it embedded at its start |

**Choice:** (a). The German dev server runs on the instance's port in place of the English one (the base URL, the cookies and the origin
check stay those of the profile); `renders.sh` refuses to render against a dev server of the other language. The first screens: Set up
client (`setup-npm-virtual`, `setup-oci-local`, `setup-npm-bastion`) and the tab Downloads (`repository-npm-remote-downloads`).
The pipeline keeps the English renders. **Rationale:** the German words are longest where a layout breaks first; a screen whose words
change gets its German look at the price of one flag. The development agent would revisit it if a German finding in the running
installation shows a screen the pass did not hold.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-176. Code: [paths.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/paths.ts), [render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts),

### Q-UI-1049 · The renders run in Firefox or WebKit on demand, into a folder of their own

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the layout checks' fixtures run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (Q-UI-1045); the screens' renders in Chromium only. The colour

### Q-UI-1046 · A journey takes a page's words by their message ID, and the lint holds the ID and the words

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the screens' rounds of 2026-11-23 changed visible words twice in a way only the pipeline's kind legs showed: a journey
chose an option by "(generic)" after the option ended in the format's name, and the security dashboard's journey compared a link's
text after the link's text had taken its icon's ligature. The rule decided that day was a search of the journeys for the old words in
the same commit. The open question was whether the journeys' words can come from the source the pages take them from.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ui('<ID>')` reads the unit's source of `messages.xlf` (the German target with `'de'`); a lint rule fails an ID without a plain text and an ID whose words in the code (`$localize` with `:@@ID:`, an element's `i18n="@@ID"`) differ from `messages.xlf`; journeys move to it when they are next changed (chosen) | `ui` in [support.ts](../../web/e2e/support.ts), [journey-texts-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/journey-texts-rule.mjs) in `npm run lint` | A change of words reaches the journeys by itself; a removed ID, or words changed and not extracted, fail the landing's lint in seconds, not the kind leg | A journey reads less plainly (`ui('nav.security-dashboard')`); a text with a placeholder stays written out |
| (b) Import the compiled `$localize` messages into the journeys | — | The exact words of the build | The journeys run in Node against the deployed build, not in the app's bundle; a second build of the messages |
| (c) The search of the journeys for old words, per commit | — | Nothing to build | A rule a builder must remember; it was forgotten once |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the translation file is already the one list of every visible word by ID, which the German build
reads; reading it in the journeys adds no second source. What the rule cannot see (a text built at run time) stays written out and
under the search of the decision of 2026-11-23. The development agent would revisit it once the extraction check of the translation
file exists, which makes the words check of this rule a part of it.

**Applied in the spec:** none (test tooling). Code: `ui` in [support.ts](../../web/e2e/support.ts), the rule and its test in
[lint-rules.test.mjs](../../web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs), the journey [16-security-dashboard.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/vuln/16-security-dashboard.spec.ts).
