### Q-UI-1060 · What a layout check can hold of the render set's blind spots, and what stays to the eye

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
Continues the reading of 2026-11-23 ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen), "What the checks leave to the eye").
**Corrected in three points by [Q-UI-1170](#q-ui-1170--the-render-checks-see-overlays-and-clipping-as-a-person-does-correcting-q-ui-1060)**
(2026-11-25): a control beside a framed box, text drawn by CSS and a text cut at the start of a wrapped line had each been seen, and
`overlay-out`, `cut` and `separator-start` hold what this decision left to the eye of absolutely placed elements, CSS-drawn
separators and clipped lines.

Context: two lists of the plan named what the layout checks of the renders do not see. The builder of W-23: a control beside a framed
box, absolutely placed elements and text drawn by CSS, the states the set does not render, an offset of 1 px or less. The builder of
W-5: a wrapping column cramped beside a roomy neighbour ("3 findings · / 0 fixable" at 1,024 px), a text cut at the start of a wrapped
line, a stacked label off its control, two words for one thing across screens. The question is which of them a check of
[layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) can hold, measured in the page of every picture; the states and the words are not
layout, and the reading of 2026-11-23 set the rule that a check comes with the fixture of a defect that was seen.

| Blind spot | Can a check hold it? | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| An offset of 1 px or less | It is held: R-UI-175's threshold is "within 1 px", and the fixtures hold it from both sides (1.5 px fails, 0.5 px passes) | Not a blind spot; nothing to build |
| A control beside a framed box (a code block, a list of members) | Yes: its rule of Q-UI-724, that the control stands on the box, is a measurement of the control's top against the box's top edge | Not built: no such defect has been seen on a render, and the exception exists because measuring it against the text inside the box found false defects; a check `on-box` comes with the fixture of the first seen one |
| A wrapping column cramped beside a roomy neighbour | Yes: in a table that stands as a table, a short text (a summary, a count with its unit) in two or more lines whose one-line width the table could give it from a column that is wider than its widest content in every row; the measurement is the one `stacked-fits` already makes (the table's columns at their least widths, undone in the same task) | **Built, with the fixture of W-5's row** (`3 findings · / 0 fixable` beside a column of fixed width): a defect of this shape was seen. Not built by the package that decided it, since a new check lands with a run of the whole render set and the repair of every screen it then finds; built on 2026-11-24 (below) |
| Absolutely placed elements (menus, tooltips, a positioned hint) | In part: their overlap with text in the flow is measurable, their place is set by their anchor by design | Not built: no defect seen; `cell-overflow` and `sideways` already leave them out on purpose |
| Text drawn by CSS (`content` of `::before` and `::after`) | No: a pseudo-element has no node, so no range and no box can be read for it; only its string is (`getComputedStyle(el, '::before').content`) | Stays to the eye: the app draws only glyphs of icons and separators this way, which the pictures show |
| A text cut at the start of a wrapped line; a stacked label off its control | Yes, by measuring every wrapped line's first glyph and every stacked label's distance to its control | Not built, as decided on 2026-11-23: no defect of either shape seen; `label-apart` holds the stacked facts of a row |
| The states the set does not render (open menus, hover, most dialogs, error states) | No: a state is a screen of the set (a walk in `screens.ts`), not a check | Screens, outside this decision; W9 added the open row menus and the shared error notice |
| Two words for one thing across screens | No: vocabulary, not layout | Stays to the eye and to the translation files' review |

**Built on 2026-11-24** (the screens' package of round 3): `cramped` in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), with the fixture
of W-5's row and, from the first run of the whole set, two cases it must pass: a mark laid out under its text (the cell keeps its lines
when set on one line, so nothing wrapped) and a short value in a column of long values that wrap (an owner's path: the column is as wide
as the list gives it, and its short values wrap at that width as its long ones do). A text counts as short up to 40 characters; the
finding names the columns that have the room. That run found it on five screens; three are repaired in the same change: the sessions' "This
session" wrapped under the time in a column of 11 rem at 1,440 px (it stands under the time at every width now); the admin area's users,
whose e-mail broke at its hyphen at 1,024 px beside a column of names with a least width of 14 rem (the e-mail is one identifier now and
does not break, and the column of names has no least width of its own: at 10 rem the next run, its times one word longer, found the same
row by 11 px); the storage page's scrub, "96 % read within 30 days" in two lines in its 6.5 rem beside a State column kept at 11
rem for "Filling 63 % of the blobs" (the share on its line, the period as the cell's muted second line; a Scrub of 11 rem stacked the
table at 1,440 px). The audit log (an action's name, by 5 and 10 px) and the admin area's tokens (an owner's path, by 14 px) passed once
the two cases were in: their columns also hold values longer than a summary that wrap (the tokens' owners, paths of about 80 characters;
the audit's actions, names of up to about 60). The run after the repairs had no finding.

**Choice:** as in the table: one check (`cramped`), built on 2026-11-24 with a run of the whole set (above); the rest are held already, have no seen
defect, cannot be measured in the page, or are not layout. **Rationale:** every check measures every one of about 4,600 pictures and
has to be right on screens it was not written for (`stacked-offset` and `label-apart` were each wrong once on older screens before
they were right); the rule that a check follows a seen defect keeps the set's cost and its false findings down, and the one seen
defect gets its check. The development agent revisits a row when its defect is seen on a render.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-173 (the check `cramped`). Elsewhere:
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen), "What the checks leave to the eye".

### Q-UI-1061 · A mirror without its bound offers no run, and says who can set the bound

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a stored mirror of a well-known registry without its bound is in the state **No bound** (Q-CUR-43): no pass starts, and a
run answers `422 mirror_unbounded`. The status still offered **Run a pass now** and its menu as active buttons, so the only way to learn
that a run cannot start was to click and read the refusal; and its sentence ended "Set one in the mirror settings and save." for
every reader, though an Owner without `repositories:write-config` keeps the mirror's settings as stored
([Q-REPO-142](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-142--who-may-switch-a-remote-to-mirror)) and cannot set one (seen in R2's renders,
`power/repository-settings-npm-mirror-unbounded-unbounded-light-1440.png`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Run a pass now** and its menu disabled in the state **No bound**, the reason beside them; the state's sentence by who reads it (chosen) | The buttons stay where they are, disabled (`aria-describedby` names the reason, "No pass runs until the mirror has a bound."); the sentence ends "Set one in the mirror settings and save." for the holder of `repositories:write-config` and "Only an administrator of the installation can set one." for every other reader | The panel says before a click what the server would answer; nobody is told to do what they cannot; the style guide's rule that a disabled action says why, next to the button | Two sentences of one state to translate |
| (b) The buttons hidden in the state **No bound** | Nothing to click | Less on the screen | The way to a pass is gone without a word, and comes back unannounced when a bound is saved |
| (c) As built: the buttons active, the refusal in words after the click | No change | The refusal is an answer (Q-UI-121) | A click to learn what the status already knows |

**Choice:** (a). **Pause** stays active: a mirror without its bound may be paused. A paused mirror keeps **Run a pass now** active, and
its refusal stays an answer in words (Q-UI-121): **Resume** stands beside the button, so the way out is one click, and the browser
journey of the mirror holds that answer (`14-mirror.spec.ts`). **Rationale:** the state is the server's and is read with the panel,
so the panel knows the run's answer; a refusal that the screen could have shown is a question the user should not have had to ask.
The development agent would revisit the paused state if a reader is seen clicking a run there.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-021. Code: [mirror-status.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/mirror-status.ts) (`canSetBound`,
`stateInfo`), [repository-detail.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-detail.html). Tests:
[mirror-status.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/mirror-status.spec.ts) ("a mirror without its bound has "Run a pass
now" and its menu disabled …", "the sentence of a mirror without its bound says …"),
[mirror-tab.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/mirror-tab.spec.ts). Rendered: `repository-settings-npm-mirror-unbounded`
(`power`, `admin`), `repository-settings-oci-mirror-stored` and `repository-settings-deb-mirror-stored` (`stored-unbounded`). The manual:
[repositories.md](../manual/admin/repositories.md#the-status-of-a-mirror).

### Q-UI-1062 · The trend's axis numbers are text of the page beside the drawing

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the trend of the vulnerabilities (R-VULN-022) drew its axis numbers (0, 1,000, 2,000) as `<text>` of its SVG at 11 viewBox units.
The drawing scales with its width, so the numbers were about 6 px high at 390 px, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit alike (seen by W15 on
2026-11-24), and about 14 px at 1,440 px.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The numbers as HTML in a column of their own beside the drawing, at the app's small text size (`--quader-type-body-small`, 12 px), each at its grid line's share of the drawing's height; the drawing keeps its aspect and starts at the plot's edge (chosen) | The SVG draws the plot alone (viewBox `40 0 596 200`), at most 48rem wide (16rem high, as it was); the axis's column is as wide as its widest number | The text is the page's at every width and in every engine; its place follows the drawing without script | The drawing stands at the start of its card instead of its middle at a wide window |
| (b) The SVG's text set to a size computed from the drawing's scale (a resize observer) | The numbers stay in the drawing | One element | Script for a size; the margin for the numbers scales too and is too narrow for "2,000" at 12 px on a phone |
| (c) A larger font in the SVG | One value | Nothing moves | Still scales: readable at 390 px means large at 1,440 px |

**Choice:** (a). The numbers are formatted as the page's numbers are (`2,000`) and hidden from assistive technology: the chart's text
alternative and its table carry every number. **Rationale:** a text that must be read at every width belongs to the page, whose sizes
do not scale; the drawing keeps what scales. The development agent would revisit it if the chart gets a time axis with labels, which would
be laid out the same way.

**Applied in the spec:** R-VULN-022 (the UI line). Code: [report-trend.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/report-trend.ts),
[_vulnerabilities.scss](../../web/src/styles/_vulnerabilities.scss). Tests:
[vulnerability-report.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.spec.ts) ("the axis's numbers are text of
the page beside the drawing …"), and in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at 358 and 1,100 px
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) ("the axis's numbers keep the small text size and stand on their grid
lines …"). Rendered: `vulnerabilities` in the three engines.

### Q-UI-1063 · Feedback outside forms is the reference's toast at the bottom right, one confirmation at a time

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
The place is the owner's (2026-11-24, 08:02: "Und diese dann bitte unten rechts einblenden, nicht links").

Context: the owner's screenshot of the same morning ("Was sind dass denn für hässlich Notifications?"): after three registries were
switched on under **Upstream registries**, three pale grey boxes stood stacked at the bottom left over the side bar, each with its
sentence and a text button **Schließen**, and covered the side bar's **Seitenleiste einklappen**. The boxes were the inverse surface of
a Material snack bar (pale in the dark scheme), without a shadow, and every confirmation added one more. The reference's toast
(its design system's `GlToast`, read from its source) is a compact box at the bottom of the window: 16 by 24 px of padding, 8 px round,
a shadow, 14 px text at weight 300 on a 16 px line, its "strong feedback" fill (neutral 800, `#3a383f`, with white text) in both schemes,
an action as a bold link in its blue 300, and a close button that is a small tertiary icon button with the label **Close**; 24 px from
the corner, at most 586 px wide, across the window with 8 px each side below 576 px. It stops its 5 seconds while the pointer is on it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A new confirmation replaces the confirmation still shown; a notice with an action and an error keep their own toast (chosen) | `Notifier.status` without an action dismisses the plain confirmation on screen before it adds its own; the polite region announces each new one | A row of switches shows its last result, not a tower; what needs the user (an action, an error) is never pushed away | A confirmation shown for a second is read by a screen reader but may be missed by eye |
| (b) One toast of any kind at a time, the rest queued | A queue behind the visible toast | Never more than one box | An error waits behind confirmations; a queue of 8 s each lags behind what the user does |
| (c) A stack of at most N | The oldest goes when the N+1st comes | Keeps some history | Still stacks; the owner's three were already too many |
| (d) Repeated confirmations merged into one ("3 registries are on") | A counter per kind of message | One box with the sum | Needs a kind per message in every caller (about 190); a sum hides which registries |

**Choice:** (a); every notice of the `Notifier` is the reference's toast. What that takes:

- **Look:** the reference's measures and its strong feedback colours as three tokens, `--quader-feedback-strong-bg` (`#3a383f`),
  `-fg` (white) and `-link` in both schemes. The link is `#66a8ea`, the reference's `#63a6e9` a hair lighter, which gives 4.49:1 on the
  grey: the same step the accent takes (R-UI-044). The shadow is `--quader-elevation-2`, the app's shadow of what floats over the page,
  not a fourth shadow token for the reference's slightly smaller one (the style guide adds no shadow). The close button is a 24 px icon
  button, the action a link-like button; both stand on the middle of the text's first line (R-UI-175), which for one line is the toast's
  middle, as the reference centres them.
- **An error** keeps the toast's shape, place and close button in the colours and with the icon of the shared error notice
  (`error-notice.ts`), so it is not told by colour alone. The reference shows an error as an alert in the page; a `Notifier` alert has no
  place in a page (a failed copy, a refused download link, anywhere), so it stays a toast.
- **Place:** the window's bottom right, the owner's; 24 px from the corner, at most 586 px wide; below 576 px across the window with
  8 px each side. Above the overlays (`z-index` 1100, as the reference's), so a confirmation of a copy in a dialog is seen. A page's own
  controls at the bottom right are not covered at 1,024 px and wider: the policy editor's save bar has its buttons at its start; at
  390 px a toast spans the window, as the reference's does, and is closed with its "×" or goes after its time.
- **Time:** 8 seconds as before (the reference's 5 are short for a sentence of a registry's name), stopped while the pointer or the
  focus is on the toast and going on with what was left, at least 1 second (the reference's least).
- **A warning of the same write** goes into the same status after its confirmation (the upstream registries' level and the ClamAV
  definitions' switch), since a second status would now replace the first.

**Rationale:** the stack was the defect the owner saw, and only plain confirmations stack in normal use (each switch, each saved
setting); replacing them ends it without hiding what needs the user. Everything else is the reference's toast as its source sets it.
The development agent would revisit (a) if a confirmation that matters is found to be replaced before it can be read; then (d) for that
caller.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042 (the bullet of the live regions). Code: [notifier.ts](../../web/src/app/core/notifier.ts),
[notices.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/notices.ts), the tokens in [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss) (the inverse
accent of the snack bar is gone), `withWarnings` in [upstream-actions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/upstream/upstream-actions.ts). Tests:
[notices.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/notices.spec.ts) (one confirmation at a time, actions and errors keep their place, the time
that stops, the close button named **Close**), [palette.spec.ts](../../web/src/styles/palette.spec.ts) (the toast's pairs). Rendered:
`admin-upstream-toasts` (one toast, a replaced one, three kinds side by side), in English and German. Docs:
[design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md) (the controls' table, the palette), [ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md#lists),
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).

### Q-UI-1064 · An age and its badge are one value that never breaks

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the layout checks of Test and Release (run 45340888441) failed on the databases of `upstream/clamav` at 1,024 px with the
`daily` built 8 days ago: the column **Age** held "8 days" over **Outdated** in two lines while the column **Database** had 26 px that
no row used, 25 px were missing for one line (R-UI-173). The finding came and went by the day: the render's build times count from its
clock, so the column **Built** shows that day's dates and hours ("Nov 16, 2026, 7:12:03 AM" is wider or narrower than the day before),
and the table's own layout shares the room by those widths.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The age and its badge on one line that never breaks, as a time and a status each never break (Q-UI-563); the column declares no width and is as wide as both (chosen) | `white-space: nowrap` on the cell | The cell reads as one value on every day; the table takes the room from the columns that wrap (the database's sentence) | The column is about 150 px wide in the row that is outdated |
| (b) The badge on a line of its own under the age, by design | A block under the age | The column stays as narrow as the badge | Two lines where one fits; the token lists put a badge under a time only where the time is a sentence of its own |
| (c) A declared width for the column | A number | Small change | A guess for one language and one font; Q-UI-563 dropped such widths |

**Choice:** (a), and the same for a word that stands in a time's place (`.no-time`: **Never**, **Not used yet** of the token lists
and a Bastion's tokens): the German pass of the renders found "Noch nicht verwendet" in two lines at 1,440 px beside the token's
column with 74 px to spare. The scanner list's database already holds its badge and its age so (Q-UI-915). The other cells that show a time and
a badge in a table put the badge under the time by their layout (the token lists, a Bastion's tokens, an issuer's keys), which the
check reads as layout and no day changes. **Rationale:** a value that does not depend on its neighbours' widths cannot flip with the
calendar. The development agent revisits it if the column pushes the table into stacked rows at a width where it fitted before.

Two fixed dates of the render set changed with the calendar as well and count from its clock now: the file of `upstream/clamav`
(`files-system`, its times are "… ago") and the Notation certificate of the signatures (it would read "expired on …" from
2027-04-30 on).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-194. Code: [clamav-databases.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/clamav-databases.ts)
(the cell without an age shows the dash too), `.no-time` in [_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) with
[token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/access/token-table.ts),
[technical-token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/features/service-accounts/technical-token-table.ts) and
[bastion-card.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-card.ts), [screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts) `systemFileView`,
[signatures.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/signatures.ts) `notationLeaf`. Rendered: `clamav-databases` (both states, every width) with no
finding; the token lists and the Bastions page with none.

### Q-UI-1065 · The tooltip is the reference's: the toast's grey, above the element, with an arrow

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the tooltip was a bubble of Quader's inverse surface (`#28272d` in the light scheme, the pale `#ececef` in the dark one), 8 px
round, under the element. The reference's tooltip (its design system's tooltip, read from its source: `tooltip.scss` on Bootstrap's
tooltip) is its "strong feedback" fill in both schemes, the same `#3a383f` with white text as its toast (Q-UI-1063): 12 px text at
weight 400 on a 16 px line, 8 by 12 px of padding, 4 px round, a medium shadow, at most 200 px wide with the text centred, above the
element by default, and an arrow of 8 by 4 px in the 4 px between the bubble and the element.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The reference's tooltip whole: the strong feedback pair, its measures, its arrow, above first and under where the window has no room above (chosen) | Colour, shape and place as the source sets them | Toast and tooltip one grey in both schemes, as in the reference; the arrow says which element the text belongs to | The bubble covers what stands above the element, where it covered what stood below |
| (b) Only the colours | The two tokens | Smallest change | Shape and place still Quader's own, against the rule to copy the reference |
| (c) Keep the inverse surface and darken it in the dark scheme | Another pair | — | A second grey for the same kind of thing |

**Choice:** (a). The shadow is `--quader-elevation-2`, as for the toast, not a shadow token of its own (the style guide adds none).
The arrow points at the element's middle, read from where the bubble stands, also where the window's edge pushed the bubble aside
(at 390 px). A scroll moves the bubble with its element, as the reference's does, where it used to close it. The inverse surface tokens had no other use and are gone. **Rationale:** the owner's direction is to copy the reference
and add no styling of one's own; the pale bubble in the dark scheme was the visible defect. The development agent revisits the
place above the element if a tooltip is found to cover the control the user needs next.

**Applied in the spec:** none (R-UI-044's tooltip rule is unchanged). Code: [tooltip.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tooltip.ts),
[_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss). Tests: [tooltip.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tooltip.spec.ts) (above
first, the text in its box beside the arrow), [palette.spec.ts](../../web/src/styles/palette.spec.ts) (the strong feedback pair, which
the tooltip now reads). Rendered: `profile-tokens-tooltip` (the token's **Rotate** focused), in English and German. Docs:
[design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md) (the controls' table, the palette), [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).

### Q-UI-1066 · A version's commands are a menu hung from a button with the format's client verb

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
**Revised by the owner on 2026-11-25** ([Q-UI-1240](#q-ui-1240--the-panel-of-a-versions-commands-is-a-tab-per-client-and-set-up-client-at-the-rows-end)): the panel's sections are tabs, one per client, with **Set up client**
at the row's end; the button stands in a version page's head too ([Q-UI-1241](#q-ui-1241--a-versions-page-has-its-command-behind-the-verbs-button-in-its-head-the-box-is-gone)).
The request is the owner's (2026-11-24, 09:50, with a picture of `upstream/docker-hub` and one of GitLab's **Code** menu): "Der Kaste
„Pull-Befehl" ist einfach mitten drin und passt dort nicht gut hinein. Der Pull-Befehl soll viel mehr in ein overlay wie in
screenshot 2 abgebildet überführt werden. Neben einer Version des Artefakts gibt es einen Button, aktuell „Befehl anzeigen" (Scheiß
Name) und wenn man da drauf klickt, öffnet das Overlay und man kann dort den jeweiligen Befehl entnehmen. Der Button sollte eher
„Info" oder „Pull" heißen. Das gilt natürlich für alle Registry-Typen".

Context: an opened row of a repository's list held a bordered box **Pull command** (**Install command**) with a client select and the
command of one version, above the versions table, whose rows had a quiet button **Show command** that only changed which version the box
showed. The box stood between the item and its versions for every format, and the button's word did not say what it did. GitLab's
**Code** button opens a panel under it: sections with a bold heading, each a read-only field with its joined copy button.

**The button's word.**

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Info** for every format | One word, the owner's first | Short, the same everywhere | Says nothing of what the panel holds (commands); "Info" is the word of a page of facts, and the version's page is that page already (R-UI-111) |
| (b) **Pull** for every format | The owner's second word | The OCI client's verb | npm, NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy clients do not pull; a reader of a Debian repository reads "pull" as git's |
| (c) The format's client verb with a chevron, as GitLab's **Code ▾**: **Pull** for an image, **Install** for a package (npm, NuGet, Debian, Ansible Galaxy, every package format), **Download** for a file (chosen) | `commandVerb` of the format's words (content-shape.ts) | Says what the commands in the panel do, in the words of the format's client (`docker pull`, `npm install`, `apt-get install`); the owner's **Pull** where it is the client's word; the chevron says that it opens something, as GitLab's does | Three words, not one; a new format names its verb (one line) |
| (d) A neutral noun, **Commands ▾** or **Use ▾** | One word that is no client's | The same everywhere | Longer than the verbs and vaguer; a reader of an image looks for "pull" |

**What the panel holds.**

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A section per client of the format, its heading the client's name, its field the command with the joined copy button, all at once (chosen) | GitLab's **Clone with SSH** and **Clone with HTTPS** | Every client's command is one click and one copy away; no choice to make and no state to keep; the same panel for one client (Debian, Ansible Galaxy, generic) and for four (npm) | One request per client when the panel opens (two for OCI, three for NuGet, four for npm) |
| (b) A segmented group of the clients above one field, the last choice remembered per device | GitLab's **SSH \| HTTPS** groups | One request at a time | npm's four names (**Yarn Berry (2 and later)**) do not fit a group at 390 px; a choice before the copy; the remembered choice hides the other clients |
| (c) The client select of the old box inside the panel | What was there | Nothing new | A form control in a menu, and two steps for a command |

**Where the button stands.** At the end of every version's row (the column of actions, its label for assistive technology only), and
at the end of every item's row for the item's latest version, the version of its column **Latest** (chosen): the version copied most
often is one click away without opening the row. Only in the versions' rows was weighed and left: the common case would take two clicks.

**What the panel is.** A non-modal dialog (`role="dialog"`, named "Pull library/ubuntu 26.10"), hung from the button by the CDK's
connected overlay: below it with its end on the button's end, above it where the window has no room below, and pushed into the window
16 px from every edge; as wide as its longest command, so that a command is read whole where there is room (Q-UI-455), from 24 to
48 rem and never wider than the window less 32 px, so at 390 px it fits without a sideways scroll; it is placed again as it grows; a
command longer than its field scrolls inside the field from its start. It takes the focus as it opens and keeps Tab inside; Escape, a
click outside it and the button close it, and the focus goes back to the button, unless the click outside landed on another control,
which keeps its focus. A menu of the CDK (`role="menu"`) was not taken: a menu holds menu items, and this panel holds fields and copy
buttons. Each section is a group named by its heading. A command is asked when the panel opens (`credentials=none`, R-API-030); a
command of several lines is the snippet's window collapsed after three lines (Q-UI-801), as on the version's page.

**Choice:** (c), the panel (a), the button in both rows. German: **Pull** (the owner's word and the command's; the glossary's "ziehen"
stays the word of running text), **Installieren**, **Herunterladen**; the field is **Befehl für npm**, its copy button **Befehl für npm
kopieren**.

**Rationale:** the owner's two words each fit one format and miss the others; the client's verb is what each format's reader looks for,
and the chevron makes it GitLab's button. A section per client is GitLab's panel and leaves nothing to choose. The development agent
would revisit (b) of the panel if a format comes with more than four clients, so that the panel would be taller than a phone's window.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052 (the versions, the row of an item, the acceptance criteria), R-UI-010 and R-UI-193 (no button where no
client is answered). Code: [client-command-menu.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.ts),
[client-command.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command.ts) (one client's command, which the head of the version page

### Q-UI-1067 · Details is the last tab of a repository's page, not a section under its list

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
The tab and its place are the owner's (2026-11-24, 09:50): "Das Details welches unten abgebildet ist, gehört in einen eigenen Reiter. An
letzter Position."

Context: a repository's further addresses, the upstream a remote caches and the members a virtual repository resolves from stood in a
closed section **Details** under the list (Q-UI-313, Q-UI-319). Only a remote repository had tabs (R-CUR-018); a local or virtual one had
none, and one tab is no strip (Q-UI-652). The section's facts depend on the reader: the reader's view of R-REPO-010 carries the
addresses and neither the upstream nor the members; the full document carried the members and the upstream, and the page built only the
format's address from it, so an Owner never saw the address for downloads by path that every other reader saw.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) **Details** a tab with its address (`…/details`), always the last, on every repository of every format and class that has details for its reader; a page that would have only its content keeps no strip, and its address `…/details` leads to the content (chosen) | One rule for every page; the strip a local or virtual repository gains is its content and **Details** | The owner's tab and place; a deep link; nothing empty is offered | A local generic repository has no tab **Details** (its only address is its client address, which Set up client shows), so a strip is not on every page |
| (b) The tab on every page, with a sentence where there is nothing | The strip everywhere | Every page alike | An empty tab on every local generic repository, for every reader |
| (c) The section kept, open, above the list | No tab | Seen at once | Not what the owner asked; the list moves down by the section's height |

**Choice:** (a). With it, the full document's addresses are built from the catalog as the reader's view lists them, the format's
address first and the address for downloads by path after it where they differ (R-REPO-002), so the tab holds the same address for an
Owner as for a reader. The tab shows each fact under its name (**Address for downloads by path (curl, wget)** with its copy button,
**Caches**, **Resolves from**), as a further address had it in the section (Q-UI-320). The section's remembered state
(`repository.details`, Q-UI-967) ends with it; the render walk of a remembered **Details** takes a file's.

**Rationale:** the owner named the place; one tab is no strip stays true (Q-UI-652), so a page gains a strip only where it has a second
view. The development agent would revisit (b) if a fact every repository has (its creation, its storage) joins **Details**: then the tab
is on every page.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052 (the tabs, the tab Details, the acceptance criteria), R-UI-193, [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md)
R-CUR-018 (the strip ends with **Details**). Code: [repository-tabs.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-tabs.ts)
(the strip of every repository, formerly the remote's), [repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts)
(`hasDetails`, `tabStrip`, the view `details`, the way from an address without details to the content), the route `details` of
[repositories.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repositories.routes.ts). Tests:
[repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts) (the strip of a local and of a
remote repository, the tab's facts, the address of a repository without details),
[remote-downloads.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.spec.ts) and
[remote-upstream.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream/remote-upstream.spec.ts) (the remote's strip ends with
**Details**). Rendered: `repository-npm-local-details`, `repository-oci-remote-details`, `repository-npm-virtual-details`. Docs:
[repositories.md](../manual/user/repositories.md#the-content-of-a-repository), [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).
### Q-UI-1070 · The Downloads button stands between Documentation and the theme, and counts what runs

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
The place at the top right is the owner's (T-26, 2026-11-24, 08:20: "Ich will als Admin oben Rechts eine Downlaod Übersicht haben").

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An icon button between **Documentation** and the theme button, a count badge while downloads run (chosen) | The order: Admin, Documentation, Downloads, theme, avatar | At the top right, where the owner's picture has it; a count is the one fact worth a glance; no motion | One more icon in the bar |
| (b) Inside the **Admin** button's area or the admin side bar | No new place | No change to the bar | Not at the top right; not seen outside the admin area |
| (c) As (a) with a moving icon while downloads run | Activity at a glance | Noticed | Motion that runs for hours; reduced-motion users get nothing more |

revisit (c) if the owner wants activity shown without a number.

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|

### Q-UI-1073 · The panel refreshes by polling while it is seen, and announces nothing

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The full list every `pollSeconds` (2 s) while open and visible; the summary every 10 s while closed and visible; no live region; closing stops it (chosen) | Polling, as the tab Downloads and System status do | No stream infrastructure (the app has none); costs nothing in a hidden tab; a screen reader is not flooded by progress | Up to 4 s behind the body (publication plus poll) |
| (b) A server-sent event stream | Push | Fresher | A stream per administrator through the edge and every replica; nothing like it exists |
| (c) A polite announcement of each end | Spoken ends | Hears what finished | A chatty region during an `npm install` |

**Choice:** (a). The button's accessible name carries the count. **Rationale:** the only option that needs nothing new on the server and
stays quiet for assistive technology. The development agent would revisit (b) if the app gains an event stream to the browser.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-210, R-UI-211. Code: [page-visibility.ts](../../web/src/app/core/page-visibility.ts).

### Q-UI-1074 · A tab strip wider than its place scrolls without a scrollbar, with a fade and a chevron at the edge

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a package version's strip **Dateien, Signaturen, Details, Schwachstellen** at 390 px in German was wider than the window
and showed a scrollbar under **Schwachstellen** (the render `package-version-oci-not-checked`, 2026-11-24). Every strip of Quader
is the one class `.tab-nav` (nine of them: a version's tabs, a repository's, the profile's, the packages' views, the search's,
a CI issuer's, System status, Download limits and the usage's views), and a repository's page holds up to four tabs since that day.
GitLab's scrollable tabs (`GlScrollableTabs` of GitLab UI) hide the strip's overflow and put a 2rem fade from the page's fill at an
edge beyond which tabs lie, holding a chevron button (`chevron-lg-left`, `chevron-lg-right`, `tabindex="-1"`) that scrolls the
strip by its width.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) As GitLab: no scrollbar, a fade with a chevron at an edge beyond which tabs lie, a click on it scrolls by a page; the strip still scrolls by a swipe, Shift and the wheel, and the keyboard; the current tab and a focused tab are scrolled clear of the fades (chosen) | One directive, `quaderTabStrip`, on every strip | GitLab's look; the hint is where the tabs are; nothing moves when it appears; a phone swipes as before | A little script per strip |
| (b) The scrollbar hidden and a fade only, drawn by the stylesheet | No script | Cheapest | No way to scroll for a mouse without a wheel; the current tab can stand beyond the edge on arrival |
| (c) The tabs wrap to a second line | No scrolling | Everything seen | Two rows read as two strips (UI-A-12); not GitLab |
| (d) The tabs that do not fit go into a menu **More** | No scrolling | Everything reachable in one place | Not GitLab; the menu's width changes with the language; a tab's place jumps between strip and menu as the window changes |

**Choice:** (a). The strip's `overflow-x` stays `auto` where GitLab hides the overflow: a swipe on a phone, the 390 px case, keeps
working. The fades are `aria-hidden` buttons out of the tab order: the tabs themselves are reached by Tab (links) or the arrow
keys (a `tablist`), and a tab that takes the focus is scrolled clear of the fade, so the keyboard needs no button of its own and a
`tablist` stays a list of tabs alone. A fade is 2rem from `--quader-surface` (the content panel's fill) to transparent; it stands
inside the strip, sticky at its edge with a negative margin, so showing it moves no tab and a strip needs no wrapper element.

**Rationale:** the owner's direction is GitLab's look; the hint has to say that more tabs lie beyond the edge without a scrollbar,
and the current tab has to be in view when the page opens on it (`?tab=vulnerabilities` at 390 px). The development agent would
revisit (d) if a strip ever holds more tabs than a phone can page through in two clicks.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-173. Code: [tab-strip.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tab-strip.ts), `.tab-nav` and `.tab-strip-fade`
of [_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss); the lint rule [tab-strip-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/tab-strip-rule.mjs)
(every strip carries the directive and its component imports it); the render check `tab-scrollbar` of
[layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts). Docs: [design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md) (the tab strip),
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md) (the checks).

### Q-UI-1068 · A stacked row's column name wraps between its words, never inside one

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: in the renders of the pull menu (2026-11-24, 10:30) a Debian repository's versions, opened in its packages at 390 px in German,
read "Veröffentli" / "cht" for **Veröffentlicht**. Two causes. The versions' list stands in a block of the packages' stacked list and is
laid out by that list's rules (its descendant selectors) without counting itself as stacked, so it measured no names and took the outer
list's column of names, 82 px for **Aktualisiert**; the versions on the tab Upstream had a fixed 7 rem on their host for the same reason.
And the column of names is the longest name up to two fifths of the list (Q-UI-1050), where a name breaks where it must
(`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so a German compound wider than two fifths broke inside itself in any list. No check saw it: the
`broken` check of a word in a cell leaves stacked tables out, and a column's name is a pseudo-element.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The column of names is never narrower than the list's longest word (the names measured once more at their least width), so a name longer than two fifths wraps between its words; a list in a block of a stacked list measures its own names (chosen) | Two measurements of the hidden list of names; a list that stacks or stops stacking asks the lists in its rows to measure again | No word broken in any language; the versions' column fits their own names, as every stacked list's does | A list with a very long single word (none of Quader's names in English or German) gives its values less room |
| (b) Hyphenation by the browser (`hyphens: auto`, the page's `lang`) | A hyphen at a syllable | The column keeps two fifths | Chromium on Linux, the runner's engine, brings no hyphenation dictionary, so the renders and the machines break differently; a name hyphenated in a column of two words reads worse than one wrapped between them |
| (c) The column as wide as its longest name, without the cap | No wrap | Simple | A long name of several words takes the values' room at 390 px |

**Choice:** (a). `overflow-wrap: break-word` stays as the last resort for a word wider than the whole list, which would otherwise run
into its value. **Rationale:** a word broken inside itself is the defect the owner's eye catches first; the measurement that fixes it
costs one more read of a hidden element, and the nested list's own names remove the fixed 7 rem. The development agent revisits (b) if a
language with long single words (Finnish, Hungarian) joins the build and a column of names takes half a phone's line.

The render run measures it: `broken` names a column's name broken inside a word in a stacked row, measured letter by letter in the
span that stands in for the pseudo-element ([layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) `nameBox`).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-174. Code: [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts) (`measure`),
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss), [upstream-package.scss](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream/upstream-package.scss)
(the fixed 7 rem gone). Tests: "R-UI-174 a stacked row's column of names is never narrower than its longest word, so a name wraps only
between words" and "R-UI-174 a list in a block of a stacked list measures the names of its own rows" in
[data-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.spec.ts); "R-UI-174 a column's name broken inside its word is found; one
that wraps between its words passes" in [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts). Docs:
[ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md), [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md). Rendered: `repository-deb-menu` in German
and English at every width ("Veröffentlicht" on one line in a column of its own at 390 px), and every screen without a walk in German at
390 px (234 pictures) with no column's name broken.

### Q-UI-1069 · A column of relative times holds the widest relative time of its language

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the layout package of the morning (Q-UI-1064) left a line: on a reused UI instance the personal token list stacked at 1,024 px
"as the token's **Created** grows from now to 9 minutes ago", which CI's fresh database would never show. Measured on 2026-11-24 it does
not hold as written: with a token made a moment before ("now") the list stacks at 1,024 px too, its columns need 773 px of the 712 its
region has, and **Created** is not one of them there (a `narrow` column, hidden below 64 rem of the list); a picture of 2026-11-20 shows
the same blocks. What the suspicion named is real all the same: a column of times is as wide as the widest age its rows show, the
renders seed ages of minutes, an installation shows "11 months ago" and "vor 23 Stunden", and a list near its budget changes its form
with the calendar (the `clamav-databases` of Q-UI-1064 was one).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The data table gives a column whose cells start with a relative time (`<quader-time-ago>`) the least width of the widest relative time of the build's language, measured from the wordings `relativeTime` can write (chosen) | `relativeTimeWords`: "now", and per unit its largest count and the words of one and two, before and after now; a hidden list the table measures; the header's `time-column` | Every list, without a change of its own; the renders show the layout an installation shows on any day | A column of times is about 100 px wide also where every row says "now"; a list near its budget may stack where it fitted with fresh ages |
| (b) The renders seed older times ("vor 59 Minuten") | A fixture per screen | Shows the case where seeded | Only the seeded screens; the installation still changes with the calendar |
| (c) The reserve on the time element itself | Every relative time as wide as the widest | No table involved | A gap after a short time inside a sentence ("created now ·"), as many times stand in running text |
| (d) A declared width per column | A number per list | Simple | A guess for one language and one font (Q-UI-1064 (c)) |

**Choice:** (a). A column that declares its least width (`width`) keeps it; such widths hold the widest time already (a Bastion's
**Time** and its tokens' **Expires**). A time inside a sentence ("Created 3 days ago", "Lifted by … 2 hours ago") makes no column of times.
**Rationale:** a list's form that does not depend on the age of its rows cannot flip with the calendar, and the render run then judges
the form every installation has. The development agent revisits it if a list that holds a time column stacks at 1,440 px.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-103, R-UI-174. Code: [format-time.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/format-time.ts)
(`relativeTimeWords`), [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts) (`startsWithTime`, the label pass, `measure`),
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) (`th.time-column`). Tests: "R-UI-103 the widest wordings of a relative
time in a language are the ones a column of times holds" in [time-ago.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/time-ago.spec.ts), "R-UI-103
R-UI-174 a column of relative times holds the widest relative time of the language, whatever age its rows show" in
[data-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.spec.ts); the check `cramped` counts the room a column of times keeps as
used ("R-UI-173 the room a column of relative times keeps for the widest one of the language is not room to give" in
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts)). Docs: [ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md),
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).

What the full render run showed, measured in every picture with and without the least width (2026-11-24, 87 screens with a column of
times; the widest English wording is 102 px): two tables change their form. A project's service account's technical tokens needed 690
px of 689 at 1,024 px with **Last used** at its widest; the token's least width is 9.5 rem now
([technical-token-table.ts](../../web/src/app/features/service-accounts/technical-token-table.ts)), which keeps it a table there
without a scrollbar beside the page, as it was with fresh ages (with one, it stood as blocks before and after). A ClamAV version's
repositories at 390 px are blocks now, one field a line. The same run found the sessions' **Created** ("Nov 24, 2026, 9:24:50 AM") in two
lines in a column of 11 rem by the clock's hour, as Q-UI-1064 found the ages: the sessions' dates are `<time>` values that never break

the exception above, and the screens re-rendered without a finding), `profile-tokens` and `profile-sessions` in both languages, and every screen without a walk in German at 390 px.

### Q-UI-1075 · A view is live by one shared poll that reads in place, and only while it is seen

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's rule of R-UI-213. Eight views polled on their own, each with its own timer and rule, most only while something
ran and some in a hidden tab too; every other view showed what it read once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One helper `live()`: a view names its interval (fast while something runs, slow while nothing does); the helper reads while the window is seen and the view shown, at once on return, with back-off; the reads replace in place (`PagedResource.refresh`, `refreshResource`) (chosen) | Polling, as the views that polled already did | Nothing new on the server; a hidden tab costs nothing; one rule for every view, tested once | Up to the interval behind; a list reads again what it shows |
| (b) A server-sent event stream of changes | Push | Fresh at once | A stream per tab through the edge and every replica, and an event for every change of every kind of row; nothing like it exists (Q-UI-1073 (b)) |
| (c) A "what changed since" endpoint, polled | One cheap call per view, the list read only on a change | Cheapest at idle | A change counter for every list a reader may see, scoped like the list (H-1847) |
| (d) Read again by restarting the view's list or resource | The existing `reload()` | No new code | The list empties and fills again (rows, open rows and focus lost); a failed read replaces the rows with an error |

**Choice:** (a). The existing polls move onto it where that is a pure simplification (System status, Jobs, Backups, Storage, the admin
dashboard, Mirror status, a Debian repository's indexes, the banner); the top bar's Downloads (R-UI-210, R-UI-211) and the tab Downloads
(R-CUR-018) keep their own. The tab Downloads moved onto it on 2026-11-25
([Q-UI-1102](#q-ui-1102--the-tab-downloads-is-live-by-the-shared-poll-5-s-while-something-moves-30-s-otherwise)). **Rationale:** the only option that needs nothing on the server and keeps every view's state; the views
that changed most often already polled, and (d) is what made the jobs list and the backups' runs jump every few seconds. A view whose
change is cheap to detect (a package's summary, the list of ClamAV databases) reads that first and the rest only on a change. The
development agent would revisit (c) when the idle cost of many open tabs shows in the replicas' request rate, and (b) if the app gains
an event stream to the browser.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-213; R-UI-021's status read (every 30 s while no pass runs). Code:
[live-refresh.ts](../../web/src/app/core/live-refresh.ts), [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts).

### Q-UI-1076 · A status too long for a pill puts its verdict on the badge and the rest after it

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: in the German renders at 390 px (2026-11-24, 11:40 and 12:00) a version's files showed the signature badge
"Signiert · Signierer nicht vertrauenswürdig" in a stacked row: 269 px as one pill, 41 px wider than the cell's column of values, so
the page scrolled sideways (`package-version-oci`, `package-version-signatures-files`). The English "Signed · signer not trusted" is
180 px and had already cost the files' table its column **Download** at 1,024 px (Q-UI-1051). A badge does not break (R-UI-171).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The badge carries the verdict, **Signed**, and the words "signer not trusted" follow it as muted text that wraps between its words: in a list's cell the cell's second line, as a refused file's reason stands under **Refused here** (R-SIG-074); in a header's facts, a fact and the details on the badge's line (chosen) | GitLab's way of a status with a qualifier: a short badge and a sentence beside it | Fits every cell in every language; the badge keeps its one line and its 20 px; the words stay the state's words, nothing is hidden | The pill no longer holds the whole state; the four badges are not built alike |
| (b) A badge may wrap between its words | A pill of two lines where its cell is narrow | Every long badge at once | Breaks R-UI-171 for every status, and a pill of two lines is no badge of the design language |
| (c) The badge cut with an ellipsis, the whole words in its title | One line | Short | A state is its words (Q-UI-128); a title is not read on a phone |
| (d) A shorter German text ("Signiert · nicht vertrauenswürdig") | A translation | Smallest change | 18 px from the edge at 390 px, it tells that the signature, not its signer, is not trusted, and the next language meets the same wall |

**Choice:** (a), for the untrusted state only. **Verified · public**, **Verified · internal** and **Invalid signature** are short enough
for a pill in every cell (the widest, "Verifiziert · öffentlich", is about 150 px). The whole words stay the state's name wherever a
fact or a sentence names it ("Signed · signer not trusted", `signatureStateWord`); where the badge opens the details' state line,
its words end with a full stop before the sentence. The badge carries `data-state`, so a walk of the
renders finds the state in every language. **Rationale:** the verdict is what a reader looks for in a column of badges, and the
qualifier is a short sentence about it; a pill that never breaks keeps every list's rows on one line. The development agent revisits
it if a verified state's words grow (a third scope), and then splits them the same way.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-171, R-SIG-035 ([signatures.md](signatures.md)). Code:
[signature-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/signatures/signature-words.ts) (`note`, `words`),
[signature-badge.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/signatures/signature-badge.ts). Tests: "R-SIG-035 each of the four states renders its
words and its shield; green only for the verified ones, red for an invalid one" and "R-SIG-035 R-UI-171 the untrusted state keeps its
badge short and says the rest after it, as text that may wrap; a fact says the whole words" in
[signatures.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/signatures/signatures.spec.ts); the render state
`package-version-signatures-untrusted-files` joins the German pass. Rendered: that screen and `package-version-signatures-files`,
`package-version-oci`, in English and German, both schemes, 1,440, 1,024 and 390 px, and every screen of the signatures in English.
At 1,024 px the files' table keeps its form in German with the state's words on the cell's second line, where the pill of 269 px
had left it a few pixels from blocks (Q-UI-1051).

### Q-UI-1077 · Below 36 rem of content a fact's term stands above its value

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-24** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: in the German renders at 390 px (2026-11-24) a Debian version's **Details** showed the maintainer
"Platform engineering &lt;platform@example.invalid&gt;" broken inside the address ("&lt;platform@example.inv" / "alid&gt;"), and an
Ansible collection's links broke inside their addresses: the term's column was as wide as its longest term, and German terms
("Suites und Komponenten", "Dokumentations-Website") left the value 162 to 164 px. Five screens had already stacked their own facts below a
width of their own (an audit event, Q-UI-972; a download's detail; the storage page; a signing identity; a limit's explanation).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every `dl.facts` puts each term above its value below 36 rem of the content panel, and a dialog's below 36 rem of the window (chosen) | GitLab's sidebar and its pages on a phone: a label over its value | One rule for every list of facts; the value gets the whole line, so an address breaks only where it is longer than the line | A phone's facts take two lines each, also short ones ("Sektion admin") |
| (b) The term's column capped (`fit-content(40%)`), a term wraps between its words | Two columns kept | Short facts stay on one line | A one-word German term ("Abhängigkeiten") cannot wrap; the value keeps 60 % at best, about 180 px at 390 px, as wide as the maintainer's address alone |
| (c) Break points in the value (`<wbr>` after `@`, `.`, `/`) | A pipe for addresses | Breaks where a reader expects | Every template that shows an address changes; a value of 164 px still breaks, only at nicer places |

**Choice:** (a). `overflow-wrap: anywhere` stays the last resort for a value wider than the whole line (a long path or key without
spaces). The 36 rem is the content panel's width the page header and the list search already switch at (Q-UI-554). The shared
stylesheet's copy of the facts in [access.scss](../../web/src/app/shared/access/access.scss), which overrode the global one for the
settings pages and kept their two columns at every width, is gone. **Rationale:** a value broken inside itself beside a term that took the room is the defect;
putting the term above the value removes the competition for the line instead of tuning it per language. The development agent
revisits (b) if a page of short facts reads too long on a phone.

The render run's `broken` check finds a fact's value broken inside a word beside a wide term (G4-10); the German pass at 390 px of every
screen without a walk found none after the change.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-171. Code: [_catalog-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_catalog-screens.scss) (`facts-stacked`).
Tests: "R-UI-171 a fact list below 36 rem of content puts each term above its value, and its long value does not break inside itself"
in [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts) (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). Rendered: `package-version-deb`,
`package-version-ansible`, `package-version-oci` in English and German, both schemes, 1,440, 1,024 and 390 px; every screen without a
walk in German at 390 px.

### Q-UI-1080 · A server sends a code, the screen says it, and a raw text folds under Technical details

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-UI-214. Three English server sentences stood in German pages on 2026-11-24; the audit of that day found thirteen more
screens that bound a server's text, of two kinds: a closed set of cases written out as English sentences (a preview's note, a save's
warnings, Valkey's reasons), and a raw diagnosis (a job's error, a host's answer, a verifier's note). The trend's basis (R-VULN-021)
and the download queue's failures (Q-CUR-169) had been changed the same day, each on its own.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A code for a case, said by the screen; a raw text folded under **Technical details** below the screen's own sentence, by one shared component (chosen) | The API answers an enum (and the parameters the sentence names); the screen writes the sentence with `$localize`; a diagnosis stays the server's English, closed, `lang="en"`, with its code | Every sentence is in the reader's language and in the glossary's words; the API's codes are what a script matches on; the raw text stays for a report; one fold looks and reads the same on every screen | A new case needs a sentence in the UI and in German; the API's enum must follow the server (held by a test) |
| (b) The server writes the sentence in the caller's language (`Accept-Language`) | A catalogue of messages on the server | One place for the text, also for the API | A second translation system beside the UI's, outside the glossary and the German checks; every format and task writes its texts twice |
| (c) Show the server's English, marked `lang="en"` | The text as it came, declared English | Nothing to build | The owner's finding as it stands: English in a German page |
| (d) Translate the server's English sentence in the UI by a table keyed by the text | A lookup of the English | No API change | Breaks with every rewording; a sentence with a host or a number in it is no key |

**Choice:** (a). Where the API already had a code beside an English `detail` (a repository's and a CI mapping's warnings), the code
became an enum and the `detail` stays for a reader of the API, as a problem's does (R-UI-042); a CI warning that names claims carries
them as `names`. Where the API had only the text, it gains the code: a preview's `note` is the code now, and Valkey's view carries
`reasonCode` (the vocabulary `/readyz` already had) beside its free `reason`, which names addresses and is folded. A mirror's
`lastCode` became an enum. The download queue's two folds of Q-CUR-169 became the shared component, so every screen has the one
**Technical details** with the text and its code. **Rationale:** the UI's i18n is the one place where texts are translated, checked
(`make web-i18n-check`, the formal German and the glossary's checks) and rendered in German; a diagnosis loses nothing by being folded
and gains a sentence the reader understands. The texts that are English by decision (the manual, a format's guide, Q-UI-86; a format's
settings schema, Q-UI-79) keep their `lang="en"`; the development agent revisits Q-UI-79 with this rule when the owner wants a format's
settings in German, and the lint rule's list of names when a new English member of the API is shown.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-214; the OpenAPI document: `RemoteDownloadPreview.note`, `RepositoryWarning.code`, `CiWarning.code` and
`MirrorErrors.lastCode` as enums, `CiWarning.names`, `ValkeyView.reasonCode`. Code:
[technical-details.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/technical-details.ts), [server-text-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/server-text-rule.mjs).

### Q-UI-1100 · A limit is one sentence above the list, a line on its waiting rows and on a bulk, its answer folded

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's tab of 2026-11-25 showed "315 of 315 versions found are queued · Running 4 · Waiting 206 · Done 105" and rows that
read "Waiting" with a dash under Progress and Failure, while Docker Hub refused every request; nothing on the screen said why, so he read
the tab as stale ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) Q-CUR-170).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One warning line above the bulks while the limit holds: who limits, since when, until when and whose time that is, in the screen's language; **Technical details** folded under it (the last answer, the waits in a row, the address, the headers of the limit, the upstream's words, the server's sentence); "Rate limit until 06:47" on each waiting row; "Waits for Docker Hub's rate limit until 06:47" on a bulk whose rows wait (chosen) | The three places the person looks | The plain sentence first, the raw answer for who wants it (R-UI-067); the row and the bulk say it where the eye lands | Three texts of one fact |
| (b) A badge "Rate limited" instead of "Waiting" | A state of its own | Seen at once | A row is not in a state the API has; the filters would not match it |
| (c) Only the sentence above the list | One place | Least | A person who opens a bulk's rows (`?bulk=`) does not see why they wait |

**Choice:** (a). The sentence's time is a time of day in the viewer's language, with the day where it is not today; the upstream is its
preset's name where the remote's address is one ("Docker Hub"), else the host. The facts reuse the mirror's words ("Last answer",
"Waits", "Waiting until"), and the headers stand among a row's facts too. **Rationale:** the sentence answers "is it done, and when does
it go on"; the development agent would revisit (b) if the queue gains a state of its own for a held row.

**Applied in the spec:** [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-018. Code:
[limit-words.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/upstream-downloads/limit-words.ts),
[remote-downloads.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.html).

### Q-UI-1101 · The top bar's panel says the queues a limit holds above Running

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A section **Waiting for an upstream (n)** above **Running**: per queue "206 downloads of upstream/docker-hub wait: Docker Hub limits requests; Quader asks again at 06:47." with the format's name and **Show in queue** (chosen) | The panel's own form: a section, rows, a link | "No download from an upstream is running" stands beside the reason; the filter narrows it | A third section |
| (b) A line under the empty sentence of Running | Smaller | One line | Not there while something else runs |
| (c) A badge on the top bar's button for waiting queues | Seen with the panel closed | Seen at once | The button counts what runs (Q-UI-1070); a number of queues beside it reads as downloads |

**Choice:** (a). With nothing held there is no section. **Rationale:** the panel's question is "what is Quader loading"; a queue that
stands answers it with "nothing, and here is why". The development agent would revisit (c) if a held queue is missed with the panel
closed.

### Q-UI-1102 · The tab Downloads is live by the shared poll: 5 s while something moves, 30 s otherwise

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It changes
Q-UI-1075's exception for the tab, and R-CUR-018's "every 5 s while something waits or runs" gains the reads in between.

Context: the owner's sentence of 2026-11-25, "Ich will nirgends F5 drücken müssen". The tab kept its own `setInterval` beside `live()`
(Q-UI-1075): it read every 5 s while a row waited or ran, also in a hidden window, never on its return, and not at all while nothing
waited or ran, so a bulk another person started or a client's failed fetch did not show until a reload; a failed read replaced the rows
with an error.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `live()` with 5 s while a row waits or runs or a bulk shown expands or waits, 30 s otherwise and while a limit holds the queue with nothing running; **Pause automatic refresh** is its `when`; a read keeps the rows, a failure keeps them and waits longer (chosen) | R-UI-213's rule | Nothing missed while the tab is open; a hidden window costs nothing and reads at once on return; a held queue is not read every 5 s for hours | One request per 30 s for an idle tab |
| (b) Keep the timer and add an idle read | Two mechanisms | Small | The hidden window and the return stay unsolved |
| (c) As built | — | Nothing new | Needs a reload for what changes while nothing ran |

**Choice:** (a); `DOWNLOADS_REFRESH_MS` stays 5 s, the tab's own interval of R-CUR-018. **Rationale:** R-UI-213's three rules (seen,
at once on return, in place) are the owner's; the development agent would revisit the 30 s if idle tabs show in the replicas' request
rate (Q-UI-1075 (c)).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-213 (the table); [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-018. Code:
[remote-downloads.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.ts).

### Q-UI-1103 · The strip's label reads the queue's counts itself on every other tab, every 30 s

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the label "Downloads · 2 failed" took the counts the tab Downloads passed last; on the content, Upstream and Details the strip
read them once, and not at all after the tab Downloads had passed some, so a row that failed meanwhile did not show until a reload.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The open tab Downloads (or Upstream) passes its counts; on every other tab the strip reads one row of the list for its counts, at once and every 30 s while the window is seen (chosen) | The strip owns its label | One small read per 30 s; the label is never older than half a minute | A read the content page did not make before |
| (b) The content page reads the queue for the strip | A second owner | — | The page and the strip would both read at the start |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the strip already read the counts once; the development agent would revisit the interval with Q-UI-1075's
idle cost.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Docker Hub lifts its limit for callers with an account, and the remote of 2026-11-25 had no credential. A sentence "Add a Docker
Hub account in the repository's settings to raise the limit" would help, if the screen knew it of the upstream.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No such sentence while no preset carries the fact (chosen) | The screen says what the server knows | No vendor's terms in the UI | The person does not learn the remedy (H-1884) |
| (b) A preset fact "an account lifts the limit" (the format contract's `UpstreamPreset`), and the sentence with a link to the settings where the remote has no credential | A fact of the format | The remedy where it applies | A contract change for one sentence; the fact may change with the vendor's terms |
| (c) A sentence for every remote without a credential | Generic | Small | Wrong for an upstream that limits everyone alike |

the development agent would build (b) if the owner wants the remedy said.
