### Q-UI-1110 · The page is the one thing that scrolls; a list's head scrolls with it

Status: **The rule decided by the owner, 2026-11-25** (R-UI-215, his words there); **the form decided by the development agent** —
selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Revises
[Q-UI-68](#q-ui-68--layout-of-the-application-shell-and-the-list-screens) (its "inner scroll with a sticky header" and "a scroll
region that is focusable") and [Q-UI-427](#q-ui-427--a-table-keeps-no-room-for-a-scrollbar-its-rows-do-not-need) (its "Against";
no gutter is reserved, as chosen).

Context: every data table scrolled inside a region of its own, capped at `max(22rem, 100dvh − 17rem)`, with a sticky head, so that the
head stayed in view (68 component files use the data table). On the owner's picture three scrollbars stood side by side: an opened
image's list, the list's region and the page, and the list's head stood over the opened image's rows, whose columns are others. The
page's scroll container is `main` on every screen (the window never scrolls, R-UI-173), so "the outermost" scrollbar is `main`'s, at
the panel's right edge.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The page scrolls and a list's head scrolls away with it (chosen) | The data table loses its cap, its own scroll, its tab stop, its region role and its sticky head; a list of any length grows the page | One scrollbar; no head stands over rows of another list; nothing to unclip; the style guide styles nothing the reference does not (its lists' heads are not described as sticking: not confirmed against the owner's GitLab, which the builder did not open) | On a long list the column names leave the view; a list's form is read from its rows |
| (b) The head sticks under the breadcrumb bar | `thead th { position: sticky }` relative to `main` | The column names stay in view | A list opened in a row reads under the outer head (the owner's picture); every wrapper between the head and `main` must stop clipping (`.collapse-region`, a pane), and the tab strip and the list's head would need offsets of their own (146 px of a 672 px view at 1,024 × 768) |
| (c) Keep the inner region | As built | Nothing changes | Refused by the owner |

**Choice:** (a). The table's room (`.table-scroll`) keeps its name and its `position: relative` (the containing block of the rows' texts
for assistive technology only, R-UI-173); the data table observes only its ruler for its width. **Kept with a scroll of their own, each a
choice the owner may refuse:** the trend's table of the vulnerabilities (18 rem) and the usage history's table (24 rem, with a frame now
and its head sticking inside the box), which stand in for charts at a fixed height (unboxed, the usage history's 288 points would add
about 14,000 px to the page), and the list box of a virtual repository's members (8 to 20 rem), whose active option moves inside it; if
he refuses a box, its rows grow the page. **What else lost a box that scrolled:** the packages drawer's list of repositories (14 rem
inside the drawer's body), an issued token's grants and claims (14 rem each inside the dialog's body), the CI snippet of a mapping
(24 rem), and the folded command of a version (R-UI-009), which cuts after its third line instead of scrolling; an unfolded or short
command had been capped at its count of lines, so a line that wrapped scrolled inside it. A sideways scroll stays where lines are kept as
they are copied (R-UI-173). **Rationale:** the owner's rule, and the one form that keeps a nested list's rows under their own head. The
development agent revisits the head when the owner says a long list's head should stay in view: then (b) for the outer lists alone,
with the opened rows' lists bounded as Q-UI-1111 has them.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-002 (list screens), R-UI-009 (the fold), R-UI-173 (the containing block), R-UI-215, the WCAG rows 1.4.10
and 2.4.11 (the `scroll-padding-top` the latter named did not exist in the code). Code: `.table-scroll` in
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss), [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts),
[code-window.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/code/code-window.ts), [usage-history.ts](../../web/src/app/features/usage/usage-history.ts).

### Q-UI-1111 · An opened item shows its ten newest versions and links all of them

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Revises the
opened row of R-UI-052.

Context: an item opened in a repository's content listed its versions twenty at a time with **Load more**, in a list of its own inside
the row. With the page as the one scroll (Q-UI-1110), an image of a hundred tags would fill the screen inside one row.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The ten newest under their own head, and **All N tags** / **All N versions** to the package's page (chosen) | A bounded peek; the package's page lists every version with filter, sort and **Load more** (R-UI-110) | An opened row is never longer than ten rows; the whole list lives where it can be filtered and sorted; the row's own head names its columns | One click more for the eleventh version |
| (b) **Load more** grows the page | As before, without the region | Every version in place | An opened row of a hundred tags fills the screen by itself: the owner's case |
| (c) No opened rows | The row links to the package's page | Simplest | R-UI-052 and W-23 want the versions and their **Pull** at hand in the list |

**Choice:** (a). The link stands under the ten where the row's count is more than ten, its accessible name with the item's name ("All
103 tags: chart-render-kit"). **The tab Upstream keeps Load more** for a package opened in its row (100 at a time): an upstream version
has no page of its own to link to, and the list grows the page. **Rationale:** the newest versions are what a reader opens a row for;
the package's page already is the list of all of them. The development agent revisits the bound of ten if the walkthrough shows rows
that need more at hand.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052, R-UI-215. Code: [repository-item-versions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-item-versions.ts),
`allVersionsText` in [content-shape.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/content-shape.ts).

### Q-UI-1112 · A navigation column sticks beside the page with a scroll of its own; any other side column sticks only while it fits

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Revises
[Q-UI-241](#q-ui-241--the-documentation-tab-is-the-file-browsers-two-panes-a-tree-with-a-search-field-and-the-page) ("each pane
scrolls on its own") and R-UI-060's layout, [Q-UI-4](#q-ui-4--layout-of-the-policy-editor-and-the-explainer-example-screenshot-requested)
and R-UI-027 (the sticky preview, which scrolled by itself at `100vh − 8rem`), [Q-UI-997](#q-ui-997--the-audit-log-keeps-five-columns-and-an-opened-event-stands-beside-it-only-where-both-keep-their-form)
and R-UI-037 (the event beside the log; the drawer stays refused as in its option (c)), and R-UI-050 (the contents' height, which
did not count the breadcrumb bar).

Context: four columns stand beside a page. The manual's contents and the tree of a collection's documentation are navigation: their
entries are what the reader moves between while the page changes. A policy's preview and an opened audit event are content. The
documentation's two panes had a height from the window and each scrolled by itself; the preview scrolled by itself beside the page,
its scrollbar 32 px from the page's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A navigation column sticks with a scroll of its own, at most as high as the panel's view; any other side column sticks only while it fits and never scrolls by itself (chosen) | `--quader-page-height` (the window less the top bar, the breadcrumb bar and the panel's gap) caps a navigation column; `quaderStickyWhenFits` gives the class `sticks` to a side column while it is no taller than the panel's view less its padding | The navigation stays at hand on a long page, as a document site's contents do; a preview or an event is read whole without a second scrollbar; one small directive for every such column | The navigation column's scrollbar is a second one beside the page's; a side column taller than the view scrolls away |
| (b) Every side column scrolls with the page | No sticky column | One scrollbar everywhere | The tree and the contents leave the view on a long page; the reader scrolls back to the top to move on |
| (c) Every side column sticks with a scroll of its own | As the preview had it | Everything at hand | Two scrollbars side by side on every such page: the owner's objection |

**Choice:** (a). **The navigation column is the one second scrollbar of a page kept by choice; the owner may refuse it**, and then the
tree and the contents scroll with the page as in (b). The documentation's page pane is as long as its page; a new page brings the pane's
top into view where it stands above the view, and **Back to the tree** (one pane at a time, under 48 rem) the entry that was read where
its group is open, else the tree's top. Closing an audit event gives the focus back to the row it was opened from, so a reader who
opened it far down the log goes on from there; the focus of an opened event is given after the render that measures whether it sticks,
so the page stays at the row where it does. **Rationale:** navigation is used while the page moves; content is read, and is read
whole. A banner above the frame is not counted in `--quader-page-height`: with a banner a navigation column's last entries may stand
under the panel's edge until the page scrolls to its end.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-027, R-UI-037, R-UI-050, R-UI-060, R-UI-215. Code: [sticky-when-fits.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/sticky-when-fits.ts),
[_browse.scss](../../web/src/styles/_browse.scss), [ansible-docs.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/ansible-docs.ts),
[help-page.scss](../../web/src/app/features/help/help-page.scss), [policy-editor.scss](../../web/src/app/features/permissions/policy-editor.scss),
[audit-log.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.ts), `--quader-page-height` in [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss).

### Q-UI-1113 · The render check inner-scroll measures every box that scrolls by itself, in the window's first height

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Extends
[Q-UI-682](#q-ui-682--the-render-run-measures-the-layout-in-the-page-and-a-finding-fails-the-screen).

Context: R-UI-215 is a rule of every screen, and a region whose height follows the window (`100dvh − X`) no longer overflows once the
render has grown the window to the page's length, so a check in the grown picture would pass the owner's case.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A check in the page, in the window's first height, light scheme only (chosen) | `innerScroll` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), beside `empty-scroll` | Sees what the user sees; place (page or overlay), nesting and stickiness are read from the laid-out page; constant cost per picture | One more walk over the page's elements per light picture |
| (b) A lint rule: `max-block-size` with `overflow-y: auto` in a stylesheet | Static | No browser | Cannot see place, nesting or a flex-bounded pane; would need an allow list that repeats this check |

**Choice:** (a). An element **scrolls** when its `overflow-y` is `auto` or `scroll` and its content is more than 1 px taller than its
box, or a `max-block-size` caps it (a region built to scroll that the seed's data may not fill). **Allowed in the page:** a box of at
most 24 rem with a border above and below that no scrolling box holds; a navigation column (the element or an ancestor below `main` is
sticky, and it is or holds `nav`, `[role=navigation]` or `[role=tree]`); a popup (an ancestor below `main` absolutely or fixed placed),
judged as an overlay; a text area, a select, an input. **Allowed in an overlay** (`.cdk-overlay-container`): one scroll; a scroll inside
another is the finding, wherever it stands. Not judged: the side bar, the window (`empty-scroll`), a tab strip, a sideways scroll
(`sideways`). No `allowed` entry exists for it. **Cost:** six fixtures in three engines, about 7 s of `make ui-layout-test`; in the
renders one walk with `getComputedStyle` per light picture in the window's first height, as `sidewaysRegions` costs; nothing per
format. **Rationale:** the rule is about what is seen at the window's height, and only the page can say where a box stands. The
development agent revisits the 24 rem and the navigation test if a screen needs another kind of kept scroll; then the rule of R-UI-215
changes first.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-215. Code: `innerScroll` in [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), its call in
[render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts), the fixtures in [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-1180 · A failure carries the facts of its answer on its ApiError

Status: **The rule decided by the owner, 2026-11-25** (R-UI-216, his words there); **the form decided by the development agent** —
selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the problem interceptor kept the status, the problem document, the request ID and Retry-After of a failed answer and threw the
rest away; the upload's own client (no interceptors) kept less. 197 notices and a dozen toasts read an `ApiError`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ApiError.answer`, made by one function for both clients (chosen) | `apiErrorOf` of failure.ts keeps the call, the time, the content type, the readable headers, a non-problem body as text, an unreadable answer, a failure of the page, the failures in a row | Every place that holds an `ApiError` holds the facts; one rule of what is left out | The error object grows by a few kilobytes at most (the body's bound) |
| (b) A store of the last failures beside the error | A service the notice asks by the call | The error stays small | Two sources of one failure; a toast or a cell would have to look it up |
| (c) The notice reads the `HttpErrorResponse` itself | No interceptor change | — | The response is gone once the interceptor threw its `ApiError` |

**Choice:** (a). A failure that is no `ApiError` (a loader that threw) becomes one with its message as `fault` (`asFailure`), not the
`ApiError(0)` that said the server could not be reached. A body the browser holds as a Blob or a buffer is read there, so a problem
document of a download is found too. **Rationale:** the facts belong to the failure; whoever shows it shows them.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216, R-UI-042. Code: [problem.ts](../../web/src/app/api/problem.ts),
[failure.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/failure.ts), [interceptors.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/interceptors.ts),
[files-api.ts](../../web/src/app/api/files-api.ts), `asApiError` of [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts).

### Q-UI-1181 · Every failure is said in the reader's language, from its code, else from its status

Status: **The rule decided by the owner, 2026-11-25** (R-UI-216); **the sentences decided by the development agent** — the owner reviews
them at the walkthrough. Revises R-UI-042's "Unknown codes show the English `detail`" and the same line of R-UI-214.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The code's sentence, else a sentence of the status, else of its class; the server's sentence a fact (chosen) | `fallback` of problem-messages.ts: 0, 401, 403, 404, 408, 413, 429, 502/504, 503, other 5xx, other 4xx, an unreadable answer, a failure of the page | A German page says every failure in German (R-UI-214); the server's text is still visible, marked English | A status's sentence is less exact than the server's |
| (b) The server's `detail` as the sentence where there is one | As before | The server's words | English in a German page; and no sentence at all without a problem document |

**Choice:** (a). A status that names its case says it with or without a problem document (a 404 of an unknown code is "does not
exist"); `known` stays false for these, so a field problem of an unknown code still shows the server's sentence under its field.
**Rationale:** the screen speaks the reader's language (R-UI-214); the server's sentence is a fact for whoever reports it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042, R-UI-214, R-UI-216. Code: `fallback` in
[problem-messages.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/problem-messages.ts).

### Q-UI-1182 · The facts stand under the sentence; what can be long is folded

Status: **The rule decided by the owner, 2026-11-25** (R-UI-216: "alle Infos die verfügbar sind"); **the form decided by the development
agent** — the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A facts list (`dl.facts`) under the sentence, the long parts under Technical details (chosen) | Status, call, time, request ID, code, server's sentence, Retry-After, sent twice, failures in a row visible; body, headers, content type, field problems, `type`, `instance`, other members folded | Short facts at a glance; a 4,000-character error page does not push the page's content down | One click for the body |
| (b) Everything visible | No fold | No click | A gateway's page or a list of headers fills the screen in every notice |
| (c) Everything folded | A sentence and one disclosure | Small | The owner's "dünn": the status and the call would stay hidden |

**Choice:** (a), with only the rows the answer had. The status is named with its reason phrase from a fixed table (`reasonPhrase`),
since HTTP/2 carries none. A path, an ID, a header and a body break inside themselves (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, `pre-wrap`): they never
push the page sideways (R-UI-173) and never scroll by themselves (R-UI-215). **Rationale:** what is short and identifies the failure is
what a reader reads first; what is long is what an administrator asks for.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216. Code: [error-notice.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.ts),
[failure-report.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-report.ts).

walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Plain text with the reader's labels, the time also in UTC (chosen) | "Status: 502 Bad Gateway", one line per fact, the folded part after them | Pastes into any ticket; the UTC time is what a log is searched by | Labels in German for a German reader |
| (b) JSON of the `ApiError` | Machine-readable | Exact | Not what a person pastes into a ticket |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the report goes to a person first. A form's error summary carries the same text folded (Q-UI-1189).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216. Code: `failureReport` in [failure-report.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-report.ts).

### Q-UI-1184 · A failed read is offered again, and a failure that may pass is read again by itself

Status: **The rule decided by the owner** (R-UI-213, 2026-11-24; R-UI-216's Retry, 2026-11-25); **the form decided by the development
agent** — the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Retry stood only for 503 and 0, whether or not the screen had a view to read again; a page whose first read failed stayed
failed until a reload, and its notice gave way to "Loading." at every retry.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Retry for every read and a write without an answer or with a gateway's; the notice reads its view again by itself after a failure that may pass, with R-UI-213's back-off (chosen) | 3 s, 6 s, 12 s … up to 5 minutes, never before Retry-After, only while the window is seen, at once when it is seen again; 0, 408, 429, 5xx and an unreadable answer; the failures in a row counted per call (`CallFailures`) | The owner's page comes back by itself; a refusal is not hammered; a write is never repeated | One timer per failed read's notice |
| (b) Every failed read again by itself, a refusal too | Every status | Simplest | A 403 or a 404 read every 5 minutes for nothing |
| (c) Through `live()` of every view | The view's own poll | One mechanism | A view not yet live, or one whose first read failed, has nothing to poll with |

**Choice:** (a). Retry stands only where the screen binds `(retry)`: the notice reads `EventEmitter.observed` (a decorated output, the
one in the app), so no notice offers a button that does nothing; the reads that had none got one (Claim tester, an issued token's use,
the documentation's search). A failed resource keeps its notice while it reads again (`failureOf`): the notice says "Trying again."
instead of giving way to "Loading.". The repository's page reads its formats and its address again with it: read once, a page that came
back said "not scanned for vulnerabilities" of an npm repository (the reproduction of 2026-11-25). **Rationale:** a failure that passes
needs no person; one that does not needs no traffic.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-042, R-UI-213, R-UI-216. Code: `passes`, `retryWaitMs` and the effect of
[error-notice.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.ts), `CallFailures` of [failure.ts](../../web/src/app/core/http/failure.ts),
`failureOf` of [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts) and its `also` in
[repository-content.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.ts) (since Q-UI-1195 and Q-UI-1196 the form
of every screen).

### Q-UI-1185 · Notices of one cause in one place are one notice, by themselves

Status: **The rule decided by the owner, 2026-11-25** (R-UI-216); **the form decided by the development agent** — the owner reviews it at
the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every notice joins a root registry; the first of a cause in a place shows it, the others nothing (chosen) | Cause: status, code and the server's sentence; place: the page (`main`) or one overlay; order: the document's | Every page that stacks notices has it without a change, the shell's notice and a page's among them; a 404 of one object and of another stay two | A notice that stands far from the first is shown there, not where its view is |
| (b) A container per page that collects its notices | The page wraps its notices | Placement chosen by the page | 46 templates with more than one notice change; the shell and the page are two components |
| (c) Same status and code only | The owner's words | Fewer notices | A 404 "No repository a" and a 404 "No file b" would read as one |

**Choice:** (a). The first notice lists every call and every request ID of its group; its Retry reads every view of the group again (a
write only where its own failure would offer Retry). **Rationale:** one cause is one thing to read and one thing to report.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216. Code: [failure-groups.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/failure-groups.ts),
[error-notice.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/error-notice.ts).

### Q-UI-1195 · A failed read's failure is cleared by its answer, in one form, and a rule refuses the other

Status: **The rule decided by the owner** (R-UI-213, 2026-11-24: never F5; R-UI-216, 2026-11-25); **the form decided by the development
agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It closes H-1963.

Context: 49 failures of a resource were made by hand (`computed` of `resource().error()`, in 35 components), and 42 reads of their own
set their failure to null at the start of the read (in 40 components). Both cleared the notice's failure when its Retry began: the notice gave way to
"Loading." and came back, so it could neither say that it tries again nor count, and a list's notice did the same in `PagedResource`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The failure is cleared by the answer, in three shapes: `failureOf(reads, { also })` for a `resource()`, `PagedResource` itself for a list, a read of its own that sets its failure after the answer; the lint rule `read-failure-rule.mjs` refuses the two forms that cleared it (chosen) | A screen takes its failure from `failureOf` or keeps its signal until the answer; the template shows the notice in place of "Loading." | Every notice of the app stays in place by the same rule; the rule makes the old form a lint error, so a new screen cannot forget it; nothing changes for a write | Three shapes, one rule; the rule reads text, not types (H-1965) |
| (b) A wrapper component around a view (`<quader-read [failure] [loading]>`) | The notice, "Loading." and the content in one element | The order of the three is in one place | Content projection with conditions needs `ng-template` in every screen; 120 templates change shape; reads of their own still clear by hand |
| (c) The notice keeps its last failure itself while it is hidden | No screen changes | One place | The screen removes the notice from the page when the failure is null: nothing is left to keep it |

**Choice:** (a). `failureOf` takes one read or several (a page of several reads shows the first failure in their order) and returns the
failure with its `retry`. `PagedResource.start` and `more` keep the error until a page answers. A read of its own sets its failure to
null after its answer. **Rationale:** the defect was the failure's lifetime, not the notice; it is fixed where the failure lives.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216. Code: [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts),
[read-failure-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/read-failure-rule.mjs), [check-rules.mjs](../../web/scripts/check-rules.mjs).

### Q-UI-1196 · The page's Retry reads its other failed reads with it, and a read that would show a wrong fact shows its failure

Status: **The rule decided by the owner** (R-UI-216: "alle Infos die verfügbar sind"; R-UI-213); **the form decided by the development
agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It closes H-1962, as far as H-1964 says.

Context: a page's reads beside the one its notice reports (the formats, the server's address, the caller's rights, a section's list)
were read once. Failed with the page, they stayed failed after it came back: the repository's page said "not scanned for
vulnerabilities" of an npm repository; the audit of 2026-11-25 found the same on the repository's settings (format names, the address,
the well-known state, the project's level, the move targets), the new repository, the downloads and the upstream tab (no actions),
the virtual members (an empty pool), the signatures section ("No trust anchor applies"), a group's policies (hidden as none), an
endpoint's addresses, the project list ("You are not a member of a project yet"), the package and the version page (no grades, no
tab Vulnerabilities, no "Blocked in"), the upstream registry ("the definitions are not updated"), and the stores of the whole app.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The page's Retry reads every read of the page that failed (`failureOf(…, { also })`, or the read of its own); a read whose absence says a wrong fact shows its failure in a notice of its own where the fact stands (chosen) | One case of the same cause is one notice (Q-UI-1185), so a 502 of everything is still one; a section's failure alone is said in the section | The page after the recovery is the page of a fresh load; a wrong fact is never shown as a fact | A notice more in a section where the read failed alone |
| (b) Every read of a page in its notice | One notice for the page | Simple | The page disappears behind the notice of a decoration (the format names) |
| (c) Read again only by the next load | As before | — | The owner's F5 |

**Choice:** (a). A read whose absence only leaves something out (a format's display name, the help's contents, a convenience button) is
read again with the page and shows no notice. **Rationale:** the person sees either the fact or that it could not be read, never a
"none" that is not true.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-216. Code: `also` of `failureOf` in [paged-resource.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/paged-resource.ts), the
screens of [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#errors-in-screens-r-ui-216).

### Q-UI-1200 · A system-only format is left out of every choice for something new, and kept wherever something is found or shown

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's finding of 2026-11-25: the page **New repository** offered **ClamAV definitions**, a format with one public source
that the product has already, and its form did not even offer the class Remote. The specification had it right
([formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001: "the creation form does not offer it"), but no screen read `systemOnly`, and the
UI's fake catalog held no system-only format, so no test met one. Every consumer of `GET /api/v1/formats` was audited for what it does:

| Place | What it does with the formats | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| The chooser of **New repository** (tiles, count, search) | A choice for something new | Left out (R-UI-080) |
| The form's address `new/<format>` | A choice for something new | No form (Q-UI-1201) |
| **Upstream registries**, a new preset's format | A choice for something new | Only formats with the class remote; a system-only format has none (`Register` refuses it, R-CLAMAV-001), and the server answers `unsupported_class` |
| A virtual repository's members, the deployment target | A choice among existing repositories of the virtual's format | A system-only format has no virtual class, so none of its repositories is ever offered |
| The exposure rule editor's repository | A choice of an existing repository | System repositories are left out already (Q-UI-901) |
| The repository lists' filters by format, the package list's, the vulnerability report's, the search | A filter of what exists | Kept: `upstream/clamav` stays findable |
| The repository's page, its settings, its client setup, the guides of the format, the version's page, the storage and endpoint pages | A display of what exists | Kept |
| Permission policies, limits | Free text and repositories, no list of formats | Nothing to do |

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A choice for something new leaves a system-only format out unless the server accepts it there; a filter and a display keep it (chosen) | One rule per kind of place, read from the catalog's fact | Nobody is offered what the server refuses; an existing `upstream/clamav` stays findable, and its client setup stays | Each new place has to be put in one of the two kinds |
| (b) The catalog answer leaves system-only formats out | The UI never sees one | No screen can forget | The repository's page, its filters and its guide would not know the format of a repository that exists |
| (c) The chooser alone | The finding's place | Smallest | The form's address still leads into the refusal |

**Choice:** (a). `creatableFormats` of [repository-class.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-class.ts) is the one
filter of a choice; no code compares a format's name, so a future system-only format is covered by the same lines.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-080; [formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001. Code:
[repository-format-chooser.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-format-chooser.ts),
[fakes-catalog.ts](../../web/src/app/api/testing/fakes-catalog.ts) (`CLAMAV_DEFINITIONS_FORMAT`, in the fake's catalog by default).

### Q-UI-1203 · A repository of a system-only format is shown as System, not as Local

Status: **Decided by the owner** (2026-11-25, from the three options below: "Nimm A, ich folge deiner Empfehlung").

Context: `upstream/clamav` is of the class `local` in the API, the catalog and the database, and the screens called it **Local**, the
class whose sentence is "Holds content that is deployed to Quader". Nobody deploys to it: the malware scan's updater fills it on a
schedule ([formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001, R-CLAMAV-002).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A badge of its own, **System**, instead of **Local**, wherever a repository's class is shown (recommended, chosen) | A word of the screens; the class stays `local` in the API, the catalog and the database | Says what the repository is; the decision is the catalog's fact `systemOnly`, so a future system-only format gets it | A fourth word beside the three classes |
| (b) **Local**, with a sentence that says that the installation fills it | | No new word | The badge says what the repository is not |
| (c) The class remote | The repository rebuilt as a remote of ClamAV's network | Matches a cache of another source | A remote asks its upstream at its readers' pace, which ClamAV's network limits per address; refused |

**Choice:** (a). The word is **System** (German "System"), its icon `settings`, the icon of the caller **System** on the usage pages,
the installation's own background work (no new colour, no green; the admin area's `dns` of its group **System** was rendered first and
read at 20 px like Local's `storage`). It stands as the class's badge or cell on the repository's page, the repository lists of a project and of every project,
the project `upstream`'s section, the search's results, a format's guide, the client setup, a version's repositories and the settings'
facts; the admin area's page of the registry says **System repository** where it said **Local repository**. Where it stands as a
badge or a cell its tooltip says "Filled by this installation itself, on a schedule; nobody publishes to it." (German "Von dieser
Installation selbst befüllt, nach Zeitplan; niemand veröffentlicht dorthin."), and the repository's page says the same sentence under
its key. Where a row's class cell says **System**, the key's badge **System** of R-UI-193 is left out (one mark, not two). A format's
guide names its class link "The system repository: filled by this installation itself". The admin dashboard counts it under **System**
by the server's count ([Q-UI-1217](#q-ui-1217--the-overview-counts-a-repository-as-the-screens-show-its-class)). Decided by the catalog's fact, never by a format's name; one place names every class
(`classLabel`, `classIcon`, `classHelp`, `shownClass` of [repository-class.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-class.ts)).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-052, R-UI-193; [formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001.

### Q-UI-1150 · An image's tags are one line of facts after the leading tag, and a line each in a block

Status: **Decided by the development agent** (2026-11-25), building Q-UI-1130's screens; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-UI-1130 says what a row of an image holds (the leading tag, the other tags muted after it, at most four on the opened item
and then "+N more", every one on the package's page, the signature badge); not how they stand at 1,440 and at 390 px, what a tag of 128
characters does, what "+N more" says where the answer names 100 of more tags, or when the link **All N tags** stands under ten rows that
may name every tag of the image.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The leading tag and the other tags as one line of facts (`.dot-separated`, the style guide's separator, so no line starts with a dot), the badge after it; in a block (a stacked list, R-UI-174) the leading tag, the other tags and the badge each start a line; a tag is an item of its own, so the line wraps between tags, and only a tag wider than the cell alone breaks inside itself (chosen) | One cell, `<quader-image-tags>`, on both screens | The tags read as the image's names, in the colour of a fact; nothing breaks a version at a hyphen; a long branch tag does not make a whole list stack | Five tags and a badge take two lines in a narrow column |
| (b) The other tags in a column of their own | A column **Other tags** | Aligned | A column of mostly one commit tag; at 390 px one more field per block |
| (c) The other tags under the leading tag at every width | Two lines a row | One rule | Every row twice as high at 1,440 px, where the line has room |

**Choice:** (a). "+N more" counts the tags the row leaves out; where the answer names 100 other tags and the image has more
(`aliasesMore`), how many is not known and the row says "+ more" on both screens. Assistive technology reads "Other tags of
portal/web 1.4.0:" before the first of them. The link **All N tags** under the opened item stands where the item holds more than the
rows show: the list goes on past the ten (its cursor is set) or a row leaves a tag out; an image of three images whose rows name all

R-UI-110. Code: [image-tags.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/image-tags.ts), `more` of
[repository-item-versions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-item-versions.ts). Tests:

### Q-UI-1151 · An opened item reads its versions again every 3 s while one it shows waits for its scan

Status: **Decided by the development agent** (2026-11-25), closing H-1890 with the rows of Q-UI-1130; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: the opened item read its versions and their grades again only when its row in the list above changed (R-UI-213): once the
latest tag was checked, an older tag's scan (queued, scanning, checked) showed only at the next change of the row. The states that pass
on their own are `queued` and `scanning` (`checkWaits`, Q-UI-1122).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The opened item is live itself while a version it shows waits: every 3 s (`LIVE_FAST_MS`), and not at all while none waits (chosen) | `live()` with `every` null while nothing waits | The state shows within seconds; an opened item with nothing waiting costs no request of its own, as before | One request pair per 3 s per opened item while a scan waits |
| (b) Every 30 s, waiting or not | A slow cadence always | Simple | Every opened row costs requests forever; a scan's progress shows late |
| (c) Keep it on the row's changes | As built | No requests | H-1890 stays live |

**Choice:** (a). Rows that are images make the reason smaller (an image's tags have one scan), not gone: an opened item shows ten
images whose scans run in turn. A scan that waits for what the installation lacks (no scanner, no database) does not pass on its own
and reads nothing. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-052. Code: `waiting` and its `live()` in
[repository-item-versions.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-item-versions.ts). Test:
`R-UI-213 an opened image is read again every 3 s while a version it shows waits for its scan…` (repository-content.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-1140 · The states of the overlays are measured at the component tier, in the unit-test builder's browser mode

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It revisits
[Q-UI-723](#q-ui-723--the-checks-are-tested-on-fixture-pages-in-the-playwright-chromium-not-in-the-angular-test-runner) option (b)
for this target only: the checks' own fixtures stay in Playwright.

Context: about 120 states of the web application were in no picture of the render set, most of them overlays: 21 of 36 dialogs, the
confirm dialog's shapes "type to confirm" and "choice", every failure notice and all but one validation inside a dialog, the conflict
dialog, both session dialogs, the token's secret and tooltips at the window's edge; nine of the layout defects found by eye between
2026-11-12 and 2026-11-25 were such states. A dialog's layout does not depend on the page behind it. Q-UI-723 had refused the Angular
test runner because jsdom lays nothing out and Vitest's browser mode was not installed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Angular unit-test builder's browser mode in headless Chromium, a target of its own (`states`, `make ui-states`), each state opened through the real dialog service or the real component against the in-memory fakes and measured by `layoutFindings` imported from the render set (chosen) | One new development dependency, the provider of the workspace's Vitest | Real layout, the app's global stylesheet and fonts, the same function as the renders; about 20 s for 69 states, no stack, nothing per format; a failure or a refusal is one line of a fake, not a routed answer | A state of the fakes, not of a running server; English only |
| (b) The same states as walks of the render set at 1,440 and 390 px | Routed failing answers and clicks in the full stack | The real server | About 3 minutes more of the longest job, a walk per state, a seed per dialog |
| (c) Playwright's component testing | Another runner | A browser | A second test runner beside Vitest and Playwright's |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** "once, at the cheapest tier" (CLAUDE.md, "Tests stay runnable"): the overlays are measured where they
cost seconds, the pages stay the render set's. The target `test` excludes the `*.states.spec.ts`, so `make web-test` is unchanged.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-176. Code: the target `states` of [angular.json](../../web/angular.json),
[states.ts](../../web/src/app/testing/states.ts), the `*.states.spec.ts`, the `Makefile` target `ui-states`.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** (2026-11-25), on the owner's finding; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

sein? Das ist ja überladen, außerdem habe ich keine Ahnung was das bedeutet und was ich damit anfangen soll." They are the package's npm
dist-tags: names a maintainer points at one version each, so that `npm install <package>@next` installs the version `next` names. The
run showed every tag, unbounded, with no word of what they are and nothing to do with them. The package's page showed the same tags as
badges on their versions' rows (Q-UI-453), without a word either, and the version's page in its header. npm is the one format with

catalogue's `tags` is empty for them, `PackageInfo.Tags` is set by npm alone).

| (b) Keep a line of tags above the versions, labelled "npm tags:" and bounded | The run with a word | Every tag in one place | Still a second list beside the list of versions, the overload the owner named |
| (c) A column **Tags** in the versions' table | A column | Aligned | Empty in nearly every row; a fourth column that the table cannot afford at 1,024 px (Q-CUR-157) |

| (a) A project's list's columns (the visibility icon before the key, format, class, **Set up client** and the menu) with **Project** after the repository; **Last activity** for the holder of `repositories:write-config` while a row has one; no copy button; the project filter a choice of the projects the caller sees, by display name; no **New repository**, the line under the heading saying where a repository is created (chosen) | One row for one repository wherever it is listed | A plain user sets up a client from the row as in a project; the address stands where its client is set up; the administrator keeps the fact of maintenance | The administrator copies an address from Set up client, one click further |
| (b) The admin list's columns as they were | Visibility column, copy button | Nothing changes for an administrator | A column and an address a plain user does not need, against R-UI-169 |
| (c) **New repository** with a project to choose in the form | The admin area's form, moved | One place to create from | A second way to create, the one the owner named to go ("A new repository is created in its project, as everywhere else") |

**Choice:** (a). The line under the heading: "The repositories you can see, in every project. A new repository is created in its
project." A system repository of `upstream` carries the badge **System** after its key (R-UI-193) and, while it answers no client,
no **Set up client** (Q-UI-896). The list reads `GET /api/v1/repositories` (R-REPO-012), which already lists what the caller may read
across projects and every repository for `repositories:read-config`, with its authorization tests at the integration tier
(`R-REPO-012 R-AUTHZ-016 the list holds the repositories the caller may read, anonymous included`); the API needed no change.
**Rationale:** the list is one more way to the same rows; it should look like the rows a user knows from a project, with the one
column a list across projects needs. The development agent would revisit the copy button if the owner misses it at the walk.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-020, R-UI-065, R-UI-066, R-UI-169. Code: [repository-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.ts),
[repository-list.html](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-list.html). Tests:

### Q-UI-1050 · A stacked row is a grid of names and values, one field a line

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Supersedes
[Q-UI-681](#q-ui-681--a-stacked-row-puts-its-cells-side-by-side).

Context: in the stacked rows of every project's repositories at 390 px (T-25's renders, 2026-11-23) **Format** stood beside
**Project** in one block and beside **Class** in the next, as the values' widths fell: Q-UI-681 put the fields side by side, as many
to a line as fit, so a field's place followed the widths of the values before it, and the eye found a field at another place in every
block. Q-UI-681's reason against one field a line, 33 versions 5,136 px high at 1,024 px, was the stacking below 48 rem of every list;
since [Q-UI-680](#q-ui-680--a-list-stacks-where-its-columns-at-their-least-widths-do-not-fit-measured-by-the-table-itself) a list
stacks only where its columns do not fit, at 390 px for most lists.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One field a line: its column's name in a column as wide as the list's longest name, at most two fifths of the list, and its value beside it; an empty field left out (chosen) | The data table measures the names its rows show (`--quader-stack-names`); each named cell is a table of two cells, its name and the browser's anonymous cell around its value | Every name of a list at one x and every value at another, in every block; a value of several pieces (a time and a state under it) stays beside its name; the stacked rows of the reference's tables have this form | A block is a line per field: a list of five fields is about twice as high at 390 px as side by side |
| (b) Fields side by side, as many to a line as fit (Q-UI-681) | A flex row | Dense | A field at another place in every block, the finding |
| (c) A grid of slots, two or three fields to a line at the wider widths, an empty field kept as a dash in its slot | A container query per width | Dense where there is room, each field in its slot | A dash per empty field in every block; a long value breaks in a slot of a third of the row; a list stacks at 1,024 px only where its columns do not fit, so the room it would save is rare |
| (d) The columns of names as a percentage of the row | One rule in the stylesheet | No measurement | A table's cell takes a width that calculates with a percentage as none (the first fixture laid the names at half the row); a share wastes room beside short names |

**Choice:** (a), in [data-table.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.ts) (`measure`) and
[_list-screens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_list-screens.scss) (Stacked rows). A field without a column's name (`stackLabel: false`, a
download, a check box) takes a line of its own across the block; a meter (`td.meter-cell`), a state with its icon and a format or a class
with its icon keep their own layout with the same column of names. In a block a column's cap of the table form does not hold: a
field takes the line, a value cut with an ellipsis takes its column of values (its copy button beside it), and a version or a media
type longer than the column of values breaks inside itself there (a database's version, an image's media type at 390 px). The render
run measures it: `stacked-place` names a field whose name
or value stands off the x of the list's other fields, or two fields of a block on one line
([layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), fixtures in [layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts)).
**Rationale:** a stacked block is read by its fields' names; a name at one place in every block is found without reading the line. The
development agent revisits (c) if a list that stacks at 1,024 px or wider grows long enough to be read by scrolling.
**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-174. Tests: "R-UI-174 a stacked list measures its longest column name" in
[data-table.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.spec.ts), the fixtures of `stacked-place` in layout-checks.spec.ts.
