### Q-API-417 · The version list of a package is read a page at a time by a keyset query in the order of publication

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That the version
list's statement gets a keyset and a limit, for every format, was set by the coordinator of the findings run of 2026-11-23 after the
measurement of H-829 ([formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md#h-829--the-package-list-of-a-remote-reads-every-tag-entry-of-an-image-to-count-it)).

Context: `PackageViewVersions` read every visible row of a package, with the size and the downloads of each, for every page; the service
grouped, sorted and paged them in memory. With 100,000 tags of one image a page of 50 took 16.6 s, the first page and one in the middle
alike. R-API-010 asks one keyset query per page. A version of the list is one entry over the rows of every repository of the scope that
holds it (its `publishedAt` is its oldest row's); the order of publication is a pair of a time and a name, the order of the format's
versions is the format's `Compare`, which no statement can sort: npm's SemVer, NuGet's precedence, Debian's dpkg order, Ansible Galaxy's
SemVer, OCI's tag order (R-OCI-031), generic files without versions.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A package that one repository of the scope holds, in the order of publication: one keyset statement on (creation time, version compared bytewise) with a limit, in the order of an index (`package_versions_listing`; a remote OCI repository's tags by `remote_cache_entries_tag_time`, Q-OCI-267); the rows with sizes and downloads are read for the page's versions alone. A package several repositories hold, and the order of the format's versions, read every visible version's name, one cheap row each, and sort in the service (chosen) | The common page (one repository, the default order) reads its page; the others read names, no size and no downloads per row | The cursor is the statement's order: the time a version was created and its name, both stored, so a version keeps its place while others come and go, in every format; the format's `Compare` stays the format's; a pre-release filter, which is the format's rule, asks again from the last version read until the page is full | A package of several repositories and the order of versions still read every name (H-1683) |
| (b) A sort key of the format's order stored with every version | `package_versions.sort_key` written by every format at a commit and a fill | The order of versions by keyset too | A column every format must fill and keep, a migration of every stored version; OCI's tags are no version rows |
| (c) Keep reading every row, cache the grouped list per package revision | A replica's cache | Repeated pages are cheap | The first page of every revision reads every row; a remote's tags change with every fill |

**Choice:** (a). The cursor of the order of publication is `[publishedAt, version]`, of the order of versions `[version]`; both are the
service's, unchanged for a client. **Revised on 2026-11-24** by [Q-API-429](#q-api-429--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row):
option (b) is built for the order of the format's versions and the latest version of a package, after the measurement of a local package
with 100,000 versions; the order of publication stays as chosen here. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-029. Code: `Versions`, `keysetPage`, `sortedPage` in
[service.go](../../internal/packages/view/service.go); `PackageViewVersionPage*`, `PackageViewTagPage*`, `PackageViewHolders`,
`PackageViewVersionNames`, `PackageViewVersions` (by package ids and versions) in [package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql);
migration [00113](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00113_version_list_keyset.sql). Tests:
`TestR_API_010_APageOfVersionsReadsNoVersionPastItsLimit` ([packages](../../test/integration/packages/versions_keyset_test.go)),
`TestR_API_010_APageOfARemotesTagsReadsNoTagPastItsLimit` ([ociremote](../../test/integration/ociremote/listing_keyset_test.go)),
`TestR_API_029_VersionList`.

### Q-API-428 · The package view's statements run without the server's JIT compilation

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the plans of the measurement of H-829 (2026-11-23) showed PostgreSQL's JIT compiling statements of the package view for 0.3 to
0.5 s each: the planner costs `package_version_listing` and the tags of a remote OCI repository far above `jit_above_cost` (an estimate of
1 row or of millions where 100,001 were read, or none), and `PackageViewCandidates` ran in 0.03 ms and took 0.26 s.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `set_config('jit', 'off', true)` as the first statement of every transaction of the view's service (chosen) | The view's reads only | No compile of 0.3 to 0.5 s on a statement that runs in milliseconds; works through a transaction-mode pooler | One statement more per transaction of the view |
| (b) `jit = off` for every session of the installation | A startup parameter, and a role default behind a pooler, checked by preflight (R-HA-058) | Every statement | A requirement on every installation's roles for a problem measured in one service |
| (c) Better estimates | Statistics, a rewritten view | The planner's other choices improve too | The view's shape (a union and a derived name) keeps estimates that are guesses |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-029 (above). Code: `Service.read` in [service.go](../../internal/packages/view/service.go).

### Q-API-429 · The order of a format's versions is a sort key stored with every version row

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough
([ADR-278](../decisions.md#adr-278--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row)). It revises
[Q-API-417](#q-api-417--the-version-list-of-a-package-is-read-a-page-at-a-time-by-a-keyset-query-in-the-order-of-publication), which had
left H-1683 open.

Context: the measurement of 2026-11-24 ([packages.md](../developer/packages.md#a-package-with-100000-versions-h-1683-measured),
[oci.md](../developer/oci.md#the-listing-of-a-remote-with-very-many-tags-h-829-measured)). With 100,000 versions of one local npm package
a page of its versions in the order of the versions took 0.40 s, the package list 0.66 s and the package's page 0.59 s; with 100,000 tags
of a remote image that point at 100,000 different manifests, the page in the order of the tags 0.58 s and the package list 1.24 s
(load average 19 to 23 on 20 cores). Each read every version's name and ordered it in the service by the format's `Compare`, the order
for a page and the latest version for the list; the list's statement ran a subplan for the downloads of every version of the scope.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A sort key of the format's order stored with every version row (chosen) | The format's view adapter gives the key (`ViewAdapter.SortKey`, contract version 12); the host's package writer stores it and the format's pre-release answer with every row; a remote OCI repository's tag entries derive the same key in PostgreSQL from the stored tag (`oci_tag_sort_key`, a generated column) | A page in the order of the versions is one keyset statement per holder on an index; the latest version is the first entry of an index of releases, else of pre-releases; the format's order stays in the format's code, next to `Compare`, and kit check 11 holds the two to one order | A column every version row carries; the tags' key is written twice, in Go and in SQL, and a test compares them byte for byte; a stored version keeps the key it was written with |
| (b) Keep ordering in the service (Q-API-417) | Every visible version's name per page and per listed package | Nothing stored | 0.4 to 1.2 s with 100,000 versions, for every page |
| (c) The key computed by PostgreSQL for every format | A function per format and a trigger on the version rows | Every writer, a test's SQL included, writes the right key; a migration can fill the stored rows | Every format's order written a second time, in SQL; the twenty formats to come each need one, tested only against a database |

**Choice:** (a). A key is a class byte (0x00 for a string that is no version, 0x01 for a version), the format's self-delimiting encoding
and the version's bytes ([versionkey](../../internal/formats/versionkey/versionkey.go)), so two strings have two keys and the cursor stays
`[version]`: the service asks the format for its key. The package list now reads, per listed package row, its latest release, its latest
pre-release when it has no release, and a remote image's latest tag (`PackageViewLatest`), each the first visible entry of an index, and
sums the downloads of the page's packages alone, by joins and not a subplan per version. The rows stored before the key existed cannot
carry it: migration 00116 adds the columns without a value for them, the background migration `version_sort_key` fills them through the
format's code, and the reads order a row without a key by the key its format gives it meanwhile ([Q-API-430](#q-api-430--a-version-row-without-a-stored-sort-key-is-ordered-by-the-key-its-format-gives-it);
[Q-HA-492](ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-492--the-fill-of-the-versions-sort-keys-records-its-completion-after-a-pass-that-leaves-no-row-without-a-key)).
**Revised on 2026-11-24**: the step had refused a database that held version rows, which every running installation does within seconds
of its start (the malware updater stores the scanner's definitions as versions), so it refused every upgrade (R-HA-020). **Rationale:** the
order of versions is the format's knowledge; a key computed where `Compare` lives is tested at the cheapest tier for every format, and the
one place it is written twice (the tags of a remote, which are cache entries the engine writes) is a rule of a few lines that one
integration test compares over a table of tags. The development agent would revisit this if a format's order cannot be encoded as bytes,
or when the count of a package's versions, still read whole (H-1683), is kept by the commit and the fill. **Applied in the spec:**
R-API-029, H-1683, [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) H-829, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008 (contract version 12). Code:
`keyPage`, `keyBatch`, `latestCandidates` in [service.go](../../internal/packages/view/service.go); `PackageViewVersionKey*`,
`PackageViewTagKey*`, `PackageViewLatest`, `PackageViewList` in [package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql);
the writer's `versionOrder` and `VersionOrder` in [hooks.go](../../internal/formathost/hooks.go); migration
[00116](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00116_version_sort_key.sql). Tests: `TestR_API_010_APageOfVersionsReadsNoVersionPastItsLimit`
([packages](../../test/integration/packages/versions_keyset_test.go)), `TestR_API_010_APageOfARemotesTagsReadsNoTagPastItsLimit`
([ociremote](../../test/integration/ociremote/listing_keyset_test.go)), kit check 11 (`viewSortKey` in
[checks_view.go](../../internal/formats/formattest/checks_view.go)) and the key tests of npm, Debian and the tag order.

### Q-API-430 · A version row without a stored sort key is ordered by the key its format gives it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It revises
[Q-API-429](#q-api-429--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row), whose migration refused a database
that held version rows.

Context: the sort key of a version is computed by its format's code, so migration 00116 cannot write it for the rows stored before it, and
during a rolling upgrade (R-HA-020) the replicas of the release before it keep writing rows without one until they stop. Every running
installation holds version rows within seconds of its start (the malware updater stores the scanner's definitions `main`, `daily` and
`bytecode` as versions), so a step that refuses such a database refuses every upgrade. The columns are therefore nullable, and the
background migration `version_sort_key` fills them ([Q-HA-492](ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-492--the-fill-of-the-versions-sort-keys-records-its-completion-after-a-pass-that-leaves-no-row-without-a-key)).
Until it has, and again for a row a replica of the release before writes after it, a version without a key must neither vanish from a
page nor be listed out of order, and the latest version must count it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The statements return a package's rows without a key after their keyed batch, and the service gives each the key its format gives it (chosen) | `PackageViewVersionKeyDesc`/`Asc` return, after the batch on the key, every visible row of the package whose key is NULL; `keyRows` computes `Adapter.SortKey(version)` for each, keeps it when it lies after the cursor's key and merges it with the keyed rows (only those count against the batch); `PackageViewLatest` returns every visible row without a key as a candidate besides the first of each index, and the format's order picks the latest among them | Right for every package at every moment, also for a row written after the fill completed (a rollback); one statement as before, no state to read and no second code path; the key the service computes is the one the fill stores (`formathost.VersionOrder`), so a page's cursor means the same before and after; once the rows are filled the extra part reads nothing (`package_versions_by_key` holds the NULL keys) | A package with many rows without a key reads all of them on every page until the fill reaches them, as every page did before Q-API-429 |
| (b) The API answers the old way until the background migration reports done | The service reads the migration's state and orders in the service (the way before Q-API-429) while it is not `succeeded` | The old way is known to be right | A switch over the whole installation for the rows of a few packages; a row a replica of the release before writes after the completion is ordered wrong or lost from the latest; the old path stays in the code beside the new |
| (c) A package with a row without a key falls back to the old way | A probe per package, then the keyset or the old sort | Each package read by the cheap path as soon as its rows are filled | Two paths per read and a probe per package; a cursor must mean the same in both, which (a) gets for free |
| (d) The keyset ignores rows without a key until they are filled | Nothing to build | — | A version vanishes from the pages and from the latest for minutes after an upgrade, and for good when written after the completion |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the rows without a key are few, short-lived and recognizable in the statement itself (a NULL key); giving
each the key the fill will store keeps one path, one cursor and the exact order, and the cost falls only on what is not filled yet. The
development agent would revisit this if a fill could leave rows without a key for long, or if the key of a stored row could differ from the
one the format gives (a change of the encoding, which a migration step then clears so the fill recomputes it). **Applied in the spec:**
R-API-029, Q-API-429. Code: `keyRows` and `keyBatch` in [service.go](../../internal/packages/view/service.go); `PackageViewVersionKeyDesc`,
`PackageViewVersionKeyAsc` and `PackageViewLatest` in [package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql); migration
[00116](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00116_version_sort_key.sql). Tests: `TestR_API_029_VersionsWithoutAStoredKeyKeepTheirPlaceBeforeAndAfterTheFill`
([packages](../../test/integration/packages/versions_unkeyed_test.go)), `TestR_HA_020_TheSortKeyStepPassesOnADatabaseOfThePreviousRelease`
([postgres](../../test/integration/postgres/version_sort_key_test.go)); `TestR_API_010_APageOfVersionsReadsNoVersionPastItsLimit` keeps
holding the keyset's bound.

### Q-API-431 · Every list of versions is newest first by its format's order, and a version the format does not rank comes below by its time

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on the owner's word of 2026-11-25 ("Nächstes Thema, ich wünsche eine Erkennung von
semantic-versioning. Ich wünsche, dass unsere Software automatisch erkennt, dass 4.16.6 höher ist als 4.2.8, die Darstellung von Versionen
ist default von der neusten zur ältesten."); the options are the development agent's, the owner reviews them at the walkthrough. It revises
[Q-API-417](#q-api-417--the-version-list-of-a-package-is-read-a-page-at-a-time-by-a-keyset-query-in-the-order-of-publication)'s default
(`-publishedAt`) and, on what the class of a key means,
[Q-API-429](#q-api-429--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row) and
[ADR-278](../decisions.md#adr-278--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row).

Context: every format already ranks its versions (`Compare`, `SortKey`), and the package's page sorted by it, but the API's default and
the opened item in the content list were the order of publication: on the owner's image the tags fetched last, the oldest versions, stood
first. And an OCI tag that is no version had the key class of a version (0x01 0x00), which no statement can tell from npm's 0x01 followed
by its first number, so "below every version" was not a rule a statement could keep.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The default `sort` is `-version`; the order has two parts, the ranked versions by key, then the versions of the class `NotVersion` newest first by time, each part a keyset (chosen) | The API's default; `PackageViewVersionUnranked*`, `PackageViewTagUnranked*` on two partial indexes; one walk across both parts in the service | One rule for every format; a format with no unranked string pays one empty index probe; a cursor stays the position in one keyset | Two cursor shapes; a package several repositories hold reads its unranked versions whole for the second part (H-1901) |
| (b) The default `-version`, unranked strings by their bytes | No second keyset | Simple | `sha-…` above `main` above `latest` says nothing (the owner's image) |
| (c) Keep `-publishedAt` as the default, the screens ask `-version` | No API change | — | Every client gets the order the owner objected to unless it knows better |

**Choice:** (a). The second part is ordered by the version's time, the first row's (push time; a remote tag's fetch time), and the name
bytewise; the latest version of a package with no ranked version is its newest unranked one (`PackageViewLatest` reads the first entry
of each partial index). **Rationale:** the order of versions is the format's knowledge, and a string the format does not rank carries
nothing but its time. The development agent would revisit the walk of several holders if a package that a local and a remote repository
both hold with many unranked versions is common (H-1901). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-029; [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-031
and Q-OCI-269. Code: `walk`, `orderPage`, `unrankedRows`, `latestOf` in [order.go](../../internal/packages/view/order.go) and
[service.go](../../internal/packages/view/service.go); the statements named above and `PackageViewLatest` in
[package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql); migration
[00123](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00123_unranked_versions.sql). Tests: `TestR_API_029_VersionList` (area `packages`, the
default), `TestR_API_029_LatestOfAPackageWithoutARankedVersionIsItsNewest` (unit), `TestR_API_010_APageOfARemotesTagsReadsNoTagPastItsLimit`
(area `ociremote`, the second part's statements read no entry past their page), `TestR_HA_020_TheUnrankedVersionsStepPassesOnADatabaseOfThePreviousRelease`
(area `postgres`).

### Q-API-432 · The list by content: one entry per manifest, on the walk of the order of the versions, with a lead check per batch and a scan budget

Status: **Decided by the development agent**, carrying out the owner's word of 2026-11-25 for the server (his objection on the tab Images of
`upstream/docker-hub`: "Außerdem sehe ich die Signaturen für Images neben den Images. Anstatt also die Images als Signiert anzuzeigen indem
sie einen passenden Icon bekommen, habe ich Signatur-Tags die ein Suchen in den Images sehr unübersichtlich machen."). The rows he meant
are commit tags (`sha-5ccfd1a`) his pipeline pushes beside each version on the same manifest; his image's 315 tags held no signature tag.
What stands: one image was two to five rows. The development agent's answer, told to him: one row per image (manifest digest) with all
its tags, the version first, found by any of them, the signature as a mark on the row
([Q-UI-1130](#q-ui-1130--an-image-is-one-row-with-its-tags-on-the-opened-item-and-on-the-packages-page),
[ADR-280](../decisions.md#adr-280--a-version-that-names-content-stores-its-digest-and-a-list-of-versions-groups-by-it)). The owner
reviews the options at the walkthrough.

Context: a version list is a keyset walk of the order of the versions (Q-API-429, Q-API-431); an image with 100,000 tags must stay a
page of tens of milliseconds (H-829). Grouping by digest means: an entry for each digest at its first tag in that order, and every other
tag of the digest left out of the walk but named on that entry.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `group=content` on the version list: the walk of the order of the versions in batches of 64; after each batch one statement per holder asks which of the batch's (version, digest) pairs a visible version earlier in the order names (`PackageViewImageSeen`, an index probe per candidate on the indexes by document); the others lead an entry; the page is cut after a version's last entry; one request reads at most 1,024 versions, so a page may be short with a cursor (chosen) | One more mode of the list, the same cursor | No state kept beside the versions: a page is right after any push, move or eviction; an image whose tags each name their own manifest costs what the plain page costs; the walk, the cursor and the visibility are the plain list's | The tags that lead nothing are read again by a later request: a run of 100,000 tags on one manifest costs one request per 1,024 of them at the end of the list (H-1900) |
| (b) A table of images kept by the commit and the fill, each with its leading tag | One row per image to page over | A page reads its images and nothing else | A write path in every tag write, every move, every eviction and every remote listing rule that changes with a download (R-OCI-036); the leading tag changes with any of them |
| (c) Group in the browser over every tag | No server change | — | Reads every tag for every opened image; the opened item shows ten |
| (d) `GROUP BY` the digest in SQL, ordered by the group's highest key | One statement | — | A sort over every tag of the image for every page; no keyset over an aggregate |

**Choice:** (a). The entry is the leading version's summary with the digest always, `aliases` (at most 100, from
`PackageViewImageTags`: of each holder at most 101 ranked versions by key and 101 unranked by time), `aliasesMore`, the image's
holders as `repositories` and its downloads (`PackageViewImageDownloads`: the files of the package that hold the manifest's bytes, each
once, a tag item only while its version is visible). Only `sort=-version` and no `prerelease`: another order would need another lead
than the first in the list, and the package's page sorts and filters in the browser. A format whose versions name no content (every
format but OCI today) answers its plain list with empty `aliases`. **Rationale:** grouping is a reading of the same order, so it is
built on the same walk and needs nothing kept; the bound per request keeps a pathological image from costing one request more than
its share. The development agent would revisit (b) if the end of a list of commit tags is a measured cost (H-1900). **Applied in the
spec:** R-API-010, R-API-029, R-UI-052, R-UI-110. Code: `Images`, `imageWalk`, `imagesSeen`, `imageFacts` in
[images.go](../../internal/packages/view/images.go); the statements `PackageViewImageSeen`, `PackageViewImageUnkeyed`,
`PackageViewImageTags`, `PackageViewImageDownloads` in [package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql);
`versionListQuery` in [packages_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/packages_api.go). Tests: `TestR_API_029_TheListByContentGroupsAndCutsAtAVersion`
(unit), `TestR_API_029_TheListByContentIsTheGroupingOfTheListByTag` (area `ociremote`, the oracle and the budget),
`TestR_API_029_AMovedTagMovesBetweenImagesOfTheListByContent` (area `oci`), `TestR_API_029_VersionList` (area `packages`).

### Q-API-433 · A format says which of its versions is a pre-release where it says its order

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-25 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
It carries out R-API-029's rule of `latestVersion` (the highest visible stable version) for every format, and revises
[Q-ARCH-257](architecture.md#q-arch-257--a-minimal-contract-the-npm-concepts-leave-the-shared-types)'s "`ViewAdapter.Prerelease` leaves
the contract, the exposure adapter's answer is the one definition"
([ADR-282](../decisions.md#adr-282--a-format-says-which-of-its-versions-is-a-pre-release-in-its-view-adapter)).

Context: the screens, the stored flag `package_versions.prerelease` (migration 00116) and the latest version read "is a pre-release" from
the format's exposure adapter. Only clamav, generic, npm and NuGet have one: OCI and Ansible Galaxy, which order their versions and know
their pre-releases (the tag order's markers, the mirror's `includePrereleases`), answered false for every version. Seen in the render seed:
the image `portal/worker` showed Latest `2.0.0-rc.1`, no image row carried the badge Pre-release, and every stored flag of an image tag
was false. Nothing made a format that orders its versions say it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ViewAdapter.Prerelease(version) bool` beside `Compare` and `SortKey`; the exposure adapter loses `Prerelease`, and `Register` composes the catalog's `Versioning` of the exposure adapter's ranges and the view adapter's answer, a string the view adapter does not rank being no version; a format whose rules narrow versions needs a view adapter; contract version 13 (chosen) | One method, one answer, read by the screens, the writer of the rows and the decision point | A format with an order cannot compile without the answer; the two answers cannot disagree because there is one; kit check 11 holds the answer against the fixture's named pre-releases or the reason the format has none | A contract change: every format moves (six view adapters, two exposure adapters lose a method); npm's exposure now reads a version strictly as its order does (`v1.0.0` is no version there either) |
| (b) Keep the exposure adapter as the definition and give OCI and Ansible one | No contract change | The definition stays where Q-ARCH-257 put it | Two formats gain an exposure surface (ranges, dimensions) nobody asked for, only to say a pre-release; a format with an order and no exposure still answers false without notice |
| (c) Both adapters answer, a kit check holds them equal | Two definitions, a test between | — | The disagreement the finding was, kept possible and caught only when a fixture happens to name the version |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** whether a version is a pre-release is part of the format's notion of its versions, the same knowledge as
its order, and the place that must exist for a format with screens is the view adapter. The exposure rules need the same answer, so they
read it from there. The development agent would revisit it if a format needs exposure rules over versions without package screens.
**Applied in the spec:** R-API-029, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008 (the contract block),
[formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-031 and Q-OCI-270, [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-026 and Q-ANS-92,
[formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-002. Code: `ViewAdapter.Prerelease` in [view.go](../../internal/formats/view.go), `versioning`
in [exposure.go](../../internal/formats/exposure.go), `CatalogEntry` and `Validate` in [formats.go](../../internal/formats/formats.go),
`orderOf` in [hooks.go](../../internal/formathost/hooks.go), the view adapters of every format; kit check 11
([checks_view.go](../../internal/formats/formattest/checks_view.go) `viewPrerelease`, `ViewFixture.Prereleases` and `NoPrereleases`).
Tests: `TestR_API_029_TheRulesAskTheViewAdapterWhichVersionIsAPrerelease` (unit), `TestR_ARCH_010_Check11ViewAdapter` (the kit's own),
`TestR_API_029_AnImageTagIsAPrereleaseByTheTagOrder`, `TestR_API_029_ACollectionVersionIsAPrereleaseByItsSemanticVersion`,
`TestR_API_029_ADebianVersionIsNoPrerelease`, `TestR_API_029_NPMVersionOrderIsSemVerPrecedence` (units of the formats), kit check 11 of
every format (`TestR_ARCH_010_Conformance`).

### Q-API-434 · A format whose ecosystem has no pre-release calls no version one

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-25 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-API-433 makes every format with an order answer the question. Debian's versions have no pre-release that every archive uses
alike ([formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-002, Q-DEB-17): a `~` sorts a version below the one it precedes and marks an upstream
pre-release (`1.0~rc1-1`) as often as a backport or a stable update (`1.0-1~bpo12+1`, `1.0-1~deb12u1`); APT installs the highest version
its pinning allows, and what a repository keeps apart is a distribution (`experimental`), not a version. A ClamAV definitions database's
version is the number of its build, and freshclam takes the newest.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Both answer false for every version; their kit fixtures say why (`NoPrereleases`) (chosen) | The latest version is the highest | What the clients install is what the screens call latest | A `~` pre-release that is the highest version is shown as the latest (H-1971) |
| (b) Debian: a `~` in the upstream part marks a pre-release | A rule of thumb | Catches `1.0~rc1` | Calls a backport or a security update of a stable release a pre-release; no client acts on it; invented |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a pre-release is what a format's clients pass over unless asked; where no client does, there is none to
show. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-029, [formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md) R-DEB-002, [formats/clamav.md](formats/clamav.md) (its
versions are build numbers). Code: `Prerelease` in [deb/view.go](../../internal/formats/deb/view.go) and
[clamav/view.go](../../internal/formats/clamav/view.go). Tests: `TestR_API_029_ADebianVersionIsNoPrerelease` (unit), kit check 11 of both
formats.

### Q-API-435 · A remote's tag entries carry whether the tag is a pre-release, and the latest tag is read by two indexes

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-25 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a remote OCI repository's tags are cache entries, not version rows (R-OCI-036); PostgreSQL derives their sort key from the tag
(`oci_tag_sort_key`, migrations 00116 and 00123), and `PackageViewLatest` took a remote image's highest tag as its candidate, which is
`2.0.0-rc.1` when that is the highest. The version rows of the release before store the old answer (false) for every image tag and every
Ansible collection version.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `oci_tag_prerelease(tag)`, the format's rule in SQL, a stored generated column `tag_prerelease` beside `tag_sort_key`, two partial indexes of the releases and the pre-releases of a name's tags, and `PackageViewLatest` reads the first entry of each; migration 00126 clears the key and the flag of the stored rows whose answer changes, and the background migration `version_sort_key` fills them again (chosen) | The remote's latest tag is two index probes, like a local package's | The latest of a remote image is right with one entry read per kind; the rows refill the way 00123 made them; a test holds the SQL equal to the Go code over one table of tags | The column writes the table once at the migration; the rule exists twice, in Go and in SQL |
| (b) Read the highest tags in key order until one is no pre-release | No column | — | An image with many pre-releases above its last release reads them all on every package list |
| (c) Compute the flag in the service for the candidates | No SQL rule | — | The highest tag is the only candidate; the release below it is never read |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the remote's tags follow the rows' design (a key and a flag beside each, an index per kind) so that the
latest version has one rule across classes. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-029, [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-270. Code:
[00126](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00126_version_prerelease.sql), `PackageViewLatest` in
[package_view.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/package_view.sql). Tests: the SQL-against-Go table and the latest tag's candidates of
`TestR_API_010_APageOfARemotesTagsReadsNoTagPastItsLimit` (area `ociremote`), `TestR_HA_020_ThePrereleaseStepRefillsTheRowsWhoseAnswerChanged`
(area `postgres`).

### Q-API-440 · Deprecation is a member of the view's summary, and the format decides the write

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: npm, NuGet and Ansible Galaxy each have a deprecation, of a version or of a whole package, and it must be marked in every list
and set where the protocol carries it (R-API-085). npm's message reached its version's page as a member of the format's metadata, which
a list never reads.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ViewData.Deprecation` and `Unlisted`, read with the summary; two optional interfaces, `DeprecationFinder` for the filter and `Deprecator` for the write; the management operation builds a request of the format and the format decides as its own protocol write does (chosen) | The format contract carries the state; the core reads it as it reads a description | Every list marks it at the cost of the summary read it makes anyway; npm's ownership, NuGet's, the lock, the revision and the audit event stay the format's; a new format adds two methods | The contract grows by two interfaces (an addition, `ContractVersion` stays) |
| (b) A column `deprecated` on the generic version rows, written by the core | One place | The filter is a column | The formats keep their own state for their documents (npm's `deprecated`, NuGet's registration, the collection document): two places to keep equal, and the core would decide a format's rules |
| (c) A metadata member per format, as npm's was | No contract change | — | Lists never read the details; every screen learns each format's member |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the state stays where the format serves it from, and the core gets one shape for the screens. Revisit when a
format needs a deprecation the summary cannot read cheaply. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-085,
[architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-008 (the contract blocks), ADR-286. Code: `internal/formats/deprecation.go`,
`internal/api/v1/deprecation_api.go`.

### Q-API-441 · A package is shown deprecated when its latest version is, and the filter asks the same

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: npm and NuGet deprecate versions, so a package may have deprecated and current versions at once (`npm deprecate pkg@"<2"`); a
list row names the package and its latest version.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The row carries its latest version's deprecation, and `deprecated=true` keeps the packages whose latest visible version is deprecated (chosen) | The mark belongs to what the row names | npm's and nuget.org's pages call a package deprecated by the version they show; an Ansible collection is the same either way; the statement picks the latest by the order the view uses (release, pre-release, unranked; the stored key) | A package with an old deprecated line is not "deprecated" in the list; its table of versions says it |
| (b) A package is deprecated when every visible version is | One rule without the latest | A package deprecated whole is found | A row whose latest is deprecated and an older one is not shows no mark, though its page says it |
| (c) A package with any deprecated version | Simplest statement | — | Most of npm's popular packages have an old deprecated version: the filter finds everything |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the mark and the filter say the same thing about the same version, and the version is the one the row
shows. The filter's statement takes the deprecated versions from the formats (`DeprecationFinder`, bounded as a search is, 100,000) and
keeps a package whose latest visible version is among them; a row whose key is not filled yet counts as unranked. **Applied in the
spec:** R-API-085, `PackageViewList` in `package_view.sql`.

### Q-API-442 · One operation on a repository's package; the format decides the subject

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `PUT`/`DELETE …/repositories/{repoKey}/packages/{packageName}/deprecation`, the version in the body or the query; the format refuses a version it cannot carry, or its absence (chosen) | One shape for every format | The repository is the one whose rows change (a deprecation of a local repository's copy); the path is the one of the owners of a name; an Ansible collection takes no version | A client must know whether to send a version; the refusal says it |
| (b) `…/packages/{packageId}/versions/{version}/deprecation` | The version's own address | — | The package id spans repositories, so the repository is a parameter anyway; a collection would need a second path |
| (c) The formats' own protocol writes only (`npm deprecate`) | No new operation | — | NuGet and Ansible Galaxy have no client command for it; the screen needs one |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the change is of a local repository's rows, decided by the format; a remote shows its upstream's state and
a virtual one its members', so both answer `409 not_applicable`. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-085, `api/openapi.yaml`.

### Q-API-443 · A suggestion is marked for a repository the caller reads whole

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the suggestions are read without the aggregation of the list (R-API-062), a package placed in one repository; a repository the
caller reads in part is decided on the package alone.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) For the suggestions placed in a repository the caller reads whole, the latest version's candidates (`PackageViewLatest`) and the formats' summaries, one statement and one read per format (chosen) | The list's rule on the shown suggestions only | At most ten packages; no version a caller may not read is consulted | A suggestion in a repository read in part carries no mark |
| (b) The list's statement for the suggestions | Every scope | — | The aggregation R-API-062 avoids |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-085, `view.Service.Suggest`.

### Q-API-444 · A Helm chart's deprecation is one bit of its configuration every reader of the version sees

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a Helm chart says it is deprecated in its `Chart.yaml`, which the chart's config blob holds. The facts of a configuration are
content and are left out for a caller who may not read the blob (formats/oci.md Q-OCI-273); the lists, the switch, the search suggestions
and the filter `deprecated` read the summary, which carries no content.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The flag is read with every summary, as a column of the statement `OCITagFacts` outside the gated configuration, and the filter reads it with `OCIViewDeprecated` (chosen) | Every reader of the version sees the mark | One bit, which `helm install` prints to everyone who pulls the chart; the same rule as npm's and NuGet's deprecation, which their documents carry for every reader | A reader who may not download the chart learns one fact of its configuration |
| (b) Only for a caller who may read the config blob | The rule of the configuration's facts | Nothing of a blob leaks | A list would ask the rules of every listed version's blob, a read per row; the mark would differ between readers of the same list |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-API-085; formats/oci.md R-OCI-042.

### Q-UI-1300 · One mark: Deprecated is a warning badge, Unlisted a plain one

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| (b) The plain badge everywhere | As the tab Upstream had it | — | A deprecation reads like "Pre-release" |

it. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-085.

### Q-UI-1301 · Deprecating is an act in the menu of the version's head, with a small dialog

| (a) A menu (`more_vert`) at the end of the head for a reader who may deploy in a local repository that holds the version: **Deprecate version**, or **Deprecate collection**; a dialog of what the format carries (npm a message, NuGet reasons, a message and an alternate, Ansible a message for Quader's pages) with a sentence of what the clients do; **Change deprecation** and **Undo deprecation** on a deprecated version, the undo without a dialog (chosen) | A repository's acts are a menu at its head's end | Simple by default: nothing on the page for a reader who may not; the act and its words follow the format; the refusal is shown in the dialog whole | One more menu in the head |

### Q-UI-1090 · A tab strip takes its tabs closer before it scrolls

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the version of an Ansible collection has seven tabs (**Dokumentation, Inhalt 1, Dateien, Signaturen, Details,
Schwachstellen, Import-Protokoll**). In German at 1,024 px, the narrowest window with the pinned sidebar, they were 710 px wide and
their strip 697 px, the content's width less the panel's scrollbar of 15 px; the strip scrolled by 11 to 14 px (the current tab's
bolder label decides how far), which R-UI-173 does not allow from 1,024 px on and the check `sideways` flagged (2026-11-24). Every
format's version page shares the strip (`quader-tab-group`); Ansible's is the one with the most tabs, and the other eight strips of
Quader (links, `.tab-nav`) hold four tabs at most. The labels and the number of tabs are decided elsewhere (Q-UI-456).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A strip whose tabs at their own padding are wider than it takes them closer: 8 px at each side of a label instead of 12 (the class `tight` of `quaderTabStrip`); it scrolls with its fades only where they do not fit that way either (chosen) | One measurement of the strip where it already measures (`TabStrip`: on its width, its current tab and a label changing) | Every strip and every format's version page in every language; 56 px of room for seven tabs, so the Ansible strip fits at 1,024 px with 43 px to spare; a strip that fits looks as before | A strip that is a little too wide shows its tabs 8 px closer than one that fits |
| (b) Shorter German labels ("Doku", "Importlog") | The texts | No code | Holds for one strip and one language; the next tab or language is the same defect; worse words |
| (c) Allow a tab strip to scroll at 1,024 px (an exception of the check `sideways` for `.tab-nav`) | The check | The strip's fades say that more tabs lie beyond | R-UI-173 says nothing scrolls sideways from 1,024 px; an exception hides the next too wide strip; the fade hid **Import-Protokoll** behind its chevron |
| (d) Narrower tab padding everywhere | The stylesheet | Simple | Changes every strip, also those that fit, away from the reference's measure (Q-UI-128) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the defect is a strip a few pixels too wide for its place, whatever the labels say; taking the tabs
closer is the smallest change that holds for every strip, language and future tab, and keeps the reference's measure where the tabs
fit. The class is taken off to measure and put back in the same task, so no frame shows the other form. The development agent
revisits (d) if the owner's GitLab draws its tabs with less room, and (c) if a strip ever holds more tabs than fit closer at 1,024 px.

The German pass renders `package-version-ansible` as the plain user only (`de: ['plain']` of a screen, which names the kinds of the
German pass): one version page holds the shared strip with the most tabs and the longest German labels; every kind would add 84
pictures that show the same strip.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-173. Code: [tab-strip.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tab-strip.ts) (`fit`, `TAB_TIGHT`), `.tab-nav.tight` of
[_controls.scss](../../web/src/styles/_controls.scss); the German pass's kinds in [screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts) and
[render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts). Tests: "R-UI-173 a strip whose tabs fit only closer together takes them closer and
does not scroll; one that fits keeps their padding" in [tab-strip.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tab-strip.spec.ts). Docs:
[design-language.md](../developer/design-language.md), [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).

### Q-UI-1091 · A long German word carries soft hyphens at the joints of its compound, and a heading never breaks inside a word

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the German heading of the authentication settings, **Authentifizierungseinstellungen** (31 letters), is wider than the
page's heading of 358 px at 390 px; the page header lets a heading break anywhere (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, the last resort for a
long name), so it read "Authentifizierungseinstellung" / "en" (2026-11-24). No check measured headings. The German file held 33 words
of more than 20 letters (74 places), each a compound (**Berechtigungsrichtlinien**, **Schwachstellendatenbank**,
**Sichtbarkeitseinstellungen**), in headings, labels and sentences alike.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A soft hyphen (`&#xAD;`) at a joint of every German compound of more than 20 letters, so that no run of letters is longer; `make web-i18n-check` refuses such a word without one; the render check `heading-broken` refuses a heading broken between two letters (chosen) | 74 places of the German file, a rule of the check, a check of the renders | Breaks at a joint with a hyphen, as German print does, only where the line is too short; the same in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (a soft hyphen needs no dictionary); every place of the word, not only headings | A translator writes `&#xAD;` into a long compound (the glossary says so, the check names the word) |
| (b) Hyphenation by the browser (`hyphens: auto` with the page's `lang`) | The stylesheet | No change of the texts | Chromium on Linux, the runner's engine, brings no hyphenation dictionary, so the renders and the machines break differently (Q-UI-1068 (b)) |
| (c) A smaller heading at narrow widths | The heading's size | No change of the texts | Away from the reference's sizes (Q-UI-128); a 35-letter word breaks again |
| (d) A shorter phrase where it breaks ("Einstellungen zur Authentifizierung", the breadcrumb's) | One text | Reads well | One screen at a time; the next long compound is the same defect |

**Choice:** (a). The threshold: 20 letters of the first heading's size take some 250 px at 390 px, which every heading's line holds
(the page's heading holds 358 px, about 29 letters); 20 keeps a dialog's and a card's heading safe too. **Rationale:** a word broken
between two letters is the defect the owner's eye catches first; a soft hyphen is the typographic answer that every engine honours
without a dictionary, and the rule over the German file catches the word before any screen shows it, where the render check
catches only the screens of the German pass. The development agent revisits (b) once every engine of the renders and the runner
brings a German dictionary. What it leaves: [H-1860](#h-1860--a-heading-narrower-than-20-letters-and-a-heading-of-a-screen-outside-the-german-pass-are-held-by-no-check).

A label of the sidebar that now wraps at its soft hyphen (**Berechtigungs-** / **richtlinien**: the word ran a few pixels past the
sidebar's line before) keeps its icon on the middle of its first line (R-UI-175): the sidebar's entries stand at their row's top, the
icon with the line rule's margins, and the padding puts a label of one line where the centring put it.

The render check `heading-broken` ([layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts)) measures each heading (`h1` to `h6`, `role="heading"`)
of two lines or more letter by letter; a break between two letters or digits is a finding, unless the text is `code` or a name
(`translate="no"`) longer than 16 characters (Q-UI-425). It takes each letter's last box: Chromium gives the first letter after a soft
hyphen a second box, the hyphen's, at the end of the line above.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-171. Code: [i18n-check.mjs](../../web/scripts/i18n-check.mjs) (`longWords`, `LONG_WORD`),
[messages.de.xlf](../../web/src/locale/messages.de.xlf), `.nav-link` of [_shell.scss](../../web/src/styles/_shell.scss), the check
`heading-broken` of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts); `admin-settings-auth` joins the German pass. Tests: "R-UI-171 a German
word longer than the narrowest heading's line carries a soft hyphen at a joint of its compound" in
[lint-rules.test.mjs](../../web/scripts/lint-rules.test.mjs); the group "a heading broken inside a word (R-UI-171)" in
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts). Docs: [GLOSSARY.md](../../web/src/locale/GLOSSARY.md),
[ui-style-guide.md](../developer/ui-style-guide.md), [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md).

### Q-UI-1092 · The rows a mirror pass filled are rendered from answers changed in the browser

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a row of a remote's list that a mirror pass filled was not in the render set (W-24, section 12 C of the plan). Such rows
differ from a client's: many at once, a version count in the hundreds, the pass's time on every row, the size of an index stored in
part (the two default platforms, Q-OCI-223), and 0 downloads where no client fetched (R-API-065, R-API-081). No pass runs on the render
stack. The walk `storedMirror` already renders a mirror's settings by changing the repository's answer in the browser.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The list's answers changed in the browser: each row and version shaped as the server answers one of the format's seeded repository (`platform/image-cache`, the long Debian key), with the values a pass leaves (chosen) | A walk, `mirrorFilled` of [mirror.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/mirror.ts) | No seed time; any data a pass can leave (214 tags, long tags, a size not known); a member the server adds to a row comes along, since the shape is read from the server | The rows are not stored: what the server would list after a real pass is the integration tests' (`mirror`, `packages`), not the picture's |
| (b) A real pass of a mirror of the installation's own `image-source`, as `image-cache` pulls through it | The seed stores a remote in mode mirror with a bound and runs a pass | The rows are the server's | A pass needs the mirror's queue, its schedule and a bound; a Debian mirror needs a signed upstream of the installation that its keyring trusts; the seed waits for the pass and every worktree's seed pays it; the rows hold only what the seed pushed (two tags, short names) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the screen is a list whose cells are what a pass leaves; the shape is read from the server at the walk's
time, so a routed row cannot drift from a real one's members, and the data that shows what a filled row does to the layout (a long tag
beside a partial size, a count of three digits) costs nothing. The development agent would revisit (b) if a pass of the profile ended in
seconds for both formats.

**Applied in the spec:** R-API-081 (rendered). Code: [mirror.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/mirror.ts) (`passRows`, `mirrorFilled`),
[screens.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/screens.ts) (`repository-oci-mirror-filled`, `repository-deb-mirror-filled`, as the plain user).
Docs: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen).

**Kept in step 2026-11-25** with the list by content (Q-API-432, Q-UI-1130): the opened image read its ten tags in an order the server
never gives (`stable` and `latest` between versions, 1.27.1 before 1.27.2). The walk now reads its template version as the opened item
does (`group=content`), answers one entry per image with the image's other tags as `aliases` in the tag order of R-OCI-031 (a release,
then its variants by their names in reverse; the tags that are no versions after the versions), and every tag its own entry where a
request asks without `group`.

### Q-UI-1160 · A limit an account would lift offers one to each reader where that reader adds it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Supersedes
[Q-UI-1104](#q-ui-1104--the-limits-sentence-offers-no-account-the-presets-do-not-say-which-upstream-an-account-lifts), whose option (b)
it is.

Context: the owner's wish of 2026-11-25 to give the upstream registries accounts from Secrets
([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) Q-REPO-483) came the morning Docker Hub's limit without an account held a
download queue for hours. Q-UI-1104 had left the remedy unsaid because no preset said which upstream an account lifts.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No sentence (Q-UI-1104) | | No vendor's terms | The remedy stays unsaid (H-1884) |
| (b) A preset fact `AccountRaisesLimit`, true for Docker Hub alone, no number; the server answers `accountRaisesLimit` where the remote sends no credential; the sentence after the limit's, by who reads it (chosen) | A fact of the format, an addition of the frozen contract ([decisions.md](../decisions.md) ADR-281) | The remedy where it applies, and where this reader applies it | The fact follows the vendor's terms; a number would age, so none is kept: the upstream's own limit headers are in **Technical details** |
| (c) A sentence for every remote without a credential | | Small | Wrong for an upstream that limits everyone alike |

**Choice:** (b). The sentences, English and German (Sie), after the limit's sentence on the tab Downloads:

| Who reads it | Sentence |
|---|---|
| A holder of `repositories:write-config`, a repository of the project `upstream` | "Docker Hub allows more requests with an account. This registry has none: add one on its page, or in the Helm values (secrets.upstreamAccounts)." and the link **Add an account** to the registry's page in the admin area |
| The writer of a project's own remote (`repositories:write-config` or the project's Owner) | "Docker Hub allows more requests with an account. This repository has none: add one in the repository's settings under Upstream." |
| Any other reader of a repository of the project `upstream` | "Docker Hub allows more requests with an account; an administrator of Quader can add one." |
| Any other reader of a project's remote | "Docker Hub allows more requests with an account; an Owner of the project can add one." |

The registry's page says "Docker Hub allows more requests with an account." while it has none (R-UI-188). The top bar's downloads panel
says nothing of it: its line leads to the tab. **Rationale:** the person who meets the limit learns the remedy and who applies it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-188; [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-012 (`accountRaisesLimit`), R-CUR-018, H-1884;
[repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073. Code:

### Q-UI-1170 · The render checks see overlays and clipping as a person does, correcting Q-UI-1060

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
Corrects [Q-UI-1060](#q-ui-1060--what-a-layout-check-can-hold-of-the-render-sets-blind-spots-and-what-stays-to-the-eye) in three points.

Context: a reading of the layout defects found by eye from 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-25 (the owner's objections, the plan's W-items, the
commits that repaired them) against what the checks of [layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts) measure. Three of its shapes had no
check: W-12's person-search list, 24 rem wide inside a drawer of 21 rem (2026-11-18); a part of a line of facts that wrapped inside
itself and lost its first letters under the clip that hides each line's first dot, "ov 18, 2026" (3d3fd6618, 2026-11-19); a separating
dot at the start of a line, "· found 1 hour ago" (4c4486c62, 2026-11-23). `sideways` measured the regions of `main` alone, and the
render grew the window by the panel's hidden length while a dialog's height is capped at the window's and a drawer is the window's
height, so an overlay was measured and pictured in a window no person has. The record also contradicts Q-UI-1060 in three points:

| Q-UI-1060 said | The record shows | Now |
|---|---|---|
| A control beside a framed box: no such defect seen | One was seen on 2026-11-19: the copy button joined to a field, 46 px beside a field of 32 (W-23), for which `joined` was built (10a28fbda) | Held for the address field by `joined`; the general rule `on-box` was measured over the whole render set and is not built (below) |
| Text drawn by CSS has no node and cannot be measured | `nameBox` has measured a stacked cell's `td[data-label]::before` through a span in its place since 2026-11-19, and two defects of that shape were seen ("Ended" half a line high, Q-UI-762; "Veröffentli" / "cht", Q-UI-1068) | Measurable by the same substitution: `separator-start` measures the separators drawn by CSS so |
| A text cut at the start of a wrapped line: no defect seen | One was seen on 2026-11-19 ("ov 18, 2026"), a kindred separator on 2026-11-23 | The checks `cut` and `separator-start` |

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Three checks in `layoutFindings`: `overlay-out` (an overlay inside the window, its content inside the overlay), `sideways` also for a region inside a dialog, a drawer or a pane of the overlay container from 1,024 px, `cut` (a line of a text past the box of its nearest ancestor that cuts sideways) and `separator-start` (a separator drawn before its item at the start of a line), with a lint rule that keeps the separators drawn by CSS to the forms the check knows; `on-box` measured, not built (chosen) | One walk over every element's style per measured picture; a fixture per defect in three engines; `make ui-states` measures the overlays by the same function | Each shape that was seen gets the check of its fixture; the dialogs' states without the stack are held by the same checks | Every new finding on a real screen is repaired or allowed by its place |
| (b) The overlay checks only; the cut and the separator stay to the eye | | Fewer checks | Both shapes were seen, and the look of rule 11 missed them before a person did |
| (c) (a) and a general `on-box` check | | The framed box held too | Its first run counted 479 cases as known layouts (W-23); no second defect seen |
| (d) Q-UI-1060 as it was | | Nothing to build | Three of its reasons are contradicted by the record |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the reading of 2026-11-23 set that a check follows a seen defect; all three shapes were seen, and each
check comes with the fixture of the defect it holds. `on-box` was measured once over the whole English render set, as the plan of the
package asked: 576 pairs of a control and a framed box in 3,478 measured pictures, 18 that the rule would flag, in three places: the copy button that stands on the top of a one-line code block in a guide and in the backups' manual run (13; 6 to 7 px above the block's middle, the form Q-UI-724 sets for a block of any length), and the Add button beside an open person-search list (5), which the search for a framed box took for one; no defect. It is built when a second defect of the shape is seen. What stays to the eye: an overlay over a control of the
page (overlap is the overlay's design), a colour (the pale tooltip in dark), the letter of a project's mark and a code window's line
numbers drawn by CSS (nothing seen wrong), the distribution of room between columns, and an offset of 1 px or less (R-UI-175's
threshold). The first run of the whole English set with the checks found one shape on real screens: `separator-start` found the breadcrumb's slash at the start of its second line at 390 px (Set up client, a repository's Details), repaired by [Q-UI-1173](#q-ui-1173--a-breadcrumbs-separator-ends-the-step-before-it); `overlay-out` and `cut` found nothing, and no place is allowed by a list. The same run measured the cost: replacing each separator by its span one at a time cost two layouts each, about 4 s per picture of the downloads panel and 0.5 s of the findings, so all are replaced at once (about 60 ms and 25 ms now); the new checks cost about 16 s of the whole set on the development machine. It also found the jobs list's Result empty for a job that runs (`empty-cell`, R-UI-146, whenever a job ran at the picture's moment): it shows the dash now. Closes H-1912 of this page.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-171 (`separator-start`), R-UI-173 (`overlay-out`, `sideways` in an overlay, `cut`). Code:
[layout.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout.ts), [separator-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/separator-rule.mjs). Tests:
[layout-checks.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/layout-checks.spec.ts), `lint-rules.test.mjs`, the harness's case of
[states.states.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/testing/states.states.spec.ts). Docs: [web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen).

### Q-UI-1171 · A state with an open overlay is pictured and measured in the window a person has

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the render grows the window by what the content panel hides, so that a picture shows a page's whole length. A dialog is at
most the window's height less 2 rem (`_dialog.scss`), its body scrolls; a drawer is the window's height (`100dvh`, `drawer.ts`); a
menu and a tooltip are placed against the window's edges. In a window grown to the page's length a dialog's body stood whole, a drawer
was as long as the page, and a menu had room below it that no window has.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The window does not grow while a pane of the overlay container holds content; that state's picture and its measurement are the window's first size (chosen) | One look at the overlay container per picture | The picture is what a person sees; `overlay-out` measures against the window an overlay is placed in; smaller pictures | The page below the window is not in that state's picture; it is in the picture of the state before |
| (b) Grow as before, and measure the overlays in a second pass in the first window | | The page's whole length in every picture | Two measurements per picture; a picture of a dialog that no window shows |
| (c) Close the overlay before growing | | | The state is gone |

**Choice:** (a). The page behind an overlay is the screen's own state, taken before the overlay opens, at every width.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-173. Code: `shoot` of [render.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/render.spec.ts). Docs:
[web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#renders-of-every-screen).

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-25** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the check `separator-start` found the slash of the breadcrumb bar at the start of its second line at 390 px: "Projects /
platform / Repositories / collections" over "/ Set up client" (Set up client, a repository's Details). The separator was the `::before`
of each step after the first (`li + li::before`), so the step that wrapped took its slash along. The same form drew the slash of the
browse view's path and the chevron of an upstream level's trail.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The separator is the `::after` of every step but the last (`li:not(:last-child)::after`), as the folder path already draws it; a wrapped line ends with the separator and starts with a step (chosen) | Three rules of the stylesheets | No line starts with a separator, whatever wraps; one form for every separator drawn after its item, which the lint rule allows | A line ends with a slash |
| (b) The clip of `.dot-separated`: each step carries its separator in front, the bar starts the separator's width further left and its clip hides each line's first one | | One form for every separator | A clip on the bar that holds the focus ring of a link; more CSS for a bar of links |
| (c) Keep `li + li::before` and allow the finding | | | A line that starts with a slash reads as a path of its own |

2026-11-25). The server's answer now carries `verdict`
([Q-REPO-488](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-488--the-upstream-tests-answer-carries-its-verdict)); what the screens still need is its
sentence and how it stands.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One table in `upstream-test-words.ts`: a sentence and a tone per verdict, `ok` (green, check), `info` (neutral, info), `warn` (warning) and `error` (chosen) | Every screen of the test reads it | One place; the registry that asks for a login without an account is neither green nor a warning | Four tones where there were two |
| (b) Green or warning, as before | Two tones | Simple | `login_asked` is neither a success to be green about (nothing was judged) nor a warning (nothing is wrong) |

**Choice:** (a). `accepted` and `answered` are `ok`; `login_asked` is `info`; `credential_withheld`, `login_required` and
`token_service_denied` are `warn` (the upstream answers, a setting keeps it from working as meant); every other verdict is `error`.
Green stays for a positive status only.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-082. Code: `upstreamVerdictText` and `upstreamVerdictTone` of
[upstream-test-words.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream-test-words.ts). Tests: `upstream-registry.spec.ts` (the owner's
case: an accepted account at a token registry, and the same registry without one), `upstream-settings.spec.ts`.

### Q-UI-1226 · A test's result shows what it learned, in one shared component with Copy report

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner, 2026-11-25, at **Admin area › Upstream registries › Docker Hub**: one line with a warning sign and nothing else,
"eine Fehlermeldung ohne technische Details, was mich und dich überhaupt nicht weiter bringt." His rule of the same morning, R-UI-216,
is that a failure shows every fact of its answer. The registry's page showed the sentence and, for some errors, the server's text
folded; the repository's settings showed the status, the credentials, the token service, the duration and the certificate in a list of
its own. The answer now names what it asked and what came back
([Q-REPO-489](repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-489--the-upstream-tests-answer-names-what-it-asked-and-what-came-back)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One component, `quader-upstream-test-result`, for every place that tests an upstream: the verdict, the facts without a click, the upstream's error answer folded, **Copy report**; the same facts for a success (chosen) | The three places (a remote's settings, the creation flow, an upstream registry) show one form | One place to change; a person who tests a connection sees what was tested, also when it passed | The settings page's own list goes |
| (b) The error notice of R-UI-216 for a failed test, the old list for a success | Reuses the notice | — | A test that answered is no failed call: its status is `200`, and the notice's facts (the call, the request ID) are the call's, not the upstream's |
| (c) Each screen extends its own markup | No new component | — | Three copies, the defect's cause |

**Choice:** (a). The facts, each only where the answer has it, in this order: **Address asked** (`probeUrl`); **HTTP status** with its
reason phrase and what it means here ("401 Unauthorized, the registry asks for a login at its token service, as it does before every
login"; a 404 "the upstream has nothing at this address: check the address and the format"), or **No answer**; **Credential sent**
(None, Username and password, Bearer token: never a value); **Token service** with how the test reached it (the upstream's own host,
or "allowed by the further host <pattern>") and whether it receives the credential; **Login address** and **Service** of the challenge;
**Login**, the token service's status with what it said about the account, or why it was not asked; **Duration**; **Certificate** with
its end; **Outbound proxy** and **Source address**; for an error the **Reason** in words, its **Code** and the **Server's message**
(English, `lang="en" translate="no"`, R-UI-216); the **Time**. The upstream's own error answer (`body`) is folded under Technical
details as text, never as markup, with its media type and size. **Copy report** copies the sentence, every fact, the time in the
reader's form and in UTC, and the answer's text. A screen projects what belongs to it under the sentence (**Allow <host>**, Q-UI-346).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-082, R-UI-216. Code: [upstream-test-result.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream-test-result.ts),
the facts and the report in [upstream-test-report.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/upstream-test-report.ts), used by
`upstream-settings.ts` and `upstream-registry.html`. Tests: `upstream-test-result.spec.ts` (four cases, about 0.15 s: thirteen answers
from an anonymous `200` to the egress refusal with their tones, sentences and facts; the rendered result and its report; an error answer
folded as text; the server's sentence marked English), `upstream-registry.spec.ts` (the owner's case), `upstream-settings.spec.ts`; the
six states of `upstream-test-result.states.spec.ts` (`make ui-states`, about 6 s) and the render walk `upstream-registry-tests` in
English and German.

### Q-UI-1228 · Every place that tests something, and the form of its result

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's rule that a decision at one place holds for every place (2026-11-19) applied to Q-UI-1226: every "Test …" of the UI
that shows a result was looked up (2026-11-25) and given the form, or recorded with why it has it already.

| Place | What the server answers | What it showed | What it shows now |
|---|---|---|---|

| **New … repository**, class Remote › **Test connection** (the same component) | The same | The same | The shared result |
| **Admin area › Upstream registries › <registry>** › **Account** › **Test connection** (`upstream-registry.html`) | `UpstreamTestResult` of `POST …/upstream-test` (saved) or `…/upstream-tests` (typed) | One sentence from its own rule, the reason, the server's text folded | The shared result |
| **Admin area › Upstream registries › Registries of this installation** (`registry-presets.ts`) | No test: a preset holds no credential and is tested where it is used, in the creation form | — | Unchanged |
| **Admin area › Settings › Storage** › **Test link** (`storage-settings.html`) | `DownloadLinkTest`: a signed link and the `curl` command; the test is the person's fetch | The link and the command; a refusal in the error notice | Unchanged: its failure is the error notice of R-UI-216 already |
| **Admin area › CI › <issuer>** › **Keys** › **Refresh keys** (`issuer-keys.ts`) | `CiKeyStatus` with the line `lastError` | The sentence, the line folded | The line's facts without a click (Q-UI-1227) |
| **Admin area › CI** (`issuer-list.ts`) | The same line per issuer | The sentence | Unchanged, a compact row (H-2001) |
| **CI › Test with claims** › **Evaluate** (`claim-tester.ts`) | `CiEvaluateResult`: every mapping looked at, each condition with expected and actual, the grants, the token | All of it | Unchanged: it shows every fact |
| An endpoint's exposure rule, the preview (`exposure-rule-editor.ts`) | `ExposureCheck`: the verdict, its reason, the rule, the warnings | All of it, in words | Unchanged |
| A permission policy, **Validate** (`policy-editor.ts`) | `PolicyValidation`: problems, warnings, the repositories it covers | All of it | Unchanged |
| **Admin area › System › Storage** › a damaged blob › **Check again** (`storage-page.html`) | `DamagedBlobRecheck`: the copies after the reads | The copies' states | Unchanged |

No place of the UI tests an OIDC provider, a Bastion (`/api/v1/bastion/check` is the Bastion's own call) or a notification: none
exists.

**Choice:** the table. One component serves the three places of the upstream test; the others answer with every fact already, or
with the error notice of R-UI-216, and get no component of their own: a shared test result for answers of other shapes would only wrap
their lists.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-082, R-UI-216.

### Q-UI-1213 · A value in running text is one code that moves whole to the next line while it fits on one

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Found on the
upstream registry's page at 390 px, English and German: "The credential is sent to auth.docker.io and registry-" / "1.docker.io." The
sentence was one string with the hosts joined into it, so the browser broke it where it may break any text, at a hyphen. A Secret's
name on the same page had been held whole that day by a rule of its own (`.secret-name { white-space: nowrap }`, Q-UI-1161), which
would run a name longer than the line out of the page.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The one mark of a value in running text is the one the templates use most already, `<code translate="no">`; `main.scss` sets it as its own box (`display: inline-block; max-inline-size: 100%; overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so it moves to the next line whole while it fits on one and breaks inside itself only where it is longer than the line; a sentence the code builds with a value is split at it (`aroundValue` of `shared/value-list.ts`) and a list of values is one element (`<quader-value-list>`, the reader's language's "a, b and c"); the Secret's own rule goes (chosen) | One rule for some 130 values of the templates at once; the sentences that held a value as plain text mark it | Exact: a value never breaks while it fits, never runs out of its box; the translation keeps its sentence, the value's place in it moving with the language | A value that stood in the sans face (a host, a package's name in a sentence) now stands in the monospace one |
| (b) `white-space: nowrap` on each value | As the Secret's name | Short | A value longer than the line runs out of its box; a rule per place |
| (c) Non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in the value | Text changed | No markup | A copied host is not the host; a search does not find it |

**Choice:** (a). A value that carries its own places to break, a Debian key's fingerprint grouped by fours, stays inline text, so it
breaks between its groups and its copy button follows its last line (`deb-signing-keys.ts`; the render check `off-line` found the button
beside the box's two lines at 390 px). A lint rule is not added: whether an interpolation of a template or a `$localize` placeholder is a value (a host, a
key) or a word (a display name) cannot be told exactly from the source. The sentences converted: the credential's hosts of a remote's
upstream and of an upstream registry's account, the hosts of **Enter the account again**, a well-known repository's key, a policy's

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-171. Code: [main.scss](../../web/src/styles/main.scss), [value-list.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/value-list.ts).

### Q-UI-1219 · A sentence that names the reader or a kind of caller is a unit of its own

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Found by the
