same class, read across the screens: the profile's **Which limit applies** put the word "you" ("Sie") into "the rule for … applies"
(right in German by chance, "für Sie"); the explanation's steps and a budget's rule put a list's label into a sentence, "the rule for
Every signed-in user applies", and the budget lowered it to fit, "für alle angemeldeten benutzer" in German; and a budget's rule was
one phrase put into two sentences, "Ihre Limits stammen aus der Regel …" and "Es gilt: der Regel …", the second in the wrong case.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A sentence that names the reader is a unit of its own ("Started by you" / "Gestartet von Ihnen", "no rule for you" / "keine Regel für Sie"), and a fact's value for the reader after "Started by" one of its own ("You" / "Ihnen"); a kind of caller in a sentence is a phrase of its own ("every signed-in user" / "alle angemeldeten Benutzer", `everyPhrase`); a phrase that two sentences need in two cases is written into each (`usage.rule.own-*`, `usage.rule.applies-*`) (chosen) | The German of each sentence written whole | The case, the capital and the pronoun are the translator's, in the sentence they stand in; `requests.asked-by-you` ("von Ihnen beantragt") had this form already | More units |
| (b) A word per case ("Sie", "Ihnen", "Ihrer") chosen by the code | Grammar in the code | Fewer units | The code would know German's cases; another language its own |
| (c) Keep the words, lower-case them in English | The capital fixed in English | Small | German stays wrong |

**Choice:** (a). A rule in `check-rules.mjs` or `i18n-check.mjs` is not added: whether a unit's text reaches another unit's sentence is a
flow of values through the code, which a search of the sources cannot follow exactly; the glossary states the rule for whoever writes a
sentence ([GLOSSARY.md](../../web/src/locale/GLOSSARY.md)). **Applied in the spec:** R-CUR-018 (the bulk's head and a row's facts),
R-UI-184 and R-UI-185 (the steps and a budget's rule). Code: `starterText`, `startedBySelf` of
[remote-downloads.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.ts), `stepText` of
[limit-explain.ts](../../web/src/app/features/usage/limit-explain.ts), `ruleSentence` of
[usage-budgets.ts](../../web/src/app/features/usage/usage-budgets.ts), `everyPhrase` of [callers.ts](../../web/src/app/features/limits/callers.ts).
Tests: `R-UI-184 names the steps and links a token to its account` of [usage.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/usage/usage.spec.ts) and
the bulk's line of [remote-downloads.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/downloads/remote-downloads.spec.ts) (unit,

answers the bulk whose rows run as started by the reader and the expanding one as started by another person).

### Q-UI-1216 · A list others write is read every 30 s, and a measured call is one that answered

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The gap
H-1871 of 2026-11-25: in the measurement of an open tab ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#what-an-open-tab-asks-of-the-server-measured))
the audit log (every 30 s) and the security dashboard's findings (every 60 s) sent no read during 60 and 75 s of a seen tab. Traced the
same day with marks in `live` and `PagedResource.refresh`: both lists did read at their interval and the answers arrived and replaced the
rows; the measurement counted a call by Playwright's `requestfinished` only, and Angular's fetch backend (`withFetch()`) aborts a request
when the client unsubscribes after its answer, which the browser reports as `net::ERR_ABORTED` for an answer it has not marked finished
yet. The two answers were the largest of the measured lists (a page of 100 events, 49 KB; 50 findings, 14 KB), so only they fell to the
race. What did hold: the findings were read every minute, the interval of a summary, though a scan or a sync of another changes them.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The findings at the slow interval (30 s) as the audit log, by the rule that a list of events or findings others write never waits longer; the measurement counts a call that has an answer whether the browser reports it finished or aborted (chosen) | One interval, one count | R-UI-213 for every list alike; the measurement shows what the server answered | Two reads a minute of the findings' first page where it was one |
| (b) Keep the minute for the findings | — | Half the reads | A new finding stays unseen for up to a minute on the page that exists to show it |
| (c) Make the client not abort an answered request | A client of its own around `fetch` | The browser's log is clean | Angular's backend is the one of every request; the abort of an answered request costs nothing |

**Choice:** (a). The measurement of 2026-11-25 with the count: the audit log reads `GET /api/v1/audit/events` twice a minute (97 KiB a
minute seen, nothing hidden, at once when seen again), the security dashboard its findings twice a minute (29 KiB a minute). **Applied in
the spec:** R-UI-213. Code: [vulnerability-report.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.ts),
[live-cost.spec.ts](../../web/e2e/renders/live-cost.spec.ts). Tests: `R-UI-213 the findings are read again every 30 s` of
[vulnerability-report.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-report.spec.ts) and R-UI-213's case of
[audit-log.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/audit/audit-log.spec.ts) (unit, fake clock, milliseconds).

### Q-UI-1229 · The spinner is the mark: three rows of six stones, lit clockwise in sandstone

Status: **The owner's choice** (2026-11-25, of four candidates shown to him: "Quader spinner sieht gut aus, aber bitte 3 reihen Steine und
damit viereckig."); the details below are the development agent's. R-UI-217.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The mark itself, `quader-mark.svg`'s square of three rows, six stones from `mark-geometry.ts`; at rest a quiet neutral of its own token, one stone after another lit in the mark's sandstone, clockwise from the top left, a round in 1.8 s; inline SVG, sizes 16 px (a line, a button) and 48 px (a page) (chosen) | One geometry, the brand's | The owner's pick; the spinner cannot drift from the mark, which `brand-logo.mjs` writes; whole pixels at 16 and 48 px | Sandstone near the warning's amber (`#995715` / `#d99530` beside `#b4690e` / `#e9a13b`) |
| (b) The candidate of two rows | — | — | Refused by the owner: not square |
| (c) A ring or the font's `autorenew` turned | The platform's look | Familiar | Not the owner's pick |

**Choice:** (a). The resting tone `--quader-spinner-stone` is `#c9c8cd` in the light scheme and `#5c5b62` in the dark one: grey of no hue,
lighter than the muted text and darker than the hairline, so it reads on the page, a dialog, a card, the frame and a disabled button and
is no text; the lit stone and its trail are the mark's sandstone, which moves, while a warning's amber is a badge with an icon and a word
that stands still: in the render walk's picture `loading-states-package` the spinner stands two rows above the badge **Blocked**; the two
share a hue, and are told apart by their form (a square of grey stones with one lit, a pill with an icon and a word) and by the movement;
the resting tone was kept grey for that reason, not tinted.
40 px of the brief would put the stones on half pixels (a stone 10 px, a joint 2.5): 48 px keeps them whole (12 and 3). Still (a picture,
no animation), the first stone is lit. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-217. Code: [spinner.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/spinner.ts),
[_spinner.scss](../../web/src/styles/_spinner.scss), `--quader-spinner-stone` of [_tokens.scss](../../web/src/styles/_tokens.scss).

### Q-UI-1240 · The panel of a version's commands is a tab per client and Set up client at the row's end

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25** (the tabs, their order and **Set up client** at the row's end); the details below were
**decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews them at the walkthrough. The owner's words, at
an image's **Pull**: "der pull-hover soll mit einem Reiter ausgestattet sein, links docker, rechts daneben podman, dann platz und daneben
ein button set up client, der einen weiterleitet." His rule: what he decides at one format holds for every format and every place that
shows the same thing.

Context: the panel of Q-UI-1066 was a section per client, each headed by the client's long name ("Docker CLI (with Buildx)"), all
commands at once; **Set up client** was in the box of the version's page only.

**The tab's words.**

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The client's long name (`Yarn Berry (2 and later)`, `.NET CLI (dotnet)`) | The setup's words | One name everywhere | npm's four tabs and the button need about 540 px, a panel at 390 px has 334 |
| (b) A short name of its own per client, a product name: Docker, Podman; npm, pnpm, Yarn Berry, Yarn Classic; .NET CLI, NuGet CLI, Visual Studio; APT, ansible-galaxy, curl (chosen) | `tab` of [clients.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/clients.ts) | npm's four tabs fit 390 px; the long name stays the field's accessible name ("Command for Yarn Berry (2 and later)") and the setup's | A second name per client |

**Where the button goes where the row is narrow.**

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) It wraps to a line of its own under the tabs, at its end (chosen) | The row is a flex row that wraps; the strip is as wide as its tabs and grows to the button | The tabs never scroll where they fit alone; the button keeps its place at the end | Two lines at 390 px for npm and NuGet |
| (b) The strip scrolls and the button stays on the row | The strip's fades | One line | A tab of four hidden behind a fade on a phone |
| (c) The button below the command | — | One line of tabs | The owner placed it on the tabs' row |

**Every command at once or the chosen one.** (a) Every client's command is asked when the panel opens and kept in the panel, the
ones not chosen hidden and inert, so the panel is as wide as the longest and switching tabs moves nothing (chosen; the request count of
Q-UI-1066 stays: two for OCI, three for NuGet, four for npm); (b) only the chosen tab's: one request at a time, a panel that changes
its width at every tab. The product's tabs (`<quader-tab-group>`, `@angular/aria`'s tabs pattern, the arrow keys) carry it: they got
`keepAll`, `compact` and a slot `tabsEnd` for the action, no second tabs component.

**The chosen tab** is kept while the button stands: the panel opens again on the client last chosen; a new page starts at the first.

**A format of one client** shows no strip of one tab: the client's short name is the row's label, on the hairline a strip stands on.

**Choice:** as marked. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-009, R-UI-052, R-UI-111, Q-UI-1066. Code:
[client-command-menu.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.ts), [tabs.ts](../../web/src/app/shared/ui/tabs.ts),

[client-command-menu.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/client-command-menu.spec.ts) (the tabs, the setup per tab, the tab
kept, one client), [repository-content.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-content.spec.ts) (OCI's two
tabs, npm's four), the journey `08-packages`; rendered `repository-*-menu` with the last tab chosen, every format, English and German.

### Q-UI-1241 · A version's page has its command behind the verb's button in its head; the box is gone

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25** (the box goes, the command is behind a button as an image's **Pull**, for every format);
the details below were **decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews them at the
walkthrough. The owner's words, at `community.docker 5.4.1`: "ich finde der eingerahmte Platz ist verschwendet, dieses Feld, in dem die
Installation der Collection beschreiben ist, gehört hinter einen Button wie bei docker image 'pull' mit einer hover-maske. Du musst dir
solche Angaben von mir echt selbstständig merken und auch auf andere Registries anwenden."

**Where the button stands.** (a) In the page's head at the right, where a page's acts stand (the repository page's **Set up client**,
**Settings**), the same button and panel as a list's row (chosen); (b) under the facts, before the tabs: a button alone on a line,
the space the owner called wasted.

**The repository picker** of a version in several repositories: (a) a select **Repository** at the panel's top, above the tabs; the
command and **Set up client** follow it (chosen; its label and its value read as one line); (b) a select after the tabs: the reader
picks a client, then the place, while the place decides every command.

**Where no command is offered** (no command that would fail, Q-UI-965, Q-UI-896 to Q-UI-899, R-UI-194):

| Case | Option chosen | The other weighed |
|---|---|---|
| Held only by disabled repositories | No button; the sentence ("The repository web/npm-local is disabled: nobody can install this version until it is enabled again.") as a muted line under the facts | A button whose panel says only that: a click to learn that nothing can be done |
| Held only by system repositories of `upstream` | No button; the sentence of Q-UI-899 under the facts | The same |
| The ClamAV definitions while their updates are on | **Set up client** with freshclam in the head, the sentence "A ClamAV installation always takes the version in use…" under the facts | A button **Install** with a panel of that sentence: there is no command per version |
| A format without clients | Nothing; no format has none today | The old sentence "There are no install instructions for this package type yet.", which no format can show |

**Other places that showed a command in a box or a field of its own** (looked for on 2026-11-25): the version's page was the only one;
a package's page, a search hit, an image's tag page (its version page) had none, and the files of a generic repository show a file's
download address, not a client's command.

**Choice:** as marked. **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-009, R-UI-111. Code: [version-command.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-command.ts)
(what the head offers, which repositories, the notes; the install panel's rules moved there), the head of
[package-version.html](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.html); `install-panel.*` and `install-command.*` are gone.
Tests: [version-command.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/version-command.spec.ts) (the repositories and their order, the

### Q-UI-1242 · A package's address is its newest version where its format leads with its documentation; its table is `…/-/versions`

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25** (a collection's name, and an npm and a NuGet package's, leads to its newest version's
documentation, R-UI-218); the addresses were **decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews
them at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The package's own address is the newest version's page; the table moves to `…/{name…}/-/versions` (chosen) | One route for the name, chosen by the format's shape | Every link by name leads there without knowing the newest version (the breadcrumb, a search suggestion, a dependency, Recently opened); the address reads as Galaxy's collection page does, always the newest | Two addresses show the newest version (the package's and its `@version`) |
| (b) Every link to a name carries the newest version (`name@5.4.1`), the package's address stays the table | — | One address per page | Every place that links a name must know the newest version; the breadcrumb has no way to; a bookmark of the package stays on a version |
| (c) The table behind a query (`?view=versions`) | — | No new route | Not an address of its own |

`-` is a segment no package name of those formats holds (npm and NuGet names and Ansible's `namespace.name` hold at most one slash,
an npm scope's, which starts with `@`); for OCI, Debian and generic files `…/-/versions` is no route, their table keeps the package's
address. The breadcrumb of the table is Packages › the package › **Versions**. No address is kept for the old table of a collection
(pre-alpha, no redirects).

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-218, R-UI-110, R-UI-111, R-UI-052. Code:
[packages.routes.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/packages.routes.ts) (`versionsMatcher`, the `canMatch` of the shape),

[package-links.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-links.ts). Tests: [app.routes.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/app.routes.spec.ts).

### Q-UI-1245 · A version without documentation opens on its first tab with content, and its README tab says so

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The owner's
rule is per package, by what is there ("wenn die dafür notwendigen Metainformationen vorhanden sind").

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The name opens the newest version's page all the same, on its first tab with content; the README tab stays and says "This version has no README to show." (chosen) | One kind of page per format | A name always leads to the same kind of page within a format; the reader sees at once that there is nothing to read, and why the page did not open on it | A tab whose content is one sentence |
| (b) A package whose newest version has no README opens on its table | The format's old page | — | The page a name opens changes with a version's content; the head has no switch there |
| (c) No README tab where there is none | As before | No empty tab | The documentation's place says nothing; the reader wonders where it is |

The sentence says "to show", not "carries none": a caller who may not read the repository's wiki is told no README exists (R-UI-057,
Q-UI-244), so the page must not claim more than it was told. A NuGet package's description in the nuspec is not a document to read:
the README is the file the nuspec names. A collection without documentation (a role archive) has no Documentation tab and opens on its
first tab, as before.

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-218, R-UI-111. Code: `firstTab` and the tab list of
[package-version.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.ts). Tests:
[package-version.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/features/packages/package-version.spec.ts) (opens on Files, the tab's sentence, no README
asked), the journey `21-visibility`.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

### Q-UI-1310 · The inventory of 2026-11-26: what still differed between the formats, and what G3 closed

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
W-30 G3. The plan was written before six packages landed; the builder rendered the tab Details and the table of versions of every
format on the main of 2026-11-26 (`package-version-*-details`, `package-*-facts*`, a package of each format with every block filled)
and put them side by side. What differed then, and what holds now:

| Property | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Links | a block **Links** in Details, at another place per format (after the image's facts for OCI, after the description for Debian); NuGet's licence address a row "License" | one row under the facts line in every format; the licence's address is the licence's link |
| Keywords and tags | npm's and NuGet's not on the version page (only "Keywords" as text in the package table's closed Details); Ansible's "Tags" as text in Package details, the package's newest version's, not the version's | chips under **Keywords** in npm, NuGet and Ansible Galaxy, the version's own (`keywords` of R-API-029) |
| Dependencies | npm four two-column lists with bold names, never linked, no bundled, no optional peer; NuGet a heading and a sub-heading per framework, two columns, never linked; Ansible two columns, unheld names small and muted; Debian a heading per field, one line per group, linked; a chart two columns with the repository under the range | one block ([Q-UI-1311](#q-ui-1311--every-formats-dependencies-are-one-block-a-group-per-kind-in-the-formats-words)) in every format |
| npm's facts | "Required runtimes" under a heading of its own; the tarball's file count, unpacked size and install script, the types and the publisher not sent | one **Package details**, with all six |
| NuGet's facts | title, licence acceptance and development dependency sent and not shown | shown |
| Debian's Installed size | "18432 KiB" | "18.0 MiB" ([Q-UI-1316](#q-ui-1316--a-size-is-said-in-the-unit-a-person-reads-wherever-it-stands)) |
| An image's date | "Published" on the version page and its package's table, "Pushed" or "Fetched" in the repository's content | "Pushed" or "Fetched" everywhere ([Q-UI-1314](#q-ui-1314--an-images-date-is-pushed-or-fetched-on-every-screen)) |
| Downloads | in no table of versions | under the last download in every one (R-UI-222) |
| An image's table | no digest | the digest under the tags |
| Install script | not shown | a note under the links |
| Upstream tab | npm "Size not told" beside an `unpackedSize`; Debian and Ansible "not analysed for vulnerabilities"; Debian's architectures as `linux/amd64` | "1.9 KiB unpacked"; the format's reason of Q-UI-1244; `amd64` |
| A role's breadcrumb | `role/16` | the role's name ([Q-UI-1317](#q-ui-1317--the-breadcrumb-names-a-package-by-its-name-where-its-address-holds-its-key)) |
| OpenAPI `metadata` | npm's members only | each format's members |

**Choice:** close every row (R-UI-221, R-UI-222). **Left, and whose:** the marks Deprecated and Unlisted in tables and the switch (the
deprecation package, R-API-085); NuGet's release notes with their line breaks, icon, licence file and symbols (W-30 G6); an image's
"Created" as its annotation writes it (W-30 G7's facts); the documentation of a package not stored yet (W-30 G2). **Applied in the
spec:** R-UI-110, R-UI-111, R-UI-221, R-UI-222, R-API-029.

### Q-UI-1336 · A command keeps its credential off the command line where the client can, and says so where it cannot

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
It applies the owner's choice for curl ([formats/generic.md](formats/generic.md) Q-GENERIC-9) to every place that shows a command with a
credential.

Context: a variable the shell expands into an argument (`-H "Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN"`, `-u quader:"$QUADER_TOKEN"`,
`--token=…`, `--api-key "…"`) puts the token into the program's arguments, which other users of the machine read in the process list and
a shell trace prints. curl's snippets hand it the credential as configuration on standard input instead (`quader_curl`, Q-GENERIC-9). A
search of the web application and of the server's snippets and guides on 2026-11-26 found the places of the table below.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One pattern for every command: curl gets its credential on standard input (`quader_curl` where the line is a request of the management API beside its JSON; `printf … \| curl --config -` or `-H @-` where a command stands alone), another client reads it from its configuration or from a variable of its environment; a client that takes a credential only as an argument keeps it there, and the page says so beside the command (chosen) | The pattern of Set up client everywhere | No token in a process list where the client allows it; where it does not, the reader knows and can run the command where nobody else is logged in | printf is a builtin of sh, bash and zsh, not of every shell; the function must be defined first |
| (b) Leave the commands as they are | — | Shorter lines | The owner's choice for curl, broken on every other page |
| (c) Show no command where the client takes a credential only as an argument | — | Nothing leaks | NuGet's push and the source commands have no other way, and a reader needs them |

**Choice:** (a). The places and what each became:

| Place | Was | Is |
|---|---|---|
| A file's **Details**, every format: "The same request with curl" | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN" <item>` | `quader_curl --fail <item>`, with a sentence naming the function |
| A package format's raw file, **Details**: "Download with curl" | `curl -L -O -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN" <file>` | `quader_curl --fail --location --output <name> <file>` |
| The repository form's and settings' "as API request" (`curlOf`) | `-H 'Authorization: Bearer $QUADER_TOKEN'` (in single quotes, which no shell expands) | `quader_curl --fail -X …`, with the sentence |
| The tab Verify of every format that Quader attests (R-SIG-056) | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${QUADER_TOKEN}"` | `printf 'header = …' "${QUADER_TOKEN}" \| curl --config -` |
| Debian: the key's download of Configure, and Publish | `curl -u quader:"${QUADER_TOKEN}"` | `printf 'user = …' quader "${QUADER_TOKEN}" \| curl --config -` |
| Ansible Galaxy: Publish | `--server <address> --token=${QUADER_TOKEN}` | `ANSIBLE_GALAXY_SERVER_QUADER_TOKEN="${QUADER_TOKEN}" ansible-galaxy collection publish … --server quader`, the server of the `ansible.cfg` snippet |
| The malware scan's settings: the upload of the signature files of an installation without internet | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${QUADER_TOKEN}" -T` | `printf … \| curl --config - -T` |
| The vulnerability sources: the upload of a mirrored database file | the same | the same |
| NuGet's guide: the push with curl, the relist, the check of the sign-in | `-H "X-NuGet-ApiKey: ${QUADER_TOKEN}"`, `curl -u any:$TOKEN` | the header from standard input (`-H @-`), the user from `--config -` |
| NuGet: `dotnet nuget add source --password`, `nuget sources add -Password`, `dotnet nuget push --api-key`, `nuget push -ApiKey`, `dotnet nuget delete --api-key` (setup, guide, the GitLab CI job of a CI identity's mapping) | the token as an argument | unchanged: **dotnet and nuget.exe take a source's password and the API key only as an argument** (neither reads them from standard input or from a variable; `setapikey` takes the key as an argument too). The page says so beside each command; for a source, the `nuget.config` snippet keeps the password in `%QUADER_TOKEN%`, and the CI job's comment says the container shows it to nobody else |
| npm's, Yarn's, the Docker CLI's, Podman's, Helm's, APT's and ansible-galaxy's configuration, curl's, wget's and PowerShell's generic snippets, ClamAV's `freshclam.conf` and script, the CI identity's exchange and revocation | — | already the pattern: a file or a variable the client reads, standard input, or a builtin's `printf` |

The token's own pages, the Bastion's pages and the CI identity's pages show no other command with a credential.

**Rationale:** one rule, whatever the format. The development agent would revisit the NuGet rows when the .NET CLI reads a credential
from the environment or standard input. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-030, R-UI-010, R-GENERIC-017; [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md)
R-ANS-025's table; code: [setup_verify.go](../../internal/api/v1/setup_verify.go), [setup_local.go](../../internal/formats/deb/setup_local.go),
[ansible/setup.go](../../internal/formats/ansible/setup.go), the NuGet guide, [mappings_snippet.go](../../internal/ci/mappings_snippet.go),
[repository-file.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-file.ts),
[repository-model.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/repository-model.ts),
[malware-settings.ts](../../web/src/app/features/settings/malware-settings.ts),
[vulnerability-sources.ts](../../web/src/app/features/vulnerabilities/vulnerability-sources.ts), the captions of
[clients.ts](../../web/src/app/features/setup/clients.ts).

### Q-API-455 · Who depends on what is one side table, written where a version's facts are written

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-API-086 asks which packages depend on a package. The dependencies are in each format's own rows (an npm manifest, NuGet's
metadata, Debian's control paragraph, an Ansible collection's map), in four shapes; a read across them by name would parse every row.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One table `package_dependencies (version_id, repo_id, name, kind, range, provides)`, written by a Go extractor per format in the transaction that writes the format's row, and by an entry of the task `remote-describe` for what was stored before (chosen) | A lookup by name; one extractor and one unit case per format | The read is one index walk; the name is matched by the format's rule once, at write time; a format adds a function | Every writer of a format's row calls it (seven places in four formats) |
| (b) The view adapters' metadata read at the read | No table | Nothing to write | Every version of a format read and parsed at every read; no index, no privacy by repository |
| (c) A trigger per format table that extracts in SQL | One mechanism in the database | No writer forgets it | Debian's relation grammar and NuGet's ID rule in PL/pgSQL; no unit case per format |

**Choice:** (a). A version whose dependencies were read is marked in `package_dependency_reads` with the extractor's version (`dependents.Reader`),
so that a version without dependencies is not read again and a changed extractor reads every version again. Both tables are derived: a
backup does not export them and the task fills them after a restore (R-BAK-004). A Helm chart's dependencies are not kept: they name a
chart and a repository address, and a chart of the same name in an OCI repository of this installation is another chart unless the
address is this installation's ([H-2221](#h-2221--a-helm-charts-dependencies-are-not-matched-to-the-charts-quader-holds)). Revisit when a
format is added whose dependencies name packages of another format. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-086. Code:
`internal/packages/dependents`, `Dependencies` of `internal/formatdata/{npm,nuget,deb,ansible}`.

### Q-API-456 · Used by lists each dependent once, by its newest version that depends, across the projects the reader may read

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The packages that depend on the package's name, each by its newest visible version that does, with that version's kinds and ranges (chosen) | Galaxy's, nuget.org's and npmjs.com's list | One read for every version of the page; the range is shown, so the reader judges it | A dependent whose range excludes the version on the page is listed |
| (b) Only those whose range holds the version on the page | "Who would install this version" | Exact for npm and NuGet | Each format's range grammar at the read (npm's, NuGet's intervals, Debian's constraints, Ansible's), per row; a different answer per version of one package |
| (c) Every version of every dependent | Complete | — | A package with 300 versions fills the list |

**Choice:** (a), and a dependent's newest visible version is a release before a pre-release, the highest key first. The read runs across
every project the reader may read, as the public registries' lists and as the rest of a version's page (its repositories are read across
projects); the operation takes `project` for a caller that wants one project's, as the package list does. A package does not use itself.
Revisit if the owner wants (b) for a format ([H-2223](#h-2223--used-by-does-not-say-whether-a-dependents-range-holds-the-version-on-the-page)).
**Applied in the spec:** R-API-086.

### Q-API-457 · A Debian package is used under the names it provides, and every alternative counts

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a Debian package depends on a virtual name (`mail-transport-agent`) that other packages provide, on `a | b`, and on `python3:any`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every alternative is a row; the architecture qualifier is dropped; a package is used under its own name and under the names its visible versions provide, one step (chosen) | APT's resolution, as far as names go | `exim4` shows who needs a mail transport agent; `python3` who asks for `python3:any` | A dependent of `a \| b` is listed under both, though it needs only one |
| (b) Only the first alternative, only the own name | — | Fewer rows | The users of a provider are missed: most of Debian's virtual packages |
| (c) (a) and the version of a versioned Provides held against the constraint | Exact | — | dpkg's version comparison per row at the read |

**Choice:** (a). Pre-Depends, Depends, Recommends, Suggests and Enhances are uses, each its own kind; Breaks, Conflicts and Replaces are not.

### Q-API-458 · A dependent the reader may not read is not read

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-30 C.4: "Used by" is not counted across repositories the reader cannot read; the brief adds that a hidden dependent must not
change the answer's time in a way a caller could measure cheaply.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The repositories the reader may read are decided first (the package list's scope); the statement walks the index `(repo_id, name)` for those alone and then applies the list's row visibility (chosen) | A hidden repository's rows are never touched | Neither the list, the count nor the time depends on them | A repository the reader may read only in part is walked whole ([H-2220](../security/search.md#h-2220--in-a-repository-read-row-by-row-the-rows-the-reader-may-not-read-are-walked)) |
| (b) An index on the name, filtered by visibility | One walk | Simple | The walk reads every dependent of the installation: the time grows with what the reader may not see |

**Choice:** (a). Measured: 5,000 dependents in a repository the reader may not read leave her read at 23 ms beside the 31 ms of a reader of
both. `whole` (the reader reads every repository of the format whole) chooses the sentence of an empty list; it says only that, and is the
same for every package. **Applied in the spec:** R-API-086. Code: `view.Service.Dependents`, `PackageViewDependents`.

### Q-API-459 · The list filters by dependsOn as by keyword, planned for its values

Status: **Decided by the development agent** on 2026-11-26 — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the package list reads every visible version (132 ms for 50,000 packages without a text); the filter must add nothing to it per

| (b) The same with the statement's cached generic plan | — | No planning | Measured: with 5,000 ids the generic plan compared every row with every id, 1.5 s per page from the sixth request on |

### Q-UI-1370 · A link to a screen whose script is gone loads its address from the server, and a failed navigation is said

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner, 2026-11-26, 08:40, of a remote's list of images in his development profile: "In dieser Übersicht kann man nicht mehr
auf die Images klicken um zu den Details des Images zu kommen. In z.B. Ansible funktioniert das." The link was there and led to the
image's page in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on the same profile, so his click was not reproduced. What was reproduced gives exactly his
picture: a screen's script is loaded when the screen is first opened, under a name that changes with every build
([R-UI-001](#r-ui-001--technology-baseline-and-delivery)); a window loaded from an earlier build asks for that build's names, and
when the server no longer answers them the router's navigation fails, the address stays and nothing is shown. A screen the window had
opened before (a collection's page) went on working, one it had not (an image's page) did not. The router had no handler for a failed
navigation at all, so a guard or a screen that threw was as silent. Where it happens: the development profile's dev server after every
build when the window missed its reload; an installation when the script of the window's release is neither on the replica nor in the
store of earlier releases' files (R-HA-020), or that store cannot be asked.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The router's handler of a failed navigation: a script that could not be loaded loads the link's address from the server; every other failure is a notice with what was said (chosen) | One place, every link of the application | The reader arrives where the link led; no click does nothing | The screen the reader left is gone from memory (an open row, a typed filter that was not in the address) |
| (b) A notice "A new version is available. Reload." | — | Nothing is lost without the reader's act | The reload R-UI-213 says nobody is asked for |
| (c) The window asks the server for its build on a timer and reloads itself | — | Also mends a screen that is open | A reload under a person who types; a poll on every window |
| (d) Nothing; the store of earlier releases' files covers an installation | — | — | The dev server and a store that cannot be asked stay silent, and so does every other failed navigation |

**Choice:** (a). `loadGoneScreen` ([gone-script.ts](../../web/src/app/core/gone-script.ts)), given to the router with
`withNavigationErrorHandler`: an error whose text is what Chromium ("Failed to fetch dynamically imported module"), Firefox ("error
loading dynamically imported module") or WebKit ("Importing a module script failed.") say of a script that did not load makes the window
load the navigation's address, with its query and fragment, from the server; the history keeps the page the reader left. A window that
has not ended a navigation yet (the router's `navigated`) was just loaded: there the script is missing on the server, the window does
not load again and shows "This screen could not be loaded, its script is missing on the server:" with the engine's sentence, which is
also what stops a loop. Every other failed navigation shows "This screen could not be opened:" with the error's text.

**Rationale:** the reader's act was a click on a link, and the least surprising answer is the page the link names; a full load costs what
opening the address in a new tab costs. The development agent would revisit it when a screen that is open has to follow a new build too
(H-2240).

### Q-UI-1490 · The audit log holds its German actions by the act's word and a shorter word where it reads right

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (W33b) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: W33's German pass of the log of one download's events found "Datei heruntergeladen" (135 px) in two lines in the action's
7.5 rem (120 px) at 1,440 px while the actor's column had 15 px no row used (the layout check `cramped`), and 8.5 rem made the log stand as
blocks at 1,024 px (Q-UI-997's budget: the time, the actor's longest word, the action, the target's project mark and the outcome's badge).
Measured in Inter at the row's 14 px and 600 (2026-11-26): 108 of the 237 actions take more lines in German than in English at 120 px and
95 at 136 px, so no width of the column holds every German name in English's lines; what a person reads most are the acts of R-OPS-056 and
the download of a file.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A row of several events names its act in one word that fits the 7.5 rem in both languages; German says "Heruntergeladen" for "File downloaded", "Bereitgestellt" for "File deployed" and "Datenschlüssel" for the act "Data keys handed", where the target beside it says the rest (chosen) | The words of the rows people read most fit; every other name wraps between its words as in English | The column keeps its width, so the log keeps five columns at 1,440 and 1,024 px; the German pass's layout checks find nothing; "Heruntergeladen" beside a file's path says what "Datei heruntergeladen" said | Many longer names of other events wrap in one line more than in English, as they did, between words and at their soft hyphens |
| (b) A width of the column per language (8.5 rem in German) | Every short German name on one line | — | The log stands as blocks at 1,024 px (W33's try) unless another column gives way |
| (c) The outcome under the action, four columns | Room for the action | Long names fit | Leaves Q-UI-997's form of the log; the outcome is read as a column |
| (d) The action's name with `white-space: nowrap` | No wrap | — | A long name makes the column as wide as itself and the log falls to blocks |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the words that stand in most rows fit, the form of the log stays, and no word breaks inside itself (the
long German words carry their soft hyphens, Q-UI-1091). The acts' words are measured: Heruntergeladen 114 px, Datenschlüssel 104,
Veröffentlicht 83, Schreiben erlaubt 107, Hochgeladen 78, Gelöscht 53, Gepusht 51.

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-037; the glossary ([GLOSSARY.md](../../web/src/locale/GLOSSARY.md)).

| (a) `?group=<first event's ID>`, the chip **Events of** with the unit's name, the caption "The events of one row", from `GET /api/v1/audit/rows/{id}/events` (chosen) | One name for every act | A push's and a delete's events are no download | — |
| (b) Keep `?download=` and **Download** | Unchanged | — | A delete's events under the chip **Download** |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the row is an act, not always a download (Q-UI-1397 holds otherwise).

**Applied in the spec:** R-UI-037.

### Q-UI-1494 · German counts a row's items as "Einträge" and a day's volume as "GB/Tag"

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A row's items are "Einträge" (an item is a file, a version's event or a decision), and the compact line of a limit profile and a rule's override say "GB/Tag" and "/Tag" (chosen) | The glossary's words | "Dateien" was wrong for a push's version and a row of writes; "day" was English in a German line | — |
| (b) Keep "Dateien" and "GB/day" | — | — | Wrong words |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-UI-037, R-UI-178; the glossary.

## What this does not cover

### H-2221 · A Helm chart's dependencies are not matched to the charts Quader holds

Stage: R-API-086, Q-API-455, OCI. A chart's `Chart.yaml` names each dependency by a chart name and a repository address (`oci://…`,
`https://…`); the chart a dependency means is the chart at that address. Only an address of this installation names a package Quader
holds, and resolving it needs the installation's base URLs at the write. Until it is built, a chart's page has no "Used by", and its
Dependencies block lists its dependencies as text. Dormant: no chart repository format exists, charts are OCI artifacts.

### H-2222 · A Debian architecture's file that goes leaves its relations with the version

Stage: R-API-086, Debian. A version's rows are those of all its files, written when a file's row is written; the removal of one
architecture's file while another stays writes nothing, so the relations of the removed file stay until the version gets a file again or
goes. Live for a version whose architectures depend on different names (rare: `Depends` differs by architecture only for a few packages).

### H-2223 · Used by does not say whether a dependent's range holds the version on the page

Stage: R-API-086, Q-API-456. Each dependent shows the range it asks for; a reader of version 1.x of a library sees an application that asks
for `^2.0.0` beside one that asks for `^1.4.0`. Deciding it needs each format's range grammar at the read. Live on every page of a package
with several majors.

### H-2224 · The worker's start asks every version of the formats whether it was read

Stage: R-API-086, the task `remote-describe`'s entry. When every version was read, the check at a worker's start walks the versions of npm,
NuGet, Debian and Ansible Galaxy by their ids to find none left: one index probe each, about 50 ms for 50,000 versions, a second for a
million. Live at every start of a worker; what makes it real is an installation with millions of versions.

### H-2240 · An open screen keeps the build its window was loaded from

A window follows a new build only when it opens a screen whose script it has not loaded and the server no longer holds
([Q-UI-1370](#q-ui-1370--a-link-to-a-screen-whose-script-is-gone-loads-its-address-from-the-server-and-a-failed-navigation-is-said)).
The screens it has loaded go on running the old build against the new server until the window is loaded again: a request the new server
answers otherwise shows as that screen's error, and a correction of a screen is not seen. Nothing compares the window's build with the
server's.

### H-2173 · A version with a mark and a signature badge puts its table into blocks at 1,024 px

Stage: the version's cell of the table of versions (R-UI-110), which keeps the version, its marks (**Pre-release**, **Deprecated**,
**Unlisted**, R-API-085) and its signature badge on one line. Subject: a package one of whose versions carries a mark and a badge (the
seed's NuGet package: "2.0.0-preview.1 Pre-release Invalid signature"). The cell's least width puts the table into blocks at 1,024 px
beside the side bar, against Q-UI-969; measured on 2026-11-26 with the downloads' line under **Last download** and without it, the same.
Live wherever signatures are checked and a version is marked. What closes it: the cell wraps between its badges, as an image's row wraps
between its tags.

### H-2172 · An image's date word follows the version's holders, not each row

Stage: `arrivedLabel` (Q-UI-1314). Subject: an image a local and a remote repository both hold, and a table whose rows are held by
different classes. The word is one per screen: Pushed where any holder is local, Fetched where all are remote, read from the version (its
page) or from the package's newest version (its table). A row of an image only a remote holds, in a table whose newest version a local
repository holds, reads Pushed. Dormant: no installation holds one image name in a local and a remote repository of one project today.

| (a) The row's act is the small button **Download** with the panel (address, clients, check), in place of the copy button of the address (chosen) | Every format's row has its verb | One look for every format's rows; the address is one click further | Copying the address takes two clicks |
| (b) The copy button stays, the panel beside it | Two controls per row | Nothing lost | A row of a file has two acts where a package's has one |
| (c) A split button per row | As the file's page | Saves the file from the list | A row of two joined buttons; the row has no content route to save from today |

**Choice:** (a). A package format's raw files keep the copy button of the address: their clients fetch packages, not paths, and an
address is no command. A row carries no
verdict of the malware scan or the signature gate (`Child`), so a refused file's row offers its panel as it offered its address, and a
client's command gets the refusal with its reason (Q-UI-882); the file's page offers no **Download** and no panel for it, and keeps its
address as a fact. **Applied in the
spec:** R-UI-010. Code: the row of [repository-files.ts](../../web/src/app/features/repositories/content/repository-files.ts).

Component: the page of the system repository `upstream/clamav` in the admin area (R-UI-194). Subject: **Address of the endpoint** and the
addresses with a client certificate are address fields with copy buttons, not freshclam's command in the panel of R-UI-218. Live while

The tree answers the changelog in every state of the documentation (R-ANS-053), but the Documentation tab draws its tree only for the
state available: a remote version whose upstream documentation is pending, unavailable or none (with `ansible.fetchDocumentation` off)
shows the state's sentence and not the changelog its cached archive holds. Live for such remote versions; the operation
`getPackageVersionDocFile` with the name `changelog` answers it.

Who may publish into a namespace is said as the project's roles and its permission policies, both links (R-UI-220); the principals a policy
grants and the owners of each package (R-AUTHZ-018) are not listed, because the effective permissions of a coordinate (R-AUTHZ-024) are not

### H-2152 · The page of a name shows the claims of the repositories whose configuration the reader may read

A `global` claim of another project's repository is in effect in this project's virtual repositories (R-REPO-023) and is not named on this
project's page of the name, since its reader may not read that repository's configuration (Q-UI-1292). The page names no claim it may not
show and counts none. Live for a reader whose virtual repositories resolve a name from another project's claim.

its own (about 40: deletes behind a confirmation, a row's menu, Run a pass now, Revoke all tokens, Export CSV). The button spins while the

### H-2051 · The rule of the spinner reads text

Stage: [busy-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/busy-rule.mjs) (Q-UI-1239). Subject: a new screen. It refuses a loading sentence by its first
word, a data table without `loadingText` and a held button without `quaderBusy`; it does not see a section that shows nothing while its

### H-2053 · The renders picture the spinner standing still

Stage: the render walk `loading-states` and `make ui-states` (R-UI-217). Subject: the travelling light, its round of 1.8 s and the

the light goes round clockwise with its trail, the mark breathes with the first stone lit), and no check measures it. Seen then too: a
change of the scheme while a spinner turns keeps the stones' colours of the scheme it started in until its load ends (Chromium resolves

during a long load.

### H-1964 · A read that fails alone while its page stands is read again only by the person or its next use

### H-1962 · A read that fails without a notice of its own is not read again with its page

Stage: the reads of a page beside its own (R-UI-216, Q-UI-1196). Subject: a page that stands while one of its other reads failed. A
read whose absence leaves something out and says nothing wrong has no notice of its own: the help's contents, the format names of the
search results, the anchors' titles and the Bastions of **Set up client**, the held dependencies of an Ansible version, the list of a
filter drawer. When it fails while the page's own read answers, nothing reads it again by itself: the page's Retry, a drawer opened
again or the page's next load does. The advisory sources' scanners and the Bastions' download-link connections come back with the
page's live read within a minute. The server's address is read again with the page's Retry; while it alone cannot be read, the offline
commands of the malware settings and the advisory sources show the placeholder host they show for an installation without an address.
Live today; real only for a failure of that one read while the rest of the page answers.

### H-1965 · The rule of a kept failure reads text, not types

Stage: the lint rule of Q-UI-1195 ([read-failure-rule.mjs](../../web/scripts/read-failure-rule.mjs)). Subject: a screen that brings a
failure to its notice by another way. The rule sees a `computed` of `.error()` through a converter, a template's conversion of
`x.error()`, and a notice or a data table whose `(retry)` clears its failure signal, in the method or in a method it calls first, before
the first `await` or `.then(`. It does not see a failure that reaches the notice through a member of another kind (a service's signal, a
`linkedSignal`), a clear in a method called after a wait, nor a read's notice that has no `(retry)` at all (which then offers no Retry
and reads nothing again, R-UI-216). Dormant: every notice of a read had its `(retry)` on 2026-11-25; real for the next screen that takes
one of these ways.

### H-1683 · The version list of a package several repositories hold, in the order of publication, reads every version, and the package list counts every version

The version list reads a page by keyset queries in the order of the format's versions, for one repository or several, and in the order
of publication for a package that one repository of the caller's scope holds (Q-API-417, Q-API-429). For a package that several
repositories hold (a name in a local repository and in a remote's cache, a virtual repository's members), in the order of publication
(`-publishedAt`), it reads the name and the creation time of every visible version, one cheap row each, and sorts them in the
service: a version's place is its oldest visible row, which a keyset over each holder cannot see without a lookup per row. The package
list reads one cheap row per visible version of the caller's scope to count the versions of each package and to find its first and last
creation; the latest version and the downloads are read for the page's packages alone (Q-API-429). Live today; real for a package with
tens of thousands of versions: measured on 2026-11-24 with 100,000 versions, a page of a package two repositories hold took 0.21 s in the
order of publication (0.03 s in the order of the versions), the package list 0.19 s, and with 100,000 tags of a remote image 0.41 s
([packages.md](../developer/packages.md#a-package-with-100000-versions-h-1683-measured)). Counts kept by the commit and the fill would end
the second part; they would have to follow every rule of what a caller may see (the scope's rows, withheld versions, a remote's listing
rules that change with a download), and none is built.

### H-1901 · The second part of the order of the versions of a package several repositories hold reads every unranked version

In the order of the versions, the versions a format does not rank (an OCI tag such as `latest` or `sha-5ccfd1a`) come after the ranked
ones newest first by their time, a version by its oldest visible row (Q-API-431). For one holder that part is a keyset on a partial index;
for a package that several repositories of the caller's scope hold (an image in a local and a remote repository, the members of a virtual
repository), a version's place is its oldest row over all of them, which a keyset over each holder cannot see, so the walk reads every
unranked visible version of the package, one cheap row each from the partial indexes, and sorts them in the service, as H-1683 does for the
order of publication. Live today; real only for an image that two physical repositories of one scope hold with thousands of tags that are
no version (a CI's commit tags); npm, NuGet, Debian and Ansible store no such version, and a virtual repository over one member is one
holder. Not measured. The remedy would be the same as H-1683's: a time per version kept across its holders.

### H-1900 · The end of a list by content whose versions lead no image costs a request per 1,024 of them

The list by content (Q-API-432) walks the order of the versions and asks, a batch at a time, which of them lead an image; a version that
names an image an earlier version leads is read and left out. One request reads at most 1,024 versions, so a run of versions that lead
nothing (an image's commit tags after its versions, a CI's `x.y.z` and `sha-…` on one manifest; 100,000 tags on one manifest) costs one
request per 1,024 of them, each answering a short or empty page with a cursor; a client that reads to the end pays them. Live today; real
for an OCI image with thousands of tags per manifest. Measured on 2026-11-25 ([oci.md](../developer/oci.md#the-list-by-content-of-an-image-with-100000-tags-q-api-432-h-1900-measured)):
100,000 tags on one manifest are 98 requests of about 108 ms each; the 50,000 commit tags after a CI image's 50,000 versions are 48
requests of 178 to 231 ms; an image whose tags each name their own manifest pages at 24 to 36 ms, as the plain list.
The remedy would be a table of images kept by the commit and the fill (Q-API-432 (b)); not built.

### H-1902 · The downloads of a page of a local image's list by content read the items that hold each image's manifest

The list by content sums an image's downloads from the files of the package that hold its manifest's bytes (`PackageViewImageDownloads`):
of a local image its manifest under its digest and one tag item per tag. For an image with tens of thousands of tags on one manifest the
page reads that many tag items for the image's row, once per page that shows it. Live today; not measured; real only for a local image with
that many tags on one manifest. A remote image's tags are cache entries and hold no item, so its read is its manifest alone.

### H-1847 · A live list reads its rows again; there is no answer of what changed

A live view (R-UI-213) reads again what it shows: a list as many pages as are shown, a version's page its version and its report,
whether anything changed or not. The server has no answer of the kind "what changed in this list since my last read" (Q-UI-1075 (c)),
so an idle tab costs one or two requests a minute per view, and a list extended with **Load more** to ten pages costs ten. Live today in
every live view; real with many open tabs (a hundred people with a repository open: some 200 list reads a minute at idle). Two views
read a cheap summary first and the rest only on a change (a package's page, the ClamAV databases). A change counter per repository and
kind of row, scoped like the list a reader may see, would let a view ask one cheap question instead.

Measured on 2026-11-25 ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#what-an-open-tab-asks-of-the-server-measured)): only a
seen tab reads, so what counts is the windows people see, not their tabs. A seen list costs 6 calls and about 26 statements a minute
(a page of 50 packages is 9 statements and 3.5 ms of CPU), an administrator's dashboard 28 calls and about 130 statements; fifty people
each with a list seen cost a replica under 1 % of a core and 22 statements a second. What a change counter would save is that idle cost;
the largest cost measured is a fast view that stays fast ([H-1870](#h-1870--a-versions-page-reads-every-3-s-for-as-long-as-its-scan-waits),
H-1848). The development agent would build the answer of what changed when the reads of live views are a tenth of a replica's API
requests or of PostgreSQL's statements in an installation's metrics, or when a live list's refresh costs more than about 50 statements.

### H-1848 · A signature check that failed keeps a version's page on the fast reads

A version's page reads every 3 s while a file's malware scan has not answered, an image's scan waits, or a signature reads
**not checked** (R-UI-213). The state `not_checked` stands for a check that waits and for one that failed (R-SIG-034,
`SignatureBadgeState`), so a version whose check failed keeps its page on the fast reads (40 requests a minute of that tab) for as long
as it is open and seen. Live today for a version whose signature check failed; it costs requests, not correctness. A state of its own
for a failed check in the badge would let the page drop to its 60 s.

### H-1870 · A version's page reads every 3 s for as long as its scan waits

A version's page reads its version and its report every 3 s while an image's scan or a file's malware scan has not answered
(R-UI-213), and there is no end to the wait: a scan that waits for hours keeps every page of it that is seen on the fast reads.
Measured on 2026-11-25 ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#what-an-open-tab-asks-of-the-server-measured)): 37 to 41 calls, about 330
statements and 115 ms of a replica's CPU a minute per seen tab, ten times a list's; fifty people with such a page seen cost a replica
about 10 % of a core and PostgreSQL 275 statements a second. Live where a scan waits long: the image scanner or ClamAV down or not
deployed while the scanning is on, a backlog after an advisory sync; on the UI development profile always, which runs no scanner. It costs
requests, not correctness. A fast cadence that slows after some minutes of waiting (3 s, then 15 s, then the page's 60 s) would bound it
without a change on the server.

Narrowed on 2026-11-25 by [Q-UI-1122](#q-ui-1122--a-versions-page-reads-fast-only-while-its-scan-passes-on-its-own): the page reads
fast only while the scan's state passes on its own (an image `queued` or `scanning`, a file's malware scan `queued`); a scan that waits
for a missing scanner or database reads every minute. What stays live is a long queue.

### H-1930 · An image's tags past the hundred its row names are not shown and not found by the filter

Component: the package's page of an image and the opened item (R-UI-110, R-UI-052, Q-UI-1130, Q-UI-1150). Subject: a reader of an image
one of whose manifests more than 101 tags name. Live since the lists by content. An entry of the list by content names at most 100 other
tags (`aliases`, Q-API-432) and says that there are more (`aliasesMore`); the row says "+ more" without a count, and the field **Filter
tags** of the package's page finds the image by none of the tags past the hundred, since the page has never read them. What makes it real:
a pipeline that tags one build many times (a tag per branch and per pipeline run on one manifest), which no image of the owner's
installation does today (his largest has five tags on a manifest, 2026-11-25). The remedy would be a search of the list by a tag on the
server, which the list by content does not offer (only `sort=-version`, Q-API-432), or every alias in the answer.

Component: `make ui-states` ([web-ui.md](../developer/web-ui.md#dialog-states), Q-UI-1140). Subject: a German reader of a dialog. Live

### H-1860 · A heading narrower than 20 letters, and a heading of a screen outside the German pass, are held by no check

The rule of the German file (Q-UI-1091) puts a soft hyphen into every German word of more than 20 letters; a word of 20 letters or
fewer has none, and the English texts have no such rule. Such a word breaks between two letters in a heading whose line is narrower than
the word (some 250 px at the first heading's size, less at a smaller one): no heading of Quader is that narrow today, but a heading in a
narrow column (a card in a grid, a side panel) would be. The render check `heading-broken` finds it only on the screens it renders: in
German the screens of the German pass, in English every screen. Live today for neither: the survey of 2026-11-25 rendered every
German screen without a walk at 390 and 1,024 px (253 each) and found no heading broken. Real once a heading stands in a column narrower
than 250 px, or a German screen outside the pass has one of 20 letters in a line too short for it.

### H-43 · General API rate limits are per replica

Component: the limiter of the management API (R-API-016) on top of R-ARCH-034 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md). Subject: every caller of `/api/v1/` and `/files/`, by token,
session user or client address. Since 2026-10-28 the `read`, `write` and `anonymous` buckets count
cluster-wide in Valkey (Q-API-3), so the configured budget no longer multiplies with the replica
count. What remains is narrower than the heading: counting per replica while Valkey is unavailable,
and counters lost in a failover. Live in the MVP in these cases:

- **Valkey outage.** While a replica cannot reach Valkey, its buckets are local, with the budget
  divided by the live `web` replicas of the registry. If only some replicas lose Valkey, the others
  still count the full budget in Valkey, so a client that spreads its requests gets up to one share
  more than the budget per cut-off replica. After a scale-up during an outage, every replica
  divides by the old count until its next registry read, for at most `system.heartbeat_interval`.
- **Counters lost after a failover.** A Sentinel failover that loses recent writes resets the
  counters it lost, which admits at most one extra window per bucket (R-ARCH-034). A Valkey
  restart without persistence has the same effect. Quader's own cache flush leaves the counters
  alone ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-047).

Tampering is not part of this gap: whoever can write under Quader's Valkey prefix can delete
counters and lift every budget, or raise them and refuse a caller with `429`, and that is H-49 in
[architecture.md](architecture.md), which covers every value Quader keeps in Valkey.

What makes it real: a client that wants more throughput than its budget, for example to scrape
package metadata, and that can time its traffic to a Valkey outage or failover. It does not weaken
credential guessing: tokens are 256-bit random values, and the break-glass lockout counts failures
in PostgreSQL (R-AUTH-038), which survives a loss of Valkey's data. Per-replica in-flight limits (`server.max_in_flight`) still protect each replica in
every case.

### H-44 · Credentials displayed in the browser are outside Quader's control

A token shown once, embedded in a snippet or copied to the clipboard (R-UI-016, R-UI-029) is readable
by browser extensions with page access, by clipboard managers and history tools, and by anyone
watching the screen. Quader reduces exposure (environment-variable references by default,
repository-scoped short-lived setup tokens, no storage, Blob URLs revoked at once), but cannot prevent
capture once the value is on screen or in the clipboard.

### H-45 · Hiding unauthorized resources is not timing-safe

With hiding on, a missing and an unreadable repository, item or package give the same status and body
(R-API-008), but the server takes different code paths, and the response time can tell them apart.
Equalizing response times is not specified; an attacker able to measure many requests can still learn
whether a key or path exists.

### H-319 · A configuration file that holds a token can be committed

Component: the client setup page (R-UI-016) and the guides (R-UI-049). Subject: the projects of users who choose "Create
a token for this setup" or "Use a token I already have". Live today. In those modes the snippets and the downloaded
`.npmrc` or `.yarnrc.yml` hold the token itself, and the project directory is where the guide tells a reader to save a
configuration file. The default mode references `QUADER_TOKEN`, the guide says never to commit a file that holds a token
and to keep such a file in the home directory, and the token of the setup page is scoped to one repository and expires
after `ui.client_setup.token_ttl`; nothing checks a repository of source code. What makes it real: a developer who
downloads the file with an embedded token into a project and commits it. Hardening: a secret-scanning rule for
`qdr_(pat|sat|cit)_` in the source-code host (the prefix and the CRC-32 of INV-8 make the token recognisable), and a
shorter `ui.client_setup.token_ttl`.

### H-320 · A guide can state what Quader no longer does

Component: the guide text of a format (R-UI-049, R-ARCH-008 `Guide()`). Subject: readers who decide on the guide's
statements, for example that a claimed name never reaches a remote member, which names an audit withholds, or that a
published version never changes. Live whenever a change of behaviour leaves the guide unchanged. The tests pin what can be
pinned (npm: every code of the troubleshooting table and its status against the problem catalog, the notices the
handlers send, the defaults the text names, the snippets against the client setup), not every sentence. What makes it
real: a change to the dependency-confusion rules, the audit forward or the publish rules whose author does not read the
format's guide. Hardening: a change to a requirement that a guide section cites is reviewed together with that section
(the developer pages name the files), and every new fact a guide states gets a test.

### H-321 · An anonymous reader learns the token variable's name from the guide of a format

Component: `GET /api/v1/formats/{format}/guide` (R-API-053). Subject: installations with public content (`publicContent`,
R-AUTH-037); dormant otherwise. The operation is as public as the format list and names `ui.client_setup.token_env_var` in its text and
snippets, besides the base URL that the format list already serves. The name is no secret, but it tells someone who can
read a developer's environment which variable holds a Quader token. What makes it real: a `public` repository, a variable
name other than the default, and an attacker with read access to process environments of developer machines or CI
runners, who could read every variable anyway.

### H-877 · The OCI logo rests on a non-commercial use under the Linux Foundation's terms

Component: the format icon of `oci` ([Q-UI-225](#q-ui-225--a-format-shows-its-owners-logo-where-the-owners-terms-allow-it-else-the-neutral-glyph)).
Subject: every installation that holds an OCI repository. Dormant today: Quader is an open-source project and is not sold.
The Linux Foundation's trademark usage permits a logo expressly only as a link to the project and for private
merchandise, and asks for written permission for a logo "in any commercial or marketing context"; a project's own
interface that names a format beside its logo is neither permitted nor forbidden in words. Quader follows every other rule
of the page (official files, no colour change, nothing on top, smaller than the name, the trademark notice). What makes it
real: Quader sold or run as a paid service with the logo in its interface, or a request of the Linux Foundation. Then the
Linux Foundation's written permission, or the neutral glyph for `oci` (one line in `formatIcon`).

### H-878 · The owner and the terms of the NuGet mark are not published

Component: the format icon of `nuget` (Q-UI-225). Subject: every installation that holds a NuGet repository. Live today.
The logo's copyright licence is the CC BY 2.0 of the NuGet project's media repository, which publishes the files for the
community. No trademark guideline for the NuGet name or logo was found from the NuGet project, the .NET Foundation or
Microsoft; nuget.org's terms (Microsoft) reserve Microsoft's logos and product icons, and Microsoft's trademark list (FY27Q2)
does not name NuGet. Not verified: who holds a trademark in the NuGet logo, and whether that holder counts it among
Microsoft's product icons. What makes it real: such a holder stating that the logo needs a licence. Then the neutral glyph
for `nuget`.

### H-879 · An owner's terms can change after the day they were read

Component: the format logos and their notice ([NOTICE.txt](../../web/public/formats/NOTICE.txt)). Subject: every
installation. Live from the day after 2026-11-11, when the terms of Q-UI-225 were read. npm's policy calls itself a living
document, Docker and the Linux Foundation reserve changes without notice, and nothing in Quader reads the pages again. What
makes it real: an owner that narrows its terms (Debian, NuGet, the Linux Foundation) while Quader still shows its logo, or one
that opens them (npm, Red Hat, Docker) while Quader still shows the glyph. Hardening: read the pages of the table in Q-UI-225
again when a format is added and before the first stable release, and record the day in the notice.

### H-980 · Sorting by grade covers the first 1,000 entries of a list

Component: the repository content list (R-UI-094, Q-UI-373). Subject: every reader who sorts a repository's items by grade. Live
from the grades on. Sorting by grade loads the list up to 1,000 entries and sorts them in the browser, because the server has no
sort by grade; a repository with more items sorts its first 1,000 by name and grade, and the worst item may be the 1,001st. The
list says so under the table. What makes it real: a remote repository that caches more than 1,000 packages, and a reader who
looks for its worst one. Hardening: a server sort over a stored grade (Q-UI-373 (b)).

### H-2001 · The list of CI issuers says a key fetch's failure in a sentence only

Stage: the list of **Admin area › CI** ([issuer-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/ci/issuer-list.ts)). Subject: an issuer whose last
key fetch failed. Live: the row says the failure in words (Q-UI-1227); its status and host are on the issuer's **Keys** tab, one click
away. A compact place, as R-UI-216's toast is; the row has no **Details** of its own.

### H-1990 · Sentences built in code still hold a value as plain text

Component: the sentences a component builds with `$localize` and a value placeholder (Q-UI-1213). Subject: a reader at 390 px, where a
host, a key or a path at the end of a line breaks at a hyphen or a dot. Live since the screens. Q-UI-1213 marked the values of the
templates' sentences and the credential's hosts; these sentences of the code still join their value into the string: the reasons of a
download link and a Bastion's handover (`links.reason.quader-host`, `links.reason.quader-host-bastion`,
`bastion.handover.reason.quader-host`), the causes of a failed download (`downloads.why.insecure-redirect-host`,
`downloads.why.foreign-host-host`, `downloads.why.class.tls-host`, `downloads.why.class.egress-host`), the advisory database's state
(`vuln.sources.db-*`), the ClamAV lines (`clamav.verification.repository`, `clamav.updater.repository`, `clamav.on.address`), the
policy explainer (`explain.covered`, `explain.not-covered`) and the install note (`pkg.install.disabled-note`). What makes it real: a
value with a hyphen or a dot that reaches the end of a line. The remedy is the one of Q-UI-1213 per sentence: the component splits the
sentence with `aroundValue` and the template sets the value as `<code translate="no">`.

### H-2080 · A remote package's README is shown only once a version is stored

Closed on 2026-11-26 by [R-CUR-028](remote-curation.md#r-cur-028--an-opened-package-of-the-tab-upstream-shows-its-documentation-and-the-facts-of-its-newest-version-read-through-and-not-stored):
a package of the tab **Upstream** that no client fetched yet shows its upstream's README read through and not stored (npm's package
document's `readme`, NuGet's README of `ReadmeUriTemplate`, the Galaxy's docs-blob and a role's content), with the facts of its newest
version. Its version page still comes with the first stored version; what remains of the gap is
[H-2200](remote-curation.md#h-2200--a-debian-package-of-the-upstream-shows-no-long-description-homepage-or-relations) to
[H-2203](remote-curation.md#h-2203--a-collections-readme-reads-its-whole-docs-blob) of remote-curation.md.

### H-2081 · Documentation that belongs to OCI, Debian and generic files is not shown as documentation

R-UI-218 turns on a format whose documentation is regularly present; OCI, Debian and generic files keep their table. Documentation some
of their packages carry is not shown: a Helm chart's README inside an OCI artifact, an image's `org.opencontainers.image.description`
annotation, a Debian package's long description and its `/usr/share/doc` files. Each would need a reader of its own and a decision of the
owner whether it is regularly present.

### H-2082 · The switch between the versions lists the ten newest only

A version older than the ten newest is reached through the table of every version (`…/-/versions`), not through the switch; the switch
has no search (Q-UI-1243).

### H-2165 · The tab Upstream does not mark a deprecated Helm chart

Stage: R-API-085, the tab Upstream of an OCI remote. A chart's deprecation is in its config blob, which the catalogue of Docker Hub, Quay,
GitHub or GitLab does not carry: a tag the remote has not cached is listed there without the mark, though `helm install` of it will warn.
A cached tag is marked in every other list. Live for every deprecated chart a remote has not pulled yet; what makes it real is a reader who
chooses a chart version from the tab Upstream alone.

### H-2166 · Which copy of a latest version the list reads is not defined

Stage: R-API-085. When two repositories of the scope hold the latest version of a package and only one of them marks it deprecated (a
copy from a deprecated local repository into another, a remote whose upstream deprecated a version that a local repository holds too), the
list's row and its filter read one of the two rows, which one is not defined; the version's page reads the copy that was stored first.
Live only for such a pair; it decides a mark, not a permission.
